tools.name: get_conversation_state
tools.description: Read the selected conversation, composer readiness, draft, attachments and generation lifecycle. A dispatched send is not a completed response; inspect this state to observe progress.

tools.name: list_conversation_content_diagnostics
tools.description: Read the selected conversation's retained content diagnostics, native rendering status and fallback receipts. Dev/staging payloads and their matched prompt are included only when already admitted for display. A diagnostic disclosure does not imply a missing widget. Follow nextOffset for all retained results; each page contains at most 128 entries and eight MiB. This does not send a request or change the conversation.

offset.description: Nonnegative diagnostic entry offset, default 0; use nextOffset from the prior page.

limit.description: Integer from 1 to 128, default 128.

tools.name: set_composer_draft

tools.description: Send a message through the current composer's ordinary submission and verification flow. Returns dispatch status; use get_conversation_state to observe acceptance, completion or failure. Never automatically retry a dispatched send.

tools.name: submitQuery
tools.description: Alias for submit_conversation_message. Returns dispatch status, not response completion.

tools.name: stop_conversation
tools.description: Request Stop for the selected conversation's current generation or pending send through its existing owner. Inspect get_conversation_state for settlement; an idle conversation returns an unavailable error.

tools.name: start_conversation

tools.name: asus_product_search
tools.description:
Search ASUS official website products by a specific product name or model keyword (e.g. "ZenBook 14 OLED", "Vivobook S 15", "ProArt P16", "RT-AX88U"), for a specific country site. Product URLs in the results are already absolute — use them as-is.

TOOL SELECTION (important): use this tool ONLY when the user explicitly names a concrete product, series name, or model number. For need-based or condition-based requests — a product category, a budget or price range, spec requirements, or a sort preference (e.g. "laptops under $1000", "a lightweight ultrabook for work", "gaming desktops", "cheapest monitor", "newest AiO PCs", "OLED 14-inch notebooks") — do NOT use this tool; use asus_productLine + asus_product_filters instead. If the request mixes a named model with extra conditions, use this tool for the named model. When in doubt (vague or need-based request), prefer asus_product_filters.

searchKey.description: Search keyword used to match product name or attributes

pageSize.description: Number of products to return per page

page.description: Page number of the product list to retrieve, starting from 1

websiteCode.description: Country/region site code to search products from

searchPDLine.description: Top-level product-line filter. Value must be the `DataName` of one of the top-level entries in `filters.SubItem` from a previous call's response (e.g. "laptops" for the "筆記型電腦" / "Laptops" category). Leave empty to search across all product lines. Must be set before searchPDLine2 can be used, since searchPDLine2 is scoped under the selected searchPDLine.

searchPDLine2.description: Second-level product-line filter, nested under searchPDLine. Value must be the `DataName` of one of the entries in the `SubItem` array belonging to the top-level item selected via searchPDLine (e.g. "for-creators" for the "創作者" / "For Creators" sub-category under "laptops"). Only valid in combination with a matching searchPDLine — do not set this without also setting the corresponding searchPDLine, and do not use a DataName from a different top-level item's SubItem list.

tools.name: asus_product_filters
tools.description:
Browse and filter ASUS official website products by product line (ProductLevel1Code / ProductLevel2Code), with optional category, series, spec, price and sort filtering. Product URLs in the returned productList are already absolute — use them as-is.

TOOL SELECTION (important): this is the DEFAULT tool for product discovery. Use asus_product_filters whenever the user does NOT name a specific model or product name — i.e. when they describe a need, a category, or any set of conditions (e.g. "laptops under $1000", "a lightweight ultrabook for work", "gaming desktops", "cheapest monitor", "newest AiO PCs", "OLED 14-inch notebooks"). Only use asus_product_search when the user explicitly names a concrete product or model keyword (e.g. "ZenBook 14 OLED", "Vivobook S 15", "ProArt P16", "RT-AX88U"). If the request mixes both a model name and conditions, prefer asus_product_search for the named model. When in doubt (vague or need-based request), choose asus_product_filters.

REQUIRED FIRST STEP: call asus_productLine with a product category keyword to obtain ProductLevel1Code and ProductLevel2Code, then pass them here together with websiteCode.

FILTER VALUES ARE DYNAMIC: the valid values for CategoryName, SeriesName and spec depend on the product line and websiteCode, and can only be obtained from THIS tool's own response (they are NOT available from asus_productLine). So when the user has category / series / spec requirements:
Step 1: call this tool with only ProductLevel1Code, ProductLevel2Code and websiteCode.
Step 2: read the returned filter object — use Category.CategoryList[].WebPath for CategoryName, Series.SeriesList[].WebPath for SeriesName, and SpecCategory.Item[].Id for spec (collect every matching value into an array, there may be more than one). Then call this tool again with those values to get the filtered product list.

NO DISCOVERY NEEDED FOR PRICE OR SORT: pass a concrete budget directly via minPrice / maxPrice as plain numbers (e.g. "under $30000" → maxPrice: 30000; "$20k–$40k" → minPrice: 20000, maxPrice: 40000). sort accepts a fixed set of values: "Recommend", "Newsest", "Most Popular", "Price High to Low", "Price Low to High".

Use page / pageSize for pagination (page starts from 1).

ProductLevel1Code.description: 主產品線 ProductLevel1Code (根據 asus_productLine 結果帶入)

ProductLevel2Code.description: 子產品線 ProductLevel2Code (根據 asus_productLine 結果帶入)

websiteCode.description: Country/region site code to search articles from

pageSize.description: Number of articles to return per page

page.description: Page number of the article list to retrieve, starting from 1

sort.description: Product sort order. Valid values can only be obtained by first calling this tool without sort, corresponding to sortType in the returned sort list.

CategoryName.description: 產品類別 (根據 asus_product_filters 的 filter 內 Category.CategoryList 中的 WebPath 結果帶入)

SeriesName.description: 產品系列 (根據 asus_product_filters 的 filter 內 Series.SeriesList 中的 WebPath 結果帶入)

spec.description: 產品篩選條件 (根據 asus_product_filters 的 filter 內 SpecCategory.Item 中的 Id 結果帶入)

minPrice.description: Minimum product price. Preferred over the price parameter when the user gives a concrete budget or price range — pass the number directly, no discovery call needed.

maxPrice.description: Maximum product price. Preferred over the price parameter when the user gives a concrete budget or price range — pass the number directly, no discovery call needed.

tools.name: searchBuses
tools.description: Search for available buses between two cities on a specific date. Resolves city names automatically. Use this tool on the HOME page when the user gives route + date + filters in one prompt. Optionally include filter preferences (AC, seat type, departure/arrival slots, operator/brand keyword like Volvo) — they are applied after navigation to the results page. Use runAfterSearchResultsLoad (same shape as runSrpBookingFlow) so open-bus + seat + continue runs automatically after results load — required for multi-step prompts because navigation unloads the home page.

source.description: Source city name (e.g., "Bangalore", "Singapore", "Kuala Lumpur", "Phnom Penh")

destination.description: Destination city name (e.g., "Chennai", "Johor Bahru", "Penang", "Siem Reap")

date.description: Travel date. Use ISO YYYY-MM-DD with the correct calendar year (same as the user's "today"). Accepts natural language ("today", "tomorrow") or "in N days". If the year is wrong/outdated, it is corrected to this year or next.

filters.description: Optional filters to pre-apply on the results page. Include every criterion the user asked for (e.g. AC + SLEEPER + Volvo) in one object.

departureTime.description: Preferred departure time slot: MORNING (6AM-12PM), AFTERNOON (12PM-6PM), EVENING (6PM-12AM), NIGHT (12AM-6AM)

arrivalTime.description: Preferred arrival time slot: MORNING (6AM-12PM), AFTERNOON (12PM-6PM), EVENING (6PM-12AM), NIGHT (12AM-6AM)

operatorOrBusBrandKeyword.description: Operator or bus brand mentioned by the user (e.g. "Volvo", "Benz"). Resolved on the results page against live filter data.

runAfterSearchResultsLoad.description: Optional. Same fields as runSrpBookingFlow (openBus, selectSeats, continueToBoardingPoints, applyFilters, waitForSearchResultsMs). Stored for the results page to execute after tuples load.

route.description: Bus route in "City to City" format (e.g., "Bangalore to Chennai"). Optional — if omitted, returns all active platform-wide offers.

tools.name: ask_business
tools.description:
Ask the store a question about its policies and services: returns, refunds and exchanges, shipping and delivery, privacy, terms, subscriptions, contact details and opening hours, or FAQ topics such as gift wrapping. The store answers it: from its own knowledge base when the store offers Ask, otherwise from its published policies, FAQ pages and articles. Put the shopper's question in ask.query in their own words, one question per call; name the topic when the shopper only implies it (e.g. a question about sending back a gift is a returns question). Read-only: it does not change the cart, place orders, or start returns. For products, prices and availability, use search_catalog or get_product.
Examples of questions:
  - What is your return policy?
  - How long does shipping to Canada take?
  - What is your phone number?
  - What are your hours of operation?
  - Do you offer gift wrapping?

ask.description: The question and optional buyer context.

context.description: Optional buyer context, such as the shopper's country or language. Send only what the question needs.

address_region.description: The buyer's state or region, e.g. "CA".

intent.description: What the shopper is trying to do, when it adds to the question (e.g. "returning a gift they received").

language.description: The preferred language, e.g. "en".

query.description: The shopper's question, in natural language.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use create_cart or update_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result confirms the destination, and no further navigation is needed to show it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Remove all items from the cart in one step. Use when the user wants to empty their cart or start over.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Create the shopper's cart with the given items, for a shopper whose cart has no items yet. It is the tool for a shopper asking to add or buy something when the cart is empty, and that request is all the authorization it needs. Each line item names a ProductVariant GID in item.id (variant_id from search_catalog or browse_store, or variants[].id from get_product for specific options) and a quantity; every item from one request fits in one call. When the cart already has items, nothing is created or changed: the result is that existing cart with an error message, and update_cart can extend it with its current lines plus the new ones. Returns the whole resulting cart, including its id and line ids. Repeating a call with the same items leaves the cart as it is.

line_items.description: The items the new cart holds.

id.description: ProductVariant GID, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123": variant_id from search_catalog or browse_store, variants[].id from get_product, or line_items[].item.id from a cart result.

quantity.description: How many of this item the line holds.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the shopper's current cart: its id, every line (line id, product and variant titles, variant id, handle, URL, image, unit price, quantity, line price) and the totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. It is also where a change to an existing cart starts from: update_cart takes the cart's id and the complete set of lines the cart should hold, and create_cart applies only to a cart with no items. Works from any page.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare a cart change — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use create_cart or update_cart for that. To view a specific variant (color/size/etc.) in the browser, use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. To add a specific variant to the cart, call get_product with catalog.selected_options to get its variant id. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result confirms the destination, and no further navigation is needed to show it.

catalog.description: Product detail parameters.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

value.description: Option value, e.g. "160cm" or "Fiberglass".

tools.name: get_ucp_profile
tools.description: Get this store's Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) profile, as served at /.well-known/ucp: the UCP version, the services the store offers with their endpoints (e.g. the store's UCP MCP server), its capabilities, and its payment handlers. Use it to discover how to continue a purchase with this store over UCP, or to check which platform operates the store. Read-only; works from any page.

tools.name: manage_orders
tools.description: Navigate to the customer's order history page. Use when the user asks about past orders, order status, tracking, or returns. The user will be prompted to log in if not already authenticated. This MOVES the browser to the order history page; the tool result confirms the destination, and no further navigation is needed to show it.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Proceed to checkout. Verifies the cart is not empty, then MOVES the browser to the checkout page. The tool result confirms the destination, and no further navigation is needed to show it.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use create_cart or update_cart for cart changes. Each product carries variant_id, its selected or first available variant. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to get that variant's id, or use show_variant to display it.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use create_cart or update_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result confirms the destination, and no further navigation is needed to show it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description:
Set the shopper's cart to exactly the given line items. This is a full replacement, not a patch: afterwards the cart holds these lines and only these.
- A listed line with its line_items[].id keeps its place and is set to the given quantity, which is absolute (2 means 2, not 2 more).
- A listed item without a line id is added, or, when that variant is already on one line of the cart, sets that line's quantity.
- A line in the cart that is not listed is removed.
It takes the cart's lines as most recently returned by get_cart, create_cart or update_cart. When the cart has changed since then (for example, the shopper edited it on the page, or a new cart replaced it), or an id is given that is not the shopper's current cart, nothing changes and the result is the current cart with an error message. Since the outcome depends only on the lines sent, repeating a call leaves the cart as it is. An empty line_items list empties the cart; leaving line_items out leaves the lines as they are. Returns the whole resulting cart, including its line ids, and messages about the call.

line_items.description: The complete set of lines the cart holds afterwards. Empty empties the cart; absent leaves the lines as they are.

id.description: Existing cart line id (line_items[].id from a cart result). Absent for an item that is not in the cart yet.
ProductVariant GID, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123": variant_id from search_catalog or browse_store, variants[].id from get_product, or line_items[].item.id from a cart result.

quantity.description: How many of this item the line holds.

id.description: Optional: the page has one cart, the shopper's, and update_cart always acts on it. When given (the id from a cart result), it is compared with the current cart, and a mismatch changes nothing.

tools.name: scan_images_c2pa
tools.description: Scan every on the current page for C2PA Content Credentials (content provenance metadata) and return a per-image summary: whether a manifest is present, the claim generator (the tool that produced or edited the image), the title, and the signer name. Use this to find which images on a page carry provenance data. Note: provenance is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

limit.description: Maximum number of images to fetch and scan (default 25, max 100).

tools.name: inspect_image_c2pa
tools.description: Fetch a single image (by CSS selector or URL) and return its fully decoded C2PA manifest store: every manifest's claim, assertions (e.g. c2pa.actions edit history, schema.org authorship), and the COSE signature details (algorithm and signing-certificate identity). Provide exactly one of `selector` or `url`. Note: the signature is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

selector.description: CSS selector for an element on the page.

url.description: Image URL (absolute, or relative to the current page) to fetch and inspect.

tools.name: zomato_get_session
tools.description: Start here. Reports whether the user is logged in, the delivery address state, the restaurant open on the page and the cart, plus the next step to take. Changes nothing.

tools.name: zomato_request_login_otp
tools.description: Send a login OTP by SMS to the phone number the user gave you. Then ask the user to read the code back and call zomato_verify_login_otp. If the user would rather not share their number or OTP, or wants email or Google, use zomato_open_login_dialog instead. Returns "logged_in" without sending anything when the session is already valid.

phone.description: The phone number the user gave you in this conversation. Never guess it. Indian numbers can include or omit +91.

tools.name: zomato_verify_login_otp
tools.description: Finish the OTP login started by zomato_request_login_otp, using the code the user read out. The phone number is remembered from that call. On success the user is logged in and the page reloads.

otp.description: The OTP the user read out in this conversation. Never guess it.

tools.name: zomato_open_login_dialog
tools.description: Open the Zomato login dialog on the page so the user signs in themselves, by phone, email or Google. Offer it to anyone who would rather not share their number or OTP with you. The page reloads when they finish, which ends this conversation.

tools.name: zomato_list_addresses
tools.description: List the saved delivery addresses with "canDeliver" and "isSelected", and say which one would be picked automatically. Changes nothing.

tools.name: zomato_select_address
tools.description: Select the delivery address. With "addressId", selects that saved address. With no arguments, keeps a valid current address or picks the default: the one last used on this browser, or the only deliverable one. When several could apply it selects nothing and returns "no_address_selected" with all the ids.

tools.name: zomato_add_address
tools.description: Save a new delivery address to the account and select it. Step 1: pass { "locationQuery" } (an area, street or landmark) to get matching locations. Step 2: once the user confirms one, call again with its "placeId" and the address details. A single unambiguous match is used directly. Missing required fields come back in "missingFields".

locationQuery.description: Area, street or landmark to look up.

placeId.description: A placeId from an earlier zomato_add_address call.

address.description: House or flat number and building.

tag.description: How to label it, e.g. Home, Work, Hotel or Other.

otherTag.description: A custom label when tag is "Other".

select.description: Select the new address for this order. Defaults to true.

tools.name: zomato_search_restaurants
tools.description: Find restaurants for a dish, cuisine or restaurant name near the delivery address. "pizza" returns restaurants that serve pizza as well as ones named after it. Each result has restaurantId, rating, etaMinutes, costForTwo, isOpen and canOrder. deliveryFee is null because it is only known once the cart is priced (zomato_quote_cart or zomato_prepare_checkout). If no address is selected it picks the default first, and reports the outcome in "address".

query.description: A dish, cuisine or restaurant name.

context.description: Optional. Defaults to "delivery" (or "takeaway" on a takeaway page). Pass "dineout" or "nightlife" only when the user wants to go out rather than order.

limit.description: Maximum restaurants to return (default and maximum 20).

tools.name: zomato_get_restaurant_menu
tools.description: Open a restaurant and return its menu in one call. Pass "restaurantId" from zomato_search_restaurants; leave it out to read the restaurant already open. The result names the active restaurant, so check it before adding items. A dish with hasAddOns true needs zomato_get_dish_options before it can be added.

orderUrl.description: Optional. The orderUrl of a search result, for a restaurant not returned by search in this conversation.

search.description: Optional text to match against dish names, descriptions and categories.

category.description: Optional category name. The result lists every category.

limit.description: Optional cap on how many dishes to return. Leave it out to get the whole menu.

tools.name: zomato_get_dish_options
tools.description: Get the add-on groups for a dish on the open restaurant. This is the only source of add-on ids. "min" above 0 means the group is required; "selectionType" single takes exactly one. Nested groups have "parentOptionId" and apply only when that option is chosen.

itemId.description: A dish id from zomato_get_restaurant_menu.

restaurantId.description: Optional. The restaurantId you expect to be open. The call fails instead of acting on a different restaurant.

tools.name: zomato_add_item_to_cart
tools.description: Add a dish to the cart. This increments: the same dish with the same add-ons goes onto the same line and raises its quantity by "quantity". Different add-ons make a new line. The result returns the "lineItemId"; to make a line an exact quantity, use zomato_set_item_quantity instead of adding again.

itemId.description: A dish id from zomato_get_restaurant_menu.

quantity.description: How many to add (default 1).

addOnIds.description: Option ids from zomato_get_dish_options. Include the parent option when choosing nested add-ons.

restaurantId.description: Optional. The restaurantId you expect to be open. The call fails instead of acting on a different restaurant.

tools.name: zomato_set_item_quantity
tools.description: Set a cart line to an exact quantity. Calling it twice with the same value changes nothing the second time. 0 removes the line. Use a "lineItemId" from zomato_get_cart or zomato_add_item_to_cart.

quantity.description: The quantity the line should have.

restaurantId.description: Optional. The restaurantId you expect to be open. The call fails instead of acting on a different restaurant.

tools.name: zomato_remove_cart_line
tools.description: Delete one whole cart line, whatever its quantity. To reduce a quantity instead, use zomato_set_item_quantity.

restaurantId.description: Optional. The restaurantId you expect to be open. The call fails instead of acting on a different restaurant.

tools.name: zomato_get_cart
tools.description: Read the cart as the user sees it: one entry per line with lineItemId, quantity, add-ons and line total, plus the restaurant it belongs to. The subtotal excludes taxes and fees; zomato_quote_cart or zomato_prepare_checkout return the full bill.

tools.name: zomato_clear_cart
tools.description: Empty the cart, including one saved for another restaurant. Destructive, so only call it when the user asks to start over.

tools.name: zomato_quote_cart
tools.description: Optional. Price the current cart with Zomato without leaving the page: every bill line (item total, taxes, delivery fee and so on) and the grand total. Use it when the user asks what the order will cost before deciding. It is not a required step: zomato_prepare_checkout prices the cart itself.

restaurantId.description: Optional. The restaurantId you expect to be open. The call fails instead of acting on a different restaurant.

tools.name: zomato_prepare_checkout
tools.description: Open the Zomato checkout page with the cart, once it has what the user asked for and a delivery address is selected. It runs the site's own continue-to-checkout flow, so the cart is priced once, by that flow, and returns that bill when the flow provides one (otherwise the checkout page shows it). It does not place the order or take payment: the user reviews the bill on the checkout page and presses the place order button themselves. Optional "quoteId" from zomato_quote_cart makes it refuse if the cart or address changed after the user saw that quote.

quoteId.description: Optional. From zomato_quote_cart, when the user was shown that quote.

restaurantId.description: Optional. The restaurantId you expect to be open. The call fails instead of acting on a different restaurant.

zomato.com.name: Zomato

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description:
Set the shopper's cart to exactly the given line items. This is a full replacement, not a patch: afterwards the cart holds these lines and only these.
- A listed line with its line_items[].id keeps its place and is set to the given quantity, which is absolute (2 means 2, not 2 more).
- A listed item without a line id is added, or, when that variant is already on one line of the cart, sets that line's quantity.
- A line in the cart that is not listed is removed.
It takes the cart's lines as most recently returned by get_cart, create_cart or update_cart. When the cart has changed since then (for example, the shopper edited it on the page, or a new cart replaced it), or an id is given that is not the shopper's current cart, nothing changes and the result is the current cart with an error message. Since the outcome depends only on the lines sent, repeating a call leaves the cart as it is. An empty line_items list empties the cart; leaving line_items out leaves the lines as they are. tools.name: ask_business
tools.description:
Ask the store a question about its policies and services: returns, refunds and exchanges, shipping and delivery, privacy, terms, subscriptions, contact details and opening hours, or FAQ topics such as gift wrapping. The store answers it: from its own knowledge base when the store offers Ask, otherwise from its published policies, FAQ pages and articles. Put the shopper's question in ask.query in their own words, one question per call; name the topic when the shopper only implies it (e.g. a question about sending back a gift is a returns question). Read-only: it does not change the cart, place orders, or start returns. For products, prices and availability, use search_catalog or get_product.
Examples of questions:

  - How long does shipping to Canada take?
  - What is your phone number?
  - What are your hours of operation?

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Product detail parameters.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

value.description: Option value, e.g. "160cm" or "Fiberglass".

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant. To change a quantity or remove something already in the cart, use update_cart_lines instead — this tool can only add.

line_items.description: Items to add (1-10).

item.description: The merchandise to add.

id.description: ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

handle.description: Product handle. Adds the selected or first available variant; call get_product first if the user requested specific options.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: How many to add. Defaults to 1.

tools.name: update_cart_lines
tools.description: Change the quantity of items already in the cart, or remove them. Every change here addresses an existing cart line by its id, so call get_cart first unless you already have line_items[].id from an earlier get_cart in this conversation. Pass the ABSOLUTE target quantity, not a delta — quantity 2 means the line ends up at 2 regardless of what it was. Use quantity 0 to remove the line entirely. Batch every change for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart_lines once per line. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. This tool cannot add new merchandise. To add something not already in the cart, use add_to_cart. To empty the whole cart at once, use cancel_cart.

line_items.description: Existing cart lines to update or remove (1-10).

id.description: Existing cart line id from get_cart line_items[].id. Required — this tool cannot resolve products by name.

quantity.description: Absolute target quantity for this line (not a delta). 0 removes the line.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Remove all items from the cart in one step. Use when the user wants to empty their cart or start over.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Proceed to checkout. Verifies the cart is not empty, then MOVES the browser to the checkout page. The tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: manage_orders
tools.description: Navigate to the customer's order history page. Use when the user asks about past orders, order status, tracking, or returns. The user will be prompted to log in if not already authenticated. This MOVES the browser to the order history page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: search_shop_policies_and_faqs
tools.description:
Used to get facts about the store's policies, FAQ, or contact details.
When the question is about specific policy kinds, set policy_types to those kinds; leave it unset for general FAQ questions.
Some examples of questions you can ask are:
  - What is your return policy? (policy_types: ["refund"])
  - What is your shipping policy? (policy_types: ["shipping"])
  - What is your phone number? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - What are your hours of operation? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - Do you offer gift wrapping? (general FAQ, no specific policy kind — leave policy_types unset)

query.description: A natural language query. Searches FAQ pages and articles, and routes policies by keyword when policy_types is omitted.

policy_types.description: Policy kinds to fetch, chosen from the user's question — e.g. ["refund"] for returns/exchanges, ["contact"] for phone/hours/address. Include every kind the question touches. Omit when no specific policy is relevant (e.g. a general FAQ question).

tools.name: searchFlights
tools.description: Search AJet flight availability for a route and date. Returns flight options with flight number, times, duration, stops and the lowest available price, plus the total number of flights found. Only outbound flights are ever returned, even for a round trip - see returnDate. Omitted fields mean the default: no stops, same-day arrival, seats available. Read-only: it never books, holds or modifies anything.

origin.description: Departure airport IATA code, e.g. "SAW". A city code such as "IST" is also accepted.

destination.description: Arrival airport IATA code, e.g. "ESB". A city code such as "ANK" is also accepted.

returnDate.description: Optional return date, YYYY-MM-DD. Prices the outbound leg as a round trip; return flights are never returned by this tool - use openFlightSearch.

adults.description: Number of adult passengers. Defaults to 1.

children.description: Number of child passengers (2-12 years). Defaults to 0.

infants.description: Number of infant passengers (under 2). Defaults to 0.

currencyCode.description: Optional ISO currency code for the returned prices, e.g. "TRY" or "EUR".

tools.name: getCalendarPrices
tools.description: Get the cheapest AJet fare per day for one or more months on a given route. Useful for answering "which day is cheapest to fly". For each month "days" maps the day of the month to that day's cheapest fare in the returned currency; a null price means no fare (also listed under "noFlight"/"noSeat"). "samePriceAllDays" means every day costs the same, so no day is cheaper. Read-only.

origin.description: Departure airport IATA code, e.g. "SAW". A city code such as "IST" is also accepted and is resolved to the airport AJet serves.

destination.description: Arrival airport IATA code, e.g. "ESB". A city code such as "ANK" is also accepted and is resolved to the airport AJet serves.

months.description: Months to query, each as "YYYY-MM" (e.g. ["2026-09", "2026-10"]). At most 2.

currency.description: Optional ISO currency code for the returned prices, e.g. "TRY" or "EUR".

tools.name: getAirportInfo
tools.description: Look up AJet airports. With no arguments it returns the full list of departure airports. With "query" it filters by IATA code, airport name, city or country. With "fromAirport" it returns the destinations reachable from that airport. Read-only.

query.description: Optional free-text filter: IATA code ("ESB"), airport name, city ("Ankara") or country. At most 100 characters.

fromAirport.description: Optional departure airport IATA code. When given, returns the destinations served from that airport instead of the full list.

tools.name: getCheapestFares
tools.description: Get the cheapest AJet one-way fares for the days around a given date on a route (a "flexible dates" view). Useful for "is it cheaper a day earlier or later". "samePriceAllDays" means no day is cheaper than another. Read-only.

origin.description: Departure airport IATA code, e.g. "SAW". A city code such as "IST" is also accepted.

destination.description: Arrival airport IATA code, e.g. "ESB".

departureDate.description: Reference date in YYYY-MM-DD format; results cover the days around it.

dateOffset.description: How many days before/after the reference date to include. Defaults to 2.

adults.description: Number of adult passengers. Defaults to 1.

currencyCode.description: Optional ISO currency code for the returned prices, e.g. "TRY".

tools.name: getFlightDates
tools.description: List the dates AJet actually flies a route, so a day can be picked before pricing it. Returns the available departure dates between startDate and endDate as YYYY-MM-DD, ready to pass to searchFlights or getCheapestFares. An empty list means the route is not flown in that range. Read-only.

origin.description: Departure airport IATA code, e.g. "SAW". A city code such as "IST" is also accepted and is resolved to the airport AJet serves.

destination.description: Arrival airport IATA code, e.g. "ESB". A city code such as "ANK" is also accepted and is resolved to the airport AJet serves.

startDate.description: First date of the range to check, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

endDate.description: Optional last date of the range, in YYYY-MM-DD format. Defaults to 30 days after startDate.

tools.name: getPassengerTypes
tools.description: List the passenger types AJet sells on a route, including discounted ones such as student or teacher, with the age limits that apply. Useful for "is there a student discount on this route". Types marked "special" need proof of eligibility at the airport; searchFlights prices adults, children and infants only, so it cannot quote a discounted fare. Read-only.

origin.description: Departure airport IATA code, e.g. "SAW". A city code such as "IST" is also accepted and is resolved to the airport AJet serves.

destination.description: Arrival airport IATA code, e.g. "ESB". A city code such as "ANK" is also accepted and is resolved to the airport AJet serves.

tools.name: getCurrencies
tools.description: Lists the currency codes AJet can show fares in, and which one the page is currently using. Use a listed code as "currencyCode" in the fare tools. Makes no request. Read-only.

tools.name: askFaq
tools.description: Answer a customer question from AJet's own published help content: baggage, pets, children and infants, check-in, seat and meal selection, special assistance and accessibility, discounts, invoices, refunds and changes. Returns the closest matching questions with their answers, in the language the page is shown in. Use this instead of relying on general airline knowledge. Ask one topic per call; a narrower question returns a fuller answer. Read-only.

query.description: The question in the user's own words, e.g. "how much cabin baggage can I take". One topic per call; specific questions match better than broad ones.

tools.name: openFlightSearch
tools.description: Runs an AJet flight search in the page the user is looking at and opens the results, exactly as pressing Search would. Use this to show the user results; use searchFlights instead to read the data yourself. Refuses while the user is in a booking flow so their progress is not lost.

origin.description: Departure airport IATA code, e.g. "SAW". A city code such as "IST" is also accepted.

destination.description: Arrival airport IATA code, e.g. "ESB". A city code such as "ANK" is also accepted.

returnDate.description: Optional return date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Its presence makes the search a round trip, so the outbound leg is priced under round-trip fare rules.

adults.description: Number of adult passengers. Defaults to 1.

children.description: Number of child passengers (2-12 years). Defaults to 0.

infants.description: Number of infant passengers (under 2). Defaults to 0.

tools.name: openCheapestDay
tools.description: Find the cheapest day to fly in a given month on an AJet route and open the results for that day in the page the user is looking at, in one step. Use this for "when is it cheapest to fly in September, show me". Replaces calling getCalendarPrices and then openFlightSearch. If every day costs the same it says so and opens the earliest one. Past days are skipped. Refuses while the user is in a booking flow so their progress is not lost.

origin.description: Departure airport IATA code, e.g. "SAW". A city code such as "IST" is also accepted.

destination.description: Arrival airport IATA code, e.g. "ESB". A city code such as "ANK" is also accepted.

month.description: Month to search, as "YYYY-MM" (e.g. "2026-09"). One month per call.

adults.description: Number of adult passengers. Defaults to 1.

children.description: Number of child passengers (2-12 years). Defaults to 0.

infants.description: Number of infant passengers (under 2). Defaults to 0.

tools.name: availability.getShownFlights
tools.description: Reads the flight results the user is currently looking at, in the order and with the filters and sort they see on screen. Makes no request and starts no new search. Use it to answer questions about the visible list; use searchFlights for a different route or date.

tools.name: availability.getSelection
tools.description: Reads which flight and fare package the user has already selected on the results page, per direction (OUTBOUND / RETURN). Makes no request. Returns an empty selection if nothing is chosen yet.

tools.name: availability.filterFlights
tools.description: Filters the flight results the user is currently looking at, by stop count and departure time of day. Only changes what is displayed — no new search is made and nothing is booked. Call with no arguments to clear the filter. Read-only alternative: searchFlights returns the data without touching the screen.

direct.description: Show non-stop flights. Defaults to false (no filter).

tools.name: qu-discover-capabilities
tools.description: List every WebMCP capability across this whole site: the intent, the page URL pattern that hosts it, and the tool names to call there. Optionally pass navigateTo to jump to the page that hosts a capability (the full page reloads; call the target tool after it loads). Use this first when the tool you need is not registered on the current page.

navigateTo.description: Optional same-origin path or URL to navigate to, e.g. a capability urlPattern with any * replaced by a real value. Cross-origin destinations are refused.

tools.name: qu-search-programs
tools.description: List Quinnipiac University academic programs that match optional filters, from the university's official program finder (undergraduate majors, graduate, law and medicine degrees, dual-degree programs, minors and certificates). Use it when a student asks what Quinnipiac offers, e.g. 'nursing programs at Quinnipiac', 'online master's degrees in business' or 'what can I study in health sciences'. It does not rank or rate programs. Filters: keyword (free text), school (e.g. 'School of Nursing'), areaOfInterest (e.g. 'Nursing', 'Health & Medical'), deliveryMethod ('On Campus', 'Online', 'Hybrid') and degreeLevel. Returns each matching program's name, degree, level, school (when known), delivery modality and page URL, plus the result count per level. Programs whose name matches the keyword exactly come first, bachelor's majors before other degree types; sameNamePrograms flags names shared by several programs so the student can pick the right degree. If a filter value is not recognized, returns the valid options. Pass a program URL to qu-get-program-details for full details. Every returned link carries its host, plus external: true when it is not a Quinnipiac site (qu.edu or quinnipiac.edu). Works on any page of the site.

school.description: School name, e.g. 'School of Nursing', 'School of Business', 'School of Health Sciences', 'School of Law'. Partial names like 'Nursing' are accepted.

areaOfInterest.description: Area of interest, e.g. 'Nursing', 'Health & Medical', 'Business & Finance', 'Computing & Technology', 'STEM-Designated Programs'.

degreeLevel.description: Which program group to search. Default: undergraduate and graduate together. 'graduate' includes master's, doctoral, law (JD) and medicine (MD). 'all' adds dual-degree programs, minors and certificates.

limit.description: Maximum programs to return (default 30, max 100).

tools.name: qu-get-program-details
tools.description: Get the details of one Quinnipiac University academic program (undergraduate, graduate, online, law or medicine) from its official program page. Pass url (a program page URL from qu-search-programs) or name (e.g. 'BS in Nursing', 'MSN Family Nurse Practitioner'); with neither, it reads the program page the browser is on. When a name matches several programs (for example 'Nursing' is both the BS in Nursing and the Accelerated BSN), it returns status 'ambiguous' with every candidate's name, degree, level and url and chooses none; ask the student, then call again with url or degree. Returns the program name, degree/credential, school, delivery modality, overview, key facts (such as duration or clinical hours), 'by the numbers' statistics (such as outcome rates), student learning outcomes, accreditation note, total credits from the curriculum page, and links to the curriculum, program admissions, tuition and financial aid, request-information and apply pages. Use it to compare programs or answer 'tell me about the nursing program'. Every returned link carries its host, plus external: true when it is not a Quinnipiac site (qu.edu or quinnipiac.edu). Works on any page of the site.

url.description: Program page URL, e.g. https://www.qu.edu/schools/nursing/programs/bachelors-degree/nursing/ or https://grad.qu.edu/programs/masters-degree/msn-family-nurse-practitioner/.

name.description: Program name to look up in the program finder when no url is known, e.g. 'Nursing', 'Physician Assistant', 'MBA'. If several programs share the name, the tool returns status 'ambiguous' with the candidates instead of choosing one.

degree.description: Optional degree to pick between programs that share a name, e.g. 'BSN', 'Accelerated BSN', 'MSN', 'Major'.

includeCurriculumCredits.description: Also fetch the curriculum page to read total credits (default true).

tools.name: qu-search-site
tools.description: Full-text search across the Quinnipiac University website (www.qu.edu and its school sites), the same search as the site's search box. Pass keyword and optionally page (12 results per page) and type to keep only one kind of result ('program', 'page', 'article', 'person'). Returns the total result count, page info and each hit's type, title, short teaser, section and URL. Person hits return name, position, department and profile URL only. For finding degree programs prefer qu-search-programs; use this for anything else (policies, housing, student life, news, offices). Every returned link carries its host, plus external: true when it is not a Quinnipiac site (qu.edu or quinnipiac.edu). Works on any page of the site.

keyword.description: Search text, e.g. 'nursing clinical placements', 'housing', 'honors program'.

page.description: Result page number, starting at 1 (12 results per page).

type.description: Optional: keep only this kind of hit from the returned page.

tools.name: qu-get-admission-deadlines
tools.description: Read Quinnipiac University's current admission deadlines live from the official admissions pages. studentType selects the page: 'first-year' (default; Early Decision, Early Action, Regular Decision), 'international', 'transfer', 'military' or 'graduate'. Pass programUrl (a program page URL from qu-search-programs) to read that program's own admissions page instead, which is where graduate programs and programs with special deadlines (for example nursing) list theirs. Returns each deadline table as rows keyed by its column headers (application type, application deadline, decision notification, FAFSA priority deadline, deposit due), plus footnotes and program-specific deadline notes, the page's own cycle and year text (yearContext, e.g. 'Apply for the fall semester' or 'for the 2026-27 application'), an asOf date, and the source page URL. Values are read at call time, never cached. Every returned link carries its host, plus external: true when it is not a Quinnipiac site (qu.edu or quinnipiac.edu). Works on any page of the site.

programUrl.description: Optional program page URL; reads its admissions subpage (e.g. .../nursing/admissions/).

tools.name: qu-get-cost-of-attendance
tools.description: Read Quinnipiac University's published tuition and cost of attendance live from the official costs-and-budgets pages. level selects the page: 'undergraduate' (default; full-time cost of attendance by student type such as first-year on campus or commuter, plus degree-completion and part-time rates), 'graduate' (tuition per credit by program, fees and possible expenses, grouped by school), 'law' or 'medicine'. By default it returns only the current academic year's tables (plus tables that state no year); pass year for another published year or 'all'. Optional filter keeps only tables whose title, tab or row labels contain that text (e.g. 'Nursing', 'Evening JD', 'Part-time'). Returns each cost table with its title, section, tab and academicYear, footnote-free row labels, column headers, rows (label plus one value per column), the table's footnotes, the other published years, the net price calculator link when present, and the source URL. Values are read at call time, never cached. Every returned link carries its host, plus external: true when it is not a Quinnipiac site (qu.edu or quinnipiac.edu). Works on any page of the site.

level.description: Which costs page to read. Default 'undergraduate'.

filter.description: Optional text to narrow tables, e.g. 'Nursing', 'Online', 'Part-time', 'Year 1'.

year.description: Academic year: 'current' (default; the year in progress, else the latest published), a year like '2025-2026', or 'all'.

tools.name: qu-find-events
tools.description: Find upcoming events on Quinnipiac University's official events calendar (calendar.qu.edu): open houses, information sessions, admissions events, lectures, arts, athletics and campus events. Optional query (free text, e.g. 'open house', 'nursing information session'), group (calendar group name, e.g. 'Undergraduate Admissions', 'School of Nursing'), from and to (YYYY-MM-DD; default from today) and limit. Returns each event's title, start and end date/time, all-day and online flags, location, calendar group, event page URL and registration link when the event has one, with events whose title matches the query listed first. Registration happens on the linked page; give the student the link. Every returned link carries its host, plus external: true when it is not a Quinnipiac site (qu.edu or quinnipiac.edu). Works on any page of the site.

group.description: Calendar group name, e.g. 'Undergraduate Admissions', 'School of Nursing'.

from.description: Earliest date, YYYY-MM-DD. Default today.

to.description: Latest date, YYYY-MM-DD.

limit.description: Maximum events to return (default 20, max 50).

tools.name: qu-list-visit-options
tools.description: List the ways a prospective student can visit or meet Quinnipiac University, each with its official registration link: upcoming open house dates, virtual and on-campus information sessions, campus tours, interviews, transfer visits and group visits. Use it for 'register me for an open house', 'book a campus tour' or 'when is the next nursing information session'. audience: 'undergraduate' (default, first-year), 'transfer', 'graduate', 'law' or 'all'; optional keyword narrows information sessions by title (e.g. 'nursing', 'MBA'). Returns openHouses and infoSessions (title, date/time, location or online flag, registrationUrl, eventUrl), visitTypes (tours, interviews, transfer and group visits with their scheduling links) and the visit planning pages. Registration happens on Quinnipiac's admissions portal, where the student reviews the form, confirms and submits it: give the student the registrationUrl and do not claim they are registered. Every returned link carries its host, plus external: true when it is not a Quinnipiac site (qu.edu or quinnipiac.edu). Works on any page of the site.

keyword.description: Optional keyword to narrow information sessions by title, e.g. 'nursing', 'physical therapy', 'MBA'.

tools.name: qu-get-request-info-link
tools.description: Get the official Quinnipiac University request-for-information form link for a prospective student, read live from the site's Request Information page. level: 'undergraduate' (first-year), 'transfer', 'degree-completion' (online bachelor's completion), 'graduate', 'law' or 'medicine'; omit it to get all of them. Returns the matching form name and URL (plus the full list). The form is hosted on Quinnipiac's admissions portal, where the student fills it in, confirms and submits it: give the student the link and do not claim the request was sent. Every returned link carries its host, plus external: true when it is not a Quinnipiac site (qu.edu or quinnipiac.edu). Works on any page of the site.

level.description: Which request-for-information form. Omit to list all.

tools.name: qu-get-apply-links
tools.description: Get the official links a student uses to apply to Quinnipiac University, read live from the matching admissions page. studentType: 'first-year' (default), 'transfer', 'international', 'graduate', 'law' or 'medicine'. Returns each option with its role ('application', 'status', 'prerequisite' such as the LSAC Credential Assembly Service, or 'credential evaluation' for third-party transcript evaluators), label, URL, host and an external flag for non-Quinnipiac sites (for example the Common App, the Coalition App, the Quinnipiac App and the application status check), plus the admissions page it came from. Applications are completed and submitted by the student on the linked application portal: give the student the link. Pair it with qu-get-admission-deadlines for dates. Every returned link carries its host, plus external: true when it is not a Quinnipiac site (qu.edu or quinnipiac.edu). Works on any page of the site.

tools.name: qu-get-contact-info
tools.description: Get official office-level contact details for Quinnipiac University from the site's Contact Us directory: admissions (undergraduate, graduate and online, law, medicine), financial aid (same four), and student support offices (registrar, residential life, accessibility, health services, public safety and more). Pass office (e.g. 'undergraduate admissions', 'graduate financial aid', 'registrar', 'nursing'); omit it to list every office. Returns each matching office's name, category, email, phone numbers, office web page and office/mailing address. If no office matches, returns the list of available offices plus related site pages from search. Use qu-list-visit-options to schedule a meeting with an admissions counselor. Every returned link carries its host, plus external: true when it is not a Quinnipiac site (qu.edu or quinnipiac.edu). Works on any page of the site.

office.description: Office or department, e.g. 'undergraduate admissions', 'financial aid', 'graduate admissions', 'registrar', 'law admissions'.

tools.name: qu-submit-contact-form
tools.description: Send a real message to a Quinnipiac University office through the 'Send a Message' form on the site's Contact Us page (/contact-us/), after the student approves it on the page. Before calling, summarize the name, email, office and message for the student and get a clear yes. The tool fills the form, then shows a confirmation bar at the bottom of the page with exactly what will be sent and to which office; nothing is sent until the student clicks Send there. Cancel or no answer within 5 minutes sends nothing. subject picks the office: Prospective Undergraduate Student (admissions@qu.edu), Prospective Graduate Student (graduate@qu.edu), Prospective Law Student (law@qu.edu), Prospective Medical Student (medicine@qu.edu), Current Student (onestop@quinnipiac.edu) or Alumni (alumni@qu.edu). For admissions inquiries where the student wants to be added to admissions communications, prefer qu-get-request-info-link instead. Returns status submitted with the site's confirmation text, cancelled, timeout, or error with the site's message. Never call it again to retry a send. If the browser is not on /contact-us/ it returns an error telling you to navigate there first.

email.description: The student's email address, for the office's reply.

subject.description: Who the student is; this picks the receiving office (see the tool description).

message.description: The message text, in the student's words.

tools.name: add_item_to_cart
tools.description:
[Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] 
Add one or more items to the shopping cart.

If no cart exists, this tool makes a new cart. This tool adds products and gift
certificates.

Steps

1. Call the 'search_products' tool to find a product.
2. Call the 'get_product_details' tool to get the variants and the modifier options.
3. Call this tool to add the item.
4. Call the 'create_checkout_url' tool to get a checkout URL.

Rules

Send 'quantity' and 'productEntityId' for each item.
If the product has variants, send 'variantEntityId'.

Modifier options

A modifier option is a product choice that is not a variant.
Examples are an engraving message and a nicotine strength.
The 'get_product_details' tool returns these options in 'modifierOptions'.

If the product has no 'modifierOptions', do not send 'selectedOptions'.
Do not send a variant option in 'selectedOptions'.
Send a variant in 'variantEntityId'.

An option is required if 'isRequired' is 'true'.
Send each required option.
If you do not send a required option, the server does not add the item.

To send an option:
1. Read the bucket name from 'selectedOptionsKey'.
2. Add the option to 'item.selectedOptions' in that bucket.
3. Send the 'optionEntityId' of the option.
4. For a choice option, send the 'valueEntityId' of the value that the user selected.

Send only the buckets that you need.

Example. A required choice option has a 'selectedOptionsKey' of "multipleChoices", an
'optionEntityId' of 108, and a selected value with a 'valueEntityId' of 251:
{
      "item": {
        "quantity": 1,
        "productEntityId": 88,
        "variantEntityId": 67,
        "selectedOptions": {
          "multipleChoices": [ { "optionEntityId": 108, "optionValueEntityId": 251 } ]
        }
      }
    }

A free-entry bucket takes a typed value in place of an ID.
'textFields' and 'multiLineTextFields' take "text".
'numberFields' takes "number".
'dateFields' takes "date".
Obey the 'constraints' of the option.

If a required option has more than one value, ask the user to select one value.
Do not select a value yourself. Do not use the default value.

If 'unsupported' is 'true', you cannot send the option.
If such an option is also required, tell the user to buy the product on the website.

tools.name: create_checkout_url
tools.description:
[Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] 
CreateResult a checkout URL for a cart assigned to a current session

Arguments:
None, but requires a cart to be present in the current session.

Returns:
- checkoutURL - the URL to redirect the user to for checkout
- errors - any errors encountered during the process (like, cart not found, etc.)

Flow:
- Call 'manage_cart' with 'create_cart' operation to create a new cart.
- Call this tool to create a checkout URL for the cart assigned to the current session.

tools.name: get_product_details
tools.description:
[Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] 
Get the details of one or more products. The details are the variants, the options, and
the images.

Arguments

productIds - The list of product IDs. Get these IDs from the 'search_products' tool.
  Request only the products that the user needs.
  The server has a maximum count of IDs. The default maximum is 20.
  If you send too many IDs, the server returns an error. Then send fewer IDs.
option_values - The option IDs and the value IDs of one variant.
  Use this argument with one product ID only. This argument applies to the B2C catalog.
  For a B2B buyer, the tool returns all the variants. Then select one variant.
channelId - Optional. This argument selects the B2B catalog.
  The default is the channel of the request.
variantCursor - Optional. This argument gets the next page of variants.
  Use this argument with one product ID only.
  Take the value from 'nextVariantCursor' in the previous result.
  If 'nextVariantCursor' is absent, or is null, or is the text "null", do not send this
  argument.

Results

The tool returns a list of products in 'products'. The output schema gives all the
fields.
A product has 'modifierOptions' only if the product has modifier options.
A variant has a price, an inventory level, a purchase flag, and bulk prices only for a
B2B buyer.
If the tool does not find a product, the list does not include that product.

Modifier options

A modifier option is a product choice that is not a variant.
Examples are an engraving message and a gift note.
A variant option is never a modifier option.
