tools.name: get_viewing_categories
tools.description: Returns, for each requested dimension, the IDs of the categories currently visible in the table. If a dimension has no explicit selection, all its categories are visible and all its IDs are returned, so no interpretation is needed. Returns IDs only (no labels or selection status). Use it to quickly check whether a category is already in the table view before calling 'select_categories_batch'. Unknown dimension IDs are omitted from the result. If 'dimensionIds' is omitted, all dimensions are returned.

dimensionIds.description: Optional array of dimension IDs to query (e.g. ['TEMPS', 'SEXE']).

tools.name: select_categories_batch
tools.description: Select or toggle categories across several dimensions in one call. Prefer this tool when the data to select is available in the table. 'mode' controls how the listed categories change the selection (see 'mode'). Returns the resulting state of each listed category in 'updatedStates' and any failures in 'errors'.

selections.description: Map of dimension IDs to array of category IDs (e.g. {'TEMPS': ['2023', '2024']}).

mode.description: Default 'replace'. 'replace': the selection of each listed dimension becomes exactly the listed categories; the rest of its categories are unselected. 'toggle': flips the selection state of each listed category (selected becomes unselected and vice versa); unlisted categories keep their state.

dataMode.description: Default 'table'. 'table' uses the categories active in the table. 'metadata' uses the complete dataset categories; in that case call 'confirm_dataset_filters' afterwards. Do NOT call 'confirm_dataset_filters' when using 'table'.

tools.name: get_dimensions
tools.description: Returns a complete list of all available dataset dimensions including their unique IDs and descriptive names.

tools.name: get_categories_by_dimensions
tools.description: Returns categories and selection status for multiple dimensions. Protocol: Call this first to check if the target categories exist in the current view. If the desired category is present in the returned list, do NOT proceed with `switch_dataset_view_mode` directly. IMPORTANT: If 'selected' is 0, it means ALL categories are active. DO NOT use `select_categories_batch` to select all if 'selected' is 0.

dimensionIds.description: Optional array of dimension IDs to filter (e.g. ['TEMPS', 'SEXE']). If omitted or empty, returns all dataset dimensions.

source.description: Source data structure. Use 'dataset' for DATASET.ds or 'metadata' for ESTAT.data.meta.

tools.name: toggle_all_categories_batch
tools.description: Selects or deselects all categories simultaneously for multiple dimensions.Note: If a dimension ends up with 0 elements selected, all elements will be shown on the table with no filtering.

toggles.description: Map of dimension IDs to selection state. Key: dimension ID (e.g., 'TEMPS', 'SEXE'). Value: true to select all categories, false to deselect all.

tools.name: configure_dimension_display_labels_batch
tools.description: Configures category display representations (showing codes, names/labels, or both) for multiple dimensions in batch.

showCodes.description: True to display category ID codes.

showNames.description: True to display category descriptive names/labels.

tools.name: move_dimension_position_batch
tools.description: Shifts the relative structural position (ordering) of multiple dimensions in a single request using direction steps: 'up_left' (shifts dimension towards top/left) or 'down_right' (shifts dimension towards bottom/right).

direction.description: Direction to move dimension position.

tools.name: download_dataset
tools.description: Triggers file download (excel, json, csv) with configuration. EXPLICIT ONLY when user explicitly asks for a file download. Otherwise NEVER use this tool.

format.description: Target file export format.

dataset.description: Export current filtered view ('taula') or entire dataset ('tot'). Default: 'taula'.

extension.description: File extension for excel export. Default: '.xlsx'.

structure.description: Structure format for JSON export. Default: 'jsonStat'.

decimal.description: Decimal point separator for CSV export.

tags.description: Category representation mode in export.

enrich.description: Enrich export with additional metadata attributes.

transposedBy.description: Dimension ID to pivot/transpose data by.

tools.name: toggle_view_options
tools.description: Enables or disables visual table display options: 'percent' (calculates and displays percentage values), 'estat' (shows or hides data quality/status flags in cells), or 'nodata' (hides empty table rows with no data values). Requires being in table data view.

option.description: Display option to toggle: 'percent' (percentage calculation), 'estat' (status flags), or 'nodata' (suppress empty rows).

active.description: Desired state: true to enable the option, false to disable it.

tools.name: change_dimensions_axis_batch
tools.description: Reorganizes table structure by moving specified dimensions between rows and columns in batch.

axes.description: Map of dimension IDs to target axis assignment. Key: dimension ID (e.g., 'SEXE', 'EDAT', 'TEMPS'). Value: 'row' (move to rows) or 'column' (move to columns).

tools.name: change_dimensions_order_batch
tools.description: Changes the internal sorting direction (ascending/descending) for categories within multiple dimensions in a single request. Primary use is reversing or setting temporal/ordinal dimension directions.

orders.description: Map of dimension IDs to target sort directions. Key: dimension ID (e.g., 'TEMPS', 'EDAT'). Value: 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending).

tools.name: set_last_periods_batch
tools.description: Enables, disables, or changes the 'last N periods' dynamic filter for time dimensions. Accepts a batch array with one entry per dimension. Returns { success, results }, with one result per entry; 'success' is true if at least one entry succeeded. An entry with active=true requires 'amount'; if it is missing or not one of the values offered by the page, that entry returns an error and is not applied.

periods.description: Array of period configurations per time dimension.

active.description: Set true to activate the 'last N periods' filter, false to disable it.

amount.description: Number N of recent periods to select (e.g. 5 for the last 5 periods). Required when 'active' is true: if omitted, that entry returns an error and is not applied. Must be one of the values offered by the page's selector. Ignored when 'active' is false.

tools.name: sort_table_by_column
tools.description: Sorts dataset rows by a specific column in ascending, descending, or original order. MUST call 'get_sortable_data_by_column' first to resolve 'columnIndex'. Fails if table has multiple row dimensions or if row dimension is temporal.

columnIndex.description: Zero-based index of the sortable column, obtained from 'get_sortable_data_by_column'.

tools.name: get_sortable_data_by_column
tools.description: Retrieves metadata (index, HTML id, headers, period/year) for all sortable table columns. MUST be called prior to 'sort_table_by_column' to resolve the required zero-based columnIndex.

tools.name: filter_geographic_dimension
tools.description: Filters the visible categories of the geographic dimension of the current dataset by a text query. If the dataset's geographic dimension is municipalities (MUN), the query is a comarca or province name and only the municipalities belonging to it are shown. Otherwise, the query is a name from the comarca/province list and only the matching categories are shown. Only changes visibility: it does NOT select any category (use 'select_categories_batch' for that). Returns { success, filteredCategories } with the IDs of the visible matching categories. An empty query clears the filter; an empty list for a non-empty query means no matches.

query.description: Name of the comarca or province used to filter the categories (e.g. 'Barcelonès', 'Barcelona'). Pass an empty string to clear the filter.

tools.name: get_available_divisions
tools.description: Lists the alternative divisions the current dataset can be switched to: territorial divisions (e.g. municipalities, comarques) and time series. Call it BEFORE 'switch_division' whenever you want to change the territorial or temporal division, and choose one of the returned items. Each item has a unique 'code', a 'label' and a 'type' ('territorial' or 'temporal'). Only available in table view. Returns { success, divisions } or { success: false, error }.

tools.name: switch_division
tools.description: Switches the current dataset to another territorial division or time series. First call 'get_available_divisions' and choose one of the returned items; do not guess the value. The switch replaces the current dataset context. Returns { success, message } or { success: false, error }.

code.description: Technical identifier code key matching a valid related link (e.g., 'mun', 'com' or specific series code).

tools.name: switch_dataset_view_mode
tools.description: Switches between the table view and the dataset ('metadata') view, where the complete set of categories can be selected. Use it ONLY as a last resort, when the target categories are not available in the current table view. Protocol: 1. Call 'get_categories_by_dimensions' to check whether the target categories are already available in the table. 2. If they are, use 'select_categories_batch' in table view and do NOT call this tool. 3. If they are not, call this tool with mode='metadata'. 4. Select the categories in metadata view using 'select_categories_batch' with dataMode='metadata'. 5. Call 'confirm_dataset_filters' to apply the changes and return to table view. Calling this tool with mode='table' only returns to table view; to apply the changes use 'confirm_dataset_filters'. Returns { success: true, message } or { error } (for example, if metadata view is unavailable because all the data is already visible in the table).

mode.description: Target view mode.

tools.name: confirm_dataset_filters
tools.description: Applies the filters selected in dataset ('metadata') view, fetches the filtered data and returns to table view. Only available in metadata view, after a successful 'switch_dataset_view_mode' with mode='metadata'; in table view it returns an error. Call it once the category selection is finished. If the selection exceeds the maximum number of observations it returns an error and nothing is applied: reduce the selected categories (you can verify with 'check_obs') and call it again. Returns { success: true, message } or { error }.

tools.name: check_obs
tools.description: Checks whether the current selection stays within the maximum number of observations allowed for dataset download. Only available in dataset ('metadata') view; in table view it returns an error. Call it before 'confirm_dataset_filters'. Returns { success: true, message } if the selection is within the limit. Returns { error } if the selection exceeds the limit (the message states the maximum): in that case, reduce the selected categories and call it again.

tools.name: search_tables
tools.description: Search the available result tables of this statistic by keywords in the table title or in the titles of the folders that contain it. Table titles are often short (e.g. 'Per sexe'), so the returned path provides the folder context. Use open_table with a returned id to open a table.

limit.description: Maximum number of results

tools.name: list_tables
tools.description: List the direct children (folders and tables) of a node of the tables tree of this statistic. Call without node to get the top-level folders, then drill down with the returned folder ids. Use open_table with a table id to open it.

node.description: Folder id to list. Omit for the top level.

tools.name: open_table
tools.description: Open a result table of this statistic in the table viewer. Once opened, the table viewer page exposes its own WebMCP tools to query the table data. Use search_tables or list_tables to find a valid table id.

id.description: Table id as returned by search_tables or list_tables

tools.name: add_item_to_cart
tools.description:
[Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] 
Add one or more items to the shopping cart.

If no cart exists, this tool makes a new cart. This tool adds products and gift
certificates.

Steps

1. Call the 'search_products' tool to find a product.
2. Call the 'get_product_details' tool to get the variants and the modifier options.
3. Call this tool to add the item.
4. Call the 'create_checkout_url' tool to get a checkout URL.

Rules

Send 'quantity' and 'productEntityId' for each item.
If the product has variants, send 'variantEntityId'.

Modifier options

A modifier option is a product choice that is not a variant.
Examples are an engraving message and a nicotine strength.
The 'get_product_details' tool returns these options in 'modifierOptions'.

If the product has no 'modifierOptions', do not send 'selectedOptions'.
Do not send a variant option in 'selectedOptions'.
Send a variant in 'variantEntityId'.

An option is required if 'isRequired' is 'true'.
Send each required option.
If you do not send a required option, the server does not add the item.

To send an option:
1. Read the bucket name from 'selectedOptionsKey'.
2. Add the option to 'item.selectedOptions' in that bucket.
3. Send the 'optionEntityId' of the option.
4. For a choice option, send the 'valueEntityId' of the value that the user selected.

Send only the buckets that you need.

Example. A required choice option has a 'selectedOptionsKey' of "multipleChoices", an
'optionEntityId' of 108, and a selected value with a 'valueEntityId' of 251:
{
      "item": {
        "quantity": 1,
        "productEntityId": 88,
        "variantEntityId": 67,
        "selectedOptions": {
          "multipleChoices": [ { "optionEntityId": 108, "optionValueEntityId": 251 } ]
        }
      }
    }

A free-entry bucket takes a typed value in place of an ID.
'textFields' and 'multiLineTextFields' take "text".
'numberFields' takes "number".
'dateFields' takes "date".
Obey the 'constraints' of the option.

If a required option has more than one value, ask the user to select one value.
Do not select a value yourself. Do not use the default value.

If 'unsupported' is 'true', you cannot send the option.
If such an option is also required, tell the user to buy the product on the website.

tools.name: create_checkout_url
tools.description:
[Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] 
CreateResult a checkout URL for a cart assigned to a current session

Arguments:
None, but requires a cart to be present in the current session.

Returns:
- checkoutURL - the URL to redirect the user to for checkout
- errors - any errors encountered during the process (like, cart not found, etc.)

Flow:
- Call 'manage_cart' with 'create_cart' operation to create a new cart.
- Call this tool to create a checkout URL for the cart assigned to the current session.

tools.name: get_product_details
tools.description:
[Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] 
Get the details of one or more products. The details are the variants, the options, and
the images.

Arguments

productIds - The list of product IDs. Get these IDs from the 'search_products' tool.
  Request only the products that the user needs.
  The server has a maximum count of IDs. The default maximum is 20.
  If you send too many IDs, the server returns an error. Then send fewer IDs.
option_values - The option IDs and the value IDs of one variant.
  Use this argument with one product ID only. This argument applies to the B2C catalog.
  For a B2B buyer, the tool returns all the variants. Then select one variant.
channelId - Optional. This argument selects the B2B catalog.
  The default is the channel of the request.
variantCursor - Optional. This argument gets the next page of variants.
  Use this argument with one product ID only.
  Take the value from 'nextVariantCursor' in the previous result.
  If 'nextVariantCursor' is absent, or is null, or is the text "null", do not send this
  argument.

Results

The tool returns a list of products in 'products'. The output schema gives all the
fields.
A product has 'modifierOptions' only if the product has modifier options.
A variant has a price, an inventory level, a purchase flag, and bulk prices only for a
B2B buyer.
If the tool does not find a product, the list does not include that product.

Modifier options

A modifier option is a product choice that is not a variant.
Examples are an engraving message and a gift note.
A variant option is never a modifier option.

If a product has no 'modifierOptions', add the product to the cart without
'selectedOptions'.

An option is required if 'isRequired' is 'true'.
Send each required option to the 'add_item_to_cart' tool.
If you do not send a required option, the server does not add the item.
A variant selection does not replace a required option.

Each option has 'optionEntityId', 'displayName', and 'selectedOptionsKey'.
'selectedOptionsKey' is the name of the field to send the option in.
A choice option has 'values'. Each value has 'valueEntityId' and 'label'.
A free-entry option has 'constraints' in place of 'values'.

If 'unsupported' is 'true', you cannot send the option. A file upload is one example.
If such an option is also required, tell the user to buy the product on the website.

Variant pages

The list of variants can be one page of a longer list. The server sets the page size.

If 'hasMoreVariants' is 'true', more variants exist than the tool returned.
Then do not tell the user that a variant does not exist. You did not receive all the
variants.

To get the next page, call this tool again. Send the same product ID, and only that
product ID. Send 'variantCursor' with the value of 'nextVariantCursor'.

A filter is better than a page walk. If the user named the variant, send 'option_values'
instead. One filtered call is cheaper than many pages.

Do not change 'option_values' between pages. The cursor is a position in the list of the
previous call. A different filter gives the wrong variants.

Stock

Each product has 'inStock'. It tells you if the store has units in stock.
It does not tell you if the user can buy the product.

If 'inStock' is 'false', do not refuse the request.
Many stores accept orders for products that are not in stock.
Tell the user that the product is not in stock, and that delivery can take more time.
Then add the product if the user agrees.
If the store blocks the purchase, the 'add_item_to_cart' tool fails and gives a reason.
Give that reason to the user.

If 'inStock' is 'true', the store reports no out-of-stock condition.
A store that does not count stock reports 'true' for all products.
Therefore do not tell the user a quantity.

'inventoryLevel' is present only if the store publishes stock counts.
If 'inventoryLevel' is absent, the count is unknown. The count is not zero.

Each variant has its own 'inStock'. Use the value of the variant if you add one variant.

Steps

1. Call the 'search_products' tool to get the product IDs.
2. Call this tool with the product IDs.
3. Call the 'add_item_to_ca

tools.name: search_products
tools.description:
[Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] 
Search products by a term

Arguments:
term - the search term to look for products. It should be at least 3 characters long.
cursor - optional, used for pagination. If provided, it will return the next page of results after.

Pagination:
Supports pagination with 'cursor' arguments. If 'cursor' is not provided, it will return the first page of results.
Value for 'cursor' can be obtained from the 'nextCursor' field in the response. If 'nextCursor' is null, it means there are no more results to fetch.
If value of cursor is null (or a string representation of 'null') dont send it in the payload.

Results:
Each product includes 'requiresFileUpload'. When true, the product has a required file-upload
option (e.g. "upload your design") and shouldn't be added to cart through this assistant. Do not
attempt to purchase it — tell the user it must be ordered on the website.

Stock:
Each product carries 'inStock'. It reports whether the store has units on hand. It does NOT
report whether the item can be bought.
- false does NOT mean the purchase will fail. Many stores accept orders for out-of-stock
  items - backorder, pre-order, or made-to-order goods that are fabricated after ordering.
  Whether a given store does is not exposed by this API.
  So: tell the user the item is out of stock and may take longer to arrive, then ADD IT if
  they still want it. Do not refuse on 'inStock: false' alone.
- If the store really does block it, 'add_item_to_cart' fails and returns the reason. Relay
  that reason to the user. Attempting the add is the only reliable way to find out.
- true only means no out-of-stock condition is reported. A store that does not track inventory
  reports true for every product, so never state or imply a quantity.
- 'inventoryLevel' appears only on stores that publish stock figures; absent means undisclosed,
  not zero.

Flow:
- Call this tool with a 'term' argument and optionally with 'cursor' to search for products.
	- if you find a matching product, call 'get_product_details' with the product ID to get its
	  variants and options (if any).
	- if 'requiresFileUpload' is true, inform the user the product needs a file upload and cannot
	  be purchased here.
- Call 'add_item_to_cart' with results of 'search_products' and 'get_product_details' (variant) tools to add the product to the cart.
    - [IMPORTANT] If product has variants ask user to pick

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description:
[Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] 
Change an item that is already in the shopping cart.

Use this tool to change the quantity, the variant, or the modifier options of one cart
item. A cart must exist and must have items.

Steps

1. Call the 'add_item_to_cart' tool to put an item in the cart.
2. Call this tool to change the item.
3. Call the 'create_checkout_url' tool to get a checkout URL.

Send 'line_item_id' to select the cart item to change.
Send 'quantity' and 'productEntityId' in 'item'.
If the product has variants, send 'variantEntityId'.

'item.selectedOptions' works as it works in the 'add_item_to_cart' tool.
The 'get_product_details' tool returns these options in 'modifierOptions'.

If the product has required modifier options, send them again in this request.
If you do not send them, the server does not change the item.
Send only the buckets that you need.

tools.description: Search FreeTaxUSA's own pages by topic, for example "1099-NEC", "Oregon", "extension" or "military", and return up to 8 matching pages with their titles, descriptions, paths and links. Open one in this tab with open_page. Help articles are searched separately, with the help search tool.

query.description: A topic, form, state or situation, for example "self-employed" or "Form 1099-K".

tools.name: open_page
tools.description: Open another FreeTaxUSA page in this tab by its path, for example "/pricing" or "/states/oregon", and return a description of the new page, as get_current_page does. Use a path from find_page or from a link on this page. Only pages on this site open; sign-in and start-return buttons have their own tools.

path.description: A path on this site starting with "/", for example "/pricing" or "/survey?name=feedback".

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Current FreeTaxUSA prices for the 2025 tax year, in US dollars, as the pricing page shows them. Federal returns are $0. The state return, Deluxe, Pro Support, Audit Defense, amended, printed, bound and prior-year prices are listed separately, plus the fee for paying out of a federal refund.

tools.name: get_key_dates
tools.description: The IRS dates on FreeTaxUSA's deadline page for the 2025 tax year: when the IRS starts processing returns, the April filing deadline, and the extension deadline, plus today's date and whether each deadline has passed. irsStartsProcessing is null until the IRS announces it. Dates are US local dates in YYYY-MM-DD form.

tools.name: search_faqs
tools.description: Search FreeTaxUSA's tax help library and return up to 5 matching articles with their ids, titles and links. Use it for questions about tax forms, credits, deductions, filing situations, and how the software handles them. Titles are not answers: read the article with get_faq before giving tax guidance. An empty results list means no article matched.

query.description: A plain-language tax question, for example "Can I deduct student loan interest?"

tools.name: get_faq
tools.description: Read up to 5 articles from FreeTaxUSA's tax help library in full, by id. Returns each article's title, its text with the formatting removed, and its link. Get ids from search_faqs or from get_current_page. An id that does not exist is left out of the results.

ids.description: Help article ids from a search result's id or from get_current_page, for example [1605].

tools.name: get_entry_links
tools.description: Returns links, without opening them: startNewReturn for a new 2025 return, signInToContinue for a return already started, priorYearReturn to start a return for taxYear (default 2024), and accountRecovery for a lost username or password. Each opens the sign-in site, where the person signs in or creates an account themselves.

taxYear.description: A prior tax year for priorYearReturn, 2018 to 2024. Defaults to 2024.

tools.name: get_state_info
tools.description: Whether FreeTaxUSA can prepare and e-file a state's 2025 return yet, as its state e-file availability page shows. For one state: whether it has a state return, its price (null when there is no return) and its page. With no state: compact lists of abbreviations by readiness, including the states with no return.

state.description: A US state name or two-letter abbreviation, for example "California" or "CA". Omit to list every state.

tools.name: search_forms
tools.description: Check whether FreeTaxUSA supports a federal or state tax form, using the same lookup as its forms page. Search by form number ("1099-K", "Schedule E", "1040-NR") or a state name. supported and primaryMatch are the verdict for the form searched; relatedMatches are other forms with similar names, often from other jurisdictions, and are not the verdict.

query.description: A form number or name, or a state name, for example "1099-K", "Schedule C", or "Ohio".

tools.name: start_return
tools.description: Open FreeTaxUSA's sign-in site to start a tax return, in this tab. product picks the starting point: a new 2025 return, one with Deluxe, Pro Support or Audit Defense added, an extension, an amended return, a prior-year return, or a paid-preparer return. The person signs in or creates an account there themselves.

product.description: What to start. Use "new" for an ordinary current-year return.

year.description: Tax year, only for prior_year (default 2024) or amended (default 2025).

tools.name: sign_in
tools.description: Open FreeTaxUSA's sign-in site in this tab so the person can sign in and continue a 2025 return they already started. The password and any verification code go into that page directly, from the person, a password manager or a passkey, never through this conversation.

tools.name: recover_account
tools.description: Open FreeTaxUSA's account recovery page in this tab, for a person who forgot their username or password or can't sign in. The person answers the recovery questions there; recovery codes and the new password go into that page directly, never through this conversation.

tools.name: open_account_page
tools.description: Open a page inside the person's FreeTaxUSA account, in this tab, after they sign in: check their e-file status, contact customer support, print or download a return they filed, or refer a friend. The browser goes to the sign-in site first; the person signs in themselves.

page.description: Which account page to open after sign-in.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_get_view
tools.description: Read what the chart is currently showing: its kind and subject, the other kinds this subject has with their labels (and the reason any of them can't be switched to), every option's current value and default, which values can be selected right now (and why the rest can't), the viewer's entitlements, the shareable URL, and whether the view is saved to the account and has unsaved work. Call this first — it grounds every other tool. Availability is a snapshot of the settings as they stand: an interval listed as unsupported may become usable in the same breath as the time period that unblocks it, which configure accepts as one patch.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_get_stats
tools.description: Summary numbers for every series on the chart — high, low, average, first and last value, with the timestamps of the high and low. Prefer this over reading the whole series for questions like "what is this asset doing", and use it to anchor drawings: these coordinates are exact, where a downsampled series is not.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_get_series
tools.description: The chart's plotted data points as { time, value } pairs in data space — the same coordinates drawings use. Downsampled by default to protect your context; the response says how many points exist and whether it reduced them, and always carries the true high and low so anchoring stays exact. Widen the time period first if you need a range the chart isn't currently showing.

maxPoints.description: Maximum points to return per series (default 100, hard cap 500). Downsampling preserves extremes, and the true high and low are returned separately regardless.

series.description: Dataset keys to include. Omit for every series on the chart.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_get_viewport
tools.description: Read the time window currently on screen, the full range the loaded data covers, the value-axis bounds, and whether anyone has panned or zoomed away from the natural range. Worth calling before reading or drawing: the viewer may have zoomed, in which case get_series and get_stats describe more than they are actually looking at.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_list_drawings
tools.description: The shapes currently drawn on the chart, with their points in data space ({ time, value }) rather than pixels. Positions here are directly comparable with what get_series and get_stats return. Each shape also carries `onScreen`, which distinguishes a drawing that is missing from one that is merely outside the window the chart is zoomed to — use get_viewport or set_viewport to bring it back into view.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_list_history
tools.description: The chart's undo/redo stack, newest first, with a human-readable label for each step. `past` can be undone, `future` can be redone. The stack covers changes since the last navigation, not the whole session.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_list_charts
tools.description: List the charts this viewer has saved, newest first, with each one's uuid, name, kind and subject. No link is returned — pass the kind and subject to navigate to open one. Use it before saving to avoid duplicating a name, or to find a chart the viewer refers to by name.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_resolve_subject
tools.description: Turn a name, ticker or category into the identifier the other tools take — pass a match's `target` straight to coinranking_prochart_compare, or to coinranking_prochart_navigate's `base`. Call this first whenever the viewer names something in words: no other tool accepts a name, and a guessed identifier plots an unnamed line rather than failing. Matches are ranked, best first, and are not filtered by what this chart can plot — compare and navigate say why if a target doesn't apply here.

query.description: What to look up: a name ("Ethereum"), a ticker ("ETH"), a category ("DeFi"), a contract address, or an identifier you already hold and want the name for.

limit.description: How many matches to return per group, 1–10. Defaults to 5.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_configure
tools.description: Change one or more chart options — time period, interval, chart type, log scale, indicators, currency, volume, high/low markers. The whole patch applies as a single undoable step. Values that the viewer can't use are refused with a reason rather than partially applied; call get_view to see what's selectable and why. Options that constrain each other are judged as the combination you ask for, not one at a time: send timePeriod and interval together and a pair like 7d + 1day is accepted, even though get_view lists 1day as unavailable while the period is still 24h.

options.description: Option keys mapped to their new values. Call get_view first for the valid keys, each option's allowed values, and which are currently selectable. Everything in the patch is applied together as one undoable step, or nothing is.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_navigate
tools.description: Switch to a different chart kind for the current asset, or point the chart at a different asset, category or the global market. A kind switch happens immediately; a subject change returns a URL to open, because it needs a fresh page load. Drawings are discarded on a kind switch, so draw after navigating rather than before.

kind.description: The chart kind to switch to for the current subject — price, market-cap, ranking, and so on. Applied immediately. See get_view for what this chart's subject supports.

id.description: A coin uuid, "global" for the whole market, or "category:<slug>". Not a name — resolve_subject turns one into this.

slug.description: The coin's slug, when known. Optional.

base.description: A different subject to chart. Returns the destination URL rather than navigating — the caller has to open it.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_set_viewport
tools.description: Zoom or pan the chart to a time window, or reset it to fit all the loaded data. This moves the view only: it is not stored in the URL, so it can't be shared or bookmarked, it does not create an undo step, and the next configure or navigate call clears it — set the time period and options first, then the window. It also cannot show data outside what timePeriod loaded; widen that instead of zooming out past it.

action.description: `set` shows a specific window; `reset` clears any pan or zoom, including the viewer's own, and fits the chart back to its data.

fromTime.description: For `set`: the left edge, a millisecond timestamp on the same scale get_series and get_stats return.

toTime.description: For `set`: the right edge. Must be later than fromTime.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_history
tools.description: Step backwards or forwards through the chart's change history, or jump straight to an entry by index. This is the same stack the undo/redo buttons drive, and it covers changes since the last navigation rather than the whole session. Call list_history for the entries, their labels and their indices.

action.description: Which way to move through the chart's history.

index.description: Required for `jump`: the entry index from list_history. Ignored otherwise.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_compare
tools.description: Add or remove an overlay plotted alongside this chart — another coin, the global market, or a category. Takes an identifier, not a name: resolve_subject turns "Ethereum" into one. One target per call, each its own undoable step. Targets that can't be plotted here are refused with the reason: the wrong chart kind for that overlay, the chart itself, a duplicate, or the account's overlay limit.

action.description: Whether to start or stop comparing against the target.

target.description: What to compare against: a currency uuid, the literal `global` for the whole market, or `category:<slug>` (e.g. `category:defi`). A name or ticker won't resolve — put it through resolve_subject first and pass the `target` it returns. Call get_view to see what's already being compared.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_draw
tools.description: Draw a line, rectangle, circle, text label or pin on the chart, remove, duplicate or restack existing ones, or clear them all. A pin is a labelled guide line spanning the chart: `time-pin` marks a moment ("halving", "listed here"), `value-pin` marks a level ("entry", "all-time high"). Anchors are data coordinates (a timestamp and a value), not screen pixels — call get_stats for exact highs and lows to anchor against. Set the chart's kind and time range BEFORE drawing: switching kind discards most annotations, because a shape anchored to price data is meaningless on another scale. A time-pin is the exception and survives, since a date means the same thing on every kind.

action.description: Add one annotation, remove one or more by id, update one by id (move / restyle / retext), duplicate one or more, reorder one or more within the stack, group two or more so they select and move together, ungroup them again, or remove all.

points.description: For `add`, or `update` to move a shape: anchors in DATA coordinates — `time` is a timestamp (Unix ms) and `value` is on the chart's own y-scale, not pixels. A line takes 2 endpoints. A rectangle or circle takes 2 opposite corners, or 4 for an exact quad. A text annotation takes 1 anchor, which becomes the centre of a box sized to the text, or 4 to place the box yourself. A pin takes 1 anchor and reads only one of its coordinates — `time` for a time-pin, `value` for a value-pin — so send the one that matters and pass 0 for the other; whatever you send for the unused one is discarded, not stored. Get exact values from get_stats (true highs/lows) or get_series. Positions are absolute, not a delta — read the current ones from list_drawings.

text.description: The caption. Required for type `text` (an empty text box is discarded). Optional for a pin, which draws its guide line with or without one. Not accepted for a line, rectangle or circle. On `update`, replaces the existing caption.

style.description: For `add`: optional appearance, defaulting to the chart's own drawing style. For `update`: only the keys given change; the rest of the shape's style is kept.

fill.description: Body fill for rectangles and circles.

fontSize.description: Text annotations only — a pin's caption is drawn in the chart's own label style.

fontFamily.description: Text annotations only — a pin's caption is drawn in the chart's own label style.

id.description: For `remove`, `update`, `duplicate` and `reorder`: which annotation, by the `id` list_drawings reports. Stable for as long as the shape exists, so it doesn't shift when another shape is removed — unlike a position. Ids are per-session: they are not carried in a shared URL, so re-read them after a reload.

ids.description: For `remove`, `duplicate`, `reorder`, `group` and `ungroup`: several annotations at once, as one change — so one undo puts them all back. Every id must resolve; if one is stale nothing happens, rather than half of what you asked for. Use instead of `id`, not alongside it. `group` needs at least two here.

placement.description: For `reorder`: whether the named annotations move to the front of the stack (drawn over everything) or the back.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_export
tools.description: Export the chart's data as CSV or the chart itself as a PNG image. CSV can be returned directly in the result; saving a file or copying to the clipboard asks the user first, since browsers only allow those during a user gesture.

format.description: `csv` for the underlying data, `png` for a picture of the chart.

destination.description: Where the export goes. `return` (CSV only) hands the text back in this result. `download` saves a file and `clipboard` copies — both prompt the user, because the browser only permits them during a user gesture. Defaults to `return` for CSV and `download` for PNG.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_share_link
tools.description: Get a link that reproduces the chart exactly as it looks now — kind, asset, time range, styling and drawings all travel in the URL. Returns the link by default; set `share` to open the device's share sheet instead, which asks the user first.

share.description: Open the device's share sheet (or copy the link where there isn't one) instead of just returning the URL. Prompts the user, so only set this when they asked to share rather than to see the link.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_save
tools.description: Save the chart to the viewer's account, save a copy under a new name, rename it, delete it, or discard unsaved edits. Saving needs a name the first time. Deleting asks the viewer to confirm. Call get_view first if you need to know whether the chart is already saved.

action.description: `save` updates the current chart (or creates it, with a name). `save_as` always creates a new one. `rename` retitles it, `delete` removes it, `discard` reverts unsaved edits.

name.description: Required for `save_as` and `rename`, and for `save` when the chart has never been saved. Without it the site would open a naming dialog, which a tool call can't sensibly drive.

tools.description: Search across the documentation to find relevant information, code examples, API references, and guides. Use this tool when you need to answer questions about Unsloth Documentation, find specific documentation, understand how features work, or locate implementation details. The search returns contextual content with titles and direct links to the documentation pages.

tools.name: getPage
tools.description: Fetch the full markdown content of a specific documentation page from Unsloth Documentation. Use this when you have a page URL and want to read its content. Accepts full URLs (e.g. https://unsloth.ai/docs//getting-started). Since `searchDocumentation` returns partial content, use `getPage` to retrieve the complete page when you need more details. The content includes links you can follow to navigate to related pages.

url.description: The URL of the page to fetch

tools.name: sendFeedback
tools.description: Report an issue in the documentation of Unsloth Documentation so the team can fix it. Use it whenever, while helping a user, you come across content that is outdated, contradictory, missing information, or otherwise unhelpful. Also use it when the user themselves reports a problem with the docs, even if you could not verify it yourself. If it's your own observation, do a quick sanity check that the issue is real before reporting — no need to exhaustively re-read the page. Send one call per distinct issue and do not report the same issue twice in a conversation. Do not use this tool to confirm that a page is accurate; it is for reporting problems only.

content.description: Explain the issue in full, as if writing to a documentation maintainer who never saw this conversation. Describe what is wrong, where on the page it appears (quote the exact sentence or section title when possible), what the user was trying to do, and, when relevant, what the correct or expected information should be. Write a few clear, specific sentences in English. Never include personal or confidential information from the conversation. Up to 2048 characters.

pageUrl.description: The full URL of the page the issue is about (e.g. https://unsloth.ai/docs//getting-started), so the finding is linked to the exact page.

goal.description: The broader end goal you were ultimately trying to accomplish (as/on behalf of the user) when you hit this issue. Gives the team the context you were working towards. Optional.

tools.name: add_item_to_cart
tools.description:
[Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] 
Add one or more items to the shopping cart.

If no cart exists, this tool makes a new cart. This tool adds products and gift
certificates.

Steps

1. Call the 'search_products' tool to find a product.
2. Call the 'get_product_details' tool to get the variants and the modifier options.
3. Call this tool to add the item.
4. Call the 'create_checkout_url' tool to get a checkout URL.

Rules

Send 'quantity' and 'productEntityId' for each item.
If the product has variants, send 'variantEntityId'.

Modifier options

A modifier option is a product choice that is not a variant.
Examples are an engraving message and a nicotine strength.
The 'get_product_details' tool returns these options in 'modifierOptions'.

If the product has no 'modifierOptions', do not send 'selectedOptions'.
Do not send a variant option in 'selectedOptions'.
Send a variant in 'variantEntityId'.

An option is required if 'isRequired' is 'true'.
Send each required option.
If you do not send a required option, the server does not add the item.

To send an option:
1. Read the bucket name from 'selectedOptionsKey'.
2. Add the option to 'item.selectedOptions' in that bucket.
3. Send the 'optionEntityId' of the option.
4. For a choice option, send the 'valueEntityId' of the value that the user selected.

Send only the buckets that you need.

Example. A required choice option has a 'selectedOptionsKey' of "multipleChoices", an
'optionEntityId' of 108, and a selected value with a 'valueEntityId' of 251:
{
      "item": {
        "quantity": 1,
        "productEntityId": 88,
        "variantEntityId": 67,
        "selectedOptions": {
          "multipleChoices": [ { "optionEntityId": 108, "optionValueEntityId": 251 } ]
        }
      }
    }

A free-entry bucket takes a typed value in place of an ID.
'textFields' and 'multiLineTextFields' take "text".
'numberFields' takes "number".
'dateFields' takes "date".
Obey the 'constraints' of the option.

If a required option has more than one value, ask the user to select one value.
Do not select a value yourself. Do not use the default value.

If 'unsupported' is 'true', you cannot send the option.
If such an option is also required, tell the user to buy the product on the website.

tools.name: create_checkout_url
tools.description:
[Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] 
CreateResult a checkout URL for a cart assigned to a current session

Arguments:
None, but requires a cart to be present in the current session.

Returns:
- checkoutURL - the URL to redirect the user to for checkout
- errors - any errors encountered during the process (like, cart not found, etc.)

Flow:
- Call 'manage_cart' with 'create_cart' operation to create a new cart.
- Call this tool to create a checkout URL for the cart assigned to the current session.

tools.name: get_product_details
tools.description:
[Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] 
Get the details of one or more products. The details are the variants, the options, and
the images.

Arguments

productIds - The list of product IDs. Get these IDs from the 'search_products' tool.
  Request only the products that the user needs.
  The server has a maximum count of IDs. The default maximum is 20.
  If you send too many IDs, the server returns an error. Then send fewer IDs.
option_values - The option IDs and the value IDs of one variant.
  Use this argument with one product ID only. This argument applies to the B2C catalog.
  For a B2B buyer, the tool returns all the variants. Then select one variant.
channelId - Optional. This argument selects the B2B catalog.
  The default is the channel of the request.
variantCursor - Optional. This argument gets the next page of variants.
  Use this argument with one product ID only.
  Take the value from 'nextVariantCursor' in the previous result.
  If 'nextVariantCursor' is absent, or is null, or is the text "null", do not send this
  argument.

Results

The tool returns a list of products in 'products'. The output schema gives all the
fields.
A product has 'modifierOptions' only if the product has modifier options.
A variant has a price, an inventory level, a purchase flag, and bulk prices only for a
B2B buyer.
If the tool does not find a product, the list does not include that product.

Modifier options

A modifier option is a product choice that is not a variant.
Examples are an engraving message and a gift note.
A variant option is never a modifier option.

If a product has no 'modifierOptions', add the product to the cart without
'selectedOptions'.

An option is required if 'isRequired' is 'true'.
Send each required option to the 'add_item_to_cart' tool.
If you do not send a required option, the server does not add the item.
A variant selection does not replace a required option.

Each option has 'optionEntityId', 'displayName', and 'selectedOptionsKey'.
'selectedOptionsKey' is the name of the field to send the option in.
A choice option has 'values'. Each value has 'valueEntityId' and 'label'.
A free-entry option has 'constraints' in place of 'values'.

If 'unsupported' is 'true', you cannot send the option. A file upload is one example.
If such an option is also required, tell the user to buy the product on the website.

Variant pages

The list of variants can be one page of a longer list. The server sets the page size.

If 'hasMoreVariants' is 'true', more variants exist than the tool returned.
Then do not tell the user that a variant does not exist. You did not receive all the
variants.

To get the next page, call this tool again. Send the same product ID, and only that
product ID. Send 'variantCursor' with the value of 'nextVariantCursor'.

A filter is better than a page walk. If the user named the variant, send 'option_values'
instead. One filtered call is cheaper than many pages.

Do not change 'option_values' between pages. The cursor is a position in the list of the
previous call. A different filter gives the wrong variants.

Stock

Each product has 'inStock'. It tells you if the store has units in stock.
It does not tell you if the user can buy the product.

If 'inStock' is 'false', do not refuse the request.
Many stores accept orders for products that are not in stock.
Tell the user that the product is not in stock, and that delivery can take more time.
Then add the product if the user agrees.
If the store blocks the purchase, the 'add_item_to_cart' tool fails and gives a reason.
Give that reason to the user.

If 'inStock' is 'true', the store reports no out-of-stock condition.
A store that does not count stock reports 'true' for all products.
Therefore do not tell the user a quantity.

'inventoryLevel' is present only if the store publishes stock counts.
If 'inventoryLevel' is absent, the count is unknown. The count is not zero.

Each variant has its own 'inStock'. Use the value of the variant if you add one variant.

1. Call the 'search_products' tool to get the product IDs.
2. Call this tool with the product IDs.
3. Call the 'add_item_to_ca

tools.name: remove_item_from_cart
tools.description:
[Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] 
Remove specific items from your shopping cart.
It is removing the item completly from the cart.
If you want to reduce quantity of the items use 'update_cart_item'

Remove unwanted items from your shopping cart by targeting specific item IDs. This tool provides precise control over cart cleanup and item removal.

Use this tool when customers want to:
-Remove specific products they no longer want
-Delete gift certificates from their cart
-Clean up their cart before checkout
-Remove items added by mistake

Features:
- Target removal by specific item ID
- Works with both products and gift certificates
- Maintains cart structure after removal
- Immediate cart updates

Flow:
- Call 'search_products' tool to find products by search term.
- Call 'get_product_details' tool to get product variants and images.
- Call 'add_item_to_cart' tool to create new cart with item
- Call 'add_item_to_cart' tool to add another item to cart
- Call 'remove_item_from_cart' tool to remove added item to cart
- Call 'create_checkout_url' tool to generate a checkout URL for the cart.

Requires an existing cart with items to remove.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description:
[Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] 
Search products by a term

Arguments:
term - the search term to look for products. It should be at least 3 characters long.
cursor - optional, used for pagination. If provided, it will return the next page of results after.

Pagination:
Supports pagination with 'cursor' arguments. If 'cursor' is not provided, it will return the first page of results.
Value for 'cursor' can be obtained from the 'nextCursor' field in the response. If 'nextCursor' is null, it means there are no more results to fetch.
If value of cursor is null (or a string representation of 'null') dont send it in the payload.

Results:
Each product includes 'requiresFileUpload'. When true, the product has a required file-upload
option (e.g. "upload your design") and shouldn't be added to cart through this assistant. Do not
attempt to purchase it — tell the user it must be ordered on the website.

Stock:
Each product carries 'inStock'. It reports whether the store has units on hand. It does NOT
report whether the item can be bought.
- false does NOT mean the purchase will fail. Many stores accept orders for out-of-stock
  items - backorder, pre-order, or made-to-order goods that are fabricated after ordering.
  Whether a given store does is not exposed by this API.
  So: tell the user the item is out of stock and may take longer to arrive, then ADD IT if
  they still want it. Do not refuse on 'inStock: false' alone.
- If the store really does block it, 'add_item_to_cart' fails and returns the reason. Relay
  that reason to the user. Attempting the add is the only reliable way to find out.
- true only means no out-of-stock condition is reported. A store that does not track inventory
  reports true for every product, so never state or imply a quantity.
- 'inventoryLevel' appears only on stores that publish stock figures; absent means undisclosed,
  not zero.

Flow:
- Call this tool with a 'term' argument and optionally with 'cursor' to search for products.
	- if you find a matching product, call 'get_product_details' with the product ID to get its
	  variants and options (if any).
	- if 'requiresFileUpload' is true, inform the user the product needs a file upload and cannot
	  be purchased here.
- Call 'add_item_to_cart' with results of 'search_products' and 'get_product_details' (variant) tools to add the product to the cart.
    - [IMPORTANT] If product has variants ask user to pick

context.description: Additional information about the request such as user demographics, mood, location, or other relevant details that could help in tailoring the response appropriately. Should not contains PII.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description:
[Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] 
Change an item that is already in the shopping cart.

Use this tool to change the quantity, the variant, or the modifier options of one cart
item. A cart must exist and must have items.

Steps

1. Call the 'add_item_to_cart' tool to put an item in the cart.
2. Call this tool to change the item.
3. Call the 'create_checkout_url' tool to get a checkout URL.

Rules

Send 'line_item_id' to select the cart item to change.
Send 'quantity' and 'productEntityId' in 'item'.
If the product has variants, send 'variantEntityId'.

Modifier options

'item.selectedOptions' works as it works in the 'add_item_to_cart' tool.
The 'get_product_details' tool returns these options in 'modifierOptions'.

If the product has required modifier options, send them again in this request.
If you do not send them, the server does not change the item.
Send only the buckets that you need.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search this store's catalogue by keyword. Returns name, price, stock and a link for each match. Use this FIRST whenever the shopper names something specific they want. It does not open anything or change the cart: call get_product for detail, add_to_cart to buy.

query.description: What to search for, in the shopper's own words

limit.description: Maximum results to return (default and maximum 20)

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse the store the way a shopper would. Called with no arguments it lists the categories the merchant features in the store navigation; called with a category permalink it lists that category's products, with name, price and a link. Stock is not included here - call get_product before adding anything from a category listing. Use it when the shopper is exploring rather than looking for something specific.

category.description: Category permalink from a previous browse_store call. Omit to list the categories.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get one product's details, OR open it in the browser. Returns description, price, stock, and for a product with variants every option and the values it accepts under "options" - not the combinations themselves; use show_variant for a specific one. Set navigate=true when the shopper wants to SEE the product ("show me", "open", "view", "take me to"). Leave it false, the default, when you need data to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart - the browser then stays where it is. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that.

product.description: The product's id or permalink, as returned by search_catalog or browse_store. A variant id is accepted too and answers about the product it belongs to.

navigate.description: Open the product page. Default false: the shopper stays where they are.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Show one specific variant of a product on the page, chosen by its option values, and report its price and stock. Opens the product page with that variant selected, so the shopper sees what is being discussed. Use it after get_product to resolve a combination.

product.description: The product's id or permalink. A variant id may be given instead, and then options can be left out: it already names one variant.

options.description: The values to show, as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Values come from get_product's "options"; matching ignores case, and a partial selection is fine: the first available variant matching it is shown.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read the shopper's current cart: line items, quantities, discounts, shipping and total. This is the same cart shown on screen, so read it before answering anything about what they are buying rather than relying on what was said earlier in the conversation.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a product to the shopper's cart, which updates on screen immediately. A variant id names what to add on its own; otherwise, for a product with variants, pass the option value ids from get_product's "options" - and if the shopper has not chosen yet, ask them, or call show_variant to show one first. Adding does not start checkout - use proceed_to_checkout when they are ready to pay.

product.description: What to add: a variant id, or a product's id or permalink from search_catalog, browse_store or get_product.

options.description: Variant selection as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Matching ignores case. Omit for products without variants, or when a variant id was given.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description: Change the quantity of a line already in the cart, or remove it by setting the quantity to 0. Use the cart_item_id from get_cart, not the product id.

tools.name: estimate_shipping
tools.description: What the store can ship to a destination and what it costs, for the cart as it stands. Ask for it when the shopper wants to know the delivery cost or time before they check out - it is the question that most often decides whether they finish. Needs a country and a region; a postal code makes the estimate exact where the store charges by it.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code, e.g. PT, CL, US

region.description: Region, state or province, as the store's checkout names it

postal.description: Postal or ZIP code, when known

municipality.description: Municipality, where the store uses one

tools.name: apply_coupon
tools.description: Apply a discount coupon code to the cart and report the resulting total.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empty the shopper's cart, removing every item and any coupon. ALWAYS confirm with the shopper first: this discards everything they chose and cannot be undone. To remove a single line use update_cart_item with qty 0 instead.

tools.name: get_recommended_products
tools.description: Products this store recommends alongside what is already in the cart. Use it to suggest genuinely related items before checkout.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Open checkout so the shopper can review and pay. Use it when they say they are done. You CANNOT place the order or enter payment details, and no tool here can: the shopper completes the purchase themselves. Once this returns, stop - do not navigate again and do not tell them the order was placed.

tools.name: add_item_to_cart
tools.description:
[Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] 
Add one or more items to the shopping cart.

If no cart exists, this tool makes a new cart. This tool adds products and gift
certificates.

Steps

1. Call the 'search_products' tool to find a product.
2. Call the 'get_product_details' tool to get the variants and the modifier options.
3. Call this tool to add the item.
4. Call the 'create_checkout_url' tool to get a checkout URL.

Rules

Send 'quantity' and 'productEntityId' for each item.
If the product has variants, send 'variantEntityId'.

Modifier options

A modifier option is a product choice that is not a variant.
Examples are an engraving message and a nicotine strength.
The 'get_product_details' tool returns these options in 'modifierOptions'.

If the product has no 'modifierOptions', do not send 'selectedOptions'.
Do not send a variant option in 'selectedOptions'.
Send a variant in 'variantEntityId'.

An option is required if 'isRequired' is 'true'.
Send each required option.
If you do not send a required option, the server does not add the item.

To send an option:
1. Read the bucket name from 'selectedOptionsKey'.
2. Add the option to 'item.selectedOptions' in that bucket.
3. Send the 'optionEntityId' of the option.
4. For a choice option, send the 'valueEntityId' of the value that the user selected.

Send only the buckets that you need.

Example. A required choice option has a 'selectedOptionsKey' of "multipleChoices", an
'optionEntityId' of 108, and a selected value with a 'valueEntityId' of 251:
{
      "item": {
        "quantity": 1,
        "productEntityId": 88,
        "variantEntityId": 67,
        "selectedOptions": {
          "multipleChoices": [ { "optionEntityId": 108, "optionValueEntityId": 251 } ]
        }
      }
    }

A free-entry bucket takes a typed value in place of an ID.
'textFields' and 'multiLineTextFields' take "text".
'numberFields' takes "number".
'dateFields' takes "date".
Obey the 'constraints' of the option.

If a required option has more than one value, ask the user to select one value.
Do not select a value yourself. Do not use the default value.

If 'unsupported' is 'true', you cannot send the option.
If such an option is also required, tell the user to buy the product on the website.

- Call this tool to create a checkout URL for the cart assigned to the current session.

tools.name: get_product_details
tools.description:
[Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] 
Get the details of one or more products. The details are the variants, the options, and
the images.

Arguments

productIds - The list of product IDs. Get these IDs from the 'search_products' tool.
  Request only the products that the user needs.
  The server has a maximum count of IDs. The default maximum is 20.
  If you send too many IDs, the server returns an error. Then send fewer IDs.
option_values - The option IDs and the value IDs of one variant.
  Use this argument with one product ID only. This argument applies to the B2C catalog.
  For a B2B buyer, the tool returns all the variants. Then select one variant.
channelId - Optional. This argument selects the B2B catalog.
  The default is the channel of the request.
variantCursor - Optional. This argument gets the next page of variants.
  Use this argument with one product ID only.
  Take the value from 'nextVariantCursor' in the previous result.
  If 'nextVariantCursor' is absent, or is null, or is the text "null", do not send this
  argument.

Results

The tool returns a list of products in 'products'. The output schema gives all the
fields.
A product has 'modifierOptions' only if the product has modifier options.
A variant has a price, an inventory level, a purchase flag, and bulk prices only for a
B2B buyer.
If the tool does not find a product, the list does not include that product.

Modifier options

A modifier option is a product choice that is not a variant.
Examples are an engraving message and a gift note.
A variant option is never a modifier option.

If a product has no 'modifierOptions', add the product to the cart without
'selectedOptions'.

An option is required if 'isRequired' is 'true'.
Send each required option to the 'add_item_to_cart' tool.
If you do not send a required option, the server does not add the item.
A variant selection does not replace a required option.

Each option has 'optionEntityId', 'displayName', and 'selectedOptionsKey'.
'selectedOptionsKey' is the name of the field to send the option in.
A choice option has 'values'. Each value has 'valueEntityId' and 'label'.
A free-entry option has 'constraints' in place of 'values'.

If 'unsupported' is 'true', you cannot send the option. A file upload is one example.
If such an option is also required, tell the user to buy the product on the website.

Variant pages

The list of variants can be one page of a longer list. The server sets the page size.

If 'hasMoreVariants' is 'true', more variants exist than the tool returned.
Then do not tell the user that a variant does not exist. You did not receive all the
variants.

To get the next page, call this tool again. Send the same product ID, and only that
product ID. Send 'variantCursor' with the value of 'nextVariantCursor'.

A filter is better than a page walk. If the user named the variant, send 'option_values'
instead. One filtered call is cheaper than many pages.

Do not change 'option_values' between pages. The cursor is a position in the list of the
previous call. A different filter gives the wrong variants.

Stock

Each product has 'inStock'. It tells you if the store has units in stock.
It does not tell you if the user can buy the product.

If 'inStock' is 'false', do not refuse the request.
Many stores accept orders for products that are not in stock.
Tell the user that the product is not in stock, and that delivery can take more time.
Then add the product if the user agrees.
If the store blocks the purchase, the 'add_item_to_cart' tool fails and gives a reason.
Give that reason to the user.

If 'inStock' is 'true', the store reports no out-of-stock condition.
A store that does not count stock reports 'true' for all products.
Therefore do not tell the user a quantity.

'inventoryLevel' is present only if the store publishes stock counts.
If 'inventoryLevel' is absent, the count is unknown. The count is not zero.

Each variant has its own 'inStock'. Use the value of the variant if you add one variant.

2. Call this tool with the product IDs.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description:
[Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] 
Search products by a term

Arguments:
term - the search term to look for products. It should be at least 3 characters long.
cursor - optional, used for pagination. If provided, it will return the next page of results after.

Pagination:
Supports pagination with 'cursor' arguments. If 'cursor' is not provided, it will return the first page of results.
Value for 'cursor' can be obtained from the 'nextCursor' field in the response. If 'nextCursor' is null, it means there are no more results to fetch.
If value of cursor is null (or a string representation of 'null') dont send it in the payload.

Results:
Each product includes 'requiresFileUpload'. When true, the product has a required file-upload
option (e.g. "upload your design") and shouldn't be added to cart through this assistant. Do not
attempt to purchase it — tell the user it must be ordered on the website.

Stock:
Each product carries 'inStock'. It reports whether the store has units on hand. It does NOT
report whether the item can be bought.
- false does NOT mean the purchase will fail. Many stores accept orders for out-of-stock
  items - backorder, pre-order, or made-to-order goods that are fabricated after ordering.
  Whether a given store does is not exposed by this API.
  So: tell the user the item is out of stock and may take longer to arrive, then ADD IT if
  they still want it. Do not refuse on 'inStock: false' alone.
- If the store really does block it, 'add_item_to_cart' fails and returns the reason. Relay
  that reason to the user. Attempting the add is the only reliable way to find out.
- true only means no out-of-stock condition is reported. A store that does not track inventory
  reports true for every product, so never state or imply a quantity.
- 'inventoryLevel' appears only on stores that publish stock figures; absent means undisclosed,
  not zero.

Flow:
- Call this tool with a 'term' argument and optionally with 'cursor' to search for products.
	- if you find a matching product, call 'get_product_details' with the product ID to get its
	  variants and options (if any).
	- if 'requiresFileUpload' is true, inform the user the product needs a file upload and cannot
	  be purchased here.
- Call 'add_item_to_cart' with results of 'search_products' and 'get_product_details' (variant) tools to add the product to the cart.
    - [IMPORTANT] If product has variants ask user to pick

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search this store's catalogue by keyword. Returns name, price, stock and a link for each match. Use this FIRST whenever the shopper names something specific they want. It does not open anything or change the cart: call get_product for detail, add_to_cart to buy.

query.description: What to search for, in the shopper's own words

limit.description: Maximum results to return (default and maximum 20)

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse the store the way a shopper would. Called with no arguments it lists the categories the merchant features in the store navigation; called with a category permalink it lists that category's products, with name, price and a link. Stock is not included here - call get_product before adding anything from a category listing. Use it when the shopper is exploring rather than looking for something specific.

category.description: Category permalink from a previous browse_store call. Omit to list the categories.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get one product's details, OR open it in the browser. Returns description, price, stock, and for a product with variants every option and the values it accepts under "options" - not the combinations themselves; use show_variant for a specific one. Set navigate=true when the shopper wants to SEE the product ("show me", "open", "view", "take me to"). Leave it false, the default, when you need data to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart - the browser then stays where it is. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that.

product.description: The product's id or permalink, as returned by search_catalog or browse_store. A variant id is accepted too and answers about the product it belongs to.

navigate.description: Open the product page. Default false: the shopper stays where they are.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Show one specific variant of a product on the page, chosen by its option values, and report its price and stock. Opens the product page with that variant selected, so the shopper sees what is being discussed. Use it after get_product to resolve a combination.

product.description: The product's id or permalink. A variant id may be given instead, and then options can be left out: it already names one variant.

options.description: The values to show, as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Values come from get_product's "options"; matching ignores case, and a partial selection is fine: the first available variant matching it is shown.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read the shopper's current cart: line items, quantities, discounts, shipping and total. This is the same cart shown on screen, so read it before answering anything about what they are buying rather than relying on what was said earlier in the conversation.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a product to the shopper's cart, which updates on screen immediately. A variant id names what to add on its own; otherwise, for a product with variants, pass the option value ids from get_product's "options" - and if the shopper has not chosen yet, ask them, or call show_variant to show one first. Adding does not start checkout - use proceed_to_checkout when they are ready to pay.

product.description: What to add: a variant id, or a product's id or permalink from search_catalog, browse_store or get_product.

options.description: Variant selection as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Matching ignores case. Omit for products without variants, or when a variant id was given.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description: Change the quantity of a line already in the cart, or remove it by setting the quantity to 0. Use the cart_item_id from get_cart, not the product id.

tools.name: estimate_shipping
tools.description: What the store can ship to a destination and what it costs, for the cart as it stands. Ask for it when the shopper wants to know the delivery cost or time before they check out - it is the question that most often decides whether they finish. Needs a country and a region; a postal code makes the estimate exact where the store charges by it.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code, e.g. PT, CL, US

region.description: Region, state or province, as the store's checkout names it

postal.description: Postal or ZIP code, when known

municipality.description: Municipality, where the store uses one

tools.name: apply_coupon
tools.description: Apply a discount coupon code to the cart and report the resulting total.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empty the shopper's cart, removing every item and any coupon. ALWAYS confirm with the shopper first: this discards everything they chose and cannot be undone. To remove a single line use update_cart_item with qty 0 instead.

tools.name: get_recommended_products
tools.description: Products this store recommends alongside what is already in the cart. Use it to suggest genuinely related items before checkout.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Open checkout so the shopper can review and pay. Use it when they say they are done. You CANNOT place the order or enter payment details, and no tool here can: the shopper completes the purchase themselves. Once this returns, stop - do not navigate again and do not tell them the order was placed.

client.description: The user's AI client.

tools.name: get_benchmark

tools.name: get_company_overview

tools.name: get_graph8_products
tools.description: The graph8 product catalog: agents, sequencer, dialer, CRM, data, signals, studio, integrations, and more. Without a product argument returns the full list; with one returns that product's summary and page. Call this for any what-does-graph8-have or product-detail question.

product.description: Optional product slug for detail.

tools.name: list_graph8_mcp_capabilities
tools.description: What an AI connected to the graph8 MCP server can do: the tool categories, scale, auth model, and example prompts. Call this to understand or explain graph8's capabilities.

tools.name: run_assessment

market.description: Who you sell to and why now. Grade 1-4.

signal.description: Reading the buying signals that say an account is ready. Grade 1-4.

message.description: Saying something the buyer finds worth a reply. Grade 1-4.

motion.description: Running the sequence and follow-up with discipline. Grade 1-4.

mastery.description: Rep skill and AI judgment that make the motion work. Grade 1-4.

measurement.description: The numbers that prove the system works and where it leaks. Grade 1-4.

Pass the user's email ONLY when they explicitly asked to subscribe or confirmed it; unsubscribing is one click in any issue. Submits through the site's own signup form, the same path a person typing takes.

email.description: The email address the user explicitly gave for the subscription.
