tools.name: get-app-guide
tools.description: Reads the app's own reference guide: what each tool, dialog and map layer does, and how to build a link that opens the map in a given state (viewport, layers, markers, drawn geometry, a planned route). Call it without a section for the summary and the list of sections, then again with the one you need.

section.description: Heading of the section to read, as listed without one.

tools.name: get-map-view
tools.description: Returns what the map currently shows: its centre, zoom, visible bounding box, the layers that are on, and the shareable URL of this exact state.

tools.name: set-map-view
tools.description: Moves the map. Give a centre, a zoom (0 = whole world, 19 = a building), or both.

tools.name: fit-map-to-area
tools.description: Zooms the map so that the given bounding box fits the screen — the way to show a whole region, town or route extent.

tools.name: list-map-layers
tools.description: Lists the map layers this app offers, with the one-letter code each is switched on by. A "base" layer is the map itself (only one at a time); an "overlay" is drawn on top of it (any number). premiumFromZoom marks a layer that needs a paid account past that zoom.

tools.name: set-map-layers
tools.description: Switches map layers on and off by their code (see list-map-layers). Naming overlays replaces the set that is on; leaving them out keeps it.

base.description: Code of the base map to show.

overlays.description: Codes of the overlays to leave on; [] takes them all off.

tools.name: search-places
tools.description: Searches for a place by name, category, OSM element id (e.g. "way/123"), coordinates, a bounding box or pasted GeoJSON, and fills the app's result list. Results are ranked around the current map view. Show one on the map with show-search-result.

tools.name: show-search-result
tools.description: Draws one result of the last search-places on the map and moves the map to it.

index.description: The result's index as search-places returned it.

tools.name: clear-search-results
tools.description: Takes the searched places off the map and empties the list.

tools.name: list-object-categories
tools.description: Finds the POI categories the objects tool can show — search them by name in the UI language ("water", "shelter", "castle"). Each row carries the filter that show-objects takes.

search.description: Part of a category name; omitted lists the first ones.

tools.name: show-objects
tools.description: Shows POIs of the given categories (filters from list-object-categories) within the current map view, and returns what was found. The map has to be at zoom 8 or closer, and a wide view finds a lot — zoom in on what is being asked about first.

categories.description: Filters as list-object-categories gives them.

tools.name: describe-place
tools.description: Says what is at a point on the map: the nearest addressable place, the OSM elements right there, and the areas containing it. Shows them on the map as it does.

tools.name: plan-route
tools.description: Plans a route through the given waypoints and draws it on the map, opening the route finder. Returns its length and estimated time. "trip" mode reorders the waypoints into the shortest round of them all; "route" keeps the given order.

transportType.description: How the route is travelled; defaults to what the app is set to (initially hiking).

tools.name: get-route-itinerary
tools.description: Returns the turn-by-turn steps of the route currently planned, with the distance and time of each. Distances are in metres, times in seconds.

tools.name: add-marker
tools.description: Puts a labelled marker on the map. The icon is `poi:<name>` for a bundled map icon (e.g. `poi:peak`) or `fa:<name>` for a Font Awesome one; anything else shows as its first two characters.

tools.name: draw-line
tools.description: Draws a line through the given points. Use draw-area for a filled shape.

tools.name: draw-area
tools.description: Draws a filled area through the given points. The ring is closed on its own — do not repeat the first point.

tools.name: list-drawings
tools.description: Lists what is drawn on the map, with the index each one is removed by.

tools.name: remove-drawing
tools.description: Removes one drawn marker, line or area by its index from list-drawings. Removing shifts the indexes of what comes after it, so list them again between removals.

tools.name: open-drawing-tool
tools.description: Opens a drawing toolbar so the user can carry on by hand — clicking points onto the map, restyling or labelling what is drawn.

tools.name: get-elevation
tools.description: Reads the height above sea level of the given points from the terrain model, in metres. A point the model has no data for comes back as null.

tools.name: get-route-elevation
tools.description: Climb, drop and the highest and lowest point of the route currently planned, in metres.

tools.name: get-map-features
tools.description: Returns everything the user has on the map — drawings, the planned route, searched places, shown objects, imported tracks — as one GeoJSON FeatureCollection.

deliver.description: `download` writes the answer to a JSON file instead of returning it — for a result too big to carry back through the agent's own channel.

tools.name: download-map-features
tools.description: Saves what is on the map to a file in the user's downloads, as GPX, GeoJSON or KML.

elevation.description: Fill elevation from the terrain model into what is written; `missing` only where there is none.

tools.name: sample-elevation-grid
tools.description: Reads the terrain model over a rectangle on a regular grid — one call instead of one per point. Elevations come back row-major from the north-west corner (row 0 is the northern edge), in metres, `null` where the model has no data. Ask for derivatives to get slope in degrees and aspect as degrees clockwise from north pointing downhill, computed from each cell's neighbours.

spacing.description: Distance between grid points, in metres.

derivatives.description: Also return slope and aspect per cell.

deliver.description: `download` writes the answer to a JSON file instead of returning it — for a result too big to carry back through the agent's own channel.

tools.name: find-objects-in-area
tools.description: Finds POIs of the given categories (from list-object-categories) inside a bounding box, wherever it is — unlike show-objects, which is bound to what the map shows and draws what it finds. This one only reports back; it leaves the map alone.

limit.description: How many objects to return at most; 200 by default.

deliver.description: `download` writes the answer to a JSON file instead of returning it — for a result too big to carry back through the agent's own channel.

tools.name: get-app-state
tools.description: Returns what the app is doing right now: the open tools and dialog, the selected feature, the UI language and who is signed in.

tools.name: open-tool
tools.description: Opens one of the app's tools — its toolbar, and whatever it takes over map clicks for.

tools.name: close-tool
tools.description: Closes one open tool.

tools.name: open-dialog
tools.description: Opens one of the app's dialogs, for the user to carry on in themselves — signing in, exporting, buying credits, configuring the map. Call get-app-guide for what each one does.

tools.name: clear-map
tools.description: Takes everything the user put on the map off it — searched places, the planned route, drawings, imported tracks.

tools.name: search_books
tools.description: Search Digitalbook's own catalogue of free audiobooks and ebooks by keyword, title or author. Returns the matches plus a link to the full results page, which also merges partner titles (Amazon, Apple, Google, Open Library) for the reader’s market — those are not in this tool’s reply.

format.description: Defaults to audiobook.

field.description: Which field to match. Defaults to keywords.

tools.name: list_shelf
tools.description: List the books on one of the reader's Digitalbook shelves. `liked` are books they saved, `started` books they have started listening to or reading, `purchased` books they have bought, and `viewed` the books viewed on this device — that last one is browser state rather than account state, so it works signed out and does not follow the reader to another device. The other three need a sign-in.

tools.name: add_favorite
tools.description: Save a book to the signed-in reader's Digitalbook liked shelf. Takes the id reported by search_books.

tools.name: remove_favorite
tools.description: Take a book off the signed-in reader's Digitalbook liked shelf. Takes the id reported by search_books or list_shelf.

tools.name: open_sample
tools.description: Open a book's free sample on the reader's own screen — the clip player for an audiobook, the EPUB reader for an ebook. This is the one thing only the page can do, and it changes what the reader is looking at, so call it when they asked to hear or see a book rather than to find out about one. Takes the id reported by search_books or list_shelf.

tools.name: close_sample
tools.description: Close whatever `open_sample` opened — the audiobook clip player or the ebook reader. Reports that nothing was open rather than failing.

tools.name: get_playback
tools.description: Report the audiobook open on the page: its chapters, which one the player is on, whether it is playing, and how far in. Call this before play_chapter or seek_playback — it is where the chapter numbers those take come from. Reports that no audiobook is open rather than failing.

tools.name: play_chapter
tools.description: Start the audiobook on the page playing. `chapter` is the number get_playback lists, counting from 1; leave it out to resume the chapter the player is already on. `at` starts that many seconds in. This plays out loud on the reader's own device, so call it when they asked to listen, not to find something out.

chapter.description: Chapter number from get_playback, counting from 1.

at.description: Seconds from the start of the chapter. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: pause_playback
tools.description: Pause the audiobook playing on the page. The position is kept, so play_chapter with no arguments picks it up again.

tools.name: seek_playback
tools.description: Move the playhead within the chapter the audiobook is on. `to` is seconds from the start of that chapter — get_playback reports where it is now, so skipping forward is that plus however far. Use play_chapter to move to a different chapter.

to.description: Seconds from the start of the current chapter.

tools.name: set_market
tools.description: Change which market the reader is browsing (an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code). This is reader state rather than a search argument: the Digitalbook catalogue is not market-segmented, but the partner results merged into the search page, the store their Amazon links point at, and the homepage they are served all follow it. Changing it changes what the reader sees, so only call it when they asked.

market.description: One of: AU, CA, FR, DE, GB, IN, IT, ES, US.

tools.name: searchDocumentation
tools.description: Search across the documentation to find relevant information, code examples, API references, and guides. Use this tool when you need to answer questions about i18next documentation, find specific documentation, understand how features work, or locate implementation details. The search returns contextual content with titles and direct links to the documentation pages.

tools.name: getPage
tools.description: Fetch the full markdown content of a specific documentation page from i18next documentation. Use this when you have a page URL and want to read its content. Accepts full URLs (e.g. https://www.i18next.com//getting-started). Since `searchDocumentation` returns partial content, use `getPage` to retrieve the complete page when you need more details. The content includes links you can follow to navigate to related pages.

url.description: The URL of the page to fetch

tools.name: sendFeedback
tools.description: Report an issue in the documentation of i18next documentation so the team can fix it. Use it whenever, while helping a user, you come across content that is outdated, contradictory, missing information, or otherwise unhelpful. Also use it when the user themselves reports a problem with the docs, even if you could not verify it yourself. If it's your own observation, do a quick sanity check that the issue is real before reporting — no need to exhaustively re-read the page. Send one call per distinct issue and do not report the same issue twice in a conversation. Do not use this tool to confirm that a page is accurate; it is for reporting problems only.

content.description: Explain the issue in full, as if writing to a documentation maintainer who never saw this conversation. Describe what is wrong, where on the page it appears (quote the exact sentence or section title when possible), what the user was trying to do, and, when relevant, what the correct or expected information should be. Write a few clear, specific sentences in English. Never include personal or confidential information from the conversation. Up to 2048 characters.

pageUrl.description: The full URL of the page the issue is about (e.g. https://www.i18next.com//getting-started), so the finding is linked to the exact page.

goal.description: The broader end goal you were ultimately trying to accomplish (as/on behalf of the user) when you hit this issue. Gives the team the context you were working towards. Optional.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Product detail parameters.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

value.description: Option value, e.g. "160cm" or "Fiberglass".

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant. To change a quantity or remove something already in the cart, use update_cart_lines instead — this tool can only add.

line_items.description: Items to add (1-10).

item.description: The merchandise to add.

id.description: ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

handle.description: Product handle. Adds the selected or first available variant; call get_product first if the user requested specific options.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: How many to add. Defaults to 1.

tools.name: update_cart_lines
tools.description: Change the quantity of items already in the cart, or remove them. Every change here addresses an existing cart line by its id, so call get_cart first unless you already have line_items[].id from an earlier get_cart in this conversation. Pass the ABSOLUTE target quantity, not a delta — quantity 2 means the line ends up at 2 regardless of what it was. Use quantity 0 to remove the line entirely. Batch every change for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart_lines once per line. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. This tool cannot add new merchandise. To add something not already in the cart, use add_to_cart. To empty the whole cart at once, use cancel_cart.

line_items.description: Existing cart lines to update or remove (1-10).

id.description: Existing cart line id from get_cart line_items[].id. Required — this tool cannot resolve products by name.

quantity.description: Absolute target quantity for this line (not a delta). 0 removes the line.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Remove all items from the cart in one step. Use when the user wants to empty their cart or start over.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Proceed to checkout. Verifies the cart is not empty, then MOVES the browser to the checkout page. The tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: manage_orders
tools.description: Navigate to the customer's order history page. Use when the user asks about past orders, order status, tracking, or returns. The user will be prompted to log in if not already authenticated. This MOVES the browser to the order history page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: search_shop_policies_and_faqs
tools.description:
Used to get facts about the store's policies, FAQ, or contact details.
When the question is about specific policy kinds, set policy_types to those kinds; leave it unset for general FAQ questions.
Some examples of questions you can ask are:
  - What is your return policy? (policy_types: ["refund"])
  - What is your shipping policy? (policy_types: ["shipping"])
  - What is your phone number? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - What are your hours of operation? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - Do you offer gift wrapping? (general FAQ, no specific policy kind — leave policy_types unset)

query.description: A natural language query. Searches FAQ pages and articles, and routes policies by keyword when policy_types is omitted.

policy_types.description: Policy kinds to fetch, chosen from the user's question — e.g. ["refund"] for returns/exchanges, ["contact"] for phone/hours/address. Include every kind the question touches. Omit when no specific policy is relevant (e.g. a general FAQ question).

tools.name: ippodo_recommend_tea
tools.description: Use when a shopper wants Ippodo tea recommendations based on taste, caffeine, brewing style, experience, gift intent, time of day, or tea category rather than a product name. Ranks the live tea-quiz assortment of matcha, gyokuro, sencha, bancha, and teabags, returning in-stock products with match reasons and the cheapest available variant. Prefer this over search_catalog for preference-based discovery such as a first latte, caffeine-free evening tea, or first-time matcha. After the shopper chooses a tea, call get_product for variants, ippodo_get_brewing_guide for preparation, or ippodo_build_tea_setup for utensils, then Shopify update_cart to add items. Leaves the cart unchanged.

category.description: Tea family to keep in the result set. Use "matcha", "gyokuro", "sencha", "bancha", or "teabags" when the shopper named a category. Use "any" when they did not. Matched against product handle, title, and type — not tags or description boilerplate.

occasion.description: When the shopper plans to drink the tea. Evening and after_meal boost lower-caffeine and roasted options; morning and daytime prefer brighter or standard-caffeine teas.

format.description: How the shopper wants to prepare tea. "matcha" keeps powdered teas, "loose_leaf" keeps leaf teas, "teabags" keeps bagged teas, and "any" does not filter by format.

flavor.description: Dominant flavor the shopper asked for. "umami" and "balanced" favor classic matcha and gyokuro; "roasted" and "smoky" favor hojicha and similar; "any" skips flavor ranking.

caffeine.description: Caffeine preference. "none" returns only caffeine-free teas such as mugicha; "low" boosts hojicha, genmaicha, and mugicha; "standard" keeps typical green-tea caffeine; "any" does not filter.

preparation.description: Brewing or serving style. "latte" boosts Ikuyo and similar culinary matcha; "koicha" boosts thicker usucha/koicha grades; "usucha" favors everyday whisking matcha; "cold_brew" and "iced" favor teas that drink well chilled.

experience.description: Shopper familiarity. "first_time" boosts approachable daily teas such as Sayaka and Ikuyo; "experienced" leaves room for richer grades such as Ummon.

gift.description: Set true when the purchase is a gift. Boosts giftable cans, classic matcha, and the Ippodo gift card.

limit.description: Maximum number of teas to return. Defaults to 3. Use 5 only when the shopper wants a wider shortlist.

tools.name: ippodo_get_brewing_guide
tools.description: Use when a shopper asks how to prepare, brew, whisk, steep, or care for a specific Ippodo product they already named. Returns the published recipe quantities and step-by-step directions for that product handle. Optional method filters recipes such as usucha, koicha, latte, hot, iced, or cold brew. Servings is context only — published quantities are never scaled or invented. Prefer this over get_product when the question is preparation rather than price or variants. Leaves the cart unchanged.

productHandle.description: Shopify product handle from the Ippodo product URL path after /products/. Examples: "sayaka-no-mukashi", "ikuyo-100", "gokujo-hojicha". Lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens only.

method.description: Optional preparation filter matched against recipe title, type, and excerpt. Examples: "usucha", "koicha", "latte", "hot", "iced", "cold brew". Omit to return every published recipe for the product.

servings.description: Requested serving count for conversation context only. The tool still returns published recipe quantities unchanged and sets quantitiesScaled to false.

tools.name: ippodo_build_tea_setup
tools.description: Use when a shopper wants a complete Ippodo tea-and-utensil kit around one named product, such as matcha with a whisk and bowl or hojicha with a kyusu. Builds from live complementary products and cheaper utensil extras, keeping matcha utensils with matcha and leaf-tea utensils with leaf teas. Optional budget is in the live catalog currency. Returns Shopify variant IDs in cartHandoff.suggestedItems for a later Shopify update_cart add after shopper review. Prefer this over repeating get_product when the shopper wants a setup, not a single item. Leaves the cart unchanged.

productHandle.description: Handle of the tea or utensil to build around, from the product URL path after /products/. Examples: "sayaka-no-mukashi" for matcha or "gokujo-hojicha" for roasted leaf tea.

budget.description: Optional maximum total in the live product currency for the tea plus utensils. Items without a known price are not budget-filtered. Omit when the shopper did not name a budget.

tools.name: ippodo_compare_teas
tools.description: Use when a shopper wants a side-by-side comparison of two to four Ippodo products they already named. Looks up each product handle and returns live price, availability, flavor, quiz guidance, variants, and subscription plans in the requested order. Prefer this over repeating get_product when comparing named teas. For an open-ended "what should I drink" request, use ippodo_recommend_tea instead. Leaves the cart unchanged.

productHandles.description: Two to four unique Ippodo product handles to compare, in the order the shopper named them. Example: ["sayaka-no-mukashi", "ummon-no-mukashi"].

items.description: One product handle from a /products/ URL, e.g. "sayaka-no-mukashi" or "ikuyo-100".

tools.name: ippodo_get_subscription_options
tools.description: Use when a shopper asks whether an Ippodo product can ship on a subscription, which delivery frequencies exist, or which variants are eligible. Returns live selling-plan groups and in-stock variants without starting a subscription. After the shopper chooses a plan, call Shopify update_cart with the merchandise ID and selling-plan identifier from this result. Prefer this over get_product when the question is specifically about subscribe-and-save. Leaves the cart unchanged.

productHandle.description: Shopify product handle from the Ippodo product URL path after /products/. Examples: "sayaka-no-mukashi", "ikuyo-100", "gokujo-hojicha". Lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens only.

tools.name: ippodo_find_store
tools.description: Use when a shopper asks for official Ippodo Tea shop locations, addresses, published hours, or closure status. Covers Kyoto Main Store, Tokyo Aoyama, Tokyo Shin Marunouchi, and New York. Prefer this over search_shop_policies_and_faqs for physical stores; use that policy tool for shipping, returns, and contact email. Filter by city or country when the shopper named one. Hours can change on holidays, so confirm with the location before visiting. Leaves the page unchanged.

city.description: Optional city name filter, matched as a case-insensitive substring. Examples: "Kyoto", "Tokyo", "New York". Omit to include every city.

country.description: Optional country name filter, matched as a case-insensitive substring. Examples: "Japan", "United States". Omit to include every country.

includeClosed.description: When true (default), include temporarily closed locations such as New York. When false, return only currently open shops.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an update_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Product detail parameters.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

value.description: Option value, e.g. "160cm" or "Fiberglass".

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart, update line item quantities, or remove items. Batch EVERY change for one request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart once per item. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use line_items[].id from get_cart to update or remove an existing line, passing the ABSOLUTE target quantity (not a delta; quantity 0 removes the line). Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant.

line_items.description: Items to add or update (1-10).

id.description: Existing cart line id from get_cart. Use to update or remove an existing line. Omit when adding new items.

item.description: The merchandise to add.

id.description: ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

handle.description: Product handle. Adds the selected or first available variant; call get_product first if the user requested specific options.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: Quantity. Defaults to 1 for adds and updates. Set to 0 with an existing line id to remove it.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Remove all items from the cart in one step. Use when the user wants to empty their cart or start over.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Proceed to checkout. Verifies the cart is not empty, then MOVES the browser to the checkout page. The tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: manage_orders
tools.description: Navigate to the customer's order history page. Use when the user asks about past orders, order status, tracking, or returns. The user will be prompted to log in if not already authenticated. This MOVES the browser to the order history page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: search_shop_policies_and_faqs
tools.description:
Used to get facts about the store's policies, FAQ, or contact details.
When the question is about specific policy kinds, set policy_types to those kinds; leave it unset for general FAQ questions.
Some examples of questions you can ask are:
  - What is your return policy? (policy_types: ["refund"])
  - What is your shipping policy? (policy_types: ["shipping"])
  - What is your phone number? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - What are your hours of operation? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - Do you offer gift wrapping? (general FAQ, no specific policy kind — leave policy_types unset)

query.description: A natural language query. Searches FAQ pages and articles, and routes policies by keyword when policy_types is omitted.

policy_types.description: Policy kinds to fetch, chosen from the user's question — e.g. ["refund"] for returns/exchanges, ["contact"] for phone/hours/address. Include every kind the question touches. Omit when no specific policy is relevant (e.g. a general FAQ question).

tools.name: search_listings
tools.description: Trả về dữ liệu tin bán/cho thuê đã xác thực trên MOSO: giá, diện tích, phòng ngủ, khu vực, link. Dùng tool này thay vì mở trang khi cần đọc/so sánh/tính toán. Returns structured listing data (price, area, bedrooms, address, url) — read this instead of scraping HTML.

query.description: Đặc điểm bất động sản, KHÔNG phải khu vực (VD: "nhà hẻm xe hơi", "sổ hồng riêng"). Tên tỉnh/quận/phường phải đặt vào tham số location — để ở đây sẽ khớp nhầm sang khu vực trùng chữ.

location.description: Tên tỉnh/quận/phường, nhiều giá trị cách nhau bằng dấu phẩy (VD: "Bình Thạnh" hoặc "Quận 7,Nhà Bè"). Khớp chính xác theo cấp hành chính, không nhầm sang khu vực trùng chữ. Ghi đủ tên — "Bình Thạnh" đúng, "1" thì mơ hồ giữa Quận 1 và Phường 1. Khớp cả tên trước và sau sáp nhập 2025, nên "Hồ Chí Minh" bao gồm cả Bình Dương và Bà Rịa – Vũng Tàu cũ; trường address của kết quả có thể vẫn ghi tên tỉnh cũ.

minPrice.description: Giá tối thiểu, VND (rent: giá thuê/tháng)

maxPrice.description: Giá tối đa, VND (rent: giá thuê/tháng)

minArea.description: Diện tích sử dụng tối thiểu, m² (khớp trường usableArea)

maxArea.description: Diện tích sử dụng tối đa, m² (khớp trường usableArea)

limit.description: Số kết quả (tối đa 20)

offset.description: Bỏ qua N kết quả đầu (phân trang)

format.description: markdown = bảng gọn cho LLM; json = dữ liệu có cấu trúc

tools.name: compare_listings
tools.description: So sánh 2–5 tin trên MOSO theo cùng một bộ tiêu chí: giá, giá/m² đất, diện tích đất/sử dụng, số phòng, số tầng, pháp lý, đường vào. Trả kèm cảnh báo cách đọc giá/m². Compares 2–5 listings side by side with a derived price per m² of land.

urls.description: Danh sách 2–5 link hoặc slug moso.vn, cách nhau bằng dấu phẩy (VD: "ban-nha-quan-7-abc,ban-nha-quan-4-xyz"). Lấy từ trường url của search_listings.

format.description: markdown = bảng so sánh gọn cho LLM; json = dữ liệu có cấu trúc

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Chuyển bất kỳ trang moso.vn thành markdown gọn (tiết kiệm ~80% token so với HTML) — dùng để đọc chi tiết một tin đăng, dự án, hoặc bài viết. Reads any MOSO URL as clean markdown.

path.description: Đường dẫn tương đối trên moso.vn, bắt đầu bằng "/" (VD: "/ban-nha-quan-7-abc")

tools.name: search_projects
tools.description: Trả về dữ liệu dự án đã công bố trên MOSO: chủ đầu tư, loại hình căn, giai đoạn bán, khoảng giá mỗi căn, khoảng diện tích căn, quy mô, tiến độ, pháp lý, link. Dùng tool này thay vì mở trang khi cần đọc/so sánh. Returns structured project data (investor, unit types, sale stage, unit price band, progress, legal).

query.description: Tên dự án hoặc từ khóa (VD: "Vinhomes Grand Park"). Không đặt tỉnh/thành ở đây — dùng location.

location.description: Tỉnh/thành, nhiều giá trị cách nhau bằng dấu phẩy (VD: "Hồ Chí Minh,Bình Dương"). Chỉ cấp tỉnh/thành — quận/phường không lọc được ở tool này.

saleStatus.description: Giai đoạn bán: upcoming = sắp mở bán, booking_open = nhận booking, open = đang mở bán

Xếp hạng theo MOSO Score giống trang danh bạ, nên chỉ phân trang được trong nhóm 50 người dẫn đầu. Returns verified broker profiles ranked exactly as the public directory ranks them.

tools.name: request_contact
tools.description: Gửi yêu cầu xem nhà hoặc yêu cầu tư vấn cho một tin cụ thể trên MOSO — thao tác DUY NHẤT ghi dữ liệu. Chuyên viên MOSO gọi lại số điện thoại đã cung cấp để xác nhận; tool này KHÔNG chốt lịch hẹn. Chỉ gọi khi người dùng đã đồng ý để lại tên và số điện thoại thật của họ. Gọi lại cùng số điện thoại cho cùng một tin trong 24 giờ sẽ trả về đúng yêu cầu cũ, không tạo bản ghi mới. Submits a viewing or consultation request for one listing; MOSO staff call back to confirm.

phone.description: Số di động Việt Nam 10 số, đầu 03/05/07/08/09 (hoặc dạng +84...). Bắt buộc.

preferredTime.description: Thời gian mong muốn, dạng văn bản tự do (VD: "chiều thứ 7", "sau 18h các ngày trong tuần")

message.description: Nội dung người dùng muốn nhắn cho môi giới

tools.name: ordenar_resultados
tools.description: Ordena los planes/seguros que se muestran en el comparador de QuePlan Chile. Dispara una nueva búsqueda con el orden elegido y devuelve cuántos resultados hay.

order.description: Criterio de orden. Opciones: recommended (recomendados), lowerPrice (menor precio), higherPrice (mayor precio), popular (más populares), distance (cercanía).

tools.name: cambiar_moneda
tools.description: Cambia la moneda en que se muestran los precios en el comparador de QuePlan Chile entre pesos chilenos (CLP) y UF. Solo afecta la visualización, no vuelve a cotizar.

currency.description: Moneda de visualización. Opciones: CLP (pesos chilenos (CLP)), UF (UF).

tools.name: setear_perfil
tools.description: Define el perfil del cotizante en el comparador de QuePlan Chile (edad, sexo y cargas/dependientes). Recalcula la cotización y devuelve cuántos resultados hay para ese perfil. Es un patch: solo se modifican los campos que envíes y el resto del perfil se conserva, así que NO reenvíes datos que el usuario no te haya dado. Para dejar el perfil sin cargas, envía "cargas": [].

ingreso.description: Opcional. Renta líquida mensual en CLP; se usa para estimar el rango de precios.

cargas.description: Cargas/dependientes del grupo familiar. Cada carga requiere al menos su edad; no envíes cargas vacías ni inventes datos que el usuario no dio.

tools.name: aplicar_filtros_comparador
tools.description: Aplica filtros al comparador de QuePlan Chile y devuelve cuántos resultados quedan. Filtros soportados: previsión, precio máximo (CLP), categoría padre (categoria), categorías hijas (insuranceTypes), compañías/aseguradoras (organizations), prestadores/clínicas (coverageOrganizations). Cada lista de IDs REEMPLAZA la selección previa de ESE filtro (enviar [x] deja solo x marcado, no lo agrega); los filtros que no envíes quedan intactos. Para agregar algo a una selección existente, lee primero estado_comparador y envía la lista completa. Usa obtener_opciones_filtro para traducir nombres a IDs.

precioMax.description: Precio mensual máximo en CLP. Es el filtro de precio principal.

precioMin.description: Opcional. Precio mensual mínimo en CLP; normalmente no se usa.

insuranceTypes.description: IDs de categorías (tipos de seguro) a marcar en el filtro de categorías. REEMPLAZA la selección actual de categorías. Enviar [] restaura el filtro a su default (todas las categorías marcadas).

prevision.description: Filtrar por previsión/dominio de salud. Opciones: Isapre_Allowed, Fonasa_Allowed.

categoria.description: Categoría PADRE a seleccionar por url o nombre (ej. "Oncologico", "Dental"). Navega el comparador a esa categoría. Usa el campo "url" o "name" de un grupo devuelto por obtener_opciones_filtro. Tiene prioridad sobre insuranceTypes.

organizations.description: IDs de compañías/aseguradoras a marcar en el filtro de organizaciones. REEMPLAZA la selección actual de compañías. Enviar [] restaura el filtro a su default (todas las compañías marcadas).

coverageOrganizations.description: IDs de prestadores/clínicas a marcar en el filtro de prestadores. REEMPLAZA la selección actual de prestadores. Enviar [] limpia el filtro (sin restricción de prestador).

tools.name: obtener_opciones_filtro
tools.description: Lista las opciones disponibles de los filtros del comparador de QuePlan Chile: categorías (insuranceTypes) y compañías/aseguradoras (organizations) se devuelven como ÁRBOL —cada grupo con sus hijas (id + nombre)—; prestadores/clínicas (coverageOrganizations) es una lista plana. Read-only. Úsala ANTES de aplicar_filtros_comparador para traducir nombres a los IDs de las hijas.

query.description: Filtra las opciones por nombre (sin distinguir mayúsculas/acentos). Ej: "alemana" para encontrar una clínica sin traer el catálogo completo.

limite.description: Máximo de PRESTADORES a devolver (default 60; hay cientos).

tools.name: estado_comparador
tools.description: Devuelve el estado ACTUAL del comparador de QuePlan Chile (read-only, no cambia nada): perfil del cotizante vigente (edad, sexo, cargas), categoría/ruta actual, moneda y orden de visualización, filtros activos, y el resultado actual (total de seguros, si está cargando o con error, y rango de precios con su moneda en "monedaPrecios": es la del backend, UF, y NO la de "filtros.precioMax", que va en CLP). Úsala para conocer el contexto antes de setear perfil, aplicar filtros o listar seguros. Por ser datos sensibles NO devuelve la renta/ingreso ni la previsión de salud del cotizante: si los necesitas, pídeselos al usuario. OJO: el usuario puede cambiar filtros, perfil, orden o página A MANO en la página en cualquier momento; antes de responder sobre resultados vuelve a llamar esta tool o listar_seguros y compara "resultado.actualizadoEn" con tu última lectura.

tools.name: listar_seguros
tools.description: Lista los seguros/productos actualmente visibles en el comparador de QuePlan Chile (según el perfil y los filtros vigentes) con sus datos clave: aseguradora, categoría, precio (con su propia moneda, que puede variar entre productos: no sumes ni compares montos de monedas distintas) y señales (nuevo, exclusivo, popular). Si un producto no tiene precio para el perfil evaluado, el precio viene null (no 0). Read-only: NO ejecuta una búsqueda nueva, solo lee el resultado actual y espera a que termine de cargar antes de listar. Para cambiar qué se lista, usa antes setear_perfil / aplicar_filtros_comparador / ordenar_resultados. Los ids son válidos SOLO para el resultado actual: si el usuario cambia filtros/perfil/página a mano (puede hacerlo en cualquier momento), vuelve a listar antes de usar un id en obtener_detalle_seguro / comparar_seguros / preparar_solicitud.

limite.description: Máximo de seguros a devolver (por defecto 18, el tamaño de página).

tools.name: ver_mas_resultados
tools.description: Avanza a la siguiente página de resultados del comparador de QuePlan Chile: la lista visible pasa a mostrar los siguientes seguros y listar_seguros los devuelve. Úsala cuando listar_seguros muestre menos seguros en página que el total y necesites más opciones.

tools.name: obtener_detalle_seguro
tools.description: Abre en pantalla la ficha de detalle de un seguro del comparador de QuePlan Chile (la misma que ve el usuario al hacer click en "Ver detalle") y devuelve sus datos: precio, coberturas, topes, deducibles y características. Usa el "id" que devuelve listar_seguros. El usuario VE la ficha abrirse: ideal para mostrar la opción de la que le estás hablando.

tools.name: comparar_seguros
tools.description: Abre la comparación lado a lado de 2 o 3 seguros en el comparador de QuePlan Chile (la misma vista que el botón "Comparar" de las cards) y devuelve sus datos para explicar diferencias. Usa los "id" de listar_seguros. REEMPLAZA la selección de comparación anterior.

ids.description: IDs de los seguros a comparar (2 a 3, de listar_seguros).

tools.name: recomendar_seguros
tools.description: Recomienda el top 3 de seguros del comparador de QuePlan Chile para el perfil y filtros ACTUALES, con razones estructuradas por cada uno, y abre la comparación lado a lado en pantalla (REEMPLAZA la selección de comparación anterior). Ajusta antes el perfil y los filtros según lo que pida el usuario; luego usa las razones para explicarle la recomendación y ofrécele preparar_solicitud si quiere avanzar con una.

criterio.description: Criterio de ranking. mejor_valor (default): score de recomendación del comparador; menor_precio: más baratos primero; mayor_cobertura: más coberturas conocidas primero.

tools.name: guardar_comparacion
tools.description: Genera un link corto para guardar o compartir la comparación ACTUAL del comparador de QuePlan Chile. Quien lo abra recupera el perfil (edad, sexo, cargas), el orden, la moneda, las categorías, compañías y prestadores marcados, el rango de precio y los seguros seleccionados para comparar; la respuesta lista exactamente qué restaura (`restaura`) y qué no (`noRestaura`: la previsión Isapre/Fonasa no viaja). Útil para "guárdame esta búsqueda", "pásale esto a mi pareja" o retomar más tarde. El link queda guardado en el sitio y contiene edad, sexo y cargas (nunca renta ni datos de contacto): díselo al usuario antes de compartirlo con terceros.

tools.name: preparar_solicitud
tools.description: Prepara la contratación/solicitud de un seguro del comparador de QuePlan Chile: abre su ficha en pantalla y resalta el botón real de contratación para que EL USUARIO lo presione. NO envía la solicitud ni ingresa datos: la decisión y el click final son siempre del humano. Úsala cuando el usuario diga que quiere avanzar con una opción concreta. Después de llamarla, indícale al usuario que revise la ficha y presione el botón resaltado si está de acuerdo; NO intentes presionarlo tú.

id.description: ID del seguro a solicitar (campo "id" de listar_seguros).

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Product detail parameters.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

value.description: Option value, e.g. "160cm" or "Fiberglass".

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant. To change a quantity or remove something already in the cart, use update_cart_lines instead — this tool can only add.

line_items.description: Items to add (1-10).

item.description: The merchandise to add.

id.description: ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

handle.description: Product handle. Adds the selected or first available variant; call get_product first if the user requested specific options.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: How many to add. Defaults to 1.

tools.name: update_cart_lines
tools.description: Change the quantity of items already in the cart, or remove them. Every change here addresses an existing cart line by its id, so call get_cart first unless you already have line_items[].id from an earlier get_cart in this conversation. Pass the ABSOLUTE target quantity, not a delta — quantity 2 means the line ends up at 2 regardless of what it was. Use quantity 0 to remove the line entirely. Batch every change for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart_lines once per line. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. This tool cannot add new merchandise. To add something not already in the cart, use add_to_cart. To empty the whole cart at once, use cancel_cart.

line_items.description: Existing cart lines to update or remove (1-10).

id.description: Existing cart line id from get_cart line_items[].id. Required — this tool cannot resolve products by name.

quantity.description: Absolute target quantity for this line (not a delta). 0 removes the line.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Remove all items from the cart in one step. Use when the user wants to empty their cart or start over.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Proceed to checkout. Verifies the cart is not empty, then MOVES the browser to the checkout page. The tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: manage_orders
tools.description: Navigate to the customer's order history page. Use when the user asks about past orders, order status, tracking, or returns. The user will be prompted to log in if not already authenticated. This MOVES the browser to the order history page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: search_shop_policies_and_faqs
tools.description:
Used to get facts about the store's policies, FAQ, or contact details.
When the question is about specific policy kinds, set policy_types to those kinds; leave it unset for general FAQ questions.
Some examples of questions you can ask are:
  - What is your return policy? (policy_types: ["refund"])
  - What is your shipping policy? (policy_types: ["shipping"])
  - What is your phone number? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - What are your hours of operation? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - Do you offer gift wrapping? (general FAQ, no specific policy kind — leave policy_types unset)

query.description: A natural language query. Searches FAQ pages and articles, and routes policies by keyword when policy_types is omitted.

policy_types.description: Policy kinds to fetch, chosen from the user's question — e.g. ["refund"] for returns/exchanges, ["contact"] for phone/hours/address. Include every kind the question touches. Omit when no specific policy is relevant (e.g. a general FAQ question).

tools.name: get_current_page
tools.description: Describe the TaxHawk page the person is on: its title, link and canonical link, its main heading and section headings, the help articles it shows and, on an article page, that article's id (ids to read in full), the sign-in and start-return buttons on it, and the tools available right now. Call it after arriving on a page or after open_page.

tools.name: find_page
tools.description: Search TaxHawk's own pages by topic, for example "1099-NEC", "Oregon", "extension" or "military", and return up to 8 matching pages with their titles, descriptions, paths and links. Open one in this tab with open_page. Help articles are searched separately, with the help search tool.

query.description: A topic, form, state or situation, for example "self-employed" or "Form 1099-K".

tools.name: open_page
tools.description: Open another TaxHawk page in this tab by its path, for example "/pricing" or "/states/oregon", and return a description of the new page, as get_current_page does. Use a path from find_page or from a link on this page. Only pages on this site open; sign-in and start-return buttons have their own tools.

path.description: A path on this site starting with "/", for example "/pricing" or "/survey?name=feedback".

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Current TaxHawk prices for the 2025 tax year, in US dollars, as the pricing page shows them. Federal returns are $0. The state return, Deluxe, Pro Support, Audit Defense, amended, printed, bound and prior-year prices are listed separately, plus the fee for paying out of a federal refund.

tools.name: get_key_dates
tools.description: The IRS dates on TaxHawk's deadline page for the 2025 tax year: when the IRS starts processing returns, the April filing deadline, and the extension deadline, plus today's date and whether each deadline has passed. irsStartsProcessing is null until the IRS announces it. Dates are US local dates in YYYY-MM-DD form.

tools.name: search_faqs
tools.description: Search TaxHawk's tax help library and return up to 5 matching articles with their ids, titles and links. Use it for questions about tax forms, credits, deductions, filing situations, and how the software handles them. Titles are not answers: read the article with get_faq before giving tax guidance. An empty results list means no article matched.

query.description: A plain-language tax question, for example "Can I deduct student loan interest?"

tools.name: get_faq
tools.description: Read up to 5 articles from TaxHawk's tax help library in full, by id. Returns each article's title, its text with the formatting removed, and its link. Get ids from search_faqs or from get_current_page. An id that does not exist is left out of the results.

ids.description: Help article ids from a search result's id or from get_current_page, for example [1605].

tools.name: get_entry_links
tools.description: Returns links, without opening them: startNewReturn for a new 2025 return, signInToContinue for a return already started, priorYearReturn to start a return for taxYear (default 2024), and accountRecovery for a lost username or password. Each opens the sign-in site, where the person signs in or creates an account themselves.

taxYear.description: A prior tax year for priorYearReturn, 2018 to 2024. Defaults to 2024.

tools.name: start_return
tools.description: Open TaxHawk's sign-in site to start a tax return, in this tab. product picks the starting point: a new 2025 return, one with Deluxe, Pro Support or Audit Defense added, an extension, an amended return, a prior-year return, or a paid-preparer return. The person signs in or creates an account there themselves.

product.description: What to start. Use "new" for an ordinary current-year return.

year.description: Tax year, only for prior_year (default 2024) or amended (default 2025).

tools.name: sign_in
tools.description: Open TaxHawk's sign-in site in this tab so the person can sign in and continue a 2025 return they already started. The password and any verification code go into that page directly, from the person, a password manager or a passkey, never through this conversation.

tools.name: recover_account
tools.description: Open TaxHawk's account recovery page in this tab, for a person who forgot their username or password or can't sign in. The person answers the recovery questions there; recovery codes and the new password go into that page directly, never through this conversation.

tools.name: open_account_page
tools.description: Open a page inside the person's TaxHawk account, in this tab, after they sign in: check their e-file status, contact customer support, or print or download a return they filed. The browser goes to the sign-in site first; the person signs in themselves.

page.description: Which account page to open after sign-in.

tools.name: WixREADME
tools.description:
# Tool: WixREADME
**Directive:** `WixREADME` is the **MANDATORY FIRST STEP** for all Wix-related tasks. Its output (including relevant linked documents) provides foundational context for all other Wix tools. Adherence to this protocol is **NON-NEGOTIABLE**.

**Mid-conversation site switching:** If the user references a different site by name or ID after WixREADME has already been called, use `GetSiteContext` directly — no need to call WixREADME again.
<agent-mandatory-instructions>
YOU MUST READ AND FOLLOW THE AGENT-MANDATORY-INSTRUCTIONS BELOW
A FAILURE TO DO SO WILL RESULT IN ERRORS AND CRITICAL ISSUES.
<goal>
You are an agent that helps the user manage their Wix site.
Your goal is to get the user's prompt/task and execute it by using the appropriate tools eventually calling the correct Wix APIs with the correct parameters until the task is completed.
</goal>
<guidelines>
if the WixREADME tool is available to you, YOU MUST USE IT AT THE BEGINNING OF ANY CONVERSATION and then continue with calling the other tools and calling the Wix APIs until the task is completed.
**Exception:** If the user asks to create, build, or generate a new Wix site/website, skip WixREADME and:
- If the user **explicitly** mentions a template, Wix Studio, or headless → call CreateWixBusinessGuide directly.
- Otherwise → call the WixSiteBuilder tool directly.
**Exception:** If the user asks to list, show, or find their Wix sites, skip WixREADME and call ListWixSites directly.
**Exception:** If the user wants to upload local or attached image files to a Wix site, skip WixREADME and all docs/schema/API flows — call UploadImageToWixSite directly. Do NOT use ExecuteWixAPI, SearchWixAPISpec, or any Media Manager REST API for image uploads.
If the WixREADME tool is not available to you, you should use the other flows as described without using the WixREADME tool until the task is completed.
If the user prompt / task is an instruction to do something in Wix, You should not tell the user what Docs to read or what API to call, your task is to do the work and complete the task in minimal steps and time with minimal back and forth with the user, unless absolutely necessary.
</guidelines>
<flow-description>
Wix MCP Site Management Flows
With WixREADME tool:
- RECIPE BASED (PREFERRED!): WixREADME() -> find relevant recipe for the user's prompt/task -> read recipe using ReadFullDocsArticle() -> call Wix API using CallWixSiteAPI() based on the recipe
- CONVERSATION CONTEXT BASED: find relevant docs article or API example for the user's prompt/task in the conversation context -> call API using CallWixSiteAPI() based on the docs article or API example
- EXAMPLE BASED: WixREADME() -> no relevant recipe found for user's prompt/task -> BrowseWixRESTDocsMenu() or SearchWixRESTDocumentation() -> find relevant method -> read method article using ReadFullDocsArticle() to get method code examples -> call API using CallWixSiteAPI() based on the method code examples
- SCHEMA BASED, FALLBACK: WixREADME() -> no relevant recipe found for user's prompt/task -> BrowseWixRESTDocsMenu() or SearchWixRESTDocumentation() -> find relevant method -> read method article using ReadFullDocsArticle() -> no method code examples found -> inspect the method schema using SearchWixAPISpec or ReadFullDocsMethodSchema -> call API using CallWixSiteAPI() based on the schema
Without WixREADME tool:
- CONVERSATION CONTEXT BASED: find relevant docs article or API example for the user's prompt/task in the conversation context -> call API using CallWixSiteAPI() based on the docs article or API example
- METHOD CODE EXAMPLE BASED: BrowseWixRESTDocsMenu() or SearchWixRESTDocumentation() -> find relevant method -> read method article using ReadFullDocsArticle() to get method code examples -> call API using CallWixSiteAPI() based on the method code examples
- FULL SCHEMA BASED: BrowseWixRESTDocsMenu() or SearchWixRESTDocumentation() -> find relevant method -> read method article using ReadFullDocsArticle() -> no method code examples found -> inspect the method schema using SearchWixAPISpec or ReadFullDocsMethodSchema -> call API using CallWixSiteAPI() based on the schema
</flow-description>
</agent-mandatory-instructions>

tools.description:
Fetches the full Wix docs article or method article with code examples for using the method.
Docs articles looks like this: https://dev.wix.com/docs/... and they can either be general docs articles or method articles.
For REST docs, use the URL as-is. For SDK docs, the URL SHOULD include ?apiView=SDK.

tools.name: ReadFullDocsMethodSchema
tools.description:
Fetches the full method schema for a given method.
This will give you the entire request/response schema with all the fields and their descriptions.
For REST API methods, prefer SearchWixAPISpec when it is available: it can fetch and inspect the exact method schema by docs URL, return the request/response shape, and inspect selected nested component schemas without dumping unrelated fields. Use ReadFullDocsMethodSchema for REST only when SearchWixAPISpec is unavailable or did not provide the needed detail.
For REST docs, use the URL as-is. For SDK docs, the URL SHOULD include ?apiView=SDK.

tools.name: ExecuteWixAPI

code.description: JavaScript async function expression to execute against the Wix REST API. The value must be the function itself, for example `async function() { ... }` or `async () => { ... }`, not a script body and not an invoked function. Return the final answer from inside the function. Do not write top-level `const`, top-level `await`, or top-level `return` outside the function body. Use `wix.request({ method, url, body })` for Wix API calls. Every call runs against the current visitor site; do not set `scope`, `siteId`, or auth headers. Full Wix API URLs and paths starting with `/` are supported. Wix REST API page size limits vary — use 100 as a safe default unless the method schema (via SearchWixAPISpec) confirms a higher limit is supported. For cursor-based APIs, pass the next cursor as `cursorPaging: { limit: 100, cursor: pagingMetadata.cursors.next }` — not inside `paging`. Check the method schema to confirm whether the API uses `paging` (offset-based) or `cursorPaging` (cursor-based) before paginating.

tools.name: GetSitePages
tools.description: Returns the COMPLETE list of pages that exist on this site, as route patterns. Only these pages exist; never guess or invent a URL (e.g. /shop, /store, /checkout, /account) - a path not listed here will show a 404. `title` is the page's name in the site menu; match it against what the visitor asks for. Static routes are exact paths (e.g. /cart). Dynamic routes contain [param] placeholders (e.g. /products/[slug]) or a rest placeholder ([...path]); `identifiers` says what fills each placeholder (e.g. slug: STORES.PRODUCT.SLUG means the product's slug from the Stores products API) and `pageIdentifier` names the Wix page type. A route with `acceptsSubpath` also accepts a concrete path below it, e.g. the product page URL returned by the Stores API. Navigate with NavigateToPage, passing the route pattern and a `params` value for every placeholder. If the page the visitor asks for is not in the list, say so instead of navigating.

Never derive a placeholder value from a name or title; take it from the record the relevant API returns.

tools.name: getWeatherForecast
tools.description: Get an hourly weather forecast from the free Open-Meteo API for a location. Provide EITHER {latitude, longitude} (e.g. from getUserLocation) OR {locationName} (e.g. 'Lisbon' or 'Paris, France') to geocode it automatically. Returns a compact CSV — one row per 3-hour step — containing only the fields you ask for, to keep the response small: pass 'fields' to pick exactly what's needed instead of the default set, and 'days' (1-7, default 2) to bound how far ahead to fetch. Prefer this over web search for weather questions — it's more precise and far cheaper on context. For activity/timing questions that hinge on cloud cover over several days (stargazing, photography, hiking windows, outdoor events), call this ALONGSIDE webSearch rather than instead of it: use this tool for the actual verified cloud/precip numbers per day, and web search for context this API can't provide (moon phase, celestial events, venue recommendations) — then reconcile the two rather than repeating an unverified weather claim from a search result. Units: temperature/apparentTemperature in °C, wind/windGusts in km/h, windDirection in degrees, precipitation is a % probability, precipitationAmount in mm, visibility in km, humidity/clouds in %, weatherCode is a WMO code (0 = clear sky, higher = increasingly cloudy/wet/severe). When the user would benefit from seeing a multi-day trend rather than reading the raw CSV (e.g. 'when's the driest afternoon this week'), follow up with showChart (type:'line', one series per field you're highlighting) instead of describing the numbers in prose — the CSV's 3-hour rows are already close to that chart's {label, value} shape.

locationName.description: City/place name to geocode, e.g. 'Lisbon' or 'Paris, France'. Ignored if latitude/longitude are given.

days.description: How many days ahead to fetch, 1-7. Default 2.

fields.description: Which hourly fields to include. Default: temperature, precipitation, wind, clouds.

tools.name: showMap
tools.description: Show an interactive map card in the chat with one or more pins, optionally connected by a route. Renders as a small card the user can click to expand full-screen — use this instead of just describing locations in text whenever the answer is about specific real-world places. Provide pins as {name, lat, lng} — omit lat/lng to have the name geocoded automatically (free OpenStreetMap lookup). IMPORTANT: bare landmark names are sometimes ambiguous against unrelated same-named places elsewhere in the world (e.g. 'The Louvre' alone can match an obscure peak on another continent) — always include enough context to disambiguate when you know it, e.g. 'Louvre Museum, Paris' rather than 'The Louvre'. But do NOT go further and add a street address on top of a venue name — 'venue, city' is the sweet spot; 'venue, street address, city' geocodes WORSE (the geocoder can't match name+address in one query; the tool falls back to simplified retries but each costs an extra round-trip). Use a street address alone (no venue name) when the address IS the place being pinned. The tool also biases each pin's search toward previously resolved pins in the same call, so listing an unambiguous pin (e.g. 'Eiffel Tower') before ambiguous ones in the same city helps. Give each pin a 'category' for its marker color: default, food, lodging, activity, transport, event, landmark, nature.
