tools.name: addUser
tools.description:
Create a new user account.

**Identity:**
- firstName, lastName: User's name
- nickname: Display name (optional)
- emails: Array of email addresses (preferred for test users)
- username: Username for login (prefer email for test users)
- password: Account password

**Role & type:**
- teacher: Set true for teacher accounts
- student: Set true for student accounts
- role: Professional role (TEACHER, SCHOOL_ADMINISTRATOR, DISTRICT_ADMINISTRATOR, INSTRUCTIONAL_COACH, etc.)
- position: Job title/position

**Organization & section:**
- addToOrg: Add user to an organization { id, roles, verified }
- addToSection: Section/class ID to add student to

**Additional:**
- identifier: External system ID
- demographics: Demographic information object
- vertical: User category (use "other" for test users)

**Example - Test teacher:**
```json
{
  "input": {
    "firstName": "Test",
    "lastName": "Teacher",
    "emails": [{"address": "test-teacher@example.com", "verified": true}],
    "password": "testpass123",
    "teacher": true,
    "vertical": "other"
  }
}
```

**Example - Student in a class:**
```json
{
  "input": {
    "firstName": "Test",
    "lastName": "Student",
    "emails": [{"address": "test-student@example.com"}],
    "password": "testpass123",
    "student": true,
    "addToSection": "sectionId123"
  }
}
```

tools.name: saveAnswer
saveDrawingParts
tools.description:
Save drawing annotations for an answer.

This is used for questions with drawing enabled (e.g., show your work, long answer with drawing).
Each drawing part represents an SVG path.

**IMPORTANT**: A submission must exist before saving drawings. Use saveSubmission first.

**Drawing Part Format:**
Each part has:
- id: A unique identifier for the path (generate a random string)
- d: SVG path data string (e.g., "M 10 10 L 50 50 L 90 10")

**Example:**
```json
{
  "input": {
    "formativeItemId": "item123",
    "saveParts": [
      { "id": "path-1", "d": "M 10 10 L 50 50" },
      { "id": "path-2", "d": "M 20 20 C 40 40, 60 40, 80 20" }
    ]
  }
}
```

**SVG Path Commands:**
- M x y: Move to point
- L x y: Line to point
- C x1 y1, x2 y2, x y: Cubic bezier curve
- Q x1 y1, x y: Quadratic bezier curve
- Z: Close path

tools.name: saveSubmission
tools.description:
Create or update a submission for a formative.

A submission represents a student's attempt at completing a formative. It tracks:
- Whether the student has started the formative
- Whether they have submitted their answers
- Timing information for timed assessments
- Retake information

**Common workflows:**

1. **Start a submission** (student begins working):
   ```json
   { "input": { "formativeId": "abc123" } }
   ```

2. **Submit the formative** (student is done):
   ```json
   { "input": { "formativeId": "abc123", "submitted": true } }
   ```

3. **Teacher force-submits for a student**:
   ```json
   { "input": { "formativeId": "abc123", "onBehalfOfStudentId": "student123", "submitted": true } }
   ```

4. **Teacher un-submits (reopen) for a student**:
   ```json
   { "input": { "formativeId": "abc123", "onBehalfOfStudentId": "student123", "submitted": false } }
   ```

5. **Student starts a retake**:
   ```json
   { "input": { "formativeId": "abc123", "startRetake": true } }
   ```

6. **Teacher pauses a student**:
   ```json
   { "input": { "formativeId": "abc123", "onBehalfOfStudentId": "student123", "pausedState": "teacherPaused" } }
   ```

**Assignment settings** (control what students see):
- returnScores: When students can see their scores
  - "never" - Never show scores
  - "afterSubmission" - Show after they submit
  - "immediately" - Show right away

- returnAnswers: When students can see correct answers
  - "never" - Never show
  - "afterSubmission" - Show after they submit
  - "immediately" - Show right away

- isPartialCredit, partialCreditMode: Scoring options
- isRandomized: Randomize choices
- hints: Hint array

- src, alternateText: For media content

**Example:**


Update an existing section (class). Note: In Formative, "section" and "class" are interchangeable terms. Requires ownership or appropriate permissions.

- title: Section name
- abbreviation: Short code displayed in UI
- color: Hex color code for the section

- locked: Lock section to prevent students from joining via code
- ownerId: Transfer ownership to an existing collaborator

- subjects: Array of subject names

**Example:**

```json
{
```

tools.name: updateUser
tools.description:
Update an existing user account.

**Identity:**
- firstName, lastName: User's name
- nickname: Display name (optional)
- emails: Array of email addresses
- username: Username for login
- password: Account password

**Role & type:**
- teacher: Set true for teacher accounts
- student: Set true for student accounts
- role: Professional role (TEACHER, SCHOOL_ADMINISTRATOR, DISTRICT_ADMINISTRATOR, INSTRUCTIONAL_COACH, etc.)
- position: Job title/position

**Service tiers (admin only):**
- partner: Set partner (gold) status
- pilot: Set pilot status
- premium: Set premium (silver) status

**Organization management:**
- addToOrg: Add user to an organization { id, roles, verified }
- updateOrg: Update user's org membership { id, roles, verified }
- removeFromOrg: Remove user from an organization (org ID string)

**Additional:**
- identifier: External system ID
- demographics: Demographic information object
- vertical: User category
- commandCenterRole: Internal admin role (requires formative team member status)
- mergeRequest: Set a pending merge request { sourceUserId, comment } or null to clear

**Example - Update profile:**
```json
{
  "id": "userId123",
  "input": {
    "firstName": "John",
    "lastName": "Smith",
    "nickname": "Johnny",
    "role": "TEACHER",
    "position": "Math Teacher"
  }
}
```

**Example - Add user to org:**
```json
{
  "id": "userId123",
  "input": {
    "addToOrg": { "id": "orgId456", "roles": ["teacher"], "verified": true }
  }
}
```

tools.name: list_clips
tools.description: List the clips of the open project with id, name, pixel size, duration, frame rate and background. The selected clip is marked with an asterisk. Filter by a name fragment with query; page with offset (40 per page). Start here to discover clip ids.

query.description: Only clips whose name contains this, case-insensitive.

offset.description: Skip this many matches (paging).

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List every saved project with its id and clip count. The open one is marked with an asterisk.

tools.name: open_project
tools.description: Switch the editor to another project. Clip tools then act on that project.

projectId.description: Project id from list_projects.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a new project, open it, and select its starter clip. Use this to keep unrelated work apart rather than piling clips into one project.

tools.name: select_clip
tools.description: Make a clip the active one in the editor. Other tools default to the selected clip.

tools.name: get_timeline
tools.description: The open timeline: settings, tracks and every item with id, type, track, start–end in seconds and source in-point. Tracks are listed top to bottom; the last video track is the picture, those above are overlays. Notes left on tracks and items (by a person, or by set_track/set_item) follow a dash — read them, they are instructions. Filter by trackId or a time window when long.

fromSeconds.description: Only items ending after this time.

toSeconds.description: Only items starting before this time.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: list_timelines
tools.description: The project as a tree: the main timeline (★, what the project delivers), the sections it plays (⧉, indented, in time order, with where they sit), then timelines placed nowhere yet. Shows claims and notes. The open one is marked *. Pass any id as timelineId to other tools to work there without opening it.

tools.name: get_timeline_state
tools.description: Playhead position, whether it is playing, timeline length, the selected item, and how many edits can be undone. Cheap; call it before capture_timeline_frame or after a batch of edits.

tools.name: list_media
tools.description: Video and audio files in the media library, with the filename to use as sourceId, duration, size, frame rate and whether each has picture and sound.

tools.name: list_transcripts
tools.description: Imported transcripts (SRT, VTT, Whisper JSON) with id, cue count, length, whether they carry word-level timings, and the media file each is bound to.

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.description: Read a transcript window. format "cues" gives timed lines, "words" gives every word with its own start/end (when the source has them), "text" gives plain prose. Times are SOURCE seconds of the media file. Output is capped, so page with fromSeconds; the last line says where to continue.

fromSeconds.description: Start of the window in source seconds. Default 0.

toSeconds.description: End of the window. Default: as much as fits.

format.description: Default "cues".

tools.name: find_in_transcript
tools.description: Find where a phrase is spoken. Returns each match with its SOURCE start/end seconds — exact to the word when the transcript has word timings, otherwise the containing cue. Feed the times to cut_source_ranges to remove that speech, or to add_to_timeline (converted through the item's in-point) to place a title where it is said.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: detect_silence
tools.description: Find silent gaps from the waveform. With itemId the gaps come back in SEQUENCE seconds for that item; with media (a filename) they come back in SOURCE seconds for the whole file. Tune with thresholdDb / minGapSeconds / keepMs. remove_silence applies the same detection.

itemId.description: Item id from get_timeline.

media.description: Media filename from list_media, when not using itemId.

thresholdDb.description: Quieter than this is silence. Default -40; raise towards -25 for a noisy room.

minGapSeconds.description: Ignore gaps shorter than this. Default 0.5.

keepMs.description: Milliseconds of each gap to keep at both ends, so cuts land after the breath. Default 150.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: check_timeline
tools.description: Preflight the timeline for what only shows after rendering: missing media or clips, items running past the end of their file, opaque clips used as overlays (they cover everything beneath), letterboxed footage, captions covering no cues, and a timeline with no sound.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: capture_timeline_frame
tools.description: Composite the timeline — footage, overlays and captions stacked exactly as the render will — and show it. With a server you get a PNG URL to fetch; with no server the stage is left parked on that frame for you to look at, and the picture is attached to the result where the runtime supports images. One frame at timeSeconds, or with count 2–12 a labelled contact sheet spread between fromSeconds and toSeconds: the quickest way to see an overlay against the footage over its whole life. The editor is left parked on the last frame.

timeSeconds.description: Timeline time to capture. Defaults to the playhead.

count.description: Frames for a contact sheet, 2–12.

toSeconds.description: Sheet end. Default the timeline end.

timelineId.description: Open this timeline first (id from list_timelines).

tools.name: create_timeline
tools.description: Add a timeline to the project and open it. Defaults to 1920x1080, 30fps, black. Comes with tracks V2, V1 (picture) and A1.

tools.name: open_timeline
tools.description: Open another timeline of the project in the editor.

timelineId.description: From list_timelines.

tools.name: set_timeline_settings
tools.description: Change a timeline's name, frame size, frame rate, background or note, or make it the main timeline. Items are not rescaled; footage refits by its fit mode. A note is read by whoever works there next — leave instructions in it.

note.description: Free text about this timeline; "" clears it.

main.description: true makes this the main timeline — the one the project delivers.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: add_media_from_url
tools.description: Bring a video or audio file into the media library. url is a public http(s) URL, or a data: URL (base64; 24 MB decoded at most) when you hold the bytes — a voice-over a tool returned, say. Sniffed on arrival: mp4, m4v, mov, webm, mkv, avi, wav, mp3, m4a, aac, flac, ogg, opus. It is probed and the reply gives the filename to use as sourceId. Anything larger: host it, or ask the person to drop the file in.

url.description: Public http(s) URL, or data:<mime>;base64,… holding the file (24 MB decoded max).

name.description: Optional filename. Its extension is corrected if it disagrees with the bytes.

tools.name: list_text_presets
tools.description: The ready-made animated title styles a text item can use — title, lower third, subtitle bar, pop-words, typewriter, impact, label, quote — with the fields each takes and its default length, plus the shapes add_shape places (rectangle, ellipse, frame, ring, highlight, line, arrow, marker, check, pulse, pointer), each with the add_shape parameters it takes. Use with add_text; no clip code needed.

tools.name: add_text
tools.description: Put an animated title on the timeline from a preset: type the words, pick the preset, place it. (For a shape — a rectangle, frame, ring, arrow, marker and so on — use add_shape.) It animates in from its start and out at its end, whatever length it is given. Placement uses anchor; style takes fontFamily, fontSize, color, accent, boxColor, weight, uppercase, align. Convertible to a clip later for full control.

preset.description: Preset id from list_text_presets. Default "title".

text.description: The words.

subtext.description: Second line, for presets that have one (lower-third role, quote attribution, title strap).

atSeconds.description: Start on the timeline. Defaults to the playhead.

durationSeconds.description: Length. Defaults to the preset default.

trackId.description: A video track id; otherwise a free overlay track is chosen or made.

anchor.description: Nudge the whole title from the preset's own placement.

style.description: fontFamily, fontSize, color, accent, boxColor, weight, uppercase, align.

name.description: Item name on the timeline; defaults to the text.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: add_shape
tools.description: Put a shape on the timeline, sized in timeline pixels and placed by anchor and offsets (default anchor top-left, so offsetX/offsetY are its top-left corner in frame pixels; anchor center places its middle). rect and ellipse are solid patches that cut in and out: in the footage's own colour (save_frame or capture_timeline_frame to read it) a rect hides an account name or a detail. frame and ring are outlines that draw themselves on around something (fill none by default). highlight is a translucent wash swiped over a line or a button. line and arrow draw from one end to the other: points is the end they draw towards, where the arrow's head is (for up or down make height the long side). marker is a numbered dot for steps (label is the number, "1" by default). check is a tick in a disc: the disc pops, then the tick draws. pulse is a dot with rings rippling outward, for "click here". pointer is a mouse pointer that lands and clicks once; its tip is the item's centre, so anchor center plus offsets place the tip. Lines are white with a small shadow by default; dashed makes a frame, ring, line or arrow dashed (it then fades in rather than drawing on). It is a text item with no words, so set_item changes it later (textStyle width/height/radius/stroke/color/accent/direction/dashed, text for a marker's number, offsetX/offsetY, opacity, timing) and it renders like any overlay.

width.description: Pixels at timeline size. Rounded to even.

height.description: Pixels at timeline size. Rounded to even.

fill.description: #rrggbb, or "none": the patch, the marker or check disc, the pulse's dot, the pointer's body. Frames and rings default to none; a highlight is drawn translucent whatever the colour.

outline.description: Line colour #rrggbb: a patch's outline, the stroke of a frame, ring, line or arrow, the marker's number, the check's tick, the pulse's rings, the pointer's edge. Default white (the pointer's is near-black).

outlineWidth.description: Line weight in pixels. 0 = no outline on a patch, marker or check; frames, rings, lines and arrows default to 6; pulse rings and the pointer's edge to 4.

corners.description: Corner radius in pixels for a rect, frame, highlight, marker or check. 999 is a circle (the marker and check default).

points.description: Line and arrow: the end it draws towards, where the head is. Default right.

dashed.description: Frame, ring, line, arrow: draw the stroke dashed. A dashed stroke fades in rather than drawing on.

label.description: Marker: the number or short label in the dot. Default "1".

anchor.description: Where the offsets are measured from. Default top-left.

atSeconds.description: Start on the timeline. Defaults to the playhead.

trackId.description: A video track id; otherwise a free overlay track is chosen or made.

name.description: Item name on the timeline; defaults to the shape name.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: add_to_timeline
tools.description: Place a source on the timeline. kind "media" takes a filename from list_media, "clip" a clip id (an overlay layer with real alpha), "transcript" an id (burnt-in captions, auto-aligned to its footage if placed), "timeline" another timeline id (a block that plays it — a section). Without trackId a free track is chosen or made; nothing is overwritten. Returns the new item id.

kind.description: What sourceId refers to. image = an image asset filename from list_assets: a still on an overlay track, held for durationSeconds (default 5), sized in set_item via imageStyle {width, height, radius, shadow} and fit.

sourceId.description: Media filename, clip id, transcript id, timeline id or image asset filename.

atSeconds.description: Where it starts on the timeline. Defaults to the playhead.

durationSeconds.description: Length on the timeline. Defaults to the source length.

trackId.description: A track id from get_timeline. Placing over an existing item trims it out of the way.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: set_item
tools.description: Change one item: timing (start, length, in-point), placement (fit for footage; anchor/offsetX/offsetY for overlays), size (scale for footage, nested blocks and animation clips; imageStyle/textStyle width and height for images and shapes; textStyle fontSize for titles), transform (rotation, flipH, flipV, crop), look (colour, blend, radius, shadow), opacity, sound (volume, muted, fades), captionStyle for captions, text/subtext/preset/textStyle for titles, or a note. Only the fields given change. A longer item trims whatever it now overlaps.

itemId.description: Item id from get_timeline.

fit.description: Footage: letterbox, crop, stretch, or native size.

anchor.description: Where an overlay (or fit:none footage) sits.

speed.description: Footage, nested blocks and animation clips only: how fast the source runs against the timeline. 1 is normal, 2 plays twice as fast, 0.5 is slow motion. The item keeps its length on the timeline and shows more or less of the source; sound is re-timed with its pitch kept. A caption or a title has no speed — its timing comes from its transcript or its own length.

dissolveInSeconds.description: Fade the picture up over this long at the start. Half of a cross dissolve.

dissolveOutSeconds.description: Fade the picture down over this long at the end.

scale.description: Footage, nested blocks and animation clips only, and only with fit:none: how big the layer is drawn against its natural size. 1 is unchanged, 0.3 is a picture-in-picture corner. An animation clip is re-rendered at that size, so it stays sharp; footage is resampled. An image, shape or title has no scale — give it a size instead.

rotation.description: Degrees clockwise, about the middle of the layer. -180 to 180.

crop.description: Footage and nested blocks only: how much of each edge to cut off before the fit, as fractions 0-0.95 — {top, right, bottom, left}. Fractions of the source, so the framing survives swapping the shot for another resolution. null clears it.

colour.description: Colour correction: {brightness, contrast, saturation} where 1 is unchanged, and {temperature} from -1 (cool) to 1 (warm). null clears it.

blend.description: How the layer mixes with what is under it.

radius.description: Round the layer's corners, in frame pixels. 0 is square.

shadow.description: A drop shadow under the layer: {blur, x, y, color, opacity}. blur 0 turns it off; null clears it. This is what makes a picture-in-picture read as a card over the footage.

captionStyle.description: Caption items: fontSize, color, boxColor, position (top|center|bottom), marginPx, maxWidthPct, uppercase, shadow, fontFamily, weight, transition (cut|fade|pop), karaoke (off|word|fill), accent.

note.description: Free text kept on the item and shown in get_timeline. Empty string clears it.

text.description: Text items: the words.

subtext.description: Text items: the second line, where the preset has one.

preset.description: Text items: switch preset (see list_text_presets).

imageStyle.description: Image items: width, height (pixels at timeline size; omit for natural size), radius (corner px), shadow (boolean). Use fit for contain/cover/fill/none.

textStyle.description: Text items: fontFamily, fontSize, color, accent, boxColor, weight (400-900), uppercase, align (left|center|right). Shapes: width, height, radius, stroke (the one line weight), color (fill), accent (line), direction (right|left|up|down), dashed; a marker's number is the item's text.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: move_item
tools.description: Move an item to a time, optionally onto another track of the same kind. Whatever it lands on is trimmed out of its way.

itemId.description: Item id from get_timeline.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: split_item
tools.description: Cut an item in two at a timeline time (default: the playhead). The tail keeps source continuity, so the cut does not jump. Returns both ids.

itemId.description: Item id from get_timeline.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: delete_item
tools.description: Remove an item. ripple:true also closes the gap by pulling everything after it on that track back.

itemId.description: Item id from get_timeline.

ripple.description: Close the gap on that track. Default false.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: cut_time_range
tools.description: Remove a stretch of SEQUENCE time from every unlocked track and close the gap — items spanning it are cut and rejoined, later items slide back. Lock a track (set_track) to protect a music bed. Undoable.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: cut_source_ranges
tools.description: Remove parts of an item by SOURCE time — the times find_in_transcript and get_transcript give — and ripple the whole timeline closed. This is how "cut the part where she repeats herself" or "drop every um" is done: find the words, pass their ranges. Captions on the same footage stay in sync. Undoable.

itemId.description: Item id from get_timeline.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: remove_silence
tools.description: Detect the silent gaps in an item and cut them all out of the timeline, rippling every unlocked track so captions and overlays stay aligned. Run detect_silence first to see what will go; lock a music bed with set_track. Undoable.

itemId.description: Item id from get_timeline.

thresholdDb.description: Quieter than this is silence. Default -40; raise towards -25 for a noisy room.

minGapSeconds.description: Ignore gaps shorter than this. Default 0.5.

keepMs.description: Milliseconds of each gap to keep at both ends, so cuts land after the breath. Default 150.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: replace_audio
tools.description: Put a different sound under an item — the new voice back from a voice tool, say. The item's own sound is muted and the new file is laid on an audio track aligned to the item's start. The reply says if the new sound is shorter or longer than the picture, so you can trim or hold it. Then edit_transcript to update the words.

itemId.description: Item id from get_timeline.

media.description: The new sound: a media filename from list_media (import it first with add_media_from_url or a drop).

inSeconds.description: In-point inside the new sound. Default 0.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: edit_transcript
tools.description: Replace what is said in a window of SOURCE time: cues wholly inside go, cues crossing an edge are cut at it, the new cues are put in. This is how the words of a re-voiced part are updated — captions on that footage recompile. Edited cues have no word timings (karaoke falls back to plain). Not part of undo_edit; undo_transcript_edit reverts it.

fromSeconds.description: Start of the window, source time.

toSeconds.description: End of the window, source time.

cues.description: The new lines, e.g. [{"fromSeconds":12.3,"toSeconds":15,"text":"…"}]. Empty array just clears the window.

tools.name: set_cue
tools.description: Change one cue by index (from get_transcript order): its text, start or end in source seconds, or delete it. Text edits drop that cue's word timings. Reverted by undo_transcript_edit.

index.description: Zero-based cue index.

text.description: New words.

tools.name: undo_transcript_edit
tools.description: Revert the last edit_transcript / set_cue on a transcript (twenty deep, this session).

tools.name: get_narration
tools.description: What is said when, in TIMELINE seconds — the map to plan overlays from ("put the keycap where he presses Ctrl"). Uses the captions placed on the timeline, else the transcript bound to its footage, mapped through each item's in-point. Filter with a time window or a query phrase.

fromSeconds.description: Only lines after this timeline time.

toSeconds.description: Only lines before this timeline time.

query.description: Only lines containing this phrase, case-insensitive.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: check_layout
tools.description: Where the overlays sit on screen, and which collide. Each overlay is drawn offscreen and the box of what it actually paints measured (at a quarter, half and three quarters of its life); pairs that share time and pixels — a title over the captions, two cards in the same corner — are reported with the overlap. Run it after placing overlays; a window keeps it quick.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: duplicate_timeline
tools.description: Copy a timeline as a new version — every track and item with fresh ids, placed right after the original, named "<name> v2" unless told otherwise. Sections (blocks playing other timelines) stay shared; deep: true copies them too, recursively, so the version can diverge all the way down. Opens the copy unless open: false. Iterate on the copy; the original is untouched.

name.description: Name for the copy. Default: the original's name with the next version number.

deep.description: Also copy the timelines its blocks play (default false: shared).

open.description: Open the copy (default true).

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: delete_timeline
tools.description: Remove a timeline document — a version you are done with. Refused for the main timeline and for one placed as a section somewhere (flatten or delete the blocks first). Its undo history goes with it; the timeline is not recoverable.

timelineId.description: The timeline to delete, from list_timelines. Required — never the open one by default.

tools.name: claim_timeline
tools.description: Say who is working on a timeline, so others keep off. Advisory: the claim shows in list_timelines and the rail; once you have named yourself here, edits to a timeline another agent holds are refused unless you take it over with force. Claims lapse after fifteen minutes; claim again to renew, release when done.

timelineId.description: Id from list_timelines. Defaults to the open timeline.

agent.description: Your name for this session, e.g. "agent-intro". Remembered for later calls.

force.description: true takes over another agent's claim.

tools.name: nest_items
tools.description: Group items into a new sub-timeline: they move into it (same layout, re-based to zero) and one block plays it in their place. The block opens as its own timeline — the unit of work to hand to an agent. Nothing is overwritten; a member on a locked track refuses the whole group. Returns the new timeline id and the block id.

itemIds.description: Item ids from get_timeline. Defaults to the selection.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: flatten_item
tools.description: Replace a timeline block with the items inside it, on parent tracks of the same kind and name (new tracks where those are busy; nothing is overwritten). Items are clipped to the block's window, volume and opacity scaled by the block's; the block's own fades are dropped. The sub-timeline itself stays in the project.

itemId.description: The block's item id from get_timeline.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: select_items
tools.description: Select items on the timeline, as shift-clicking them would. The selection is what the Export parts dialog and the multi-item actions start from; an empty list clears it.

timelineId.description: Open this timeline first (id from list_timelines).

tools.name: detach_audio
tools.description: Separate an item's sound from its picture: the sound becomes its own item on an audio track (same file, in-point and length) and the picture is muted. Then either can be trimmed, moved, replaced (replace_audio) or silenced on its own. One undo step.

itemId.description: Item id from get_timeline.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: add_track
tools.description: Add a video track (above the others) or an audio track (below).

kind.description: Track kind.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: export_captions
tools.description: One subtitle file from the timeline's caption items — every caption item when itemIds is empty, or just those — timed as the captions fall on the timeline, so it lines up with the rendered video (times "source" keeps the original file's times; one transcript only). SRT, WebVTT or plain text (the words alone). Written into Exports; fetch the returned URL.

itemIds.description: Caption item ids from get_timeline. Omit for all of them.

format.description: Default srt.

name.description: File name without extension. Defaults to the item or timeline name.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: move_track
tools.description: Reorder a track among those of its kind. Order is stacking order: the top track draws over everything beneath it, in the preview and in the render, so an overlay track that must show over another goes above it. Video tracks always stay above audio tracks. Give a direction (up, down, top, bottom) or a position counted from the top within the kind (0 = topmost). get_timeline lists tracks top to bottom.

trackId.description: Track id or name from get_timeline.

direction.description: One step, or all the way.

index.description: Position from the top among tracks of the same kind, 0 = topmost. Overrides direction.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: set_track
tools.description: Rename, colour, annotate, mute, hide or lock a track. A note is free text shown in get_timeline — leave instructions for later. A locked track is skipped by cut_time_range, cut_source_ranges and remove_silence.

note.description: Free text kept on the track. Empty string clears it.

hidden.description: Hide a video track from preview and render.

timelineId.description: Work in this timeline (id from list_timelines) instead of the open one. It need not be open; the view stays where it is.

tools.name: seek_timeline
tools.description: Move the timeline playhead so the preview shows that moment.

timelineId.description: Open this timeline first (id from list_timelines).

tools.name: speech_setup
tools.description: What this browser can currently do with speech: whether transcription and a voice are set up, which provider each uses, and where the audio would go. Call it before promising to transcribe or narrate — none of it is configured by default, and only the person at the keyboard can add a key. In the UI this is the Speech tab in the left rail: its foot names the provider for each job, and its Providers… button is where one is set up when nothing is.

tools.name: transcribe_media
tools.description: Write down what is said in a library file, using whatever transcription the person has set up, and add the words as a transcript. Comes back with word timings where the provider gives them, so the result can be placed as karaoke captions. Check speech_setup first. The same job as the Transcribe button in the Speech rail, on a media tile with sound, and in a selected item’s Sound section.

tools.name: add_voice_over
tools.description: Read a script aloud into an audio file and drop it on an audio track. Needs a voice that returns audio — the computer’s own voices cannot be recorded. Check speech_setup first; use time_script to see how long a script runs before committing to it. The same job as the Write a voice-over… button in the Speech rail, Voice-over… in a selected item’s Sound section, and Voice-over from these lines… on a caption item.

text.description: What should be said.

voice.description: Voice id from list_voices. Default: the one chosen in the panel.

language.description: ISO code the script is in (es, en, pt…). Picks a voice of that language where each voice speaks one, or is sent with the script where voices are multilingual. Default: the language chosen in the panel, else auto.

name.description: A name for the audio file.

atSeconds.description: Where on the timeline it starts. Defaults to the playhead.

tools.name: list_voices
tools.description: The voices the chosen voice provider can speak with, grouped by language, each with the id to pass as voice to add_voice_over — and which voice and language the person has selected. With VoiceBox it also counts the built-in presets add_voice can save as profiles. Check speech_setup first.

language.description: Only voices of this language, as an ISO code such as es or en.

tools.name: add_voice
tools.description: Give the chosen voice provider a new voice and select it. VoiceBox: one of its built-in presets ("kokoro/ef_dora", from list_voices) saved as a profile, or a clone of a recording in the library — fromSourceId plus referenceText, the words said in it (the recording’s transcript is used when there is one). ElevenLabs: an instant clone of a recording, which sends the audio there. Returns the voice id for add_voice_over.

preset.description: VoiceBox only: "<engine>/<voice id>" from list_voices, e.g. "kokoro/em_alex".

fromSourceId.description: A library recording with sound (filename from list_media) to clone.

referenceText.description: What is said in that recording, for VoiceBox. Default: its transcript.

language.description: ISO code of the voice’s language, e.g. es. Default: the preset’s, else the panel’s choice.

tools.name: time_script
tools.description: How long a script takes to say, and when each word lands, without recording anything or sending it anywhere. Uses the computer’s own voice silently, so it always works, costs nothing, and is the cheap way to check a script fits a shot before paying anyone to voice it.

text.description: The script to time.

tools.name: render_timeline
tools.description: Render the whole timeline to a file: animation and caption layers are rendered to alpha first, then ffmpeg composites them over the footage and mixes the audio. mp4 = H.264+AAC; mov = ProRes 4444+PCM with alpha; webm = VP9+Opus. Takes seconds to minutes; run check_timeline first.

format.description: Default mp4.

quality.description: CRF for mp4/webm, lower is better. Default 20.

timelineId.description: Open this timeline first (id from list_timelines).

tools.name: save_frame
tools.description: Grab one frame into the asset library as a PNG: "footage" takes the exact source frame of the footage under the playhead (or timeSeconds); "composite" takes the whole stacked frame — footage, overlays, captions. Use it in a clip with : freeze frames, before/after, a still to draw over.

timeSeconds.description: Timeline time. Defaults to the playhead.

source.description: Default "footage".

name.description: A name for the asset file, e.g. "L4-ultima-fila". Default: the footage name and time.

timelineId.description: Open this timeline first (id from list_timelines).

tools.name: set_keyframe
tools.description: Make a value different at two moments and the editor draws the line between: where the layer sits (offsetX, offsetY), how big it is (scale) and how solid (opacity). Times are the *item's own*, counted from its start, so trimming its head does not re-time the move inside it. Leave value out to key whatever the item is at right now. Rotation cannot be keyframed — turning changes the size of the box a layer needs, and a box that changed size every frame would make the placement arithmetic time-varying everywhere.

itemId.description: Item id from get_timeline.

atSeconds.description: Where, in the item's own time (0 = its start). Defaults to the playhead.

value.description: What it should be there. Defaults to what it is now.

ease.description: How it leaves this key. ease slows in and out, linear is a straight line, hold stays put until the next. Default ease.

tools.name: list_keyframes
tools.description: Every keyframe on an item, per property, in the item's own time.

itemId.description: Item id from get_timeline.

tools.name: clear_keyframes
tools.description: Remove keyframes from an item — one property, or all of them. It goes back to standing still at whatever its plain values are.

itemId.description: Item id from get_timeline.

property.description: Leave out to clear every property.

tools.name: freeze_frame
tools.description: Hold one frame: save it to Assets and place it on the timeline as a still. A freeze is a picture of a shot rather than a property of it, so what you get is an ordinary image item — it trims, moves, scales, turns and renders like any other.

atSeconds.description: Which moment. Defaults to the playhead.

source.description: composite = everything the preview shows; footage = the raw shot with no overlays. Default composite.

tools.name: add_marker
tools.description: Pin a moment on the timeline — a beat to cut on, a mistake to come back to, the top of a section. Markers belong to the timeline rather than to any item, because what they usually mark is the join between two, and a note on either would go when that one was trimmed. Dropping one on a moment that already has a marker renames it instead of stacking two.

label.description: What happens here.

tools.name: get_space
tools.description: Read the active floor (dimensions, object IDs and footprints, robot settings; floor reads another in full without switching to it), the building (every floor with its level and x/z position in building metres), the current simulation summary and revision. Parts leave out fields at their default (rotation 0, y 0, blocks as the kind, no tags). partFingerprints supplies exact saved-part fingerprints for apply_changes floors.patch[].base.parts; use them instead of hashing the compact parts. building.spaceHash fingerprints the layout process results depend on; processResult says whether the last one is stale (computed for another layout). detail=summary gives every floor in brief without parts; detail=full every floor in full; select reads only some parts of a large floor (by id, kind, tag, group or a rectangle). persistence reports browser autosave status/reason and whether the last named browser project holds this exact snapshot; storage status does not change revision. If autosave failed, save_local_project can keep a complete named copy, then read persistence.namedLocal=current to confirm. Read summary/full before understanding an unfamiliar space; use detail=status for lightweight revision, busy, Undo/Redo, persistence, activeFloor, spaceHash and latest result/playback checks once its inputs are known. status cannot be combined with floor or select and omits geometry, catalogs, quantities and checks. Does not expose chat, account data or source images.

detail.description: status: revision, busy, Undo/Redo, persistence, activeFloor, spaceHash and latest process result/playback status only; no geometry, catalog or checks. Use summary/full to understand a space not yet read. summary: floors, part counts, zones, groups, connections and scenario IDs, without parts; floor (default): the active floor in full (or floor); full: every floor in full.

floor.description: With detail=floor: this floor area in full instead of the active one (its parts, checks and quantities). Does not switch the editor.

select.description: With detail=floor: only the parts that match, for a large floor. A part matches when it is in ids, or passes every other filter given (kinds and tags and groups and within). The room itself (size, outline, holes) stays whole; selection says how many matched of how many, and names ids not found. The part catalog, capabilities and limits are left out (get_part_catalog and detail=floor without select have them).

ids.description: These parts, whatever the other filters say.

kinds.description: Parts of any of these kinds (wall, rack, table…).

tags.description: Parts carrying any of these tags.

groups.description: Parts in any of these groups.

within.description: Parts whose footprint reaches into this rectangle (floor metres, top-left corner and size).

tools.name: get_space_quantities
tools.description: Areas and quantities of the drawn model: each floor area (outline less holes), each zone on the floor (turned and polygon zones exactly; the part off the floor reported apart), zoned and unzoned area, areas by tag (the union of the tagged zones) and by marking kind (parking, lawns, roads), part counts by kind (walls, partitions and fences with their length), and totals by level, building of the site, use (space type) and the whole site. definitions says how overlapping zones are counted: once in totals and tags, in full in each zone row. floor limits the floor rows to one area; totals stay whole. Square metres to 0.01. When editable solids exist, floors also report solids with ideal analytic closed volume, transformed bounds, decoration status and exact-prism/unsupported-3d analysis; this does not add decorative volume to floor area or claim curved mesh and ideal volume are identical. Read-only; free; no AI call. It measures the drawing, not a legal floor area.

floor.description: Only this floor area’s rows; every floor when left out.

tools.name: get_part_catalog
tools.description: Search basic parts, size presets and grouped sets by use and name. Sizes are illustrative metres, not certified product specifications. Place a result with edit_space.place using its item ID. These create static parts, not process resources or floor connections. Round appearances still use the stored collision footprint. Free; no AI API or simulation is called. source=saved_assemblies reads the active account/workspace browser library when this host supports it; list returns metadata, id returns one closed editable pack. Large packs use content.data chunks: retain assetRevision and pass nextContentOffset as contentOffset; concatenate and verify sha256. A changed revision is refused. Unavailable is an error; this tool never saves or deletes library entries.

id.description: Get one exact item, including every component.

limit.description: Items per call: up to 200, the whole library at once.

tools.name: check_space
tools.description: Deterministic geometry check of the requested floor area (floor, else the active one): overlapping obstacles and passages narrower than minClearance (turned and polygonal parts exactly, by their outlines), doors lying across a wall instead of along it (door_not_in_wall, which opens nothing), parts in front of a door on either side (door_blocked), parts people are routed under lower than the headroom they need (low_headroom), connection ends inside a part in the way or off the floor (link_end_blocked, link_end_off_floor), parts off a shaped floor (outside_outline), zones the saved scenarios go to whose goto point parts close off from the rest of the zone (zone_center_enclosed, as a run warns anchor.enclosed; use a spot), and, on a floor with a gate, zones a pedestrian (radius 0.3 m, height 1.7 m, every connection) cannot reach from any gate (zone_unreachable, with the route failure reason), with object IDs and a bounding rectangle. Zones are ignored otherwise unless they block, but a zone tagged passage or egress holds every gap across it to passageClearance. Gaps inside one group or between parked vehicles are not walkways: counted in excludedGaps (gaps=all lists them). Parts hung above head height neither narrow nor block a walkway. With reach.agent.oneWayPassages, exact opening IDs select forward/backward against physical passageHeading (at most 64 unique floor/part pairs); real endpoints on their finite plane are refused and wall/body clearance still applies. The default pedestrian has no scenario direction rules. With reach, it also routes one agent (a pedestrian unless given) from one place to up to 20 others through every floor and connection, as run_process_scenario routes a goto, and returns reach[]: reachable, lengthMetres (null when not), reason (no-path, link-not-allowed, link-blocked, floor-too-large, too-many-route-nodes, anchor-blocked, anchor-missing, oneway-endpoint; null when reachable) and links (connections taken, or those concerned). For a door or exit (an object that is a door, gate or a small part tagged exit or entrance) reach[] also gives doorWidth, effectiveWidth (the narrowest clear width a pedestrian has across the doorway on the way in or out: less than doorWidth when parts stand in front of it, 0 when shut; a route only has to touch the door, so reachable stays true for a doorway that is mostly blocked) and blockedBy; when effectiveWidth is under the smaller of the door’s own width and doorClearance, reach[].narrowed says so and it is listed as a critical door_narrowed finding (left out where door_blocked already names that door). Geometry only: no queues, capacities or times. Routing works on floors of any size (beyond 120 m on a coarser route graph). With floors ("all" or a list of floor IDs) instead of floor, it checks every one of those areas in one call and answers per floor: counts by issue type, the first issuesPerFloor issues, and notChecked for areas left over when the time budget ran out (check those next). Each finding also carries severity (critical: a door or exit closed or a route cut; major; minor), where and nearest (words and the nearest wall, door or exit and zone), and for gaps, overlaps and door fronts a rough hint/suggest (which part to move which way, at least how far: a guide, not a solution); findings come most serious first. A door set in a gap of the wall and a small part tagged exit or entrance keep their front clear like a wall door, and a gap at the room edge names the door or exit at it. A note first says how many gaps are not shown. Read-only; free; no AI call. Whether the drawing matches the real site is not checked.

floor.description: Floor area to inspect; defaults to the active area. Does not switch the editor.

floors.description: Instead of floor: check several floor areas in one call, "all" or a list of floor IDs. Each floor is summarized: counts by issue type and its first issuesPerFloor issues.

issuesPerFloor.description: With floors: the issues listed for each floor (20 when left out); the counts cover them all. Lists are shortened further when the whole answer would pass 1 MB.

minClearance.description: Report passages narrower than this many metres.

gaps.description: walkways (the default): narrow gaps inside one group of furniture or equipment, and between parked vehicles (cars, trucks, bicycles, forklifts, carts, trolleys, roll cages, robots, aircraft), are an assembly or parking, not walkways: counted in excludedGaps and not listed. all: list them too, each with its context.

passageTags.description: Tags that make a zone a passage people must be able to use (passage and egress when left out): every gap across it is held to passageClearance, in a group or not.

passageClearance.description: Width a passage zone keeps clear, metres: 1.2 when left out (a corridor with rooms on one side under Japan’s Building Standard Law; the IBC asks 1.12 m).

doorClearance.description: Depth kept clear on both sides of a door, metres: 0.9 when left out (a door leaf’s sweep); 1.22 to 1.52 for a wheelchair user’s approach (ADA §404.2.4.1).

headroom.description: Headroom people need under a raised part they are routed under, metres: 2.03 when left out (ADA §307.4, IBC §1003.3.1).

reach.description: Route check through the building (all floors and connections) as a process goto would take it: whether each place can be reached, the route length, and why not.

agent.description: Who goes; a pedestrian (radius 0.3, height 1.7, every connection) when left out.

oneWayPassages.description: Building-graph goto/pool crossings of named wall openings (not straight-distance move or simulate_space): [{floor, object, direction: "forward" | "backward"}]. Forward follows the opening passageHeading; backward opposes it. Exact IDs, at most 64, no duplicates. Real endpoints on a governed opening plane are invalid; physical clearance still applies.

height.description: Metres; parts raised at least this high are passed under.

links.description: Connection kinds the agent may use, and no others (a robot that cannot take stairs or escalators lists passage and elevator: passage is corridors and ramps).

recall.description: The place this job remembered under the name (goto only): a goto or an arrival with remember stored it.

spot.description: Stand at one of the spots inside a zone part (0.8 m apart) instead of its centre: random, or free (one nobody else is at or on the way to).

within.description: With a tag, in a goto: only its parts on the floor area the job is on (floor), on its level of the same building (level: the hall of the storey it is on), or in its building (structure; the ground when it is in none).

side.description: Stand beside a part that is in the way on this side instead of the nearest free point: north (towards smaller z), south, east or west on the plan; or front (the side it faces: a counter’s customer side, a machine’s working side) or back, for parts with a front (get_part_catalog front: true), turning with the part.

open.description: Only the first n parts with the tag (building order: floor, then part id) are candidates: the open tills.

from.description: Where from: {"object": id}, {"tag": t} (its first part), {"point": {x, z}} (on the checked floor area; add "floor": id for another) or {"link": id, "end": "from" | "to"}.

recall.description: The place this job remembered under the name (goto only): a goto or an arrival with remember stored it.

spot.description: Stand at one of the spots inside a zone part (0.8 m apart) instead of its centre: random, or free (one nobody else is at or on the way to).

within.description: With a tag, in a goto: only its parts on the floor area the job is on (floor), on its level of the same building (level: the hall of the storey it is on), or in its building (structure; the ground when it is in none).

side.description: Stand beside a part that is in the way on this side instead of the nearest free point: north (towards smaller z), south, east or west on the plan; or front (the side it faces: a counter’s customer side, a machine’s working side) or back, for parts with a front (get_part_catalog front: true), turning with the part.

open.description: Only the first n parts with the tag (building order: floor, then part id) are candidates: the open tills.

to.description: Places to reach; a tag takes its nearest part, a point without floor is on the checked floor area.

tools.name: create_space
tools.description: Replace the active floor with an editable 3D space; other floors of the building stay as they are, and so do the building’s name and the floor’s underlay. To start afresh in a tab that holds another project, give fresh: true (a new project of this one space; the chat stays). Neither fresh nor a plain replacement drops parts the user locked: the call is refused with code locked_parts, naming them and the ways on (export_project first, or create the space on a new floor area, or, only when the user asks, unlock them). Parts are boxes with a height (optionally turned by rotation, raised by y, or given a polygon footprint), not a mesh. Object IDs, labels and heights can be omitted. addArray places a prepared box or polygon part in a two-direction array without listing every cell. Robot settings/stations get illustrative defaults. Clears previous simulation results; Undo restores the previous space. Simulation requires an explicit simulation tool call within the account’s current access. No application AI API call.

expectedRevision.description: Use revision from the most recent get_space or successful edit.

width.description: Metres along x; taken from the outline when one is given.

depth.description: Metres along z; taken from the outline when one is given.

outline.description: The floor boundary as a simple polygon, corners in order (either winding), metres. Its bounding box becomes width × depth: it is moved to the origin, and parts and stations move with it. Parts are not clipped to it; check_space reports those outside it.

holes.description: Openings in the floor (an atrium, a courtyard), each a simple polygon inside the outline, apart from each other. [] removes them.

scaleConfirmed.description: Ignored: only the user confirms dimensions, with the Measured box in the editor. A new or resized space is unconfirmed.

solid.description: Closed editable solid v1. Profile u/v are 0..1: extrusion section (axis y: x/z, axis x: z/y, axis z: x/y); revolve radius/height. w/d/h are reference dimensions. Mirror around reference-box centre, then right-handed X→Y→Z degree rotations around that centre, then outer plan rotation and placement. Partial revolutions (0.1..359.9 degrees) have closed end caps; exactly 360 is a full turn. No holes. Curves use deterministic 64 segments/full turn. blocks:false explicitly marks decoration; unsupported blocking 3D geometry cannot be used as a routing proxy.

rotation.description: Degrees counter-clockwise on the plan about the centre of the box; 0 when omitted. x/z/w/d stay the unrotated box. A multiple of 90° is stored as the turned box (w/d swapped for a quarter turn) without rotation, the turn of a part with a front kept in facing.

passageHeading.description: Physical positive normal of a rectangular door/dock_door/gate in its canonical box frame, degrees (-180,180]; effective heading adds rotation. 0 toward +x, 90 toward -z. Permission is selected per agent by oneWayPassages.

facing.description: Which way a part with a front (catalog front: true, e.g. chairs, vehicles, stairs, toilets) faces within its box: the quarter or half turn, degrees counter-clockwise on the plan, that a rotation of 90°, 180° or -90° left; 0 when omitted: front toward +z (south); 90 toward +x (east), 180 or -180 toward -z (north), -90 or 270 toward -x (west). Set it to turn the front without moving the box; rotation, turn and rotate turn the front with the box. Display only; other kinds ignore it.

y.description: Elevation of the underside above the floor, metres; 0 when omitted.

footprint.description: Polygon base as {x,z} vertices in the unrotated box (0..w, 0..d), 3-32, no self-crossing, spanning the whole box; the box when omitted.

blocks.description: Whether the part blocks movement; overrides the kind default.

accent.description: A second colour 0xRRGGBB for the members drawn apart: a rack's beams (its posts keep the structure colour), a sign's face, a door's leaf. Display only.

doorType.description: How a door opens, for its plan symbol and 3D picture: hinged (one leaf, the default), double, sliding, automatic (two sliding leaves) or revolving. Doors and gates only; display only.

text.description: Words shown on it: a sign or menu board carries them on its face, a floor marking (zone, parking, road, sidewalk, lawn, rug) painted on the floor. Display only.

symbol.description: A symbol painted on a floor marking: arrow (along its length, turned with it), wheelchair (the accessible bay sign), crosswalk (zebra stripes across its length), bays (parking bay lines every 2.5 m along its length) or hatch (a no-go area). Floor markings only; display only.

tags.description: Up to 8 tags, each /^[a-z0-9_-]{1,24}$/, for scenarios to refer to.

source.description: Where its position and size come from: drawing (read off a plan), measured (on site) or assumed (a typical size, or hidden in the drawing). Display only: not part of any calculation.

note.description: A note for whoever checks the model (what was assumed, what to confirm on site), up to 300 characters; not drawn on the plan and not part of any calculation.

polygon.description: Instead of x/z/w/d: the corners of the part on the floor, in order, metres (3-32, no self-crossing); x, z, w, d and the footprint are derived from them, unturned.

items.description: A prepared part. Give kind and the minimum x/z corner; omit w/d/h to use the part size listed in get_space.parts. Or give polygon (corners on the floor) instead of x/z/w/d for a part of any outline.

solid.description: Closed editable solid v1. Profile u/v are 0..1: extrusion section (axis y: x/z, axis x: z/y, axis z: x/y); revolve radius/height. w/d/h are reference dimensions. Mirror around reference-box centre, then right-handed X→Y→Z degree rotations around that centre, then outer plan rotation and placement. Partial revolutions (0.1..359.9 degrees) have closed end caps; exactly 360 is a full turn. No holes. Curves use deterministic 64 segments/full turn. blocks:false explicitly marks decoration; unsupported blocking 3D geometry cannot be used as a routing proxy.

part.description: The part to repeat. Omit part.id: each cell needs a distinct ID. Set idPrefix on the array to choose stable IDs. Give x/z or polygon as for an ordinary part.

rowStep.description: Metres from one row or column to the next; diagonal steps are allowed.

columnStep.description: Metres from one row or column to the next; diagonal steps are allowed.

idPrefix.description: IDs of the cells, row by row: prefix-1, prefix-2, …; generated when omitted.

items.description: Place a part at every row/column offset from part.x/z (or shift every corner of part.polygon). The first cell is at the supplied position; rows and columns include it. IDs are generated, or idPrefix-1, idPrefix-2, … row by row. In part.label, {n} becomes the cell number and {row}/{column} its row and column (from 1): "Shelf {n}", "Seat {row}-{column}".

fresh.description: Start a new project with this space, named after it: the other floors, the underlays, scenarios, saved options and comparisons, the latest run and named views go (one Undo brings them back); the chat and the display settings stay. Without it only the active floor is replaced.

operationId.description: Your own unique name for this change, such as a UUID; optional. Sending the same call again with the same operationId returns the earlier result (replayed: true) instead of applying it twice, and get_operation tells whether it applied. Use a new one for each new change.

requestGroupId.description: Attach this live edit to an open request group. Requires a fixed operationId and the current owned expectedRevision. Only the advertised five editing tools support groups.

tools.name: edit_space
tools.description: Edit several objects and room dimensions of one floor (floor, else the active one; or the same edit on several with floors) in one atomic change. room width and depth grow or shrink the floor on its +x and +z sides (east and south); its parts and holes keep their places unless scaleContents. Order: room, remove, update, move, rotate (90°), turn (any angle), align, distribute, rotateSelection, copy, copySelection, copyArray, add, addArray, walls, openings, group. assemblies edits floor-local definitions and instances, typed parameters and sparse component overrides; detach explicitly turns an instance into ordinary parts. Read scene.modelAssemblies and use assemblyPartId/provenance from the kit. Generated parts reject ordinary updates/copies; use assemblies overrides or detach first. Surviving generated IDs are stable when arrays change; references to disappearing IDs must be retargeted in the same apply_changes. Selection operations take explicit object IDs. Updates need only an existing ID and changed fields. Add prepared parts by kind and position; sizes default to get_space.parts. For a part of any outline (an L-shaped counter, a round column), give add[].polygon: its corners on the floor instead of x/z/w/d. addArray creates a two-direction array of one prepared part; copyArray repeats an existing assembly across rows and columns. Draw slanted walls with walls and put their doors with openings rather than computing angles and corners. Coordinates are metres. Invalid edits leave the space unchanged. The result gives the new revision, changes (the part IDs added, removed and changed), the scene of the active floor, checks (counts of the quick checks of the floor that was edited: overlaps, narrow passages, doors blocked and so on; check_space gives the IDs, severity and hints) with checksFloor naming that floor, and the building in brief; result=brief leaves the scene out. After editing another floor, scene stays the active floor, checks and checksFloor are still the edited floor’s (editedFloor.checks repeats them), activeFloorChecks gives the active floor’s counts, and editedFloor gives the edited one (id, scene, changes, checks). With floors, editedFloors[].checks is each floor’s. Stations stay put unless explicitly supplied or autoPlaceStations=true. Editing does not run a simulation; call simulate_space explicitly when authorized.

assemblies.description: Edit floor-local assembly definitions/instances, typed parameters and component overrides; detach explicitly makes regular parts. Generated parts cannot be edited directly.

solid.description: Closed editable solid v1. Profile u/v are 0..1: extrusion section (axis y: x/z, axis x: z/y, axis z: x/y); revolve radius/height. w/d/h are reference dimensions. Mirror around reference-box centre, then right-handed X→Y→Z degree rotations around that centre, then outer plan rotation and placement. Partial revolutions (0.1..359.9 degrees) have closed end caps; exactly 360 is a full turn. No holes. Curves use deterministic 64 segments/full turn. blocks:false explicitly marks decoration; unsupported blocking 3D geometry cannot be used as a routing proxy.

rotation.description: Degrees counter-clockwise on the plan about the centre of the box; 0 when omitted. x/z/w/d stay the unrotated box. A multiple of 90° is stored as the turned box (w/d swapped for a quarter turn) without rotation, the turn of a part with a front kept in facing.

passageHeading.description: Physical positive normal of a rectangular door/dock_door/gate in its canonical box frame, degrees (-180,180]; effective heading adds rotation. 0 toward +x, 90 toward -z. Permission is selected per agent by oneWayPassages.

facing.description: Which way a part with a front (catalog front: true, e.g. chairs, vehicles, stairs, toilets) faces within its box: the quarter or half turn, degrees counter-clockwise on the plan, that a rotation of 90°, 180° or -90° left; 0 when omitted: front toward +z (south); 90 toward +x (east), 180 or -180 toward -z (north), -90 or 270 toward -x (west). Set it to turn the front without moving the box; rotation, turn and rotate turn the front with the box. Display only; other kinds ignore it.

y.description: Elevation of the underside above the floor, metres; 0 when omitted.

footprint.description: Polygon base as {x,z} vertices in the unrotated box (0..w, 0..d), 3-32, no self-crossing, spanning the whole box; the box when omitted.

blocks.description: Whether the part blocks movement; overrides the kind default.

accent.description: A second colour 0xRRGGBB for the members drawn apart: a rack's beams (its posts keep the structure colour), a sign's face, a door's leaf. Display only.

doorType.description: How a door opens, for its plan symbol and 3D picture: hinged (one leaf, the default), double, sliding, automatic (two sliding leaves) or revolving. Doors and gates only; display only.

text.description: Words shown on it: a sign or menu board carries them on its face, a floor marking (zone, parking, road, sidewalk, lawn, rug) painted on the floor. Display only.

symbol.description: A symbol painted on a floor marking: arrow (along its length, turned with it), wheelchair (the accessible bay sign), crosswalk (zebra stripes across its length), bays (parking bay lines every 2.5 m along its length) or hatch (a no-go area). Floor markings only; display only.

tags.description: Up to 8 tags, each /^[a-z0-9_-]{1,24}$/, for scenarios to refer to.

source.description: Where its position and size come from: drawing (read off a plan), measured (on site) or assumed (a typical size, or hidden in the drawing). Display only: not part of any calculation.

note.description: A note for whoever checks the model (what was assumed, what to confirm on site), up to 300 characters; not drawn on the plan and not part of any calculation.

expectedRevision.description: Use revision from the most recent get_space or successful edit.

result.description: What the result gives of the edited floor: scene (every part, with the IDs the edit made) or brief (only the IDs added, removed and changed, and its checks), for large floors.

preview.description: Check the proposed edit without applying it: returns the proposed floor and geometry issues. If it meets the user’s requirements, repeat with preview=false and the latest revision to apply it.

floor.description: Floor id (get_space.building.floors) to edit; the active floor when omitted. Another floor is edited in place and stays inactive.

floors.description: The same edit on several floors at once, instead of floor: typical floors copied from one another share part IDs, so an update of 'corridor' widens it on every storey listed. All of them change or none, as one Undo step; the result gives each floor's checks. Not with preview.

skipMissing.description: With floors: on a floor that lacks a part the edit names, leave out what names it (an update, a removal, a move, an opening on that wall; the ID from a list) instead of refusing the whole edit, and list the IDs left out per floor. For storeys whose parts differ (a ground floor with a lobby under typical floors).

outline.description: A new floor boundary (see create_space.outline); [] returns to the width × depth rectangle (null does too). The holes move with it; holes given in the same edit are in the same frame as the outline and move with it too. Resizing an outlined floor with width/depth scales the outline with it; its holes, like its parts, keep their places unless scaleContents (a site grown to the south or east keeps the holes under its buildings).

holes.description: Openings in the floor (an atrium, a courtyard), each a simple polygon inside the outline, apart from each other. [] removes them.

scaleConfirmed.description: Ignored: only the user confirms dimensions, with the Measured box in the editor. A new or resized space is unconfirmed.

scaleContents.description: When resizing, proportionally scale floor positions and footprints; heights stay unchanged. Otherwise only room bounds change.

items.description: A prepared part. Give kind and the minimum x/z corner; omit w/d/h to use the part size listed in get_space.parts. Or give polygon (corners on the floor) instead of x/z/w/d for a part of any outline.

place.description: Place catalog items, including complete sets, in this same atomic edit. x/z is the minimum corner of the complete rotated bounds, in metres. Sizes are preserved; oversized sets are rejected. Sets get a new group unless group is specified. Use preview=true to check the proposal first.

item.description: Catalog ID from get_part_catalog: a basic part, size preset, or reusable set.

addArray.description: Place prepared parts in a two-direction array in one edit; supports boxes and polygon prisms. Each cell gets a unique ID.

part.description: The part to repeat. Omit part.id: each cell needs a distinct ID. Set idPrefix on the array to choose stable IDs. Give x/z or polygon as for an ordinary part.

rowStep.description: Metres from one row or column to the next; diagonal steps are allowed.

columnStep.description: Metres from one row or column to the next; diagonal steps are allowed.

idPrefix.description: IDs of the cells, row by row: prefix-1, prefix-2, …; generated when omitted.

items.description: Place a part at every row/column offset from part.x/z (or shift every corner of part.polygon). The first cell is at the supplied position; rows and columns include it. IDs are generated, or idPrefix-1, idPrefix-2, … row by row. In part.label, {n} becomes the cell number and {row}/{column} its row and column (from 1): "Shelf {n}", "Seat {row}-{column}".

update.description: Change fields of existing objects by ID. null takes passageHeading, rotation, facing, y, footprint, blocks, color, group or tags back to the default, and footprint [] makes a polygon part its box again. A rotation given sets the whole turn of a part with a front, its facing included (rotation 180 again leaves it as it is). Objects with locked: true stay unchanged unless the same update sets locked: false (only when the user asks).

solid.description: null removes the recipe; change kind away from solid in the same update.

Set it to turn the front without moving the box; rotation, turn and rotate turn the front with the box. Display only; other kinds ignore it. null faces the part the way its kind is drawn.

y.description: Elevation of the underside above the floor, metres; 0 when omitted. null puts it back on the floor.

blocks.description: Whether the part blocks movement; overrides the kind default. null returns to the kind's default.

color.description: null returns to the kind's colour.

material.description: null removes the PBR material assignment.

accent.description: A second colour 0xRRGGBB for the members drawn apart: a rack's beams (its posts keep the structure colour), a sign's face, a door's leaf. Display only.
