tools.description: The page of postext.dev on screen, its language and theme, the languages the site is in, its main sections and every page of the documentation. postext.dev documents Postext, an open-source layout engine that sets Markdown as books, magazines and textbooks in the browser; its Sandbox (/sandbox) is the editor, and offers its own tools (sandbox_*) while it is the page on screen.

tools.name: site_search
tools.description: Search the documentation and the Cookbook of postext.dev in the language on screen: sections of the docs and recipes that match the words, each with its path (to read with site_read_page or open with site_open_page) and the passage that matched. Setting names (bodyText.avoidOrphans), Markdown directives (::resource) and plain questions all work as queries.

language.description: The language (the one on screen when left out).

limit.description: Most results of each kind (default 8).

tools.name: site_read_page
tools.description: The text of a page of postext.dev as Markdown — a documentation page (/docs/configuration-text, /docs/document-format), a recipe (/cookbook/<slug>), the glossary, the home page (/) — without leaving the page on screen. Long pages come in parts: pass the offset the answer gives to read on.

path.description: The page's path, e.g. /docs/sandbox.

language.description: The language (the one on screen when left out).

offset.description: Character to start from, to read a long page on.

tools.name: site_open_page
tools.description: Show a page of postext.dev to the reader: the home page (/), a documentation page (/docs/<page>, with #heading to land on a section), the Cookbook (/cookbook, or /cookbook?q=words to show it filtered), a recipe (/cookbook/<slug>), the glossary (/glossary#<term>), the Sandbox (/sandbox). The tools on offer follow the page: the Sandbox's appear once it is on screen.

path.description: The page's path.

language.description: The language (the one on screen when left out).

tools.name: site_list_recipes
tools.description: The recipes of the Postext Cookbook: each solves one layout problem (a drop cap, a table that breaks across pages, a bilingual page, a comic strip) and comes with its Markdown, its settings and the pages they produce. Lists them by chapter, or only those of one chapter or matching some words, with the question each one answers and its path.

query.description: Words the recipe's title, question or summary must contain.

chapter.description: Only the recipes of this chapter (its id or number, as the answer's chapters give them).

language.description: The language (the one on screen when left out).

limit.description: Most recipes to list (default 60).

tools.name: site_open_recipe_in_sandbox
tools.description: Open a Cookbook recipe in the Sandbox as a book the reader can edit — its Markdown, settings, resources and fonts — so its technique can be tried and changed. The recipe is imported as a project the first time; later the reader's copy opens, edits included.

slug.description: The recipe's slug, as site_list_recipes gives it.

language.description: The language (the one on screen when left out).

tools.name: site_lookup_term
tools.description: What a typographic or typesetting term means, from the site's glossary: widow, orphan, runt, leading, kerning, baseline grid, kinsoku, tate-chu-yoko, kashida, and the abbreviations the documentation uses. Matches the term, part of it, or its form in another of the site's languages.

term.description: The term, or part of it.

language.description: The language (the one on screen when left out).

tools.name: site_set_preferences
tools.description: Switch the site (the Sandbox's interface included) to another of its languages, staying on the same page, or between the light and the dark theme. The choice is remembered by the reader's browser.

language.description: The language to switch the site to.

postext.dev.blurb: Sandbox get state, Sandbox render page and Sandbox inspect pages.
postext.dev.name: Postext

tools.name: cad.new_project
tools.description: Create and open one fresh Cadding project for this agent session. Repeated calls reuse the same editor project. Set forceNew only when the user explicitly asks for another separate project.

forceNew.description: Create another separate project instead of reusing the current agent editor. Use only when the user explicitly requests a new additional project.

tools.name: cad.open_editor
tools.description: Open a fresh public Cadding editor project. This compatibility alias behaves like cad.new_project.

tools.name: cad.get_editor_link
tools.description: Return a shareable Cadding link. For a guest browser scene, persist a copy as an account-free MCP editor link; signed-in account-project sharing remains available through the Share UI.

tools.name: cad.add_shape
tools.description: Create one primitive part. The primitive kind is the shape parameter; tube and ring are not operations. Sphere, hemisphere, and cylinder are the starting mass for curved shells that later boolean_parts will isolate — do not skip them in favor of a planar extrude when the body is not flat.

shape.description: Primitive shape. Use hollow_cylinder for a tube and torus for a ring.

name.description: Display name for the new part.

parameters.description: Shape-specific dimensions and controls. Use the keys documented by the selected shape. For ring/torus: majorRadiusMm, minorRadiusMm, axis ("z" for flat on plate), and optional Sweep arc (radians) or arcDeg — 2π/360 full, 3π/2/270 three-quarter, π/180 half, π/2/90 quarter.

positionMm.description: Exact CAD position [x, y, z] in millimeters.

rotationDeg.description: Exact CAD rotation [x, y, z] in degrees.

parentPartId.description: Optional GROUP id to nest under. It must resolve to type=group; never pass a solid enclosure/body id because that makes the child a boolean operand and destroys separate appearance. Use boolean_parts for real unions/subtractions. When replacing a nested body, pass its deleted parent only when that parent is a group.

tools.name: cad.add_tube_between
tools.description: Create a straight tube whose local axis is automatically oriented from startMm to endMm in the fixed CAD frame (+Z up). Use this for handles, pipes, axles, struts, and cable runs when a bent sweep is unnecessary. Do not manually guess Euler rotationDeg.

startMm.description: CAD start point {x,y,z} or [x,y,z] in millimeters.

endMm.description: CAD end point {x,y,z} or [x,y,z] in millimeters.

wallThicknessMm.description: Wall thickness in millimeters. Omit or set 0 for a solid rod.

componentId.description: Opaque owner/component ID for deterministic coverage tracking.

parentPartId.description: Optional GROUP id to nest under.

tools.name: cad.add_construction
tools.description: Create one editable, reusable construction family as a coherent parametric part tree. This is the preferred fast path for common mechanical roots such as shells, brackets, hole patterns, bosses, bushings, shafts, wheels, clamps, hinges, lids, snap-fits, threads, adapters, rails, gears, pulleys, bearing holders, knobs, hooks, and flanges. Dimensions inside parameters are millimeters. The result stays editable through its Construction parameters. Hole Pattern creates subtractive cutter geometry; use boolean_parts mode=subtract to apply it to a host.

family.description: Construction family. Use get_construction_catalog(family) when exact parameters or option values are not already known.

name.description: Optional Layers name for this family instance.

parameters.description: Family-specific parameters. All dimensional values, including position arrays inside structured fields, are millimeters; angles are degrees; counts and ratios are unitless.

positionMm.description: Exact instance position [x, y, z] in millimeters. Omit for safe automatic placement.

rotationDeg.description: Exact instance rotation [x, y, z] in degrees.

placementFrame.description: Optional placement frame with positionMm/originMm and rotationDeg. Top-level positionMm/rotationDeg win.

targetPartId.description: Optional related target part. The relationship is recorded for later CAD operations; geometry is not silently fused or cut. Use boolean_parts or assemble explicitly.

targetFace.description: Optional target face identifier associated with targetPartId.

parentPartId.description: Optional GROUP id to nest the new family under.

tools.name: cad.add_robot_part
tools.description: Create one of the verified robotics building blocks. Dimensions inside parameters are millimeters; hole positions are millimeter pairs. These are intentionally simple parts for reliable AI assembly planning.

tools.name: cad.add_profile_shape
tools.description: Create geometry from a profile, sketch, image trace, revolve, sweep, or loft. method=trace_image is only for a user-requested trace of a verified orthographic/planar true prism; extrude is only for a true prism (both large faces planar AND parallel, thickness = one extrude axis). Do not trace a general perspective product photo as a substitute for reconstructing its 3D form. Do not flatten a cupped wall into an extruded 2D outline, and do not fake a lean with extra rotationDeg — that mapping is sketch-plane onto CAD axes only (typically 90° about one axis). Circular-pattern phase belongs on pattern_parts. Curved shells use method=revolve or loft, or add_shape primitives plus boolean_parts. Prefer add_shape cylinder|truncatedCone|tube (or shell_part) when the axisymmetric wall is constant radius or a single linear taper with a coaxial bore — do not invent a custom revolve meridian or high radialSegments for that case. For a vessel with a genuinely changing meridian, use revolve with an outer meridian only, shell="hollow", openTop=true, openBottom=false, wallThicknessMm, and radialSegments ≤ 64; do not use a primary mouth cutter. For a handle/grip/loop/spout, use sweep with either absolute pathPointsMm or startMm/endMm plus optional viaPointsMm, pathMode="curve", profileKind="circle", tubeRadiusMm, and endpoints penetrating the host; do not follow that authored sweep with a generic mate_parts call.

method.description: Construction method. trace_image requires an explicit user trace request and a verified orthographic/planar true-prism view; extrude also requires a true prism (planar AND parallel large faces). For ordinary perspective reference images, reconstruct the full visible 3D form instead. extrude/sketch_extrude requires parameters.profilePointsMm, segments, or profilePreset on the call. Extra rotationDeg is not a substitute for curvature; pattern phase is pattern_parts, not the prototype. If the wall cups, use revolve/loft or add_shape + boolean_parts. Use sweep for a constant-section member along a bent 3D path. Prefer parameters.startMm + parameters.endMm + optional parameters.viaPointsMm for a simple handle; use parameters.pathPointsMm for a multi-waypoint route. All points are absolute CAD x=right,y=front/back,z=up millimeters. Use pathMode=curve for an intentional smooth bend, profileKind=circle|rect, and tubeRadiusMm or rectWidthMm/rectDepthMm. Authored sweep endpoints should contact the host directly, so generic mate_parts is normally unnecessary and unsafe.

name.description: Display name for the new part.

guideMode.description: Loft guide interpolation. Use spline with guidePointsMm for a smooth centripetal spline rail; omit it or use polyline for straight station interpolation.

parameters.description: Method-specific profile, path, section, and dimension data. Millimeter suffixes are authoritative. For method=extrude/sketch_extrude, set profilePlane="XY" for a top/footprint outline or "XZ" for a side/elevation outline (U/V map to the named CAD plane; extrudeDepthMm is perpendicular to that plane). For method=trace_image, require an explicit user trace request and a verified orthographic/planar true-prism view; only then set useReferenceImage=true and extrudeDepthMm (and optional referenceWidthMm/widthMm). For ordinary perspective product photos, reconstruct the 3D geometry instead of tracing. Use silhouettePrompt / isolateFromReference only to isolate one explicitly named component from a multi-object photo, or when no photo is attached and silhouette generation is explicitly requested. For method=revolve: parameters.segments is the visible outer wall as EDGES (Umm=radius from the spin axis, Vmm=height along CAD +Z), bottom→top. One line per straight run; arc/bezier (midUmm/midVmm on the curve) for blends; two meeting lines for a sharp corner. Do not sample a curve as many short lines (that lathes into stacked rings). Do not include the inner wall or axis-seal points — set shell/openTop/openBottom instead. Call-level radiusMm/axialHeightMm are envelope fallbacks only when segments are omitted.

positionMm.description: Exact CAD position [x, y, z] in millimeters.

rotationDeg.description: Exact CAD rotation [x, y, z] in degrees.

targetPartId.description: Optional host/body id for an attached sweep or other profile member. Use the exact live id from scene context or an explicit result alias such as "$handle"; never use latest-created/prototype order or a display name. This records the intended relationship; sweep endpoints still define the exact placement.

targetFace.description: Optional host face id for the attached profile member; inspect the host first and do not guess.

parentPartId.description: Optional GROUP id to nest under. It must resolve to type=group; never pass a solid enclosure/body id because that makes the child a boolean operand and destroys separate appearance. Use boolean_parts for real unions/subtractions. When replacing a nested body, pass its deleted parent only when that parent is a group.

tools.name: cad.inspect_part
tools.description: Read exact transform, dimensions, bounds, faces, face frames, edges, vertices, hierarchy, and editable parameters. Revolve and extrusion parts include profilePointsMm; loft parts include pointsAMm/pointsBMm and loftHeightMm for a later edit_part / set_dimensions reshape.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

tools.name: cad.get_scene
tools.description: Read every live part, hierarchy relationship, transform, dimensions, visibility, and stable ID in the current scene.

tools.name: cad.get_construction_catalog
tools.description: Read the authoritative construction-family defaults, units, options, and full parameter vocabulary before creating a precision family.

family.description: Optional family filter. Omit to list all families.

tools.name: cad.get_robot_part_catalog
tools.description: Read the verified robotics building-block catalog and millimeter defaults.

tools.name: cad.get_component_kit
tools.description: Read the required functional hardware and interface checklist for a production-oriented product profile. Use this before building a chair, robot, wallet, pen, or other multi-part product so connections, supports, retention, and cable interfaces are explicit.

product.description: Product profile. Omit for the universal hardware checklist.

tools.name: cad.get_mcmaster_catalog
tools.description: List curated preferred McMaster hardware (M3 screws, nuts, USB-C, etc.) plus any live-fetched cache. Not the full McMaster site — search by query (e.g. "m3 screw", "usb-c") then place with add_mcmaster_part.

query.description: Optional part number or name filter.

partNumber.description: Exact part number filter (alias of query).

partFamily.description: Optional physical family filter such as motor, connector, wheel, cable_harness, or fastener.

manufacturingClass.description: Optional acquisition filter such as purchased_component or cable_or_harness. McMaster items are normally purchased components, not printable geometry.

printability.description: Optional print filter. McMaster hardware normally returns not_applicable; use the unified component catalog for printable procedural parts.

tools.name: cad.add_mcmaster_part
tools.description: Place one licensed McMaster-Carr catalog part by part number. If missing from the local Coolify library, live-fetches STEP via the authorized McMaster session (cookies) and caches it. Mate afterward with connect_parts / mate_parts when needed.

mediaUrl.description: Optional override URL for the STEP/mesh asset.

componentId.description: Opaque owner/component ID for coverage tracking.

parentPartId.description: Optional GROUP id to nest under.

tools.name: cad.get_faces
tools.description: Read stable face IDs, centers, normals, and local frames for one part.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

tools.name: cad.get_edges
tools.description: Read stable edge IDs and their measured CAD polylines for one part.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

tools.name: cad.get_vertices
tools.description: Read stable vertex IDs and measured local/world CAD coordinates for one part.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

tools.name: cad.get_parameters
tools.description: Read editable CAD parameters and transform state for one part without changing the scene. Revolve and extrusion parts include profilePointsMm — copy those {x,y} stations into edit_part.changes.profilePointsMm or set_dimensions.profilePointsMm to reshape the live body without deleting it. Loft parts include pointsAMm/pointsBMm (closed UV end loops) and loftHeightMm — copy those into edit_part.changes or set_dimensions; do not delete and recreate.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

tools.name: cad.select_parts
tools.description: Select one or more parts by stable ID.

tools.name: cad.select_topology
tools.description: Select one measured face, edge, or vertex on a part (IDs from get_faces / get_edges / get_vertices / inspect_part).

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

elementId.description: Stable face, edge, or vertex ID.

tools.name: cad.set_transform
tools.description: Set or offset a part world position and world rotation using CAD Z-up coordinates. Scale is the part's parent-local scale, matching the scale reported by get_parameters and the scene context. Nested positions/rotations are converted into the parent local frame automatically.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

mode.description: Set exact values or apply deltas.

scale.description: Parent-local scale [x, y, z]. Copying a sibling's reported scale therefore produces the same scale inside their shared parent.

tools.name: cad.set_dimensions
tools.description: Set exact local size in millimeters. For primitives: width/depth/height (or diameterMm). For extrusions after create: widthMm/profileWidthMm (profile X), depthMm/lengthMm/profileDepthMm (profile length), heightMm/extrusionHeightMm (extrusion thickness), optional cornerRadiusMm, cornerSegments (1–24), and profileEdgeStyle (straight|curvy|soft — keeps the same outline vertices). For revolves/extrusions, top-level profilePointsMm replaces the live profile — do not delete and recreate. Revolve: x=radiusMm from the spin axis, y=heightMm along +Z. Extrude: closed UV outline in mm. For lofts: heightMm/loftHeightMm, widthMm/depthMm, surfaceMode (straight|ruled|rectilinear|smooth|curved|bulge|twist), and/or top-level pointsAMm/pointsBMm closed UV end loops from get_parameters.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

dimensionsMm.description: width/depth/height in mm. Extrusion: profileWidthMm, profileDepthMm/lengthMm, extrusionHeightMm, cornerRadiusMm, cornerSegments, profileEdgeStyle (straight/curvy/soft). Loft: loftHeightMm, widthMm, depthMm, surfaceMode. Omit when only profilePointsMm or pointsAMm/pointsBMm is sent.

profilePointsMm.description: Replace the live revolve meridian or extrusion outline. Stations are {x,y} mm from get_parameters. Revolve: x=radiusMm, y=heightMm along +Z. Extrude: closed UV outline.

pointsAMm.description: Replace the live loft start/bottom closed UV loop in mm (U=CAD X, V=CAD Y on the plate). Copy from get_parameters. Omit to keep the current loop.

pointsBMm.description: Replace the live loft end/top closed UV loop in mm (same frame as pointsAMm). Copy from get_parameters. Omit to keep the current loop.

tools.name: cad.set_appearance
tools.description: Set a part name and/or color.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

tools.name: cad.set_visibility
tools.description: Show or hide a part without deleting it.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

visible.description: True to show, false to hide.

tools.name: cad.delete_parts
tools.description: Delete parts by stable ID.

tools.name: cad.duplicate_parts
tools.description: Duplicate parts and return the created IDs.

tools.name: cad.group_parts
tools.description: Create one hierarchy group without fusing geometry. On a new multi-body object, wrap the members under one named parent so later scale/move/rotate is a single set_transform. When the members share a parent assembly group, the new group is nested under that same parent (not promoted to the scene root). Pass name for the Layers folder label. Needs two or more members — wrapping one nested solid is not how you split for print.

name.description: Folder label for the new group (kept exact when free; numbered only on collision).

tools.name: cad.combine_parts
tools.description: Fuse one or more selected solids or solid containers into one editable combined result. Unlike group_parts, this creates one baked solid and preserves the original operands so uncombine_parts can restore them. A container ID may be passed to combine its visible base and construction children together. Pass name to preserve the requested Layers label; otherwise the first meaningful operand name is retained with a Combine suffix.

partIds.description: Stable IDs of solids or solid containers to combine. Pass one expandable container to combine its visible contents.

name.description: Optional Layers label for the combined result. Keep an explicit name such as "Solid Circle - Combine".

tools.name: cad.ungroup_parts
tools.description: Promote a group’s children to independent parts (the group’s parent, or the scene root). Pass the covering group id or any member id. Nested members resolve to their covering parent even when the member is itself a group. Nested construction subtracts stay on their host solids. Use this when the user wants separate printable/exportable/movable pieces — do not wrap a single member in group_parts, and do not hide nested construction subtracts as a print-package step.

targetPartId.description: Group id or any member id of the covering group to dissolve.

partIds.description: Optional extra member or group ids; each covering group is dissolved once.

tools.name: cad.uncombine_parts
tools.description: Restore the original operands preserved by a combine_parts result. Pass the combined result ID, not a regular group or an arbitrary solid.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the combined result to restore.

tools.name: cad.edit_part
tools.description: Apply a coordinated edit to a part. Put only allowed keys in changes: dimensionsMm, positionMm, rotationDeg, scale, name, color, visible, profilePointsMm (revolve meridian or extrusion outline copied from get_parameters), pointsAMm/pointsBMm (loft end loops), loftHeightMm/widthMm/depthMm/surfaceMode for an existing loft, sweep {profileKind, tubeRadiusMm, rectWidthMm, rectDepthMm, pathPointsMm, pathMode} for an existing sweep, plus shape CAD params from get_parameters. Sweep and loft edits preserve the existing feature and omit fields you are not changing. Do not rewrite children, modifiers, features, id, or type. For small station tweaks, copy profile arrays into edit_part/set_dimensions. For a new irregular planar silhouette, use trace_image only if the user explicitly requested a trace and the view is verified to be a true prism; otherwise author an explicit profile instead of inventing a long profilePointsMm list.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

changes.description: Allowed keys: dimensionsMm {width,depth,height,cornerRadiusMm,cornerSegments,loftHeightMm,surfaceMode}, positionMm [x,y,z], rotationDeg [x,y,z], scale [x,y,z], name, color, visible, profilePointsMm [{x,y}, …] from get_parameters (revolve x=radiusMm y=heightMm; extrude closed UV), pointsAMm/pointsBMm [{x,y}, …] loft end loops, loftHeightMm/widthMm/depthMm/surfaceMode for an existing loft, sweep {profileKind, tubeRadiusMm, rectWidthMm, rectDepthMm, pathPointsMm, pathMode} for an existing sweep, and CAD params (widthMm/depthMm/heightMm/radiusMm/…). Not allowed: children, modifiers, features, id, type.

tools.name: cad.split_part
tools.description: Cut one part into two pieces with a plane. Use axis for the cut direction, and ratio 0–1 for where the cut sits (0.5 = halfway). Prefer ratio; use offsetMm only when you need an exact millimeter offset from the part center.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

axis.description: Local cut direction. z = top/bottom split (height). x / y = side splits (width / depth).

ratio.description: Where to cut along the axis, from 0 to 1. 0.5 = middle. Do NOT use 50 — that is wrong. Example: 0.5 for half, 0.25 for one-quarter from the low end.

offsetMm.description: Optional exact cut offset in millimeters from the part center. Leave empty when using ratio.

tools.name: cad.boolean_parts
tools.description: Union parts or attach existing tool parts as LIVE subtractive operands under targetPartId. Creating a cutter alone does not cut anything. After subtracting, KEEP tool parts under their host: delete_parts on a cutter removes the opening. Subtract overlapping primitives to isolate curved-shell segments; do not flatten those segments into an extruded outline.

mode.description: Boolean operation.

targetPartId.description: Host part for subtraction.

toolPartIds.description: Parts to union or use as cutters.

tools.name: cad.add_hole
tools.description: Create a circular, polygonal (including hexagonal), or slot opening on a part.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

face.description: Target face ID or semantic face label.

parameters.description: Diameter, width, length, depth, offsets, polygon side count, and tilt in millimeters/degrees.

tools.name: cad.add_feature
tools.description: Add a recess, rim, raised detail, or face-stamped text. Letters/logos on a host face MUST use feature=text (or add_text) after the host exists — never add_shape shape=text, which stands on the plate along +Z.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

feature.description: Feature kind. text = emboss/engrave glyphs on the host face.

face.description: Target face ID or semantic label (required for text).

text.description: Lettering for feature=text.

mode.description: emboss = shallow raised glyphs on the face; engrave = recessed. Default emboss.

parameters.description: Feature-specific dimensions. For text: text, fontSizeMm, depthMm, mode, optional inPlaneRotationDeg (readable spin; omitted = world-up upright default).

tools.name: cad.shell_part
tools.description: Hollow a part and optionally remove declared faces. For a revolve, this rebuilds the editable outer meridian as a native hollow C-section with the requested wall thickness; use openFaces=["Top"] for an open vessel mouth instead of a cavity cutter.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

openFaces.description: Face IDs or semantic labels to remove.

tools.name: cad.trash_faces
tools.description: Remove declared faces while preserving the remaining shell.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

thicknessMm.description: Wall thickness used when the result needs a shell.

tools.name: cad.pattern_parts
tools.description: Create a linear, circular, or mirrored repetition from an existing part. Circular patterns require an explicit shared center: provide centerMm in absolute CAD millimeters or centerPartId for a live part whose world center is the pivot. Never assume the prototype center is the pattern center.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

mode.description: Pattern mode.

axis.description: CAD x, y, or z axis.

count.description: Total instance count.

centerMm.description: Required for circular mode: absolute world pivot [x,y,z] in CAD millimeters.

centerPartId.description: Required for circular mode: existing live part ID whose world center is the shared pivot.

tools.name: cad.align_parts
tools.description: Line parts up after they are already roughly placed (usually after assemble). center = match centers on an axis. flush = push parts so they share the same outer face on that axis. distribute = keep outermost centers fixed and space the middle parts evenly along one axis (needs 3+; no referencePartId). rotation = copy the reference world orientation onto the movers (center stays put; axis selects which Euler components to match, default xyz = full orientation). Pick which parts move with partIds, and which stays put with referencePartId (center/flush/rotation only).

mode.description: center = share the same center on the axis. flush = share the same outer side on the axis. distribute = even spacing between outermost centers (3+ parts). rotation = match the reference orientation (full or per-axis).

partIds.description: Parts that should move into alignment (or be redistributed for distribute).

referencePartId.description: Part that stays fixed for center/flush/rotation. Unused for distribute (outermost on the axis stay fixed). Defaults to the first partIds entry if omitted.

axis.description: CAD axis to align on. Use x/y/z for one axis, or xz to center in the build-plane. For mode=rotation, x/y/z/xyz selects which orientation components to match (default xyz).

direction.description: Only for flush: which side of the reference to flush against.

tools.name: cad.mate_parts
tools.description: Stick two parts together so movingFace meets fixedFace (normals oppose). For several copies on the same face (pins, legs, posts), put the sideways station in arguments.inPlaneOffsetMm {uMm,vMm} — do not write the offset only in reason text. Omit inPlaneOffsetMm to keep the moving part’s current sideways placement; pass {uMm:0,vMm:0} to center. Do not use a generic face mate on an explicitly authored sweep/curvedTube whose absolute path endpoints already contact the host; edit its path or provide measured movingPointMm/fixedPointMm anchors instead.

movingFace.description: Face on the moving part that should touch (e.g. Bottom). From get_faces / inspect_part.

fixedFace.description: Face on the fixed part to land on (e.g. Top). From get_faces / inspect_part.

movingPointMm.description: Optional local contact point on the moving part [x,y,z] mm instead of a whole face.

fixedPointMm.description: Optional local contact point on the fixed part [x,y,z] mm instead of a whole face.

inPlaneOffsetMm.description: Face-frame offset from the fixed face center { uMm, vMm }. Required when two+ copies share one face and need different stations. Omit = keep current sideways placement. {uMm:0,vMm:0} = center.

tools.name: cad.place_on_plate
tools.description: Ground parts on the CAD Z=0 build plate. Default layFlat=false (translate only — keep authored rotation). layFlat:true may tip a body onto its largest face; use only when a part is clearly upside-down or on a thin edge vs the reference.

layFlat.description: If true, also rotate to a max-footprint face before grounding. Prefer false so image-matched rotation is kept.

tools.name: cad.place_inside
tools.description: Place a part inside a hollow container using a measured interior face returned by get_faces. Solid parts expose no interior faces and are rejected.

partId.description: Part to move inside the container.

interiorFace.description: Measured interior face ID, usually interior:bottom or interior:wall.

movingFace.description: Measured face on the inserted part that should contact the interior face.

clearanceMm.description: Gap from the measured interior face in millimeters.

inPlaneOffsetMm.description: Optional measured face-frame offset { uMm, vMm } from the interior face center.

tools.name: cad.edit_topology
tools.description: Edit one measured face, edge, or vertex by ID from get_faces / get_edges / get_vertices. Face parameters: scaleX/scaleY/scaleZ (or width/depth/height mm). Edge: offsetMm. Vertex: offsetX/offsetY/offsetZ mm.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

elementId.description: Face, edge, or vertex ID from inspect_part / get_faces / get_edges / get_vertices.

parameters.description: Face: { scaleX, scaleY, scaleZ } or { width, depth, height }. Edge: { offsetMm }. Vertex: { offsetX, offsetY, offsetZ }. Do not mix kinds.

tools.name: cad.fillet_edges
tools.description: Round edges. Prefer selector (all, all_vertical, top_rim, bottom_rim) or pass edgeIds from get_edges. Required: radiusMm. Optional: segments, direction (outward|inward). Do not nest fields in parameters{}.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

edgeIds.description: Measured edge IDs from get_edges. Optional when selector is set.

selector.description: Semantic edge group when you do not want to list IDs.

direction.description: Fillet side when supported.

tools.name: cad.add_connector
tools.description: Place a mechanical connector. Complete hardware (hinge, pin-hinge, thread, twist-lock) can omit targetPartId and sit on the plate as its own part. Face features (holes, snaps, studs) still need a host part and usually a face.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

connectorType.description: Ready mechanical Connect-tool kind. Screw Hole pairs with Screw at the same M-size; snap types pair tab+slot; press-fit peg/hole pair; stud-grid places an 8 mm-pitch stud array (mate click cuts sockets); magnet-pocket takes a disc magnet; hinge places a complete flush hinge (both leaves + pin) as its own part — no host face required. joint-pin-hinge is a legacy alias of hinge. Legacy snap-male / snap-female aliases map to snap-tab / snap-slot.

face.description: Host face label (Top/Bottom/Front/Back/Left/Right, Face N, or interior:*).

studsX.description: Stud grid columns for connector-stud-grid. Default 2.

studsY.description: Stud grid rows for connector-stud-grid. Default 4.

fit.description: FDM clutch fit for stud-grid sockets. Default normal.

tools.name: cad.add_mechanical_joint
tools.description: Mate two parts face-to-face and generate a paired mechanical interface (currently pin hinge). The moving part is aligned to the host, then hinge/barrel geometry is added to both.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the moving part to align to the host.

face.description: Face on the moving part that contacts the host.

referenceFace.description: Face on the host that contacts the moving part.

mechanicalJointKind.description: Interface kind. Only pinHinge is committable.

jointId.description: Opaque joint id used by generated geometry.

parameters.description: Optional joint parameters (pin diameter, barrel length, etc.).

tools.name: cad.connect_parts
tools.description: Atomically connect two live parts through measured ports. Resolves both world frames, moves only the target body into contact, creates paired interface geometry, persists the assembly graph edge, and rolls back the entire call if any step fails. Use this instead of mixing mate_parts with add_connector for one interface; groups are organizational and do not replace a connection.

sourcePartId.description: Exact live ID or explicit result alias (for example "$base") of the fixed/source part. Do not use prototype, last_created, or a display name.

sourcePort.description: Measured source port: {face, localPointMm?, localNormal?, localTangentUMm?}; a face string is accepted for simple planar ports.

targetPartId.description: Exact live ID or explicit result alias (for example "$lid") of the moving/target part. Do not use prototype, last_created, or a display name.

targetPort.description: Measured target port: {face, localPointMm?, localNormal?, localTangentUMm?}; a face string is accepted for simple planar ports.

sizeMm.description: Nominal connector or shaft size in millimeters.

motion.description: Optional motion constraint, for example {type:"revolute", axis:"X", limitsDeg:[0,120]}.

tools.name: cad.route_cable
tools.description: Create a continuous swept cable between two measured ports and atomically attach both endpoints. The path is authored in absolute CAD millimeters; endpoint contact and clearance are validated, and crossing another part without endpoint interfaces never counts as connected.

targetPartId.description: Stable target endpoint part ID.

pathPointsMm.description: At least two absolute CAD points; first/last are replaced by the measured port anchors.

parentPartId.description: Optional GROUP id for organization; the cable is nested without changing its world pose.

tools.name: cad.add_joint
tools.description: Add a connector or mechanical joint between measured parts/faces.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

kind.description: Joint kind.

referencePartId.description: Second part for a mechanical joint.

tools.name: cad.get_auth_status
tools.description: Check whether the current Cadding browser session is signed in and whether protected project operations are available. Returns no credentials or tokens.

tools.name: cad.request_sign_in
tools.description: Open Cadding’s sign-in page and return to the editor afterward. The user must complete sign-in in the browser; never ask for or pass passwords, OTPs, recovery codes, or tokens to this tool.

tools.name: cad.list_projects
tools.description: List projects owned by the signed-in user, including public sharing metadata.

limit.description: Maximum projects to return (1–200).

tools.name: cad.open_project
tools.description: Open a saved project owned by the signed-in user in the current editor session.

projectId.description: Saved Cadding project ID.

tools.name: cad.save_project
tools.description: Save the live editor scene to the signed-in user’s Cadding account. Call this before publishing so the public model contains the latest edits.

tools.name: cad.set_project_public
tools.description: Publish or unpublish the active saved project. When publishing, returns a durable publicUrl that the agent should send to the user. Requires sign-in and a successful save_project call first.

isPublic.description: True to publish and obtain a public URL; false to make the project private.

publicSlug.description: Optional requested public slug. Omit to retain or generate the project slug.

tools.name: cad.export_model
tools.description: Export the live model. Signed-in users receive a durable public download URL saved in Exports; guests can request a browser download but do not receive a durable URL.

format.description: Export file format. Use stl-package for one STL per printable component plus an assembly guide.

download.description: Also start a browser download for the user.

tools.name: cad.generate_ai_mesh
tools.description: Generate a controlled AI mesh and add it to the live scene. Use for explicit organic, character, sculpture, figurine, relief, logo, or decorative geometry that is inefficient to model parametrically. Requires sign-in. The realization declares whether the result is decorative or intended for later manufacturing validation.

prompt.description: Text description of the mesh to generate.

imageUrl.description: Source image URL. Use prompt or imageUrl, not both.

name.description: Display name for the generated part.

realization.description: Mesh role. Decorative meshes remain separate visual parts; manufacturing candidates require validation before print or boolean operations.

tools.name: cad.generate_mold
tools.description: Generate a multi-part mold around one target part.

targetPartId.description: Stable ID of the part to inspect or modify.

marginMm.description: Margin around the source body in millimeters.

tools.name: cad.capture_viewport
tools.description: Capture the current editor viewport, a standard view, or a crop of one visible part as an image data URL.

targetPartId.description: Optional visible part ID to crop around.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.description: Saved snapshots of a board, newest first.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

stripped.description: leave out descriptions, checklists, attachments and comments

tools.name: get_proposal

tools.name: switch_board

tools.name: set_view

tools.name: set_filter

tools.name: clear_filters

tools.name: withdraw_proposal

tools.name: create_board

tools.name: rename_board

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: set_board_background
tools.description: Board background: a gradient by name (Sky, Sunset, Forest, Berry, Ocean, Plum, Slate, Mint) or a solid #rrggbb colour. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Batchable in apply_changes.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: create_column
tools.description: Add a column (list). Returns column_id. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Batchable in apply_changes.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

position.description: 0-based position; omit to append

tools.name: update_column
tools.description: Rename a column, set its soft WIP limit (0 = none), or collapse it. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Batchable in apply_changes.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: move_column
tools.description: Reorder a column to a 0-based position. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Batchable in apply_changes.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

position.description: 0-based position; omit to append

tools.name: create_card
tools.description: Add a card to a column, with optional description (markdown), priority, due date, labels and members. Returns card_id. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Batchable in apply_changes.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

position.description: 0-based position; omit to append

tools.name: update_card
tools.description: Change a card. Give only the fields to change. due_date null clears it; label_ids, member_ids and checklist replace the whole list (checklist items keep their id when you pass it). Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Batchable in apply_changes.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: move_card
tools.description: Move a card to a column, at a 0-based position (default: the end). Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Batchable in apply_changes.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

position.description: 0-based position; omit to append

tools.name: add_checklist_items
tools.description: Append unchecked items to a card checklist. Returns their item_ids. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Batchable in apply_changes.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: update_checklist_item
tools.description: Tick, untick or reword one checklist item. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Batchable in apply_changes.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description: Comment on a card (markdown). author_member_id names a board member; omit it for an anonymous comment. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Batchable in apply_changes.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: add_attachment
tools.description: Embed a file in a card, as base64. HTML, SVG and XML are refused because a browser could run them. 25 MB limit. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Batchable in apply_changes.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: create_label
tools.description: Add a label to a board. Returns label_id. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Batchable in apply_changes.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: update_label
tools.description: Rename or recolour a label. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Batchable in apply_changes.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: create_member

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: update_member
tools.description: Rename or recolour a member. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Batchable in apply_changes.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: apply_changes
tools.description: Several board edits as one proposal and one undo step. Each change is {tool, input, as?}; tools must be batchable (see describe_tools). Name a created thing with "as" and use "$name" in a later change's id field. If any change fails, none is applied. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Step the board back one change (50 steps per board, this tab only). Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Re-apply the change undo stepped back from. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: take_snapshot
tools.description: Save a named copy of a board that restore_snapshot can bring back. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: set_auto_snapshot
tools.description: Turn automatic snapshots on or off: before destructive changes, and once a day. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome.

tools.name: import_boards
tools.description: Add boards from a KanZen JSON export. Existing boards are kept; clashing ids get new ones. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome.

data.description: a KanZen export: one board object, {boards:{...}}, or the same as a JSON string

tools.name: import_trello
tools.description: Create a board from a Trello JSON export: lists, cards, labels, members and checklists. Attachments are skipped. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome.

data.description: the Trello export, or it as a JSON string

tools.name: import_share_link

tools.name: set_team_mode
tools.description: Split a board into one file per card for git-friendly collaboration, or join it back into one file. Needs a Folder or Crate. Lossless both ways. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: set_palette
tools.description: Colour palette: default, sumi, kinari, tadelakt, sang, snow, mumbai. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome.

tools.name: delete_column
tools.description: Delete a column and every card in it. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Destructive.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: delete_card
tools.description: Delete a card. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Destructive.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: remove_checklist_item
tools.description: Remove one checklist item from a card. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Destructive.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: delete_comment
tools.description: Delete one comment from a card. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Destructive.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: remove_attachment
tools.description: Remove an embedded file from a card. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Destructive.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: delete_label
tools.description: Delete a label and take it off every card. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Destructive.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: delete_member
tools.description: Remove a member from a board and from every card. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Destructive.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: restore_snapshot
tools.description: Replace a board with a snapshot of it. A safety snapshot is taken first. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Destructive.

board_id.description: board to act on; default: the open board

tools.name: delete_snapshot
tools.description: Delete a saved snapshot. Waits for the person's approval: returns {status:"pending_approval", proposal_id}; call get_proposal for the outcome. Destructive.

tools.name: get_diagram
tools.description: Read the current architecture as DSL plus a structured summary (nodes, groups, edges, provider, plan, parse errors). Call this before editing.

tools.name: set_diagram
tools.description: Replace the whole architecture with new DSL. Grammar: `id [kind: <kind>, label: "...", attr: value]` for nodes, `group "Label" { ... }` for groups, `a > b: "label" [ops: 2]` for edges (`ops` = calls per request), `direction right|down`, `title "..."`, `provider cloudflare|vercel`. Kinds: client, edge-cache, waf, bot-shield, rate-limit, static, ssr, compute, kv, sql, blob, queue, actor, workflow, vector, llm, ai-gateway, search, cron, realtime, hyperdrive, images, stream, browser, turnstile, email, load-balancer, zaraz, analytics, access, container, flags, sandbox, middleware, external. Prefer patch_diagram for small edits.

tools.name: patch_diagram
tools.description: Apply small edits to the architecture: add/remove/set nodes, groups and edges, or set direction/title/provider. Node attrs that matter to the simulator: hit (cache 0..1), cpuMs, bytesKb, rowsRead, writeShare, limitRps, neurons, ops on edges. Third-party services: kind external with attrs { service: "openai.gpt55_chat" } (ids from list_services).

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: List starting-point architectures (id, name, tagline, lesson). Load one with load_template.

tools.name: load_template
tools.description: Load a template architecture by id onto the canvas, replacing the current diagram.

tools.name: list_products
tools.description: List the generic product kinds and what each maps to on Cloudflare and Vercel, including gaps where a provider has no first-party product.

tools.name: explain_product
tools.description: Explain one product kind on both providers: what it is, when to use it, limits, recommended stack, billing meters, and the counterpart gap.

tools.name: set_provider
tools.description: Switch the whole architecture between Cloudflare and Vercel. Nodes are re-labelled and re-priced; the diagram itself does not change.

tools.name: set_plan
tools.description: Choose which plan to price against: free (Cloudflare Free / Vercel Hobby) or paid (Workers Paid / Vercel Pro).

tools.name: set_traffic_mix
tools.description: Set requests per day and the share of each request class (human, googlebot, ai-crawler, scraper, botnet). Shares are normalised. Omitted fields keep their value.

tools.name: set_protection
tools.description: Set a gate node's protection mode. Modes: off, bots (block scrapers + botnets), bots+ai (also block AI crawlers), all-bots (also block search crawlers, which hurts SEO). Works on bot-shield, waf and rate-limit nodes.

tools.name: get_snapshot
tools.description: Current simulation state: offered traffic by class, what was blocked/dropped, and per-node arrivals. Use it to explain where requests go.

tools.name: get_bill
tools.description: Projected monthly bill for the current architecture and traffic, priced from the official pricing pages (with source URLs). Optionally for a different provider or plan.

tools.name: compare_providers
tools.description: Price the same architecture on Cloudflare and Vercel, free and paid, side by side, with the gaps each provider has for the kinds in use.

tools.name: explain_charge
tools.description: Explain what drives a meter: which nodes contribute, how much, and which request classes are behind it. Without a meter, explains the top five by monthly volume.

tools.name: analyze_product
tools.description: Analyse a product from its URL or a description: what it is, the core loop vs polish features, which platform primitives it needs, and a build verdict. Follow with propose_architecture.

tools.name: propose_architecture
tools.description: Generate an architecture from the last analyze_product result (or from explicit needs flags) and put it on the canvas. Needs: auth, sql, kv, blob, queue, realtime, llm, vector, search, cron, payments, email, ssr.

tools.name: export_config
tools.description: Generate deployable configuration for the current architecture: wrangler.jsonc and a Worker entry for Cloudflare, or vercel.json and a setup guide for Vercel, plus the recommended stack.

tools.name: describe_studio
tools.description: Start here. What freenet.free is and how it thinks (request classes, gates, caches, free-tier quotas), a map of the UI, which tool to use for what, common workflows, and the current state: provider, plan, traffic, clock position, view, selection, open blueprint.

tools.name: get_layers
tools.description: The layer view: every node with the meters it drives, projected monthly volume against the plan's allowance (percent used, over or not), unit cost and what happens past the quota. This is what the timeline tracks and the Inspect overview show.

tools.name: set_simulation_period
tools.description: Choose what the timeline simulates: a day (hours), a month (30 days) or a year (12 months with monthly quota resets). Restarts the clock and starts playing; the whole period plays in about 90 real seconds.

tools.name: control_timeline
tools.description: Drive the timeline: play, pause, reset to the start, or seek to a position given as a fraction of the period (0 = start, 1 = end; seeking pauses). Returns the clock readout. Use seek 1 to jump to the end-of-period totals.

tools.name: set_view
tools.description: Arrange the canvas: layout snake (rows that wrap, the default), vertical or horizontal; edge style curved, step or straight; relayout true re-runs auto layout and discards manual nudges.

tools.name: focus_node
tools.description: Select a node, centre the canvas on it and open its details in the Inspect panel. Returns the node's product, role, attributes and per-day flow. Pass an empty id to clear the selection.

tools.name: open_panel
tools.description: Open a right-hand panel: inspect (overview, layers, node details), bill (per-meter lines) or chat (the AI tab), optionally a chat sub-tab: chat, activity (tool log) or alternatives.

tools.name: list_alternatives
tools.description: Third-party and cross-provider alternatives for a product kind, or for every kind on the canvas: what it is on Cloudflare, what it is on Vercel, gaps, and services people use instead.

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: Third-party services you can put on the canvas next to the platform: OpenAI models and tools, Shopify commerce APIs, Netlify hosting primitives. Each has a service id, vendor pricing meters and default consumption per request. Add one with patch_diagram: add_node with kind external and attrs { service: "openai.gpt55_chat" }; override a meter with a numeric attr named after it, e.g. { output_tokens: 900 }.

tools.name: list_blueprints
tools.description: Saved blueprints in this browser (id, name, provider, plan, node count, where it was remixed from, last updated), and which one is open.

tools.name: save_blueprint
tools.description: Save what is on the canvas as a new blueprint (optionally named) and open it, so further edits autosave to it.

tools.name: open_blueprint
tools.description: Open a saved blueprint by id onto the canvas (replaces the current diagram, provider, plan, traffic and protections).

tools.name: rename_blueprint
tools.description: Rename the open blueprint (or one by id) and set the diagram title to match.

tools.name: remix_blueprint
tools.description: Duplicate a saved blueprint (by id) or a template (by templateId) into a new blueprint and open it, keeping the original untouched.

tools.name: delete_blueprint
tools.description: Delete a saved blueprint by id. Cannot be undone; the canvas keeps its current contents.

tools.name: create
tools.description: Create a game; omitted fields are generated compatibly by the engine.

review.description: Pause automatic pickup at a review decision before transferring anything. Explicit selection or cancellation required.

lootPatterns.description: Case-insensitive literal substrings of the perceived singular item name. Add to category and arrow inclusions; never match hidden identity.

ignorePatterns.description: Case-insensitive literal substrings of the perceived singular item name. Override every inclusion.

tools.name: observe
tools.description: Read the currently loaded session's full observation and standing decision.

tools.name: inspect
tools.description: Read revision-bound attempts for here or an adjacent square using only perceived knowledge.

tools.name: lookup
tools.description: Look up a name in the pinned game encyclopedia.

tools.name: navigation
tools.description: Read perceived frontiers and known downward stairs under the knownWalking policy.

tools.name: route
tools.description: Find a shortest known walking route in the perceived current level.

tools.name: resume

lootPatterns.description: Case-insensitive literal substrings of the perceived singular item name. Add to category and arrow inclusions; never match hidden identity.

ignorePatterns.description: Case-insensitive literal substrings of the perceived singular item name. Override every inclusion.

tools.name: attack

tools.name: explore

maxFrontiers.description: Maximum successive perceived frontiers to reach (default 1). The total maxActions budget and decision/change stops still apply. A door attempt always ends the call.

tools.name: descend

tools.name: select-f1-data
tools.description: Fill in F1 data selections (year, event, session, drivers) plus chart/telemetry toggles and submit; the dashboard applies them.

tools.name: get-current-selection
tools.description: Returns the homepage's current state as JSON: selected year, event, session, drivers, active tab (chart/data/docs), view mode (essential/expert), all chart/telemetry toggles, chart visibility picks, annotation mode, and saved favorite drivers.

tools.name: list-available-options
tools.description: Returns the current year/event/session/driver dropdown options as JSON (including driver full names/teams when the session drivers.json has loaded). Use this before select-race-data to discover valid values.

tools.name: get-data-status
tools.description: Returns whether lap times have finished loading for the currently selected drivers: status idle|no-drivers|loading|partial|ready, plus loaded/missing driver lists.

tools.name: wait-for-data
tools.description: Polls until lap times are loaded for all currently selected drivers (or until timeout). Returns the final get-data-status payload. Call after select-race-data / set-drivers before reading lap tools.

drivers.description: Optional subset of driver codes to wait for (defaults to current selection).

tools.name: get-lap-times
tools.description: Returns per-lap timing for selected drivers from the loaded homepage dataset (respects Fuel Correction and Hide Outliers toggles unless overridden). Default cleanOnly=true excludes pit-in/out, deleted, and 107% outlier laps.

cleanOnly.description: If true (default), only clean racing laps. If false, all laps with isClean/isOutlier flags.

tools.name: get-stint-summary
tools.description: Returns per-stint pace stats (compound, lap range, best/mean/median, crude deg) for selected drivers from loaded lap data. Uses the same clean-lap / fuel / outlier rules as get-lap-times.

tools.name: get-race-pace-comparison
tools.description: Head-to-head clean-lap pace comparison (shared-lap deltas, stint H2H, rolling pace). delta = driverA − driverB (negative = driverA faster). Defaults to the first two selected drivers.

drivers.description: Two-or-more driver codes (default: current selection; first two used as A/B).

tools.name: get-positions
tools.description: Returns lap-by-lap race position series for selected drivers from loaded lap data.

tools.name: get-data-table
tools.description: Returns the Data-tab style lap table as structured JSON rows (not a file download). Includes compound/stint/life/pos/sectors and clean/outlier flags. Prefer this over trigger-csv-export for agents.

hideOutliers.description: Override outliers toggle (flags only; all rows still returned).

tools.name: get-telemetry-summary
tools.description: Returns which telemetry laps are loaded in state.telData (dataKeys, drivers, laps, channel lists, point counts). Call select-lap first. For channel units see list-telemetry-channels.

tools.name: list-telemetry-channels
tools.description: Returns the TracingInsights telemetry channel catalog (ids, aliases, units, descriptions) from DATA_REFERENCE.md / Q.py tel.json fields: speed, throttle, brake, drs, rpm, gear, distance, rel_distance, acc_x/y/z, x/y/z, DriverAhead, DistanceToDriverAhead, time.

tools.name: get-telemetry-status
tools.description: Returns whether selected telemetry laps are present in state.telData: idle|no-laps|loading|partial|ready.

laps.description: Optional dataKeys or 'DRV-lap' pairs; defaults to selectedLaps.

tools.name: wait-for-telemetry
tools.description: Polls until the requested (or currently selected) telemetry laps are in state.telData. Use after select-lap / auto-fastest.

laps.description: dataKeys or 'ANT-58' style refs (defaults to selectedLaps).

tools.name: get-telemetry-stats
tools.description: Aggregate stats for loaded telemetry laps: top/avg/min speed, throttle/brake/DRS duty, gear shifts, peak accelerations, lap distance. Does not return full sample arrays.

laps.description: dataKeys or DRV-lap refs (default: all loaded / selected).

tools.name: get-telemetry-channel
tools.description: Returns distance/time-aligned samples for one channel on a loaded lap (decimated; default maxPoints=150, max 500). Channels: speed, throttle, brake, drs, rpm, gear, acc_x/y/z, x/y/z, DistanceToDriverAhead, etc. Prefer get-telemetry-stats for aggregates.

lap.description: dataKey or 'ANT-58' / driver+lap via separate fields.

driver.description: 3-letter code if not using full dataKey.

lapNumber.description: Lap number if not using full dataKey.

tools.name: compare-telemetry
tools.description: Distance-aligns lap B onto lap A and returns decimated samples with delta = A − B for a channel (default speed). Both laps must be loaded via select-lap. For cumulative lap-time gap vs Distance (the Time Delta chart), use get-time-delta — do not pass channel "time".

channel.description: Channel to compare (default "speed"). Not "time" — use get-time-delta.

tools.name: get-time-delta
tools.description: Returns the same Distance-vs-gap series as the telemetry Time Delta chart. reference = first lap (lapA), compare = second (lapB). delta = compare − reference in seconds (positive = compare behind/slower). mode auto uses sector-anchored math when Align is on and sector times exist (same as the UI); otherwise classic length-scaled interpolation. Prefer this over compare-telemetry channel=time.

lapA.description: Reference lap dataKey or DRV-lap (default: first selected/loaded).

lapB.description: Compare lap dataKey or DRV-lap (default: second selected/loaded).

mode.description: auto (default) follows Align toggle; "classic" / "sector" force an algorithm.

tools.name: get-fastest-laps
tools.description: From loaded lap-times data, returns each selected driver's fastest clean (non pit-in/out, non-outlier) lap with sector times, plus ranking and head-to-head gap. Optional quali segment filter (Q1/Q2/Q3). Use before select-lap / get-time-delta.

segment.description: Optional qualifying segment filter, e.g. "Q3". Omit for whole session.

tools.name: get-corners
tools.description: Returns corners.json for the current session (number, distance m, x/y, angle) plus track rotation. Loaded automatically when the first telemetry lap is selected.

tools.name: select-race-data
tools.description: Sets the year, event, session and/or drivers on the F1 telemetry homepage in one call. Each provided value is applied in order (year → event → session → drivers), waiting for the UI to load each downstream list. Omit a field to leave it unchanged.

event.description: Event / Grand Prix name as shown in the dropdown, e.g. "British Grand Prix".

tools.name: set-year
tools.description: Selects a season year on the homepage. Resets event, session and drivers (they must be re-selected afterwards).

tools.name: set-event
tools.description: Selects an event / Grand Prix for the currently selected year. Resets session and drivers.

event.description: Event name as shown in the dropdown, e.g. "British Grand Prix".

tools.name: set-session
tools.description: Selects a session (e.g. Race, Qualifying) for the currently selected event. Resets drivers. Waits for the driver list to refresh for the new session.

tools.name: set-drivers
tools.description: Selects which drivers to compare for the current session, by 3-letter code (e.g. VER, HAM). Waits for the driver list to load if needed.

tools.name: switch-tab
tools.description: Switches the main view between the Chart, Data (lap times table) and Docs (FIA documents) tabs.

tools.name: set-view-mode
tools.description: Switches between the Essential (core charts) and Expert (advanced charts) view modes.

mode.description: View mode to activate.

tools.name: set-chart-option
tools.description: Enables or disables a homepage toggle. Lap chart: outliers, smoothing, fuel, trackStatus, autoFastest, sessionTime. Race/stint: raceTraceShadow, stintLowess. Telemetry: markers, corners, decimation, align, editLayout. Expert: annotation. enabled must be a real boolean.

enabled.description: true to enable, false to disable.

tools.name: set-data-table-column
tools.description: Shows or hides a Data-tab column group (same as the table column toggles). Columns: compounds, stints, tyre-life, track-status, positions, personal-best, pitstops, sector-times. Open the Data tab first so the table is rendered.

enabled.description: true to show, false to hide.

tools.name: set-telemetry-layout
tools.description: Reorders telemetry charts (same as Edit layout drag/up-down). Pass an ordered list of chart ids; omitted ids are appended in the default order. Ids: speedchart, deltachart-section, throttlechart, brakechart, driveractionchart, gearchart, rpchart, drschart, driveraheadchart, distancetodriveraheadchart, gaptodriveraheadchart, acc_xchart, acc_ychart, acc_zchart, elevationchart.

order.description: Desired chart id order (partial lists are completed with defaults).

tools.name: set-stint-lowess-frac
tools.description: Sets the stint chart LOWESS smoothing fraction (0.05–1.0), same as the Smoothing slider next to Tyre Performance.

tools.name: clear-selected-laps
tools.description: Removes all laps from the Selected Laps control (clears loaded telemetry compare set).

tools.name: remove-selected-lap
tools.description: Removes one lap from Selected Laps (e.g. driver VER lap 10).

tools.name: set-quali-segment
tools.description: Filters lap/stint/tyre charts to a qualifying segment (Q1/Q2/Q3/SQ1/…). Pass "All" or "" to clear. Only available for qualifying-style sessions after data loads.

tools.name: set-sector-visibility
tools.description: Shows or hides a sector series on the Expert sector chart (S1/S2/S3 chips). Requires Expert mode and loaded lap data so the sector controls exist.

enabled.description: true to show the sector, false to hide it.

tools.name: list-stint-chips
tools.description: Returns the current stint analysis chips (driver, stint number, visible, pinned) from the Expert stint driver form. Empty if Expert mode is off or stint data has not rendered.

tools.name: set-stint-visibility
tools.description: Toggles a stint checkbox in the Expert stint analysis form (same as the per-stint chips). Pass driver + stint + enabled, or driver + mode "all"|"none" for Select all / Hide all.

stint.description: Stint number (1-based), required unless mode is set.

enabled.description: true to show the stint, false to hide (ignored when mode is set).

mode.description: Bulk action: "all" = Select all, "none" = Hide all for that driver.

tools.name: set-stint-pin
tools.description: Pins/unpins a stint on the Expert stint chart (📌 buttons). Pass driver + stint + pinned, or clearAll:true to unpin every stint.

pinned.description: true to pin, false to unpin.

clearAll.description: If true, clicks Unpin all (ignores other args).

tools.name: set-annotation-tool
tools.description: Selects the active annotation toolbar tool (Expert annotation mode): select, pencil, text, arrow, line, rect, ellipse, eraser.

tools.name: set-annotation-color
tools.description: Sets the global annotation stroke/fill color (hex, e.g. #00ff00).

tools.name: annotation-undo
tools.description: Undoes the last annotation action on all registered charts.

tools.name: annotation-redo
tools.description: Redoes the last undone annotation action on all registered charts.

tools.name: annotation-clear
tools.description: Clears all annotations on registered charts (same as Clear All on the toolbar).

tools.name: set-chart-visibility
tools.description: Shows or hides a lap-time or telemetry chart (same as the Expert Chart settings modal). Lap charts: lapchart, heatmap, stint, sector, tyre, position, race-trace. Telemetry: speed, delta, throttle, brake, driver-action, gear, rpm, drs, driver-ahead, distance-ahead, gap-ahead, acc-x, acc-y, acc-z, elevation.

chart.description: Which chart to show or hide.

visible.description: true to show, false to hide.

tools.name: reset-chart-visibility
tools.description: Restores the default Chart settings picks so every lap-time and telemetry chart is visible again.

tools.name: reset-telemetry-layout
tools.description: Restores the default telemetry chart order (same as the Reset layout button next to Edit layout in Expert mode).

tools.name: add-favorite-driver
tools.description: Saves a 3-letter driver code to the user's favorites (used for auto-selection when the driver is available).

tools.name: clear-favorites
tools.description: Removes all saved favorite driver codes.

tools.name: select-lap
tools.description: Loads and selects a specific lap's telemetry for the current session (e.g. VER lap 12). Year, event and session must already be selected; the lap appears in the selected-laps control once loaded.

tools.name: trigger-chart-screenshot
tools.description: Triggers a PNG download of a chart — the same action as clicking its Download button. Charts: lapchart, heatmap, stint, sector, tyre-strategy, position-changes, race-trace, weather, track-map, speed, delta, throttle, brake, gear, rpm, drs, elevation.

tools.name: trigger-csv-export
tools.description: Triggers a CSV download of the lap-times data table. The Data tab must be populated first (session + drivers selected).

tools.name: set-annotation-mode
tools.description: Switches the chart annotation toolbar on or off (expert mode).

enabled.description: true to enable annotation mode, false to disable.

tools.name: valor_list_workspaces
tools.description: List ValorAI's safe browser workspaces and their purpose before choosing where to navigate.

tools.name: valor_get_current_workspace
tools.description: Identify the current ValorAI workspace from the page path without reading profile, document, medical, or claim contents.

tools.name: valor_search_guidance
tools.description: Search ValorAI's public educational guidance about VA benefits and claim preparation. Do not include personal, medical, or claim-specific information in the query.

query.description: A general VA benefits or claim-preparation topic.

tools.name: valor_open_guidance
tools.description: Open a public ValorAI knowledgebase article returned by valor_search_guidance. This only navigates to a validated article slug.

slug.description: A knowledgebase slug returned by valor_search_guidance.

tools.name: valor_find_va_forms
tools.description: Find public VA form catalog entries by form number, title, or benefits category. This only returns catalog metadata and never starts or submits a form.

search.description: Optional form number or general title keywords.

category.description: Optional public benefits category.

tools.name: valor_open_va_form
tools.description: Open a VA form workspace returned by valor_find_va_forms. This only navigates and never fills, saves, signs, or submits a form.

formNumber.description: A VA form number returned by valor_find_va_forms.

tools.name: valor_open_workspace
tools.description: Open a named ValorAI workspace in the current tab so the browser agent can inspect and operate its visible UI. This tool only navigates; it does not itself create, change, submit, or delete claim data.

tools.name: valor_get_session_state
tools.description: Report whether the current ValorAI browser session is signed in without returning a user, session, or anonymous identifier.

tools.name: valor_start_sign_in
tools.description: Open ValorAI sign-in in the current tab with an optional allowlisted relative product redirect. No credential is read or entered by this tool.

tools.name: valor_start_sign_up
tools.description: Open ValorAI sign-up in the current tab with an optional allowlisted relative product redirect. No credential is read or entered by this tool.

tools.name: valor_get_entitlements
tools.description: Return the signed-in account's bounded Free or Plus feature flags without Stripe, customer, subscription, or billing identifiers.

tools.name: valor_get_onboarding_state
tools.description: Return the signed-in account's bounded onboarding completion, persona, and recommended relative path without onboarding answers or narrative.

tools.name: valor_open_onboarding_step
tools.description: Open a saved-persona-valid onboarding step in the current tab. The server rejects steps outside the account's actual flow.

tools.name: valor_get_product_capabilities
tools.description: List the bounded safe product capability catalog. Signed-out callers receive the Free view; admin, developer, credential, billing-change, destructive, and submission surfaces are excluded.

tools.name: valor_list_chats
tools.description: List bounded metadata for the signed-in user's chats. Message content and attachments are never returned.

tools.name: valor_open_chat
tools.description: Owner-check a chat returned by valor_list_chats, then open it in the current tab without returning or placing chat text in the URL.

tools.name: valor_list_assessments
tools.description: List bounded saved-assessment metadata for the signed-in user without answers, results, narrative, or bearer resume tokens.

tools.name: valor_resume_assessment
tools.description: Owner-check a saved assessment returned by valor_list_assessments, then open the visible assessment funnel without a resume token.

tools.name: valor_get_recent_activity
tools.description: Return bounded signed-in activity metadata without event detail, evidence text, or private narrative.

tools.name: valor_get_appeals_summary
tools.description: Return a bounded signed-in appeals status summary without evidence, denial narrative, or claim contents.

tools.name: valor_get_connected_services
tools.description: Return bounded connected-service state without VA subject identifiers, tokens, scopes, or credentials.

tools.name: valor_get_settings_summary
tools.description: Return bounded settings flags without contact channels, push endpoints, or quiet-hour clock values.

tools.name: valor_whoami
tools.description: Return the current ValorAI subject type and plan flags without names, email addresses, or other PII.

tools.name: valor_get_next_action
tools.description: Return the signed-in user's read-only next-action summary. This may reveal account progress and requires the user's current browser session.

tools.name: valor_get_exam_prep_notes
tools.description: Return educational C&P exam-prep notes. Obtain immediate user approval before sending a personal medical or claim condition; when approval is absent, recommend generic exam-prep topics instead. This is not medical or legal advice.

tools.name: valor_list_form_drafts
tools.description: List only the signed-in user's form-draft metadata; field values are never returned.

tools.name: valor_list_documents
tools.description: List only the signed-in user's redacted document metadata; filenames, URLs, and document text are never returned.
