tools.description: Add/remove tags on a stacks entry by `path`. Tags are stamped source:'llm' and mirrored into the note’s frontmatter / the file’s .meta.json sidecar (portable, Obsidian-readable). Returns the updated entry.

path.description: Entry path

tools.name: weir_stacksTrash
tools.description: Delete a stacks entry by `path` — but weir never really deletes: the file (+ sidecar) is moved into /stacks/.trash/ (a hidden folder the scanner ignores), so it disappears from weir while the bytes survive on disk, recoverable. Drops the index entry. Returns { ok, trashed, dest }.

path.description: Entry path to delete

tools.name: weir_mcpDiag
tools.description: Diagnostics for weir's numen fs channels (transport debugging — for tracking down why a channel won't connect). No input. Per known channel returns: connection state + clientId, whether a token is set, the folder-handle NAME it points at, what weir reads from that folder's bridge.live (present? session, ageMs, fresh under 90s?), and the folder's top-level entries. Reading: bridgeLive absent or stale while the bridge insists it is announcing ⇒ FOLDER MISMATCH (weir and the bridge are on different directories); bridgeLive fresh but clientId null ⇒ STALE HANDSHAKE (re-dial / token). If a channel shows hasHandle:false, open weir Settings → Connections once to cache the handle, then re-run.

tools.name: sandhi.status
tools.description: One read of the whole situation: title, counts, check counts by class, closest arc, unsaved state, undo depth, last call. Start here.

tools.name: sandhi.story.get
tools.description: The full story as JSON (schema sandhi:1): beats, threads, notes. The only read that grows with the story.

tools.name: sandhi.story.update
tools.description: Set the title, logline, belief, or per-principle notes ("In this story"). An empty note removes it. Undo reverses it.

tools.name: sandhi.story.new
tools.description: Replace the story with a blank Story Spine of five beats. Undo brings the old story back.

tools.name: sandhi.story.start
tools.description: Start a new story from Story Spine lines, in order: lines [{stage, text}] with stage once, everyday, oneday, because, until or since; plus title, logline and belief. The stage words set the joints (one day: but; because of that, until finally, ever since then: therefore). The New-story wizard calls this. Undo brings the old story back.

tools.name: sandhi.story.demo
tools.description: Replace the story with "The whistle", the ten-beat demo from the explainer. Undo brings the old story back.

tools.name: sandhi.story.load
tools.description: Replace the story with the given JSON (schema sandhi:1). It is validated first; on failure the story is unchanged. Undo reverses it.

tools.name: sandhi.story.save
tools.description: Download the story as <title>.sandhi.json. Nothing is uploaded.

tools.name: sandhi.story.recent
tools.description: The last three stories a replace pushed aside (newest first): k, title, when, beat count. Pass k to get that story in full; story.load brings it back (undoable).

tools.name: sandhi.story.paste
tools.description: Replace the story with pasted prose, one beat per paragraph, every label left to the writer. No model, nothing guessed. Undo brings the old story back.

tools.name: sandhi.beat.add
tools.description: Insert a beat after the beat with id `after` (default: at the end). Returns the new id and position.

tools.name: sandhi.beat.update
tools.description: Change fields of one beat: label, spine, joint (into this beat), text, fortune, tags, marks, driver, avastha, kis, drafts. Arrays replace whole. Undo reverses it.

tools.name: sandhi.beat.remove
tools.description: Remove a beat. Threads that point at it lose that plant or payoff, and tidbits placed there are unplaced. Undo restores them.

tools.name: sandhi.beat.move
tools.description: Move a beat to a 1-based position.

tools.name: sandhi.tidbit.add
tools.description: Keep a tidbit: a real-life observation that could give the story life (a curious train stop; meat kept too long gets freezer burn). It waits unplaced until the writer weaves it into beats. Undo removes it.

tools.name: sandhi.tidbit.update
tools.description: Change a tidbit's text, note, or the beats it is placed in (placed replaces whole; [] unplaces it).

tools.name: sandhi.tidbit.remove
tools.description: Remove a tidbit. Undo restores it.

tools.name: sandhi.thread.add
tools.description: Add a plant-and-payoff thread (Chekhov's gun, the bīja): a label, the beat that plants it, the beats that pay it off.

tools.name: sandhi.thread.update
tools.description: Change a thread's label, plant beat, payoff beats (payoffs replace whole), or open: true to leave it open on purpose (a planted thread with no payoff is then not flagged).

tools.name: sandhi.thread.remove
tools.description: Remove a thread. Undo restores it.

tools.name: sandhi.checks
tools.description: The checks on the current labels (SPEC §2): each with class, beat position, message and the next step. A clean story returns count 0.

tools.name: sandhi.arc
tools.description: Pearson fit of the fortune line against the six arcs (Reagan et al. 2016); best shape and every score.

tools.name: sandhi.coverage
tools.description: For each of the 13 principles, the beat positions tagged with it.

tools.name: sandhi.view.focus
tools.description: Focus the page on one principle (dims other beats, opens its panel), or "all" to clear.

tools.name: sandhi.undo
tools.description: Undo the last story change (100 steps).

tools.name: sandhi.redo
tools.description: Redo the last undone change.

tools.name: sandhi.journal
tools.description: The last n tool calls (default 20, max 200): tool, class, door, ms, time. The trajectory across sessions.

tools.name: sandhi.reader.status
tools.description: The AI ladder, closest first: a model server on this machine, Gemini Nano in Chrome, your provider with your key. Which rungs can read, the chosen rung and where its words go, the provider and model, key fingerprints (never keys). probe: true also looks for a local server (Chrome may ask to allow local network access).

tools.name: sandhi.reader.select
tools.description: Choose the rung ("machine", "device", "provider"), the provider (openrouter, openai, anthropic, gemini, groq, mistral, deepseek, together, custom), the local server, and the model id for the chosen rung. A custom address is set with its key, by the writer (reader.key).

tools.name: sandhi.reader.models
tools.description: The model ids the chosen rung offers: a local server's list, or your provider's list fetched with your key.

tools.name: sandhi.chapter.start
tools.description: Start a chapter at a beat: the name goes on that beat and on the beats after it, up to the next beat that already starts or belongs to another chapter. An empty name ends the chapter there (the same beats lose their name). Undo reverses it.

tools.name: sandhi.learn.get
tools.description: How stories work: the 13 principles (line, what each source says and who pushes back, the beats of this story that serve it), the six fortune shapes, and the sources. principle narrows it to one.

tools.name: sandhi.write.questions
tools.description: Ask the chosen reader 2 to 4 questions about one beat, each from a principle the beat does least for. Questions only; nothing enters the story. The result replaces any earlier suggestion (write.get). It uses the reader the writer chose.

tools.name: sandhi.write.options
tools.description: Ask the chosen reader what could happen at one beat: the obvious option, named and set aside, then 3 to 5 others, each one line with its joint, fortune, principle and why; at least one where things get worse. Proposals only: nothing enters the story, and there is no tool that writes an option into a beat; the writer writes. It uses the reader the writer chose.

tools.name: sandhi.write.joints
tools.description: Ask the chosen reader to judge every joint the writer labelled therefore or but: holds, slack (and then fits better) or unsure, with a reason and a question. Advice only; no joint is relabelled. It uses the reader the writer chose.

tools.name: sandhi.write.shape
tools.description: Ask the chosen reader how to bring the beats that sit 2 or more from the writer's sketched fortune line toward it: one line per beat, with why. Proposals only; no fortune or text changes. Needs a sketch (story.sketch). It uses the reader the writer chose.

tools.name: sandhi.write.interview
tools.description: Ask the chosen reader for one question aimed at the weakest place in the story (empty beats, the checks, thin beats, principles no beat serves), with where the answer belongs: a beat's text, a tidbit or a note. The writer answers in their own words (beat.update, tidbit.add, story.update); nothing is written by the model. It uses the reader the writer chose.

tools.name: sandhi.write.depth
tools.description: Ask the chosen reader how to give one thin beat depth: 2 to 4 suggestions, each a tidbit to look for or use, a plant, or a question, never prose. Nothing enters the story. It uses the reader the writer chose.

tools.name: sandhi.write.plot
tools.description: Ask the chosen reader how the structure changes around a new plot element: up to 6 changes, each a new empty beat (its stage, joint, fortune and a one-line label) or a relabel of an existing beat's stage, joint or fortune, with why. A proposal with a diff (write.get); nothing changes until the writer applies it (write.apply, person-only). It uses the reader the writer chose.

element.description: the plot element, in a line

tools.name: sandhi.write.place
tools.description: Ask the chosen reader where each unplaced tidbit fits: a beat, whether it lives there as action, character or setting, how in one line, and why. Proposals only; placing one is tidbit.update {placed}. It uses the reader the writer chose.

tools.name: sandhi.story.sketch
tools.description: Set the shape the writer wants the fortune to follow: points [{t, v}] with t from 0 (the first beat) to 1 (the last) and v from -5 to 5, resampled to 25 values; an empty list clears it. The chart draws it under the fortune line and rings beats 2 or more from it. Undo reverses it.

tools.name: sandhi.write.get
tools.description: The current suggestion (questions, options or joint verdicts), or no_proposal.

tools.name: sandhi.write.dismiss
tools.description: Drop the current suggestion. Nothing was kept from it.

tools.name: sandhi.read.run
tools.description: Read a story (prose) with the chosen rung and stage a proposed structure; the story does not change. Beats are the writer's own text cut at the model's exact quotes; quotes not found in the text are dropped. Long stories are read in parts, then as a whole outline; a manuscript with chapter headings is read a chapter at a time, one beat per chapter, and resumes where it stopped (report: chapters, resumed); Gemini Nano cannot read in parts and refuses them (too_long) before any model call. strategy: "whole" (one call reads and labels) or "split" (one call finds the beats, a second labels them). Spends: on the provider rung the story goes to the writer's provider, billed to the writer, so an agent may use that rung only when the writer chose it.

tools.name: sandhi.read.paragraphs
tools.description: Stage prose split one beat per paragraph, with no model and every label left to the writer, as a proposal like a read (read.get shows it; the writer accepts it in the page). The story does not change.

tools.name: sandhi.read.get
tools.description: The staged proposal: the proposed story (schema sandhi:1) and the read report.

tools.name: sandhi.read.cancel
tools.description: Stop the read that is running. Its model call is aborted; nothing is staged.

tools.name: sandhi.read.discard
tools.description: Drop the staged proposal. The story is unchanged; the proposal cannot be brought back.

tools.name: get_site_overview
tools.description: START HERE. Returns a map of this site: what it is, its areas, which tools back each area, common multi-step flows, parameter conventions, and suggested first queries. Call this once to get oriented before using the other tools. This is a read-only analytics dashboard for the Orderly Network perpetual-futures DEX; it does not place trades.

tools.name: get_dashboard_main
tools.description: Daily platform totals for Orderly: taker/cumulative volume, revenue (fees), TVL, deposits/withdrawals, new accounts/addresses, and active builders, as a historical time series. For a live snapshot use get_market_summary; for weekly/monthly user aggregates use get_metrics_overview. Returns rows newest-last over the trailing `days` window.

tools.name: get_tvl_by_chain
tools.description: Total Value Locked broken down by chain, plus a total row. Drives the TVL By Chain widget. Returns newest snapshot rows.

tools.name: get_tvl_by_token
tools.description: TVL and token balance held per collateral token over a trailing window. Drives the TVL By Token widget.

tools.name: get_weekly_symbol_volume
tools.description: Weekly per-symbol volume and listed-markets count from the analytics API. For the live market list (prices, 24h change, open interest) use get_markets.

tools.name: get_funding_rates
tools.description: 8-hour funding rates for every perpetual symbol, from a trailing start date. For cross-exchange funding comparisons use get_funding_comparison.

days.description: Trailing days for the start date (default 30).

tools.name: get_daily_liquidations_by_symbol
tools.description: Daily liquidation notional aggregated per perpetual symbol across all markets. For individual recent liquidation events of one symbol use get_recent_liquidations.

tools.name: get_staking_daily
tools.description: Daily $ORDER staking metrics: staked/unstaked/net amounts, cumulative staker addresses, buybacks, and burned ORDER. Drives the Staking Daily widget.

tools.name: get_builder_daily
tools.description: Per-builder daily metrics: taker/maker/total volume, active users, broker fees, and net flow. Drives the Builder Volume, Builder Active Traders, Builder Revenue, and Net Flow By Builder widgets.

tools.name: get_fund_flows_by_broker
tools.description: Daily deposits, withdrawals, and net fund flow per broker. Drives the Net Flow By Builder widget (fund-flow variant).

tools.name: get_fund_flows_by_chain
tools.description: Daily deposits, withdrawals, and net fund flow per chain. Drives the Fund Flows By Chain widget.

tools.name: get_dex_users
tools.description: Per-builder user activity snapshot: DAU/WAU/MAU with day/week/month-over-month deltas and new-user counts. Drives the DEX Users widget.

tools.name: get_metrics_overview
tools.description: Weekly and monthly aggregates for new users, active users, trading volume, and Orderly revenue. For daily historical totals use get_dashboard_main.

tools.name: get_volume_segments
tools.description: Weekly trading volume split by market-maker vs retail segment. Drives the Volume Segments widget.

tools.name: get_stake_users
tools.description: Weekly average active stakers. Drives the Stake Users widget.

tools.name: get_stake_vs_supply
tools.description: Weekly ORDER staked vs circulating supply and staking ratio. Drives the Stake vs Supply widget.

tools.name: get_omnivault_tvl
tools.description: Weekly average TVL per OmniVault (USD millions). Drives the OmniVault TVL widget.

tools.name: get_distributor_stats
tools.description: Referral distributor statistics: invitee counts, graduated invitees, revenue share, and fee tier. Drives the Distributors widget. Returns an array of distributor rows.

tools.name: get_distributor_invitees
tools.description: Per-invitee detail for referral distributors: invite date, DEX, status, and 30D volume/revenue share. Returns an array of invitee rows.

tools.name: get_market_share
tools.description: Orderly's DEX perpetuals market share vs. other on-chain perp venues, computed from CoinGecko 24h derivatives volume and DefiLlama open interest. Drives the Market Share widget. Returns ranked protocols with volume, open interest, and share %.

tools.name: get_markets
tools.description: Snapshot of all active perpetual markets: the futures market list, 24h price changes, and per-symbol open interest. Drives the Markets page. Returns an object { markets, priceChanges, openInterest }. Optional search (a case-insensitive substring on the symbol), sort_by (24h_volume | 24h_change | open_interest | symbol), limit (max 200), and desc (default true) filter and rank the markets and trim the priceChanges / openInterest arrays to the same symbol set. Defaults to 50 markets in API order; pass limit: 200 for the full set.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring on the symbol (e.g. "btc", "sol", "perp_btc").

sort_by.description: Rank markets by this metric (default: API order).

limit.description: Max markets to return after filter/sort (default 50; max 200).

tools.name: get_market_detail
tools.description: Composite single-symbol bundle for the market detail page. Returns only the requested sections (default: all of market info, top-50 orderbook levels, recent trades, funding history, and OHLCV candles). Requesting fewer sections keeps the payload small. Drives the Price Chart, Orderbook, Recent Trades, and Funding Chart.

symbol.description: Perp symbol. Accepts a base tick (BTC) or full form (PERP_BTC_USDC).

include.description: Sections to return; omit for all.

tools.name: get_symbol_info
tools.description: Full configuration for a single perpetual symbol: leverage limits (1/base_imr), tick/lot sizes, price precision, and status flags. Returns the symbol info object.

symbol.description: Perp symbol: base tick (ETH) or full form.

tools.name: get_market_summary
tools.description: Live platform-wide market snapshot: 24h volume, open interest, trader counts, and fee totals across all symbols. For historical daily time series use get_dashboard_main; for weekly/monthly user aggregates use get_metrics_overview.

tools.name: get_funding_comparison
tools.description: Cross-exchange funding rate comparison: last value plus 1d/7d/30d averages per symbol across venues (Orderly vs. Binance, Bybit, etc.). Omit symbol for all symbols. For per-symbol 8h funding history use get_funding_rates.

symbol.description: Perp symbol: base tick (BTC) or full form; omit for all.

tools.name: get_recent_liquidations
tools.description: Recent individual liquidation events for one symbol: side, size, notional, mark/liquidation price, and the liquidated account. For daily liquidation totals aggregated across all symbols use get_daily_liquidations_by_symbol.

symbol.description: Perp symbol: base tick (BTC) or full form (PERP_BTC_USDC).

limit.description: Max events (default 50, max 500).

tools.name: get_top_traders
tools.description: Top addresses ranked by a chosen metric (notional, volume, PnL, or trade count) for a symbol or platform-wide. Paginated via cursor. Drives the Top Traders panel and Whale Leaderboard.

symbol.description: Perp symbol: base tick (BTC) or full form; omit for platform-wide.

limit.description: Page size (default 50, max 200).

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response — pass it back unchanged.

tools.name: get_whale_context
tools.description: Whale research bundle for a single address: account state (collateral, PnL), open positions, and recent trades. Requires an address; optionally scope to a broker or account_id. Drives the Whale Detail modal.

address.description: Wallet address (EVM 0x…).

tools.name: get_platform_positions
tools.description: Platform-wide open positions for a symbol (large-position liquidation-heatmap data). Returns up to 1000 positions filtered by minimum notional. Drives the Liquidation Heatmap.

symbol.description: Perp symbol: base tick (BTC) or full form.

tools.name: get_insurance_fund
tools.description: Orderly insurance fund balance, holdings, and status. Drives the Insurance Fund widget.

tools.name: get_leaderboard
tools.description: Daily trading leaderboard: realized PnL and perp volume per trader over a date range (YYYY-MM-DD). Supports pagination, broker/address filters, sort, and aggregation by address, account, or date. Drives the Leaderboard (trading) tab.

page.description: 1-based page (default 1).

sort.description: Default descending_realized_pnl.

address.description: Filter to a wallet address.

tools.name: get_positions
tools.description: Open-positions leaderboard: largest open positions by notional, optionally filtered by account, broker, or symbol. Drives the Leaderboard (positions) tab.

symbol.description: Perp symbol: base tick (BTC) or full form (PERP_BTC_USDC).

offset.description: Pagination offset (default 0).

limit.description: Page size (default 50, max 500).

tools.name: resolve_address
tools.description: Resolve a wallet address or account ID into its Orderly broker/account pairs. Accepts an EVM address (0x + 40 hex), a Solana address (43-44 base58 chars), or an account ID (0x + 64 hex). Returns an array of {broker_id, account_id, …} pairs for the identity. For address queries (not account IDs) each account is enriched with 90-day perp_volume and realized_pnl, sorted by volume descending — matching the Search results page. First step of the Explorer/address flow.

address.description: EVM address, Solana address, or Orderly account ID.

tools.name: get_events
tools.description: Historical trading events for an account: trades, settlements, liquidations, ADLs, and margin transfers (versioned v1/v2/v3 already flattened to a uniform shape). Time range is capped at 31 days; omit both times for the most recent page. Drives the address Events tab. Returns { events, nextCursor, pageSizeLimit, tradesCount }; pass the nextCursor back as the cursor param to fetch the next page.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor (the nextCursor value from a prior response). Do not construct this object yourself — only pass back the cursor you received.

tools.name: get_account_state
tools.description: Account snapshot for an address: collateral, margin ratios, 24h PnL, and all OPEN positions (qty, notional, entry/mark price, leverage, est. liquidation price). Drives the address Positions tab.

address.description: Wallet address (EVM 0x…).

tools.name: get_portfolio
tools.description: Daily account-value time series with cumulative PnL (equity curve) for an address, up to 365 days. Drives the Portfolio Chart on the address page.

address.description: Wallet address (EVM 0x…).

limit.description: Max snapshots (default 90, max 365).

tools.name: get_brokers
tools.description: Directory of all Orderly brokers (broker_id → human-readable broker_name), sorted by name. Use to label broker_id values returned by other tools.

tools.name: get_all_symbols
tools.description: Every known perp symbol (including delisted) as a hash→name map: {symbol, symbol_hash}. Use to resolve keccak256 symbol hashes in event/position data to display names. Active symbols are also available via get_markets.

tools.name: get_all_tokens
tools.description: Every known settlement/collateral token as a hash→name map: {token, token_hash}. Use to resolve keccak256 token hashes in settlement/fee fields to display names.

tools.name: open_market
tools.description: Navigate the user to a market detail page. Pass a base tick (BTC), the full form (PERP_BTC_USDC), or a broker-suffixed variant (PERP_AAPL_USDC_mythos). The page renders a graceful "Market Not Found" for unknown symbols, so no pre-validation is performed — the user lands on the right place regardless.

symbol.description: Market symbol (e.g. BTC, ETH, PERP_BTC_USDC).

tools.name: open_address
tools.description: Navigate the user to an address / account detail page. Accepts an EVM address (0x + 40 hex), an Orderly account_id (0x + 64 hex), or a Solana base58 address. Solana addresses are url-safe-base64 encoded to match in-app AddressLink links.

address.description: EVM address, Solana address, or Orderly account_id.

tools.name: focus_widget
tools.description: Scroll a dashboard widget into the user's view and highlight it briefly. Only widgets present on the current page can be focused (widgets render on specific pages, not everywhere). Use get_site_overview to learn which widgets live where.

tools.name: share_widget
tools.description: Open the share dialog for a dashboard widget, presenting the user with the widget's embed/share link. Only works when the widget and its share button are rendered on the current page (share buttons are hidden on embeds).

tools.name: get_current_view
tools.description: Read-only snapshot of what the user is currently looking at: the current route/URL, the page area, the active market symbol (base tick) when on a market page, and the list of widget ids currently rendered on screen (valid inputs for focus_widget / share_widget / get_widget_url). Call this to ground yourself in the user's current view before navigating or pointing at a widget. After open_market or open_address, call this to confirm the destination rendered — the result includes a status (loading | ready | not-found | error) and, when available, a short summary.

tools.name: get_widget_url
tools.description: Return the embeddable share URL for a dashboard widget — the same link the Share dialog produces — without opening any UI. Use this to give the user a link to a widget. Market widgets (market-*) take an optional symbol.

widget_id.description: Widget id to get a link for.

symbol.description: Symbol for market widgets (e.g. BTC). Ignored for non-market widgets.

tools.name: fiyat_gecmisi
tools.description: Bir kategorinin medyan/ortalama fiyat zaman-serisini (günlük snapshot) döndürür + dönem medyan değişim yüzdesi. Fiyat trendi/enflasyon soruları için. Kategori slug ile.

tools.name: sozluk_terim
tools.description: Sektör terimleri sözlüğünü döndürür. Terim verilmezse tüm terimleri; terim verilince o terimin tanımını + ilgili aramayı. Makine/ekipman terimlerini (ekskavatör, motosaat, CE belgesi, TCO…) açıklamak için.

tools.name: finansman_karsilastir
tools.description: Bir tutar için 12/24/36/48/60 ay vadelerinde taksit karşılaştırma matrisi döndürür (aylık taksit, toplam geri ödeme, toplam faiz). Sunucu-taraflı, birden çok vade tek çağrıda.

tools.name: stok_durumu
tools.description: Bir ilanın güncel durumunu döndürür: aktif/preorder/discontinued + son güncelleme tarihi. İlan slug ile.

tools.name: trend_kategoriler
tools.description: Son 30 günün trend aramalarını (en çok aranan terimler) ve popüler kategorileri döndürür. "Şu an ne aranıyor / gündemde ne var" için.

tools.name: fiyat_dagilimi
tools.description: Bir kategorinin fiyat dağılımını döndürür: histogram (fiyat aralıkları + adet) + özet (min/P10/P25/medyan/P75/P90/max/ortalama TL). "X ne kadar, fiyatlar nasıl dağılıyor" soruları için. Kategori slug ile.

tools.name: benzer_fiyatli
tools.description: Verilen bütçeye en yakın ilanları bir kategoride bulur (gauss yakınlık). Kategori slug + fiyat (TL) ile; opsiyonel adet. "500.000 TL bütçeyle hangi ekskavatörler" gibi.

tools.name: satici_kategorileri
tools.description: Bir satıcının hangi kategorilerde kaç aktif ilanı olduğunu döndürür (satıcının uzmanlık alanı). Satıcı slug ile.

tools.name: kategori_agaci
tools.description: Tüm ilan kategorilerini TAM hiyerarşik ağaç olarak (üst kategori → alt kategoriler) ilan sayılarıyla tek çağrıda döndürür. Her düğümde dogrudan_ilan + toplam_ilan (alt-ağaç rollup). Kategori yapısını keşfetmek için kategori_gez'e göre daha zengindir.

tools.name: kategori_ozet
tools.description: Bir kategorinin pazar özetini döndürür: toplam ilan, satıcı sayısı, fiyat bandı (min/ortalama/max TL) ve popüler üretici markaları. "Forklift pazarı nasıl?" gibi sorular için. Kategori slug ile çağrılır.

tools.name: finansman_hesapla
tools.description: Makine alımı için basit leasing/taksit hesaplar. Yerel hesap, PII gerektirmez.

tools.name: talep_durumu

tools.name: arama_kaydet

tools.name: teklif_gonder

tools.name: karsilastirma_listesi

tools.name: get_project_state
tools.description: Overview of the whole pixel art project: palette with indices, all sprites (ids, names, sizes, kinds, frame counts), which sprite/frame is on the human's screen, and tilemap info. Call this first to ground yourself.

tools.name: read_sprite
tools.description: Read one frame of a sprite as ASCII art rows plus a color legend, so you can see exactly what the human is drawing. '.' = transparent; other characters use the 64-symbol palette alphabet returned in the legend.

spriteId.description: Sprite id. Defaults to the active sprite.

layerId.description: Layer id. Defaults to the first layer.

tools.name: set_pixels
tools.description: Paint specific pixels on a sprite frame. Each valid requested pixel is applied in order, one cell at a time on the page. Use fill_region or flood_fill for bulk areas.

pixels.description: List of pixel changes, applied one cell at a time, e.g. [{"x":3,"y":4,"color":"#38b764"}]

color.description: Color to paint. Use a palette index (number), a hex string like '#38b764' (auto-added to the palette), 'transparent', or null to erase.

allFrames.description: Apply the same change to every frame.

layerId.description: Layer id. Defaults to the first layer.

tools.name: fill_region
tools.description: Fill a rectangular region of a sprite frame with one color. Great for blocking in base shapes quickly.

color.description: Color to paint. Use a palette index (number), a hex string like '#38b764' (auto-added to the palette), 'transparent', or null to erase.

tools.name: flood_fill
tools.description: Bucket-fill: starting at x,y, replace all connected pixels of the same color with the new color (transparent counts as a color). Fails clearly if the start pixel is out of bounds.

color.description: Color to paint. Use a palette index (number), a hex string like '#38b764' (auto-added to the palette), 'transparent', or null to erase.

tools.name: clear_frame
tools.description: Erase every pixel of one sprite frame, making it fully transparent.

tools.name: transform_sprite
tools.description: Apply a geometric transform to a sprite. Ops: flip_h, flip_v, rotate_90 (clockwise), rotate (RotSprite-style nearest-neighbor angle in degrees), shift (wrap-around move by dx/dy), outline (adds outlineColor around silhouettes). Applies to all frames unless frameIndices given.

angle.description: rotate only: clockwise angle in degrees; keeps the sprite dimensions

color.description: outline only: outline color (defaults to palette index 0)

tools.name: replace_color
tools.description: Swap every occurrence of one palette color for another across a sprite (or the whole project if no spriteId). Accepts palette indices or hex strings.

from.description: Color to replace.

to.description: Replacement color ('transparent'/null erases).

spriteId.description: Scope to one sprite; omit for all sprites.

layerId.description: Scope to one layer; omit for all layers.

tools.name: add_palette_color
tools.description: Add a new hex color to the shared project palette and get its index back.

tools.name: set_palette_alpha
tools.description: Set the selected palette entry's opacity from 0 to 1 without changing its color index.

tools.name: move_palette_color
tools.description: Reorder a palette entry while remapping all pixel indices so the artwork keeps its appearance.

tools.name: set_active_sprite
tools.description: Switch the human's editor view to a given sprite (and optionally frame). Use this to show them something you made or want them to review.

tools.name: add_frame
tools.description: Add a new animation frame to a character sprite, copying an existing frame by default so it can be nudged into the next pose.

copyFrameIndex.description: Frame to duplicate. Defaults to the last frame.

layerId.description: Layer id. Defaults to the selected layer.

tools.name: delete_frame
tools.description: Delete one animation frame from a sprite. Requires confirm:true. Refuses to delete a sprite's last remaining frame.

layerId.description: Layer id. Defaults to the selected layer.

confirm.description: Must be true to perform the deletion

tools.name: link_frame
tools.description: Link two cels on one layer so future pixel edits stay synchronized across both frames.

targetIndex.description: Zero-based cel to link it with

layerId.description: Layer id. Defaults to the selected layer.

tools.name: unlink_frame
tools.description: Detach one cel from its linked group so it can be edited independently.

layerId.description: Layer id. Defaults to the selected layer.

tools.name: add_layer
tools.description: Create an empty animation layer above the selected layer. It starts with matching cels so it can be painted immediately.

spriteId.description: Sprite id; defaults to the active sprite.

aboveLayerId.description: Insert above this layer; defaults to the top.

tools.name: duplicate_layer
tools.description: Copy a layer, including every cel, and place the copy directly above it.

tools.name: delete_layer
tools.description: Delete a layer after explicit confirmation. A sprite must keep at least one layer.

tools.name: move_layer
tools.description: Move a layer one slot up or down in the stack. Direction 1 moves toward the top.

tools.name: set_layer_properties
tools.description: Update a layer name, visibility, lock, opacity, or blend mode.

tools.name: set_animation_preview
tools.description: Control playback mode, tagged range, speed, and onion-skin display without changing sprite pixels.

tools.name: set_canvas_options
tools.description: Set zoom, grid, pixel-perfect stroke, shading ink, tiled preview, and dither brush options. The default canvas is a 256x256 logical grid displayed at 1px per cell; zoom in for detailed editing.

tools.name: add_frame_tag
tools.description: Create a named animation section over a range of frames, such as idle or walk.

tools.name: delete_frame_tag
tools.description: Delete a named animation section after explicit confirmation.

tools.name: rename_sprite
tools.description: Rename an existing sprite (e.g. after giving an untitled sprite an identity).

tools.name: add_sprite
tools.description: Create a new empty sprite (character, item, or tile for the tileset). It becomes the active sprite so the human sees it immediately. Character sprites default to 4 empty animation frames and items/tiles default to 1; pass frameCount to choose another count. Optionally copy dimensions/content from an existing sprite.

kind.description: 'tile' adds it to the tileset for map painting.

copyFromId.description: Clone pixels from this sprite id if sizes match.

frameCount.description: Animation frame count. Defaults to 4 for characters and 1 for items/tiles.

tools.name: get_tilemap
tools.description: Read the tilemap grid as ASCII rows where each token maps to a tileset sprite via the returned legend. Maps with more than 64 tiles use two-character tokens and return tokenWidth: 2.

tools.name: ensure_tilemap
tools.description: Create the project tilemap (or resize it, preserving overlapping cells) so tiles can be placed. Cols/rows are clamped to 2-64; default to 12x9 when unsure. No-ops with ok:true if the map already has these dimensions.

tools.name: place_tile
tools.description: Put one tileset sprite at a map coordinate. Pass tileId=null or 'empty' to clear the cell.

tools.name: fill_tiles
tools.description: Fill a rectangular region of the tilemap with one tileset sprite. Pass tileId=null or 'empty' to clear the area.

tools.name: critique_artwork
tools.description: Run the built-in pixel-art tutor analysis on a sprite: color discipline, value contrast, outline strength, noise, centering, symmetry, animation readiness. Returns a score, stats and findings with concrete tips. Use it to give the human structured feedback before/after you edit.

tools.name: export_project
tools.description: Serialize the entire project (palette, sprites, frames, tilemap) as JSON that can be re-imported via the import_project tool, the Sprites > Project file > Import button, or a share permalink.

tools.name: import_project
tools.description: Replace the current project with one previously exported via export_project (or a project file). The JSON is sanitized and validated; the human sees the imported project immediately.

tools.name: new_canvas
tools.description: Replace the current project with a fresh blank 256x256 logical canvas (one empty character sprite, default palette, no tilemap). Defaults to 4 empty animation frames; pass frameCount to choose another count. Requires confirm:true. The human sees the blank canvas immediately; use this to start a new drawing together.

confirm.description: Must be true to clear the current project

frameCount.description: Optional animation frame count; defaults to 4.

tools.name: start_tutorial
tools.description: Open the step-by-step guided tour overlay (shared with the room, so following humans see the same step) and jump to a step. Use it to walk the human through the whole app, then guide them to a first project together with your drawing tools.

step.description: Zero-based step index. Defaults to 0 (the beginning).

tools.name: tutorial_goto
tools.description: Jump the shared guided-tour overlay to a given step (0-based). Pair each step with a live demo using your drawing tools.

tools.name: end_tutorial
tools.description: Close the shared guided-tour overlay on this window (following humans keep their own copy until they close it). Call it when the tour is done so it never pops back up.

tools.name: rename_project
tools.description: Rename the current project (e.g. 'guided-tutorial-01' when starting a tutorial piece). The human sees the new title immediately.

tools.name: save_project
tools.description: Save the current project into the on-device library under a name (defaults to the project name), so it can be reopened later with open_project. Saved names are listed in get_project_state.

name.description: Slot name, e.g. 'guided-tutorial-01'. Defaults to the project name.

tools.name: open_project
tools.description: Replace the current project with a saved one from the on-device library. Requires confirm:true. The human sees the opened project immediately.

confirm.description: Must be true to replace the current project

tools.name: save_palette
tools.description: Save the current shared palette into the on-device library under a name, so it can be merged into any project later with apply_palette. Saved names are listed in get_project_state.

tools.name: apply_palette
tools.description: Merge a saved palette into the current project: missing colors are appended (up to 64), existing indices never move so artwork is untouched. Reports how many colors were added.

tools.name: scan_images_c2pa
tools.description: Scan every on the current page for C2PA Content Credentials (content provenance metadata) and return a per-image summary: whether a manifest is present, the claim generator (the tool that produced or edited the image), the title, and the signer name. Use this to find which images on a page carry provenance data. Note: provenance is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

limit.description: Maximum number of images to fetch and scan (default 25, max 100).

tools.name: inspect_image_c2pa
tools.description: Fetch a single image (by CSS selector or URL) and return its fully decoded C2PA manifest store: every manifest's claim, assertions (e.g. c2pa.actions edit history, schema.org authorship), and the COSE signature details (algorithm and signing-certificate identity). Provide exactly one of `selector` or `url`. Note: the signature is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

selector.description: CSS selector for an element on the page.

url.description: Image URL (absolute, or relative to the current page) to fetch and inspect.

tools.name: scan_images_c2pa
tools.description: Scan every on the current page for C2PA Content Credentials (content provenance metadata) and return a per-image summary: whether a manifest is present, the claim generator (the tool that produced or edited the image), the title, and the signer name. Use this to find which images on a page carry provenance data. Note: provenance is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

limit.description: Maximum number of images to fetch and scan (default 25, max 100).

tools.name: inspect_image_c2pa
tools.description: Fetch a single image (by CSS selector or URL) and return its fully decoded C2PA manifest store: every manifest's claim, assertions (e.g. c2pa.actions edit history, schema.org authorship), and the COSE signature details (algorithm and signing-certificate identity). Provide exactly one of `selector` or `url`. Note: the signature is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

selector.description: CSS selector for an element on the page.

url.description: Same-origin image URL (absolute same-origin, or relative to the current page) to fetch and inspect. Cross-origin URLs are rejected.

tools.name: find_tool
tools.description: List the tools on 𓁹𓁹 (text, code, images, randomness, time, sharing) with the address of each. Give words to narrow the list. Each tool's page offers its own actions to agents once it is open.

query.description: Words to look for, such as "password" or "time zone". Leave out to list every tool.

tools.name: make_qr_code
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Make a QR code for text or a link, black on white with a one-module border: a PNG image to show or save, and the same code as SVG markup. Higher error correction survives more damage but holds less text. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

text.description: The text or link to encode.

size.description: The image's width and height in pixels, border included.

errorCorrection.description: How much of the code may be damaged and still scan: about 7%, 15%, 25% or 30%.

tools.name: make_ean13_barcode
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Make an EAN-13 retail barcode from 12 digits (the check digit is added) or 13 (the check digit is verified). For a 12-digit UPC-A code, put a 0 in front. Returns the number, the barcode as a PNG image to show or print, and the same barcode as svg markup. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

digits.description: 12 or 13 digits; spaces and hyphens are ignored.

tools.name: clean_up_lines
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Tidy a list of lines: trim each, drop empty ones, remove duplicates, and sort (natural order, so item2 comes before item10) or reverse. On the scratchpad's page, the pad's own text is used when none is given, and the pad is left as it is. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

text.description: Lines to tidy. On the scratchpad's page, leave it out to use the pad's text.

order.description: keep the order, sort asc or desc (natural: item2 before item10), or reverse it.

dedupe.description: Keep the first of each line that repeats.

trim.description: Take spaces off both ends of each line.

tools.name: search_directory
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Search a hand-picked directory of 118 long-lived websites (reference, archives, tools, learning, reading, maps and data, directories, the weird web) by name, description, address or group. Leave out the query to list them all. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

query.description: Words that must all appear, such as "public domain books". Every site when left out.

tools.name: base64_encode
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Encode text (as UTF-8) to base64, optionally the url-safe alphabet without padding. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

text.description: The text to encode, as its UTF-8 bytes.

urlSafe.description: Use - and _ and drop the = padding.

tools.name: base64_decode
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Decode standard or url-safe base64 back to UTF-8 text. Refuses input that is not base64 or does not decode to UTF-8 text. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

base64.description: Standard or url-safe base64; spaces, line breaks and missing padding are fine.

tools.name: hash_text
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Compute the md5, sha-1, sha-256, sha-384 and sha-512 digests of a text's UTF-8 bytes, in hex or base64, and check one against a digest you have. md5 is fine for spotting accidental corruption but broken for security. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

text.description: The text; its UTF-8 bytes are hashed, as they are, with no trimming.

uppercase.description: Uppercase hex; base64 has no case to choose.

compare.description: A digest to check against, such as one a download page lists: hex or base64, alone or as a line of a checksum file ("sha256: …", "SHA256 (file) = …"). Its length says which algorithm it is.

tools.name: hash_file
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Compute the md5, sha-1, sha-256, sha-384 and sha-512 digests of a file, such as a download whose checksum you want to check, and compare one with the digest you were given. Send the file as base64, up to 10 MB; on the hash page the file the visitor chose is hashed when none is sent, at any size, without leaving the browser. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

file.description: The file, as base64 or a data: URL. On the hash page, leave it out to use the file the visitor chose.

uppercase.description: Uppercase hex; base64 has no case to choose.

compare.description: A digest to check against, such as one a download page lists: hex or base64, alone or as a line of a checksum file ("sha256: …", "SHA256 (file) = …"). Its length says which algorithm it is.

tools.name: generate_ids
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Make a batch of ids from Web Crypto randomness: uuid v4 (random), uuid v7 (time-ordered), ulid (time-ordered, 26 characters), or short ids from an alphabet of your choosing. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

kind.description: v4: random uuid. v7: uuid that sorts by time. ulid: 26 characters, sorts by time. short: like nanoid, from an alphabet.

count.description: How many ids.

length.description: Short ids only; 21 when left out.

alphabet.description: Short ids only; the characters to draw from, each equally likely. Letters, digits, _ and - when left out.

tools.name: generate_passwords
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Make passwords (letters, digits and symbols, easily confused ones left out), passphrases (hyphen-joined words) or numeric pins, from Web Crypto randomness. Returns the values and their strength in bits. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

kind.description: password: letters, digits and symbols, easily confused ones left out. passphrase: words joined by hyphens. pin: digits.

length.description: Characters, or words for a passphrase. 20, 12 and 6 when left out.

count.description: How many to make.

tools.name: clean_code
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Format code as its language's usual formatter would: Prettier for JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, Markdown, YAML and the rest of the web; ruff for Python; gofmt for Go; clang-format for C, C++, C#, Java and Objective-C; sql-formatter for twenty SQL dialects; and more, named by the language's id. Code that does not parse returns the formatter's error. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

language.description: The language's id, such as python, typescript, cpp, postgresql or yaml.

indent.description: usual keeps the formatter's own: 4 spaces for Python, tabs for Go.

examples.code: select a,b from t where x=1

tools.name: format_json
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Check that text is valid JSON and lay it out with 2 or 4 spaces or tabs, or minify it. Numbers, key order and duplicate keys are kept exactly as written. Invalid JSON returns the parser's error. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

indent.description: Indentation, or minify for one line.

tools.name: escape_json_string
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Turn text into a JSON string literal, quotes and escapes included, ready to paste into JSON or JavaScript. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

text.description: Any text, line breaks and quotes included.

tools.name: unescape_json_string
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Turn a JSON string literal, in double quotes, back into the text it stands for. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

json.description: A JSON string literal, quotes included.

tools.name: parse_url
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Split an absolute URL into scheme, user, host, port, path, query, fragment and decoded query parameters. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

url.description: An absolute URL, scheme included.

tools.name: percent_encode
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Percent-encode text so it can sit in a URL path segment or query value. With form encoding, spaces become + as in submitted forms. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

text.description: The text to encode.

formEncoding.description: Spaces as +, as a submitted form writes them.

tools.name: percent_decode
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Decode percent-encoded text from a URL. With form encoding, + is read as a space. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

text.description: The percent-encoded text.

formEncoding.description: Read + as a space, as a submitted form means it.

tools.name: convert_case
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Rewrite text or an identifier in every common case at once: camel, pascal, snake, kebab, constant, dot, path, title, sentence, lower and upper. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

text.description: The text or identifier to rewrite, such as "user id", userId or USER_ID.

tools.name: convert_color
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Give a color as hex, rgb, hsl and oklch, each ready to paste into CSS. Accepts opaque hex, rgb(), hsl() and CSS color names such as rebeccapurple; the color page also reads oklch() and every other CSS color. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

color.description: The color, such as #1e90ff, rgb(30 144 255), hsl(210 100% 56%) or tomato.

tools.name: resize_image
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Resize an image, convert it between png, jpeg and webp, or both, and get it back as an image, with its size in pixels and bytes before and after. Give a width or a height to keep its proportions, or both to set each; give neither to only convert. A photo is turned upright as its orientation tag says. Send the image as base64, up to 10 MB and 16 megapixels: png, jpeg, webp or gif (its first frame). On the img page, the image the visitor chose is used when none is sent, the browser reads more formats, and avif can be written where it can. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

image.description: The image, as base64 or a data: URL. On the img page, leave it out to use the image the visitor chose.

format.description: What to write; the image's own format when left out (a gif becomes png). avif only on the img page, in a browser that writes it.

quality.description: For jpeg, webp and avif: higher is sharper and larger.

tools.name: diff_text
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Compare two texts line by line and return a unified listing: two spaces before a line both share, + before a line only in after, - before a line only in before. Up to 5,000 lines a side. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

ignoreSurroundingSpaces.description: Treat lines that differ only in leading or trailing spaces as the same.

tools.name: convert_timestamp
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Turn a unix timestamp (seconds or milliseconds) or a date such as 2026-08-21T12:00:00Z into UTC, ISO 8601 and both unix forms. Leave value out for the current moment. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

value.description: A date, such as 2026-08-21T12:00:00Z, or a unix timestamp in seconds or milliseconds. The current moment when left out.

unit.description: How to read a bare number; auto picks by size.

tools.name: count_text
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Count words, characters (as a person sees them), characters without spaces, Unicode code points, UTF-8 bytes, lines and sentences in a text, and estimate its reading time at 200 words a minute. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

text.description: The text to count.

tools.name: generate_lorem_ipsum
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Make lorem ipsum placeholder text: a number of paragraphs (short, medium or long), sentences or words. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

count.description: How many paragraphs, sentences or words; at most 100, 1,000 and 10,000.

paragraphLength.description: For paragraphs: how many sentences each has.

tools.name: random_numbers
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Pick up to 100 whole numbers between a minimum and a maximum, inclusive, optionally without repeats. The source is csrng (Web Crypto, fit for secrets; the default), trng (a public drand beacon whose signature is verified, so anyone can check the round later; needs the network) or prng (Math.random, not for security). Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

min.description: The smallest number that may come up.

count.description: How many numbers.

unique.description: Never pick the same number twice; then count can be no more than the range holds.

source.description: csrng: Web Crypto, fit for secrets. trng: a drand beacon, verified, that anyone can check later by its round; reaches the network. prng: Math.random, predictable.

tools.name: roll_dice
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Roll up to 100 dice of 2 to 1,000,000 sides. The source is csrng (Web Crypto; the default), trng (a public drand beacon whose signature is verified, so anyone can check the round later; needs the network) or prng (Math.random, predictable). Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

source.description: csrng: Web Crypto, fit for secrets. trng: a drand beacon, verified, that anyone can check later by its round; reaches the network. prng: Math.random, predictable.

tools.name: flip_coins
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Flip up to 100 coins. The source is csrng (Web Crypto; the default), trng (a public drand beacon whose signature is verified, so anyone can check the round later; needs the network) or prng (Math.random, predictable). Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

count.description: How many coins.

source.description: csrng: Web Crypto, fit for secrets. trng: a drand beacon, verified, that anyone can check later by its round; reaches the network. prng: Math.random, predictable.

tools.name: inspect_text
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] List every character in a text with its code point and UTF-8 bytes, naming the ones that are invisible or look like a space (zero-width, no-break, direction marks, control characters). With the ascii set, codes are ascii decimals and anything past 127 is marked. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

text.description: The text to look through, such as a line that should match another but does not.

set.description: ascii gives ascii decimals and marks anything past 127.

tools.name: look_up_character
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Find one character from the character itself, a decimal number, a U+ or 0x code, an html entity such as © or ©, or an ascii control name such as LF, and give its decimal, code point, UTF-8 bytes, html, javascript, css and url forms. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

query.description: One character, or a code or name for one: é, 233, U+00E9, 0xE9, é, é or LF.

tools.name: read_image_metadata
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Read the metadata inside an image: camera, lens, exposure, dates, gps position, color profile, dimensions and more, from exif, iptc, icc and the file's own headers, as "group · tag" fields. Reads jpeg, tiff, png, webp, heic, avif, gif and jpeg xl. Send the image as base64, up to 10 MB. On the metadata page, xmp is read too, and the image the visitor chose is used when none is sent. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

image.description: The image, as base64 or a data: URL. On the metadata page, leave it out to use the image the visitor chose.

tools.name: make_spectrogram
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Draw a sound's spectrogram: time left to right, frequency from 0 at the bottom to half the sample rate at the top, louder as brighter (white on black, 80 dB of range). Returns the picture as a PNG image with the sound's length, sample rate and channels. Send the sound as base64, up to 10 MB and about six minutes of stereo: wav, mp3, flac, ogg vorbis or opus. On the spectrogram page, the browser reads more formats (m4a, aac, webm) and the file the visitor chose is drawn when none is sent. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

audio.description: The sound, as base64 or a data: URL. On the spectrogram page, leave it out to use the file the visitor chose.

width.description: Pixels across: one column of the transform each.

height.description: Pixels from 0 Hz to the top frequency.

tools.name: convert_time_zone
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Say what a local date and time in one IANA time zone is in another, handling daylight saving: a time that never happens (the clock skipped it) is refused, and one that happens twice (the clock went back) uses the first unless told otherwise. Leave out dateTime for now. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

dateTime.description: Local date and time in the from zone, as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM. Now when left out.

from.description: IANA zone such as America/Chicago, or UTC.

to.description: IANA zone such as Asia/Tokyo.

occurrence.description: Which one, when the local time happens twice.

tools.name: calculate
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Evaluate an arithmetic expression: + - × ÷ (or * /), ^ for powers, parentheses, sqrt, abs, round, floor, ceil, pi and e. A percent divides by 100, so 200 * 10% is 20. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

tools.name: convert_units
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Convert a number between units of one quantity. Units, by symbol: length m cm mm km in ft yd mi; weight kg g mg lb oz t; temperature °C °F K; area m² km² ft² ha ac; volume L mL m³ gal qt pt cup fl oz; speed km/h mph m/s kn; duration s ms min h d wk; data B bit kB MB GB TB KiB MiB GiB TiB. Names such as "miles" work too. Volume units are US liquid; kB, MB and GB are powers of 1,000 and KiB, MiB and GiB of 1,024. Runs on the eyes.tools server, which keeps nothing it is sent.

value.description: The amount to convert.

from.description: Unit symbol or name, such as km or kilometers.

to.description: A unit of the same quantity, by symbol or name.

tools.name: read_scratchpad
tools.description: Read the text in the visitor's scratchpad, which is kept in this browser and autosaves.

tools.name: add_to_scratchpad
tools.description: Add text at the end of the visitor's scratchpad, on a new line, and save it in this browser. What is already there is kept.

tools.name: set_brand_colors
tools.description: Set primary, secondary, and/or accent colors. Generates shade scales and accepts hex, rgb/rgba, or CSS names.

tools.name: assign_color_role
tools.description: Recolor a widget region by role, palette family, and intensity.

tools.name: set_typography
tools.description: Set font family, size, weight, and line height.

tools.name: set_roundness
tools.description: Set roundness by style or granular radius values.

radius.description: Granular px or CSS length overrides.

tools.name: set_color_scheme
tools.description: Set light/dark/auto color scheme and optional edit target.

tools.name: apply_preset
tools.description: Apply a complete built-in preset, replacing theme tokens. Call get_theme_overview to list preset ids.

tools.name: configure_widget
tools.description: Toggle launcher position, feature flags, and message layout.

tools.name: set_copy_and_suggestions
tools.description: Set welcome copy, input placeholder, send label, and suggestion chips.

tools.name: set_theme_fields
tools.description: Advanced escape hatch: set fields by id or raw dot-path. Values are validated when metadata exists.

tools.name: check_contrast
tools.description: Run WCAG checks over key text/background pairs.

level.description: Default: AA.

tools.name: manage_session
tools.description: Undo, redo, reset defaults, or export the theme snapshot.

tools.name: screenshot_preview
tools.description: Capture the current rendered state of the theme preview as an image: exactly what the user sees. Returns one JPEG per visible preview frame (two when a compare mode is active, labeled e.g. Light/Dark). Call after applying a batch of theme changes to verify the visual result, especially when matching a reference image.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Search the product catalog by free-text query (e.g. 'waterproof trail shoe', 'blue running', 'jacket'). Returns matching products with SKU, title, brand, color, price, imageUrl, and imageAlt.

tools.name: view_product
tools.description: Look at one product in detail by SKU (from search_products results). Highlights it on the page and returns its full description plus imageUrl/imageAlt. Read-only.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a product to the shopper's cart by SKU (from search_products results). Returns the updated cart so you can confirm the running total.

tools.name: remove_from_cart
tools.description: Remove a product from the cart by SKU, or reduce its quantity. Omit quantity to remove the line entirely. Returns the updated cart.

tools.name: apply_promo
tools.description: Apply a promo code to the cart (e.g. TRAIL10, TRAILVIP, SUMMIT20). Returns whether it was accepted and the updated cart with the discount applied.

tools.name: get_calendar_state
tools.description: Read the current calendar state: current local date-time, selected date, visible week, timezone, total event count, visible events, and the valid users (with the userIds create_event accepts). Call this before creating or editing events. All event times are local wall-clock times in the calendar timezone.

tools.name: get_events
tools.description: List calendar events. Optionally filter by month in YYYY-MM format, userId, or a text search over title/description/location.

search.description: Optional text search.

tools.name: find_availability
tools.description: Find open slots on a date, optionally for a single user. Workday is 9am-5pm local time. Returned slot times are local wall-clock times in the calendar timezone.

tools.name: select_date
tools.description: Move the calendar UI to a specific date without creating an event.

tools.name: create_event
tools.description: Create a calendar event and render it on the page. startDate/endDate are LOCAL wall-clock times in the calendar timezone, formatted YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm: never append "Z" or a UTC offset (any offset is ignored and the stated clock time is used as-is). Use a userId from get_calendar_state.

title.description: Event title.

startDate.description: Event start as local wall-clock time, e.g. 2026-06-11T08:00. No "Z" or UTC offset.

endDate.description: Event end as local wall-clock time, e.g. 2026-06-11T09:00. No "Z" or UTC offset.

location.description: Optional location or video link.

tools.name: update_event
tools.description: Update an existing event by eventId. Only supplied fields are changed. startDate/endDate are LOCAL wall-clock times (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm, no "Z" or UTC offset).

startDate.description: Local wall-clock time, e.g. 2026-06-11T08:00. No "Z" or UTC offset.

endDate.description: Local wall-clock time, e.g. 2026-06-11T09:00. No "Z" or UTC offset.

tools.name: delete_event
tools.description: Delete an event from the calendar by eventId.

tools.name: get_deck_overview
tools.description: Read the deck: title, active theme, slide count, and per-slide {id, position, title, elementCount}. Call this first to orient yourself; positions are 1-based.

tools.name: get_slide
tools.description: Read one slide's full contents: every element with its id, geometry, and style. Call this before editing a slide's elements. Defaults to the slide open in the editor.

position.description: 1-based slide position (alternative to slideId).

tools.name: get_selection
tools.description: Read the elements the user currently has selected on the canvas: ids, types, geometry, and styles. Use this whenever the user says 'this', 'these', or refers to something they clicked.

tools.name: list_themes
tools.description: List the available deck themes with their palettes and fonts.

tools.name: goto_slide
tools.description: Open a slide in the editor (navigation only: changes nothing).

position.description: 1-based slide position.

tools.name: add_slide
tools.description: Insert a new slide from a layout. 'title' = centered title + subtitle; 'title-body' = heading + body text; 'two-col' = heading + two text columns (body fills the left, right starts empty); 'blank' = empty. Returns the new slide id and its element ids so you can refine them with update_element.

title.description: Slide heading text.

body.description: Body text. Use \n for line breaks, • for bullets.

position.description: 1-based position to insert at; defaults to the end of the deck.

tools.name: duplicate_slide
tools.description: Copy a slide (and all its elements) right after the original. Returns the new slide id.

position.description: 1-based position of the slide to copy.

tools.name: delete_slide
tools.description: Permanently remove a slide and all its elements.

position.description: 1-based slide position.

tools.name: reorder_slides
tools.description: Move a slide to a new 1-based position. Returns the resulting slide order.

position.description: 1-based target position.

tools.name: set_slide_props
tools.description: Update a slide's title and/or background color.

position.description: 1-based slide position.

background.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

tools.name: add_element
tools.description: Add one element (text box, rectangle, ellipse, line, or image) to a slide. Lines draw from the top-left to the bottom-right corner of their bounding box. Returns the new element id.

slideId.description: Target slide id; defaults to the slide open in the editor.

x.description: Slide units; the canvas is 960 wide x 540 tall, origin at the top-left.

rotation.description: Degrees clockwise.

z.description: Stacking order; higher renders on top.

text.description: Text elements only. Use \n for line breaks.

fontFamily.description: Font stack, or a theme token: 'theme.heading' / 'theme.body'. Prefer tokens.

color.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

fill.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

stroke.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

src.description: Image URL, or 'placeholder' for a styled placeholder block.

tools.name: update_element
tools.description: Merge a partial patch into one element: position, size, text, and style in a single call. Omitted keys are unchanged. Returns the updated element.

patch.description: Partial element properties to merge; omitted keys are unchanged.

x.description: Slide units; the canvas is 960 wide x 540 tall, origin at the top-left.

rotation.description: Degrees clockwise.

z.description: Stacking order; higher renders on top.

text.description: Text elements only. Use \n for line breaks.

fontFamily.description: Font stack, or a theme token: 'theme.heading' / 'theme.body'. Prefer tokens.

color.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

fill.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

stroke.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

src.description: Image URL, or 'placeholder' for a styled placeholder block.

tools.name: delete_elements
tools.description: Permanently remove one or more elements by id.

tools.name: align_elements
tools.description: Align elements to the slide or to their shared bounding box, and/or space them evenly along an axis (distribute needs 3+ elements; the first/last stay put). Same shape as align_selection. Returns the new positions.

distribute.description: Space the elements evenly along this axis; needs 3+ elements.

relativeTo.description: Default 'slide'. 'selection-bounds' aligns within the group's own bounding box.

tools.name: set_deck_title
tools.description: Set the deck's title.

tools.name: apply_theme
tools.description: Switch the deck's theme. Every element using theme tokens ('theme.accent', 'theme.heading', …) restyles across ALL slides.

tools.name: enter_presenter_mode
tools.description: Enter full-screen presenter mode. NOTE: this replaces your editing tools with presentation controls (next_slide, prev_slide, jump_to_slide, exit_presenter_mode) until the show ends.

position.description: 1-based slide to start from; defaults to slide 1.

persona-chat.dev.blurb: Get theme overview, Set brand colors and Assign color role.
