tools.name: styles_make_component
tools.description: Moves selected layers and their motion into a linked component, replacing them with an instance. Like Group, uses selected siblings in the first selected layer's parent and leaves other parents alone. Adjacent layers keep their appearance; non-adjacent layers change stacking as Group does, at the first selected sibling's stack position. Returns componentId and instanceId.

artboardId.description: Artboard id. Defaults to the first artboard.

tools.name: styles_add_instance
tools.description: Places a linked component at its own size, centred by default. Returns instanceId.

artboardId.description: Artboard id. Defaults to the first artboard.

tools.name: styles_update_instance
tools.description: Merges layer overrides and changes offset (ms), loop or the linked component. resetOverrides clears all overrides first; an empty layer override clears that layer.

artboardId.description: Artboard id. Defaults to the first artboard.

tools.name: styles_list_components
tools.description: Lists each component id, name, width, height and number of instances across the design.

tools.name: styles_set_document
tools.description: Sets name, export credit (default on), 3D mode, watermark or film transitions. Fetch nested fields with describe_schema domain:command name:set_document.

anyOf.description: Fields/example: describe_schema {domain:"command",name:"set_document"}, property mark.

tools.name: styles_add_artboard
tools.description: Adds an artboard (one image or video when you export). Give a format id (x-16x9, x-1x1, x-4x5, x-9x16, x-header, ig-post, ig-square, ig-story, ...) or a width and height. Optionally copy another artboard.

tools.name: styles_update_artboard
tools.description: Changes an artboard: name, width, height (or format id), duration (ms), fps, background, bgFx {noise, blur, vignette}, camera {zoom, x, y, rotation, rx, ry}, vfx {type, intensity}. Resizing lays the design out again for the new shape (keepLayout false leaves layers where they are).

artboardId.description: Artboard id. Defaults to the first artboard.

keepLayout.description: When resizing, scale layer positions to the new size (default true).

tools.name: styles_add_layer
tools.description: Adds a layer on top, at index, or inside parentId. Requires layer.type; fetch its fields/defaults with describe_schema domain:layer. Returns layerId.

artboardId.description: Artboard id. Defaults to the first artboard.

index.description: 0 is the bottom. Default: top.

tools.name: styles_update_layer
tools.description: Changes any properties of a layer (position x/y is the centre, width, height, rotation, scale, opacity 0..1, rx/ry tilt in degrees, shadow, blur, fill, text, style, media, model, finish, frame...). Nested objects like style, media, browser and shadow are merged, so you can send only what changes.

artboardId.description: Artboard id. Defaults to the first artboard.

tools.name: styles_delete_layers
tools.description: Deletes layers (and their animations).

artboardId.description: Artboard id. Defaults to the first artboard.

tools.name: styles_add_animation
tools.description: Animates a layer or @artboard camera. Requires anim.kind, target, start, end; end > start. Fetch kind fields with describe_schema domain:animation. Returns animId.

artboardId.description: Artboard id. Defaults to the first artboard.

replaceId.description: Replace this animation in the same command.

tools.name: styles_list_layers
tools.description: Lists the layers of an artboard (id, type, name, box) from bottom to top, flattened, with their parent group.

artboardId.description: Artboard id. Defaults to the first artboard.

tools.name: styles_describe_schema
tools.description: Returns detailed JSON input schema, example and shared vocabulary on demand. Domains: layer (type or patch), animation (kind or patch), document (doc/artboard/background/bgFx/camera/mark/film/asset/audio/fill/textStyle/easing), command (any edit_design verb). Omit name to list topics. Fetch before constructing complex payloads; schemas include all supported fields and constraints.

name.description: Omit to list names. layer: type or patch; animation: kind or patch; document: part; command: editing verb.

tools.name: styles_list_templates
tools.description: Lists templates (id, name, category, format, tags). Start with create_design {template:id}.

tools.name: styles_list_formats
tools.description: Lists sizes for artboards. Use a format id with create_design or add_artboard.

tools.name: styles_list_devices
tools.description: Lists device model ids, finishes and screen sizes for add_layer.

tools.name: styles_list_layouts
tools.description: Lists device layouts for edit_design → apply_layout.

tools.name: styles_list_backgrounds
tools.description: Lists up to 150 background presets. Pass bg and fx to update_artboard.

tools.name: styles_list_fonts
tools.description: Lists installed font families and weights for text style. Choose an exact family name.

tools.name: styles_replace_design
tools.description: Restores a full validated document. get_design.docId becomes doc.id in the snapshot. Undo brings back the previous design.

doc.description: Full snapshot; describe_schema {domain:"document",name:"doc"}. Restore get_design with doc.id = docId.

tools.name: styles_make_release_kit
tools.description: Makes four editable artboards from supplied release notes and an optional screenshotAssetId already in this design. No content is fetched. An existing kit updates its common content while preserving layout. Otherwise it replaces the current design; Undo restores it. Submit all common fields on updates; omitted optional fields reset to defaults. Returns named artboard ids; render Release motion as video.

tools.name: styles_make_post_film
tools.description: Makes an animated social post card from supplied text, name and handle. Nothing is fetched.

tools.name: styles_make_milestone
tools.description: Makes an animated celebration of a number, with optional growth history.

tools.name: styles_make_code_video
tools.description: Makes an animated code window from supplied code.

tools.name: styles_render_video
tools.description: Renders MP4, WebM or GIF in this browser and returns a browser-local blob URL. Default short side 720, fps 30. film:true plays all artboards.

tools.name: styles_export_lottie
tools.description: Exports Lottie JSON in this browser. Default Light scale 0.5; Sharp scale 1. Returns a browser-local blob URL and notes.

tools.name: styles_get_design
tools.description: Reads the open design. Browser designId is its local document id; remote designIds are different.

tools.name: styles_create_design
tools.description: Starts an empty design or a template in this editor. Undo brings back the previous design. Default format x-4x5.

tools.name: styles_apply_template
tools.description: Replaces the open design with a template. Media is kept; undo restores the previous design.

tools.name: styles_edit_design
tools.description: Applies up to 80 edits atomically, all or none, as a single undo step. steps.command lists every verb; fetch input fields/examples with describe_schema domain:command name:<verb>.

steps.description: Atomic; use existing or explicitly assigned ids. Read returned ids in a prior call.

tools.name: styles_add_icon
tools.description: Adds an editable Lucide path; x/y default to the artboard centre. Find names with search_icons.

strokeWidth.description: Line width in the icon’s 24 px grid.

tools.name: styles_search_icons
tools.description: Finds up to 20 Lucide icon names by words. Use a returned name with add_icon.

tools.name: styles_paste_layers
tools.description: Pastes layers and linked components from this local document. fromDesignId must equal get_design.designId. To import another document, use replace_design first.

fromDesignId.description: Design to copy from (remote), or current document id (browser).

tools.name: styles_add_media
tools.description: Adds a screenshot or image from base64 (up to 3 MB) or a public URL via the server’s safe fetch. deviceId explicitly replaces a screenshot; otherwise only an empty device is used. place defaults to device.

tools.name: styles_add_media_from_url
tools.description: Compatibility alias for add_media {url,place:"layer"}. Images download through the same-origin safe-fetch route, avoiding CORS. Videos must be uploaded in the editor.

tools.name: styles_select_artboard
tools.description: Shows an existing artboard. Read artboard ids with get_design.

tools.name: styles_play
tools.description: Plays or pauses the preview, or seeks to t milliseconds (clamped to this artboard’s duration).

tools.name: styles_undo
tools.description: Run undo in the editor’s shared history. Batch edits are one history step.

tools.name: styles_redo
tools.description: Run redo in the editor’s shared history. Batch edits are one history step.

tools.name: styles_see_design
tools.description: Returns a preview at t milliseconds (default after intros, matching remote MCP).

tools.name: styles_render_image
tools.description: Returns PNG, JPEG or WebP bytes as image content for the agent. scale 0.25–2, default 1. made with styles is included unless credit:false.

tools.name: styles_export_image
tools.description: Downloads PNG, JPG or WebP to the person’s browser. Scale 1–4 (default 1); larger exports take longer. Returns image content too. Use render_image for agent inspection.

tools.name: bankgraph.get_site_context
tools.description: Read the current Bankgraph page, published FDIC quarter, available research layouts, and the actions an agent can take before entering the research board.

tools.name: bankgraph.search_banks
tools.description: Search the current FDIC institution snapshot by name, state, activity, and asset size before opening a bank or starting a research board. Returns up to 50 banks and an offset for the next page.

query.description: Bank name, city, or FDIC certificate search text.

items.description: Two-letter state code.

assetMin.description: Minimum assets in FDIC USD thousands; 50,000,000 means $50B.

assetMax.description: Maximum assets in FDIC USD thousands.

tools.name: bankgraph.navigate
tools.description: Move this tab to any Bankgraph surface: the system homepage, research board, institution directory, economy, methodology, or a bank profile. A research destination can carry a question, layout, banks, states, asset range, and reporting quarter into the full board toolset. Research resumes the saved board unless fresh is true or the blank layout is requested.

question.description: Research question to place on the board.

template.description: Optional research layout. Use blank when the agent should compose the board.

cert.description: FDIC certificate number when destination is bank.

certs.description: FDIC certificate numbers to select on a research board.

items.description: Two-letter state code.

assetMin.description: Minimum assets in FDIC USD thousands.

assetMax.description: Maximum assets in FDIC USD thousands.

tools.name: bankgraph.set_appearance
tools.description: Switch every Bankgraph surface in this browser between the day and night themes.

tools.name: bankgraph.get_context
tools.description: Read the current page, screen, selected banks, exact comparison pair, chart history, peer cohort, takeaways, watchlist intent, board presentation, data date, and revisions. Use this before editing and after a person changes the board.

tools.name: bankgraph.read_current_screen
tools.description: Read the exact current screen recipe and its ranked bank records without changing the workspace. Returns 25 complete records by default and up to 50, shrinking a page only when its serialized payload requires it. Each cursor is bound to the workspace revision, full filter definition, result revision, and visible ordering.

pageSize.description: Complete bank records requested for this page; defaults to 25.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page.

tools.name: bankgraph.configure_screen
tools.description: Replace the visible question, bank screen, and result order. The matching institutions become the current analysis cohort in the same order, up to 200 banks. Read bankgraph.get_context first and pass its revision as ifRevision. Conditions use AND and exclude missing values. Assets and deposits use FDIC USD thousands: 10,000,000 means $10 billion.

items.description: Two-letter US state or territory code.

assetMin.description: Minimum total assets in FDIC USD thousands; 10,000,000 means $10B.

assetMax.description: Maximum total assets in FDIC USD thousands; 10,000,000 means $10B.

metric.description: Assets and deposits use USD thousands; ratios use reported percent; offices and employees use counts.

value.description: Assets and deposits use FDIC USD thousands; 10,000,000 means $10B. Ratios use reported percent.

upperValue.description: Upper bound in the selected metric's raw unit.

ifRevision.description: Only apply if the workspace still has this revision.

tools.name: bankgraph.configure_comparison
tools.description: Change only the requested part of the live comparison and preserve everything else. Use bankMode add or remove for spoken follow-ups such as ‘add Citi’; replace is the default when certs are supplied. Metrics, dates, chart style, and focus are independently optional. Read bankgraph.get_context once after a person changes the board, then pass its revision.

items.description: FDIC certificate number.

bankMode.description: How certs change the current banks. When omitted, supplied certs replace the selection; omitted certs keep it.

items.description: Metric available in the linked workspace.

metricMode.description: How metrics change the current measures. When omitted, supplied metrics replace them; omitted metrics keep them.

asOfQuarter.description: Quarter-end date YYYYMMDD or YYYYQn; quarter labels are normalized to 0331, 0630, 0930, or 1231.

comparisonMode.description: Basis for the exact quarter compared with asOfQuarter.

rangeStartQuarter.description: Quarter-end date YYYYMMDD or YYYYQn; quarter labels are normalized to 0331, 0630, 0930, or 1231.

customQuarter.description: Quarter-end date YYYYMMDD or YYYYQn; quarter labels are normalized to 0331, 0630, 0930, or 1231.

historyMode.description: Keep the chart window, replace it with historyFrom/historyTo, or clear it.

historyFrom.description: Quarter-end date YYYYMMDD or YYYYQn; quarter labels are normalized to 0331, 0630, 0930, or 1231.

historyTo.description: Quarter-end date YYYYMMDD or YYYYQn; quarter labels are normalized to 0331, 0630, 0930, or 1231.

ifRevision.description: Only apply if the workspace still has this revision.

tools.name: bankgraph.set_peer_cohort
tools.description: Replace the peer cohort recipe and exact exclusion list used by the comparison. Read bankgraph.get_context first and pass its revision as ifRevision. Latest-metric conditions use the same deterministic vocabulary and units as bank search.

items.description: Two-letter US state or territory code.

assetMin.description: Minimum total assets in FDIC USD thousands; 10,000,000 means $10B.

assetMax.description: Maximum total assets in FDIC USD thousands; 10,000,000 means $10B.

metric.description: Assets and deposits use USD thousands; ratios use reported percent; offices and employees use counts.

value.description: Assets and deposits use FDIC USD thousands; 10,000,000 means $10B. Ratios use reported percent.

upperValue.description: Upper bound in the selected metric's raw unit.

items.description: FDIC certificate number.

maximumPeers.description: WebMCP peer analyses support at most 200 banks per workspace.

ifRevision.description: Only apply if the workspace still has this revision.

tools.name: bankgraph.read_current_cohort
tools.description: Read the exact peer-cohort definition and complete member records. Returns 25 complete records by default and up to 50, shrinking only when required by the serialized result budget. Counts, coverage, freshness, and the cursor remain tied to the exact definition.

pageSize.description: Complete records requested in the selected section; defaults to 25.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page.

tools.name: bankgraph.analyze_cohort_change
tools.description: Compare one to six canonical measures across any two reporting quarters for the current workspace cohort. Publishes per-measure coverage, breadth, distributions, matched totals where addition is valid, gross movement, concentration, movers, and optional group movement into the visible workspace. Membership is held fixed across both quarters. boardSpan accepts quarter, half, three-quarter, or full; omission keeps current defaults. Read bankgraph.get_context first and pass its revision as ifRevision.

from.description: Quarter-end date YYYYMMDD or YYYYQn; quarter labels are normalized to 0331, 0630, 0930, or 1231.

to.description: Quarter-end date YYYYMMDD or YYYYQn; quarter labels are normalized to 0331, 0630, 0930, or 1231.

items.description: Metric available in the linked workspace.

groupPageSize.description: Groups requested in this response; defaults to 25.

groupCursor.description: Opaque group cursor from the previous response.

boardSpan.description: Width on the 12-column human board: quarter (3 columns), half (6), three_quarter (9), or full (12). When omitted, existing view-dependent half/full defaults are preserved.

ifRevision.description: Only apply if the workspace still has this revision.

tools.name: bankgraph.find_temporal_patterns
tools.description: Apply one declared multi-quarter predicate to one to three canonical measures for every current workspace cohort member. Supports k-of-n direction, streaks, cumulative change, acceleration or deceleration, and threshold crossings. Publishes matches with exact periods, coverage, trigger quarters, and bounded series. boardSpan accepts quarter, half, three-quarter, or full; omission keeps current defaults. Read bankgraph.get_context first and pass its revision as ifRevision.

items.description: Metric available in the linked workspace.

startPeriod.description: Quarter-end date YYYYMMDD or YYYYQn; quarter labels are normalized to 0331, 0630, 0930, or 1231.

endPeriod.description: Quarter-end date YYYYMMDD or YYYYQn; quarter labels are normalized to 0331, 0630, 0930, or 1231.

items.description: Quarter-end date YYYYMMDD or YYYYQn; quarter labels are normalized to 0331, 0630, 0930, or 1231.

pageSize.description: Matched banks requested; defaults to 25.

cursor.description: Opaque matched-bank cursor from the previous response.

boardSpan.description: Width on the 12-column human board: quarter (3 columns), half (6), three_quarter (9), or full (12). When omitted, existing view-dependent half/full defaults are preserved.

ifRevision.description: Only apply if the workspace still has this revision.

tools.name: bankgraph.analyze_financial_composition
tools.description: Analyze asset, funding, or loan mix for one selected bank, all selected banks, or the current workspace cohort. Uses ratios of sums over the same complete reporters, shows the loan-basis residual, and can compare quarters on a matched-reporter basis. Publishes the exact composition. boardSpan accepts quarter, half, three-quarter, or full; omission keeps current defaults. Read bankgraph.get_context first and pass its revision as ifRevision.

period.description: Quarter-end date YYYYMMDD or YYYYQn; quarter labels are normalized to 0331, 0630, 0930, or 1231.

compareFrom.description: Quarter-end date YYYYMMDD or YYYYQn; quarter labels are normalized to 0331, 0630, 0930, or 1231.

boardSpan.description: Width on the 12-column human board: quarter (3 columns), half (6), three_quarter (9), or full (12). When omitted, existing view-dependent half/full defaults are preserved.

ifRevision.description: Only apply if the workspace still has this revision.

tools.name: bankgraph.analyze_failure_patterns
tools.description: Build an exact-quarter event study for FDIC-reported failures, then rank the full eligible active-bank universe by descriptive trajectory similarity. The limit controls only returned analogues. This reusable visible view does not estimate failure probability or forecast. boardSpan accepts quarter, half, three-quarter, or full; omission keeps current defaults. Read bankgraph.get_context first and pass its revision as ifRevision.

boardSpan.description: Width on the 12-column human board: quarter (3 columns), half (6), three_quarter (9), or full (12). When omitted, existing view-dependent half/full defaults are preserved.

ifRevision.description: Only apply if the workspace still has this revision.

tools.name: bankgraph.read_research_board
tools.description: Read the exact visible answer order, focus, titles, spans, semantic bindings, and valid configuration fields on the current Bankgraph research board. The default is a fast structure-only read; then use bankgraph.read_board_block for exact data from each needed view. includeData focused or all is an optional bounded overview whose requested page size may be reduced to fit, without limiting continuation through read_board_block. No screenshot or DOM reading is needed.

includeData.description: Optional bounded exact-data overview. none (default) reads structure and per-view read affordances; focused reads one view; all samples every visible view. For complete data, follow with read_board_block.

pageSize.description: Requested values per visible view for the bounded overview; defaults to 2 and may be reduced to fit. Use bankgraph.read_board_block for up to 100 rows and continuation cursors.

tools.name: bankgraph.read_board_block
tools.description: Read one visible board view and a page of the exact source data behind it: rows, series, groups, components, members, or analogues. This is the semantic data used to draw the live view, not a screenshot. Failure analogue details default to 5 complete bank trajectories per page and support up to 10; other sections default to 25 and support up to 100.

tools.name: bankgraph.list_board_templates
tools.description: List the same curated research-board starting points available to a person in Bankgraph. Templates contain semantic live views and source-bound history, never copied result rows.

tools.name: bankgraph.apply_board_template
tools.description: Build one curated live board from the current selected banks, measures, and history window. Append it to the current board or replace the board; the same template is available in the human interface.

idPrefix.description: Optional stable prefix used only by legacy board hosts.

tools.name: bankgraph.add_workspace_view
tools.description: Add or replace one live semantic workspace view on the research board. The binding follows the current comparison, banks, metrics, cohort, geography, or economic context as the shared workspace changes; it never stores snapshot rows. Choose quarter, half, three-quarter, or full width on the 12-column board.

title.description: Visible, natural-language view title.

view.description: Live semantic workspace view. Its current values are rendered from shared workspace state, not persisted snapshot rows.

span.description: Width on the 12-column human board: quarter (3 columns), half (6), three_quarter (9), or full (12).

tools.name: bankgraph.plot_metric_history
tools.description: Publish a source-bound bank history chart on the visible research board. The view stores bank certificates, canonical measures, dates, and presentation choices; Bankgraph loads the reported values. Choose quarter, half, three-quarter, or full width on the 12-column board according to the comparison density.

title.description: Visible, natural-language view title.

span.description: Width on the 12-column human board: quarter (3 columns), half (6), three_quarter (9), or full (12).

tools.name: bankgraph.publish_exact_table
tools.description: Publish a horizontally scrollable exact bank-by-measure table into the visible research board. Choose fixed reporting endpoints or follow the workspace comparison; Bankgraph loads reported values from the published data. Quarter and half widths pack beside related views; three-quarter and full widths suit denser tables.

title.description: Visible, natural-language view title.

span.description: Width on the 12-column human board: quarter (3 columns), half (6), three_quarter (9), or full (12).

tools.name: bankgraph.upsert_takeaway
tools.description: Add or replace one plain-text takeaway on the visible board. The text must refer to at least one existing board view and cannot contain executable markup or numerical arrays. Choose quarter, half, three-quarter, or full width on the 12-column board.

title.description: Visible, natural-language view title.

items.description: Stable caller-supplied board view ID.

span.description: Width on the 12-column human board: quarter (3 columns), half (6), three_quarter (9), or full (12).

tools.name: bankgraph.arrange_research_board
tools.description: Set the complete answer order exactly once. Every current view ID must appear exactly once. Focus can be kept, cleared, or set in the same atomic workspace revision.

items.description: Stable caller-supplied board view ID.

tools.name: bankgraph.configure_board_view
tools.description: Change only the requested part of an existing view and preserve everything else. First read bankgraph.read_research_board and use that block's configurationAffordances. Bank, measure, and period sources are independent: supplying certs, metrics, or dates fixes only that anchor. Set bankSource to workspace to apply current and future workspace banks without changing the view's measures or periods. followWorkspace remains a shorthand for reconnecting or fixing every anchor. Revision guards are optional because every field is an exact, idempotent setting.

blockId.description: Existing block ID from read_research_board; consult its configurationAffordances entry before choosing fields.

title.description: Visible, natural-language view title.

focus.description: Use true to focus this view. Use false to clear focus when this view is focused.

presentation.description: Source-bound history views only; chooses one primary measure or small multiples.

followWorkspace.description: Compatibility shorthand for all anchors. true reconnects banks, measures, and periods and cannot be combined with fixed values; false fixes all three at their current effective values and may include replacement values.

bankSource.description: workspace applies current and future workspace banks to this view; fixed keeps its current effective banks unless certs is also supplied.

metricSource.description: workspace follows workspace measures; fixed keeps the current effective measures unless metrics is also supplied.

periodSource.description: workspace follows workspace periods; fixed keeps current effective periods unless date fields are also supplied.

certs.description: Fix only the bank anchor for a data-bearing view. Do not send with bankSource=workspace.

metrics.description: Fix only the measure anchor for a data-bearing view. Do not send with metricSource=workspace.

asOf.description: Fix the point-in-time reporting period without changing bank or measure sources. Do not send with periodSource=workspace.

compareWith.description: Fix the comparison period without changing bank or measure sources. Do not send with periodSource=workspace.

view.description: Stored analysis views only. Use that block's configurationAffordances.viewValues; compatible values depend on result kind.

tools.name: bankgraph.remove_board_blocks
tools.description: Remove one or more visible board views by stable ID. A retry after those views are already absent is a successful no-op.

items.description: Stable caller-supplied board view ID.

tools.name: bankgraph.clear_research_board
tools.description: Remove every visible board view in one operation while retaining the selected banks, cohort, measures, and period. The human interface offers the same recoverable clear action.

tools.name: bankgraph.reset_board_layout
tools.description: Keep every view and analytical selection, but return the board to its automatic layout, default view sizes, default time ruler, and no focused view.

tools.name: bankgraph.reset_research_board
tools.description: Clear the board and its research question, selected banks, cohort, measures, dates, saved findings, and analysis results in one exact operation. The product-level watchlist is retained.

tools.name: bankgraph.rank_cohort_on_board
tools.description: Rank the current cohort by one reported measure, select up to 10 banks from either tail, and optionally replace the board with exact values, histories, a peer distribution, and a relationship view. Use this for questions such as which banks have the highest loan-to-deposit ratio when bank names are not known in advance. The full cohort remains the benchmark behind the selected answer set. Read bankgraph.get_context first and pass its revision as ifRevision.

metric.description: Metric available in the linked workspace.

bankCount.description: Number of ranked banks to place on the board.

items.description: Metric available in the linked workspace.

question.description: Optional board title or research question.

boardMode.description: Replace the current views with a comparison board, or keep its views.

ifRevision.description: Only apply if the workspace still has this revision.

tools.name: bankgraph.read_metric_history
tools.description: Read exact quarterly values for up to ten requested banks and forty reporting periods. Returns all requested bank series by default with aligned periods, missing values, raw units, and source field; an explicitly smaller page can continue with nextCursor.

metric.description: Metric available in the linked workspace.

items.description: FDIC certificate number.

endingAt.description: Quarter-end date YYYYMMDD or YYYYQn; quarter labels are normalized to 0331, 0630, 0930, or 1231.

pageSize.description: Complete bank series requested; defaults to every requested bank.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page.

tools.name: bankgraph.inspect_change
tools.description: Explain a reported change across consecutive quarters. Workspace metrics return supported endpoint evidence; assets, quarterly net income, and loan-to-deposit ratio also return component bridges. Results include units, method, provenance, available peer movement, and any FDIC structural event mapped to the certificate inside the comparison window.

metric.description: Metric with a deterministic quarter bridge.

from.description: Quarter-end date YYYYMMDD or YYYYQn; quarter labels are normalized to 0331, 0630, 0930, or 1231.

to.description: Quarter-end date YYYYMMDD or YYYYQn; quarter labels are normalized to 0331, 0630, 0930, or 1231.

tools.name: bankgraph.investigate_bank
tools.description: Open a linked, multi-metric investigation for one bank across two consecutive reporting quarters. The operation configures the visible workspace, then returns deterministic metric changes, reported component bridges, peer-relative evidence, mapped structural events, and optional direct-agency economic context. Read bankgraph.get_context first and pass its revision as ifRevision.

items.description: FDIC certificate number.
Metric with a deterministic quarter bridge.

from.description: Quarter-end date YYYYMMDD or YYYYQn; quarter labels are normalized to 0331, 0630, 0930, or 1231.

to.description: Quarter-end date YYYYMMDD or YYYYQn; quarter labels are normalized to 0331, 0630, 0930, or 1231.

historyPeriods.description: Quarterly observations to show in the linked history view.

maxComponents.description: Largest reported components to return for each supported bridge.

ifRevision.description: Only apply if the workspace still has this revision.

tools.name: bankgraph.share_or_export
tools.description: Create a live workspace link that replays the current choices against published data, a public workspace-state JSON artifact, or a release-fenced bank-data CSV. certs is valid only with bank_csv; share_link and workspace_json always use the current workspace and must omit certs.

format.description: share_link and workspace_json use the current workspace and reject certs; bank_csv accepts optional certs or uses the selected banks.

items.description: FDIC certificate number.

certs.description: bank_csv only. Omit for share_link and workspace_json.

ifRevision.description: Only apply if the workspace still has this revision.

tools.name: bankgraph.read_bank_directory
tools.description: Read the filters, ordering, pagination, and a bounded set of results visible in the bank directory.

limit.description: Visible banks to return from the current page.

tools.name: bankgraph.open_directory_bank
tools.description: Open one bank from the visible directory page in the shared research workspace. The certificate number must belong to a current visible result.

cert.description: FDIC certificate number from the current visible page.

tools.name: bankgraph.open_directory_screen
tools.description: Carry the directory's current question, filters, ordering, and matching cohort into the shared workspace. Existing map and peer exclusions are cleared so the workspace opens the same bank population.

tools.name: bankgraph.read_macro_evidence
tools.description: Read bounded observations and agency provenance for macro series loaded in this banking view.

seriesIds.description: Loaded series IDs, such as FRB_FEDFUNDS, UST10Y2Y, or BLS_UNRATE.

limit.description: Recent observations per series.

tools.name: bankgraph.read_macro_bank_relationships
tools.description: Read the fixed-plan contemporaneous co-movement results shown in the macro view.

tools.name: bankgraph.open_in_workspace
tools.description: Carry the evidence visible on this page into the shared Bankgraph workspace, then open the workspace.

tools.description: Return the current Lectern interface language, text direction (ltr/rtl), and the supported locale list.

tools.description: Change the Lectern chrome language (header, buttons, onboarding, co-pilot). Does not rewrite lesson manuscript content. Supported: en, es, pt-BR, zh-Hans, hi, ar, ja, ko, fr, de, uk, tr, vi, id, th, it, pl. Arabic (ar) switches the page to RTL. Russian is not available.

locale.description: Locale code: en, es, pt-BR, zh-Hans, hi, ar, ja, ko, fr, de, uk, tr, vi, id, th, it, pl

tools.name: lectern_get_lesson
tools.description: Return the full Lectern lesson document: meta, sections (each has kind: built-in material/example/summary or a custom short label), quiz items, gaps, mode, and annotations. Use this before editing or answering student questions. Do not scrape the DOM; tool descriptions are the how-to (rasters/video: lectern_offer_media). Users may paste a LECTERN_QUIZ reference copied from Q1/Q2 — extract quizId and use that item.

tools.name: lectern_list_gaps
tools.description: Analyze whether the lesson is complete enough to teach: title, objectives, materials, and tests. Prefer fixing blockers before publish. Pair-write on the page; do not dump a worksheet in chat.

tools.name: lectern_list_activity
tools.description: List the co-pilot activity history on this tab (newest first): agent tool calls and teacher edits, with ids for lectern_get_activity / lectern_restore_activity. Does not add a card to the log. Use this instead of scraping the co-pilot panel.

limit.description: Max cards to return (default 40, max 100)

tools.name: lectern_get_activity
tools.description: Fetch one co-pilot history card by id from lectern_list_activity, including folded AMDP/json-chunk steps when present.

tools.name: lectern_get_section
tools.description: Fetch one lesson section by id (title, body, kind, media) and any nested quiz checks for that section so the agent can answer grounded questions without inventing content. kind may be a built-in role or a custom label the teacher defined. Users may paste a LECTERN_SECTION reference copied from a material — extract sectionId from that block and call this tool.

sectionId.description: Section id from lectern_get_lesson, or from a pasted LECTERN_SECTION reference

tools.name: lectern_set_mode
tools.description: Switch between teacher (authoring) and student (read-only + annotations) modes.

mode.description: teacher = edit materials/tests; student = read + annotate

tools.name: lectern_restore_activity
tools.description: Check out a past co-pilot card and load that lesson snapshot into the teacher manuscript (same as tapping Restore on the card). Later cards stay until the next edit. Use lectern_activity_head to return to now.

tools.name: lectern_activity_head
tools.description: Leave a checked-out history card and restore the current (newest) lesson snapshot. Same as Return to current on the co-pilot banner.

tools.name: lectern_set_meta
tools.description: Update lesson title, audience, subject, and learning objectives. Use this to harden a teacher draft into a complete lesson header.

title.description: Lesson title

objectives.description: Learning objectives students should leave with

tools.name: lectern_upsert_section
tools.description: Create or update a lesson section as textbook manuscript prose. Set kind to material, example, or summary when those roles fit; when they do not, pass a custom short label (Lab, Discussion, Warm-up, Primary source, …) instead of forcing a built-in. Prefer complete educational writing with paragraphs, callouts, and KaTeX math. Pair sections with schematic figures via lectern_generate_section_media (30 templates) or lectern_attach_section_media. Body format: Markdown with blank-line paragraphs; inline math $...$; display math with $$...$$ on their own lines; callouts as blockquotes starting with **Definition.**, **Takeaway.**, **Notation.**, **Note.**, **Misconception.**, or **Example.**; lists and tables welcome. Pass id to update an existing section.

title.description: Section heading

body.description: Manuscript body (Markdown + LaTeX). Use $$ display equations and > **Takeaway.** callouts so the page renders like a textbook.

kind.description: Page badge for this section. Prefer built-ins when they fit: material (reading), example (worked example), summary (takeaways). If the pedagogical role does not fit those three, invent a custom short Title Case label (max 40 chars) such as Lab, Discussion, or Primary source — do not force-fit a built-in. Omit on create to default to material.

order.description: Display order, 0-based

tools.name: lectern_plan_visual_learning
tools.description: Create a visual-learning plan for one section. Returns an ImageGen-ready prompt for an engaging raster illustration AND a recommended Lectern SVG template for explaining the idea. Use this proactively when enriching materials, even if the teacher did not explicitly request visuals. Then generate the raster, attach it with AMDP (lectern_offer_media, then every intake rank until CAS present, then bind and STOP), and create the schematic with lectern_generate_section_media.

tools.name: lectern_attach_generated_illustration
tools.description: Attach a raster illustration that you generated for a section. This preserves an AI marker and the required transparency caption automatically. Use after lectern_plan_visual_learning; do not use SVG here - SVG explainers belong in lectern_generate_section_media. AMDP is the default for rasters and video — do not put pixels in chat JSON. Cite first: lectern_offer_media (sha256, byteLength, mimeType). Try AMDP intakes in this order until lectern_media_status present is true (or offer disposition is have), then lectern_compress_media if it is a raster, lectern_bind_media, and STOP. Do not skip a later rank because an earlier one failed. Do not keep transferring after success. 1) cas-hit: bind immediately. 2) plane-put: stage the file in the OS temp directory (%TEMP% / $TMPDIR), not the workspace — Chrome’s upload tool often has no workspace roots and only allows temp. tools.name: origami_guide
tools.description: START HERE. The Origami contract: what a Fold is, the read-edit-write chunk protocol, every kind schema, the inert/active rules, the capability model and the tool catalog. Pass topic:"quickstart" FIRST if you are building a deck — under 3 KB, the five calls that do it, with a complete add_fold example. topic: quickstart | contract | kinds | recipes | starters | issues | tools | blocks. Pass kind for one kind's schema.

kind.description: Optional: one kind to detail (else the whole contract)

topic.description: Optional: one section only — contract | kinds | recipes | starters | issues | tools | blocks

tools.name: get_kind_schema
tools.description: The markup contract for one slide/block kind: what structure and attributes are valid. Changes nothing.

kind.description: Kind key, e.g. "free", "gantt", "chart"

tools.name: create_deck
tools.description: Create a NEW Fold and OPEN IT IN THIS TAB. It renders immediately. Call this FIRST when building from nothing, then add folds with add_fold and finish with save_deck. The single fold it mints is a real COVER carrying your title (plus subtitle/eyebrow if given) — there is no placeholder text to overwrite or delete, so do NOT add a cover fold of your own. foldType: "deck" (default) | "scroll" (long-form document) | "ledger". If a Fold with UNSAVED changes is already open this refuses; pass discard:true to replace it anyway.

title.description: Deck title (default "Untitled deck"); the cover h1, and it seeds the suggested filename

subtitle.description: A supporting line under the title on the cover (.lede). Omitted entirely when absent

eyebrow.description: A small label above the title on the cover, e.g. "Q3 review". Omitted entirely when absent

discard.description: Replace an open Fold that has unsaved changes, losing them. Default false (refuse instead)

tools.name: list_chunks
tools.description: Table of contents of the open Fold: every editable chunk with id, kind, label and hidden flag, in order, plus the deck title, theme, foldType and capabilities.

tools.name: read_chunk
tools.description: Read one chunk for editing: the deck context, the kind schema and the slide <template>. Edit it and send the whole element back via write_chunk. Prefer get_block when you only want a data block's JSON.

tools.name: write_chunk
tools.description: Apply an edited chunk to the open Fold — this CHANGES THE DECK the human is looking at and re-renders it. Send the whole <template data-origami-slide=...> element from read_chunk, edited; the slide id and kind are immutable and drift is rejected. Scripts, styles, iframes and remote URLs are ALLOWED but mark the deck "active" (recipients open it locked). Refused only when the content would break the single-file structure, or a data block fails its kind's schema. dryRun:true runs the WHOLE gate and applies nothing — same verdict, deck byte-identical.

chunkId.description: The chunk the edit was for

html.description: The edited <template> element (a full chunk reply is fine too)

dryRun.description: Validate only: same verdict/error, nothing applied, deck byte-identical. Default false

tools.name: add_chunk
tools.description: Add a new slide to the open Fold — this CHANGES THE DECK the human is looking at and re-renders it. Prefer add_fold when building a card from data; use this for raw markup, a starter, or a composite block. Defaults to a "free" slide with starter content at the end. Supply html for a built-in kind (get_kind_schema first), block + fields for a COMPOSITE defined in this Fold, or starter for a ready-made seeded fold (list_starters). dryRun:true builds and validates WITHOUT adding — same verdict, deck byte-identical.

kind.description: Slide kind (default "free")

position.description: 0-based insert index (default: end)

label.description: Sidebar label (default: kind/def name)

html.description: Slide inner markup; required for kinds other than "free"

block.description: A composite block kind (x.<name>) already defined in this Fold

fields.description: Field values for the composite block (block instance values)

starter.description: A ready-made fold from list_starters (roadmap | flowchart | node-graph | drawing | venn | ledger). Not combinable with html or block

dryRun.description: Validate only: same verdict/error, nothing added, deck byte-identical. Default false

tools.name: add_custom_fold
tools.description: Add a whole CUSTOM FOLD (a full page) as one fold — this CHANGES THE OPEN FOLD and re-renders it. Pass `html`, the fold's inner. Prefer add_fold when building a card from data; use this to paste a report verbatim, or for markup add_fold cannot express. For a page a human EDITS by clicking, use inline-editable blocks in a <div class="slide-inner">: h2/h3, p, p.lede, p.eyebrow, ul>li, .card-grid>.stat-card. Active content is ALLOWED but flags the deck active so recipients open it under the padlock; a stray <template>, an unbalanced <script>, or a data block that fails its schema is rejected.

html.description: The fold's inner HTML — a whole page (editable Origami blocks in a .slide-inner, or a raw report)

label.description: Sidebar label (default: "Custom fold")

position.description: 0-based insert index (default: end)

tools.name: move_chunk
tools.description: Move one chunk to a different place in the open Fold — this CHANGES THE DECK the human is looking at and re-renders it. `position` is the 0-based index the chunk ENDS UP at, counting hidden folds. Order only: no content, label or kind is touched. A position outside the deck is REFUSED rather than clamped, so a wrong index never silently means "last". One undo step.

position.description: 0-based index to move it to (0 = first)

tools.name: set_chunk_meta
tools.description: Set one chunk's label, speaker notes or hidden flag — this CHANGES THE DECK the human is looking at. `label` is the sidebar and tab name; `notes` is presenter text that never renders; hidden:true takes a fold out of the show without deleting it, and set_chunk_meta({chunkId, hidden:false}) is the ONLY way back for a fold delete_chunk hid. Fields you do not pass are left alone ("" clears). Content and kind are untouched. One undo step.

label.description: Sidebar/tab label ("" clears it)

hidden.description: true takes the fold out of the show; false puts it back

notes.description: Speaker notes — never rendered on the fold ("" clears them)

tools.name: delete_chunk
tools.description: Hide or DELETE a slide in the open Fold — this CHANGES THE DECK the human is looking at. Default mode "hide" keeps the slide in the file but out of the show (recoverable — prefer it); mode "delete" removes the slide template entirely. A hidden fold comes back with set_chunk_meta({chunkId, hidden:false}); a deleted one only comes back through undo. Use propose_delete when the human should approve first.

mode.description: Default "hide"

tools.name: define_block
tools.description: Register (or update) a COMPOSITE BLOCK definition in the deck — a reusable typed component a human can still edit field by field: a template of inert primitives plus a field manifest. Author instances with add_chunk({block, fields}). The template MUST render inert — no <script>, <style>, <iframe>, on* handlers or remote URLs — and an active one is rejected. This CHANGES THE OPEN FOLD.

kind.description: x.<name> — lowercase letters/digits/hyphens; never collides with built-ins

fields.description: the human-edit contract — the Studio auto-generates a control per field

name.description: identifier, referenced in the template as {{name}}

options.description: required for type "select"

template.description: inert HTML using {{field}} placeholders (HTML-escaped at render)

tools.name: list_block_defs
tools.description: List the composite block definitions registered in this deck (kind, name, version, fields). Use a kind with add_chunk({block, fields}).

tools.name: list_starters
tools.description: The ready-made FOLDS you can add in one call: roadmap, flowchart, node-graph, drawing, venn, ledger. Each is a free card already holding one seeded data block, copied from the Studio's own palette. Add one with add_chunk({starter:"<key>"}). Use a starter when a seeded example is a fine base you will edit; use add_fold when you already have the data.

tools.name: delete_block
tools.description: Delete a composite block definition. Non-destructive to content: every placed instance keeps its baked output but loses its data-script, becoming plain inert content, so nothing dangles and the deck stays valid. This CHANGES THE OPEN FOLD.

kind.description: Block kind x.<name> from list_block_defs

tools.name: set_header
tools.description: Set the deck-level masthead in the header bar: a subtitle line under the title and metadata chips (e.g. ["5 plants","Q3 2026"]). This CHANGES THE OPEN FOLD. The bar's COLOURS and thickness are theme tokens, not set here. Pass "" or [] to clear.

subtitle.description: A line under the deck title

tools.name: set_deck_meta
tools.description: Set the deck TITLE and/or theme — this CHANGES THE DECK the human is looking at and re-renders it. `title` is the manifest and header-bar name; it does NOT rename the file. `themeName` renames the theme; ON ITS OWN IT CHANGES THE LABEL AND NOTHING ELSE — use apply_theme for colours. `themeTokens` patches CSS custom properties onto the ones in force (the rest survive); only the 17 the stylesheet reads are honoured, and braces, semicolons, angle brackets, @ and url() are rejected with nothing applied. One undo step.

title.description: Deck title (manifest + header bar); does not rename the file

themeName.description: Theme name, e.g. "origami-default" — a label, not a restyle

themeTokens.description: CSS custom properties to patch, e.g. {"accent":"#3F7268"} — merged onto the theme in force

tools.name: set_fold_type
tools.description: Set the deck's reading experience — this CHANGES THE OPEN FOLD. "deck" (default) is the card-stage: one fold at a time with tabs and pips. "scroll" is a continuous document: every fold stacked top to bottom (pair with document-kind folds). "ledger" is reserved. "deck" writes no key, so the file stays byte-stable.

tools.name: inspect_render
tools.description: SEE THE DECK YOU CANNOT SEE. Lays the open Fold out in a real browser, off-screen, reports each fold's geometry and names four defects it can PROVE: OVERFLOW, masthead CLIP, EMPTY fold, SVG label COLLISION. Stated viewport, 1280x720 default. Read `outcome` first: clean | defects | unknown — unknown = something was NOT measured; never ship on unknown. `clean` is true only for a clean WHOLE deck. Too big for the 15s budget? It answers with the folds it reached plus `remeasure`: pass that back as `foldIds` (or use `maxFolds`) to measure a subset directly.

viewport.description: Screen to measure against (default 1280x720). Width 320-3840, height 240-2160.

foldIds.description: Measure ONLY these chunk ids (deck order is kept). An unknown id is refused. Folds not listed come back skipped:true and the deck-level `clean` stays false.

maxFolds.description: Measure at most this many folds, from the top of the deck (after foldIds, if both are given).

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Reverse the LAST change to the open Fold and re-render it. One tool call is one undo step, so a run_batch of six is six steps. It covers every writer (origami_guide({topic:"tools"}) lists them). It does NOT cross create_deck or a Fold the human opened — both reset the stack — does not touch bytes already on disk, and does not cover a staged proposal (reject_proposal) or a saved theme (delete_theme). 50 steps deep, no redo. revert_to_saved drops a whole run_batch in one call.

tools.name: revert_to_saved
tools.description: Drop EVERY unsaved change on the open Fold in ONE call — NOT undo (one step at a time). Jumps to the last save_deck, or to how the Fold was created/opened if never saved, clearing the undo stack in the same move — the safe pivot after a bad run_batch. Cannot itself be undone. Touches no disk. Refuses when nothing is open or nothing is unsaved.

tools.name: list_activity
tools.description: What has been DONE in this tab, newest first — one entry per tool call, whoever made it: seq, at, source (agent | human | console | replay), tool, ok plus the error, the target, ms and a one-line summary. The summary NEVER carries slide html, so reading the feed cannot cost what reading the deck costs — use read_chunk or export_deck for content. It is not the undo stack and not part of the Fold: nothing here is saved, a reload starts empty, and only the 500 newest are held.

limit.description: How many of the newest entries to return (default 50, capped at the 500 held)

tools.name: export_deck
tools.description: Hand YOURSELF the complete .origami.html text of the open Fold, as a string in the result — to hash it, diff it, or quote a fragment. It writes NOTHING, saves NOTHING and changes NOTHING, so calling this INSTEAD of save_deck ends the job with the work stranded in your context. save_deck stamps a fresh manifest.modified and this does not. A Fold over 4 MB is refused with its size — use save_deck.

tools.name: save_deck
tools.description: FINISH THE JOB: re-validate the Fold and put it somewhere durable. READ THE RESULT — only one of three outcomes is a save. saved:true means bytes were written to a real file AND read back. opfs.written means it is safe in this browser's private storage — invisible outside the page and evictable; the human retrieves it with "Download last save". downloadStarted means a download was fired but the page cannot see where it landed, so it is NEVER reported as saved. When saved is false the human must still press Save — say so rather than reporting success. It never throws and never opens a picker, so always end on it. Safe to call repeatedly; it changes no content.

tools.name: propose_chunk
tools.description: Propose an edit to a chunk WITHOUT applying it — STAGED for a human (or another agent) to review (a "document PR"). It appears as a review card in the page; if nobody is watching, resolve it yourself with accept_proposal. Same edit contract as write_chunk, validated NOW so a broken proposal never reaches review. accept_proposal refuses with a 3-way view if the chunk changed since — never a silent overwrite. Returns a proposalId.

html.description: The edited <template> element (a full chunk reply is fine)

title.description: Short summary of the change (the PR title)

prompt.description: What you were asked to do (optional provenance)

tools.name: propose_add
tools.description: Propose a NEW slide WITHOUT adding it — staged for review (the add equivalent of propose_chunk). Same content args as add_chunk; the content is rendered, baked and validated now, then a slide.insert is staged. It appears as a review card for a watching human; resolve it yourself with accept_proposal if nobody is.

kind.description: Slide kind (default "free")

position.description: 0-based insert index (default: end)

label.description: Sidebar label

html.description: Slide inner markup; required for kinds other than "free"

block.description: A composite block kind (x.<name>) already defined in this Fold

fields.description: Field values for the composite block

starter.description: A ready-made fold from list_starters. Not combinable with html or block

title.description: Short summary (the PR title)

prompt.description: What you were asked to do (optional provenance)

tools.name: propose_delete
tools.description: Propose hiding or deleting a slide WITHOUT doing it — staged for review, as a card in the page and a queue entry you can resolve yourself. mode "hide" (default, recoverable) or "delete". accept_proposal refuses if the chunk is already gone.

mode.description: Default "hide"

title.description: Short summary (the PR title)

prompt.description: Why (optional provenance)

tools.name: list_proposals
tools.description: The review queue: every staged proposal with author, title, target chunk, the before/after content and a conflict flag (true if that chunk changed since). Empty until a propose_* call stages something. The human accepts or rejects by clicking the cards.

tools.name: accept_proposal
tools.description: Accept a staged proposal — apply its edit to the open Fold immediately. Refuses if the target chunk changed since, returning the proposed and current content so you can re-propose against the new base (never a silent overwrite), and re-checks the data blocks against the CURRENT deck. Same action the human takes by clicking Accept, so use it when running unattended.

tools.name: reject_proposal
tools.description: Drop a staged proposal without applying it. The same action the human takes by clicking Reject on the card.

tools.name: get_block
tools.description: READ A DATA BLOCK BEFORE YOU REPLACE IT. Returns one data block's JSON exactly as stored, plus its caption and kind schema. Address it by chunkId + kind (chart | venn | flow | graph | gantt | draw | table) and nth when the fold holds more than one of that kind (0 = first, the default). Leave kind out to get EVERY data block on the fold — one call instead of one per block. set_block REPLACES a block rather than patching it, so read here, edit what you read, send the whole thing back. Changes nothing.

kind.description: One block kind: chart | venn | flow | graph | gantt | draw | table. Omit for every block on the fold

tools.name: set_block
tools.description: Replace the WHOLE JSON of one data block on one fold — this CHANGES THE DECK the human is looking at and re-renders it. Address it by chunkId + kind (chart | venn | flow | graph | gantt | draw | table) + nth (0 = first, the default) and pass the COMPLETE data: it REPLACES what is there, so call get_block first to keep part of it. The kind's validator runs before anything is applied and a bad shape is refused with the violation named; a table's formulas are baked; a flow/graph node with no `tone` and an edge with no `label` get "" (their legal blank, no meaning changes). A fold with no block of that kind is refused with the kinds it has — this never CREATES one, use add_fold. One undo step.

kind.description: The block kind to replace: chart | venn | flow | graph | gantt | draw | table

data.description: The block's COMPLETE JSON — call get_kind_schema(kind) for the shape

caption.description: Optional: the caption under the figure ("" clears it; left alone when absent)

tools.name: add_fold
tools.description: BUILD A WHOLE FOLD IN ONE CALL — this CHANGES THE DECK the human is looking at and re-renders it. Give the card as DATA: an eyebrow, a heading, then `blocks` in order. Each entry names EXACTLY ONE of chart | venn | flow | graph | gantt | draw | table (that kind's own JSON plus an optional caption — get_kind_schema for the shape) or text (an HTML string: p, p.lede, h3, ul/li), bullets (strings), stats (up to 4 {value,label}), quote ({text,by}). Every data block is validated before anything is added and a bad one is refused naming the block index and the violation; tables are baked; flow/graph node `tone` and edge `label` get "" when absent (their legal blank, no meaning changes). columns:2 lays the blocks in two tracks. A chart or graph that names no size is SIZED TO FIT the card. One call is ONE fold and ONE undo step. Returns the chunkId and the (kind, nth) address of every data block, which is what set_block takes.

title.description: The fold's heading (rendered as the h2) and the default sidebar label

eyebrow.description: The small label line above the heading, e.g. "Q3 review" (omit for none)

label.description: Sidebar/tab label (default: the title, trimmed to ~28 characters)

position.description: 0-based insert index (default: the end)

columns.description: 1 (default) or 2 — lay the blocks out in two tracks

blocks.description:
The card's content, in order. Each entry names exactly ONE of: chart | venn | flow | graph | gantt | draw | table | text | bullets | stats | quote — e.g. { "chart": { "type": "bar", "labels": ["Q1","Q2"], "series": [{ "name": "Revenue", "color": "#4A8CC4", "values": [12,19] }], "yMax": null }, "caption": "Revenue by quarter" }, or { "stats": [{ "value": "48", "label": "Decks shipped" }] }, or { "text": "

A line of copy.

" }. SIZE: a venn | flow | graph | gantt | table entry may add "width" and/or "height", whole CSS px (width 160-2600, height 120-2160) — leave them out and the card picks a height that fits 1280x720 (a default graph overflows it). A chart takes "width" only (its height is plotHeight in its own JSON, fitted for you); a draw block takes neither (wpct in its JSON). A size the runtime would ignore is REFUSED, not written

tools.name: add_ledger
tools.description: ADD A LEDGER FOLD IN ONE CALL — a titled card holding one live spreadsheet block. This CHANGES THE DECK the human is looking at and re-renders it. `formulas` maps an A1 cell to a formula and the calc engine RUNS them on the way in, so the file carries numbers, not an engine: {"D1":"=B1-C1","B5":"=SUM(B1:B4)"}. `totals` is a footer row: {"on":true,"fns":{"1":"SUM","2":"SUM"}} — the keys are COLUMN INDICES as strings, 0-based. `kpis` pins cards above the table: [{"name":"planTotal","ref":"B5"}] — `name` is an identifier, `ref` an A1 cell. A column `format` is an OBJECT — {"kind":"currency"|"number"|"percent"|"date"|"text"|"general"} — never a string. `currency` sets the PREFIX every currency column prints; without it the format library prints "$". Validated before anything is applied; a bad shape is refused with the violation named. One undo step.

title.description: The fold's heading (rendered as the h2) and the default sidebar label

eyebrow.description: The small label line above the heading, e.g. "Q3 review" (omit for none)

label.description: Sidebar/tab label (default: the title, trimmed to ~28 characters)

position.description: 0-based insert index (default: the end)

columns.description: Column definitions: [{ label, align?: "left"|"right"|"center", format?: { kind: "general"|"number"|"currency"|"percent"|"date"|"text", decimals?: int } }]

rows.description: Cells, row by row, as strings: [["Rent","1200"], …]. Leave a formula cell "" — the calc engine fills it

currency.description: The PREFIX every currency-kind column prints, e.g. "€" or "EUR" or "£". It is printed LITERALLY, not resolved from an ISO code: "EUR" gives "EUR1,234.50" and "€" gives "€1,234.50". Default: the format library's own "$"

named.description: Named outputs other blocks can reference, e.g. { "grandTotal": "=B3" }

totals.description: A footer row: { "on": true, "fns": { "1": "SUM", "2": "SUM" } } — keys are COLUMN INDICES as strings, 0-based

kpis.description: Cards pinned above the table: [{ "name": "planTotal", "ref": "B5" }] — name is an identifier, ref an A1 cell or a cellName

cellFormats.description: Per-cell format overrides by A1 reference, e.g. { "B3": { "kind": "currency" } }

caption.description: The line under the table (default: none)

tools.name: list_themes
tools.description: Every palette apply_theme can use: the four presets the runtime ships (origami-default, boardroom, meadow, dusk) plus anything save_theme kept in this browser, each with its complete token map and whether it is a preset or saved. Call this before apply_theme rather than guessing a name. Changes nothing.

tools.name: apply_theme
tools.description: Put a whole named palette on the open Fold — this CHANGES THE COLOURS the human is looking at and re-renders it. `name` is a preset or saved theme from list_themes; an unknown name is refused with the ones that exist. Its tokens merge onto the ones in force, so tokens it does not name survive. This is the tool that restyles a deck: set_deck_meta({themeName}) only renames the label. One undo step.

name.description: A theme name from list_themes (preset or saved)

tools.name: save_theme
tools.description: Keep a palette of your own so apply_theme can use it — stored IN THIS BROWSER, surviving a reload; it does NOT change the open Fold. `basedOn` takes a preset or saved theme as the base and merges your tokens on top, so a one-colour variant is one token. ONLY the 17 custom properties the deck stylesheet reads are accepted (list_themes reports them); anything else — primary, background, textColor — is REFUSED with that list, never stored and silently ignored. Returns a WCAG contrast report for ink/bg, ink/paper, accent/paper and chrome-ink/chrome, warning under 4.5:1. A preset name is refused; one of your own is replaced.

name.description: Theme key: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, e.g. "house-navy"

label.description: Human-facing name (default: the key)

tokens.description: CSS custom properties, e.g. {"accent":"#38628F","ink":"#19222C"} — merged onto basedOn when one is given

basedOn.description: A preset or saved theme whose tokens are the base (default: none — tokens stand alone)

tools.name: delete_theme
tools.description: Forget a theme you saved — it is GONE from this browser and apply_theme can no longer name it. undo does not cover this: a theme is not part of the Fold. A deck already wearing those colours KEEPS them, because a theme is applied by value. Presets cannot be deleted.

name.description: A saved theme name from list_themes

tools.name: run_batch
tools.description: Run several tool calls in ONE turn — this CHANGES THE DECK exactly as the same calls made one at a time would. `calls` is [{tool, args}] run IN ORDER, stopping at the FIRST failure; you get every result up to and including it, so a batch that half-lands says where it stopped and what landed. Each call takes the normal route, so the feed records every step and undo reverses them ONE AT A TIME. create_deck then five add_fold calls then apply_theme is one turn instead of seven. Nesting is refused, the cap is 25, and a read-only answer only arrives when the batch returns — put inspect_render last.

calls.description: The calls, in order: [{ "tool": "add_fold", "args": { … } }, …]. Max 25. Stops at the first failure.

tool.description: A tool name from this page

args.description: That tool's arguments (omit for a tool that takes none)

message.description: Optional message to echo back.

tools.name: list_documents

tools.name: get_disclosure_policy

tools.name: get_page_text

page.description: Page number (1-based)

reason.description: Why the agent needs this page

tools.name: request_disclosure
tools.description: Request just-in-time disclosure for a denied scope.

scope.description: Scope to disclose

reason.description: Why it is needed

level.description: once | session | always

tools.name: propose_transactions
tools.description: Scan loaded statements and propose transaction rows for human review.

doc.description: Document id, or "all" for all loaded documents

tools.name: get_review_status
tools.description: Get the current state of staged proposals, including accept/reject notes.

tools.name: reconcile_statement
tools.description: Check that debits + credits match the closing balance on a statement.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: List default spending categories.

tools.name: list_accepted_transactions
tools.description: List the locally extracted transactions the human explicitly accepted for processing. Use this tool—not get_page_text—when categorising spending, identifying merchants, proposing mappings, or inspecting transaction descriptions. It returns only accepted structured rows and never exposes raw statement text, account details, or rejected transactions.

tools.name: propose_category_mappings
tools.description: Inspect accepted extracted transactions and stage recognized merchant/category rules for human approval. Use this whenever the user asks to categorise spending or show a category chart. It never reads raw statement text or silently applies classifications. For unmatched merchants, use list_accepted_transactions and propose_mapping. After proposing, ask the human to approve the visible mappings; approval updates the chart.

tools.name: propose_mapping
tools.description: Propose a merchant/category classification rule based on accepted transaction descriptions. Call list_accepted_transactions first; raw statement text and get_page_text are not needed for categorisation. This creates a rule, not individual rows. One approved rule classifies every matching transaction, now and on future statements. Staged until a human approves; applied at read time only, never rewrites a stored transaction.

pattern.description: Lowercase substring to match against transaction descriptions, e.g. "amzn mktp"

category.description: Category, e.g. Dining out, Groceries, Subscriptions, Transport, Health, Bills, Income, Other

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Get the current goal (null if none is set yet — savings goal or debt/loan goal, whichever the human is currently working on). Reflects the page right now, including unsaved slider drags.

tools.name: get_plan
tools.description: Get the current plan — goal, per-category adjustments, and the human's notes — reflecting exactly what's on screen right now, including slider drags the human hasn't explicitly saved. Always call this before judging a plan (e.g. "is this feasible?") rather than assuming it still matches what you last proposed. Null if no goal is set yet.

tools.name: get_plan_feasibility
tools.description: Check whether the current plan's required savings/payment is actually achievable given the account's real average monthly surplus (income minus expense) from the loaded statements. Use this whenever asked "is this plan feasible?" instead of eyeballing the numbers.

tools.name: propose_savings_plan
tools.description: Draft a savings plan toward a goal (e.g. a car, an emergency fund) and advise which accepted spending categories offer realistic savings opportunities. Every adjustment must include a rationale grounded in the user's category spending. Staged until approved; renders as advice plus editable sliders on the page.

goal.description: Goal object: { label, target, current, rate? } — rate is an assumed annual return, as a plain percentage number where 5 means 5% (not 0.05). Omit or 0 if you're not assuming any investment growth.

adjustments.description: Savings advice as an array of { category, currentMonthly, targetMonthly, rationale }. Recommend only categories supported by accepted transaction data, and explain why each reduction is realistic. currentMonthly must be a true monthly average — use get_spend_by_category's avgMonthly field, never its total (which is summed across every month of statements loaded, not one month) — or the plan will propose an unaffordable amount.

tools.name: propose_repayment_plan
tools.description: Draft a debt repayment plan: outstanding balance, interest rate, and monthly payment freed up from spending adjustments. Staged until approved; renders as sliders on the page.

goal.description: Goal object: { label, current, target?, rate } — current is the outstanding balance, target is the payoff target (default 0), rate is the annual interest rate (APR) as a plain percentage number where 20 means 20% (not 0.20)

adjustments.description: Array of { category, currentMonthly, targetMonthly, rationale } — freed cash applied as extra payment toward the balance. currentMonthly must be a true monthly average (get_spend_by_category's avgMonthly field, not its total) or the payment plan won't be affordable.

tools.name: get_spend_summary
tools.description: Aggregate summary of committed transactions: income, expense, savings rate, top spending categories. Use for open-ended questions about spending patterns.

tools.name: get_spend_by_category
tools.description: Spend per category across accepted transactions, sorted highest first—both the total across all loaded statements and the monthly average. This and list_accepted_transactions are sufficient for categorisation and planning; never request raw statement text for those tasks. Use `avgMonthly`, not `total`, as a category's "currentMonthly" when drafting a plan.

tools.name: plot_spend_by_category
tools.description: Render the "Spend by category" chart from accepted transactions and human-approved mappings. If mappings are pending or none are approved, this waits instead of applying hidden guesses: call propose_category_mappings and ask the human to approve the visible proposals first.

tools.name: get_monthly_cashflow
tools.description: Net cashflow (income minus expense) per month across committed transactions.

tools.name: find_recurring
tools.description: Find repeating charges across committed transactions.

tools.name: propose_results
tools.description: Scan loaded lab reports and propose result rows for human review.

doc.description: Document id, or "all" for all loaded documents

tools.name: propose_reference_range
tools.description: Propose a standard reference range for an analyte the report printed no range for. Staged until a human approves it; never applied silently.

unit.description: Unit

source.description: Cited source, e.g. "Mayo Clinic Laboratories"

population.description: Population the range applies to, e.g. "adult male"

reason.description: Why this fallback is being proposed

tools.name: list_series
tools.description: List accepted lab results grouped by analyte, as time series with the effective reference range for each.

tools.name: plot_series
tools.description: Get the plotted time series for one analyte, with its reference band, so the agent can describe the trend.

tools.name: plot_panel
tools.description: Get the plotted time series for every analyte in a named panel (e.g. "Lipid Panel").

panel.description: Panel name as printed on the report

tools.name: plot_heatmap
tools.description: Get a matrix of every analyte over every collection date, each cell normalised to its position in the reference band (0 = low bound, 1 = high bound) so drift is visible at a glance.

tools.name: find_out_of_range
tools.description: List accepted results currently outside their effective reference band, most recent first — a starting point for a diet plan goal.

tools.name: propose_diet_plan
tools.description: Create or revise the diet-plan artifact shown in the page table. Always use this tool—not browser clicks or typing—when the user asks for a new plan or asks to add, remove, replace, or change an existing plan item. For a revision, first call get_plan, apply the requested change to the returned goal and adjustments, then call propose_diet_plan with the complete revised plan. The proposal renders immediately for human review and is saved only after approval.

goal.description: Goal object with analyte, label, target, current, unit

adjustments.description: Array of {item, action, targetAnalyte, rationale} objects

tools.name: review_diet_plan
tools.description: Publish a final review of the latest edited diet-plan table on the page. Before calling, use get_plan to inspect every row. Pass a finding for every dietary claim. Format summary as 3–6 concise newline-separated bullets, each beginning with "• ": cover unresolved/resolved labs, uncovered issues, questionable plan items, and the recommended next step. The page renders this summary, so never leave it only in chat. Multi-analyte targets such as "Vitamin D and Total Cholesterol" are matched separately against lab results.

findings.description: One entry per plan row: {item, status: "supported" | "questionable" | "unsupported", note}. Include user-added rows and flag false or weak claims.

summary.description: A readable 3–6 line summary. Every line must be one concise bullet beginning with "• ". Include lab status, plan concerns, and next steps; do not submit a paragraph.

nouploadmcp.app.blurb: Ping items, List plugins and Select plugin.
nouploadmcp.app.name: Nouploadmcp

tools.name: get_parameter_reference
tools.description: Reference for synth, drum, project and patch parameters, lookup tables, mod matrix, macros and the song format. Call with no section for the section list and best practices; call with a section before using complex tools so parameter names are exact. Sections: synth, patch, drums, project, lookup_tables, mod_matrix, macros, song_format, best_practices.

section.description: Section name, or empty for the overview.

tools.name: load_song
tools.description: Load a complete song (patterns, sounds, FX, mixer, song order) into the project, replacing it. The song format is the hardware server's: see get_parameter_reference("song_format"). CRITICAL: all patterns share one length (16 or 32); include "sounds" for both synths; synth p-locks use the step/track "macros" key, drum automation the track "params" key; mod matrix names are space separated ("filter frequency") while macro targets use snake_case parameter names ("filter_frequency"); gate max 16. Pattern names map to slots 1-8 and the "song" list to scenes. Then start_sequencer to listen and export_song_to_project to save.

song.description:
Complete song description for the Circuit Tracks.

Defines patterns, sounds, FX, mixer, and song structure.
Use ``get_parameter_reference`` to look up valid synth parameter names,
mod matrix sources/destinations, and macro destinations.

song.description: Ordered list of pattern names for playback (max 16 scenes).
