tools.description: Open the intelligence brief panel for a country by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g. "DE", "IR"). Routes the user to the country deep-dive view; the brief itself is fetched by the same path a click would take. This can consume daily briefing quota. To only pan the map, use focus_country.

tools.name: openSearch
tools.description: Open the global search command palette so the user can find countries, signals, alerts, and other entities tracked by World Monitor.

tools.name: get_dashboard_context
tools.description: Read a bounded snapshot of the visible dashboard: active variant, map view, center, zoom, map mode (2d or 3d), time range, enabled layers, and mounted or enabled panel IDs.

tools.name: list_map_layers
tools.description: Page the canonical map-layer catalog, including disabled layers. Omit monitor for every registered layer; world lists only that variant. Each result has the stable ID, label, enabled state, monitor availability, renderer compatibility, entitlement, and a reason when the current page cannot enable it with set_map_layers. Does not load map datasets.

monitor.description: Omit for every non-sunset registered layer; world lists only that variant.

state.description: Filter to enabled layers, or layers the current page can enable.

cursor.description: Previous page last layer ID; reuse only with the same filters.

limit.description: Page size from 1 to 8.

tools.name: list_dashboard_panels
tools.description: Page the canonical dashboard panel catalog for this tab, including disabled and unmounted panels. Optional variant, category, enabled, and available filters. Follow nextCursor until hasMore is false. Does not return panel data or enable panels. Gated panels include a stable unavailableReason.

variant.description: Monitor variant to list. Omit to include every canonical panel ID.

category.description: Settings category key, such as core or marketsFinance.

enabled.description: If set, keep panels whose enabled state matches.

available.description: If set, keep panels the current session can open.

cursor.description: Catalog cursor from the previous page nextCursor.

limit.description: Maximum panels in this page, from 1 to 8.

tools.name: switch_monitor
tools.description: Switch the visible dashboard to World (full), Tech (tech), Finance (finance), Commodity (commodity), Energy (energy), or Good News (happy) through the header variant switcher. Use those stable keys, not display labels. Returns the selected destination and effective dashboard state.

monitor.description: Stable monitor key: full, tech, finance, commodity, energy, or happy.

tools.name: open_settings
tools.description: Open the dashboard settings overlay through the same header gear path a person uses. Opening settings does not change its contents. Returns the selected destination and effective dashboard state.

tools.name: open_alerts
tools.description: Open the alerts notifications tab through the same settings path the visible UI uses. Opening alerts does not change their contents. Unavailable dashboards return a stable reason without account details.

tools.name: open_dashboard_panel
tools.description: Open and scroll to an already-live, currently enabled dashboard panel through the same entitlement-aware control path used by World Monitor. For the commodities panel, tab can also select commodities, physical, fx, or xau through the same tab path used by a person. Disabled panels return panel_disabled. Use set_panel_enabled to change whether a catalog panel is enabled; this tool does not enable panels itself.

panelId.description: Dashboard panel ID, such as "markets" or "strategic-risk".

tab.description: Optional commodities-panel subtab. Other panels reject this field.

tools.name: set_panel_enabled
tools.description: Enable or disable a dashboard panel by its stable ID through the same settings path a person uses. Returns the requested state, effective state, and whether anything changed. Enabling unknown, incompatible, unentitled, or free-tier-capped panels is denied; disabling a live catalog panel still succeeds. Requires target-side cancellation because it persists dashboard settings.

panelId.description: Dashboard panel ID, such as "markets" or "giving".

enabled.description: True to enable the panel, false to disable it.

tools.name: get_panel_layout
tools.description: Read the effective dashboard panel layout: stable panel IDs, named regions (sidebar or bottom), order index, collapsed state, and fullscreen state. When panelsTruncated is true, pass nextCursor to continue. Use before collapse, move, or fullscreen tools.

cursor.description: Optional panel ID cursor from a previous truncated get_panel_layout page.

tools.name: set_panel_collapsed
tools.description: Collapse or expand a mounted panel by stable ID through the same control and persistence path as the visible collapse button. Idempotent when the state already matches. Requires target-side cancellation because collapsed state persists.

collapsed.description: True to collapse the panel, false to expand it.

tools.name: move_panel
tools.description: Move a mounted panel to a named layout region (sidebar or bottom) at a 0-based index through the same persistence path as keyboard reorder. Do not use pointer coordinates. Requires target-side cancellation because order persists.

region.description: Target layout region.

index.description: 0-based destination index in the target region after the move.

tools.name: set_panel_fullscreen
tools.description: Enter or exit panel fullscreen by stable ID through the same visible fullscreen control as Live News and Live Webcams. Idempotent when the state already matches. Session view-state only; it does not persist across reload.

fullscreen.description: True to enter fullscreen, false to exit.

tools.name: set_map_view
tools.description: Move the visible map to a named world region or a bounded latitude/longitude pair, with an optional zoom level.

lat.description: Web Mercator latitude; provide with lon.

lon.description: Longitude from -180 to 180; provide with lat.

tools.name: set_map_layers
tools.description: Enable or disable explicit visible map layers through World Monitor’s variant, renderer, and entitlement-aware control path.

layers.description: Map layer IDs mapped to true (enable) or false (disable).

tools.name: set_time_range
tools.description: Set the visible map time range through the same 1h, 6h, 24h, 48h, 7d, or all control used by the dashboard. Returns the requested and effective range.

tools.name: focus_country
tools.description: Focus the visible map on a country bounding box by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code without opening a country brief or consuming briefing quota.

tools.name: set_map_mode
tools.description: Switch the visible map between 2d (flat) and 3d (globe) through the same dashboard control, including renderer layer compatibility.

mode.description: Visible map mode: 2d or 3d.

tools.name: search_dashboard
tools.description: Search the current World Monitor country, signal, map, panel, finance, and action indexes without opening the command palette or changing the dashboard. executable is true only when live dashboard state and this host’s cancellation support both allow the bound effect.

query.description: Search text. It is never included in analytics.

scope.description: Optional dashboard surface to search.

limit.description: Maximum number of concise results to return.

tools.name: open_search_result
tools.description: Open one result previously issued by search_dashboard after rechecking that it is still live, allowed, compatible, and entitled. Cancellation uses the bound effect class, which callers cannot supply or downgrade. View-state results run without a target-side AbortSignal; persistent, quota-consuming, and external-navigation results require one and may return target_cancellation_unsupported.

resultKey.description: Opaque key returned by search_dashboard on this page.

tools.name: list_dashboard_tabs
tools.description: List dashboard tabs as named persistent panel workspaces. Returns each tab id, name, active flag, plus whether another tab can be created and why add is locked. Use tab ids, not display names, for select, rename, and delete. When tabsTruncated is true, tabCount is the total persisted workspace count and this page omitted later tabs; pass nextCursor to list the rest. Call list_dashboard_tabs again after mutations.

cursor.description: Inclusive start tab id from a previous nextCursor. Omit to start at the first workspace.

tools.name: select_dashboard_tab
tools.description: Activate a dashboard tab by stable tab id from list_dashboard_tabs. Selecting the already-active tab is a successful no-op. Unavailable without target-side cancellation because tab changes persist to worldmonitor-tabs-v1 and the live panel workspace (same class as openCountryBrief/set_map_layers).

tabId.description: Stable dashboard tab id from list_dashboard_tabs.

tools.name: create_dashboard_tab
tools.description: Create a dashboard tab as a named persistent panel workspace, then activate it. Omit name to use the dashboard default. Creating a tab whose trimmed name already exists returns that tab without duplicating it. Honors the same tab cap and entitlement lock as the dashboard tab bar. Unavailable without target-side cancellation because tab changes persist to worldmonitor-tabs-v1 and the live panel workspace (same class as openCountryBrief/set_map_layers).

name.description: Optional display name. Omit to use the dashboard default.

tools.name: rename_dashboard_tab
tools.description: Rename a dashboard tab by stable tab id. Names are trimmed and capped at 40 characters, matching the dashboard tab bar. Renaming to the current name is a successful no-op. Unavailable without target-side cancellation because tab changes persist to worldmonitor-tabs-v1 and the live panel workspace (same class as openCountryBrief/set_map_layers).

tabId.description: Stable dashboard tab id from list_dashboard_tabs.

name.description: New display name for the tab.

tools.name: delete_dashboard_tab
tools.description: Delete a dashboard tab by stable tab id. Requires confirm=true. Refuses to delete the last remaining tab. Unavailable without target-side cancellation because tab changes persist to worldmonitor-tabs-v1 and the live panel workspace (same class as openCountryBrief/set_map_layers).

tabId.description: Stable dashboard tab id from list_dashboard_tabs.

confirm.description: Must be true. Delete is a destructive persistent mutation.

tools.name: list_mission_presets
tools.description: List every bundled mission preset for the current monitor. Each item uses a stable preset ID and panel/layer counts without premium payloads. Available rows include intended view and time range. Includes active, monitorCompatible, entitled, and available flags with a stable unavailableReason when gated.

available.description: If set, keep only presets the current session can apply.

tools.name: apply_mission_preset
tools.description: Apply a bundled mission preset by stable ID through the same mission-control path a person uses. Reports entitlement and monitor compatibility before writing. Requires target-side cancellation because it persists panels, layers, map view, and time range. On failure, restores the prior dashboard state.

presetId.description: Bundled mission preset ID from list_mission_presets.

tools.name: open_mission_picker
tools.description: Open the mission preset picker through the same mission-control path a person uses. Opening the picker does not apply a preset. Returns the destination and effective dashboard state.

tools.name: list_followed_countries
tools.description: Read the current followed-country list through the same anonymous or signed-in state used by the dashboard. Returns only ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, access state, and the free-tier limit.

tools.name: set_country_followed
tools.description: Follow or unfollow one country through the dashboard service that owns ISO validation, access state, the free-tier cap, sign-in handoff, and storage. Idempotent for the requested state. Requires target-side cancellation because it persists state or writes to the signed-in account.

followed.description: True to follow the country; false to unfollow it.

tools.name: get_access_context
tools.description: Read whether this tab is signed out, still loading account state, or signed in. Returns product tier, capability flags, panel and dashboard-tab limits, and whether the host can cancel tools. Contains no names, emails, account IDs, tokens, or session details.

tools.name: open_sign_in
tools.description: Open the existing Clerk sign-in dialog on this page. Does not accept credentials, one-time codes, or provider choices. Returns a stable reason when Clerk is unavailable or the dialog is already open.

happy.worldmonitor.app.blurb: Opencountrybrief items, Opensearch items and Get dashboard context.
happy.worldmonitor.app.name: Happy

tools.name: get_occupancy
tools.description: READ — call first, every session. The map of the scene: goal (the board's standing goal — build toward it when set), scene (type, story, seed, phase), zones, filled lots as lot:id:owner, empty lots you can actually stand on, human_locks (never write there), the human's selection and last actions, and next_step — what the lifecycle wants from you now. THE LIFECYCLE for a scene request: plan_scene (understand + plan, no mutation) → compose_scene (architecture: footprint, zones, walls, stairs, water, paths, terrain) → populate_zones (the story objects, zone by zone) → create_environment (the framing boundary) → get_scene / inspect_region (look) → validate_scene (the completeness score) → repair_scene or targeted repairs → validate_scene again until complete. build_scene runs that whole loop in one call when you cannot steer. To GROW a scene that already stands from a new prompt ('add a fishing harbor with boats', 'build on this with a market and more people') call extend_scene — it is ADDITIVE: it annexes the zones the prompt needs, fills them, frames them, and validates the whole; nothing standing is removed. Never compose_scene or build_scene for that — they replace the architecture. A SMALL request ('add a tree beside the house') is ONE targeted call (place_piece / create_vegetation / move_piece), never a rebuild.

tools.name: get_scene_rules
tools.description: READ — the world-building LAWS this application enforces, the completeness model (six scored dimensions), the scene archetypes it knows (backyard picnic, graveyard, market, house, castle, forest camp, harbor, arcade, village, street, skate park, arena, farm, park), the theme roster, and the ground palette. validate_scene runs every applicable law; the hard ones (stairs, walkways, off-scene lots) refuse violating writes at placement time. Read once before building.

tools.name: list_catalog
tools.description: READ — the Kenney catalog (1,813 pieces, 22 packs). Filter with pack (furniture, pets, food, nature, coaster, toy-car, …), kind (pet|food|furniture|building|cave|space|nature|coaster|character|car|boat|stall|machine|tree|prop|crate|dungeon|pirate|ramp), or query (substring of id/label). Use ids in place_piece / place_batch. You rarely need this — the archetype composer and populate_zones choose pieces themselves.

pack.description: Pack slug, e.g. furniture, pets, mini-arcade, toy-car.

kind.description: Catalog kind, e.g. pet, food, furniture, building, nature, coaster.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring of id or label.

limit.description: Max ids per pack (default 40).

tools.name: get_scene
tools.description: READ — the inspect step: every placed piece as id:lot:kind:zone:facing:owner, paginated (limit 40, page 0…). Filter by zone id/type or kind. Call after every significant build phase to see what actually landed before deciding the next move; use inspect_region for one zone in depth and lookup_object for one piece.

page.description: 0-based page (default 0).

limit.description: Pieces per page, max 80 (default 40).

zone.description: Only pieces inside this zone id or type.

kind.description: Only pieces of this catalog kind.

tools.name: inspect_region
tools.description: READ — look closely at one zone (zone id/type) or the area around a lot (lot + radius): its purpose, the pieces inside with their placement records (lot, zone, level, surface, facing, on_path), path and stair cells, and empty standable lots. The inspect step for a zone you just built or are about to repair.

zone.description: Zone id or type from get_occupancy.

lot.description: Center lot (A1-style) when not inspecting a zone.

tools.name: lookup_object
tools.description: READ — the full placement record for one piece id: catalog id, kind, lot, zone, level, surface, facing, clearance, whether it stands on a path, owner/locked/label, plus its nearest neighbours. Use it to check a single piece before moving or removing it.

tools.name: get_selection
tools.description: READ — what the human has selected right now plus their recent edits. Build around the human's focus instead of guessing.

tools.name: tell_story
tools.description: READ — a short narrated recap of everything built so far (a few paragraphs of prose) to relay to the human when they ask what happened or for a summary.

tools.name: plan_scene
tools.description: PLAN (read-only, no mutation) — the UNDERSTAND + PLAN step for any medium or complex request. Pass theme (free text, e.g. 'a backyard picnic with burgers and cake'), optional type (an archetype id: backyard_picnic|graveyard|market|house|castle|forest_camp|harbor|arcade|village|street|skate_park|arena|farm|park), optional seed (same theme + same seed = the same plan; omit to mint a fresh world). Returns the intent (scene type, story, focal point, required and supporting elements, complexity), the zone program (which places, where, why), the environment (theme, ground, boundary), circulation, the seeded composition summary per zone, and next — the exact call sequence to build it. Nothing is placed and nothing on the canvas changes: read the plan, adjust if you must (create_zone, apply_theme after composing), then call compose_scene with the plan_id. Do NOT call this for a small addition.

theme.description: What to build. Defaults to the board's standing goal when omitted.

type.description: Optional archetype id to force, e.g. graveyard.

requirements.description: Short phrases the scene must include; folded into the theme.

seed.description: Scene seed like PICNIC-8F42KQ. Omit to mint a fresh one.

tools.name: compose_scene
tools.description: COMPOSE (mutation, architecture only) — stage a plan's composition onto the canvas: the footprint, themed ground, zones with their walls/stairs/water/road/rise, and the paths between them. NO props are placed. Pass plan_id from plan_scene (or theme/type/seed to plan and compose in one step). The agent's previous build is swept; human pieces are preserved. Returns the zones and circulation and what to call next: populate_zones, then create_environment, then validate_scene. For a small change to an existing scene do NOT call this (it replaces the architecture); use create_zone / create_path / place_piece instead, and extend_scene to grow a standing scene from a new prompt.

theme.description: Free text when you skipped plan_scene.

seed.description: Scene seed to reproduce a world.

tools.name: populate_zones
tools.description: EXECUTE (bulk, semantic) — build the story objects of the composed scene: the focal anchor of every zone first, then each zone's required and supporting elements arranged by their own grammar (seats ring the table facing it, food beside it, stalls face the aisle, furniture backs the walls, graves in rows), then the people, facing the action. Pass zones (ids from compose_scene; default all) and/or only (element roles such as 'seating', 'burgers', or 'people') to fill part of a scene or repair a gap validate_scene named. Already-realized pieces are skipped, so it is safe to call again. Returns per-zone placed/skipped with reasons and the first placement records. Follow with create_environment, then validate_scene.

zones.description: Zone ids to fill (default: every zone).

only.description: Element roles to place (default: all), e.g. ['seating', 'people'].

intent.description: Short phrase shown live on the canvas.

tools.name: create_environment
tools.description: EXECUTE (bulk, semantic) — the environmental framing in one call: the seeded boundary along the coast (a forest edge, standing stones — whatever the theme says), undergrowth, and a little scene texture, with deliberate gaps at the entrance, piers, roads, and functional zones. Placements go through the same collision/lock/walkway rules as everything else. Optional density (low|medium|high) and style (catalog flavor, e.g. 'dead trees'). The repair for a bare or thin boundary. Call after populate_zones; follow with validate_scene.

style.description: Optional catalog flavor for the boundary.

tools.name: build_scene
tools.description: ORCHESTRATOR — the complete lifecycle in ONE call, for hosts that cannot steer step by step: plan_scene → compose_scene → populate_zones → create_environment → get_scene → validate_scene → repair_scene → validate_scene, all dispatched through the same WebMCP tools (they appear nested in the trace). Pass theme (and optional seed to reproduce a world). Prefer the staged calls when you want to read the plan or steer the composition; never use this for a small addition, and never to add to a scene that already stands — that is extend_scene.

seed.description: Scene seed to reproduce a world; omit to mint a fresh one.

tools.name: extend_scene
tools.description: GROW (mutation, ADDITIVE) — build ON the scene that already stands from a new prompt, never replacing it: understands the prompt, reuses zones of the types it needs and annexes the rest beside the footprint (a harbor digs water and builds a pier, a market lays a square, a house raises a walled room), fills them with the prompt's story objects and people through the archetype grammar, frames the new ground, then validates the WHOLE scene (the base plus every addition) and repairs. Human pieces and the existing build stay exactly where they are. Pass prompt ('a fishing harbor with boats at anchor', 'a market with stalls and more people', 'a garden with benches'). Requires a scene — build_scene first on an empty board. The share link replays every addition in order, so the grown world is reproducible.

prompt.description: What to add to the current scene.

max_repairs.description: Repair budget after validation (default 6; 0 skips repair).

validate.description: Validate and repair inside this call (default true). A steering host may pass false and run validate_scene / repair_scene itself.

tools.name: create_zone
tools.description: SEMANTIC — add ONE functional zone to the current environment (architecture only, no props). The usual repair when validate_scene says a zone is missing, or the way to grow a scene ('add a garden to the west'). Pass type (plaza|home|market|garden|harbor|street|arcade|workshop|keep|lab|camp|skyline), optional location (north|south|east|west|center), size (small|medium|large), label. Interior types raise a walled terrace with a stair; garden lays a bed; harbor digs water and builds a pier; street pours road. A walk to the plaza is threaded automatically. On an empty board this also creates the starter footprint. Fill it afterwards with populate_zones {zones: [id]}.

label.description: Display name, e.g. 'the fish market'. Max 40 chars.

tools.name: create_path
tools.description: SEMANTIC — thread a walking path between two points; the repair for a zone validate_scene says is cut off. Pass from and to as zone ids ('market'), zone types, lot ids ('M13'), or 'entrance' (the south coast). Clipped to the decks; ends one cell short of a zone's focal so the landmark stays a pedestal.

from.description: Zone id/type, lot id, or 'entrance'.

to.description: Zone id/type or lot id.

tools.name: create_prop_cluster
tools.description: SEMANTIC (bulk) — furnish ONE zone by its own grammar in one call; the single-zone form of populate_zones (which is preferred for a composed scene). Pass zone (id or type) and optional theme to flavor the picks. Never furnish a zone piece by piece.

zone.description: Zone id or type, e.g. 'market' or 'garden-2'.

theme.description: Optional flavor, e.g. 'fresh fruit and bread'.

tools.name: create_focal_point
tools.description: SEMANTIC — give a zone its visual anchor: the archetype's focal element (a picnic table, a monument, a fountain, a campfire) or, without one, the most massive themed landmark — or a specific catalog id. Stands it at the zone's focal lot, nudging at most a cell. Pass zone (id or type; default the scene's focal zone) and optional theme or id. The repair for a missing-focal-point validation failure.

theme.description: Optional flavor for choosing the landmark, e.g. 'fountain'.

id.description: Exact catalog id to use instead of letting the page choose.

tools.name: create_vegetation
tools.description: SEMANTIC (bulk) — plant a group in one call; never place trees one at a time. area: 'edge' rings the coastline (the same framing create_environment lays, for when you want a specific style or density), or a zone id/type plants inside that zone. Optional style (e.g. 'pine trees rocks', 'dead trees') and density (low|medium|high). Placements obey collision, lock, and walkway rules.

area.description: 'edge' for the coastline boundary, or a zone id/type from get_occupancy.

style.description: Optional catalog flavor, e.g. 'dead trees', 'palm trees rocks'.

tools.name: create_ground_patch
tools.description: SEMANTIC — paint one themed ground patch: an intentional region of a different material, not noise. Pass material (see get_scene_rules), optional near (zone id/type or lot id — defaults to the island center), and size (small|medium|large).

material.description: A ground material, e.g. moss, dirt, cobble, snow, candy-pink.

near.description: Zone id/type or lot id to center the patch on.

tools.name: apply_theme
tools.description: SEMANTIC — restyle the whole environment with a theme's material ecosystem: repaints the ground to the theme's primary, lays fresh seeded patches, sets the walk material. Pass theme (an id from get_scene_rules or free text, e.g. 'spooky graveyard'). Pieces are untouched — follow with create_environment if the boundary should change too.

theme.description: Theme id (e.g. spooky, candy, snow) or free text.

tools.name: place_piece
tools.description: PRIMITIVE — ONE object. Use for a single targeted addition ('a tree beside the house': relative_to the house id, side), a unique landmark, or a correction after validate_scene. NEVER build a scene or a group with repeated calls: plan_scene → compose_scene → populate_zones builds worlds; create_vegetation plants groups; place_batch places an explicit list in one call. Pass id (catalog id, preferred — e.g. market-display-fruit, pirate-ship-pirate-large, pets-animal-cat, food-burger-cheese, furniture-lounge-sofa, nature-tree-oak, coaster-station, toycar-vehicle-racer, space-room-large) or kind. Target lot (A1-style) OR relative_to (piece id) + side (north|south|east|west) + gap (1-4); with no target the page grows the scene. rot (0|90|180|270: 0 faces camera-south, 90 west, 180 north, 270 east) sets facing. Refuses occupied, off-scene, stair, walkway (bulky pieces), and human-locked lots; a collision nudges at most 2 cells and the record says so (requested_lot, drift). Returns the placement record and the map. Lots are A1-style ids (M13 is the home center); there are no x,y. Never target human_locks. Every write returns the placement record (lot, requested_lot, drift, zone, level, surface, facing) — read it. Pass intent (a short phrase) so the canvas can narrate.

id.description: Any catalog id from list_catalog, e.g. pirate-ship-pirate-large or furniture-lounge-sofa.

kind.description: Fallback when no id: stall|prop|character|tree|crate|machine|ramp|dungeon|boat|pirate|car|pet|food|furniture|building|cave|space|nature|coaster.

intent.description: Short phrase shown live on the canvas, e.g. 'docking the pirate ship'.

lot.description: Lot id like C4. Omit to place relative or auto.

reason.description: Story reason ('the centerpiece', 'out over the water') for the narrator.

tools.name: place_batch
tools.description: PRIMITIVE (bulk) — an explicit list of placements in ONE call, for an arrangement you designed yourself (a row of lanterns, three characters around a fire). For a composed scene prefer populate_zones; for vegetation prefer create_vegetation. Pass intent (what you noticed + what you will build) and items: place_piece specs ({id|kind, lot? or relative_to+side+gap?, flip?, rot?, reason?}), max 48, applied in order. Locks and collisions are skipped, not fatal. Returns per-item records (lot, requested_lot, drift, zone) and the map. Lots are A1-style ids (M13 is the home center); there are no x,y. Never target human_locks. Every write returns the placement record (lot, requested_lot, drift, zone, level, surface, facing) — read it. Pass intent (a short phrase) so the canvas can narrate.

intent.description: One line: what you noticed + what you will build. Shown live on the canvas.

tools.name: move_piece
tools.description: REPAIR primitive — relocate one piece. Say WHAT is wrong and the page finds the lot: off:"path" (a walkway blocker), away_from:<piece id> (overlap or crowding the landmark), into_zone:<zone id> (a stray outside every zone), or give lot / relative_to + side + gap explicitly. Refuses human-locked pieces, occupied, off-scene, stair, and (for bulky pieces) walkway targets. Returns the new placement record. Lots are A1-style ids (M13 is the home center); there are no x,y. Never target human_locks. Every write returns the placement record (lot, requested_lot, drift, zone, level, surface, facing) — read it. Pass intent (a short phrase) so the canvas can narrate.

intent.description: Short phrase shown live on the canvas.

away_from.description: Piece id to get clear of.

off.description: Step off a walkway or a stair approach.

tools.name: orient_piece
tools.description: REPAIR primitive — turn one piece to face something: pass face (a piece id) or face_lot (a lot) and the page picks the quarter turn, or rot (0|90|180|270) explicitly, or flip. The fix when validate_scene says a chair or character faces away from the action. Refuses human-locked pieces.

tools.name: label_piece
tools.description: PRIMITIVE — set the text label on one piece: id, text (40 chars max). Labels only. Refuses human-locked pieces.

text.description: Max 40 chars. Empty string clears.

tools.name: remove_piece
tools.description: REPAIR primitive — remove one agent-owned piece by id when validate_scene flags clutter, an overlap, or a piece in the wrong kind of place. Never to restart a scene (compose_scene sweeps and rebuilds). Human-owned pieces are refused unless the human has that piece selected AND force:true is passed. There is no clear-all.

force.description: Only for a human-owned piece the human has selected.

tools.name: validate_scene
tools.description: VALIDATE (read-only) — the scene completeness score and the ONLY arbiter of done. Tool success ≠ scene success. Scores six dimensions (intentCoverage, composition, spatialCoherence, environment, navigation, placementValidity) from the world-building laws — does the scene contain what was asked for, in the right zones; is there a landmark with room around it; do seats and people face the action; are zones furnished for their purpose; can you enter, walk, and climb; is everything grounded, un-overlapped, and where the plan put it; is the edge framed. Returns complete, completion %, verdict, per-check notes, and STRUCTURED repairs (tool + args) — apply them with repair_scene or by hand, then validate again. Never declare a scene finished without complete:true.

theme.description: What the scene is supposed to be. Defaults to the current scene's prompt / the standing goal.

tools.name: repair_scene
tools.description: REPAIR (semantic) — validate, then apply the prescribed repairs THROUGH the other WebMCP tools (populate_zones for missing elements, create_path for cut-off zones, move_piece off paths / away from overlaps / into zones, orient_piece for wrong facings, create_environment for a bare edge, create_focal_point, remove_piece for misplaced kinds), most important first, up to max (default 6), then validate again. Never rebuilds the scene. Returns before/after scores, what was applied, and what remains. Loop validate_scene → repair_scene until complete.

only.description: Restrict to these rule ids, e.g. ['paths_clear', 'orientation'].

exclude.description: Rule ids to leave alone, e.g. ['zones'] to keep repairs from laying new ground.

theme.description: What the scene is supposed to be (defaults to the current prompt).

tools.name: get_scene_seed
tools.description: READ — the current scene's identity: seed, prompt, scene type, generator version, and the share_url that reproduces this world (prompt + seed, never coordinates). has_seed:false for freeform boards.

tools.name: generate_scene_seed
tools.description: SEED — mint a fresh unique seed (like PICNIC-8F42KQ) WITHOUT building anything, to pass to plan_scene / build_scene or offer the human a choice of worlds.

concept.description: Optional concept word for the prefix.

tools.name: set_scene_seed
tools.description: SEED — import a specific seed (e.g. from a shared scene) as the board's identity and, by default, REBUILD its world deterministically through build_scene (pass rebuild:false to only stamp the identity). Pass seed and optional prompt (defaults to the current prompt / standing goal).

tools.name: regenerate_scene
tools.description: SEED — remix: mint a NEW seed and rebuild the same concept as a meaningfully different composition (different footprint, zone arrangement, picks) through build_scene. Human pieces are preserved. Returns the new seed and share_url.

prompt.description: Optional new prompt; defaults to the current scene's.

tools.name: openCountryBrief
tools.description: Open the intelligence brief panel for a country by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g. "DE", "IR"). Routes the user to the country deep-dive view; the brief itself is fetched by the same path a click would take. This can consume daily briefing quota. To only pan the map, use focus_country.

tools.name: openSearch
tools.description: Open the global search command palette so the user can find countries, signals, alerts, and other entities tracked by World Monitor.

tools.name: get_dashboard_context
tools.description: Read a bounded snapshot of the visible dashboard: active variant, map view, center, zoom, map mode (2d or 3d), time range, enabled layers, and mounted or enabled panel IDs.

tools.name: list_map_layers
tools.description: Page the canonical map-layer catalog, including disabled layers. Omit monitor for every registered layer; world lists only that variant. Each result has the stable ID, label, enabled state, monitor availability, renderer compatibility, entitlement, and a reason when the current page cannot enable it with set_map_layers. Does not load map datasets.

monitor.description: Omit for every non-sunset registered layer; world lists only that variant.

state.description: Filter to enabled layers, or layers the current page can enable.

cursor.description: Previous page last layer ID; reuse only with the same filters.

limit.description: Page size from 1 to 8.

tools.name: list_dashboard_panels
tools.description: Page the canonical dashboard panel catalog for this tab, including disabled and unmounted panels. Optional variant, category, enabled, and available filters. Follow nextCursor until hasMore is false. Does not return panel data or enable panels. Gated panels include a stable unavailableReason.

variant.description: Monitor variant to list. Omit to include every canonical panel ID.

category.description: Settings category key, such as core or marketsFinance.

enabled.description: If set, keep panels whose enabled state matches.

available.description: If set, keep panels the current session can open.

cursor.description: Catalog cursor from the previous page nextCursor.

limit.description: Maximum panels in this page, from 1 to 8.

tools.name: switch_monitor
tools.description: Switch the visible dashboard to World (full), Tech (tech), Finance (finance), Commodity (commodity), Energy (energy), or Good News (happy) through the header variant switcher. Use those stable keys, not display labels. Returns the selected destination and effective dashboard state.

monitor.description: Stable monitor key: full, tech, finance, commodity, energy, or happy.

tools.name: open_settings
tools.description: Open the dashboard settings overlay through the same header gear path a person uses. Opening settings does not change its contents. Returns the selected destination and effective dashboard state.

tools.name: open_alerts
tools.description: Open the alerts notifications tab through the same settings path the visible UI uses. Opening alerts does not change their contents. Unavailable dashboards return a stable reason without account details.

tools.name: open_dashboard_panel
tools.description: Open and scroll to an already-live, currently enabled dashboard panel through the same entitlement-aware control path used by World Monitor. For the commodities panel, tab can also select commodities, physical, fx, or xau through the same tab path used by a person. Disabled panels return panel_disabled. Use set_panel_enabled to change whether a catalog panel is enabled; this tool does not enable panels itself.

panelId.description: Dashboard panel ID, such as "markets" or "strategic-risk".

tab.description: Optional commodities-panel subtab. Other panels reject this field.

tools.name: set_panel_enabled
tools.description: Enable or disable a dashboard panel by its stable ID through the same settings path a person uses. Returns the requested state, effective state, and whether anything changed. Enabling unknown, incompatible, unentitled, or free-tier-capped panels is denied; disabling a live catalog panel still succeeds. Requires target-side cancellation because it persists dashboard settings.

panelId.description: Dashboard panel ID, such as "markets" or "giving".

enabled.description: True to enable the panel, false to disable it.

tools.name: get_panel_layout
tools.description: Read the effective dashboard panel layout: stable panel IDs, named regions (sidebar or bottom), order index, collapsed state, and fullscreen state. When panelsTruncated is true, pass nextCursor to continue. Use before collapse, move, or fullscreen tools.

cursor.description: Optional panel ID cursor from a previous truncated get_panel_layout page.

tools.name: set_panel_collapsed
tools.description: Collapse or expand a mounted panel by stable ID through the same control and persistence path as the visible collapse button. Idempotent when the state already matches. Requires target-side cancellation because collapsed state persists.

collapsed.description: True to collapse the panel, false to expand it.

tools.name: move_panel
tools.description: Move a mounted panel to a named layout region (sidebar or bottom) at a 0-based index through the same persistence path as keyboard reorder. Do not use pointer coordinates. Requires target-side cancellation because order persists.

region.description: Target layout region.

index.description: 0-based destination index in the target region after the move.

tools.name: set_panel_fullscreen
tools.description: Enter or exit panel fullscreen by stable ID through the same visible fullscreen control as Live News and Live Webcams. Idempotent when the state already matches. Session view-state only; it does not persist across reload.

fullscreen.description: True to enter fullscreen, false to exit.

tools.name: set_map_view
tools.description: Move the visible map to a named world region or a bounded latitude/longitude pair, with an optional zoom level.

lat.description: Web Mercator latitude; provide with lon.

lon.description: Longitude from -180 to 180; provide with lat.

tools.name: set_map_layers
tools.description: Enable or disable explicit visible map layers through World Monitor’s variant, renderer, and entitlement-aware control path.

layers.description: Map layer IDs mapped to true (enable) or false (disable).

tools.name: set_time_range
tools.description: Set the visible map time range through the same 1h, 6h, 24h, 48h, 7d, or all control used by the dashboard. Returns the requested and effective range.

tools.name: focus_country
tools.description: Focus the visible map on a country bounding box by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code without opening a country brief or consuming briefing quota.

tools.name: set_map_mode
tools.description: Switch the visible map between 2d (flat) and 3d (globe) through the same dashboard control, including renderer layer compatibility.

mode.description: Visible map mode: 2d or 3d.

tools.name: search_dashboard
tools.description: Search the current World Monitor country, signal, map, panel, finance, and action indexes without opening the command palette or changing the dashboard. executable is true only when live dashboard state and this host’s cancellation support both allow the bound effect.

query.description: Search text. It is never included in analytics.

scope.description: Optional dashboard surface to search.

limit.description: Maximum number of concise results to return.

tools.name: open_search_result
tools.description: Open one result previously issued by search_dashboard after rechecking that it is still live, allowed, compatible, and entitled. Cancellation uses the bound effect class, which callers cannot supply or downgrade. View-state results run without a target-side AbortSignal; persistent, quota-consuming, and external-navigation results require one and may return target_cancellation_unsupported.

resultKey.description: Opaque key returned by search_dashboard on this page.

tools.name: list_dashboard_tabs
tools.description: List dashboard tabs as named persistent panel workspaces. Returns each tab id, name, active flag, plus whether another tab can be created and why add is locked. Use tab ids, not display names, for select, rename, and delete. When tabsTruncated is true, tabCount is the total persisted workspace count and this page omitted later tabs; pass nextCursor to list the rest. Call list_dashboard_tabs again after mutations.

cursor.description: Inclusive start tab id from a previous nextCursor. Omit to start at the first workspace.

tools.name: select_dashboard_tab
tools.description: Activate a dashboard tab by stable tab id from list_dashboard_tabs. Selecting the already-active tab is a successful no-op. Unavailable without target-side cancellation because tab changes persist to worldmonitor-tabs-v1 and the live panel workspace (same class as openCountryBrief/set_map_layers).

tabId.description: Stable dashboard tab id from list_dashboard_tabs.

tools.name: create_dashboard_tab
tools.description: Create a dashboard tab as a named persistent panel workspace, then activate it. Omit name to use the dashboard default. Creating a tab whose trimmed name already exists returns that tab without duplicating it. Honors the same tab cap and entitlement lock as the dashboard tab bar. Unavailable without target-side cancellation because tab changes persist to worldmonitor-tabs-v1 and the live panel workspace (same class as openCountryBrief/set_map_layers).

name.description: Optional display name. Omit to use the dashboard default.

tools.name: rename_dashboard_tab
tools.description: Rename a dashboard tab by stable tab id. Names are trimmed and capped at 40 characters, matching the dashboard tab bar. Renaming to the current name is a successful no-op. Unavailable without target-side cancellation because tab changes persist to worldmonitor-tabs-v1 and the live panel workspace (same class as openCountryBrief/set_map_layers).

tabId.description: Stable dashboard tab id from list_dashboard_tabs.

name.description: New display name for the tab.

tools.name: delete_dashboard_tab
tools.description: Delete a dashboard tab by stable tab id. Requires confirm=true. Refuses to delete the last remaining tab. Unavailable without target-side cancellation because tab changes persist to worldmonitor-tabs-v1 and the live panel workspace (same class as openCountryBrief/set_map_layers).

tabId.description: Stable dashboard tab id from list_dashboard_tabs.

confirm.description: Must be true. Delete is a destructive persistent mutation.

tools.name: list_mission_presets
tools.description: List every bundled mission preset for the current monitor. Each item uses a stable preset ID and panel/layer counts without premium payloads. Available rows include intended view and time range. Includes active, monitorCompatible, entitled, and available flags with a stable unavailableReason when gated.

available.description: If set, keep only presets the current session can apply.

tools.name: apply_mission_preset
tools.description: Apply a bundled mission preset by stable ID through the same mission-control path a person uses. Reports entitlement and monitor compatibility before writing. Requires target-side cancellation because it persists panels, layers, map view, and time range. On failure, restores the prior dashboard state.

presetId.description: Bundled mission preset ID from list_mission_presets.

tools.name: open_mission_picker
tools.description: Open the mission preset picker through the same mission-control path a person uses. Opening the picker does not apply a preset. Returns the destination and effective dashboard state.

tools.name: list_followed_countries
tools.description: Read the current followed-country list through the same anonymous or signed-in state used by the dashboard. Returns only ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, access state, and the free-tier limit.

tools.name: set_country_followed
tools.description: Follow or unfollow one country through the dashboard service that owns ISO validation, access state, the free-tier cap, sign-in handoff, and storage. Idempotent for the requested state. Requires target-side cancellation because it persists state or writes to the signed-in account.

followed.description: True to follow the country; false to unfollow it.

tools.name: get_access_context
tools.description: Read whether this tab is signed out, still loading account state, or signed in. Returns product tier, capability flags, panel and dashboard-tab limits, and whether the host can cancel tools. Contains no names, emails, account IDs, tokens, or session details.

tools.name: open_sign_in
tools.description: Open the existing Clerk sign-in dialog on this page. Does not accept credentials, one-time codes, or provider choices. Returns a stable reason when Clerk is unavailable or the dialog is already open.

tools.name: lens_scan
tools.description: Scan a URL in the Lens window on this page, the one the person is watching. The panes repaint as it runs and this returns once the scan has settled. Prefer lens_inspect when you only want the data: that one answers you privately and leaves the screen alone. Use this one when the person should SEE what you found. [safety: changes what is on the person's screen, and nothing else; repeat calls repeat the effect; fetches from the public internet.]

url.description: an absolute http(s) URL

tools.name: lens_compare_onscreen
tools.description: Put two URLs through the same rubric side by side, in the Lens window on this page. Returns the comparison and leaves it on screen. The head-to-head costs a tighter per-visitor budget than a single scan, so do not loop it. [safety: changes what is on the person's screen, and nothing else; repeat calls repeat the effect; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: lens_show
tools.description: Change what the Lens window is displaying. `pane` picks the split (both, human, machine, browser, delta) and `tab` picks which machine lens is open (anatomy, reader, wire, structured, ai, terms, discovery, tools, nlweb, markdown, readiness). This only moves the view. Five tabs hold nothing until somebody pays for the fetch, so follow it with lens_run_tab when the pane comes back empty. [safety: changes what is on the person's screen, and nothing else.]

tools.name: lens_run_tab
tools.description: Pay for one of the opt-in machine tabs and wait for it: reader (a third-party extractor's guess at the article), wire (every request the page makes, through a real browser), tools (the MCP catalog the origin advertises), nlweb (ask the origin's own /ask endpoint a question), markdown (replay the Accept header each named agent client sends, and report which representation each one gets). Each one is a fresh fetch of somebody else's site from this visitor's budget, which is why none of them run on their own. Needs a scan on screen first. [safety: changes what is on the person's screen, and nothing else; repeat calls repeat the effect; fetches from the public internet.]

query.description: nlweb only: the question to ask the origin

tools.name: lens_read_screen
tools.description: Read what the Lens window is showing right now: the URL that was scanned, its status, which pane and machine tab are open, the agent-readiness score, which Delta switches are flipped, and which opt-in tabs already hold data. The one tool here that changes nothing. Call it to find out what the person is looking at before you touch anything. [safety: read-only.]

tools.name: lens_delta
tools.description: Flip one of the Delta counterfactual switches and repaint. Each switch simulates a fix the scanned site has not made (markdown, semantic, contract, authority, receipt, dictionary, ech) and shows what it would have bought. Nothing is sent anywhere: the whole simulation is arithmetic on the scan already on screen. [safety: changes what is on the person's screen, and nothing else.]

tools.name: ask
tools.description: Ask aadhar.sh a natural-language question and get NLWeb-shaped results: for each match a url, name, site, score (0-100), description, and a schema.org schema_object. Retrieval is lexical over the site's own corpus and descriptions are extractive, so this returns the passages that answer the question rather than a written answer. mode=summarize and mode=generate are refused by name: this origin runs no language model. [safety: read-only.]

site.description: NLWeb site token; this origin serves one site, so "aadhar.sh" or "all"

mode.description: list (the only one served here); summarize and generate are refused rather than degraded

prev.description: previous queries. Received and NOT resolved, since decontextualization needs a model; send decontextualized_query instead

decontextualized_query.description: the fully self-contained form of a follow-up question. When present this is what gets searched

tools.name: search_site
tools.description: Search the public pages, writing, garage notes, and utility descriptions on aadhar.sh. [safety: read-only.]

tools.name: now_playing
tools.description: Read the cached current rn playlist and its tracks. A cold cache may refresh from the public Spotify embed using AadharshBot. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: photo_query
tools.description: Query the published photo archive by caption, camera, lens, film simulation, film-recipe setting, or date range. `q` is free text scored per term across the caption, the EXIF and an offline term expansion, so "classic chrome bridge" matches the film simulation AND the subject; the named parameters stay exact filters. Results are ranked and carry `score` and `matched` (which fields answered). `ranking.mode` says whether every term was covered (all-terms), only some (partial), or none (no-match), and `ranking.dropped` / `ranking.common` name terms ignored as stopwords or as too widespread to tell photos apart. Each result carries a `recipe` card naming the in-camera settings the shot was made with, so a look can be read back and re-shot. GPS and unlisted EXIF fields are never returned. [safety: read-only.]

q.description: free-text query, ranked; multiple words are scored independently

film.description: film simulation name, e.g. "Classic Chrome", "Nostalgic Neg", "Acros"

recipe.description: substring match anywhere in the recipe card, e.g. "DR400", "Clarity: -2", "Grain Effect: Strong, Large", "+2 Red"

from.description: inclusive YYYY-MM-DD prefix

to.description: inclusive YYYY-MM-DD prefix

tools.name: coffee_availability
tools.description: Read bookable coffee slots in the host timezone. If the calendar is stale or unavailable, the result is explicitly unavailable and contains no slots. [safety: read-only.]

tools.name: change_radar
tools.description: Read the bounded historical diff of the latest AadharshBot neighborhood observations. Raw crawled bodies are not stored or returned. [safety: read-only.]

tools.name: lens_inspect
tools.description: Inspect one public HTTP(S) URL through Lens and return a compact agent-readiness observation. Private, local, and non-HTTP targets are rejected. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: lens_page
tools.description: Read one public URL and return only what derives from the page's own bytes: anatomy, structured data, a markdown rendering, and what it costs an agent to ingest. Skips the origin-level fan-out entirely, so it is far cheaper and far faster than lens_inspect. Readiness, agent doors and terms are ABSENT from the result (not zero) because they were not checked; `phases.discovery` is false. Use lens_inspect when you need those. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: lens_compare
tools.description: Inspect two public HTTP(S) URLs and compare status, content, readiness, spectrum, agent doors, and discovery surfaces. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: find_events
tools.description: Search the Serendipity event pool (community events worth going to, and who's RSVP'd) by keyword. Returns events the pool's contributors actually said yes to; pass rsvp:"all" to include events that were only browsed. [safety: read-only.]

q.description: optional keyword filter on event name, place, or contributor

rsvp.description: defaults to going (the events with real rosters)

topic.description: optional: only events classified as this topic; unclassified events are counted in `untagged`

format.description: optional: only events classified as this format (talks, meal, social, ...)

tools.name: image_inspect
tools.description: Inspect an image's dimensions, format, and animation/frame information. Image bytes are processed ephemerally and are not stored. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

image_data.description: base64 image bytes, optionally as a data URL

tools.name: image_transform
tools.description: Run a bounded web image transform through Cloudflare Images and return the transformed image inline plus an exact byte receipt. The output is ephemeral. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: image_compare
tools.description: Encode one image into up to three bounded format variants and report exact byte sizes and hashes. It does not pretend to score visual quality. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: photo_recipe
tools.description: Return the exact public Fuji recipe for a named archive photo, archive URL, or exact published thumbnail bytes. Arbitrary visual lookalikes are not treated as matches. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

image_data.description: base64 bytes from a published thumbnail

tools.name: representation_capture
tools.description: Capture bounded public HTTP representations under browser, bot, Markdown, or identity request profiles and store only normalized headers, metadata, and body digests. Writes: each call persists a new snapshot row, so this tool is not read-only and not idempotent. [safety: WRITES DATA on this origin; repeat calls repeat the effect; fetches from the public internet. This page asks the person to confirm before it runs.]

tools.name: representation_read
tools.description: Read one normalized HTTP representation snapshot from the vault. Raw response bodies are never returned because they are never stored. [safety: read-only.]

tools.name: representation_compare
tools.description: Refetch the same HTTP representation profile, compare it with a stored snapshot, and persist the new normalized observation. Writes: each call persists a new snapshot row, so this tool is not read-only and not idempotent. [safety: WRITES DATA on this origin; repeat calls repeat the effect; fetches from the public internet. This page asks the person to confirm before it runs.]

url.description: optional replacement URL, otherwise the snapshot URL

tools.name: finger
tools.description: Look up who runs aadhar.sh, as a drivable terminal program. Panes: overview, writing, reading, listening, photos, around, coffee, deploys, search. Send `keys` to move (1-9 pane, j/k cursor, <cr> open, h back, ? help) and pass the returned `url`'s params back to continue. Returns a rendered 80-column frame. [safety: read-only.]

keys.description: a key sequence, up to 32 keys, e.g. "2jj<cr>"

open.description: id of the row to open (slug, index, or version number)

tools.name: photos
tools.description: Browse the published photo archive as a terminal frame, filterable by caption, film simulation, body, and lens. Opening a frame shows its exposure and the in-camera recipe it was shot with. Send `keys` (j/k cursor, <cr> open, n/p page). [safety: read-only.]

open.description: photo stem to open

tools.name: radar
tools.description: Render signal readings you have already measured (wifi/Bluetooth RSSI) as a terminal instrument: concentric strength bands, a meter and trend per source, and findphone's field calibration (-45 arm's reach, -60 same table, -72 same room). This origin has no antenna and does not sense anything; you supply the samples. Nothing is stored. Angles in the plot are decorative because RSSI carries no bearing. [safety: read-only.]

kind.description: optional tag, e.g. wifi or ble

history.description: optional trailing readings for the trend

source.description: optional label for what did the sampling

tools.name: encode
tools.description: Read a JPEG or AVIF at a URL and report what its encoder actually did: chroma subsampling, baseline vs progressive and the scan count, an estimated quality with the deviation from the IJG Annex K table shown, AVIF bit depth, and whether ICC/EXIF/XMP is riding along. NO PIXELS ARE DECODED — every fact comes from the container — so this works on files a Worker could never decode. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: agent_ready
tools.description: Grade how much of an origin a machine can actually use: llms.txt, a markdown twin, an agent card, an API catalog, and a real tools/list against its MCP server. Doors are COUNTED, never scored — a check that could not run is reported as unreadable rather than as a failure. Called with no url it audits aadhar.sh itself and prints what building that cost in files and lines. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: dict
tools.description: Will a browser ever actually use the compression dictionary a URL is serving? Compression dictionaries fail in total silence — Chromium declines to register a perfectly good one because of a cache directive, with no warning anywhere. Returns a rendered frame grading every registration rule, plus whether a delta-serving response varies on available-dictionary. Same route as /dict. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: cache
tools.description: Does a URL's ETag ever actually 304? A BEHAVIORAL probe rather than a header read: fetches twice to see whether the validator survives two identical requests, then replays it with If-None-Match and reports what the origin did. Also checks Accept negotiation against Vary. Returns a rendered frame. Same route as /cache. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: lens
tools.description: Inspect one public HTTP(S) URL and render the observation as a terminal frame: readability, agent doors, and what a single scan costs to read. Same rate limit and same refusals as lens_inspect; use lens_inspect instead if you want the fields rather than the frame. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

doors.description: also READ what is behind the agent doors: llms.txt, the markdown twin, the agent card, and a real tools/list against their MCP server. Their catalog is listed, never called.

tools.name: fitness_get_today
tools.description: What the user is scheduled to do today, based on their active plans and the local weekday. Returns the exercises with their targets, plus whether today is a training day at all. Start here when the user asks what they should do now.

tools.name: fitness_get_plans
tools.description: All of the user's training plans with their phases and exercises. Optionally filter by status ("active", "paused", "completed", "archived"). Use this to find a plan id before editing anything.

status.description: Only return plans in this status.

tools.name: fitness_get_plan
tools.description: One plan with every phase and exercise, including each exercise id. You need the exercise ids from here to update or remove individual movements.

tools.name: fitness_get_streak
tools.description: Current and longest streak. A streak counts only days the plan schedules — missing an unscheduled rest day never breaks it, and a scheduled day that has not happened yet does not either.

tools.name: fitness_get_progress
tools.description: The full picture over the last N days: streak, completion rate, total workouts, recent pain notes, recent plan edits, and target-vs-actual for each exercise in the active phase. Read this before advising on whether to add load.

days.description: Window to summarise, in days. Defaults to 30.

plan_id.description: Restrict the exercise trends and edits to one plan.

tools.name: fitness_get_calendar
tools.description: Day-by-day training status for one month: which days were scheduled, which were trained, how complete each session was, and which carry notes.

month.description: Month as "YYYY-MM". Defaults to the current month.

tools.name: fitness_get_workouts
tools.description: Past workout logs, newest first, each with the exercises performed and how they went. Filter by date range or limit the count.

limit.description: Maximum number of logs. Defaults to 10.

tools.name: fitness_get_workouts_on
tools.description: Every workout logged on a specific date — a day can hold more than one. Use this to find a workout id before editing or deleting it.

tools.name: fitness_get_badges
tools.description: All nine badges and whether the user has earned each one, how many times, and the context of each award. Useful for encouragement and for telling them what is close.

tools.name: fitness_get_body_metrics
tools.description: Body measurements over time, oldest first. Units: weight in pounds (lbs); height, bust, waist and hips in centimetres; body fat as a percentage.

days.description: How far back to read, in days. Defaults to 180.

tools.name: fitness_get_edit_history
tools.description: Every change made to exercise targets, by whom (the person or an agent) and why. Read this to understand what equipment the user actually has and how their load has been trending before suggesting a change.

days.description: How far back to read, in days. Defaults to 14.

tools.name: fitness_get_templates
tools.description: The built-in starter plans a user can adopt in one step. Offer these when someone wants to begin but does not know what to do, then call fitness_create_plan_from_template.

tools.name: fitness_get_settings
tools.description: The user's display name and what they call their coach. Read this to address them properly.

tools.name: fitness_create_plan
tools.description: Build a complete training plan with phases and exercises. `schedule` sets which weekdays to train. Each phase holds an ordered list of exercises; the first phase becomes the active one. For strength work fill target_reps and target_weight; for holds like planks fill target_duration instead. Ask about injuries and available equipment before calling this.

description.description: What the plan is for and how to approach it.

schedule.description: Which weekdays to train, e.g. {"mon": true, "wed": true, "fri": true}. Omitted days are rest days.

duration_days.description: How long this phase runs, in days. Optional.

notes.description: Notes about this phase.

exercise_name.description: Name of the movement, e.g. "Goblet Squat".

category.description: Defaults to "strength".

target_reps.description: Reps per set. Use this for strength work; leave null for timed holds.

target_weight.description: Working weight in pounds (lbs). Null for bodyweight movements.

target_duration.description: Seconds per set, for timed movements like planks or wall sits. Use instead of target_reps.

rest_seconds.description: Rest between sets, in seconds. Defaults to 60.

form_cues.description: One short coaching cue shown during the set.

notes.description: Any extra note about this movement.

tools.name: fitness_create_plan_from_template
tools.description: Adopt one of the built-in starter plans. The result is a normal, fully editable plan — adjust it afterwards with fitness_update_exercise. Call fitness_get_templates first to see the ids.

tools.name: fitness_update_plan
tools.description: Change a plan's name, description, weekday schedule, status, or dates. Set status to "paused" when someone needs a break and "active" when they return — a paused plan stops counting toward streaks.

schedule.description: Which weekdays to train, e.g. {"mon": true, "wed": true, "fri": true}. Omitted days are rest days.

status.description: New status.

tools.name: fitness_add_exercise
tools.description: Append a movement to a phase of a plan. Get the block id from fitness_get_plan. For strength work set target_reps and target_weight; for timed holds set target_duration.

exercise_name.description: Name of the movement, e.g. "Goblet Squat".

category.description: Defaults to "strength".

target_reps.description: Reps per set. Use this for strength work; leave null for timed holds.

target_weight.description: Working weight in pounds (lbs). Null for bodyweight movements.

target_duration.description: Seconds per set, for timed movements like planks or wall sits. Use instead of target_reps.

rest_seconds.description: Rest between sets, in seconds. Defaults to 60.

form_cues.description: One short coaching cue shown during the set.

notes.description: Any extra note about this movement.

tools.name: fitness_update_exercise
tools.description: Change the targets on one planned movement. Every changed field is written to the edit history with your reason, and shown to the user next to that exercise — so always pass `reason`, phrased for them ("knee felt tight last session"). Only send the fields you are changing.

rest_seconds.description: New rest between sets, in seconds.

notes.description: New note.

reason.description: Why this is changing. Shown to the user in the plan view.

tools.name: fitness_activate_block
tools.description: Make a phase of a plan the current one. Earlier phases are marked completed and later ones upcoming. Use this when the user has finished a block and is ready to progress.

tools.name: fitness_log_workout
tools.description: Record a completed workout. `date` defaults to today. For each movement record what was actually done, not what was planned — if they did fewer reps or dropped the weight, log that. Mark anything they skipped with skipped=true and a skip_reason. Put anything that hurt in pain_notes; it surfaces in progress summaries. Returns any badges this unlocks so you can congratulate them.

plan_exercise_id.description: The planned exercise this fulfils, when there is one. Links the log to the plan so progress trends work.

skipped.description: True if the movement was skipped entirely.

notes.description: Any note about this movement in this session.

date.description: Date of the workout, "YYYY-MM-DD". Defaults to today.

plan_id.description: The plan this session belongs to, if any.

block_id.description: The phase this session belongs to, if any.

pain_notes.description: Anything that hurt or felt off. Important — it drives future advice.

general_notes.description: Any other note about the session.

tools.name: fitness_update_workout
tools.description: Fix an existing workout log — add a note they forgot, correct the weight, or replace the exercise list wholesale. Find the workout id with fitness_get_workouts_on. Passing `exercises` replaces the whole list, so include every movement, not just the changed one.

plan_exercise_id.description: The planned exercise this fulfils, when there is one. Links the log to the plan so progress trends work.

skipped.description: True if the movement was skipped entirely.

notes.description: Any note about this movement in this session.

tools.name: fitness_log_body_metrics
tools.description: Record body measurements. Send only what was actually measured — nothing needs to be complete. Units: weight in pounds (lbs); height, bust, waist and hips in centimetres; body_fat as a percentage like 28.5. Logging the same date twice updates that day, overwriting only the fields you send.

notes.description: Any note about this measurement.

tools.name: fitness_update_settings
tools.description: Set what the app calls the user and what they call their coach. If the user tells you their name, or asks you to go by a particular name, record it here so the app greets them consistently.

coach_name.description: What the coach is called in the UI.

coach_tagline.description: Small label above the coach's note on the home screen.

tools.name: fitness_check_badges
tools.description: Re-run the badge checks and award anything newly earned. Logging a workout already does this, so you rarely need it on its own.

tools.name: fitness_delete_plan
tools.description: Remove a training plan and its phases. The user must approve this in the app before it happens; you will get back whether they did. Workout history is kept — deleting a plan never erases what they actually did.

tools.name: fitness_delete_exercise
tools.description: Take a movement out of a plan. The user must approve it in the app first. Prefer fitness_update_exercise when the goal is to make something easier rather than remove it.

tools.name: fitness_delete_workout
tools.description: Erase a logged workout — for a duplicate or something logged by mistake. The user must approve it in the app first. This changes their streak, so prefer fitness_update_workout when the log is merely wrong.

tools.name: fitness_navigate
tools.description: Switch the app to a screen so the user is looking at what you are talking about. Do this before explaining something visual — send them to "calendar" when discussing consistency, "badges" when congratulating them.

tab.description: today = home and next session; plan = the training plan; calendar = training history; body = measurements and charts; badges = the badge wall.

tools.name: fitness_start_session
tools.description: Open the guided session flow so the user can start training right now — it walks them through each set with a rest timer. Use it when they say they are ready to work out. Defaults to today's scheduled session.

plan_id.description: Plan to train. Defaults to today's scheduled plan, or the active one.

block_id.description: Phase to train. Defaults to the active phase.

tools.name: fitness_open_plan_editor
tools.description: Open the plan editor for the user to fill in themselves, rather than building it for them. Use this when they want to make the choices — or when they ask for something you should not decide alone. Pass a plan_id to edit an existing plan, or omit it to start a blank one.

plan_id.description: Plan to edit. Omit to open a blank editor.

tools.name: fitness_highlight_exercise
tools.description: Scroll to an exercise in the plan view and flash it, so the user can see which movement you mean while you talk about it.

exercise_id.description: The planned exercise to point at.

tools.name: list_components

tools.name: list_nets

tools.name: review_design

tools.name: audit_design

tools.name: crossref_net

tools.name: compare_schematic_pcb

tools.name: export_schematic_pcb_comparison

tools.name: summarize_design
tools.description: Return an agent-friendly loaded-design summary.

tools.name: find_components
tools.description: Find loaded components by refdes, MPN, value, description, or footprint.

tools.name: query_bom_item
tools.description: Find normalized BOM rows by refdes, MPN, or text pattern.

tools.name: list_pin_connections
tools.description: List compact pin-to-net rows for one loaded component.

tools.name: query_net

tools.name: list_component_types

tools.name: list_diagnostics
tools.description: Return parser diagnostics for loaded designs.

tools.name: compare_bom_pcb
tools.description: Compare normalized BOM rows against matching PCB components.

tools.name: list_single_pin_nets
tools.description: List schematic nets with exactly one connected pin.

tools.name: query_pcb_component

tools.name: query_pcb_net

tools.name: summarize_pcb

tools.name: list_design_rules

tools.name: review_fabrication_readiness
tools.description: Review loaded PCB data for fabrication-readiness signals.

tools.name: get_lens_prescription
tools.description: Read the complete Lens Editor prescription or one visible Object, surface, or Image row.

tools.name: set_lens_prescription
tools.description: Replace the complete Lens Editor prescription after strict validation. Numeric input guidance: Flat surfaces use `0` for radius of curvature. Infinity object/image distances use `1e10`. Material input guidance: catalog glass requires `manufacturer` to be one of `CDGM`, `Hikari`, `Hoya`, `Ohara`, `Schott`, or `Sumita`; special materials and reflective surfaces use an empty manufacturer. Single-index model glass uses `{"medium": "<refractive_index>", "manufacturer": ""}`. Model glass with `nd` and `vd` uses `{"medium": "<nd>", "manufacturer": "<vd>"}`. All numeric values must be stringified. Material input special cases guidance: reflective surfaces use `{"medium": "REFL", "manufacturer": ""}`. Air, water, fluorite/fluorspar/CaF2, fused silica, and Schott D263 T eco use `{"medium": "air" | "Water" | "CAF2" | "Fused Silica" | "D263TECO", "manufacturer": ""}`. Some Ohara names ending in a single digit, including `S-BSL7`, `S-FSL5`, and `S-NBH5`, require canonical names with whitespace: `S-BSL 7`, `S-FSL 5`, and `S-NBH 5`.

tools.name: insert_lens_surface
tools.description: Insert a default physical lens surface after Object or a visible surface index. Numeric input guidance: Flat surfaces use `0` for radius of curvature. Infinity object/image distances use `1e10`. Material input guidance: catalog glass requires `manufacturer` to be one of `CDGM`, `Hikari`, `Hoya`, `Ohara`, `Schott`, or `Sumita`; special materials and reflective surfaces use an empty manufacturer. Single-index model glass uses `{"medium": "<refractive_index>", "manufacturer": ""}`. Model glass with `nd` and `vd` uses `{"medium": "<nd>", "manufacturer": "<vd>"}`. All numeric values must be stringified. Material input special cases guidance: reflective surfaces use `{"medium": "REFL", "manufacturer": ""}`. Air, water, fluorite/fluorspar/CaF2, fused silica, and Schott D263 T eco use `{"medium": "air" | "Water" | "CAF2" | "Fused Silica" | "D263TECO", "manufacturer": ""}`. Some Ohara names ending in a single digit, including `S-BSL7`, `S-FSL5`, and `S-NBH5`, require canonical names with whitespace: `S-BSL 7`, `S-FSL 5`, and `S-NBH 5`.

tools.name: update_lens_row
tools.description: Update applicable simple or nested fields on a visible Object, surface, or Image row. Numeric input guidance: Flat surfaces use `0` for radius of curvature. Infinity object/image distances use `1e10`. Material input guidance: catalog glass requires `manufacturer` to be one of `CDGM`, `Hikari`, `Hoya`, `Ohara`, `Schott`, or `Sumita`; special materials and reflective surfaces use an empty manufacturer. Single-index model glass uses `{"medium": "<refractive_index>", "manufacturer": ""}`. Model glass with `nd` and `vd` uses `{"medium": "<nd>", "manufacturer": "<vd>"}`. All numeric values must be stringified. Material input special cases guidance: reflective surfaces use `{"medium": "REFL", "manufacturer": ""}`. Air, water, fluorite/fluorspar/CaF2, fused silica, and Schott D263 T eco use `{"medium": "air" | "Water" | "CAF2" | "Fused Silica" | "D263TECO", "manufacturer": ""}`. Some Ohara names ending in a single digit, including `S-BSL7`, `S-FSL5`, and `S-NBH5`, require canonical names with whitespace: `S-BSL 7`, `S-FSL 5`, and `S-NBH 5`.

tools.description: Delete one physical lens surface by its current visible positive index.

tools.name: get_system_specs
tools.description: Read the current draft OpticalSpecs from the Lens Editor.

tools.name: set_system_aperture
tools.description: Stage a supported Object EPD/NA or Image F/# pupil specification for the Lens Editor.

tools.name: set_half_field
tools.description: Stage a relative Object Height/Angle or Image Height half-field specification with one to ten samples.

tools.name: set_wavelengths
tools.description: Stage one to seven wavelength/weight tuples and an in-range reference wavelength index.

tools.name: recompute_optical_system
tools.description: Recompute and commit the complete optical system, including glass validation, analyses, layout, selected-index clamping, and auto-aperture results.

tools.name: focus_optical_system
tools.description: Focus the current draft optical system using the selected chromaticity and metric, then recompute it. This focusing only changes the thickness of the space between the last optical surface and the image plane, so it is not suitable for all optical systems.

tools.name: get_paraxial_data
tools.description: Read the complete first-order data shown by the Paraxial Data dialog. Reads the current committed optical system. To include pending Lens Editor edits, call `recompute_optical_system` first. Stored results must belong to that exact model; after optimization Apply, call `recompute_optical_system` if results are missing or stale.

tools.name: get_3rd_order_seidel_data
tools.description: Read complete third-order Seidel and primary chromatic surfaceBySurface (S-I to S-V, C-I axial color, C-II lateral color), surface-by-surface wavefront in waves (W040, W131, W222, W220P Petzval curvature, W220 field curvature, W311, W020 axial color, W111 lateral color), transverse, and curvature data, including surface labels and sum totals. Aspheric contributions are included in their surface's column. C-I, C-II, W020, and W111 use the index difference between the first and last wavelengths and are zero with fewer than 3 wavelengths. Reads the current committed optical system. To include pending Lens Editor edits, call `recompute_optical_system` first. Stored results must belong to that exact model; after optimization Apply, call `recompute_optical_system` if results are missing or stale.

tools.description: Read complete Zernike data and labeled terms using the current app image reference.
