tools.name: apply_palette
tools.description: Applies a palette preset to a room or the whole home: wall colour, floor material and the textile family used for re-tinted fabrics. Presets: warm-clay, sage-linen, dusk, nordic, terrazzo, ochre-sun.

room.description: Room id or name, e.g. living or Living Room. Defaults to the active room.

scope.description: Apply to one room or the whole home; default room.

tools.name: arrange_room
tools.description: Re-arranges all unlocked furniture in a room in one animated pass. Styles: conversation (seating faces each other around a focal point), media (seating faces the TV or media wall), open (maximum clear floor and walkways), work (desk by the window, storage on the walls). Keeps door swings and clearances free and reports what moved with the conflict count before and after.

room.description: Room id or name, e.g. living or Living Room. Defaults to the active room.

style.description: Arrangement style: conversation, media, open or work.

keep_locked.description: Keep locked furniture in place; default true.

focus.description: Optional focal point: an item id or name (e.g. the fireplace or TV) or window:<id>.

tools.name: clear_home
tools.description: Removes every item from every room after the human confirms in a dialog on the page. The removed layout is kept so restore_furniture (or undo) can bring it back. Returns cancelled if the human declines.

tools.name: clear_room
tools.description: Removes every item from a room after the human confirms in a dialog on the page. The removed layout is kept so restore_furniture (or undo) can bring it back. Returns cancelled if the human declines.

room.description: Room id or name, e.g. living or Living Room. Defaults to the active room.

tools.name: export_design_board
tools.description: Creates a design board PNG for a room: dollhouse render, plan view, palette swatches and an itemised list with prices and the total, then starts the download in the page. Use it to present or share a finished layout.

room.description: Room id or name, e.g. living or Living Room. Defaults to the active room.

title.description: Board title (default the room name).

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: The shopping cart: each line with product, colorway, quantity, unit and line price in USD, the subtotal, the design budget and how much of it remains, and whether checkout is available. Lines note which placed item they belong to.

tools.name: get_conflicts
tools.description: Lists layout problems in a room or the whole home: overlapping items, items outside the room, missing clearance in front of seating, beds and desks, blocked door swings, pinched traffic paths and, when accessibility mode is on, paths under 90 cm and missing 150 cm turning circles. Each conflict names the items involved and a concrete fix in cm.

room.description: Room id or name, or all for the whole home. Defaults to the active room.

tools.name: get_design_report
tools.description: Design critique of a room scored 0–10 on balance, focal point, conversation seating, lighting coverage, storage and traffic flow, with an overall score out of 100 and the top three improvements. Use it to review a layout or to explain why a room feels off.

room.description: Room id or name, e.g. living or Living Room. Defaults to the active room.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Full details of one catalog product: dimensions in cm, price in USD, colorways, front clearance needed, seat count, style tags and which walls of a room it fits with the spare cm. Pass compare_to (a placed item) to learn whether the product matches that item's size exactly, closely or not. Use it to confirm a product before placing, previewing or adding it to the cart.

product.description: Catalog product id (e.g. sofa-endre) or product name from search_catalog.

room.description: Room id or name, e.g. living or Living Room. Defaults to the active room.

compare_to.description: Placed item id or name (or selected) to compare sizes with; adds size_match with the cm difference per side.

tools.name: get_room_details
tools.description: Details of one room: walls (id, side, length in cm and the free spans where furniture can go), openings (doors, windows, arches with wall, offset, width and swing) and every placed item with id, name, position, rotation, footprint and colorway. Coordinates are room-local in cm: origin at the north-west corner, x east, y south. Use it before placing or moving furniture in that room.

room.description: Room id or name, e.g. living or Living Room. Defaults to the active room.

tools.name: get_scene_summary
tools.description: Overview of the whole home: every room with id, name, type, size in m², wall sides with lengths in cm, item count and conflict count; plus the current mode, view, time of day, accessibility flag, active room, the human's selection, cart subtotal and design budget in USD. Call it first to learn room and item ids before reading details or placing furniture.

tools.name: get_selection
tools.description: What the human is pointing at right now: the selected item, hovered item, last moved item (and whether the human or the agent moved it), the selected room and the camera focus. Use it to resolve words like this, that, here or the one I clicked before acting.

tools.name: load_variant
tools.description: Restores a previously saved layout variant of a room by name, replacing the room's current furniture. Save the current layout first if you want to keep it.

room.description: Room id or name, e.g. living or Living Room. Defaults to the active room.

tools.name: measure
tools.description: Measures in cm: a wall's length and free spans, an item's footprint, the gap between two items, or the distance from an item to a wall or opening. Subjects are wall sides (north, east, south, west), wall ids (w0…), item ids or names, or opening ids. Use it to check fit before placing or moving.

subject.description: What to measure: a wall side or id, an item id or name, or an opening id.

to.description: Optional second thing (wall, item or opening) to measure the gap or distance to.

room.description: Room id or name, e.g. living or Living Room. Defaults to the active room.

tools.name: move_furniture
tools.description: Moves and/or rotates a placed item. Give an anchor in words (wall + along, facing, next_to, centered, under), a raw pos in cm, a delta in cm, a rotation (0, 90, 180 or 270 clockwise; 0 faces south) or rotate_by, and optionally another room. Snaps and nudges like place_furniture and returns the resolved position and any conflicts.

item.description: Placed item id (e.g. sofa-1) or its name. Use selected for the human's current selection.

wall.description: Wall the back goes against: north, east, south, west, or a wall id such as w2.

along.description: Position along that wall: start, center, end, or a number of cm from the wall's start (clockwise).

facing.description: What the front faces: an item id or name, room_center, wall:<side>, or window:<id>.

next_to.description: Item id or name to sit beside.

side.description: Side of next_to to use: left, right, front or behind (from that item's point of view).

gap_cm.description: Gap in cm between the two items (default 10).

centered.description: true to centre the item in the room.

under.description: window:<id> to centre the item under that window with its back to the wall.

anchor.description: Where to put it, in words: wall + along, facing, next_to + side + gap_cm, centered, or under a window. Preferred over pos.

x.description: Footprint centre x in cm; positive points east.

y.description: Footprint centre y in cm; positive points south.

pos.description: Raw footprint centre in cm, room-local (origin north-west corner, x east, y south). Use anchor when possible.

delta_cm.description: Shift by this many cm: x positive = east, y positive = south.

x.description: East-west shift in cm; positive is east.

y.description: North-south shift in cm; positive is south.

rotation.description: 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees clockwise; 0 = front faces south.

room.description: Move the item into this room (id or name). Defaults to its current room.

tools.name: place_furniture
tools.description: Places a catalog product in a room as a new item. Position it with an anchor in words (back against a wall at start, center, end or N cm along it; facing an item or the room centre; next to an item with a gap; centred; or under a window) or with a raw pos in cm and a rotation. The engine snaps to the wall, nudges up to 60 cm to avoid collisions and reports conflicts. Returns the new item id.

product.description: Catalog product id (e.g. sofa-endre) or product name from search_catalog.

room.description: Room id or name, e.g. living or Living Room. Defaults to the active room.

wall.description: Wall the back goes against: north, east, south, west, or a wall id such as w2.

along.description: Position along that wall: start, center, end, or a number of cm from the wall's start (clockwise).

facing.description: What the front faces: an item id or name, room_center, wall:<side>, or window:<id>.

next_to.description: Item id or name to sit beside.

side.description: Side of next_to to use: left, right, front or behind (from that item's point of view).

gap_cm.description: Gap in cm between the two items (default 10).

centered.description: true to centre the item in the room.

under.description: window:<id> to centre the item under that window with its back to the wall.

anchor.description: Where to put it, in words: wall + along, facing, next_to + side + gap_cm, centered, or under a window. Preferred over pos.

x.description: Footprint centre x in cm; positive points east.

y.description: Footprint centre y in cm; positive points south.

pos.description: Raw footprint centre in cm, room-local (origin north-west corner, x east, y south). Use anchor when possible.

rotation.description: 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees clockwise; 0 = front faces south.

colorway.description: Colorway id or name, e.g. oak, sage, terracotta, dusty-blue.

tools.name: preview_in_room
tools.description: Try before you buy: shows a translucent ghost of a catalog product at an anchor or position in a room with its price, fit and conflicts, without changing the layout or the cart. One preview at a time; confirm_preview keeps it and cancel_preview discards it.

product.description: Catalog product id (e.g. sofa-endre) or product name from search_catalog.

room.description: Room id or name, e.g. living or Living Room. Defaults to the active room.

wall.description: Wall the back goes against: north, east, south, west, or a wall id such as w2.

along.description: Position along that wall: start, center, end, or a number of cm from the wall's start (clockwise).

facing.description: What the front faces: an item id or name, room_center, wall:<side>, or window:<id>.

next_to.description: Item id or name to sit beside.

side.description: Side of next_to to use: left, right, front or behind (from that item's point of view).

gap_cm.description: Gap in cm between the two items (default 10).

centered.description: true to centre the item in the room.

under.description: window:<id> to centre the item under that window with its back to the wall.

anchor.description: Where to put it, in words: wall + along, facing, next_to + side + gap_cm, centered, or under a window. Preferred over pos.

x.description: Footprint centre x in cm; positive points east.

y.description: Footprint centre y in cm; positive points south.

pos.description: Raw footprint centre in cm, room-local (origin north-west corner, x east, y south). Use anchor when possible.

rotation.description: 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees clockwise; 0 = front faces south.

colorway.description: Colorway id or name, e.g. oak, sage, terracotta, dusty-blue.

tools.name: remove_furniture
tools.description: Removes one placed item from its room. If the item is linked to a cart line, that line is removed as well and the result says so. Use clear_room to empty a whole room.

item.description: Placed item id (e.g. sofa-1) or its name. Use selected for the human's current selection.

tools.name: resize_furniture
tools.description: Changes a placed item's size in cm: width, depth and height, or scale_percent of its catalog size; reset restores the catalog size. The 3D model stretches to the new size and every rule (overlap, clearance, walls) uses it. Nudges the item up to 60 cm to stay inside the room and reports conflicts. Returns the new and the catalog dimensions and the closest catalog product to the new size.

item.description: Placed item id (e.g. sofa-1) or its name. Use selected for the human's current selection.

width_cm.description: New width in cm (10–1000), left–right facing the front. Sides not given keep their current size.

height_cm.description: New height in cm (10–1000), floor to top.

scale_percent.description: Scale every side to this percentage of the catalog size, 25–400; 100 restores it.

tools.name: restore_furniture
tools.description: Brings back the furniture removed by the last clear_home or clear_room, into the rooms it came from. Items whose room no longer exists are skipped and listed. Returns not_found when nothing has been cleared.

tools.name: save_variant
tools.description: Saves the current furniture layout of a room under a name (for example Cosy or Media wall) so it can be restored with load_variant or, once two or more exist, compared side by side with compare_variants.

name.description: Short name for this saved room layout.

room.description: Room id or name, e.g. living or Living Room. Defaults to the active room.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Searches Hearth Studio's furniture catalog (Shopify). Filter by category, maximum price in USD, maximum width and depth in cm, style, colorway, or the wall it must fit (fits_wall) in a room. Give target dimensions (width_cm, depth_cm, height_cm) or like_item to rank by closest size: each result then says exact, close or off with the cm difference. Returns up to 6 products with id, price, dimensions, colorways and a fit note. Ids feed place_furniture, preview_in_room and update_cart.

query.description: Free-text search, e.g. small oak desk.

category.description: Furniture category.

fits_wall.description: Only products whose width fits a free span on this wall (north, east, south, west or wall id) of the room.

room.description: Room id or name, e.g. living or Living Room. Defaults to the active room.

style.description: Style tag such as scandinavian, japandi, mid-century, rustic, modern.

colorway.description: Colorway id or name, e.g. oak, sage, terracotta, dusty-blue.

limit.description: Maximum results, from 1 to 6; default 6.

width_cm.description: Target width in cm; results are ranked by how close their size is (see dims_match).

depth_cm.description: Target depth in cm; results are ranked by how close their size is (see dims_match).

height_cm.description: Target height in cm; results are ranked by how close their size is (see dims_match).

like_item.description: Placed item id or name (or selected) whose current size is the target; its category is used unless category is given.

tolerance_cm.description: How many cm per side still count as close (default 10). exact = every side within 1 cm.

tools.name: set_accessibility_mode
tools.description: Turns accessibility mode on or off. On: paths must be at least 90 cm wide, a 150 cm turning circle is required beside the bed, desk and sofa, reach zones are shown, and get_conflicts and the overlays report these rules. Off: standard 60 cm walkways.

enabled.description: true enables accessibility layout rules; false restores standard rules.

tools.name: set_colorway
tools.description: Changes a placed item's colorway (for example oak, sage, terracotta or dusty-blue). If the product is in the cart, the cart line switches to the matching variant. Lists the available colorways when the requested one is unknown.

item.description: Placed item id (e.g. sofa-1) or its name. Use selected for the human's current selection.

colorway.description: Colorway id or name, e.g. oak, sage, terracotta, dusty-blue.

tools.name: set_mode
tools.description: Switches the studio mode. build: edit rooms and openings (enables apply_template, create_room, update_room, add_opening, move_opening and remove_opening). design: place and arrange furniture. shop: browse products and manage the cart with prices shown; enables get_checkout_link. Design and shop tools stay available in every mode.

mode.description: Studio mode: build, design or shop.

tools.name: set_time_of_day
tools.description: Sets the lighting time of day: morning (cool soft light), noon (bright with short shadows), golden (warm low sun) or evening (dusk, every lamp glows). Changes the look only; the layout stays the same.

time.description: Lighting time: morning, noon, golden or evening.

tools.name: set_view
tools.description: Changes the camera: plan (top-down) or dollhouse (isometric), optionally focused on the whole home with focus: "home", a room, or an item, with the isometric yaw at nw, ne, se or sw. Use it to show the human what you are working on.

focus.description: Use home for the entire home, or give a room/item id or name. Defaults to the active room.

yaw.description: Dollhouse compass yaw: nw, ne, se or sw.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undoes the last change(s) to the scene, whether made by the agent or the human, 1 to 10 steps at a time. Returns what was undone.

steps.description: Number of scene changes to undo, from 1 to 10; default 1.

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the Shopify cart. add: adds a product (by product id or a placed item) in a colorway with a quantity; remove: removes that product's line; set_quantity: sets the line's quantity. Returns the new subtotal in USD and the remaining budget. Purchases are completed by the human at checkout.

action.description: Cart action: add, remove or set_quantity.

product.description: Catalog product id or name. Give either product or item.

item.description: Placed item id or name; its product and colorway are used and the cart line is linked to it.

colorway.description: Colorway id or name, e.g. oak, sage, terracotta, dusty-blue.

quantity.description: Quantity for add (default 1) or set_quantity.

hearth.yadneshsalvi.com.name: Hearth

tools.name: plan_job_workflow
tools.description: Pass one required goal: complete_job_hunt, find_roles, compare_roles, save_search, monitor_search, manage_saved_search, prepare_application, withdraw_application_consent, enable_recovery, or recover_workspace. Search, compare, and prepare default to headless; use follow only when asked to open them. Jobbbler-managed email updates use monitor_search, not a client-side scheduler. Returns route-aware decision steps. Advisory only; grants nothing.

goal.description: The outcome to plan for.

tools.name: get_search_filters
tools.description: Read Jobbbler's exact search vocabulary: accepted categories, work models, seniorities, salary options, and sort orders. Use when an enum is unclear, not before every search; search_jobs already documents common values.

tools.name: search_jobs
tools.description: Search Jobbbler's source-backed catalog directly. Do not use external job sources when the person asks for this site's tools. Pass only the criteria the person stated; leave categories, employmentTypes and unknownPolicy unset so nothing is narrowed silently. For ‘Berlin or remote’, pass locations=['Berlin'] with remoteOrLocations=true. Default headless keeps the page unchanged; use follow only when asked to watch. Results include IDs, salary, seniority, evidence, and a cursor.

query.description: Technology role, skill, or outcome to search for.

categories.description: Technology job functions to include.

employmentTypes.description: Employment arrangements that matching roles must use.

locations.description: Cities, countries, or regions to include. Do not use Remote as a place; use remoteOrLocations for requests such as ‘Berlin or remote’.

remoteOrLocations.description: Match listed locations OR remote roles anywhere. Requires a location; for remote-only, use workModels=['remote'].

skills.description: Technology skills to prefer in match ranking.

excludeKeywords.description: Keywords that must not appear in a matching role.

salary.description: Annual, monthly, or hourly compensation constraint.

postedWithinDays.description: Maximum age of a posting in days.

sort.description: Result ordering.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from search_jobs; keep every other search criterion unchanged.

limit.description: Fixed agent page size. Omit this field or pass 3 so nextCursor reaches every result.

presentation.description: headless keeps the current page unchanged; follow opens and synchronizes the visible search.

tools.name: open_job_details
tools.description: Navigate to a role returned by search_jobs while preserving the current criteria. Every Jobbbler tool stays registered across the navigation.

jobId.description: A job ID returned by search_jobs.

tools.name: prepare_application
tools.description: Use one job ID the person selected to create or reopen its private application and return the application ID, URL, and next tool. Default headless keeps the current page; use presentation=follow only when the person asks to open it. This grants no preparation authority, shares no candidate data, and submits nothing.

jobId.description: A job ID returned by search_jobs or get_job_details.

presentation.description: headless keeps the current page unchanged; follow opens the application workspace.

tools.name: get_applications
tools.description: Use optional limit and offset with a current or recovered owner session to return application and job IDs, each application's page href, role details, status, update time, receipt availability, and nextOffset without returning answers, contact data, or credentials.

limit.description: Number of applications to return, from 1 to 20. Defaults to 10.

offset.description: Zero-based offset into applications sorted newest first. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: open_jobbbler_page
tools.description: Use a supported page name plus exact job or application IDs when required to open Search, Saved searches, Applications, the WebMCP guide, a comparison, or one application, and return the opened page and URL without changing stored data.

tools.name: enable_workspace_recovery
tools.description: Use the current owner session and the person's exact email to start, then its challengeId and the six-digit code the person supplies to finish, returning only the phase and next tools; this is not data consent, not submission approval, and not email-update permission.

email.description: Email explicitly supplied by the person for optional recovery.

challengeId.description: Exact challengeId returned by this tool's start action.

code.description: Six-digit code explicitly supplied by the person in the agent client.

tools.name: recover_jobbbler_workspace
tools.description: Use the verified email the person supplies to start, then its exact recoveryId and six-digit code to finish, returning only the phase and next tools without exposing the email, code, owner, or session credential.

email.description: Verified email explicitly supplied by the person in the agent client.

recoveryId.description: Exact recoveryId returned by this tool's start action.

code.description: Six-digit code explicitly supplied by the person in the agent client.

tools.name: get_search_state
tools.description: Read the latest headless or visible search. Use detail=summary for a bounded explanation, or detail=exact for criteria accepted by save_job_search and request_search_alert. Returns whether the search is visible and never reruns it.

detail.description: summary for display; exact for criteria reusable by save_job_search or request_search_alert.

tools.name: get_job_details
tools.description: Read one technology role's full description, requirements, provenance, compensation, known unknowns, and fit evidence. Pass the exact Jobbbler role ID in jobId. It works from any page and changes nothing.

jobId.description: A Jobbbler job ID returned by search_jobs or another Jobbbler tool.

tools.name: compare_jobs
tools.description: Compare source-backed roles after two or three exact job IDs are known. Pass every selected ID in jobIds. Default headless keeps the current page; use presentation=follow only when the person asks to open the comparison. Never call it with one role; search or ask for the missing target first.

jobIds.description: Two or three distinct job IDs returned by Jobbbler tools.

items.description: A Jobbbler job ID returned by search_jobs or another Jobbbler tool.

presentation.description: headless keeps the current page unchanged; follow opens the visible comparison.

tools.name: get_comparison
tools.description: Read the current one-to-three-role comparison, including fit evidence, compensation, provenance, and unknowns. Use when the user asks about the comparison already open. If the person asks which role is best, which to keep, or which to remove without giving a ranking preference, ask for the person's ranking criteria instead of asking them to choose a role ID.

tools.name: remove_job_from_comparison
tools.description: Remove a specified job from the comparison already open. Use only for a job ID in the visible set. This updates local page state and does not change server data.

jobId.description: A job ID present in the visible comparison.

tools.name: add_job_to_comparison
tools.description: Add a job by ID to the comparison already open. The comparison holds at most three distinct roles; the visible page and URL update to include the new set.

jobId.description: A job ID from search_jobs or get_job_details to add to this comparison.

tools.name: get_saved_alerts
tools.description: Use optional limit and offset with the current private owner to list saved searches newest first, returning each saved-search ID, email-update state, next check, and nextOffset without exposing an email address or sign-in information.

limit.description: How many saved searches to return, from 1 to 6. If omitted, return 6.

offset.description: How many saved searches to skip, starting with the newest. If omitted, skip none.

tools.name: request_search_alert
tools.description: When the person asks Jobbbler to keep checking a search or email changes, ask in the agent client for any missing name, schedule, time zone, or email, then use the exact supplied values to return one review for approve or decline with decide_search_alert. This is server-side monitoring that continues after the browser closes; do not substitute client automation. Require a six-digit code only for a new email.

name.description: A short name the person will recognize for these email updates.

query.description: Technology role, skill, or outcome to search for.

categories.description: Technology job functions to include.

employmentTypes.description: Employment arrangements that matching roles must use.

locations.description: Cities, countries, or regions to include. Do not use Remote as a place; use remoteOrLocations for requests such as ‘Berlin or remote’.

remoteOrLocations.description: Match listed locations OR remote roles anywhere. Requires a location; for remote-only, use workModels=['remote'].

skills.description: Technology skills to prefer in match ranking.

excludeKeywords.description: Keywords that must not appear in a matching role.

salary.description: Annual, monthly, or hourly compensation constraint.

postedWithinDays.description: Maximum age of a posting in days.

sort.description: Result ordering.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from search_jobs; keep every other search criterion unchanged.

limit.description: Number of visible results to request.

criteria.description: Search choices from search_jobs or the exact choices from get_search_state.

time.description: Time on the person's clock, written in 24-hour HH:mm form, for example 09:30.

timeZone.description: Time zone name, for example Europe/Kyiv.

time.description: Time on the person's clock, written in 24-hour HH:mm form, for example 09:30.

timeZone.description: Time zone name, for example Europe/Kyiv.

days.description: Days of the week to check. List each day only once.

email.description: Email address the person gave for job updates.

tools.name: decide_search_alert
tools.description: Use the exact requestId and reviewToken from request_search_alert, the person's explicit approved or declined decision, and a six-digit code only when requested to return the decision and turn on only the unchanged reviewed updates.

requestId.description: Copy the requestId returned by request_search_alert.

reviewToken.description: Copy the reviewToken returned by request_search_alert exactly as given.

code.description: The 6-digit code sent to the person's email. Include it only when request_search_alert asks for it; otherwise leave it out.

requestId.description: Copy the requestId returned by request_search_alert.

reviewToken.description: Copy the reviewToken returned by request_search_alert exactly as given.

tools.name: set_job_alert_state
tools.description: Pause or resume email updates with the scheduleId from get_saved_alerts or the savedSearchId of the search; delete permanently only with the exact savedSearchId and confirmation after the person clearly requests it, and return the resulting state or deletion receipt; an ambiguous stop request means pause, and more than one possible match requires a question.

action.description: Pause email updates. Keep the saved search.

scheduleId.description: The scheduleId returned by get_saved_alerts for this alert.

savedSearchId.description: Alternatively, the savedSearchId returned by save_job_search or decide_search_alert; its alert is resolved for you.

action.description: Turn email updates back on for this paused alert.

scheduleId.description: The scheduleId returned by get_saved_alerts for this alert.

savedSearchId.description: Alternatively, the savedSearchId returned by save_job_search or decide_search_alert; its alert is resolved for you.

action.description: Permanently delete one saved search and stop its email updates, if any.

savedSearchId.description: The savedSearchId returned by get_saved_alerts for this search.

confirmation.description: Use only after the person clearly asks to permanently delete this saved search and its email updates.

tools.name: open_saved_search
tools.description: Use a savedSearchId from get_saved_alerts to open its exact choices on the results page and return the opened route and saved-search ID without changing the criteria.

savedSearchId.description: The savedSearchId returned by get_saved_alerts for this search.

tools.name: get_latest_search_update
tools.description: Use a savedSearchId plus optional limit and offset to return counts and a paged list of job IDs that are new, updated, closed, or no longer match since the latest check, including nextOffset when more changes remain.

savedSearchId.description: The savedSearchId returned by get_saved_alerts for this search.

limit.description: How many changed jobs to return, from 1 to 5. If omitted, return 5.

offset.description: How many changed jobs to skip. If omitted, skip none.

tools.name: save_job_search
tools.description: Use a short name and exact choices the person supplied or get_search_state(detail=exact) to save and return a saved-search ID with email updates off; ask for missing values, and use request_search_alert instead when the person wants notifications.

name.description: A short name the person will recognize for this saved search.

query.description: Technology role, skill, or outcome to search for.

categories.description: Technology job functions to include.

employmentTypes.description: Employment arrangements that matching roles must use.

locations.description: Cities, countries, or regions to include. Do not use Remote as a place; use remoteOrLocations for requests such as ‘Berlin or remote’.

remoteOrLocations.description: Match listed locations OR remote roles anywhere. Requires a location; for remote-only, use workModels=['remote'].

skills.description: Technology skills to prefer in match ranking.

excludeKeywords.description: Keywords that must not appear in a matching role.

salary.description: Annual, monthly, or hourly compensation constraint.

postedWithinDays.description: Maximum age of a posting in days.

sort.description: Result ordering.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from search_jobs; keep every other search criterion unchanged.

limit.description: Number of visible results to request.

criteria.description: Search choices from search_jobs or the exact choices from get_search_state.

tools.name: get_application_readiness
tools.description: Pass the application ID returned by prepare_application as draftId. Read safe completion counts, missing field keys and labels, receipt state, and the next useful action without returning private answers.

draftId.description: An application ID returned by prepare_application.

tools.name: request_application_assistance
tools.description: Pass the application ID returned by prepare_application as draftId. The person's request to apply is the authority: assistance is granted at once, without a question, and propose_application_updates is the next step. Nothing is sent to an employer until the person approves the exact completed application.

draftId.description: An application ID returned by prepare_application.

tools.name: decide_application_assistance
tools.description: Assistance is granted automatically; call this only when the person asks to stop the agent's help. Pass draftId, the requestId from request_application_assistance, and withdraw (or declined) to revoke active assistance bound to it; it never shares data or submits.

draftId.description: An application ID returned by prepare_application.

decision.description: The person's explicit decision in the agent client.

tools.name: propose_application_updates
tools.description: Pass draftId for the application and update up to 24 distinct fields from known facts in one call. For cover_letter, use the full role and local CV context but send only the finished letter. Ask once, in a single message, for every fact readiness reports as missing; skip optional fields the person never mentioned.

draftId.description: An application ID returned by prepare_application.

patches.description: Answers from known facts only. For cover_letter, use get_job_details and local CV facts; send only the letter. Ask; never invent missing facts.

fieldKey.description: A field key reported by get_application_readiness.

value.description: A truthful answer written from supplied facts. A cover_letter should be complete and role-specific, not a generic motivation sentence.

tools.name: request_submission_review
tools.description: Pass draftId for the completed application. Freeze its exact field values and return them to the already-authorized agent client. Present every value before asking for one final decision. The review link is an optional browser fallback; this submits nothing.

draftId.description: An application ID returned by prepare_application.

tools.name: decide_application_submission
tools.description: Pass draftId for the same application, the exact requestId and draftVersion returned by request_submission_review, and the person's explicit decision. Never approve on the person's behalf. On approval, store disclosure consent, seal the unchanged payload, submit once, and return a receipt; on decline, share and submit nothing.

draftId.description: An application ID returned by prepare_application.

requestId.description: The review request ID returned by request_submission_review.

draftVersion.description: The exact draft version returned with the review request.

decision.description: The person's explicit decision in the agent client.

tools.name: withdraw_application_consent
tools.description: Pass draftId for the owner-accessible application to immediately withdraw every live consent-based permission tied to it. This stops future processing under that consent; it does not erase the application or retract a submission already sent.

draftId.description: An application ID returned by prepare_application.

tools.name: componentAdd
tools.description: Add an A-Frame component to an entity with an optional initial value (e.g. component 'animation__spin', value 'property: rotation; to: 0 360 0; loop: true; dur: 4000'). Use entityUpdate to change a component the entity already has, and managedStreetUpdate for street-segment generated components.

entityId.description: The ID of the entity to add the component to

component.description: The component name, including a multi-instance suffix when several of the same type are wanted (e.g. 'animation__spin')

value.description: Initial component value as an A-Frame attribute string ('prop: v; prop2: v2'); omit for component defaults

tools.name: componentRemove
tools.description: Remove an A-Frame component from an entity. Undoable — the removed value is restored on undo.

entityId.description: The ID of the entity to remove the component from

component.description: The component name as it appears on the entity (e.g. 'animation__spin')

tools.name: detachAllClones
tools.description: Detach every clone a generator (street-generated-clones, street-generated-stencil or street-generated-pedestrians component on a managed street segment) currently places, so each vehicle, tree, prop, stencil or pedestrian becomes a plain entity that can be moved, rotated, duplicated or deleted on its own, and remove that generator from the segment so nothing regenerates. The rest of the street stays managed. Use detachClone for a single object and convertStreetToShapes for the whole street. Name the generator by the segment entity and the component name on it; segments list their generators as 'street-generated-*' components in the scene state.

segmentId.description: ID of the street-segment entity carrying the generator

component.description: Generator component name on that segment, e.g. 'street-generated-clones__1', 'street-generated-stencil__1' or 'street-generated-pedestrians__1'

tools.name: detachClone
tools.description: Detach one generated clone (a vehicle, tree, prop, stencil or pedestrian placed by a street-generated-clones, street-generated-stencil or street-generated-pedestrians component on a managed street segment) from its generator so it becomes a plain entity that can be moved, rotated, duplicated or deleted on its own; the rest of the segment stays generated. Name the clone by the segment entity, the generator component on it and the clone slot index (0-based creation order from the start of the segment; a slot already detached has no clone, and the generator's skip array lists the detached placements as 'x z' keys), or omit all three to detach the currently selected clone. Optional position/rotation place the detached entity.

segmentId.description: ID of the street-segment entity carrying the generator

component.description: Generator component name on that segment, e.g. 'street-generated-clones__1', 'street-generated-stencil__1' or 'street-generated-pedestrians__1'

slotIndex.description: 0-based slot of the clone in the generator creation order along the segment

position.description: Optional "x y z" segment-local position for the detached entity (default: where the clone is)

rotation.description: Optional "x y z" rotation in degrees for the detached entity (default: the clone rotation)

tools.name: entityClone
tools.description: Clone an entity (including its children) and insert the copy as its next sibling. Returns with the clone selected; read getSelectedEntity for the new id.

entityId.description: The ID of the entity to clone

tools.name: entityCreate
tools.description: Create a new entity in the A-Frame scene with specified components and transforms

mixin.description: The mixin id value for the new entity (e.g., "box-truck-rig")

position.description: Position as space-separated x y z values (e.g., "0 1.5 -3") default 0 0 0

rotation.description: Rotation as space-separated x y z values in degrees (e.g., "0 45 0") default 0 0 0

scale.description: Scale as space-separated x y z values (e.g., "2 2 2") default 1 1 1

tools.name: entityRemove
tools.description: Remove an entity from the scene. Undoable via the undo tool.

entityId.description: The ID of the entity to remove

tools.name: entityUpdate
tools.description: Update an entity in the A-Frame scene with new properties or components

entityId.description: The ID of the entity to update

component.description: The component to update (e.g., position, rotation, mixin)

property.description: The property to update within the component (optional)

value.description: The new value to set

expressionForValue.description: Mathematical expression to evaluate for the value (e.g., "5 - 2"). Use this instead of value when calculation is needed.

tools.name: updateSceneTitle
tools.description: Update the scene title in the global state

value.description: The new scene title

tools.name: managedStreetCreate
tools.description: Create a new managed street from a cross-section (array of segments, listed from one edge to the other). If the scene has geographic context (setLatLon / Google 3D Tiles), the tiles already supply the surroundings: do NOT add boundary segments, buildings or other land-use models unless the user explicitly asks for synthetic surroundings — the cross-section should normally begin and end with sidewalks. For each segment, omit surface/color/elevation/direction/generated to receive the type's preset — the same content a user gets by picking that type in the sidebar (e.g. bike-lane → green asphalt, bike-arrow stencils, cyclists; bus-lane → BUS ONLY stencil, buses; sidewalk → pedestrians). Call listSegmentPresets to see them. Only supply `generated` to override a preset. Returns entityId, width, presetsApplied, warnings and a readBack of what actually mounted.

length.description: Length of the street in meters (default: 60)

position.description: Position as space-separated x y z values (e.g., "0 0 0")

segments.description: Array of segment definitions for the street

items.description: Segment definition

type.description: Type of segment. Valid values: "drive-lane", "bike-lane", "sidewalk", "parking-lane", "divider", "grass", "rail", "bus-lane", "boundary". "boundary" is SYNTHETIC flanking land use (buildings, waterfront, fences) for scenes without geographic context — it renders outside the travelled way at the street edge and auto-tiles models edge-to-edge (`variant` + `side`, no `generated` needed). Do not add boundaries when the scene has a location: the Google 3D Tiles already show the real surroundings and synthetic buildings would overlap them.

surface.description: Surface material (e.g., "asphalt", "concrete", "grass", "sidewalk", "gravel", "sand", "planting-strip", "none", "solid"). Optional for building segments — the variant supplies a sensible default. For hatched dividers use `generated.striping` with `striping: "hatched"` instead of a surface.

elevation.description: Vertical offset in meters (0 = road level, 0.15 = curb/sidewalk height). Negative values are not supported.

direction.description: Traffic direction ("none", "inbound", "outbound")

variant.description: Variant preset for `type: "boundary"` segments. Valid values: "brownstone" (urban mixed-use SM3D blocks), "suburban" (detached single-family houses), "arcade" (arched street-front buildings), "water" (seawall), "grass" (fenced grass strip), "parking" (fenced parking lot), "sp-mixeduse" (StreetPlan mixed-use), "sp-residential" (StreetPlan single-family/townhouse), "sp-big-box" (StreetPlan big-box stores), "custom" (preserve existing settings). Setting variant on a boundary segment auto-fits the model array; do NOT pass `generated.clones` for boundaries unless you want full control. Only meaningful when `type: "boundary"`, and only for scenes without geographic context (see `type`).

side.description: Side of the street the segment sits on. Required for `type: "boundary"` (controls placement outside the travelled way edge and which direction the models face). Valid values: "left", "right". Frame of reference is the street's own cross-section, not the camera: "left" is the inbound side and "right" the outbound side (right-hand-drive convention; swap for left-hand-drive countries). segments[0] sits at the first edge; getGeoContext reports the compass bearing of each edge.

generated.description: Optional generated content — omit to receive the type preset. Two different systems: `clones` places 3D models (vehicles, cyclists, trees, lamps, furniture — any listMixins id with generator "clones"); `stencil` paints flat road markings (arrows, sharrows, words like BUS ONLY — only ids with generator "stencil"). Never put a vehicle in `stencil` or a marking in `clones`.

mode.description: Clone mode ("random", "fixed", "single")

modelsArray.description: Comma-separated 3D model ids from listMixins (generator "clones"), e.g. "sedan-rig, box-truck-rig" or "bus". Unknown ids are rejected.

count.description: Number of models (for random mode)

modelsArray.description: Comma-separated painted-marking ids (generator "stencil"), e.g. "bike-arrow", "sharrow", "word-bus, word-only". Unknown ids are rejected — use listMixins.

direction.description: Stencil orientation

side.description: Side of segment ("left", "right")

tools.name: takeSnapshot
tools.description: Render a snapshot of the scene and return it as a JPEG image (max 1280 px wide) plus `metadata.camera` (tilt, isTopDown, isNorthUp, screenUpBearingDeg, lat/lon). To VERIFY placement or alignment use type "plan": top-down, north-up, whole scene — the only view with absolute orientation. One plan snapshot beats several angled ones; do not take multiple perspective shots to check position. In a geospatial scene "plan" is the default when type is omitted.

caption.description: Optional caption to display with the snapshot

focusEntityId.description: Optional entity ID to focus on before taking the snapshot

type.description: View to render. "plan": top-down, north-up, whole scene — use this to judge orientation and alignment (default in geospatial scenes). "focus": current view, or framed on focusEntityId (default otherwise). "birdseye", "straightOn", "closeup": presentation shots of the first managed street — not orientation references; use them only when the user asks for a picture, not to verify.

zoomOut.description: Plan view only: altitude multiplier applied after the top-down fit. 1 = street fills the frame; 2 (default in geospatial scenes) shows about twice the ground extent so the real roads around the street are visible; use 3-4 for a wider context check. The result reports `metadata.groundExtent` (visible metres across the viewport).

tools.name: setLatLon
tools.description: Set the latitude and longitude for the scene, which triggers elevation lookup and activates the Google 3D Tiles map layer. Signed-in users can set any location; signed-out sessions are limited to locations within California (demo).

tools.name: getScene
tools.description: Return the full 3DStreet scene as Format-1 JSON (the same data the Save button writes), plus the currently selected entity id and scene id.

tools.name: getEntity
tools.description: Return one entity serialized as Format-1 JSON.

entityId.description: The DOM id of the entity to read

tools.name: getSelectedEntity
tools.description: Return the entity the user has selected in the scene graph (or null).

tools.name: selectEntity
tools.description: Programmatically select an entity (mirrors clicking it in the scene graph). Pass an empty entityId to clear selection.

entityId.description: The DOM id to select; pass empty string to clear selection.

tools.name: listMixins
tools.description: List available A-Frame mixins (model assets) grouped by category. Optional category arg filters to one category.

category.description: Optional category label to filter by

tools.name: listSegmentPresets
tools.description: List the per-type segment presets (surface, color, elevation, default direction, and the generated stencils/clones/pedestrians) that managedStreetCreate and managedStreetUpdate apply when a segment omits those fields — identical to picking the type in the editor sidebar. Read this before composing a cross-section so you only override what you need.

tools.name: getSessionInfo
tools.description: Return the running build version, signed-in user, current scene id/url/title, whether edits are being persisted (`saved`: cloud scene exists and the user is its author, so autosave is on — otherwise call saveScene), and viewport size.

tools.name: getManagedStreet
tools.description: Return one managed-street entity as Format-2 segment-list JSON (reverse of the parser, reads live DOM so it includes per-segment edits).

entityId.description: The DOM id of a managed-street entity

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Step the editor history back by one command.

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Step the editor history forward by one command.

tools.name: getGeoContext
tools.description: Return the exact relationship between scene coordinates and geographic coordinates: the lat/lon at the scene origin, the compass bearing of the scene axes, the camera pose (tilt, north-up state, lat/lon), and optionally one entity converted to lat/lon + compass heading (for a managed street: centerline bearing and both endpoint coordinates), and/or a lat/lon converted to a scene world position. Conversions use the live Google 3D Tiles WGS84 frame, so they match where the map renders. Errors with a reason when the geo layer is off or still loading — call setLatLon or retry.

entityId.description: Optional entity to describe geographically (position → lat/lon, heading → compass bearing; managed streets also get endpoint coordinates).

latitude.description: Optional latitude to convert to a scene world position (pair with longitude).

longitude.description: Optional longitude to convert to a scene world position (pair with latitude).

tools.name: orientPlanView
tools.description: Move the editor camera to a top-down, north-up plan view using the same compass action a user clicks (perspective camera, framing the whole scene), optionally pulled back by `zoomOut`. Returns the resulting camera state (tilt, needle angle, isTopDown, isNorthUp, lat/lon, groundExtent in metres). Use before takeSnapshot when judging alignment or orientation; focusCamera reframes around one entity and is NOT a reliable orientation reference. takeSnapshot type "plan" does this for you.

zoomOut.description: Altitude multiplier after the fit: 1 = scene fills the frame, 2 = twice the ground extent (see surrounding real roads), 3-4 = wide context.

tools.name: focusCamera
tools.description: Frame an entity in the viewport (same effect as double-clicking it in the scene graph). This reframes and rotates the view around that entity, so the result is NOT a north-up or alignment reference — use orientPlanView + takeSnapshot for that.

entityId.description: The DOM id to focus on

tools.name: saveScene
tools.description: Persist the current scene to the signed-in user's cloud account. Edits are NOT saved until this is called once; afterwards autosave persists every further edit in this tab. Returns sceneId and sceneUrl — always give the user the sceneUrl (or remember the sceneId) so the work can be reopened in a later session with loadScene. Signed out: opens the sign-in modal and errors; ask the user to sign in, then retry. If the open scene belongs to someone else, saves a copy.

title.description: Optional scene title to set before saving (e.g. "Geary Blvd BRT").

tools.name: loadScene
tools.description: Replace the current scene with a saved cloud scene by id — the way to resume earlier work (e.g. when the user says "resume my scene" and you remember its sceneId, or from a sceneUrl). Unsaved edits in the current scene are discarded, so saveScene first if they matter.

sceneId.description: Scene UUID, or a 3DStreet URL containing /scenes/<uuid>.

tools.name: get_current_page_context
tools.description: Read the page the user is currently viewing in Ramp: path, title, context_version, functional_client_tools, and any capabilities currently registered by that page. Use this again after navigation or after a table/form tool reports that its target is unavailable. Leave kinds and ids blank to get all registered page capabilities.

kinds.description: Only return page capabilities with one of these kinds. Leave blank to get all registered page capabilities.

ids.description: Only return page capabilities with one of these ids. Leave blank to get all registered page capabilities.

tools.name: list_page_tables
tools.description: List the data tables mounted on the page the user is viewing, with their table keys, labels, and row counts. isVisible: false means the table is not currently rendered (on a hidden tab or collapsed section) — reading or changing it is refused until the user brings it into view, so ask them to switch to it first. isOperable: false means the table is read-only (no toolbar): read_table_rows still works, but filter/sort/group/column tools are refused. Use a returned tableKey with the other table tools. If a call returns table_missing, table_hidden, or table_read_only, follow recovery_guidance and the live available_tables snapshot rather than repeating discovery or the failed call. Never substitute another dataset without user confirmation. Rebuild a call at most once after the target becomes available; if it fails again, explain the blocker.

tools.name: get_table_state
tools.description: Get the current state of a visible table: active filters, sort, grouping, column order/visibility, plus the valid sort keys, group-by fields, and columns for this table. Call this before changing table config. Only works on operable tables (isOperable: true from list_page_tables); read-only tables have no config to inspect — use read_table_rows for their data. If a call returns table_missing, table_hidden, or table_read_only, follow recovery_guidance and the live available_tables snapshot rather than repeating discovery or the failed call. Never substitute another dataset without user confirmation. Rebuild a call at most once after the target becomes available; if it fails again, explain the blocker.

table_key.description: The tableKey of a currently visible table. Available table keys are included in the message context and from list_page_tables.

tools.name: read_table_rows
tools.description: Read the rows currently displayed on the table page (current page only, visible columns only, values formatted the way the user sees them). Use this to answer questions about the data the user is looking at. Works on any visible table, including read-only (isOperable: false) tables with no toolbar. The only optional row-count field is "max_rows" (1-50); never send limit, offset, count, page_size, cursor, or pagination aliases. Results are capped; check "truncated". If a call returns table_missing, table_hidden, or table_read_only, follow recovery_guidance and the live available_tables snapshot rather than repeating discovery or the failed call. Never substitute another dataset without user confirmation. Rebuild a call at most once after the target becomes available; if it fails again, explain the blocker.

table_key.description: The tableKey of a currently visible table. Available table keys are included in the message context and from list_page_tables.

max_rows.description: Maximum rows to return (default and cap: 50).

tools.name: set_table_filter
tools.description: Apply one filter to a visible, operable table. First call list_table_filters for this exact table_key and use its category_key and valueHint. For a listbox with searchable options, then call list_table_filter_options and pass returned labels in "values"; do not use value, filter_value, or option IDs. The parameters depend on the category's "kind": listbox → "values" (add "exclude" only where supported). date_range → "start_date"/"end_date" (YYYY-MM-DD, either alone for open-ended) or "last_period". amount_form (e.g. Amount) → "min" and/or "max" as plain numbers in major currency units: "over $3k" = min 3000, "under $500" = max 500. free_text → "text". currency → "text" with the currency code. If a call returns table_missing, table_hidden, or table_read_only, follow recovery_guidance and the live available_tables snapshot rather than repeating discovery or the failed call. Never substitute another dataset without user confirmation. Rebuild a call at most once after the target becomes available; if it fails again, explain the blocker.

table_key.description: The tableKey of a currently visible table. Available table keys are included in the message context and from list_page_tables.

text.description: Value for free_text or currency categories.

min.description: Minimum amount for amount_form categories, in major currency units (e.g. 3000 for $3,000). Omit for no minimum.

max.description: Maximum amount for amount_form categories, in major currency units. Omit for no maximum.

exclude.description: Invert the filter to exclude the given values (listbox categories that support it).

tools.name: get_form_schema
tools.description: Read the schema of a form open on the user's screen: fields with labels, kinds, current values, validation errors, and selectable options (option tokens). A form is open ONLY when it is listed as a `form` surface in the current page context (the page_capabilities hint sent with the message, or get_current_page_context). If no `form` surface is listed, no form is open — there is nothing to read, so do not call this. Call it before filling a listed form. Omit form_id only for initial discovery when exactly one form is open and no intended form_id is already known. Keep using the intended form_id after failures; never omit or replace it to recover from a closed-form error.

form_id.description: The open form to target, from get_current_page_context form capabilities. Optional only for initial discovery when exactly one form is open and no intended form_id is already known. Values must match the field kind from get_form_schema; select fields take an option token and multiselect fields take an array of option tokens. Returns validation errors so you can self-correct. Changed fields are highlighted for the user and can be undone. Never claim to submit the form — ask the user to review the highlighted fields and submit.

form_id.description: The open form to target, from get_current_page_context form capabilities. Optional only for initial discovery when exactly one form is open and no intended form_id is already known. Keep using the intended form_id once known; never omit or replace it to recover from a closed-form error.

values.description: Map of field name (from get_form_schema) to new value. Use option tokens for select fields and arrays of option tokens for multiselect fields.

tools.name: search_field_options
tools.description: Search the selectable options of a select or multiselect field on a form listed as a `form` surface in the current page context. Use this to resolve a real option token when the inline options in get_form_schema were truncated or did not match. When has_more_options is true, refine the query until the intended option is returned.

form_id.description: The open form to target, from get_current_page_context form capabilities. Optional only for initial discovery when exactly one form is open and no intended form_id is already known. Keep using the intended form_id once known; never omit or replace it to recover from a closed-form error.

query.description: Search text to match option labels.

tools.name: get_skill_editor_state
tools.description: Read the live state of the skill editor open on the user's screen: editor kind, name, description, read-only reference material, and the full document as markdown, including unsaved edits. Call this before editing so you work with the user's current draft rather than the last saved version.

tools.name: set_skill_editor_fields
tools.description: Edit the skill editor open on the user's screen. Sets the name (when is_skill_name_editable), description, and/or replaces the document body markdown in the live editor WITHOUT saving. Content replaces require the editor_revision from a fresh get_skill_editor_state read and are rejected if the user edited in between. Never claim to have saved — ask the user to review the editor and save.

skill_name.description: New name for the skill or agent being edited. Only accepted when get_skill_editor_state reports is_skill_name_editable, and expected whenever it reports a skill_name_hint. For editor_kind ask_ramp_skill this is only settable while creating a new skill and must be lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens as separators; for editor_kind procurement_agent it is the free-text agent title.

content_markdown.description: Replacement markdown for the full document body. Replaces the entire live document, so include unchanged parts. Do not open it with the skill or agent name as an H1: the name is a separate field set with skill_name, and a leading H1 is moved into that field. Requires expected_editor_revision.

expected_editor_revision.description: The editor_revision returned by get_skill_editor_state that this update was computed from. Required with content_markdown; the update is rejected if the user has edited the draft since that read.

tools.name: get_procurement_report_editor
tools.description: Read the procurement report open in the fullscreen editor, including unsaved changes, section stable IDs, and editor_revision. Read before editing. The execution_id comes from the procurement_agent_report_editor page capability. This is the report, not the agent instructions or request fields.

tools.name: edit_procurement_report
tools.description: Edit sections of the live procurement report draft WITHOUT saving. Requires execution_id and expected_editor_revision from get_procurement_report_editor. Apply at most 20 edits per call; read again before each additional batch. Update only the requested sections; omitted header/body fields and all other sections are preserved. Preserve source citations and links. Put section headings in header, not body_markdown. Insert after a stable ID, or at the start with after_stable_id=null. Remove deletes only that section. Edits apply atomically and fail if the user changed the draft since your read. Read again after a conflict. Never claim changes are saved; the user reviews the editor and clicks Save.

tools.name: get_spend_program_editor_state
tools.description: Read the live state of the spend program editor open on the user's screen: program shape, every settings section in the shape set_spend_program_settings accepts, the names and available choices behind referenced ids (policies, merchant categories, accounting coding), approval and change request workflow pointers, custom request form questions (intake) and change order form questions (change_request_intake, purchase order programs only) with their ids, and editor_revision. Includes unsaved edits. Call this before the first write and again after a revision conflict.

tools.name: prepare_spend_program_workflow_edit
tools.description: Save current questions as a draft before using them in Blank Canvas workflow conditions. Requires expected_editor_revision from a fresh get_spend_program_editor_state read. Use form="request" for approval workflows and form="change_request" for dedicated change request workflows. Change request preparation saves the request form first. Await success, then pass the returned template_id and custom_form_collection_log_entry_uuid to GetBlankCanvasConditionFields and ApplyBlankCanvasWorkflowEdits. The template_id is resolved after preparation; use it instead of earlier editor or autosave pointers. Prepare again after question edits; discard cached condition fields when the returned revision changes. On failure, reread the editor and prepare again rather than falling back to published questions. Does not save or publish the program or edit the workflow.

expected_editor_revision.description: The editor_revision returned by get_spend_program_editor_state that this update was computed from. The update is rejected if the editor changed since that read.

tools.name: set_spend_program_settings
tools.description: Edit settings of the spend program editor open on the user's screen WITHOUT saving. Send one or more complete sections as read from get_spend_program_editor_state with your changes applied; fields left out keep their current value. Requires the editor_revision from a fresh read and is rejected if the editor changed since. Returns applied fields, fields that could not be applied for this program shape, and the form's validation errors so you can self-correct. Never claim to have saved.

tools.name: set_spend_program_intake_questions
tools.description: Create, name, rename, or remove request form sections and add, update, or remove custom questions in the spend program editor open on the user's screen WITHOUT saving. Requesting programs only. form selects the target: request (default) edits the request form and takes ids from intake.sections; change_request edits the change order form requesters fill in when changing an approved request and takes ids from change_request_intake.sections, which only purchase order programs have. Read the target form from get_spend_program_editor_state first: it lists every question with its id, and built-in fields you must not duplicate. Section operations are only supported for form=request. add_section names the sole untitled section if present, preserving its questions, or appends a new section. update_section names or renames an existing section by section_id while preserving its id, questions, and conditions. remove_section deletes the section and all its questions and clears dependent visibility or required-when rules, including change order rules. A section containing a protected question cannot be removed. Removing the last section leaves a fresh empty untitled section. Create sections first, then use created_section_ids from the result as section_id when adding questions. If the request form uses sections, every section must have a meaningful, nonblank title and at least one question before saving or publishing. When organizing a form into sections, use update_section to name any existing unnamed sections. A sole section with title=null is the default unsectioned form and may remain unnamed and empty, including after removing the last section. Leave new question descriptions blank unless the user explicitly requests them; do not repeat the question title. Only add question types listed in that form's available_question_types; other types are rejected for this program. Select choices carry ids: when replacing a question's choices, pass { id, label } for every choice you keep or rename so visibility rules that depend on it keep working, and a bare string only for new choices. Operations apply in order; a visibility rule may only reference an earlier BOOLEAN or select question by id, so add controlling questions first and use the ids this tool returns. Requires the editor_revision from a fresh read. Returns the merged questions with ids and the form's validation errors. Never claim to have saved.

form.description: Which form to edit. request: the request form (ids from intake.sections). change_request: the change order form requesters fill in when changing an approved request (ids from change_request_intake.sections); only purchase order programs have one.

operations.description: Applied in order. Create sections first, then use their returned ids to add questions. Add a controlling question in one call and reference its returned id before adding dependent questions.

title.description: Section heading for the request form only. Names the sole untitled section if one exists, preserving its questions; otherwise appends a new section. Use the returned created_section_ids to add questions in a subsequent call. Every section needs at least one question before saving or publishing.

title.description: Name or rename a request form section, preserving its id, questions, and conditions.

section_id.description: Section id from intake.sections. Removes the request form section and all its questions. Rejected if any contained question cannot be deleted. Rules depending on deleted questions are cleared, including change order rules. Removing the last section leaves a fresh empty untitled section.

description.description: Helper text under the question. Leave blank unless the user explicitly requests it; do not repeat the title.

choices.description: Choice labels, in order. Only for TEXT_SINGLE_SELECT and TEXT_MULTI_SELECT.

is_one_of.description: For a select controlling question: show when the answer is one of these choice labels.

position.description: Zero-based index within the section. Defaults to the end.

question_id.description: id from the target form (intake.sections or change_request_intake.sections) in get_spend_program_editor_state.

choices.description: Replacement choices, in order. Existing choices left out are removed; removal is rejected when another question's or section's rule depends on the choice. The type cannot change.

id.description: Choice id from the target form (intake.sections or change_request_intake.sections) in get_spend_program_editor_state. Ids change when the user saves, so read them from the same editor_revision you write against.

visible_when.description: Replace the visibility rule; null always shows the question.

equals.description: For a BOOLEAN controlling question: show when the answer equals this value.

Requires the editor_revision from a fresh get_spend_program_editor_state read and is rejected if the editor changed since. Applies to the live editor WITHOUT saving.

draft_template_id.description: For custom: draft template id of that workflow when it has unsaved draft edits. Omitting it leaves the current draft pointer unchanged when workflow_id matches the workflow already selected; when workflow_id selects a different workflow, omitting it points at that workflow with no draft.
