tools.name: add_criterion
tools.description: Propose adding one criterion to the cohort. The user sees a confirmation card and accepts or rejects.

operator.description: Measurement value operator (only for Measurement domain)

value.description: Threshold value (only for Measurement domain)

tools.name: add_criteria
tools.description: Propose adding multiple criteria to the cohort with AND/OR logic. ALWAYS provide a `name` describing the rule (e.g. "On metformin or sulfonylurea", "Excludes pregnancy"); never omit it. Prefer add_inclusion_rule when cardinality or temporal constraints are needed.

name.description: Short, human-readable label for this group (REQUIRED). E.g. 'Confirmatory T2DM treatment', 'Exclude Type 1 DM'.

operator.description: Measurement value operator (only for Measurement domain)

value.description: Threshold value (only for Measurement domain)

tools.name: add_qualifying_criterion
tools.description: Restrict the ENTRY EVENT itself rather than the person — the editor's "Restrict initial events". Use when the qualifying event must coincide with something, e.g. an inpatient visit, a diagnosis recorded on the same admission. Distinct from add_criterion, which qualifies the person over a window.

isExcluded.description: Optional exclusion flag for concept-set items

tools.name: set_censor_window
tools.description: Bound the study period with fixed dates (YYYY-MM-DD): nobody is followed before startDate or after endDate, whatever their observation. Use when the user names a study window ('2015 to 2019') — without it the cohort spans the whole database and the counts answer a different question.

tools.name: set_era_collapse
tools.description: Gap in days below which two stretches of cohort membership are merged into one era (the editor's era collapse). Default 0 — a person who leaves and re-enters counts as two episodes. Raise it when brief gaps should not split a person's follow-up.

gapDays.description: Merge stretches separated by fewer than this many days.

tools.name: set_event_limits
tools.description: Choose which qualifying events count, per person. 'first' is the new-user / first-diagnosis design — one row per person at their earliest qualifying event; 'all' (the default) puts a person in the cohort once per qualifying event, so counts mean episodes rather than people. Set this deliberately whenever the design is about new users or incident disease; phenotype_patterns reports what accepted definitions of the condition use.

entryEvents.description: Which entry events qualify a person ('Cohort entry on' in the editor).

qualifyingEvents.description: Which qualifying events the inclusion rules apply to ('Apply rules to').

inclusionRuleEvents.description: Which events remain after the inclusion rules are applied.

tools.name: add_demographic_criterion
tools.description: Restrict the cohort by age or sex — the criteria that have no concept set. Use for "adults", "age 18 and over", "women aged 40 to 70": pass minAge / maxAge in years and/or sex. Without this a cohort NAMED for adults contains children, because nothing in the definition says otherwise. Added as an inclusion rule, which is where CIRCE keeps demographic criteria.

minAge.description: Lowest age in years, inclusive. 18 for adults.

sex.description: Restrict to one sex. Omit for any.

name.description: Rule name shown in the editor. Defaults to a label like "Age 18+".

tools.name: use_concept_set
tools.description: Use an EXISTING saved concept set in the cohort being built, by its id from search_existing_concept_sets. Prefer this over rebuilding the same set concept by concept: it reuses the definition the user already curated, and stays in step with it. The host reads the saved set's concepts and adds the criterion. Use group 'entry' for a qualifying event, 'inclusion' to require it, 'exclusion' to require its absence.

conceptSetId.description: Id of the saved concept set (from search_existing_concept_sets).

group.description: Where the criterion goes. Defaults to 'inclusion'.

name.description: Rule name to show in the editor. Defaults to the concept set name.

tools.name: remove_inclusion_rule
tools.description: Remove an inclusion rule from the cohort being edited, by its name (as shown in the editor) or its id. Use this when the user asks to drop, delete or undo a rule you added — do not rebuild the cohort to get rid of one rule.

name.description: Exact rule name as it appears in the cohort.

id.description: Rule id, if you have it.

tools.name: remove_entry_event
tools.description: Remove one entry event from the cohort being edited, identified by the concept it was built from. Use when the cohort qualifies on several entry events and the user wants one dropped. To replace the entry event entirely, call set_entry_event instead.

conceptId.description: Concept id of the entry event to remove.

conceptName.description: Concept name, if the id is not to hand.

tools.name: set_entry_event
tools.description: Set the cohort's primary qualifying entry event. Replaces any existing entry event.

isExcluded.description: Optional exclusion flag for concept-set items

tools.name: set_observation_window
tools.description: Set the prior + post observation window (in days) around the entry event. priorDays = days of continuous observation required BEFORE entry; postDays = days of continuous observation required AFTER entry.

tools.name: add_exit_criterion
tools.description: Define how a patient exits the cohort. Strategy: end_of_observation = end of continuous observation period; fixed_duration = N days after entry; continuous_drug = persistence-window-driven exit.

offset.description: Days offset (for fixed_duration and continuous_drug)

persistenceWindow.description: Gap days between exposures for continuous_drug

surveillanceWindow.description: Trailing days after final exposure for continuous_drug

isExcluded.description: Optional exclusion flag for concept-set items

concept.description: Drug concept whose exposure eras define the exit (for continuous_drug)

tools.name: set_censor_event
tools.description: Add a censoring criterion that ends a patient's time-at-risk when the event occurs.

isExcluded.description: Optional exclusion flag for concept-set items

tools.name: create_standalone_concept_set
tools.description: Create a NEW reusable concept set on the server via WebAPI, saved globally and usable across cohorts. This is NOT the default: criteria capabilities (set_entry_event, add_criterion, add_criteria, add_inclusion_rule) already build the concept set they need inside the cohort definition, which is what most phenotypes want. Reach for this only when the set is meant to be reused — the user asked for a standalone concept set, or the same set is needed by several cohorts or analyses. The host persists it, then attaches it to the open cohort if there is one, otherwise navigates to the concept-set editor. Use a clinical, descriptive name (e.g. 'Statins', 'Inhaled corticosteroids', 'Type 2 Diabetes diagnoses').

name.description: Concept set name (REQUIRED). Clinical and descriptive.

isExcluded.description: Optional exclusion flag for concept-set items

tools.name: navigate_to
tools.description: Suggest moving the user to a different view in ATLAS. The user sees a 5s undo toast after the navigation is applied (no approval card). Always include a one-sentence `reason` so the toast is self-explanatory. Each `view` accepts a specific set of params — see the route manifest.

view.description: Route name from the Atlas3 route manifest (resources/routes.manifest.json — generated by Atlas3/scripts/emit-route-manifest.mjs). Edit the manifest to add a new view.

reason.description: One short sentence; surfaced in the undo toast.

tools.name: add_inclusion_rule
tools.description: Add an inclusion rule: a named group of criteria with AND/OR logic and optional cardinality (AT_LEAST/AT_MOST count) or temporal window. Prefer this over add_criteria when the model needs cardinality or temporal constraints.

count.description: Required for AT_LEAST and AT_MOST

temporalWindow.description: Optional temporal window for the criteria, relative to the index (cohort entry) start date.

startDays.description: Window start in days vs index start: negative = before index, 0 = at index, null = all time prior.

endDays.description: Window end in days vs index start: positive = after index, null = all time after. Default 0 (index date).

operator.description: Measurement value operator (only for Measurement domain)

value.description: Threshold value (only for Measurement domain)

tools.name: create_feature_analysis
tools.description: Persist a NEW feature analysis (covariate definition) on the server. The user sees an approval card; on accept, ATLAS navigates to the editor. `type` controls the design shape: PRESET (built-in OHDSI preset id as a string), CRITERIA_SET (JSON object with conceptSets + criteria), or CUSTOM_FE (raw SQL string). Pass `design` accordingly.

type.description: PRESET for built-in feature library entries; CRITERIA_SET for custom criteria sets; CUSTOM_FE for raw SQL.

design.description: Type-dependent: string for PRESET/CUSTOM_FE; object for CRITERIA_SET.

tools.name: create_characterization
tools.description: Persist a NEW cohort characterization on the server. REQUIRES at least one cohort and at least one feature analysis attached. Before calling this you MUST have called search_existing_cohorts and search_existing_feature_analyses to find the IDs. cohorts.description: REQUIRED. One or more cohorts to characterize. Each item is {id, name} pulled from search_existing_cohorts results.

featureAnalyses.description: REQUIRED. One or more feature analyses to apply. Each item is {id, name} pulled from search_existing_feature_analyses results.

allowRepeats.description: Whether the same event can repeat in a pathway (default false)

tools.name: generate_analysis

Use after the analysis exists (create_pathway / create_characterization / create_incidence_rate returned an id). Results appear in the editor when the job finishes. Omit sourceKey to use the source the user is currently working against.

analysisType.description: Which kind of analysis to run. REQUIRED.

isExcluded.description: Optional exclusion flag for concept-set items

items.description: Full replace — overwrites the existing items array.

isExcluded.description: Optional exclusion flag for concept-set items

itemsToAdd.description: Append-only — skips items whose conceptId already exists.

tools.name: update_feature_analysis
tools.description: Apply a partial edit to an existing feature analysis: rename, change description, change type/domain/statType, or replace the design payload. Mutates the open editor; user clicks Save to persist.

design.description: Type-dependent: string for PRESET/CUSTOM_FE; object for CRITERIA_SET. Replaces the existing design entirely.

tools.name: update_characterization

tools.name: update_pathway

tools.name: get_space
tools.description: Inspect the active space: apps, actors, backend, and exposed_types. Types with expose: true live on the account space and every app here shares those records — use that for data two apps both need (clients, organisations). App-only types do not appear here. Example: get_space({}).

tools.name: get_spec
tools.description: Return the live spec, including generated default views, forms, and pages, and types the space exposes (those have expose: true — shared across apps). App-local types omit expose. Use get_space for the space-level exposed_types list. Use export_spec for the portable authored spec (defaults omitted).

tools.name: get_widgets
tools.description: Discover page widgets and their configuration contract. Call without widget to list or search widgets. Pass a widget key for its inputs. Also pass view for exact compatible field options before calling upsert_page.

view.description: Optional View key used to resolve compatible field inputs

query.description: Optional text search when listing widgets

category.description: Optional category filter when listing widgets

tools.name: get_automation_primitives
tools.description: Discover the canonical structured-workflow grammar, registered conditions and effects, and this runtime's capability profile. Call with a condition or effect key for its parameter contract before authoring a workflow.

tools.name: export_spec
tools.description: Export the portable authored spec as YAML or JSON. Generated default views, forms, and pages are omitted; they are recreated from types on import. Use get_spec to inspect the live spec including defaults.

tools.name: query_view
tools.description: Run a named view and return its rows. Views can filter, sort, limit, and derive live grouped measures — list_records returns every source record (list_<type> in typed mode). Discover view keys via get_spec. Example: query_view({ view: "active_projects" }).

expose.description: Runtime values for the view's expose filters, e.g. { status: "active" }

record_id.description: Current record id when the view filters on $record.id

tools.name: apply_spec
tools.description: Replace the entire active app spec with a YAML or JSON document. Not a merge: types, views, forms, workflows, and pages missing from the document are deleted. Generated defaults are recreated from types. Requires confirm: true. A document with no types is refused unless wipe: true — { key: "foo" } is not a full spec. Example: apply_spec({ spec: "<full yaml or json>", confirm: true }).

spec.description: Full YAML or JSON document for the app spec

confirm.description: Must be true. apply_spec replaces the entire spec.

wipe.description: Required with confirm if the document has no types and the app already has some.

tools.name: upsert_type
tools.description: Create or update a type and its fields. Use a singular key and label for one record; optional collection_label overrides the automatically pluralized list name. Providing fields replaces the type's field list; omitting fields leaves existing fields unchanged. Field type is canonical; compatible format, presentation, validation, and conditional behavior are optional. lifecycle turns one enum field into a validated state machine. Add or change one field with upsert_field. expose: true stores the type on the account space so every app shares its records. Example: upsert_type({ key: "task", fields: [{ key: "status", type: "enum", values: ["draft", "done"] }], lifecycle: { field: "status", initial: "draft", terminal: ["done"], transitions: [{ key: "complete", from: ["draft"], to: "done" }] } }).

collection_label.description: Optional plural label for lists and navigation. Omit it to infer an English plural from label; pass an empty string to clear an existing override.

expose.description: If true, the type lives on the account space and all apps share its records. If false or omitted, the type belongs only to this app.

anyOf.description: Optional state machine attached to one enum field

field.description: Enum field containing the current state

initial.description: State assigned to every new record

lifecycle.description: State machine definition, or null to remove the existing lifecycle

fields.description: Fields to create with the type. Array of field objects, or a map of field key → field (or shorthand type string).

target.description: Referenced type key (reference fields)

anyOf.description: Shorthand field type, e.g. text

target.description: Referenced type key (reference fields)

tools.name: rename_type
tools.description: Rename a technical type key while preserving its stable identity, records, and direct spec references. Explicit view, form, page, and workflow keys remain unchanged.

tools.name: upsert_field
tools.description: Add or update one field without replacing the type's other fields. type identifies the record type; kind is the field kind. Formats, presentations, and validation must be compatible with that kind. Enum fields need values, reference fields need target, currency fields need currency, and rating fields use max from 2 to 10. Example: upsert_field({ type: "submission", key: "stage", kind: "enum", values: ["submitted", "winner", "rejected"], presentation: "badge", value_semantics: { submitted: "neutral", winner: "success", rejected: "danger" } }).

kind.description: Field kind

target.description: Referenced type key (reference fields)

tools.name: rename_field
tools.description: Rename a field key while keeping its identity and stored values.

tools.name: delete_field
tools.description: Remove a field from a type and drop its SQLite column.

tools.name: upsert_view
tools.description: Create or update a named view (a stored query: filter, sort, limit, columns, or live grouped measures). For a normal view, include fields in the order people should see them, such as fields: ["name", "status", "client.name"]. If fields is omitted while creating a normal view, builder.run chooses up to six useful source fields automatically; an empty fields array is invalid. Omitting fields while updating preserves the existing selection. For a grouped view, omit fields to derive them from group_by and measure aliases. group_by accepts one source field. measures supports count, sum, avg, min, and max; avg accepts field or fields. Sort aggregate aliases with order_by. Run it with query_view. Example: upsert_view({ key: "scores", source: "review", group_by: "submission", measures: { review_count: { op: "count" }, overall_score: { op: "avg", fields: ["quality", "impact"] } }, order_by: { overall_score: "desc" } }).

fields.description: Ordered visible columns for a normal view. Reference labels may use paths such as client.name. Omit on creation to infer useful defaults; omit on update to preserve existing columns; omit for grouped views to derive aggregate columns.

measures.description: Named live aggregates for a grouped view

tools.name: upsert_form
tools.description: Create or update a record-backed or standalone form. Record forms use type plus ordered field keys. Standalone forms own reusable field definitions under inputs and emit form.submitted with {form, values}. submit.success optionally customizes the standalone confirmation; workflow behavior belongs in a workflow listening for form.submitted. Example: upsert_form({ key: "contact_us", mode: "standalone", inputs: { name: { type: "text", required: true }, email: { type: "text", format: "email" } }, submit: { success: { title: "Thanks" } } }).

inputs.description: Named field definitions for a standalone form.

target.description: Referenced type key (reference fields)

tools.name: upsert_workflow
tools.description: Create or update a structured workflow. Call get_automation_primitives first. Use registered effects and {$ref:"vars.name"} bindings. Gates contain pass/fail steps; loops and parallel branches contain their own steps. expose: ["agent"] registers invoke_<key>. Example: upsert_workflow({ key: "mark_paid", expose: ["agent"], input: { invoice: { record: "invoice" } }, steps: [{ effect: { key: "records.set", params: { record: {$ref:"vars.invoice"}, values: {status:"paid"} } } }] }).

input.description: Named inputs. Each value is {record:"type_key"} or {value:"text|number|boolean|date|object|array"}.

trigger.description: Optional {key, config?}. Omit for a callable workflow.

steps.description: Canonical nested steps returned by get_automation_primitives.

tools.name: upsert_page
tools.description: Create or update a page of grids and widgets. Call get_widgets first to discover widget keys, required values, and compatible fields. Widget values are validated against that contract. Optional folder groups it in the app menu. Optional icon is one of: page, dashboard, table, chart, line, donut, board, calendar, list, inbox, people, money, time. If icon is omitted when creating a page, a one-time default is inferred from its widgets; later edits do not change it. A group nests children in a blocks array even when there is only one widget. columns is how many widgets sit side by side; unused columns stay empty. Example: upsert_page({ key: "board", icon: "board", path: "/board", blocks: [{ kind: "group", columns: 1, blocks: [{ kind: "widget", widget: "table", values: { view: "active_projects" } }] }] }).

blocks.description: Page layout. A group nests children in a blocks array — always an array, even for one widget.

columns.description: Widgets side by side in this group (1–4). Unused cells stay empty.

tools.name: create_app
tools.description: Create an app in the active space and switch to it. The new app can use types the space already exposes (see get_space.exposed_types) — do not recreate those types in the app. Example: create_app({ name: "Invoicing" }).

tools.name: delete_app
tools.description: Delete an app created from this account space. Shared records stay.

tools.name: switch_app
tools.description: Switch the active app by id. Space-exposed types stay available; app-local types change with the app.

tools.name: create_space
tools.description: Create a new account space with its own apps. After switching to it, upsert_type({ expose: true }) creates types every app in this space shares — e.g. a customer type used by both a CRM and invoicing. Example: create_space({ name: "Studio" }).

tools.name: list_samples
tools.description: List gallery sample applications that can be loaded as an app.

tools.name: list_records
tools.description: List every record of one type, unfiltered. Use query_view when you need filtering, sorting, limits, or aggregates.

type.description: Type key from get_spec or describe_type

tools.name: get_record

type.description: Type key from get_spec or describe_type

tools.name: create_record
tools.description: Create a record of one type. Call describe_type first for fields and constraints; lifecycle state and audit fields are system-managed.

type.description: Type key from get_spec or describe_type

values.description: Field values accepted by the selected type. Use describe_type for the contract.

tools.description: Update fields on one record. Call describe_type first; use transition_record for lifecycle state changes.

type.description: Type key from get_spec or describe_type

values.description: Field values accepted by the selected type. Use describe_type for the contract.

type.description: Type key from get_spec or describe_type

tools.name: transition_record
tools.description: Apply a named lifecycle transition to a record. Use describe_type with the record id to discover transitions currently available.

type.description: Type key from get_spec or describe_type

tools.name: ui_list
tools.description: List the agent-operable UI elements on the page. Call it first: it gives each element's id, state, and the tools that act on it — pass that id as target, except an action_<id> tool, which names its element. Pass target to list an element's children — the recovery when one reports childrenOmitted. A cut listing, or any you window with offset or limit, reports window — walk by advancing offset by window.returned. A listed state is current; ui_read gives detail the digest omits.

target.description: An element id: given, the tool lists that element's children instead of the whole page. Use it on an element that reports childrenOmitted.

offset.description: Index of the first element to return. Defaults to 0.

limit.description: How many elements to return. Defaults to as many as fit.

tools.name: ui_read
tools.description: Read the current semantic state of one UI element by id; use ui_list first for valid ids. Actions already return the element's post-change state, so this is for detail an action result windowed away and for elements you did not just act on. Pass offset or limit and the reply always reports window — field, offset, returned, true total — so returned equal to total means that is every entry the element holds. The budget windows a long list unasked. Walk by advancing offset by window.returned.

target.description: The id of the UI element to act on, as returned by ui_list.

offset.description: Index of the first entry to return from this element's largest list. Defaults to 0.

limit.description: How many entries of that list to return. Defaults to as many as fit; the output budget may clamp it, and window.returned reports what actually returned.

tools.name: button_press
tools.description: Press a button, exactly as a person clicking it would. The button's own name — the text a person reads on it, like "Send Invitation" — is its label in ui_list. Pressing may submit a form, open a dialog, navigate, or trigger whatever the button is wired to. The result carries the element's full state after the change, so a follow-up ui_read on the same element is unnecessary; when the result reports window, walk the rest with ui_read by advancing offset by window.returned.

target.description: The id of the UI element to act on, as returned by ui_list.

tools.name: dialog_open
tools.description: Open a dialog element. The result carries the element's full state after the change, so a follow-up ui_read on the same element is unnecessary; when the result reports window, walk the rest with ui_read by advancing offset by window.returned.

target.description: The id of the UI element to act on, as returned by ui_list.

tools.name: dialog_close
tools.description: Close a dialog element. The result carries the element's full state after the change, so a follow-up ui_read on the same element is unnecessary; when the result reports window, walk the rest with ui_read by advancing offset by window.returned.

target.description: The id of the UI element to act on, as returned by ui_list.

tools.name: ui_fill
tools.description: Fill several elements in one call — a form's fields, say. values maps an element id to its new value: a string for an input, select or tabs, a boolean for a checkbox, an array for a multi-select. Fillable kinds: tabs, select, multi-select, checkbox, input, slider, date. Each value travels through that element's own action, so the page reacts as it does to that tool. Every id is checked first, so one bad id changes nothing. Submitting is a separate press.

values.description: An object mapping element ids to their new values. Call ui_list for valid ids and kinds.

tools.name: tabs_select
tools.description: Switch the active tab of a tabs element to the given value. The result carries the element's full state after the change, so a follow-up ui_read on the same element is unnecessary; when the result reports window, walk the rest with ui_read by advancing offset by window.returned.

target.description: The id of the UI element to act on, as returned by ui_list.

value.description: The tab value to activate. Call ui_read on the target to see available values.

tools.name: select_choose
tools.description: Choose a value on a select or combobox element. The result carries the element's full state after the change, so a follow-up ui_read on the same element is unnecessary; when the result reports window, walk the rest with ui_read by advancing offset by window.returned.

target.description: The id of the UI element to act on, as returned by ui_list.

value.description: The value to choose. Call ui_read on the target to see available values.

tools.name: select_clear
tools.description: Clear the selection on a select or combobox element. The result carries the element's full state after the change, so a follow-up ui_read on the same element is unnecessary; when the result reports window, walk the rest with ui_read by advancing offset by window.returned.

target.description: The id of the UI element to act on, as returned by ui_list.

tools.name: multi_select_set
tools.description: Set the selected values of a multi-select element, replacing the previous selection. The result carries the element's full state after the change, so a follow-up ui_read on the same element is unnecessary; when the result reports window, walk the rest with ui_read by advancing offset by window.returned.

target.description: The id of the UI element to act on, as returned by ui_list.

values.description: The values to select, replacing any previous selection. Pass an empty array to clear the selection. Call ui_read on the target to see available options.

tools.name: checkbox_set
tools.description: Set the checked state of a checkbox or switch. The result carries the element's full state after the change, so a follow-up ui_read on the same element is unnecessary; when the result reports window, walk the rest with ui_read by advancing offset by window.returned.

target.description: The id of the UI element to act on, as returned by ui_list.

checked.description: Whether the checkbox should be checked.

tools.name: disclosure_open
tools.description: Open a collapsible or popover element. The result carries the element's full state after the change, so a follow-up ui_read on the same element is unnecessary; when the result reports window, walk the rest with ui_read by advancing offset by window.returned.

tools.name: check_ai_crawler_access
tools.description: Return a read-only RFC 9309 robots.txt access report for AI and search crawlers. Accepts robots.txt text or a public robots.txt URL plus an optional path. Includes merged matching groups, octet-normalized longest-match decisions, per-crawler evidence, transport status, crawler-registry provenance and policy snippets.

content.description: Pasted robots.txt content to validate locally, e.g. 'User-agent: GPTBot'.

crawlers.description: Crawler tokens to evaluate as an array, e.g. ['GPTBot','Google-Extended'].

path.description: Path to evaluate against robots.txt rules, e.g. '/' or '/tools/'.

url.description: Robots.txt URL or bare domain to fetch, e.g. 'https://example.com/robots.txt'.

tools.name: validate_llms_txt
tools.description: Validate the required initial H1, optional summary and project details, and any H2 resource lists with link titles, URLs, optional descriptions, findings, and source-line evidence.

content.description: Pasted llms.txt Markdown content to validate locally, e.g. '# Example'.

detail.description: Optional response size: 'compact' (default) returns findings, counts, section summaries and bounded link evidence; 'full' also returns the raw llms.txt source and the complete per-section and per-link document model, e.g. 'full'.

url.description: llms.txt URL or bare domain to fetch, e.g. 'https://example.com/llms.txt'.

tools.name: validate_a2a_agent_card
tools.description: Return a read-only version-aware A2A Agent Card validation report. Includes v0.2, v0.3 and v1.0 structure plus discovery-path evidence without claiming endpoint, authentication or signature conformance.

json.description: Pasted Agent Card JSON to validate locally, e.g. '{"name":"Agent"}'.

url.description: Agent Card URL or bare domain to fetch, e.g. 'https://example.com/.well-known/agent-card.json'.

tools.name: validate_webmcp_tool
tools.description: Return a read-only WebMCP report for pasted or fetched source. Includes declarative and imperative static-source evidence separately from caller-provided runtime observation; pasted JavaScript is never executed and active runtime tools are never inferred from source alone.

detail.description: Optional response size: 'compact' (default) returns findings, counts and static-source evidence; 'full' also returns the complete fetched page text in metadata.text, e.g. 'full'.

source.description: Pasted HTML or JavaScript source to validate locally, e.g. 'data-tool-name=demo'.

url.description: Public page URL to fetch for WebMCP validation, e.g. 'https://example.com/'.

tools.name: check_mx_records
tools.description: Return a read-only MX routing report for a mail domain. Accepts a domain name. Includes exchanger hosts, preferences, Null MX, CNAME risk, address resolution and actionable mail-routing warnings.

domain.description: Mail domain to check via DNS MX lookup, e.g. 'example.com'.

tools.name: check_email_auth_records
tools.description: Return a read-only SPF, DMARC and DKIM report for a mail domain. Accepts a domain plus optional pasted TXT values. Includes syntax, policy strength, alignment, DNS evidence and record-specific warnings.

dkim_record.description: Pasted DKIM TXT value, e.g. 'v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=...'.

dmarc_record.description: Pasted DMARC TXT record, e.g. 'v=DMARC1; p=reject'.

selector.description: DKIM selector to query, e.g. 's1' or 'default'.

spf_record.description: Pasted SPF TXT record, e.g. 'v=spf1 redirect=spf.example.com'.

tools.name: analyze_email_headers
tools.description: Return a read-only email message header report. Accepts pasted RFC 5322 headers. Includes raw Received order, recorded Authentication-Results and caller-configured authserv-id trust; it does not perform cryptographic authentication or reverse-DNS verification.

headers.description: Full email headers to analyze, e.g. 'Authentication-Results: ...'.

trusted_authserv_ids.description: Optional authserv-id values explicitly trusted by the caller; without them, Authentication-Results remain unverified recorded claims.

tools.name: validate_arc_chain
tools.description: Return a read-only ARC structural validation report. Accepts pasted ARC-Seal, ARC-Message-Signature and ARC-Authentication-Results fields. Includes structural completeness, instance continuity and recorded cv state; cryptographic validation and sealer trust are not evaluated.

headers.description: Message headers containing ARC fields, e.g. 'ARC-Seal: i=1; ...'.

tools.name: check_bimi_record
tools.description: Return a read-only BIMI readiness report for a mail domain. Accepts a domain, selector and optional BIMI, DMARC, logo or certificate evidence. Includes TXT syntax, DMARC dependency, asset URL findings and a conservative BIMI draft.

dmarc.description: Pasted DMARC TXT record for BIMI policy review, e.g. 'v=DMARC1; p=reject'.

evidence_url.description: BIMI VMC or evidence URL to inspect, e.g. 'https://example.com/vmc.pem'.

logo_url.description: BIMI SVG logo URL to inspect, e.g. 'https://example.com/logo.svg'.

record.description: Pasted BIMI TXT record, e.g. 'v=BIMI1; l=https://example.com/logo.svg'.

selector.description: BIMI selector to query, e.g. 'default'.

tools.name: check_mta_sts_policy
tools.description: Return a read-only MTA-STS deployment report for a mail domain. Accepts a domain plus optional TXT, policy, MX and TLS-RPT evidence. Includes mode, max-age, syntax, id consistency, MX coverage, conformance findings and remediation warnings.

domain.description: Mail domain for MTA-STS checks, e.g. 'example.com'.

mode.description: Generated MTA-STS policy mode: 'testing', 'enforce', or 'none', e.g. 'testing'.

mx_hosts.description: Known MX hostnames, one per line, e.g. 'mail.example.com'.

policy.description: Pasted MTA-STS policy text, e.g. 'version: STSv1'.

tls_rpt.description: Pasted TLS-RPT TXT value, e.g. 'v=TLSRPTv1; rua=mailto:tls@example.com'.

tools.name: check_tls_rpt_policy
tools.description: Return a read-only SMTP TLS Reporting report for a mail domain. Accepts a domain plus optional TLS-RPT TXT or RUA values. Includes version syntax, reporting destinations, external-provider use, conformance findings and remediation warnings.

domain.description: Mail domain for TLS-RPT checks, e.g. 'example.com'.

tools.name: check_smtp_tls_readiness
tools.description: Return a read-only SMTP TLS delivery readiness report for a mail domain. Accepts a domain and optional MTA-STS, TLS-RPT, DANE and FCrDNS checks. Includes MX, STARTTLS, certificate, policy-alignment and downgrade-risk findings.

check_dane.description: Include DANE/TLSA checks; pass true or false, e.g. true.

check_fcrdns.description: Include forward-confirmed reverse DNS checks; pass true or false, e.g. true.

check_mta_sts.description: Include MTA-STS checks; pass true or false, e.g. true.

check_tls_rpt.description: Include TLS-RPT checks; pass true or false, e.g. true.

domain.description: Mail domain for SMTP TLS readiness checks, e.g. 'example.com'.

tools.name: validate_dnssec_records
tools.description: Return a read-only DNSSEC evidence report for a domain. Accepts a domain plus optional DS, DNSKEY, RRSIG and resolver-status data. Includes chain readiness, algorithms, missing records, validation findings and warnings.

dnskey_records.description: DNSKEY records for the zone, one per line, e.g. '257 3 13 <key>'.

ds_records.description: DS records for the domain, one per line, e.g. '12345 13 2 <digest>'.

rrsig_records.description: RRSIG records for validation context, one per line, e.g. 'example.com. RRSIG ...'.

status.description: Resolver validation status: '', 'secure', or 'bogus', e.g. 'secure'.

tools.name: generate_tlsa_record
tools.description: Return a read-only DANE TLSA record report. Accepts host, port, protocol, usage, selector, matching type and optional certificate data. Includes owner name, digest, generated TLSA data and DNS comparison findings.

file.description: Certificate file content to parse, e.g. PEM text from a .crt file.

host.description: TLS service host for TLSA generation, e.g. 'mail.example.com'.

pem.description: Certificate PEM, DER base64, or hex input, e.g. '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----'.

port.description: TLS service port number, e.g. '25' or '443'.

selector.description: TLSA selector: 0=full certificate or 1=SPKI, e.g. '1'.

tools.name: validate_dane_records
tools.description: Return a read-only DANE service validation report. Accepts service host, port, protocol, TLSA records, DNSSEC status and optional certificate evidence. Includes owner names, TLSA syntax, DNSSEC dependency and certificate-match findings.

host.description: DANE service host to validate, e.g. 'mail.example.com'.

mode.description: DANE validation mode: 'smtp' or 'tls', e.g. 'smtp'.

port.description: DANE service port number, e.g. '25' or '443'.

tlsa_records.description: TLSA records to validate, one per line, e.g. '3 1 1 <sha256>'.

tools.name: check_caa_records
tools.description: Return a read-only CAA certificate-authority policy report for a domain. Accepts a domain plus optional CAA records and issuer details. Includes issue, issuewild, iodef, ACME parameters, policy gaps and record-generation guidance.

ca.description: CA domain for generated CAA records, e.g. 'letsencrypt.org'.

domain.description: CAA domain to check, e.g. 'example.com' (no scheme).

issuemail.description: CAA issuemail issuer-domain value from RFC 9495, optionally followed by issuer parameters, e.g. 'letsencrypt.org; validationmethods=dns-01'.

records.description: CAA records to inspect, one per line, e.g. '0 issue letsencrypt.org'.

tools.name: check_dns_records
tools.description: Return a read-only DNS lookup report for a public DNS name. Accepts a name and record type, an overview of common record types, the RFC 10023 _for-sale check, pasted _for-sale TXT records or _for-sale generator content. Includes RCODE, flags, alias chain, TTLs, raw and readable answers, resolver provenance, resolver-reported DNSSEC AD and RFC 10023 findings. Raw records only; MX routing, SPF/DMARC/DKIM, CAA, DNSSEC, DANE, HTTPS/SVCB and delegation analysis use the specialized admintoolkit tools.

for_sale_content.description: Content for the RFC 10023 generator, one tag-value pair per line, e.g. 'fval=EUR500' or 'furi=https://example.com/sale'; an empty line produces a version-only record.

for_sale_records.description: Optional pasted TXT RDATA for local RFC 10023 validation, one record per line, e.g. '"v=FORSALE1;fval=EUR500"'; when present no DNS query is sent.

for_sale_ttl.description: TTL in seconds for generated _for-sale records; RFC 10023 recommends 3600 or less (default 3600).

mode.description: 'records' for one type, 'overview' for the common types, 'for-sale' for the RFC 10023 check or validation, 'for-sale-generate' to draft RFC 10023 records.

name.description: DNS name to look up, e.g. 'example.com' or '_dmarc.example.com' (no scheme); an IP address is converted to its PTR name.

type.description: DNS record type, e.g. 'A', 'MX', 'TXT' or 'HTTPS'; ignored in overview and _for-sale modes.

tools.name: check_https_svcb_records
tools.description: Return a read-only RFC 9460 HTTPS/SVCB service binding report for a host or pasted records. Accepts a host with optional port, record type and scheme for a live lookup, pasted records, or generator parameters. Includes AliasMode/ServiceMode resolution, SvcParam syntax and self-consistency, ALPN, port, address hints versus A/AAAA, ECH configuration, generated records and an explicit statement that endpoint connectivity was not tested.

alpn.description: Generator alpn SvcParam as a comma-separated list, e.g. 'h3,h2'.

ech.description: Generator ech SvcParam: a Base64 ECHConfigList (RFC 9848).

host.description: Origin host or URL, e.g. 'example.com' or 'https://example.com:8443/'; private and special-use names are rejected.

ipv4hint.description: Generator ipv4hint SvcParam as a comma-separated list of IPv4 addresses.

ipv6hint.description: Generator ipv6hint SvcParam as a comma-separated list of IPv6 addresses.

mode.description: 'lookup' (default with host), 'validate' (default with records) or 'generate'.

no_default_alpn.description: Generator: set the no-default-alpn SvcParam (requires alpn).

params.description: Generator SvcParams in presentation form, e.g. 'alpn=h3,h2 ipv4hint=192.0.2.1'.

port.description: Optional origin port, e.g. '8443'; HTTPS uses port prefix naming for ports other than 443.

priority.description: Generator SvcPriority: '0' for AliasMode, '1' or higher for ServiceMode.

records.description: Optional pasted records in zone-file form, e.g. 'example.com. 3600 IN HTTPS 1 . alpn=h3,h2'; validated locally without DNS queries.

scheme.description: URI scheme for SVCB query names, e.g. 'dns' for _dns (RFC 9461); not used for HTTPS.

svc_port.description: Generator port SvcParam, e.g. '8443'; omit to use the authority port.

target.description: Generator TargetName, '.' or a DNS name such as 'svc.example.net'.

tools.name: check_dns_delegation
tools.description: Return a read-only DNS delegation and authoritative name server report for a domain. Accepts a domain. Includes the parent referral NS set and glue, required-glue findings, direct authoritative SOA and NS answers per name server address, SOA serial and NS set comparison, the DS-to-DNSKEY link and the hosting environment's direct-query capability; recursive discovery is labelled separately.

domain.description: Domain or zone to check, e.g. 'example.com' (no scheme).

tools.name: analyze_http_headers
tools.description: Return a read-only HTTP response-header report for a public endpoint. Accepts pasted headers or a public URL. Includes security, cache, framing, duplicate/conflicting header fields, prioritized findings and remediation notes.

headers.description: Pasted HTTP response headers, e.g. 'Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000'.

url.description: Public URL to fetch for HTTP header analysis, e.g. 'https://example.com/'.

tools.name: decode_ssl_certificate
tools.description: Return a read-only X.509 TLS certificate report. Accepts PEM text or public TLS host details. Includes subject, issuer, SANs, validity, fingerprints, key usage, extensions, hostname and certificate-health findings.

host.description: TLS certificate host to connect to, e.g. 'example.com'.

pem.description: Certificate PEM text to decode, e.g. '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----'.

tools.name: validate_security_txt
tools.description: Return a read-only RFC 9116 security.txt report. Accepts pasted content or a public security.txt URL plus optional contact fields. Includes contact, expiry, canonical, encryption, policy, language fields, findings and draft output.

content.description: Pasted security.txt content, e.g. 'Contact: mailto:security@example.com'.

url.description: Public security.txt URL or bare domain, e.g. 'https://example.com/.well-known/security.txt'.

tools.name: check_tls_configuration
tools.description: Return a read-only public TLS configuration report for a host. Accepts host and port plus optional HSTS evidence. Includes separate exact-version probes, a distinct verified default handshake, SAN identity/trust evidence, negotiated cipher and ALPN evidence, and HTTPS-only HSTS checks; it does not claim cipher or ALPN enumeration.

host.description: Public TLS DNS host or IP literal to check, e.g. 'example.com' or '1.1.1.1' (no scheme; private/reserved targets are rejected).

hsts.description: Optional pasted HSTS header, e.g. 'max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains'.

port.description: TLS port number to check, e.g. '443'.

tools.name: check_redirect_indexability
tools.description: Return a read-only redirect, canonical and indexability report for a public URL. Accepts a URL. Includes bounded per-hop status and SSRF evidence, final URL, HTML and HTTP canonical hints, robots meta and scoped X-Robots-Tag directives, hreflang, separate sitemap reachability and membership, and evidence completeness.

url.description: Public URL to check for redirects and indexability, e.g. 'https://example.com/'.

tools.name: show_public_ip_context
tools.description: Return a read-only same-origin IP context report for the current request. Requires no input. Includes the canonical primary address, directly observed peer, trusted-proxy decision, preserved forwarded-header claims and observed address family; one request path does not prove dual-stack capability and no third-party Geo-IP lookup is performed.

tools.name: calculate_cidr_subnet
tools.description: Return a read-only local IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR report. Accepts a CIDR block plus optional split prefix and address family. Includes exact BigInt-derived boundaries and address counts, RFC 3021 /31 and host-route /32 semantics, no IPv6 broadcast claim, embedded-IPv4 parsing and a capped subnet preview.

target.description: Split target prefix length, e.g. '26' for /26 subnets.

tools.name: decode_edid_data
tools.description: Return a read-only share-safe local EDID capability report. Includes strict hex or local file text decoding, checksum and trust state, a readable timing/VIC/Y420 matrix, CTA audio and speaker topology, qualified HDMI Forum transport, HDR and DisplayID evidence, coverage and byte provenance. WebMCP omits display identifiers, serials, filenames, physical addresses, raw bytes and vendor payload values; it does not infer Atmos, DTS:X, HDMI certification, cable capability or source mode selection.

edid_hex.description: Pasted strict EDID hexadecimal text, e.g. '00ffffffffffff00...'.

file.description: Local EDID file content represented as strict hexadecimal text; binary file selection is available in the visible browser UI.

tools.name: dug_investigate
tools.description: Answer a question that takes more than one lookup, and build the case on the page while you do. You choose the commands and the order: this is your plan, not a preset. Each screen is left on the page, in sequence, under the question that produced it, so the person watching ends up with the evidence, not your summary of it. Prefer this over calling the single-command tools yourself whenever the person has described a symptom instead of naming a lookup, and whenever one answer won’t settle it. Steps use the same grammar as the other tools: a command name, {target} where the domain goes, and an optional second argument; each step runs once per target, in order. For example "why is mail from this domain going to spam" with steps ["MAIL {target}","SPF {target}","DIG {target} MX","RDAP {target}"], or "has my dns change taken effect" with steps ["PROP {target}","TTL {target}","NS {target}","DNSSEC {target}"]. A step naming a command that doesn’t exist is skipped and reported back to you; the rest still run.

question.description: The question being answered, in the words the person would use. It becomes the heading the evidence is filed under. Not a restatement of the commands.

targets.description: The domains or hosts under investigation, bare names, one entry when there is one. The steps run against each in this order.

steps.description: The commands to run, in order, each a full command line such as "MAIL {target}" or "DIG {target} MX". Three to five is usually right: enough to be conclusive, few enough to read.

tools.name: canix_get_execution_quote
tools.description: Compile one or more unsigned groups (POST /execution/quotes). Algorand shapes return Algorand groups; Morpho shapes (base:morpho:vault:*), Aave shapes (base:aave:v3:*), and Aerodrome shapes (base:aerodrome:v2:*) return unsigned Base calldata. Pass an Algorand userAddress unless the shape is on Base. Omitting a Base address does not change rank, eligibility, price, or access. Pass quotes: [{ shapeKey, input }, ...]. Required input fields vary by shapeKey — call canix_list_execution_shapes and use each shape's requiredInputs (userAddress is always required). Response data is an ExecutableQuote array. Paid flat ~0.10 USDC per request on Algorand or Base (not per item). On failure, error.details includes quoteIndex and shapeKey. Do not guess pool discovery, opt-ins, min-balance, slippage, liquidity limits, or app upgrades — read protocol/docs/execution-shapes/protocol-caveats.md and each shape's docsPath. Haystack Launch compiles here too: mainnet:haystack:v1:launch:token takes an existing ipfs:// or https:// assetUrl, and mainnet:haystack:v1:buy:bonding buys a token still on the curve (direct bonding-asset payment, or a Haystack-router leg). A bonding buy is not canix_swap.

tools.description: Get a stateless multi-router swap quote via POST /swaps/quote. Quotes enabled routers in parallel and returns the best expected net out. Optional router forces one adapter. Pass the response data unchanged into canix_optin / canix_swap.

address.description: Account address.

tools.name: canix_optin
tools.description: Build missing output-asset and application opt-ins via POST /swaps/optin for the winning quote. Free endpoint; pass the quote data object unchanged.

address.description: 58-character account address.
58-character account address.

tools.name: canix_swap
tools.description: Build unsigned swap transactions via paid POST /swaps/transactions (~0.005 USDC) for the winning quote. Omit paymentSignature for x402 preflight, then retry with the same inputs. Canix does not sign or submit.

address.description: 58-character account address.
58-character account address.

paymentSignature.description: Optional PAYMENT-SIGNATURE base64 payload. Omit on first call to receive PAYMENT-REQUIRED metadata.

sessionReceipt.description: Prepaid session receipt (X-Canix-Session). Omit to pay per request with paymentSignature. If this header was sent, Caddy skipped x402; a 402 SESSION_* means drop the header and retry with paymentSignature.

tools.name: canix_create_session
tools.description: Buy a prepaid agent session (POST /sessions, ~0.25 USDC). One x402 payment mints a walletless receipt that unlocks N research calls and M quotes/plans until TTL. Sessions are receipts, not keys. Create/refresh cannot be paid with an existing session.

paymentSignature.description: Optional PAYMENT-SIGNATURE base64 payload. Omit on first call to receive PAYMENT-REQUIRED metadata.

tools.name: canix_refresh_session
tools.description: Refresh a prepaid session (POST /sessions/refresh, ~0.25 USDC). Resets N/M and TTL in place, or mints a new receipt if the previous one is gone. One-shot only.

paymentSignature.description: Optional PAYMENT-SIGNATURE base64 payload. Omit on first call to receive PAYMENT-REQUIRED metadata.

tools.name: canix_get_session
tools.description: Read remaining N/M and expiry for a prepaid session receipt (GET /sessions/{sessionId}). Free. Prefer this over the public indexer /transactions showcase.

tools.name: canix_create_watch
tools.description: Register a paid wallet watch retainer (POST /watch, ~0.25 USDC). Address + thresholds + optional HTTPS webhook. HMAC secret shown once. Canix never stores wallet keys.

address.description: 58-character account address.

paymentSignature.description: Optional PAYMENT-SIGNATURE base64 payload. Omit on first call to receive PAYMENT-REQUIRED metadata.

tools.name: canix_refresh_watch
tools.description: Refresh a paid watch retainer (POST /watch/refresh, ~0.25 USDC). Extends TTL. Optionally rotateSecret. One-shot only.

paymentSignature.description: Optional PAYMENT-SIGNATURE base64 payload. Omit on first call to receive PAYMENT-REQUIRED metadata.

tools.name: canix_get_watch
tools.description: Read a watch receipt and recent threshold firings (GET /watch/{watchId}). Free. Does not return the HMAC secret.

tools.name: canix_rotate_watch_secret
tools.description: Rotate the watch webhook HMAC secret (POST /watch/{watchId}/rotate-secret). Free. Requires the current secret.

canix402.compx.io.blurb: Canix health, Canix get metadata and Canix get discovery.

tools.name: cognistration_get_session_state
tools.description: Read the visible Cognistration tone machine state and current browser controls.

tools.name: cognistration_set_session_controls
tools.description: Set bounded, visible tone-machine controls in the current browser session, such as a gamma direction with a 246 Hz carrier. This does not save an account record.

tools.name: cognistration_adjust_session_control
tools.description: Make a relative live change to one visible tone-machine slider. Map speed up or slow down to rhythm faster or slower, carrier smaller or larger to the shared tone, and quieter or louder to volume. The existing oscillator and gain nodes are updated without pausing playback.

direction.description: Carrier uses smaller/larger; rhythm uses slower/faster; volume uses quieter/louder.

step.description: Optional magnitude. Defaults are 24 Hz carrier, 1 Hz rhythm, or 8 volume points.

tools.name: cognistration_set_session_direction
tools.description: Select a published Delta, Theta, Alpha, Beta, or Gamma direction in the visible machine. This covers direction buttons and presets and keeps any current audio running while the beat and optional controls update.

tools.name: cognistration_nudge_carrier
tools.description: Read the current visible carrier and move it a modest bounded step smaller or larger, returning both the previous and new absolute values.

direction.description: Whether the carrier should move down or up.

tools.name: cognistration_generate_tone
tools.description: Match a short user intention to a public Cognistration tone and apply the resulting controls to the visible machine.

intention.description: What the listener wants to practice next.

tools.name: cognistration_clarify_intention
tools.description: Help the listener choose a simple session direction when their request is too broad to route confidently. This returns choices only and does not change controls or start audio.

intention.description: What the listener has in mind, even if it is incomplete.

tools.name: cognistration_calibrate_tone
tools.description: Adjust the visible machine from a listener response such as too intense, too quiet, too bright, too slow, too flat, or just right. It never starts audio.

tools.name: cognistration_compare_tone_directions
tools.description: Compare a few approved public listening directions for an intention, including practical fit and tradeoffs without making a medical claim.

intention.description: What the listener wants to practice next.

limit.description: Number of directions to compare.

tools.name: cognistration_plan_listening_session
tools.description: Build a bounded arrive, practice, and close plan from an intention. This plans a session without starting audio or saving a record.

intention.description: What the listener wants to practice next.

mode.description: Optional listening mode.

tools.name: cognistration_get_session_cue
tools.description: Get a short journaling, focus, reset, or creative cue to pair with a listening direction. It never reads or stores diary content.

intention.description: Optional listening intention used to choose the cue.

mode.description: Optional cue mode.

tools.name: cognistration_begin_ritual
tools.description: Build and stage an interactive arrive, practice, and close ritual in the visible machine. It applies only the first phase controls; it does not start audio or save a record.

intention.description: What the listener wants to practice next.

mode.description: Optional listening mode.

tools.name: cognistration_advance_ritual
tools.description: Move a staged ritual to arrive, practice, or close and apply that phase’s bounded visible controls. The transition is manual and never starts audio.

tools.name: cognistration_prepare_session_recipe
tools.description: Prepare a portable session recipe containing only a safe intention label, state, carrier, beat, volume, and duration. It never includes diary text, account data, or audio.

intentionLabel.description: A safe direction label, not diary text.

tools.name: cognistration_open_science_guide
tools.description: Reveal the visible click-through Cognistration science guide for the current machine direction. It explains the two-channel signal, FFR, descriptive frequency bands, evidence limits, and safe listening; it never starts audio or saves a user record, and its PDF export is a static technical snapshot without diary content.

toneId.description: Optional ID from the public tone catalog.

tools.name: cognistration_search_tone_packs
tools.description: Public finished tone-pack browsing for relaxation, sleep preparation, journaling, focus, or creative work. Results include metadata and preview tracks without starting audio.

query.description: Optional pack search or intention text.

tools.name: cognistration_preview_tone_pack
tools.description: Start one public tone-pack preview in the current browser after the user or agent explicitly confirms audio should begin. Search for a pack first and use one of its listed tracks.

confirmed.description: Must be true to start pack audio.

tools.name: cognistration_get_policy_info
tools.description: Canonical policy lookup for Cognistration safety, terms, privacy, cookies, AI use, pricing, or account creation, with a source-grounded summary and page link.

tools.name: cognistration_get_account_options
tools.description: Account and access overview for questions about a free trial, account, platform access, or cost. It explains the free public preview and one-time private workspace without collecting credentials or submitting payment.

tools.name: cognistration_begin_preview
tools.description: Start the visible browser audio preview after the user or agent explicitly confirms they want audio to begin.

confirmed.description: Must be true to start browser audio.

tools.name: cognistration_stop_preview
tools.description: Stop local browser audio in the visible machine without changing the selected controls. This is safe to repeat.

tools.name: cognistration_open_fullscreen
tools.description: Request the visible machine in the host’s larger display mode without changing its controls or audio.

tools.name: cognistration_open_account_signup
tools.description: Navigate the current browser to the semantic Cognistration account-creation form. The user must review and submit it.
