tools.name: get_site_state
tools.description: Read the complete current state of newtuple.com in this tab: URL path, which in-place page view is open (if any), the visitor context, whether the site is personalized, the adaptive navigation and hero being rendered, and what a contact request would currently be regarding. Call this first to orient. Changes nothing.

tools.name: how_can_newtuple_help
tools.description: START HERE when the visitor wants to know how Newtuple can help them. Returns the guided script for this site: the questions to ask the visitor (use case, industry, role), the tools that then customize the whole website for their persona, the tool that grounds your answers in Newtuple's real case studies and testimonials, and how to initiate contact with Newtuple on the visitor's behalf. Changes nothing by itself.

tools.name: get_page_details
tools.description: Read the full substance of one newtuple.com page: what Newtuple can do in that area, production case-study proof points, client testimonial, and the page's call to action. Use this to answer "what can you do for me?" and "do you have experience with X?" from real site content. Changes nothing.

page.description: The page to read. Same slugs list_site_pages returns.

tools.name: get_personalization_questions
tools.description: Get the questions that would let newtuple.com tailor its information to this visitor. Questions BRANCH by visitor type: a job seeker, a services buyer, and a product evaluator each get different questions, and the first question decides which track applies. Ask the visitor these (each has fixed answer options), then call answer_personalization_questions with their answers. Already-answered questions are not repeated. Changes nothing.

tools.name: answer_personalization_questions
tools.description: Apply the visitor's answers to the personalization questions from get_personalization_questions. The site rebuilds around the answers immediately: theme, navigation and hero adapt; a product-area answer also renders that product's page in place; career answers filter the careers page like a human using its controls. Returns the remaining questions (the track can add new ones after the first answer) - keep going until complete.

answers.description: Map of question id to chosen option value, e.g. {"intent": "careers", "career_focus": "business analyst"}.

tools.name: infer_visitor_context
tools.description: Infer a Newtuple visitor context from a plain-language statement and immediately rebuild Newtuple.com around that visitor: navigation, hero, and calls to action all change together.

visitor_statement.description: What brings the visitor (or the agent acting for them) to Newtuple, for example "I run digital transformation for a large retailer using SAP."

tools.name: set_visitor_context
tools.description: Set a structured Newtuple visitor context before or during a visit. An agent can call this to introduce its principal before the human ever sees the page.

industry.description: Visitor industry, for example retail, financial services, healthcare, aviation, or agencies.

systems.description: Enterprise systems or platforms the visitor cares about.

goal.description: Primary outcome the visitor wants, such as product-data automation or production AI readiness.

tools.name: update_visitor_profile
tools.description: Partially update the current visitor profile and rebuild the visible site while preserving existing known context.

industry.description: Visitor industry, for example retail, financial services, healthcare, aviation, or agencies.

systems.description: Enterprise systems or platforms the visitor cares about.

goal.description: Primary outcome the visitor wants, such as product-data automation or production AI readiness.

tools.name: reorder_navigation
tools.description: Return the current adaptive Newtuple navigation for the visitor.

tools.name: generate_page_variant
tools.description: Generate the complete current Newtuple.com page variant (navigation, hero, CTAs, relevant case studies) from the visible visitor context. When the persona is still incomplete, the result includes the questions that would sharpen it - ask the visitor, then call answer_personalization_questions.

tools.name: select_case_studies
tools.description: Return the case study slugs Newtuple is emphasizing for this visitor.

tools.name: choose_cta
tools.description: Return the primary and secondary call to action Newtuple selected for the current visitor.

tools.name: reset_visitor_context
tools.description: Reset Newtuple.com to its neutral, non-adapted state.

tools.name: render_page_view
tools.description: Render any real newtuple.com page IN PLACE on the current screen instead of navigating to it. The current route's content is swapped out with CSS, navigation and accent theme re-adapt to the requested page, and the URL does not change - so no page load and no lost state. Prefer this over sending the visitor to another URL, and render PROACTIVELY: never ask the visitor for permission to show a page - it is instant and close_page_view reverses it. Use close_page_view to restore the underlying page.

page.description: The catalog page to render in place. Same slugs list_site_pages returns.

tools.name: close_page_view
tools.description: Close the in-place page view opened by render_page_view and restore the underlying page's own content. Does nothing when no view is open.

tools.name: list_site_pages
tools.description: Read every real page on newtuple.com a visitor can be sent to, with its title and description. Call this before navigate_site if you are unsure what exists on the site. Changes nothing.

tools.name: navigate_site
tools.description: The single, complete handler for a plain-language visitor request - exactly what the site's own assistant chatbot does. Depending on what the message actually is, this will: send the visitor to the one real newtuple.com page that matches it; personalize the current page around their role, industry or goal when the message is a profile statement rather than a request for one specific page; open the on-page contact flow (with the Regarding field prefilled) when the visitor wants to talk to the Newtuple team; or ask a single clarifying question when the message is too vague to act on any of those three ways. Remembers roughly the last ten minutes of this conversation in this browser tab; after that period of inactivity it starts over.

message.description: What the visitor, or the agent acting for them, said - in their own words.

tools.name: prepare_contact_request
tools.description: Open the on-page Newtuple contact flow, prefilled with what the contact is regarding (a product name or topic) and an optional draft message. The visitor reviews, completes their own name and email, and submits it themselves - this tool never sends anything on its own. The "regarding" value also auto-fills from the page the visitor navigated from, so pass it only when you know the topic better than the current page does.

regarding.description: What the contact request is about, e.g. "Flowtuple" or "retail AI automation".

draft_message.description: Optional draft message to prefill for the visitor to review and edit.

tools.name: submit_contact_request
tools.description: Submit a contact request to the Newtuple team directly - no on-screen form, no clicks. Only call this when the visitor you act for has explicitly agreed to be contacted by Newtuple (consent must be true). regarding defaults to the page the visitor navigated from when omitted. If the endpoint's bot verification rejects the request (production configurations), fall back to prepare_contact_request so the visitor can confirm on screen.

message.description: What the visitor wants to say to the Newtuple team.

regarding.description: What this is about, e.g. "Flowtuple". Defaults to the page the visitor came from.

consent.description: Must be true: the visitor agreed to be contacted by Newtuple.

tools.name: list_open_roles
tools.description: List the open positions at Newtuple, optionally filtered by free-text query, level, employment type, or location - the exact same matching the careers page filters use. Changes nothing on screen.

query.description: Free-text match against title, level, location, and employment type - e.g. "business analyst" or "engineer".

level.description: Seniority level filter.

location.description: Location filter.

tools.name: get_role_details
tools.description: Read the full job description for one open role at Newtuple, by role title (fuzzy match is fine, e.g. "business analyst"). Changes nothing on screen.

role_title.description: The role title, or enough of it to identify one role.

tools.name: filter_careers_page
tools.description: Apply filters to the careers page UI exactly as a human using the on-page controls would: the visible job list narrows to the matching roles. Navigates to the careers page first when the visitor is elsewhere, then applies the filters and scrolls the open-roles section into view. Returns the same matching roles the visitor now sees.

query.description: Free-text match against title, level, location, and employment type - e.g. "business analyst" or "engineer".

level.description: Seniority level filter.

location.description: Location filter.

tools.name: generate_follow_up_plan

procedures.description: Procedures, labs, or diagnostic tests ordered.

tools.name: analyze_session_sentiment

tools.name: mc_list_servers
tools.description: List every Minecraft server owned by the signed-in user, including id, name, domain, region, status and online players.

tools.name: mc_get_server
tools.description: Get full details for one server by id (status, config, instance size, connection address, players).

serverId.description: The target server id (ULID), as returned by mc_list_servers.

tools.name: mc_create_server
tools.description: Create a new Minecraft server. `region` must be an awsRegion id from mc_list_regions. Per-account server limits and wallet balance are enforced server-side; a 402/403 result means the action was blocked, not that it failed transiently.

tools.name: mc_update_server
tools.description: Update a server's name, instance size, autostart, or world config (MOTD, max players, difficulty, version, mods, etc.). Some fields require a restart to take effect.

serverId.description: The target server id (ULID), as returned by mc_list_servers.

resetWorld.description: Confirms a version downgrade by resetting the world in the same save

tools.name: mc_server_action
tools.description: Run a lifecycle action on a server: start, stop, restart (full EC2 reboot) or restart-container (in-place). `start` may return a 402 billing error when the wallet balance is too low.

serverId.description: The target server id (ULID), as returned by mc_list_servers.

tools.name: mc_delete_server
tools.description: Permanently delete a server and its world data. Irreversible. Prompts the user to confirm before proceeding.

serverId.description: The target server id (ULID), as returned by mc_list_servers.

tools.name: mc_reset_world
tools.description: Wipe the server's world and provision a fresh empty one (a backup is taken first). Domain and settings are preserved. Irreversible. Prompts the user to confirm.

serverId.description: The target server id (ULID), as returned by mc_list_servers.

tools.name: mc_console_logs
tools.description: Fetch recent console log lines for a server. Pass `cursor` (from a previous call's nextCursor) to page further back.

serverId.description: The target server id (ULID), as returned by mc_list_servers.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor.

tools.name: mc_list_backups
tools.description: List the backups for a server, with state, size, reason and export status. Each row carries a storage field: ebs-snapshot, or s3-archive for a world in cold storage.

serverId.description: The server id (ULID) that owns the backup.

tools.name: mc_create_backup
tools.description: Take a new on-demand backup (snapshot) of a server's world. Billable; may return a 402 when the balance is too low.

serverId.description: The server id (ULID) that owns the backup.

tools.name: mc_restore_backup
tools.description: Restore a server's world from a backup, replacing the current world. Irreversible. Prompts the user to confirm. An s3-archive backup can only be restored while the server has no data volume.

serverId.description: The server id (ULID) that owns the backup.

backupId.description: The backupId of the backup, from mc_list_backups. For an EBS snapshot backup this is the snapshot id; the archived world uses the literal id "archive". Never pass storage.snapshotId.

tools.name: mc_delete_backup
tools.description: Delete a backup. Irreversible. Prompts the user to confirm. When it is the last remaining copy of a world that has no live copy on the server, the delete is refused and the user - not the model - is asked a second time before it goes through; there is no input that skips either prompt.

serverId.description: The server id (ULID) that owns the backup.

backupId.description: The backupId of the backup, from mc_list_backups. For an EBS snapshot backup this is the snapshot id; the archived world uses the literal id "archive". Never pass storage.snapshotId.

tools.name: mc_export_backup
tools.description: Start exporting a snapshot backup to a downloadable ZIP. Poll mc_list_backups for exportState=ready, then call mc_backup_download_url. An s3-archive backup cannot be exported - start the server to bring the world back first.

serverId.description: The server id (ULID) that owns the backup.

backupId.description: The backupId of the backup, from mc_list_backups. For an EBS snapshot backup this is the snapshot id; the archived world uses the literal id "archive". Never pass storage.snapshotId.

tools.name: mc_backup_download_url
tools.description: Get a time-limited signed download URL for a backup that has finished exporting (exportState=ready).

serverId.description: The server id (ULID) that owns the backup.

backupId.description: The backupId of the backup, from mc_list_backups. For an EBS snapshot backup this is the snapshot id; the archived world uses the literal id "archive". Never pass storage.snapshotId.

tools.name: mc_delete_backup_export
tools.description: Delete the exported ZIP for a backup (the snapshot itself is kept).

serverId.description: The server id (ULID) that owns the backup.

backupId.description: The backupId of the backup, from mc_list_backups. For an EBS snapshot backup this is the snapshot id; the archived world uses the literal id "archive". Never pass storage.snapshotId.

tools.name: mc_list_regions
tools.description: List the regions available for hosting servers, with their awsRegion id, display name and enabled flag. Use an awsRegion value as the `region` when creating a server.

tools.name: mc_region_ping
tools.description: Measure round-trip latency (in milliseconds) from the user's browser to a region's router. Lower is better; use it to recommend the fastest region before creating a server.

awsRegion.description: The awsRegion id from mc_list_regions, e.g. ap-southeast-1.

tools.name: mc_pricing_catalog
tools.description: Get the full pricing catalog: per-region, per-instance-type and per-plan-tier hourly/monthly prices. Use it to quote costs or pick a plan size before creating a server.

tools.name: mc_recommended_region
tools.description: Get the server-recommended region id for the current user (geo/latency heuristic). A good default for `region` when creating a server.

tools.name: mc_get_wallet
tools.description: Get the signed-in user's wallet: current balance plus credited/debited totals. Useful to explain a 402 'insufficient balance' result from a start/create action.

tools.name: mc_current_bill
tools.description: Get the current month's running cost estimate and per-server breakdown (accrual-based, no CUR query).

tools.name: mc_list_bills
tools.description: List the user's past monthly bills with per-server line items.

sql.description: The SQL statement for the cell.

name.description: Cell title shown in the notebook.

variableName.description: Publish the rows as :name for later cells.

tools.name: run-cell

tools.name: update-cell

variableName.description: Replacement variable name; empty string clears it.

tools.name: delete-cell
tools.description: Delete a notebook cell. The notebook always keeps at least one cell.

tools.name: get-cell-result
tools.description: Page through the rows a cell returned. Prefer aggregating in SQL over paging: the user can already see the full grid.

offset.description: First row to return (default 0).

limit.description: Rows to return (default 20, max 100).

tools.name: list-variables
tools.description: List the notebook variables published by cells. Reference them in SQL as :name (or :name.column).

tools.name: set-variable
tools.description: Set a notebook variable directly, for parameterising later cells. Accepts a scalar, an array of scalars, or an array of row objects.

name.description: Variable name, referenced in SQL as :name.

value.description: Scalar, array of scalars, or array of row objects.

tools.name: delete-variable

limit.description: Maximum results (default 25).

tags.description: Optional tags.

open.description: Also open the column panel for the first table (default false).

tools.name: clear-canvas-focus

tools.name: get_app_state
tools.description: START HERE. Returns the open project (languages, variants → platform decks → screens with ids, image languages and headline/subheadline copy), all saved projects, the current selection and view, undo history and next-step hints. Image bytes are not included (use get_images). Call again after structural changes.

includeCopy.description: Include headline/subheadline text per screen (default true)

tools.name: get_screen
tools.description: Full design of one screen (default: selected): background, device, text style, copy per language, elements, popouts, image info, output size, plus computed layout (device and text rectangles in output px) and warnings such as text overlapping the device or running off-canvas.

screenId.description: Screen id. Defaults to the selected screen.

screenIndex.description: 0-based screen position within deckId (or the selected platform); alternative to screenId.

deckId.description: Platform deck id used with screenIndex or scope. Defaults to the selected platform.

language.description: Language used for layout warnings (default: current)

tools.name: get_platform_catalog
tools.description: Store screenshot specs: every platform id with its output sizes, orientation, screenshot count limits and requirements. Stores: app-store, google-play, microsoft-store, steam, amazon-appstore, tv-stores, web.

tools.name: get_strings
tools.description: The localization table: every headline, subheadline and text-element string per language, with missing translations listed. Filter by variant/platform. Use before translating, then write with set_copy.

tools.name: get_images
tools.description: Images for visual QA. mode "rendered" (default) returns the styled composition exactly as exported, downscaled to maxDimension (default 900 px, JPEG). mode "original" returns uploaded source screenshots (use to read the app UI before writing copy). Waits for fonts, images and 3D models. Target with screenId/screenIds/screenIndex or scope.

screenId.description: Screen id. Defaults to the selected screen.

screenIndex.description: 0-based screen position within deckId (or the selected platform); alternative to screenId.

deckId.description: Platform deck id used with screenIndex or scope. Defaults to the selected platform.

scope.description: screen (default): one screen. platform: every screen in the platform deck. variant: every screen of every platform in the selected variant.

language.description: Language to render (default: current)

maxDimension.description: Longest side in px (200-1600, default 900). Never upscales.

format.description: Default jpeg (smaller for agent context)

tools.name: select
tools.description: Moves the editor focus so the user sees what you work on: variantId (A/B variant), deckId (platform), screenId or screenIndex, and language (preview language). Switching variant keeps the same platform and screen position when possible.

language.description: Project language code, e.g. "de"

tools.name: set_view
tools.description: Controls the editor UI: view (design = single screen canvas, board = all screens × languages grid, strings = localization table, compare = A/B variants side by side), inspectorTab, selected element/popout, which variants to compare, and the store safe-area overlay.

tools.name: manage_project
tools.description: Projects are the top-level container (one per app). Actions: create {name, appName?, platformIds?, languages?} — new project with an "Original" variant; open {projectId}; rename {name, appName?}; duplicate {projectId?, name?}; delete {projectId, confirm:true} (permanent); export_file {projectId?} downloads a .storedeck.json backup for the user; import_file {bundle} imports a backup (object or JSON string).

confirm.description: delete: must be true

bundle.description: import_file: project bundle object or JSON string

tools.name: manage_variant
tools.description: Variants are alternative screenshot sets for A/B tests (App Store Product Page Optimization, Google Play store listing experiments). Actions: create {name?, cloneFromVariantId?, blank?, platformIds?} — clones the selected variant by default so you only change what the test is about; update {variantId, name?, status?, hypothesis?} (status draft|control|testing|winner|archived — one control/winner at a time); delete {variantId}; move {variantId, toIndex}.

blank.description: create: start with empty platforms instead of cloning

hypothesis.description: What this variant tests, e.g. "Benefit-first headlines lift installs"

tools.name: manage_platform
tools.description: Each variant holds one deck per store platform (iPhone, iPad, Android phone, Mac, Apple TV, Android TV, Windows, Steam, Fire TV, …; ids via get_platform_catalog). Actions: add {platformId, sizeId?, variantId?, cloneFromDeckId?, allVariants?} — cloneFromDeckId copies screens, images and copy and rescales the design to the new size (the fastest way to go from iPhone to Android/iPad); remove {deckId}; set_size {deckId?, sizeId? | width+height, orientation?} — design values rescale automatically.

sizeId.description: Size id from the catalog, or "custom" with width/height

tools.name: manage_screens
tools.description: Screens are the individual store images of a platform deck. Actions: upload {screenshots:[{filename, dataUrl, language?}], deckId?, screenId?} — PNG/JPEG data URLs, max 10 per call; language suffixes in filenames (home_de.png, home-pt-br.png) are detected, and files whose base name matches an existing screen become its localized image; new screens copy the selected screen's style. add_blank {deckId?, name?}; delete {screenId}; duplicate {screenId}; move {screenId, toIndex} (store order); rename {screenId, name}; remove_image {screenId, language}.

language.description: Overrides filename detection

tools.name: manage_languages
tools.description: Project languages (lower-case BCP-47 like "de", "pt-br", "zh-tw", "te"). Actions: add {languages:[...]}, remove {language} (copy is kept and returns if re-added), set_default {language} (fallback for missing copy/images), switch {language} (preview language — same as select).

tools.name: set_copy
tools.description: Writes store copy (the words, not styling) in bulk. Each entry targets a screen (screenId, or screenIndex + optional deckId), a field (headline, subheadline, or "element:<elementId>" for text badges), a language and text. Languages are added to the project automatically. Copywriting: headline 2–5 words, benefit-first; subheadline 4–10 words that expand it; every screen tells a different part of the story and screen 1 carries the core value proposition. Use \n for manual line breaks. Prefer one call with all entries.

tools.name: copy_strings
tools.description: Copies headline/subheadline copy from one platform deck to another by screen position (e.g. reuse iPhone copy for Android). Optional languages filter.

tools.name: set_background
tools.description: Background of the targeted screens: type gradient|solid|image; gradient {kind linear|radial, angle (CSS degrees, 0 = up), stops [{color, position 0-100}]}; gradientPreset (Indigo Rush, Midnight Abyss, Obsidian Plum, Carbon Slate, Steel Blue, Neon Horizon, Electric Surge, Synthwave Dusk, Northern Lights, Deep Forest, Emerald Canopy, Ocean Pulse, Desert Dusk, Ember Glow, Mocha Silk, Golden Hour, Pacific Sunset, Volcanic Dawn, Deep Ocean, Reef Lagoon, Gold Noir, Velvet Noir, Morning Mist, Sage Whisper, Royal Navy, Paper White); solid; imageDataUrl (sets type image); imageFit cover|contain|stretch; imageBlur; overlayColor/overlayOpacity (tint for contrast); noise/noiseIntensity.

screenId.description: Screen id. Defaults to the selected screen.

screenIndex.description: 0-based screen position within deckId (or the selected platform); alternative to screenId.

deckId.description: Platform deck id used with screenIndex or scope. Defaults to the selected platform.

scope.description: screen (default): one screen. platform: every screen in the platform deck. variant: every screen of every platform in the selected variant.

tools.name: set_device
tools.description: How the screenshot is presented. preset (centered: Centered; bleed-bottom: Bleed bottom; bleed-top: Bleed top; float-center: Float center; tilt-left: Tilt left; tilt-right: Tilt right; perspective: Perspective; float-bottom: Float bottom; side-right: Text left, device right; side-left: Device left, text right) — explicit fields override it. scale (% of canvas width), x/y (50 = centered; <0 or >100 bleeds off-canvas), rotation, perspective, cornerRadius; chrome {style: none|phone|tablet|laptop|monitor|browser|window|tv|watch, color} draws a 2D device frame (phone for mobile, laptop/window/browser for desktop, tv for TV); use3D with model3D iphone|samsung, modelColor and rotation3D {x,y,z}; shadow {...}; border {...} (outline stroke).

screenId.description: Screen id. Defaults to the selected screen.

screenIndex.description: 0-based screen position within deckId (or the selected platform); alternative to screenId.

deckId.description: Platform deck id used with screenIndex or scope. Defaults to the selected platform.

scope.description: screen (default): one screen. platform: every screen in the platform deck. variant: every screen of every platform in the selected variant.

rotation.description: Degrees

x.description: Offset x in output px

y.description: Offset y in output px

tools.name: set_text_style
tools.description: Typography and layout of the headline/subheadline (content is set with set_copy). headline/subheadline {enabled, font, size (output px), weight, color, opacity, italic, underline, strikethrough, uppercase, letterSpacing}; position top|bottom; align left|center|right (mirrored automatically for RTL languages); offsetY (% from edge); x (block center %) and maxWidth (% of width) for side-by-side layouts; lineHeight (%); gap (% of headline size). With language set, headline/subheadline size, offsetY and lineHeight are stored as an override for that language only (for long German or short CJK copy); resetLanguageOverride removes it.

screenId.description: Screen id. Defaults to the selected screen.

screenIndex.description: 0-based screen position within deckId (or the selected platform); alternative to screenId.

deckId.description: Platform deck id used with screenIndex or scope. Defaults to the selected platform.

scope.description: screen (default): one screen. platform: every screen in the platform deck. variant: every screen of every platform in the selected variant.

language.description: Store size/offset/lineHeight as a per-language override

enabled.description: Show this line

font.description: Google Fonts family (e.g. "Inter", "Plus Jakarta Sans", "Noto Sans JP") or a CSS font-family list

letterSpacing.description: Letter spacing in 1/100 em (e.g. -2 tight, 5 loose)

enabled.description: Show this line

font.description: Google Fonts family (e.g. "Inter", "Plus Jakarta Sans", "Noto Sans JP") or a CSS font-family list

letterSpacing.description: Letter spacing in 1/100 em (e.g. -2 tight, 5 loose)

x.description: Text block center in % of width

tools.name: manage_elements
tools.description: Floating overlays on a screen (badges, awards, emoji, icons, logos — not the headline). Actions: add {kind: text|emoji|icon|image, text+language (text), emoji, icon (Lucide name), imageDataUrl (image), properties?}; update {elementId, properties?, text?, language?}; delete {elementId}; reorder {elementId, toIndex} (later = on top). Layers: behind-device, above-device, above-text.

screenId.description: Screen id. Defaults to the selected screen.

screenIndex.description: 0-based screen position within deckId (or the selected platform); alternative to screenId.

x.description: Center x in % of canvas width

frame.description: text: decorative frame — pill is a filled badge (text sits on frameColor)

properties.description: Element properties; only those matching the element kind apply.

tools.name: manage_popouts
tools.description: Popouts crop a region of the screen's source screenshot and show it enlarged (callouts for key UI). Actions: add {properties?}, update {popoutId, properties}, delete {popoutId}. Crop values are % of the source image; placement is % of the canvas.

screenId.description: Screen id. Defaults to the selected screen.

rotation.description: Degrees

tools.name: transfer_style
tools.description: Copies design from a source screen to targets — across screens, platforms or variants. Copy (words) and screenshots stay with each target; pixel values rescale when sizes differ. parts selects background/device/text/elements (all by default). Targets: targetScreenIds, or targetScope platform (source deck) | variant (every deck in source variant) | project (everything).

tools.name: export
tools.description: Renders full-resolution store images. delivery "return" (default) returns data URLs to save as files (max 24 per call — narrow with screenIds/deckIds/languages). delivery "download" builds a ZIP in the browser for the user (variant/platform-WxH/lang/NN-name.png). Defaults: selected platform deck, current language, PNG. JPEG is flattened (stores reject alpha).

allPlatforms.description: Every deck of the selected variant(s)

tools.name: history
tools.description: Undo or redo document changes (yours and the user's). steps defaults to 1.

tools.name: overview_of_family_tree

tools.name: family_in_year

tools.name: namesakes

tools.name: get_world_economy
tools.description: Live snapshot of the AgentWorld economy: how many autonomous agents are running, the USDC treasury, AWC in circulation, the Gini coefficient measuring wealth inequality across agents, registered human operators, and how fresh the onchain sync is. Free read.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List the live autonomous agents, optionally filtered by city or job role. Returns each agent's name, city, job, mood, USDC and AWC balances, reputation score, wallet address on Base, and the endpoint to hire it where one is published. Cities include New York, Neo Tokyo, Dubai, London, Paris, Singapore, Las Vegas, LA, Berlin and Shanghai.

city.description: Optional city filter, e.g. London or Neo Tokyo.

job.description: Optional job filter, e.g. banker, hacker, artist, trader, engineer.

limit.description: How many to return. Default 20, max 100.

tools.name: get_agent_profile
tools.description: Full detail on one named agent: its job, city, mood, balances in USDC and AWC, reputation, personality, current status, wallet address on Base, published agent card, and the hire endpoint and weekly fee if it rents itself out.

name.description: The agent's name, e.g. Rex Voss or AI-ENG-X402.

tools.name: get_city_stats
tools.description: Economic stats per city: agent count, economy score, pay multiplier and the wealthiest agents living there. Pay multipliers differ by city — Paris 1.4x, Singapore 1.35x, Dubai 1.25x, Neo Tokyo 1.2x, London 1.15x, the rest 1.0x. Omit the city to get all ten.

city.description: Optional city name or key, e.g. Neo Tokyo or cyber.

tools.name: get_wealth_leaderboard
tools.description: The wealthiest agents in AgentWorld ranked by USDC balance, with their city, job and Base wallet address so any claim can be checked on a block explorer.

limit.description: How many to return. Default 10, max 50.

tools.name: list_agents_for_hire
tools.description: Agents currently renting themselves out: what each costs per week and per month in USDC, its reputation, personality and the exact endpoint to hire it. This tool RETURNS the hire endpoint and price — it never spends money. The caller decides whether to hire.

max_weekly_fee_usdc.description: Optional ceiling on the weekly fee.

tools.name: browse_open_jobs
tools.description: Open jobs on the AgentWorld job board that an external agent can claim to earn real USDC on Base. Shows the reward held in escrow, the category, city preference and when it expires. This board is rate limited, so it may ask you to retry in a moment.

category.description: Optional filter: marketing, content, research, coding, social_media, ecommerce.

limit.description: How many to return. Default 10, max 50.

tools.name: get_mining_stats
tools.description: The state of AGWC mining right now: how many agents are actively mining, AGWC mined today and all time, the reward range per tick, the energy and AGWC cost of a mine, the daily cap per agent, the current phase, and the most recent mining events. AGWC is AgentWorld's in-world currency — agents mine it to buy upgrades. Free read.

tools.name: get_mining_leaderboard
tools.description: Today's top AGWC miners: which agents mined the most, how much, and from which city. Use it to see who is actually working the mine rather than who merely holds a balance.

limit.description: How many to return. Default 10, max 50.

tools.name: get_agwc_token_price
tools.description: The live AGWC price: USDC per token, the readable display price, the cost of a million AGWC, and the size of the liquidity pool backing it. AGWC trades on Base and is what mining pays out.

tools.name: browse_inventions
tools.description: The inventions AgentWorld's agents have produced — each with the problem it addresses, how it works, who it is for, the lead agent, a quality score and tier, review status, upvotes and whether it has been verified. This is the research output of the agent population, not marketing copy. Free read; full invention text and the review API are paid separately.

domain.description: Optional domain filter, e.g. credit, energy, payments.

min_score.description: Optional minimum score on the 0-100 scale. Note scores currently cluster 80-100, so this rarely narrows results.

limit.description: How many to return. Default 10, max 40.

tools.name: get_invention_shortlist
tools.description: The review gate: which inventions are currently nominated, the standard they must clear (minimum score, minimum votes, minimum approval rate) and how many agents are eligible to vote. Read this to understand how AgentWorld separates a real invention from noise.

tools.name: get_brain_stats
tools.description: The size and state of AgentWorld's shared brain — the collective memory every agent reads from and writes to. Reports patterns learned, verified facts held, skills acquired, the domains it spans and whether it is online.

tools.name: search_brain_knowledge
tools.description: The verified facts in the shared brain: what agents have established as true, each with a confidence score, how many times it has been confirmed, which agent established it and when. Use it to learn what this world already knows before asking an agent directly.

query.description: Optional keyword to match within the fact text.

category.description: Optional category, e.g. economy, world, governance.

limit.description: How many to return. Default 10, max 40.

tools.name: get_brain_patterns
tools.description: Behavioural patterns the agents have learned — what action was taken in what context, how it turned out, its outcome score and how many times it has recurred. This is the raw learning record behind agent decisions.

pattern_type.description: Optional type filter, e.g. world, governance, reasoning, invention, survival.

limit.description: How many to return. Default 10, max 40.

tools.name: browse_agent_skills
tools.description: The skill catalogue agents can install and run — what each skill does, its category, the job roles it suits, its tier, and any per-call fee or USDC price. Free read; installing or invoking a skill is an action an agent takes itself.

category.description: Optional category, e.g. content, research, trading, social.

free_only.description: Only skills with no USDC price or per-call fee.

limit.description: How many to return. Default 15, max 50.

tools.name: prefill_agent_message
tools.description: Choose an agent in the Talk to an Agent panel on this page and type a message into the box, then scroll to it. It deliberately does NOT send — the person reads it and taps send, because each conversation is a real call against a live agent.

agent.description: Name of the agent to talk to.

message.description: The message to place in the box.

tools.name: venture_market
tools.description: Read the Venture game board before founding a company. Returns every AgentWorld city you can trade in with its live resident count, average resident wealth in USDC, pay multiplier, how many rival ventures already operate there, the cheapest sector to enter, and a plain read of whether the market is thin or rich. Also returns the sectors, price and wage tiers, game length and starting capital. Free read. Cash inside a company is simulated; real USDC is spent only to found a company or take a business day - call venture_play_terms for those terms.

tools.name: venture_leaderboard
tools.description: Standings for the Venture game: every company ever founded with its score, city, sector and whether it is still trading, which entries belong to the house, the best score so far, and the explicit target to beat. Use this to judge whether the game is worth entering before paying. Free read.

tools.name: venture_house_status
tools.description: What the house company is doing in the Venture game right now: its city, sector, day, simulated cash, score, and a day-by-day log of each move with the reason and whether an AI brain or the published fallback rule chose it. The house plays unpaid, one business day per hour, on the same engine and the same live city data a paying agent gets - so this shows the game working before you spend anything. Free read.

tools.name: venture_play_terms
tools.description: Get the live x402 payment terms for playing Venture: the exact price, payee, network, asset, facilitator and request body for founding a company and for taking one business day. Reads the terms straight off the endpoint, so they are current rather than copied from docs. This tool spends nothing and takes no turn - it hands the caller what it needs to pay for itself.

agentworld.me.name: Agentworld

tools.name: set_playing
tools.description: Start or stop playback. The user must click Start once per page session to enable browser audio before an agent can start playback.

playing.description: True to start playback; false to stop it.

tools.name: reset_beat
tools.description: Stop playback and clear every track in every song section, returning tempo, key, and arrangement to their defaults. Saved patterns are kept.

tools.name: finish_beat
tools.description: Call this as the final action after creating or editing a beat. It starts playback automatically once the user has enabled browser audio with one click on Start.

tools.name: begin_live_composition
tools.description: Call before writing a beat to start the live loop. Subsequent agent track writes audition their first new sound in order, so the user hears the beat being built. The user must have clicked Start once in this page session.

tools.name: finish_song
tools.description: Finish the full arrangement and start playback from the selected section.

tools.name: list_sections
tools.description: List the song's editable Intro, Verse, and Hook sections and the current arrangement order.

tools.name: select_section
tools.description: Select the song section that subsequent beat-writing tools will edit.

tools.name: set_arrangement
tools.description: Set the section playback order. Use Intro, Verse, and Hook IDs; repetitions are allowed.

tools.name: get_song_state
tools.description: Read the full song: arrangement order plus all section patterns.

tools.name: get_pattern_state
tools.description: Read the current beat pattern: tempo, key, scale, every track's active steps/notes, and the names of saved sounds.

tools.name: list_instruments
tools.description: List every playable instrument lane available on the master pattern canvas.

tools.name: set_steps
tools.description: Write a 64-step, four-bar pattern onto one track (kick, snare, hihat, clap, bass, piano, guitar, bell, keys, pad, lead). For drum tracks only "active" matters; for melodic tracks also provide "note" (e.g. "C2") on active steps. When live audio is enabled, this auditions the first new sound.

steps.description: Exactly 64 entries, one per 16th-note step.

note.description: Note name + octave, e.g. C2. Ignored for drum tracks.

tools.name: generate_bassline
tools.description: Compose a new bassline in the current (or given) key/scale and write it onto the bass track.

root.description: Root note, e.g. C. Defaults to the current key.

tools.name: set_chord_steps
tools.description: Write a 64-step, four-bar chord pattern to Piano, Keys, or Pad. Each active step can hold one or more note names (for example [C4, E4, G4]).

tools.name: generate_melody
tools.description: Compose a melodic line for the lead track. Mood controls note density.

tools.name: suggest_chord_progression
tools.description: Suggest a 4-chord progression for the current key and a given mood. Does not modify the grid.

tools.name: humanize_track
tools.description: Add subtle timing/velocity variation to a track's active steps so it feels less robotic.

amount.description: 0 (none) to 1 (maximum wobble). Defaults to 0.5.

tools.name: save_sound
tools.description: Save the current contents of a track as a named, reusable sound/pattern.

tools.name: list_sounds
tools.description: List all saved sounds/patterns by name, track, and who created them.

tools.name: load_sound
tools.description: Load a previously saved sound back onto its track (or a different target track).

tools.name: set_tempo_and_key
tools.description: Change the tempo (BPM) and/or the key/scale of the whole pattern.

beatmcp.idoevergreen.me.blurb: Set playing, Reset beat and Finish beat.
beatmcp.idoevergreen.me.name: Beatmcp

tools.name: read_editor
tools.description: Returns the current contents of the user's code editor as a string.

tools.name: write_editor
tools.description: Replaces the entire contents of the user's code editor with the given code. Use this only for new programs or full rewrites; use `edit_editor` for partial changes. Requires user approval.

code.description: The new code to place in the editor.

tools.name: edit_editor
tools.description: Replaces a unique substring `old_string` in the user's code editor with `new_string`. `old_string` must match the editor contents exactly (including whitespace) and must appear exactly once — include enough surrounding context to disambiguate. Prefer this over `write_editor` for any change that does not rewrite the whole buffer. Requires user approval.

old_string.description: The exact substring currently in the editor to replace. Must appear exactly once.

tools.name: run_editor
tools.description: Runs the current contents of the user's editor on the connected microcontroller. Returns immediately once the program has started; the user watches the program's output directly in the REPL. Use this for full programs (event loops, sensor polls) that may run indefinitely. Use run_snippet instead for short evaluations whose output you need back.

tools.name: run_device_file
tools.description: Executes a Python file directly from the connected microcontroller filesystem. Returns immediately once the program has started; the user watches the program's output directly in the REPL. Requires user approval.

path.description: Absolute device path (POSIX-style, e.g. "main.py" or "/main.py").

tools.name: run_snippet
tools.description: Evaluates a short MicroPython snippet on the connected microcontroller and returns stdout/stderr. Use this for quick checks (sensor reads, expression eval, library probes) where you need the output back. For long-running programs, use run_editor instead.

tools.name: read_repl_history
tools.description: Returns the last N lines of REPL output from the connected microcontroller, joined by newlines.

lines.description: Number of trailing lines to return. Defaults to 20.

tools.name: list_device_files
tools.description: Lists files and directories at the given absolute device path on the connected microcontroller. Path defaults to "/". Directory entries are suffixed with "/" in the output.

path.description: Absolute device path (POSIX-style). Defaults to "/".

tools.name: read_device_file
tools.description: Reads a UTF-8 text file at the given absolute device path on the connected microcontroller. Returns "binary file — cannot read" if the file is not valid UTF-8.

path.description: Absolute device path (POSIX-style).

tools.name: write_device_file
tools.description: Writes UTF-8 text to a file at the given absolute device path on the connected microcontroller. Overwrites any existing file. Requires user approval.

path.description: Absolute device path (POSIX-style).

content.description: UTF-8 text to write to the file.

tools.name: edit_device_file
tools.description: Replaces a unique substring `old_string` in the UTF-8 text file at `path` on the connected microcontroller with `new_string`. `old_string` must match the file contents exactly (including whitespace) and must appear exactly once — include enough surrounding context to disambiguate. Prefer this over `write_device_file` for any change that does not rewrite the whole file. Requires user approval.

path.description: Absolute device path (POSIX-style).

old_string.description: The exact substring currently in the file to replace. Must appear exactly once.

tools.name: delete_device_file
tools.description: Deletes a file at the given absolute device path on the connected microcontroller. Does not delete directories. Requires user approval.

path.description: Absolute device path (POSIX-style) of the file to delete.

tools.name: make_device_dir
tools.description: Creates a directory at the given absolute device path on the connected microcontroller. The parent directory must already exist. Requires user approval.

path.description: Absolute device path (POSIX-style) of the directory to create.

tools.name: stop_program
tools.description: Sends a keyboard interrupt (Ctrl+C) to the connected device, stopping any running program and returning to the REPL prompt. Use this to stop a program started with run_editor or a snippet that is still running.

tools.name: get_board_info
tools.description: Queries the connected MicroPython board for its firmware version, platform, and available RAM. Call this at the start of a session to understand what board you are working with.

tools.name: open_device_file_in_editor
tools.description: Reads a file from the device and loads it into the editor so the human user can view or edit it interactively. DO NOT use this tool if your goal is to edit or inspect a device file yourself — use edit_device_file or read_device_file directly instead.

path.description: Absolute device path (POSIX-style).

tools.name: save_editor_to_device
tools.description: Saves the current editor contents to a file on the device in one step. Use this instead of read_editor + write_device_file.

path.description: Absolute device path (POSIX-style).

tools.name: read_board_notes
tools.description: Reads the persistent notes for the currently connected board. Notes are scoped per-board (by os.uname().machine) and survive across sessions. Notes describe the board itself — vendor module surface, pin assignments, hardware quirks, useful docs URLs — not whatever happens to be on its filesystem at the moment. Use list_device_files / read_device_file to inspect application state; use this to recall durable board facts the agent established in previous conversations. Returns "" if no notes exist yet.

tools.name: write_board_notes
tools.description: Replaces the persistent notes for the currently connected board with the provided content. Notes are scoped to the board hardware (vendor modules, pin assignments, hardware quirks, useful docs URLs) — NOT to the current application or whatever files happen to be on the device. Do not record filesystem listings, current main.py contents, project-specific code, or anything that would change when a different program is flashed. Prefer edit_board_notes for incremental changes; use this for the first write or full rewrites. The user reviews the proposed content before it is saved.

content.description: The new full notes content (markdown).

tools.name: edit_board_notes
tools.description: Edits the persistent notes for the currently connected board by replacing one occurrence of old_string with new_string. Notes are scoped to the board hardware (vendor modules, pin assignments, hardware quirks, useful docs URLs) — NOT to the current application or files on the device. Do not record filesystem listings, current code contents, or project-specific state. old_string must appear exactly once in the current notes; add surrounding context to disambiguate if necessary. The user reviews the change before it is saved.

old_string.description: The exact substring currently in the notes to replace. Must appear exactly once.

tools.name: fetch_url
tools.description: Fetches the contents of a URL and returns the body as text. Use this when the user provides a documentation URL, when board notes record a URL worth consulting, or when you need to read a known docs page (including raw GitHub files for MicroPython upstream docs). GitHub repo and blob URLs auto-translate to raw.githubusercontent.com. On failure, returns a descriptive error string (CORS-blocked, 404, network error) so you can decide on a fallback.

url.description: The URL to fetch (http or https).

cobweb.bandarra.me.blurb: Read editor, Write editor and Edit editor.
cobweb.bandarra.me.name: Cobweb

tools.name: get_wardrobe
tools.description: Read the shopper's wardrobe as compact rows (id, category, brand, size, colour, for), optional category filter, at most 12 rows plus the total. Rows stay on this page.

tools.name: get_my_sizes
tools.description: Sizes the shopper owns, optionally filtered by brand.

tools.name: find_gaps
tools.description: Categories missing or thin, plus categories whose oldest garment is past its replacement life (a `due` block: report it with report_demand_gap kind 'replace'). Carries only the date, months elapsed and size.

tools.name: check_fit
tools.description: Fit advice for a store product handle, based on sizes the shopper already owns. Read-only; uses the store's public catalog.

tools.name: get_preferences
tools.description: Read the shopper's stated preferences: fit, colour family, materials to avoid, price ceiling, liked brands. Stays on this page unless the sharing level lets a field travel.

tools.name: add_garment
tools.description: Add a garment the shopper owns to the private wardrobe.

tools.name: report_demand_gap
tools.description: Send one data-minimized demand signal. The shopper must press Approve next request on the page first; one press releases one signal. Use kind 'replace' for a `due` gap. The sharing level sets which fields travel (0 blocks everything). Never a shopper id or wardrobe rows. Returns the exact payload sent.

tools.name: import_receipt
tools.description: Import pasted receipt or order-email text (no OCR, no network). Adds each item to the purchase log and recognised items to the wardrobe. Nothing is sent to a merchant.

tools.name: get_offers
tools.description: Read approved personal offers for requests this closet sent: size, price, code, validity, purchase link. Read-only; the shopper decides Bought or Passed on the page, no tool can buy.

tools.name: get_campaign_state
tools.description: Read the campaign: facts (price, discount, code, dates, disclaimer), their human lock state, brief, scenes, and format. When facts are locked, agents cannot change them — write copy that matches.

tools.name: set_brief
tools.description: Set the creative brief (tone, pacing, angle). Free-form; not rendered copy.

tools.name: add_scene
tools.description: Append a scene. heading/body are rendered copy, claim-validated against locked facts before anything is applied.

tools.name: update_scene
tools.description: Patch a scene's copy, kind, or duration. The patched result is claim-validated before it is applied.

tools.name: reorder_scenes
tools.description: Reorder scenes. Pass every current scene id exactly once.

tools.name: seek_preview
tools.description: Seek the live preview to a time (seconds). Deterministic, same t, same frame.

tools.name: validate_claims
tools.description: Dry-run the claim validator over a piece of copy, or over the whole campaign when no text is given.

tools.name: export_composition
tools.description: Export the campaign as a standalone HyperFrames HTML composition; the page receives the download and the result carries size and scene count. Fails while any claim violation remains.

tools.name: get_offer
tools.description: Read the locked offer as data a shopping agent can act on: product, prices, promo code, validity dates, disclaimer, purchase link, sizes in stock. Pass requestId for the approved personal offer on one request.

tools.name: import_product
tools.description: Import product facts by handle from the connected demo storefront into the unlocked fact set. The merchant must review and lock afterward; import is refused while facts are locked.

tools.name: get_demand
tools.description: Consented demand grouped by category and size, with request ids for propose_offer and a verdict per group (can-offer, size-not-in-stock, category-mismatch). Counts are exact; at most 3 ids per group, so read total, groups and omitted. No shopper identifier travels.

tools.name: propose_offer
tools.description: Propose a personal offer for one request inside the locked offer rules (cost, margin floor, max discount). Staged only; a human approves it before the shopper sees it. Returns the proposal and its margin check.

hemloop.app.name: Hemloop

tools.name: get_site_metadata
tools.description: Returns site-level metadata: domain, CMS and template version, data schema, active languages. Call this first to understand the site before using other tools, and use its values to parametrize subsequent calls instead of assuming them.

tools.name: get_supported_languages
tools.description: Returns the default language and the list of supported languages. Use it to validate any lang parameter before calling other tools.

tools.name: get_structure_data
tools.description: Returns the authoritative profile of the business behind this site: name, address, city, phone, email and billing data. Use it for any question about identity, location or contact details, and never infer these values from page text.

tools.name: get_hotel_facts
tools.description: Returns the practical facts the property has declared: rating, check-in and check-out times, facilities, accepted payment methods, opening hours and policies on pets, smoking, accessibility and children. Only declared facts are returned: a missing field means unknown, never "not available" or "not allowed". Prefer it over page text for the facts it contains.

tools.name: get_social_profiles
tools.description: Returns the official social profiles of the business, with one URL per network and language. Use the returned URLs verbatim.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: list_menus
tools.description: Returns all site menus with their items, targets and sort order. Use it to understand navigation or to discover valid menu ids. Use the returned names and URLs verbatim.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: get_menu
tools.description: Returns one menu with its full item list. Requires a menuId obtained from list_menus.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: get_menu_voice
tools.description: Resolves where a menu item points to. Read tipo_link to handle the target: pagina means use id_pagina with get_page, camera means use id_camera with get_room_by_id, her means use opzione_her as a booking link, url means use the url directly. If risolvibile is false the target is unpublished: answer with url, not with the id.

voiceId.description: Menu item id, from list_menus or get_menu.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: Returns all site pages with titles, slugs and meta tags, optionally filtered by type: interna is a content page, camera a single room page, raccoltacamere a room listing. Use the returned ids for get_page instead of guessing them.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

pageType.description: Optional page type filter, as returned by this same tool.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Returns the full content of one page as sections and columns with titles, texts, buttons, images and room references, in the requested language only. Requires a pageId from list_pages or a resolved menu target.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: get_page_by_url
tools.description: Returns the full page content starting from a URL of this site, absolute or relative. Use it when the user references a link whose page id is unknown. URLs of other domains are rejected: their content is not available here. On failure, verify the URL or browse the navigation first.

url.description: Absolute or relative URL to resolve.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: list_room_groups
tools.description: Returns room groups, each with its ordered rooms. Prefer this over list_pages when the user asks about room types or categories, because it preserves the grouping defined by the property. Use the returned room ids for get_room_by_id.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: get_room_group
tools.description: Returns one room group with all its rooms. Requires a groupId from list_room_groups.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: list_rooms
tools.description: Returns a flat list of all rooms sorted by position, optionally filtered by group. Use list_room_groups instead when the user asks about categories.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: get_room_by_id
tools.description: Returns the full detail of one room: preview, content blocks and the related page reference. Requires a roomId from list_rooms, list_room_groups or get_room_group.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: get_room_by_slug
tools.description: Returns the full detail of one room from its slug or URL path; the last segment is extracted automatically. Prefer it over get_room_by_id when you have a URL but no id.

slug.description: Room slug or URL path, case-insensitive.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: get_page_room_references
tools.description: Returns every room referenced by a page, the main room plus those embedded in its sections, deduplicated. Prefer it over get_page when you only need the room ids and not the full page content.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: list_faq_groups
tools.description: Returns the frequently asked questions published on this site, grouped by topic, with question and answer in the requested language. Prefer it over page search when the user asks a direct question about rules, services or practical details.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: get_faq_group
tools.description: Returns one FAQ group with all its question and answer pairs. Requires a groupId from list_faq_groups.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: search_site_content
tools.description: Full-text search across the site content available here: pages, rooms, menu, faq. Use it when the user asks about a topic without naming a specific page, then follow the returned ids with the matching detail tool. If count is 0, retry with a broader term before answering that nothing was found.

term.description: Search term, case-insensitive.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

scope.description: Restrict the search to one kind of content. Default: all.

tools.name: prenota_ora
tools.description: LANGUAGE: Always reply in the same language used by the user in the prompt. Book a room at this hotel for specific dates. USE THIS TOOL whenever the user wants to make a reservation, book a room, check availability, request rates, or get a quote for specific dates - in any language. This form uses CHECKIN (arrival date) + CHECKOUT (departure date). Always submit DD/MM/YYYY format strictly. If the year is missing in user input, you MUST use the current year (2026). Ensure the resulting date is in the future. CRITICAL: each parameter value MUST be a plain string, NEVER wrapped in an object. Examples of CORRECT format: { "CHECKIN": "16/05/2026", "CHECKOUT": "22/05/2026", "NUMCAMERE": "1", "NUMADULTI": "4" }. Examples of WRONG format (do NOT use): { "CHECKIN": { "date": "16/05/2026" } }.

Use it when the user asks about a topic without naming a specific page, then follow the returned ids with the matching detail tool. If count is 0, retry with a broader term before answering that nothing was found.

term.description: Search term, case-insensitive.

tools.name: prenota_ora
tools.description: LANGUAGE: Always reply in the same language used by the user in the prompt. Book a room at this hotel for specific dates. USE THIS TOOL whenever the user wants to make a reservation, book a room, check availability, request rates, or get a quote for specific dates - in any language. This form uses CHECKIN (arrival date) + CHECKOUT (departure date). Always submit DD/MM/YYYY format strictly. If the year is missing in user input, you MUST use the current year (2026). Ensure the resulting date is in the future. CRITICAL: each parameter value MUST be a plain string, NEVER wrapped in an object. Examples of CORRECT format: { "CHECKIN": "16/05/2026", "CHECKOUT": "22/05/2026", "NUMCAMERE": "1", "NUMADULTI": "4" }. Examples of WRONG format (do NOT use): { "CHECKIN": { "date": "16/05/2026" } }.

tools.name: get_context
tools.description: Call this first. Describes this Jupyter page: the open documents (widget id, path, unsaved changes, kernel id and status, active notebook cell), the cursor and selection of the current editor, the running kernels, the file browser directory, the open dialogs and the pending tool calls. In JupyterLite, the kernels are those of this browser tab.

tools.name: list_all_commands
tools.description: Find Jupyter commands, for tasks that no other tool covers. Every word of "query" must appear in the command id, label, caption or usage. In each result, "args" is the JSON schema of the arguments (not values) and "tool" is the dedicated tool to use instead, if any. Run commands with execute_command.

query.description: Words to search for, for example "notebook run" or "theme".

limit.description: Maximum number of commands to return (default 50).

tools.name: execute_command
tools.description: Run any Jupyter command by id (find ids and argument schemas with list_all_commands), for example {"command_id": "apputils:change-theme", "args": {"theme": "JupyterLab Dark"}}. Most commands act on the active document. To target an open notebook or console that is not active, add "semanticWidget": "<widget id from get_context>" and "activate": false to the args of notebook:* and console:* commands.

tools.name: answer_dialog
tools.description: Click a button of the dialog that is shown, for example to confirm a kernel restart reported by a pending result. Input fields keep their current value. Pass dialogId when several dialogs are open (shown or queued); queued dialogs cannot be answered. If the dialog opened during a tool call whose result you did not get yet, returns the result of that call (or a pending status).

button.description: The button label (case-insensitive), or its 0-based index.

dialogId.description: The dialog id, only needed when several dialogs are open (see get_context).

tools.name: wait_for_result
tools.description: Wait for a tool call that returned status "pending" and return its final result. If the call is still running when the wait ends, returns status "pending" again.

pendingId.description: The pendingId of the pending result.

timeout.description: Maximum seconds to wait, capped to the execution timeout setting.

tools.name: open_document
tools.description: Show a file (notebook, text file, image...) to the user: open it in the main area, or bring its tab to the front. Not needed to read or edit files. "factory" picks a viewer (for example "Editor" to see a notebook as JSON) and "options.mode" a layout (for example "split-right"). On a page that shows one document (see get_context), the document opens in a new browser tab with its own tools, and the result has "disposed": true. A pop-up blocker can stop that tab: then ask the user to open the document.

path.description: The path of the file to open

options.description: Additional options for opening the widget

ref.description: The reference widget id for the insert location (default `null`)

mode.description: The insertion mode relative to a reference widget ("split-top", "split-bottom", "split-left", "split-right", "tab-before", "tab-after")

rank.description: The rank order of the widget among its siblings

type.description: Type of widget to open, used to load user customization (typically a factory name or widget id)

tools.name: list_directory
tools.description: List the files and folders of a directory. Paths are relative to the root of the file browser; "" is the root.

path.description: Path to the directory to list. If not provided, lists the root directory

includeHidden.description: Whether to include hidden files (default: false)

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a text file, including unsaved changes in an open editor. For notebooks, use read_notebook.

filePath.description: Path to the file to read. If not provided, uses the currently active file in the editor.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Replace the whole content of an existing text file and save it. Read the file first. Use create_file for a new file, and the notebook tools for notebooks.

filePath.description: Path to the file to update

content.description: The new content to set for the file

tools.name: create_file
tools.description: Create a text file with optional content. "fileName" is a name, not a path; "cwd" is the directory (default: the root). Fails if the file exists.

fileName.description: Name of the file to create

fileType.description: Registered JupyterLab file type to create. Common examples: text, python, markdown, json, javascript, typescript, yaml, julia, r, csv

content.description: Initial content for the file (optional)

cwd.description: Directory where to create the file (optional)

tools.name: create_notebook
tools.description: Create the notebook "<name>.ipynb" at the root with a kernel for "language" (the default kernel otherwise) and open it without taking the focus. Returns notebookPath. Fails if the file exists.

language.description: Programming language for the notebook (for example python, r, julia, or javascript). If omitted, the default kernel is used.

name.description: Name for the notebook file (without the .ipynb extension)

tools.name: read_notebook
tools.description: Read a notebook as nbformat JSON (cells with their id, type, source and outputs), including unsaved changes. The other notebook tools take the cell ids from here. Cells of notebooks older than nbformat 4.5 have no id in this result.

notebookPath.description: Path to the notebook file. If not provided, uses the currently active notebook

tools.name: read_cell
tools.description: Read one notebook cell: type, source, outputs and execution count.

notebookPath.description: Path to the notebook file. If not provided, uses the currently active notebook

cellId.description: nbformat cell ID of the cell to get information for. If not provided, uses the currently active cell

tools.name: add_cell
tools.description: Insert a cell with optional content next to "referenceCellId" ("position": below by default) and return its cellId. Without referenceCellId the cell goes next to the active cell: to append, pass the id of the last cell. A single empty first cell is replaced. Not saved: call save_notebook.

notebookPath.description: Path to the notebook file. If not provided, uses the currently active notebook

referenceCellId.description: nbformat cell ID of the reference cell. If not provided, uses the currently active cell

content.description: Content to add to the cell

position.description: Position relative to the reference or active cell (above or below)

tools.name: edit_cell
tools.description: Replace the whole source of a notebook cell (the cell type does not change). Read the cell first. Not saved: call save_notebook.

notebookPath.description: Path to the notebook file. If not provided, uses the currently active notebook

cellId.description: nbformat cell ID of the cell to modify. If not provided, targets the currently active cell

content.description: New content for the cell

tools.name: delete_cell
tools.description: Delete a notebook cell. Not saved: call save_notebook.

notebookPath.description: Path to the notebook file. If not provided, uses the currently active notebook

cellId.description: nbformat cell ID of the cell to delete

tools.name: run_cell
tools.description: Run a code cell in the notebook kernel and return its status and outputs, which the notebook also shows. Errors return success false with the traceback.

notebookPath.description: Path to the notebook file. If not provided, uses the currently active notebook

cellId.description: nbformat cell ID of the cell to run

tools.name: save_notebook
tools.description: Save a notebook.

notebookPath.description: Path to the notebook file. If not provided, uses the currently active notebook

tools.name: run_code
tools.description: Run code in a running kernel and return the outputs, which no notebook shows. Kernel ids come from get_context; the kernel of an open notebook shares its variables.

kernelId.description: The ID of the kernel to execute code in

stopOnError.description: If true, abort the execution queue on an error (default: false)

tools.name: interrupt_kernel
tools.description: Interrupt the code running in a kernel. Kernel ids come from get_context.

kernelId.description: The ID of a running kernel.

tools.name: restart_kernel
tools.description: Restart a kernel without confirmation: all its variables are lost. Kernel ids come from get_context.

kernelId.description: The ID of a running kernel.
