Also returns the projected weekly weight change as a percent of body weight. Deterministic and local-only; mirrors the FitCraft macro calculator page.

goal.description: Goal mode. aggressive-cut = 22.5 percent below maintenance with a 1.8 g/kg protein floor; moderate-cut = 15 percent below; maintain = no change; lean-bulk = 7.5 percent above; standard-bulk = 15 percent above. The legacy values cut, maintenance and bulk map to moderate-cut, maintain and standard-bulk.

calories.description: Optional maintenance calories. If omitted, maintenance is estimated from the sex/age/height/activity fields.

sex.description: Sex, used by the Mifflin-St Jeor equation when maintenance calories are not supplied.

age.description: Age in years. Required when maintenance calories are not supplied; also drives the PROT-AGE 1.6 g/kg protein floor at 65 and older.

height.description: Height. Required when maintenance calories are not supplied.

activity_level.description: Daily activity level used to turn BMR into maintenance calories. Defaults to moderate.

training.description: Resistance-training experience, which sets the protein base before the goal mode shifts it. Defaults to intermediate. The legacy values recreational and serious map to intermediate and advanced.

body_fat_percent.description: Optional body-fat percentage; switches maintenance estimation to Katch-McArdle.

tools.name: calculate_bmi_and_wthr
tools.description: Calculate BMI and optionally waist-to-height ratio using FitCraft health-screening logic.

tools.name: calculate_body_fat
tools.description: Estimate body-fat percentage with the US Navy circumference method (default), or from caliper skinfolds with the Jackson-Pollock 3-site or 7-site equations.

sex.description: Biological sex; selects the sex-specific equation.

method.description: navy (default) uses height, neck, waist and, for women, hip circumferences. jackson_pollock_3 uses age plus chest, abdomen, thigh (men) or triceps, suprailiac, thigh (women) skinfolds in mm. jackson_pollock_7 uses age plus all seven skinfolds in mm.

unit.description: Navy method only: unit for height and all circumferences. Defaults to in.

hip.description: Navy method: hip circumference, required for female estimates.

chest.description: Skinfold in mm: diagonal fold between nipple and front of armpit.

midaxillary.description: Skinfold in mm (7-site): vertical fold on the side of the torso at the level of the bottom of the sternum.

triceps.description: Skinfold in mm: vertical fold on the back of the upper arm, midway between shoulder and elbow.

subscapular.description: Skinfold in mm (7-site): diagonal fold just below the lower tip of the shoulder blade.

abdomen.description: Skinfold in mm: vertical fold 2 cm to the right of the navel.

suprailiac.description: Skinfold in mm: diagonal fold just above the front of the iliac crest.

thigh.description: Skinfold in mm: vertical fold on the front of the thigh, midway between hip and knee.

tools.name: calculate_ffmi
tools.description: Calculate fat-free mass index (FFMI), height-normalized FFMI, lean body mass and fat mass from height, weight and sex, with an optional body fat percentage. With body fat, fat-free mass is weight x (1 - body fat); without it, lean body mass is estimated with the Boer 1984 formula. Returns a sourced category band (Schutz et al. 2002 population medians, ESPEN low cutoffs, college-athlete norms, and the 25.0 value Kouri et al. 1995 observed in steroid-free athletes, presented as an observation rather than a hard ceiling). Mirrors the FitCraft FFMI Calculator page.

sex.description: Sex; selects the Boer formula coefficients and the reference bands.

body_fat_percent.description: Optional body fat percentage. Supplying it switches from the Boer estimate to a direct fat-free mass calculation.

tools.name: calculate_one_rep_max
tools.description: Estimate one-rep max and training loads from lifted weight and reps.

unit.description: Weight unit.

rpe.description: Optional RPE from 6 to 10. Defaults to 10.

tools.name: calculate_heart_rate_zones
tools.description: Estimate maximum heart rate from age by Tanaka 2001, Fox 1971 (220 minus age), Nes 2013, and Gulati 2010, then the five training zones by percent of max and by the Karvonen heart rate reserve method.

formula.description: Max HR formula used for the zones: tanaka (default, recommended), gulati (women), nes (active adults), legacy (Fox 1971, 220 minus age, unvalidated). Every formula is returned in max_heart_rate.byFormula regardless of this choice.

resting_heart_rate.description: Optional resting heart rate in bpm. Unlocks Karvonen heart rate reserve zones.

measured_max_hr.description: Optional measured or watch-learned max HR in bpm. Overrides the age formula and feeds the zones directly.

tools.name: assess_body_recomposition
tools.description: Assess whether body recomposition (losing fat and gaining muscle at the same time) fits a person, and return their maintenance calories, recomposition calorie target, daily protein target, lifting frequency, and an expected timeline.

sex.description: Biological sex; used by the Mifflin-St Jeor equation and the body-fat bands.

activity_level.description: Daily activity level. Defaults to moderate.

training_status.description: Resistance training experience. new covers never trained or returning after a long break. Defaults to under_1_year.

body_fat_percent.description: Optional body-fat percentage. When supplied, protein is set from fat-free mass and the recomposition verdict uses measured body fat instead of a BMI estimate.

tools.name: calculate_calories_burned
tools.description: Estimate calories burned for a workout from activity, intensity, duration and body weight. Covers walking, treadmill, running, a steps-to-calories mode, cycling, swimming, hiking, stair climbing, jump rope, bodyweight and HIIT circuits, strength training, and yoga or Pilates. Returns gross calories, calories above resting, calories per minute and the MET value, with the 2024 Adult Compendium code behind it.

activity.description: Activity performed. walking, treadmill and running take speed_mph and incline_percent. steps takes steps and cadence_steps_per_min. Everything else takes effort.

speed_mph.description: walking, treadmill and running only: pace in miles per hour. Snapped to the nearest Compendium code for the compendium method; used exactly by the ACSM equations.

incline_percent.description: walking, treadmill and running only: percent grade. Defaults to 0.

effort.description: Effort-based activities only (cycling, swimming, hiking, stair_climbing, jump_rope, bodyweight_hiit, strength_training, yoga_pilates). Defaults to moderate.

steps.description: steps activity only: total step count.

cadence_steps_per_min.description: steps activity only: walking cadence in steps per minute. Snapped to the nearest CADENCE-Adults threshold of 80, 100, 110, 120 or 130. Defaults to 100.

duration_minutes.description: Minutes of actual movement. Required for every activity except steps, where it is derived from the step count and cadence.

method.description: Pace-based activities only: compendium (default) uses 2024 Adult Compendium MET codes, acsm uses the ACSM walking and running metabolic equations.

tools.name: calculate_steps_to_distance
tools.description: Convert a step count into miles and kilometers using a step length estimated from standing height and sex, with separate walking and running step lengths, an optional measured step-length override, and an optional calorie estimate.

steps.description: Number of steps to convert.

height_unit.description: Unit for height. Defaults to in.

sex.description: Sets the step-length coefficient: 0.415 x height for male, 0.413 for female.

mode.description: Walking or running. Running steps are much longer. Defaults to walk.

pace.description: Pace. Walking: casual (2.5 mph), average (3.0 mph, default), brisk (3.5 mph), very_brisk (4.0 mph). Running: easy_jog (5.0 mph), steady (6.2 mph, default), fast (7.0 mph).

weight.description: Optional body weight. Supplying it adds a calorie estimate.

weight_unit.description: Unit for weight. Defaults to kg.

step_length.description: Optional measured step length. Overrides the height-based estimate.

step_length_unit.description: Unit for the measured step length. Defaults to in.

tools.name: calculate_water_intake
tools.description: Estimate how much water to drink per day from sex, body weight, daily exercise minutes and climate. The starting range runs from the EFSA 2010 to the IOM 2005 Adequate Intake for total water, adjusted for body weight, temperature, humidity and altitude with the water-turnover equation of Yamada et al. 2022, plus a sweat-based exercise add-on. Returns a drinks target and range, total water including food, water from food, the exercise add-on and cups, in mL, liters and US fluid ounces.

sex.description: Sex; selects the IOM and EFSA Adequate Intakes (women 2.0 to 2.7 L, men 2.5 to 3.7 L of total water a day) and the reference weight.

exercise_minutes.description: Minutes of sweaty exercise on a typical day, 0 to 480. Defaults to 0.

climate.description: Where the person spends most of the day: temperate (about 20 C / 68 F, or air-conditioned indoors, default), warm (about 27 C / 80 F), hot (about 32 C / 90 F), hot_humid (32 C at 80 percent humidity) or altitude (about 2,000 m / 6,500 ft).

tools.name: calculate_weight_loss_percentage
tools.description: Calculate the percent of starting body weight lost, the amount lost, which clinical milestone that reaches (3 to 5% where benefits begin, 5% clinically meaningful, then 10, 15 and 20%), the weight at the next milestone, optional progress toward a goal weight, and an optional average weekly pace as a percent of body weight judged against the 0.5 to 1% per week band. Includes STEP 1 and SURMOUNT-1 trial benchmarks. Mirrors the FitCraft Weight Loss Percentage Calculator page. Never returns dosing advice.

starting_weight.description: Weight at the start, in weight_unit. 70 to 700 lb or 32 to 318 kg.

goal_weight.description: Optional goal weight in weight_unit. Must be below starting_weight. Adds progress toward the goal.

weeks_elapsed.description: Optional weeks since starting_weight was recorded, 1 to 520. Adds the average weekly pace.

country.description: Two-letter country code, e.g. IE or US.

Returns JSON {crisis: true, message, country?, emergency, lines: [{name, contact, hours?}], elsewhere: {emergency, find_a_helpline}, note}.

country.description: Two-letter country code, e.g. IE, GB or US. Default: where the person is browsing from.

tools.name: search_gyfts

Returns JSON {results: [{type, name, detail?, url}], page, next_page?, note}, 6 per page. For details of one result call get_topic, get_practitioner or get_offering. To find practitioners who offer a practice (e.g. reiki), use find_practitioners. Directory information only, not medical advice.

query.description: What to look for, e.g. "reiki", "anxiety", or a practitioner name.

type.description: Only return results of this type. "modality" is a practice; "pathway" is a journey.

page.description: Page of results, from 1. Use next_page from the previous answer.

tools.name: find_practitioners
tools.description: List published Gyfts practitioners who offer a practice or modality, e.g. "reiki" or "acupuncture", optionally in a country or city. Returns JSON {matched: {name, url}, results: [{name, url, where?, verified?}], page, next_page?, note}, 6 per page, verified practitioners first unless sort is "name". Call get_practitioner with the last part of a url for services, prices and formats. Read-only. Directory information only, not medical advice.

practice.description: The practice or modality name, e.g. "reiki".

country.description: Two-letter country code, e.g. IE or US.

sort.description: verified: verified first, then A–Z (default). name: A–Z.

page.description: Page of results, from 1. Use next_page from the previous answer.

tools.name: find_offerings
tools.description: List published courses, workshops, programs, retreats, classes, 1:1 sessions and events on Gyfts, optionally by format, price, country, city and date range. Returns JSON {results: [{name, url, by, format, price, starts?, where?}], page, next_page?, note}, 6 per page, soonest first unless sorted by price (prices compared as listed, not converted). Call get_offering with a url for details. Read-only: it does not book anything; the person books on the page.

query.description: Optional words to match in the title or host name.

mode.description: online, in person (onsite) or both (blended).

country.description: Two-letter country code, e.g. IE or US.

city.description: Only items held in this city, e.g. "Cork". Online-only items drop out.

from.description: Only items starting on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Excludes undated items.

to.description: Only items starting on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Excludes undated items.

sort.description: Default soonest.

page.description: Page of results, from 1. Use next_page from the previous answer.

tools.name: find_organizations
tools.description: List published Gyfts organizations: clinics, wellness centers, retreat centers, training schools, associations, practices. Filter by type, practice (e.g. "yoga"), country and city; give at least one. Returns JSON {matched?: {name, url}, results: [{name, url, type, where?}], page, next_page?, note}, 6 per page, A–Z. Call get_organization with the last part of a url for details. Read-only.

type.description: training_school = a school or academy; association = a professional body.

practice.description: A practice the organization offers, e.g. "yoga" or "acupuncture".

country.description: Two-letter country code, e.g. IE or US.

city.description: City name, e.g. "Galway". Also matches an organization's other sites.

page.description: Page of results, from 1. Use next_page from the previous answer.

tools.name: get_topic
tools.description: Details of one condition, symptom, practice, treatment, specialty or journey on Gyfts: its reviewed short summary and page URL, and for a condition the practices its page lists. Returns JSON {result: {type, name, url, summary?, related_practices?: [{name, url}], next_step?}, note}. A listed practice is not a recommendation. Not medical advice, a diagnosis or a treatment plan.

type.description: practice = a modality (/modalities/…); journey = a pathway (/journey/…).

slug.description: The topic, e.g. "anxiety" from /conditions/anxiety: the last part of its Gyfts URL.

tools.name: get_practitioner
tools.description: A published Gyfts practitioner's public profile summary. Returns JSON {result: {name, url, where?, verified?, practices?, specialties?, languages?, years_experience?, formats?, about?, services?: [{id, name, price, minutes?, format?}], book_url?}, note}. No contact details. Use a service id with check_availability and open_booking.

slug.description: The practitioner, e.g. "jane-doe" from /ie/jane-doe: the last part of its Gyfts URL.

tools.name: get_organization
tools.description: A published Gyfts organization's public summary. Returns JSON {result: {type, name, url, org_type, where?, about?, practices?: [{name, url}], locations?: [{name, city?}], next_step}, note}. No contact details. For its courses, classes and events, call find_offerings with its name as the query.

slug.description: The organization, e.g. "bright-cove" from /ie/organizations/bright-cove: the last part of its Gyfts URL.

tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: A practitioner's open time windows over up to 14 days, optionally for one service (only windows long enough for it). Read-only: nothing is held or booked. Returns JSON {result: {practitioner, url, service?, from, to, times_are: "UTC", open_windows: [{start, end}], book_url, how_to_book}, note}. To book, call open_booking; the person picks the time and pays.

slug.description: The practitioner: the last part of its Gyfts URL.

from.description: First day to check (YYYY-MM-DD). Default today.

days.description: How many days to check. Default 7.

tools.name: get_offering
tools.description: Details of one event, course, workshop, retreat, organization offering or practitioner session, from a url returned by find_offerings. Returns JSON {result: {type, name, url, host?, starts?, ends?, timezone?, format?, where?, price?, minutes?, tickets?: [{name, price}], about?, how_to_book}, note}. Read-only.

url.description: The offering url from find_offerings, e.g. /events/sound-bath-dublin.

tools.name: get_this_page
tools.description: Details of the practitioner, organization, topic or offering shown on the current Gyfts page, in the same shape get_practitioner, get_organization, get_topic or get_offering return. Returns JSON {result: {...} | null, error?, note}; result is null on pages that are not about one of those (e.g. the homepage or a listing).

tools.name: open_page
tools.description: Navigate this tab to a public Gyfts page, e.g. a url from any other tool. Only Gyfts pages; account, admin, sign-in and booking pages are refused (use open_booking to book). Returns JSON {opened} or {error}.

url.description: A Gyfts path such as /modalities/reiki, or a full gyfts.io URL.

tools.name: open_booking
tools.description: Open a practitioner's Gyfts booking page, optionally with one service chosen, so the person can pick a time and pay. The agent does not book or pay: the person signs in and completes it themselves. Returns JSON {opened} or {error}.

tools.name: WixREADME
tools.description:
# Tool: WixREADME
**Directive:** `WixREADME` is the **MANDATORY FIRST STEP** for all Wix-related tasks. Its output (including relevant linked documents) provides foundational context for all other Wix tools. Adherence to this protocol is **NON-NEGOTIABLE**.

**Mid-conversation site switching:** If the user references a different site by name or ID after WixREADME has already been called, use `GetSiteContext` directly — no need to call WixREADME again.
<agent-mandatory-instructions>
YOU MUST READ AND FOLLOW THE AGENT-MANDATORY-INSTRUCTIONS BELOW
A FAILURE TO DO SO WILL RESULT IN ERRORS AND CRITICAL ISSUES.
<goal>
You are an agent that helps the user manage their Wix site.
Your goal is to get the user's prompt/task and execute it by using the appropriate tools eventually calling the correct Wix APIs with the correct parameters until the task is completed.
</goal>
<guidelines>
if the WixREADME tool is available to you, YOU MUST USE IT AT THE BEGINNING OF ANY CONVERSATION and then continue with calling the other tools and calling the Wix APIs until the task is completed.
**Exception:** If the user asks to create, build, or generate a new Wix site/website, skip WixREADME and:
- If the user **explicitly** mentions a template, Wix Studio, or headless → call CreateWixBusinessGuide directly.
- Otherwise → call the WixSiteBuilder tool directly.
**Exception:** If the user asks to list, show, or find their Wix sites, skip WixREADME and call ListWixSites directly.
**Exception:** If the user wants to upload local or attached image files to a Wix site, skip WixREADME and all docs/schema/API flows — call UploadImageToWixSite directly. Do NOT use ExecuteWixAPI, SearchWixAPISpec, or any Media Manager REST API for image uploads.
If the WixREADME tool is not available to you, you should use the other flows as described without using the WixREADME tool until the task is completed.
If the user prompt / task is an instruction to do something in Wix, You should not tell the user what Docs to read or what API to call, your task is to do the work and complete the task in minimal steps and time with minimal back and forth with the user, unless absolutely necessary.
</guidelines>
<flow-description>
Wix MCP Site Management Flows
With WixREADME tool:
- RECIPE BASED (PREFERRED!): WixREADME() -> find relevant recipe for the user's prompt/task -> read recipe using ReadFullDocsArticle() -> call Wix API using CallWixSiteAPI() based on the recipe
- CONVERSATION CONTEXT BASED: find relevant docs article or API example for the user's prompt/task in the conversation context -> call API using CallWixSiteAPI() based on the docs article or API example
- EXAMPLE BASED: WixREADME() -> no relevant recipe found for user's prompt/task -> BrowseWixRESTDocsMenu() or SearchWixRESTDocumentation() -> find relevant method -> read method article using ReadFullDocsArticle() to get method code examples -> call API using CallWixSiteAPI() based on the method code examples
- SCHEMA BASED, FALLBACK: WixREADME() -> no relevant recipe found for user's prompt/task -> BrowseWixRESTDocsMenu() or SearchWixRESTDocumentation() -> find relevant method -> read method article using ReadFullDocsArticle() -> no method code examples found -> inspect the method schema using SearchWixAPISpec or ReadFullDocsMethodSchema -> call API using CallWixSiteAPI() based on the schema

code.description: JavaScript async function expression to execute against the Wix REST API. The value must be the function itself, for example `async function() { ... }` or `async () => { ... }`, not a script body and not an invoked function. Return the final answer from inside the function. Do not write top-level `const`, top-level `await`, or top-level `return` outside the function body. Full Wix API URLs and paths starting with `/` are supported. Wix REST API page size limits vary — use 100 as a safe default unless the method schema (via SearchWixAPISpec) confirms a higher limit is supported. For cursor-based APIs, pass the next cursor as `cursorPaging: { limit: 100, cursor: pagingMetadata.cursors.next }` — not inside `paging`. Check the method schema to confirm whether the API uses `paging` (offset-based) or `cursorPaging` (cursor-based) before paginating.

**Directive:** `WixREADME` is the **MANDATORY FIRST STEP** for all Wix-related tasks. Its output (including relevant linked documents) provides foundational context for all other Wix tools. Adherence to this protocol is **NON-NEGOTIABLE**.

**Mid-conversation site switching:** If the user references a different site by name or ID after WixREADME has already been called, use `GetSiteContext` directly — no need to call WixREADME again.

- Otherwise → call the WixSiteBuilder tool directly.

tools.name: ExecuteWixAPI

code.description: JavaScript async function expression to execute against the Wix REST API. The value must be the function itself, for example `async function() { ... }` or `async () => { ... }`, not a script body and not an invoked function. Return the final answer from inside the function. Do not write top-level `const`, top-level `await`, or top-level `return` outside the function body. Use `wix.request({ method, url, body })` for Wix API calls. Every call runs against the current visitor site; do not set `scope`, `siteId`, or auth headers. Full Wix API URLs and paths starting with `/` are supported. Wix REST API page size limits vary — use 100 as a safe default unless the method schema (via SearchWixAPISpec) confirms a higher limit is supported. For cursor-based APIs, pass the next cursor as `cursorPaging: { limit: 100, cursor: pagingMetadata.cursors.next }` — not inside `paging`. Check the method schema to confirm whether the API uses `paging` (offset-based) or `cursorPaging` (cursor-based) before paginating.

tools.name: GetSitePages
tools.description: Returns the COMPLETE list of pages that exist on this site, as route patterns. Only these pages exist; never guess or invent a URL (e.g. /shop, /store, /checkout, /account) - a path not listed here will show a 404. `title` is the page's name in the site menu; match it against what the visitor asks for. Static routes are exact paths (e.g. /cart). Dynamic routes contain [param] placeholders (e.g. /products/[slug]) or a rest placeholder ([...path]); `identifiers` says what fills each placeholder (e.g. slug: STORES.PRODUCT.SLUG means the product's slug from the Stores products API) and `pageIdentifier` names the Wix page type. A route with `acceptsSubpath` also accepts a concrete path below it, e.g. the product page URL returned by the Stores API. Navigate with NavigateToPage, passing the route pattern and a `params` value for every placeholder. If the page the visitor asks for is not in the list, say so instead of navigating.

tools.name: playground_execute_php
tools.description:
Run arbitrary PHP code in WordPress Playground
			and return the output.

			WordPress is NOT bootstrapped automatically. To use
			WordPress functions, start your code with:
			require("/wordpress/wp-load.php");
			Always include the opening <?php tag.

			The response JSON contains three fields:
			- "text": stdout output
			- "errors": PHP warnings, notices, and fatal error
			  messages from stderr
			- "exitCode": 0 on success, non-zero on fatal error
			Check both "errors" and "exitCode" to determine
			whether the call succeeded.

			WARNING: output is returned in full with no
			truncation — avoid queries that produce unbounded
			output (e.g. SELECT * without LIMIT). Keep output
			under 50 KB to avoid filling the context window.

PHP code to execute. Example:
					"<?php echo get_bloginfo('name');"

tools.name: playground_request
tools.description:
Make an HTTP request to the WordPress site
			running in Playground. REST API requests
			(/wp-json/* or ?rest_route=) are automatically
			authenticated with a valid nonce — no manual
			auth needed.

			Tool selection guide:
			1. Use this tool (playground_request) with the
			   REST API for standard content CRUD — posts,
			   pages, users, terms, comments, settings, etc.
			   The REST API handles serialization, pagination,
			   and field filtering for you. Prefer compact
			   REST responses: use _fields to request only the
			   fields needed and per_page/page for large
			   collections. Before using endpoint-specific
			   filters, inspect the route metadata from
			   /wp-json/ and use only args documented for that
			   route.
			2. Use this tool with the WordPress REST API to
			   discover and call registered abilities when the
			   site exposes the Abilities API:
			   - GET /wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities
			     lists registered abilities. Always assume this
			     response may be large and start with _fields,
			     e.g.
			     /wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities?_fields=name,category,label,description
			     Do not assume filters like search or category
			     exist unless /wp-json/ route metadata documents
			     them.
			   - GET /wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities/{name}
			     gets one ability, including schemas and
			     metadata. Ability names include "/" in the
			     path; do not encode it. For example, use
			     /wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities/memex/save-note
			     for "memex/save-note".
			   - GET, POST, or DELETE
			     /wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities/{name}/run
			     executes the ability. Inspect the ability
			     metadata first, then call /run with the
			     documented method. POST bodies usually wrap
			     arguments in an "input" object, e.g.
			     {"input":{"title":"Hello"}}.
			   - GET /wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/categories
			     lists ability categories. Each category includes
			     _links.abilities; follow that URL to list
			     abilities in that category. The abilities
			     collection can also be filtered directly with
			     /wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities?category={slug}.
			3. Use playground_execute_php when the data you
			   need is not exposed by the REST API (e.g.
			   raw options, direct database queries, or
			   custom table access).
			4. Use this tool as a plain HTTP request (non-REST)
			   when the HTTP layer itself matters: verifying
			   redirects, status codes, cookies, or response
			   headers.

tools.name: ExecuteWixAPI

code.description: JavaScript async function expression to execute against the Wix REST API. The value must be the function itself, for example `async function() { ... }` or `async () => { ... }`, not a script body and not an invoked function. Return the final answer from inside the function. Do not write top-level `const`, top-level `await`, or top-level `return` outside the function body. Use `wix.request({ method, url, body })` for Wix API calls. Every call runs against the current visitor site; do not set `scope`, `siteId`, or auth headers. Full Wix API URLs and paths starting with `/` are supported. Wix REST API page size limits vary — use 100 as a safe default unless the method schema (via SearchWixAPISpec) confirms a higher limit is supported. For cursor-based APIs, pass the next cursor as `cursorPaging: { limit: 100, cursor: pagingMetadata.cursors.next }` — not inside `paging`. Check the method schema to confirm whether the API uses `paging` (offset-based) or `cursorPaging` (cursor-based) before paginating.

reason.description: One sentence explaining the original user request and why you are executing code to complete it.

hasMutations.description: Whether this code creates, updates, deletes, publishes, imports, uploads, or otherwise mutates site data on the visitor’s behalf. Set this to true for create/update/delete/bulk create/import/upload calls even if the reason is inspection, verification, or response-shape discovery. Read-only GET/query/list/search calls can use false.

sourceDocUrls.description:
The URLs of the documentation, recipes, API articles, or schema sources where you confirmed the Wix REST endpoints, HTTP methods, request body shapes, auth contexts, and required fields used by this code.
Include every docs/schema source needed for the endpoints and request shapes used in the code.
MAKE SURE THE ENDPOINT URLS AND REQUEST SHAPES ARE REALLY THERE AND YOU ARE NOT GUESSING THEM !!!
Each value must be a valid URL like:
- https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/... (REST API reference docs)
Use ["user-provided"] if the user gave you all endpoint and request details directly.
Use ["other"] ONLY IF YOU HAVE A VERY GOOD REASON TO DO SO

tools.description: Returns the COMPLETE list of pages that exist on this site, as route patterns. Only these pages exist; never guess or invent a URL (e.g. /shop, /store, /checkout, /account) - a path not listed here will show a 404. `title` is the page's name in the site menu; match it against what the visitor asks for. Static routes are exact paths (e.g. /cart). Dynamic routes contain [param] placeholders (e.g. /products/[slug]) or a rest placeholder ([...path]); `identifiers` says what fills each placeholder (e.g. slug: STORES.PRODUCT.SLUG means the product's slug from the Stores products API) and `pageIdentifier` names the Wix page type. tools.name: plan-trip
tools.description: Answer "which eSIM should I buy for this trip?". Give it the stops, a country code and the days spent in each, and it compares one plan covering the whole route against one plan per country against a mix of the two, on live prices, then flags the cheapest option that covers everything and explains the choice in a sentence you can quote. It also estimates the data each stop needs, names any country SimFuse cannot cover, and returns package ids that go straight into create-checkout-session. Use it whenever a trip has two or more countries, and for a single country when the traveller wants a recommendation rather than a list. Read-only: nothing is reserved and nothing is charged, and the totals are today's catalog prices, not a quote held for later.

stops.description: The trip, one entry per country, in travel order. 1 to 12 stops, e.g. [{"country":"JP","days":7},{"country":"KR","days":5}].

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, e.g. "JP" for Japan. Look one up with list-destinations rather than guessing. Each country may appear once: give one stop with the total days rather than two visits.

days.description: Days spent in that country, 1 to 365. Count the nights of the stay.

usage.description: Optional. How heavily data is used during this stop: "light" (about 300 MB a day, maps and messaging), "regular" (about 800 MB a day) or "heavy" (about 2 GB a day, video and hotspot). Overrides the trip-wide `usage` for this stop only.
Optional. Trip-wide data usage for stops that do not set their own: "light" (about 300 MB a day), "regular" (about 800 MB a day) or "heavy" (about 2 GB a day). Defaults to "regular".

start.description: Optional. Departure date as YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2026-04-18". Only used to date the stops in the answer; it does not change prices. Defaults to today.

currency.description: Optional. ISO 4217 three-letter code every price is quoted in, e.g. "USD", "EUR", "GBP". Defaults to EUR. An unknown code falls back to EUR rather than failing.

tools.name: list-destinations
tools.description: Find the countries SimFuse sells eSIMs for, with the cheapest plan price ("from" price) for each in the currency you ask for. Start here when someone names a place: it turns "Portugal" into the two-letter country code the other tools take, and shows what that destination starts at. For one destination, follow it with list-plans; for a trip covering two or more countries, use plan-trip instead. Read-only, and it answers from the SimFuse catalog alone.

search.description: Optional. Match destinations by name, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 code, case-insensitively. A partial name works: "port" matches Portugal. Omit to list every destination.

currency.description: Optional. ISO 4217 three-letter code the "from" prices are quoted in, e.g. "USD", "EUR", "GBP". Defaults to EUR. An unknown code falls back to EUR rather than failing.

limit.description: Optional. Maximum destinations to return, 1 to 300. Defaults to 300, which is the whole list.

tools.name: list-regions
tools.description: Discover available eSIM regions, including worldwide scopes, with their canonical slugs, display names, member countries and starting prices. Only published regions with active displayed regional plans are listed. Pass a returned region slug to list-plans as region, not destination. Country membership describes the region, not a promise that every plan covers every member: check get-plan-coverage for a specific plan. Read-only; no account or key is needed.

search.description: Optional. Case-insensitive partial match on the canonical region slug or display name, e.g. "asia". Omit to list all available regions.

currency.description: Optional. ISO 4217 code for starting prices, e.g. "EUR" or "USD". Defaults to EUR; unknown codes fall back to the base currency.

limit.description: Optional. Maximum regions to return, 1 to 300. Defaults to 300. total reports the match count before this limit.

tools.name: get-destination-info
tools.description: Details for one destination: its name and codes, region, how many eSIM plans are sold there, the cheapest and most expensive, the smallest and largest data bundles, and its storefront page. Takes a country name ("Japan") or two-letter code ("JP"). Use this to describe a destination before pulling its full plan ladder with list-plans. Whether a plan can be topped up varies by plan and is reported by list-plans, not here.

destination.description: The destination: a country name ("Japan") or a two-letter code ("JP").

currency.description: Three-letter currency code for the prices (e.g. "USD", "EUR"). Defaults to EUR.

tools.name: list-plans
tools.description: Show the eSIM plans on sale for one country or region, or search the whole catalog, narrowing by data allowance, validity and price. Use destination with a country code from list-destinations, or region with a slug from list-regions; never both. Use it when the traveller wants to compare what is available or find a plan inside a budget. Prices are live retail prices in the currency you ask for. For a trip covering two or more countries, use plan-trip first: it compares one plan for the whole route against one plan per country and picks the cheapest complete answer. Pass a plan id from here to get-plan, get-plan-coverage or create-checkout-session. Read-only, and it answers from the SimFuse catalog alone.

destination.description: Optional. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 destination country code, e.g. "US", "GB", "DE". Look it up with list-destinations rather than guessing. Cannot be combined with region. Omit both destination and region to search the whole catalog.

region.description: Optional. Canonical region slug, e.g. "europe", "southeast-asia" or "global", to search that regional shelf. Cannot be combined with destination. Unknown regions return no plans.

min_data_amount_mb.description: Optional. Only plans with at least this much data, in MEGABYTES: 1 GB is 1024, 10 GB is 10240.

max_data_amount_mb.description: Optional. Only plans with at most this much data, in megabytes.

min_validity_days.description: Optional. Only plans valid for at least this many days, e.g. 14 for a two-week trip.

max_validity_days.description: Optional. Only plans valid for at most this many days.

min_price_cents.description: Optional. Only plans at or above this retail price, in minor units (cents) of `currency`: 500 is 5.00.

max_price_cents.description: Optional. Only plans at or below this retail price, in minor units (cents) of `currency`: 2500 is 25.00.

currency.description: Optional. ISO 4217 three-letter code prices are quoted and filtered in, e.g. "USD", "EUR", "GBP". Defaults to EUR. An unknown code falls back to EUR rather than failing.

limit.description: Optional. Maximum plans to return, 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

tools.name: get-plan
tools.description: Read everything about one eSIM plan by its id: data allowance, how long it stays valid, what happens after a fair-use cap, whether hotspot and top-ups are supported, the network it runs on, and the retail price in the currency you ask for. Use it to answer a specific question about a plan already found with list-plans or plan-trip, and before buying, to confirm the plan really matches what the traveller asked for. Ask get-plan-coverage instead when the question is which countries it works in. Read-only: it reserves nothing and charges nothing.

plan_id.description: The plan id: a 26-character ULID as returned by list-plans or plan-trip, e.g. "01JVQ2S6D4X8N0RMB7YQZ5K3TA". Slugs and supplier codes are not accepted, and an id must never be invented.

currency.description: Optional. ISO 4217 three-letter code the price is quoted in, e.g. "USD", "EUR", "GBP". Defaults to EUR. An unknown code falls back to EUR rather than failing.

tools.name: build-plan
tools.description: Build an eSIM plan to the traveller's liking for one destination: how much data, for how many days, optionally which network it runs on and whether calls and texts are bundled. Returns the one real plan that matches, with its id and live price, never a made-up combination: a shape nobody sells is snapped to the nearest one that is, one axis at a time, and every change is spelled out in `adjustments` so you can read it back. Use it when the traveller knows what they want ("10 GB on Docomo for two weeks"); use plan-trip when they want a recommendation or the trip has several countries. To buy, pass `plan.id` to get-checkout-link when a person is paying, or to create-checkout-session when you are. Read-only: it reserves nothing and charges nothing.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the destination, e.g. "JP". Look it up with list-destinations rather than guessing.

data_mb.description: Data allowance wanted, in megabytes: 1 GB is 1024 MB, so 5 GB is 5120. Pass 0 for an unlimited plan. Snapped to the nearest size sold when no plan has exactly this size.

validity_days.description: How many days the plan should stay valid, 1 to 365. Snapped to the nearest length sold for the chosen size.

network.description: Optional. The mobile network the plan should run on, by carrier name as `options.networks` lists them, e.g. "NTT Docomo" or "au". Matching is case-insensitive and a single carrier of a multi-network plan is enough. Omit for the cheapest network.

voice.description: Optional. True to require a plan that bundles calls and texts. Defaults to false, data only. If no such plan exists the answer is data only and says so.

currency.description: Optional. ISO 4217 three-letter code the price is quoted in, e.g. "USD", "EUR", "GBP". Defaults to EUR. An unknown code falls back to EUR rather than failing.

tools.name: get-plan-coverage
tools.description: List every country one eSIM plan works in, plus any country of its own region that it leaves out. Use it to answer "does this plan also cover Austria?" for a regional or worldwide plan, where the plan name says a region and the traveller needs the actual list. For a single-country plan the answer is that one country. Ask get-plan instead for the data allowance, validity or price. Read-only.

plan_id.description: The plan id: a 26-character ULID as returned by list-plans or plan-trip, e.g. "01JVQ2S6D4X8N0RMB7YQZ5K3TA". Slugs and supplier codes are not accepted, and an id must never be invented.

tools.name: check-coverage
tools.description: Answer "does this eSIM plan work in X?" for one destination, as a yes or no rather than a country list. Takes a plan id and a destination (a country name or two-letter code). Reports whether the destination is covered, and separately whether it is explicitly excluded from an otherwise regional plan. Use get-plan-coverage when you need the full list of countries instead.

plan_id.description: The plan id (a ULID) as returned by list-plans.

destination.description: The country to check: a name ("Japan") or a two-letter code ("JP").

tools.name: get-checkout-link
tools.description: Get the page where a person buys one specific eSIM plan, for an assistant to hand them a link. The page sells exactly this plan with Apple Pay, Google Pay and card, takes the email at payment, and sends the eSIM there. Nothing is charged or reserved by this call and the buyer needs no account. Use this whenever a PERSON is going to pay. Use create-checkout-session instead when the agent is settling the purchase itself, or for more than one plan or unit.

plan_id.description: The plan id (a ULID) as returned by list-plans, get-plan or plan-trip.

currency.description: Three-letter currency code for the price quoted back to you (e.g. "USD", "EUR"). Defaults to EUR. The page itself prices in the buyer's own currency.

source.description: The name of the assistant or app sending the buyer, recorded as the campaign source on the link (e.g. "claude"). Optional.

tools.name: create-checkout-session
tools.description: Get the checkout page for each plan the person in this browser wants to buy. In this browser the person pays, so this returns links to SimFuse plan pages (Apple Pay, Google Pay and card, eSIM delivered by email, no account needed) rather than an agent payment session. Nothing is charged or reserved. Pass the plan ids returned by plan-trip, list-plans or get-plan.

items.description: The plans to buy.

id.description: Plan id (a ULID) from plan-trip, list-plans or get-plan.

quantity.description: How many of this plan. Defaults to 1.

currency.description: Three-letter currency code for the prices quoted back, e.g. "EUR". The page prices itself in the buyer's own currency.

tools.name: get-order-status
tools.description: Check an eSIM order after payment: whether it completed and whether its eSIMs have been provisioned yet. Identified by the order id together with the email that bought it, both of which are on the buyer's confirmation email. Provisioning usually finishes within a minute of payment, so an order that is paid but lists no eSIMs yet is normal: check again shortly. Once an eSIM is listed, use get-esim-activation to fetch its QR code and install details.

order_id.description: The order id from the buyer's confirmation email or order page.

email.description: The email address the order was bought with. Required: the order id alone does not identify a buyer.

tools.name: get-esim-activation
tools.description: Fetch the installable eSIM(s) for a paid order: the QR code image, the LPA activation string, the SM-DP+ address and activation code for manual entry, one-tap install links for iPhone and Android, and a hosted install page to send the buyer. Identified by the order id together with the email that bought it. Returns an empty esims list while provisioning is still in flight, which normally clears within a minute of payment.

order_id.description: The order id from the buyer's confirmation email or order page.

email.description: The email address the order was bought with. Required: the order id alone does not identify a buyer.

tools.name: check-esim-usage
tools.description: How much data an eSIM has used and how much is left, for one eSIM on a paid order. Identified by the order id and the email that bought it, plus the ICCID from get-order-status or get-esim-activation. Allowances are in megabytes. Readings are served from a cache refreshed every couple of minutes: checked_at says when the reading was taken. An unlimited plan reports its full-speed allowance for the current period rather than a total.

order_id.description: The order id from the buyer's confirmation email or order page.

email.description: The email address the order was bought with.

iccid.description: The ICCID of the eSIM to read, as returned by get-order-status.

tools.name: list-topup-options
tools.description: Data top-ups that can be added to an eSIM the buyer already has, narrowed to what its network will actually accept. Identified by the order id and the email that bought it, plus the ICCID. Read-only: a top-up is bought in the SimFuse app, not through this server, and the response carries the link that opens this eSIM there. Do not pass these package ids to create-checkout-session, which would buy a separate new eSIM rather than add data to this one.

order_id.description: The order id from the buyer's confirmation email or order page.

email.description: The email address the order was bought with.

iccid.description: The ICCID of the eSIM to top up, as returned by get-order-status.

currency.description: Three-letter currency code for the prices (e.g. "USD", "EUR"). Defaults to EUR.

tools.name: open-trip-planner
tools.description: Open the visual trip planner in this browser tab, pre-filled with the given route, so the user can see and edit the comparison. Use after plan-trip when the user wants to look at the options.

stops.description: The route as comma-separated COUNTRY:DAYS stops, e.g. "JP:14,KR:4". An optional per-stop usage suffix works too: "JP:14:heavy".

tools.name: WixREADME
tools.description:
# Tool: WixREADME
**Directive:** `WixREADME` is the **MANDATORY FIRST STEP** for all Wix-related tasks. Its output (including relevant linked documents) provides foundational context for all other Wix tools. Adherence to this protocol is **NON-NEGOTIABLE**.

**Mid-conversation site switching:** If the user references a different site by name or ID after WixREADME has already been called, use `GetSiteContext` directly — no need to call WixREADME again.
<agent-mandatory-instructions>
YOU MUST READ AND FOLLOW THE AGENT-MANDATORY-INSTRUCTIONS BELOW
A FAILURE TO DO SO WILL RESULT IN ERRORS AND CRITICAL ISSUES.
<goal>
You are an agent that helps the user manage their Wix site.
Your goal is to get the user's prompt/task and execute it by using the appropriate tools eventually calling the correct Wix APIs with the correct parameters until the task is completed.
</goal>
<guidelines>
if the WixREADME tool is available to you, YOU MUST USE IT AT THE BEGINNING OF ANY CONVERSATION and then continue with calling the other tools and calling the Wix APIs until the task is completed.
**Exception:** If the user asks to create, build, or generate a new Wix site/website, skip WixREADME and:
- If the user **explicitly** mentions a template, Wix Studio, or headless → call CreateWixBusinessGuide directly.
- Otherwise → call the WixSiteBuilder tool directly.
**Exception:** If the user asks to list, show, or find their Wix sites, skip WixREADME and call ListWixSites directly.
**Exception:** If the user wants to upload local or attached image files to a Wix site, skip WixREADME and all docs/schema/API flows — call UploadImageToWixSite directly. Do NOT use ExecuteWixAPI, SearchWixAPISpec, or any Media Manager REST API for image uploads.
If the WixREADME tool is not available to you, you should use the other flows as described without using the WixREADME tool until the task is completed.
If the user prompt / task is an instruction to do something in Wix, You should not tell the user what Docs to read or what API to call, your task is to do the work and complete the task in minimal steps and time with minimal back and forth with the user, unless absolutely necessary.
</guidelines>
<flow-description>
Wix MCP Site Management Flows
With WixREADME tool:

code.description: JavaScript async function expression to execute against the Wix REST API. The value must be the function itself, for example `async function() { ... }` or `async () => { ... }`, not a script body and not an invoked function. Return the final answer from inside the function. Do not write top-level `const`, top-level `await`, or top-level `return` outside the function body. Use `wix.request({ method, url, body })` for Wix API calls. Every call runs against the current visitor site; do not set `scope`, `siteId`, or auth headers. Full Wix API URLs and paths starting with `/` are supported. Wix REST API page size limits vary — use 100 as a safe default unless the method schema (via SearchWixAPISpec) confirms a higher limit is supported. For cursor-based APIs, pass the next cursor as `cursorPaging: { limit: 100, cursor: pagingMetadata.cursors.next }` — not inside `paging`. Check the method schema to confirm whether the API uses `paging` (offset-based) or `cursorPaging` (cursor-based) before paginating.

tools.name: GetSitePages
tools.description: Returns the COMPLETE list of pages that exist on this site, as route patterns. Only these pages exist; never guess or invent a URL (e.g. /shop, /store, /checkout, /account) - a path not listed here will show a 404. `title` is the page's name in the site menu; match it against what the visitor asks for. Static routes are exact paths (e.g. /cart). Dynamic routes contain [param] placeholders (e.g. /products/[slug]) or a rest placeholder ([...path]); `identifiers` says what fills each placeholder (e.g. slug: STORES.PRODUCT.SLUG means the product's slug from the Stores products API) and `pageIdentifier` names the Wix page type. A route with `acceptsSubpath` also accepts a concrete path below it, e.g. the product page URL returned by the Stores API. Navigate with NavigateToPage, passing the route pattern and a `params` value for every placeholder. If the page the visitor asks for is not in the list, say so instead of navigating.

Yaqeen's team includes scholars like Dr. Omar Suleiman, Dr. Tesneem Alkiek, Dr. Tahir Wyatt, Sh. Mohammad Elshinawy, and 200+ researchers and contributors.

slug.description: URL slug of the scholar, e.g. "omar-suleiman" or "tesneem-alkiek"

tools.name: browse_yaqeen_series
tools.description: Browse Yaqeen Institute's multi-part content series, or get the full table of contents for a specific series. Returns series titles, descriptions, and episode counts. Pass a slug to get all episodes in order. Use this when a user asks for a series, a collection of videos or articles on a topic, a guided learning path, or 'what can I watch during Ramadan.' Popular series include 'Angels in Your Presence,' '40 Hadiths on Social Justice,' 'The Beginning and the End,' and 'Qur’an 30 for 30.'

slug.description: Optional: slug of a specific series to get its full table of contents, e.g. "angels-in-your-presence"

limit.description: Optional: max number of series to return when browsing (default 20)

tools.name: get_related_content
tools.description: Find content related to a specific Yaqeen article, paper, or video. Returns companion resources including PDFs, study guides, infographics, series, and related articles. Use this after retrieving an article to find additional resources on the same topic, or when a user asks "what else should I read on this?" or "is there an infographic version of this?"

slug.description: URL slug of the article to find related content for

tools.name: browse_yaqeen_curriculum
tools.description: Browse Yaqeen Institute's Islamic education curriculum for high school and middle school students and educators. Returns topics and units with descriptions and downloadable teaching materials. Use this when a user is a teacher, parent, or educator looking for structured Islamic education resources, lesson plans, or classroom materials on topics like faith, ethics, and principles of Islam.

topic_slug.description: Optional: slug of a specific curriculum topic to get its full unit list with download links, e.g. "principles-of-faith"

tools.name: browse_yaqeen_topics
tools.description: Browse Yaqeen Institute's full topic taxonomy. Returns all research areas with descriptions and article counts. Use this when a user asks what topics or areas Yaqeen covers, or to find the correct topic name to pass to search_yaqeen_content. Yaqeen's top-level research areas include: Faith (iman, Allah, Quran, angels, prophets, afterlife), Sharia (Islamic law, acts of worship, fiqh, methodology), Politics & Practical Theology (identity, Islamophobia, social justice, gender, epistemology), History (seerah, Islamic civilization, Islam in the West), Psychology & Mental Health (mental health, trauma, spirituality, doubt, religious identity), Family & Community (parenting, marriage, education, culture), Nature & Science (evolution, health, technology, environment), and Data (research reports, datasets).

parent_only.description: If true (default), returns only top-level parent topics. Set to false to include sub-topics.

tools.name: browse_yaqeen_books
tools.description: Browse Yaqeen Institute's collection of free downloadable Islamic books. Returns titles, descriptions, authors, and PDF download links. Optionally pass a slug for a specific book. Use this when a user asks about Islamic books, wants free reading material, or is looking for Ramadan reading recommendations.

slug.description: Optional: slug of a specific book for its full detail

tools.name: get_yaqeen_annual_report
tools.description: Retrieve Yaqeen Institute's annual impact reports with PDF links. Shows research output, community impact, and financial transparency. Use this when a user asks about Yaqeen's impact, how donations are used, or requests accountability information before donating.

year.description: Optional: filter by fiscal year, e.g. 2024

tools.name: search_audio_content
tools.description: Find Yaqeen Institute audio content a user can listen to while multitasking — including podcast episodes, full podcast series, and audiobooks. Use this tool when a user asks: 'Is there a podcast about X?', 'I want to listen to something about Islam while driving/working out', 'Can I listen to this instead of reading it?', 'What Islamic podcasts does Yaqeen have?', 'Is there an audio version?', 'I want Islamic content about mental health / OCD / grief / faith / Ramadan / Quran that I can listen to'. Pass a query to search for episodes and audiobooks on that specific topic. Returns Yaqeen's three podcast series (DoubleTake, Dogma Disrupted, Quran Convos Tadabbur) along with matching podcast episodes and audiobooks. Note: many individual papers also have audio narrations available directly on their article pages — the response will guide the user on how to find those.

query.description: Topic to search for in podcast episodes and audiobooks, e.g. 'mental health', 'OCD', 'grief', 'Ramadan', 'faith doubts'. Leave empty to browse all available audio content.

tools.name: search_video_transcript
tools.description: Search the transcript of a specific Yaqeen Institute video for a topic or keyword, and return the exact timecoded segments where it is discussed — including YouTube deeplinks that jump directly to that moment. Use this after finding a relevant video slug via search_yaqeen_content. Pass the video's URL slug and a search query (e.g. 'challenges Salahuddin faced', 'proof of God', 'dealing with grief'). Returns up to 8 matching transcript segments, each with a formatted timecode (MM:SS), the spoken text, and a YouTube deeplink with ?t= that takes the user directly to that moment in the video.

slug.description: URL slug of the Yaqeen video, e.g. "the-beginning-and-the-end-ep-1". Obtain this from search_yaqeen_content first.

query.description: The topic or phrase to search for in the transcript, e.g. "Salahuddin Jerusalem" or "proof of God existence"

tools.name: get_islamophobia_resources
tools.description: Retrieve Yaqeen Institute's curated research and media specifically organized to counter Islamophobia and anti-Muslim narratives. Use this tool when a user: (1) has encountered a negative claim about Islam or Muslims — e.g. 'Muslims are violent,' 'Islam oppresses women,' 'Muslims want to impose Sharia law,' 'Islam is incompatible with Western values,' 'Muslims support terrorism,' or 'Islam is an irrational faith'; (2) is asking how to respond to Islamophobia, anti-Muslim prejudice, or discrimination; (3) asks what Islamophobia is or why anti-Muslim bias exists; (4) is a Muslim who feels targeted, misrepresented, or exhausted by having to defend their faith. Returns myth-by-myth sections each with a refutation narrative, a counterpoint summary, and a curated list of papers, videos, animations, and infographics with direct links. Optionally pass a myth_topic keyword to filter to the most relevant section.

myth_topic.description: Optional keyword to filter to the most relevant myth section, e.g. "violence", "women", "sharia", "culture", "terrorism", "faith"

tools.name: get_imam_resources
tools.description: Return Yaqeen Institute's research and data specifically about the professional and personal lives of Muslim religious leaders — imams, chaplains, and mosque leaders — in North America. Use this tool when a user asks: 'What does research say about imam burnout?', 'Are there resources about imam compensation or job satisfaction?', 'I am an imam struggling with work-life balance — what has Yaqeen published on this?', 'Where can I find Yaqeen's imam survey?', 'What are the challenges facing mosque leadership in America?', 'Is there data on the mental health of Muslim religious leaders?', 'Our mosque board wants to understand fair compensation for imams'. Returns direct links to the imam well-being report and the institutional dataset.

tools.name: get_new_muslim_resources
tools.description: Return curated starter resources for new Muslims (converts/reverts) and born-Muslims returning to practice. Use this tool when a user says: 'I just became Muslim', 'I took my shahada', 'I'm a revert', 'I'm a convert', 'where do I start learning about Islam?', 'how do I pray?', 'it's my first Ramadan', 'I'm not sure how to practice as a new Muslim', 'I feel pressure to give up my culture as a convert', or 'I want to reconnect with my faith'. Optionally pass a topic to prioritize the most relevant resources. Returns a structured guide with direct links to Yaqeen content specifically designed for people beginning or restarting their Islamic journey.

topic.description: Optional: the user's most immediate need. Use 'prayer' for salah questions, 'ramadan' for fasting and Ramadan questions, 'quran' for Quran connection, 'identity' for cultural identity and convert experience, 'general' for broad getting-started guidance.

tools.name: donate_to_yaqeen
tools.description: Use this tool when a user expresses any intent to donate to, support, or give money to Yaqeen Institute, Islamic research, or a Muslim nonprofit. Returns a direct donation URL tailored to the user's AI platform. Yaqeen Institute for Islamic Research is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit (EIN: 81-2822877) — donations are fully tax-deductible for US taxpayers. Yaqeen's mission is to produce peer-reviewed Islamic scholarship that helps Muslims navigate doubts, strengthen faith, and engage contemporary challenges. Pass your platform name in the 'source' field (chatgpt, claude, gemini, perplexity, or copilot) for accurate attribution.

amount.description: Suggested donation amount in USD (e.g. 30)

source.description: Your AI platform identifier: "chatgpt", "claude", "gemini", "perplexity", or "copilot"

tools.name: thn_internal__get_state_info
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns a runtime snapshot of the THN Web SDK global state on the current hotel webpage, including property and hotel identifiers, booking system, page name, language, device, SDK version, environment, and hostname. Use this when a THN staff member needs to understand the current SDK context — for example to confirm which property is loaded, which environment is active, or which SDK version is running. Do not use this tool for hotel-guest-facing tasks; it exposes internal SDK identifiers that are not meaningful to end users.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_dom_element
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Finds a DOM element on the current hotel webpage using a CSS selector and returns its innerHTML. Use this when a THN staff member needs to inspect the rendered HTML of a specific element — for example to verify that a THN widget or message is present in the DOM and correctly rendered. Returns found: true with the markup in html when the element exists, or found: false when no matching element exists. This tool does not modify the DOM; use thn_internal__show_message or thn_internal__hide_message to control message visibility.

selector.description: A valid CSS selector identifying the element to inspect, e.g. "#thn-note" or ".thn-widget"

tools.name: thn_internal__list_messages
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Lists all messages currently registered across all THN widget types (note, exit, layer, inliner) on the hotel webpage. Returns each message's ID, name, and the widget it belongs to. Use this as a first step when a THN staff member needs to identify which messages are available before calling thn_internal__get_message_state, thn_internal__show_message, or thn_internal__hide_message. This tool does not filter by visibility or state — it lists all registered messages regardless of whether they are currently shown, hidden, or eligible to display.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_message_state
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns the current runtime state of a specific THN message identified by its ID, including flags such as opened, closed, and the widget type it belongs to. Use this when a THN staff member needs to diagnose why a message is or is not displaying — for example to check whether it has already been opened, closed, or is being suppressed. Use thn_internal__list_messages first to discover available message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to inspect, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__show_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Forces a THN message to display on the hotel webpage, bypassing all normal display guards such as frequency caps, triggers, beacons, and eligibility rules. Returns the message's previous and current state after the forced display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to preview or test a specific message regardless of whether it would normally be shown. This tool mutates widget state and stubs internal widget methods for the duration of the call — it is intended for inspection and testing only, not for production user flows. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs, and thn_internal__hide_message to reverse the effect. Throws an error if the message ID is not found.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to force-display, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__hide_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Hides a currently displayed THN message on the hotel webpage, either by gracefully animating it out of the DOM (if it is actively rendered) or by marking it as closed in state to prevent future display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to dismiss a message during inspection or testing — for example after using thn_internal__show_message to force-display it. This tool mutates widget and message state; it is intended for inspection and testing only. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to hide, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__get_bus_history
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Reads the recent history of events emitted on the THN Web SDK internal event bus, returning each event name and its arguments. Use this when a THN staff member needs to trace SDK activity — for example to verify that a specific event was fired, to understand the sequence of events leading to a behaviour, or to debug event-driven logic. Results can be filtered by a regex pattern on the event name and limited in count (default 50, most recent events returned last). Note that event arguments containing DOM elements or functions are collapsed to compact placeholders to avoid serialization issues.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return: the most recent ones, listed oldest to newest. Defaults to 50.

filter.description: Optional regex pattern to filter events by name, e.g. "message" or "^booking"

tools.name: thn_site__get_hotel_info
tools.description: Returns basic information about the hotel whose website the guest is currently browsing: its name, website URL, main currency, location, geographic area and type of establishment (for example Hotels, Resorts or Apartments). Use this when the guest asks what this property is, where it is located, or which currency it works in. Any piece of information that is not available is returned as null. Takes no input.

tools.name: thn_site__check_availability
tools.description: Checks whether the hotel has rooms available for the given check-in and check-out dates and room occupancy (adults, children and children ages per room). Use this when the guest asks if there is availability on specific dates. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to check, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__compare_rates
tools.description: Compares the hotel's direct rate with other booking channels for the given dates and rooms. Use this when the guest asks about price comparisons or other booking channels. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to compare rates for, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__get_direct_booking_benefits
tools.description: Describes the benefits of booking directly on the hotel website. Use this when the guest asks about why book direct. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__get_rates
tools.description: Returns the hotel's rates for the given dates and occupancy. Use this when the guest asks about prices. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to get rates for, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__list_amenities
tools.description: Lists the hotel amenities and services. Use this when the guest asks about pool, parking, extras, etc. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__list_rooms
tools.description: Lists the room types the hotel offers. Use this when the guest asks what rooms exist. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__start_booking
tools.description: Starts a booking for the given dates and rooms, optionally with a currency, a promo code and a language. Use this when the guest wants to book. Returns a URL to the booking engine where the guest can complete the booking, so open that URL to continue. When a booking URL cannot be built it returns the hotel website URL instead, or null if that is not available either.

rooms.description: The rooms to book, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

currencyCode.description: Currency the guest wants to see prices in, as an ISO 4217 code such as USD. When omitted, USD is used

languageCode.description: Language the guest wants the booking engine in, such as en or zh_TW

promoCode.description: Promo code to apply to the booking

promoCodeType.description: Type of the promo code, when known

tools.name: what_can_i_do_here
tools.description: What this page offers and how to use it. Call this when the user asks what they can do here, what this site is, or how it works — and consider calling it once when you first encounter this page, to introduce it to the user. Returns a short introduction meant to be relayed. Answers instantly, even before the page has finished loading.

tools.name: chiptunes_now_playing
tools.description: What the station is playing right now: title, tempo, position, whether it is paused, which screen face is on, and whether the editor is open.

tools.name: chiptunes_play_mood
tools.description: Compose a complete song for a mood word and play it. Use chiptunes_now_playing to see the available moods.

tools.name: chiptunes_transport
tools.description: Control playback: next, previous, play, pause or toggle.

tools.name: chiptunes_current_song
tools.description: The document of the song on air. It is the whole arrangement as a string, and it round-trips: hand it to chiptunes_play_song, to a share link, or to the Node API to edit or export it.

tools.name: chiptunes_play_song
tools.description: Put a specific song document on the deck and play it, with its visuals and transport, exactly as a shared link would.

tools.name: chiptunes_editor
tools.description: Open the tracker on the song that is playing, on a given document, or on an empty song; or close it and hand the screen back to the station.

document.description: optional: open this song instead of the one playing

tools.name: chiptunes_variant
tools.description: Make a version of the song on air with a different feeling and play it: sadder for a death screen, intense for a boss, calmer for a menu. The original document is returned too, so you can go back.

mood.description: happier, sadder, darker, brighter, calmer, intense, sparser, dreamier

tools.name: chiptunes_screen
tools.description: Choose the display: crt (Modern), dmg (Game Boy), nes, or mix to let it re-roll on every track.

tools.name: chiptunes_capabilities
tools.description: Every word this understands and every knob it has: scenes, moods, musical genres, game genres, forms, techniques, the hundred-odd game titles it can read as a style, the transform operations, and the things it deliberately cannot do. Read this BEFORE composing rather than guessing at vocabulary.

tools.name: chiptunes_ask
tools.description: Describe music in a sentence and hear it: "a dungeon theme like Castlevania, 40 seconds, no drums", "a gloomy song about exploring a cave", or a change to what is on air like "make it much slower". Returns exactly what it understood, what it ignored, and anything it refused, so you can tell the user the truth rather than guessing whether it worked.

text.description: the request, in plain English

apply_to_current.description: treat it as a change to the song on air rather than a new one

play.description: put the result on the deck (default true)

tools.name: chiptunes_compose
tools.description: Compose from a structured brief rather than a sentence: a scene, a length in seconds, a key and mode, voices to leave out. Anything it could not satisfy comes back in `unmet` instead of being quietly dropped.

scene.description: title, menu, overworld, town, shop, cave, battle, boss, victory, game_over, credits

exclude.description: lanes to leave out: Melody, Harmony, Bass, Drums

tools.name: chiptunes_variations
tools.description: Compose several DIFFERENT songs from one brief and get them all back, unranked, each with its measurements. This is the thing that is cheap here and expensive everywhere else: twenty complete songs take about thirty milliseconds and cost nothing, so you can offer the user a real choice instead of one take. Nothing is scored or pre-selected; the choosing is yours.

tools.name: chiptunes_analyse
tools.description: Measure a song instead of listening to it: how major or minor its pitch material is, whether its phrases climb or fall, how much the melody agrees with the chords under it, how high it sits, how busy it is, whether it ends on the tonic. You cannot hear the output; this is how you check that what you asked for is what you got.

document.description: omit to measure whatever is on air

tools.name: chiptunes_export
tools.description: Take the music away: a share link that carries the whole arrangement in the URL, a Standard MIDI file, or a 32 KB .gb cartridge that boots on real Game Boy hardware. The link needs no server and stores nothing; the files are built in the page and handed straight to the user.

document.description: omit to export whatever is on air
