Use this when a THN staff member needs to diagnose why a message is or is not displaying — for example to check whether it has already been opened, closed, or is being suppressed. Use thn_internal__list_messages first to discover available message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to inspect, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__show_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Forces a THN message to display on the hotel webpage, bypassing all normal display guards such as frequency caps, triggers, beacons, and eligibility rules. Returns the message's previous and current state after the forced display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to preview or test a specific message regardless of whether it would normally be shown. This tool mutates widget state and stubs internal widget methods for the duration of the call — it is intended for inspection and testing only, not for production user flows. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs, and thn_internal__hide_message to reverse the effect. Throws an error if the message ID is not found.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to force-display, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__hide_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Hides a currently displayed THN message on the hotel webpage, either by gracefully animating it out of the DOM (if it is actively rendered) or by marking it as closed in state to prevent future display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to dismiss a message during inspection or testing — for example after using thn_internal__show_message to force-display it. This tool mutates widget and message state; it is intended for inspection and testing only. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to hide, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__get_bus_history
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Reads the recent history of events emitted on the THN Web SDK internal event bus, returning each event name and its arguments. Use this when a THN staff member needs to trace SDK activity — for example to verify that a specific event was fired, to understand the sequence of events leading to a behaviour, or to debug event-driven logic. Results can be filtered by a regex pattern on the event name and limited in count (default 50, most recent events returned last). Note that event arguments containing DOM elements or functions are collapsed to compact placeholders to avoid serialization issues.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return: the most recent ones, listed oldest to newest. Defaults to 50.

filter.description: Optional regex pattern to filter events by name, e.g. "message" or "^booking"

tools.name: thn_site__get_hotel_info
tools.description: Returns basic information about the hotel whose website the guest is currently browsing: its name, website URL, main currency, location, geographic area and type of establishment (for example Hotels, Resorts or Apartments). Use this when the guest asks what this property is, where it is located, or which currency it works in. Any piece of information that is not available is returned as null. Takes no input.

tools.name: thn_site__check_availability
tools.description: Checks whether the hotel has rooms available for the given check-in and check-out dates and room occupancy (adults, children and children ages per room). Use this when the guest asks if there is availability on specific dates. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to check, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__compare_rates
tools.description: Compares the hotel's direct rate with other booking channels for the given dates and rooms. Use this when the guest asks about price comparisons or other booking channels. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to compare rates for, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__get_direct_booking_benefits
tools.description: Describes the benefits of booking directly on the hotel website. Use this when the guest asks about why book direct. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__get_rates
tools.description: Returns the hotel's rates for the given dates and occupancy. Use this when the guest asks about prices. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to get rates for, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__list_amenities
tools.description: Lists the hotel amenities and services. Use this when the guest asks about pool, parking, extras, etc. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__list_rooms
tools.description: Lists the room types the hotel offers. Use this when the guest asks what rooms exist. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__start_booking
tools.description: Starts a booking for the given dates and rooms, optionally with a currency, a promo code and a language. Use this when the guest wants to book. Returns a URL to the booking engine where the guest can complete the booking, so open that URL to continue. When a booking URL cannot be built it returns the hotel website URL instead, or null if that is not available either.

rooms.description: The rooms to book, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

currencyCode.description: Currency the guest wants to see prices in, as an ISO 4217 code such as USD. When omitted, USD is used

promoCode.description: Promo code to apply to the booking

tools.name: everaw_check_allergens
tools.description: Check which allergens an Everaw product contains, and whether it is made in a facility that handles nuts. Use this whenever someone asks about nuts, peanuts, allergies or whether a product is safe for an allergic child. Pass a product name, or "all" to list every product. Returns plain text: product name, an allergen line naming tree nuts or peanuts where present, the shared-facility statement, and ingredients. For "all", two named groups plus that statement.

product.description: Product name, or "all" for the whole range.

tools.name: everaw_find_by_dietary_need
tools.description: Find Everaw products matching a dietary requirement: no nuts, no added sugar, vegan, gluten free, or suitable for children. Use this when someone describes a need rather than naming a product, for example "something nut free for my toddler". Returns plain text: for no-nuts the shared-facility caveat comes FIRST, then one line per match as "- Name (price INR): url". Relay the caveat, it qualifies every item listed.

need.description: The dietary requirement to match against.

tools.name: everaw_lab_reports
tools.description: Report whether an Everaw product has been independently laboratory tested, and point to the published reports. Use this when someone asks if the products are tested, verified, third party checked, or whether the published nutrition can be trusted. Pass a product name, or "all" for the range. Returns plain text: whether the product is independently tested, the report date if any, and the URL of the published reports. Says so plainly when none exists.

product.description: Product name, or "all".

tools.name: everaw_product_facts
tools.description: Get the factual details of one Everaw product: ingredients, allergens, net weight, serving size, shelf life and storage. Use this for questions about what is in a product or how long it keeps. Does not cover price or stock, which come from the Shopify catalog tools. Returns plain text, one field per line: name, ingredients, allergens with the facility statement, dietary claims, weight and serving, shelf life, usage, URL.

product.description: Product name.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Product detail parameters.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

value.description: Option value, e.g. "160cm" or "Fiberglass".

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant. To change a quantity or remove something already in the cart, use update_cart_lines instead — this tool can only add.

line_items.description: Items to add (1-10).

item.description: The merchandise to add.

id.description: ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

handle.description: Product handle. Adds the selected or first available variant; call get_product first if the user requested specific options.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: How many to add. Defaults to 1.

tools.name: update_cart_lines
tools.description: Change the quantity of items already in the cart, or remove them. Every change here addresses an existing cart line by its id, so call get_cart first unless you already have line_items[].id from an earlier get_cart in this conversation. Pass the ABSOLUTE target quantity, not a delta — quantity 2 means the line ends up at 2 regardless of what it was. Use quantity 0 to remove the line entirely. Batch every change for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart_lines once per line. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. This tool cannot add new merchandise. To add something not already in the cart, use add_to_cart. To empty the whole cart at once, use cancel_cart.

line_items.description: Existing cart lines to update or remove (1-10).

id.description: Existing cart line id from get_cart line_items[].id. Required — this tool cannot resolve products by name.

quantity.description: Absolute target quantity for this line (not a delta). 0 removes the line.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Remove all items from the cart in one step. Use when the user wants to empty their cart or start over.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Proceed to checkout. Verifies the cart is not empty, then MOVES the browser to the checkout page. The tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: manage_orders
tools.description: Navigate to the customer's order history page. Use when the user asks about past orders, order status, tracking, or returns. The user will be prompted to log in if not already authenticated. This MOVES the browser to the order history page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: search_shop_policies_and_faqs
tools.description:
Used to get facts about the store's policies, FAQ, or contact details.
When the question is about specific policy kinds, set policy_types to those kinds; leave it unset for general FAQ questions.
Some examples of questions you can ask are:
  - What is your return policy? (policy_types: ["refund"])
  - What is your shipping policy? (policy_types: ["shipping"])
  - What is your phone number? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - What are your hours of operation? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - Do you offer gift wrapping? (general FAQ, no specific policy kind — leave policy_types unset)

query.description: A natural language query. Searches FAQ pages and articles, and routes policies by keyword when policy_types is omitted.

policy_types.description: Policy kinds to fetch, chosen from the user's question — e.g. ["refund"] for returns/exchanges, ["contact"] for phone/hours/address. Include every kind the question touches. Omit when no specific policy is relevant (e.g. a general FAQ question).

tools.name: get_map_state
tools.description: Read the current map view: camera (center, zoom, bearing, pitch), the visible bounds, how many features are loaded, the selection, and everything drawn or noted on the map by either side. Every count is exact; the lists are capped (selection.ids at 20, drawings.items and annotations.items at the ten most recent each, annotation notes at 80 characters). features_loaded counts everything searchable, including any point-of-interest category fetched this session, which tier2.loaded names once there is one. Use this instead of a screenshot to know what the map shows. The page keeps its agent chrome hidden until an agent acts, and the human can also open or close that chrome by hand at any time - so bounds always describes the rectangle actually on screen right now: narrowed while the inspector lane is up, full-width while the chrome is closed, and the same rectangle list_features_in_view tests against either way.

tools.name: set_map_view
tools.description: Move the map camera. Give a place name or a feature id to jump to something by name, fit to frame something whole, or center/zoom/bearing/pitch to position the camera directly. place and feature_id fly to the thing at zoom 15, or keep the current zoom when it is already closer than that - going to a place never zooms you out; pass zoom to say otherwise. fit takes a drawing id or a feature id and frames that thing against what is currently on screen: an area (a district, a park, a circle or a route) is fitted so all of it is visible, which can zoom OUT when the thing is bigger than the view, while a target with no extent - a point of interest, a pinned note - behaves exactly like feature_id. fit needs the map to have rendered once; before that it answers "map not ready" rather than guessing how much you can see. Returns the new map state, so no follow-up read is needed.

center.description: Exact camera centre. Cannot be combined with place or feature_id.

zoom.description: Zoom level: 10 shows a city, 15 a neighbourhood, 18 a building. With place or feature_id it defaults to 15 without ever zooming out past the current view - the closer of the two wins - so pass zoom to override, including to pull back. Cannot be combined with fit, which decides its own zoom.

bearing.description: Map rotation in degrees clockwise from north; 0 is north-up.

pitch.description: Camera tilt in degrees; 0 looks straight down.

place.description: Name of a place in the loaded data, e.g. "Daan Station". Station suffixes are optional. If several places match equally well the map does not move and the answer lists candidates to choose from. Like every place name, it needs the base data the page loads on open; before that it answers "map data not ready" rather than guessing, and asking again works.

feature_id.description: Id of a loaded feature, e.g. "osm:node:123". Use this instead of place when you already have an id, or to resolve an ambiguous place.

fit.description: Frame this whole thing: a drawing id as draw_shape returns and map state lists ("drawing:1", including a shape the human drew by hand), or the id of a loaded feature ("district:daan", "osm:way:10"). An area is fitted to what is on screen and may zoom out to get all of it in; a target with no extent behaves exactly like feature_id, at any starting zoom - the two paths share one rule. Cannot be combined with center, place or feature_id, and not with zoom either - the fit is what decides the zoom.

tools.name: list_features_in_view
tools.description: List the loaded features whose bounding box overlaps the current view, nearest to the centre of the view first, each with its distance in metres and an 8-point compass direction from that centre, which comes back as origin. The test is a bounding-box overlap, so a large area counts as in view when any part of it is. This is how you describe what is on screen without taking a screenshot. Pass query to search the screen by text - the same match find_features makes, scoped to what is in view, and combining with categories rather than replacing it, so "which of the cafes on screen is a Louisa?" is one call. Called without categories it also returns category_counts - how many of each category the answer covers, which is the same set features and total describe, so with a query only the features that matched it are counted - and, when there are point-of-interest categories it has not fetched, unsearched_categories with their city-wide totals.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring of the local or English name, brand, cuisine, or address. A result may have matched on a field the list does not echo; get_place_details shows all of a feature's tags. Only the features already in view are searched; omit to list every feature in view. Combines with categories instead of replacing it.

categories.description: Which categories to search. Always in memory: mrt_station, park, school, supermarket, listing, district. Points of interest, fetched for the whole city the first time you name one and kept for the rest of the session: restaurant, cafe, fast_food, bakery, bar, convenience, pharmacy, clinic, hospital, place_of_worship, bank, hotel, parking, bicycle_rental, library, museum, post_office, police. Naming a category is how you search it - there is no way to search all of them at once. Omit this and the search covers the always-in-memory categories plus the points of interest fetched earlier in this session; the answer then lists what it did not search under unsearched_categories, with how many exist city-wide.

limit.description: Maximum number of features to return (default 20, max 100). The "total" field reports how many matched in all.

tools.name: find_features
tools.description: Search every loaded feature, not only the visible ones. Filter by text (name, brand, cuisine or address), category, distance from a place, a feature or a coordinate (up to 10000 m), and by whether a feature is inside a shape on the map - including one the human drew by hand. Results come back nearest first, each with its distance in metres and an 8-point compass direction from that origin, which is echoed as origin - together with radius_m when near or radius_m limited the search. Naming a point-of-interest category (restaurant, cafe, pharmacy and so on) fetches it for the whole city on first use and then searches all of it, wherever the map happens to be pointing; searching without categories answers from what is already loaded and lists the rest under unsearched_categories. With query, the answer also carries unloaded_matches when the same text matches in point-of-interest categories this session has not fetched: {category, count} for each, biggest first, at most 6 of them (unloaded_matches_omitted counts any further ones). This is how a search that returned nothing can still tell you where the matches are - the count is city-wide, matched on the same name, brand, cuisine and address fields this tool matches once a category is loaded, so call find_features again with that category in categories to load it and get the features. Nothing is fetched on your behalf: naming the category is still your call.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring of the local or English name, brand, cuisine, or address. A result may have matched on a field the list does not echo; get_place_details shows all of a feature's tags. Omit to match every name.

categories.description: Which categories to search. Always in memory: mrt_station, park, school, supermarket, listing, district. Points of interest, fetched for the whole city the first time you name one and kept for the rest of the session: restaurant, cafe, fast_food, bakery, bar, convenience, pharmacy, clinic, hospital, place_of_worship, bank, hotel, parking, bicycle_rental, library, museum, post_office, police. Naming a category is how you search it - there is no way to search all of them at once. Omit this and the search covers the always-in-memory categories plus the points of interest fetched earlier in this session; the answer then lists what it did not search under unsearched_categories, with how many exist city-wide.

near.description: Origin for distances and for the radius filter: a feature id returned by an earlier call (e.g. "osm:node:123"), a place name to look up in the loaded data (e.g. "Daan Station"), or an explicit coordinate. Omit to measure from the centre of the current view.

anyOf.description: A feature id, or the name of a station, park or district. A name needs the base data the page loads on open; before that it answers "map data not ready" rather than guessing, and asking again works.
Explicit coordinate.

radius_m.description: Keep only features within this many metres of "near" (default 800 when "near" is given, no radius filter otherwise, at most 10000). A larger radius is refused rather than quietly narrowed. Measured to a feature point, or to the centroid of an area.

within.description: "drawing:<n>" - restrict results to features inside that drawing, as returned by draw_shape or listed in map state under drawings (the ten most recent; drawings.count is the true total). A circle or polygon works; a line has no inside. Combines with the other filters instead of replacing them.

limit.description: Maximum number of features to return (default 20, max 100). The "total" field reports how many matched in all.

tools.name: select_features
tools.description: Highlight features on the map and in the sidebar so a sighted person can see what you are talking about. Pass explicit ids (from find_features, list_features_in_view or describe_surroundings), or the same query/near/radius_m (at most 10000 m)/categories/within filter as find_features — the filter resolves to the same set of features, but unlike find_features it does not stop at the limit: every match is selected, and state.selection.count reports the true number. Pass an empty ids array to clear the selection. Returns the resulting selection and the new map state; selected lists at most 20 of them. A filter that matches more than 500 point-of-interest features is refused rather than highlighting half a city: the answer gives the true count, and near + radius_m, within or query narrows it. On a page opened from a share link whose point-of-interest categories are still loading, the ids that belong to them stay selected and come back in pending_ids instead of selected: they are not lost, and state.tier2.loading names what is still arriving.

ids.description: Feature ids to select, as returned by find_features or list_features_in_view (at most 100; use the filter instead for larger sets). An empty array clears the selection. Ids that are not loaded are reported in unknown_ids instead of failing the call - except while a share link's categories are still loading, where an id they may contain is kept, selected and reported in pending_ids.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring of the local or English name, brand, cuisine, or address. A result may have matched on a field the list does not echo; get_place_details shows all of a feature's tags. Exactly as in find_features.

near.description: Origin for distances and for the radius filter: a feature id returned by an earlier call (e.g. "osm:node:123"), a place name to look up in the loaded data (e.g. "Daan Station"), or an explicit coordinate. Omit to measure from the centre of the current view.

anyOf.description: A feature id, or the name of a station, park or district. A name needs the base data the page loads on open; before that it answers "map data not ready" rather than guessing, and asking again works.
Explicit coordinate.

radius_m.description: Keep only features within this many metres of "near" (default 800 when "near" is given, no radius filter otherwise, at most 10000). A larger radius is refused rather than quietly narrowed. Measured to a feature point, or to the centroid of an area.

within.description: "drawing:<n>" - restrict results to features inside that drawing, as returned by draw_shape or listed in map state under drawings (the ten most recent; drawings.count is the true total). A circle or polygon works; a line has no inside. Combines with the other filters instead of replacing them.

categories.description: Which categories to search. Always in memory: mrt_station, park, school, supermarket, listing, district. Points of interest, fetched for the whole city the first time you name one and kept for the rest of the session: restaurant, cafe, fast_food, bakery, bar, convenience, pharmacy, clinic, hospital, place_of_worship, bank, hotel, parking, bicycle_rental, library, museum, post_office, police. Naming a category is how you search it - there is no way to search all of them at once. Omit this and the search covers the always-in-memory categories plus the points of interest fetched earlier in this session; the answer then lists what it did not search under unsearched_categories, with how many exist city-wide.

replace.description: true (the default) replaces the current selection; false adds to it.

tools.name: draw_shape
tools.description: Draw a circle, a polygon or a line on the map, so the human can see the area you are talking about. A circle takes a centre (a coordinate, a feature id or a place name) and a radius in metres; a polygon and a line take a list of [lng, lat] points. Returns the drawing id plus its area in square metres (circle, polygon) or its length in metres (line), and the new map state. Pass the id to find_features({within}) or select_features({within}) to ask what is inside it. Shapes the human drew by hand appear in the same list with source "user" and can be queried the same way.

type.description: circle: centre plus radius_m. polygon: a closed area from coordinates. line: a route or a measurement from coordinates.

center.description: Circle only: where the circle is centred. A coordinate, a feature id from an earlier call, or a place name such as "Daan Station". If a name matches several places the map is left alone and the answer lists the candidates.

anyOf.description: A feature id, or the name of a station, park or district. A name needs the base data the page loads on open; before that it answers "map data not ready" rather than guessing, and asking again works.
Explicit coordinate.

radius_m.description: Circle only: radius in metres (default 800, a comfortable walk; at most 10000). A larger radius is refused rather than shrunk, so what you draw is always what you asked for.

items.description: One point as [lng, lat] in degrees.

coordinates.description: Polygon or line only: the points, as [lng, lat] pairs. A polygon needs at least 3 distinct points and is closed for you if you do not repeat the first one; a line needs at least 2. At most 500 points.

label.description: Short name shown on the map and in map state, e.g. "10-minute walk" (at most 80 characters).

tools.name: plan_route
tools.description: Plan a walk between two places and draw it on the map as a line the human can see. Walking only: the route is on foot, and there is no driving, cycling or transit profile here. It comes from the OpenStreetMap-based routing service run by FOSSGIS (routing.openstreetmap.de), which is the one thing on this map fetched at the moment you ask: when it cannot answer, nothing is drawn, the map is unchanged and the answer says so plainly rather than guessing a line. Both ends take the same three forms as anywhere else - a coordinate, a feature id from an earlier call, or a place name. Returns the drawing id, the service's own distance in metres and duration in seconds, both ends as it resolved them, and the new map state. What it leaves behind is an ordinary drawing: measure gives its length and remove_from_map takes it off again. A line has no inside, so find_features({within}) and select_features({within}) cannot be asked what is inside a route - measure it for its length, or draw a circle somewhere along it to ask what is near it. A route with more points than the map can redraw is simplified, and simplified says so; distance_m is always the service's figure for the real walk, not the drawn line's.

from.description: Where the walk starts: a coordinate, a feature id such as "osm:node:123", or a place name such as "Daan Station". If a name matches several places nothing is drawn and the answer lists the candidates.

anyOf.description: A feature id, or the name of a station, park or district. A name needs the base data the page loads on open; before that it answers "map data not ready" rather than guessing, and asking again works.
Explicit coordinate.

to.description: Where the walk ends, in any of the same three forms as from.

anyOf.description: A feature id, or the name of a station, park or district. A name needs the base data the page loads on open; before that it answers "map data not ready" rather than guessing, and asking again works.
Explicit coordinate.

label.description: Short name shown on the map and in map state (at most 80 characters). Omit it and the walk is named after the two places, e.g. "walk: 大安 → 台北車站".

tools.name: annotate
tools.description: Pin a short note to a place on the map, so the human sees what you found where you found it. The location can be a coordinate, a feature id from an earlier call, or a place name. Returns the annotation id and the new map state; map state lists notes with their first 80 characters and says whether the agent or the human wrote each one.

at.description: Where to pin the note: a coordinate, a feature id such as "osm:node:123", or a place name such as "Daan Station". If a name matches several places nothing is pinned and the answer lists the candidates.

anyOf.description: A feature id, or the name of a station, park or district. A name needs the base data the page loads on open; before that it answers "map data not ready" rather than guessing, and asking again works.
Explicit coordinate.

note.description: The note itself, at most 500 characters. One or two sentences a human can read on the map, not a paragraph.

icon.description: Optional short marker label or emoji, e.g. "star" (at most 24 characters).

tools.name: remove_from_map
tools.description: Take something off the map: a shape or a note an agent put there, or a feature out of the highlighted selection. Ids come in three forms and can be mixed in one call - "drawing:<n>" and "annotation:<n>", as map state lists them under drawings and annotations, and the id of a currently selected feature such as "osm:node:123". This never deletes map data. Features and places cannot be removed; naming a selected feature only takes it out of the highlight. Taking a shape or a note off the map is permanent: there is no undo, and the only way back is to draw or pin it again. Shapes and notes the human made themselves - source "user" in map state - are not removed: they come back under refused, and the human takes their own mark off by tapping it on the map and pressing Remove. Everything else in the same call still happens. No per-id problem fails the batch: what could not be removed is accounted for by name under refused (with one refused_reason for all of them), not_selected (a loaded feature that was not highlighted, so there was nothing to take out), unknown_ids, and malformed_ids with one malformed_error saying which forms do work. Returns what was removed and the new map state, so no follow-up read is needed.

ids.description: What to take off the map, in any mix of the three forms: "drawing:<n>" for a shape, "annotation:<n>" for a note, or the id of a currently selected feature, which leaves the selection and stays on the map (at most 100; repeats count once). There is no "remove everything": an empty array is refused, and clearing the highlight is select_features({ids: []}).

tools.name: describe_surroundings
tools.description: Describe what is around a point the way a person would say it out loud: the district it is in, and the nearby features grouped by compass direction, nearest first, each with its feature id, name and distance in metres. Pass an id straight to select_features or set_map_view to act on something you just described. Use this to answer "what is around me?" or "what is near this listing?" without a screenshot. When from named an id or a place, name is the place it resolved to, so you can check it is the one you meant. total is how many features are inside radius_m, returned is how many are described (at most 30, the nearest ones): when total is larger, narrow radius_m or use find_features with a category filter - widening the radius will not reveal the ones that were left out.

from.description: Where to look from: a coordinate, a feature id from an earlier call, or a place name. Omit to describe the surroundings of the centre of the current view.

anyOf.description: A feature id, or the name of a station, park or district. A name needs the base data the page loads on open; before that it answers "map data not ready" rather than guessing, and asking again works.
Explicit coordinate.

radius_m.description: How far to look, in metres (default 500, roughly a five-minute walk; at most 10000).

categories.description: Which categories to describe. Always in memory: mrt_station, park, school, supermarket, listing, district. Points of interest, fetched for the whole city the first time you name one and kept for the rest of the session: restaurant, cafe, fast_food, bakery, bar, convenience, pharmacy, clinic, hospital, place_of_worship, bank, hotel, parking, bicycle_rental, library, museum, post_office, police. Naming a category is how you search it - there is no way to search all of them at once. Omit this and the answer describes mrt_station, park, school, supermarket, listing plus the points of interest fetched earlier in this session, and lists what it did not describe under unsearched_categories with how many exist city-wide; district is never described, because the district you are standing in is its own field.

tools.name: compare_areas
tools.description: Compare two places in one call: how many features of each category are within radius_m of a, how many are within radius_m of b, and the nearest one of each category on each side. Both places are given the same way as anywhere else - a feature id, a place name such as "Zhongshan Station", or a coordinate - and both are counted with exactly the filter find_features uses, so the numbers match what a per-category search would return. Read "summary" out; use by_category to reason and its feature ids to act (select_features, set_map_view). A point of interest tagged as two categories - a bakery that also serves fast food - is counted under each of them, exactly as both of their find_features queries return it, so by_category can add up to slightly more than total, which counts places. This replaces one find_features call per category per place.

a.description: The first place: a feature id from an earlier call, a place name such as "Daan Park Station", or an explicit coordinate. If a name matches several places nothing is counted and the answer lists the candidates.

anyOf.description: A feature id, or the name of a station, park or district. A name needs the base data the page loads on open; before that it answers "map data not ready" rather than guessing, and asking again works.
Explicit coordinate.

b.description: The second place, in any of the same three forms as a.

anyOf.description: A feature id, or the name of a station, park or district. A name needs the base data the page loads on open; before that it answers "map data not ready" rather than guessing, and asking again works.
Explicit coordinate.

radius_m.description: How far around each place to count, in metres (default 800, a comfortable walk; at most 10000). The same radius is used on both sides - that is what makes the two counts comparable. A larger radius is refused rather than quietly narrowed.

categories.description: Which categories to count. Always in memory: mrt_station, park, school, supermarket, listing, district. Points of interest, fetched for the whole city the first time you name one and kept for the rest of the session: restaurant, cafe, fast_food, bakery, bar, convenience, pharmacy, clinic, hospital, place_of_worship, bank, hotel, parking, bicycle_rental, library, museum, post_office, police. Naming a category is how you search it - there is no way to search all of them at once. Omit this and the answer counts mrt_station, park, school, supermarket, listing plus the points of interest fetched earlier in this session, and lists what it did not count under unsearched_categories with how many exist city-wide; district is never counted, because it is a property of a place rather than something near it.

tools.name: measure
tools.description: Measure one thing on the map and get whole metres back: a shape drawn by you or by the human ("drawing:1", the ids map state lists under drawings), or a loaded feature (an id from find_features, list_features_in_view or describe_surroundings). A line answers with length_m; a circle or a polygon with area_m2 and perimeter_m. A point has a location but no extent, so measuring one is refused - ask find_features for distances instead.

target.description: What to measure: a drawing id such as "drawing:1" (yours or the human's) or a feature id such as "osm:way:123". Names are not accepted; look the place up with find_features first and pass the id it returns.

tools.name: get_place_details
tools.description: Everything this map holds about one place, for the questions a list answer is too lean to carry: opening hours, phone, address, website, wheelchair, and whatever its kind of place is tagged with - a hotel's star rating, a car park's fee and capacity, a pharmacy's dispensing, a place of worship's religion and denomination, a hospital's emergency department. Takes one feature id per call, as returned by find_features, list_features_in_view, describe_surroundings or select_features: those answer with a name, a category and a distance for many places, and this answers with one place in full, including its coordinate and every category it is tagged in. Every field comes from OpenStreetMap and exists only where a contributor entered it, so a field that is absent means nobody has recorded it - not that the place has none; say it that way round, and expect most places to carry only some of them. "wheelchair" is the OSM tag as tagged (yes, no or limited): report it as what OpenStreetMap says, never as a verified accessibility claim, and tell the human to ring ahead if it matters. Shapes and notes on the map are not places - use measure for a drawing's size and get_map_state for what is drawn or noted.

id.description: The feature id to look up, e.g. "osm:node:123" - one per call, exactly as an earlier answer spelled it. A point-of-interest id only resolves once its category has been loaded, which is what naming that category in find_features or select_features does.

tools.name: get_share_link
tools.description: Build a link that reproduces this map for whoever opens it: the camera, the selection, every shape and every note, plus the names of any point-of-interest categories loaded this session so the other side loads the same data and the selected places resolve there too, all encoded in the URL itself. Nothing is uploaded and no account is needed - the state travels inside the link, so the person who opens it sees the map you are looking at now, with the human's own drawings still marked as theirs. Give the URL to the human as a URL, so they can send it on. Returns the url and its size in bytes. A map carrying very large hand-drawn shapes can exceed the byte limit a URL has to stay under; then there is no url, only an error saying what to remove. If "omitted" comes back, that many shapes or notes could not be encoded and are not in the link - say so rather than promising a complete map.

tools.name: add_note
tools.description: Pin a note to the current map centre

note.description: e.g. quiet street, good light

tools.description: Search vanity phone numbers that spell a keyword. Public, no login. Returns local numbers near the zip (or the visitor's location) and toll-free numbers, each with e164, display, kind and available_now. Empty results include keyword suggestions.

keyword.description: 2-7 letters or digits the number should spell, e.g. CASA

zip.description: US zip code for local numbers; omit to use the visitor's location

region.description: US (default) or PR for Puerto Rico

show_all.description: Return every match instead of the first five

tools.name: get_quote
tools.description: Price a specific number before buying. Public. Returns total_cents, next_charge_on and the quote_token that purchase_number requires. Show the customer the total and the terms_url before purchasing.

keyword.description: The keyword, for the display form

tools.name: get_plan_info

tools.name: request_login_code

tools.name: verify_login_code

tools.name: logout
tools.description: Log the customer out of this browser.

tools.name: get_account_status
tools.description: Requires login. The customer's card on file, their numbers with status and renewal dates, failed payments with retry dates, and card_url for adding a card.

tools.name: purchase_number
tools.description: SENSITIVE: charges the customer and activates the number. Requires login, a quote_token and total_cents from get_quote, accept_terms true and confirm true after the customer said yes to that exact charge. Pays with payment_token (a Stripe shared payment token from the customer's agent wallet) when given, otherwise the card on file; with neither, returns card_required with a card_url for the customer. A wallet-paid number has no card on file: the response says the date a card is needed by. requires_action means the bank wants the customer to authenticate: open handoff_url, then call again with attempt_id.

total_cents.description: The total the customer agreed to, from get_quote

accept_terms.description: true once the customer accepted the terms at terms_url

confirm.description: true once the customer said yes to this exact charge

payment_token.description: Optional Stripe shared payment token (spt_...) from the customer's agent wallet

attempt_id.description: Only when resuming a requires_action or processing result

tools.name: list_numbers

tools.name: get_number

tools.name: set_forwarding

forward_calls_to.description: Phone number that should ring, e.g. (305) 555-0134

tools.name: cancel_number

confirm.description: true once the customer confirmed the cancellation

tools.name: reactivate_number

tools.name: get_receipt

tools.name: thn_internal__get_state_info
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns a runtime snapshot of the THN Web SDK global state on the current hotel webpage, including property and hotel identifiers, booking system, page name, language, device, SDK version, environment, and hostname. Use this when a THN staff member needs to understand the current SDK context — for example to confirm which property is loaded, which environment is active, or which SDK version is running. Do not use this tool for hotel-guest-facing tasks; it exposes internal SDK identifiers that are not meaningful to end users.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_dom_element
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Finds a DOM element on the current hotel webpage using a CSS selector and returns its innerHTML. Use this when a THN staff member needs to inspect the rendered HTML of a specific element — for example to verify that a THN widget or message is present in the DOM and correctly rendered. Returns found: true with the markup in html when the element exists, or found: false when no matching element exists. This tool does not modify the DOM; use thn_internal__show_message or thn_internal__hide_message to control message visibility.

selector.description: A valid CSS selector identifying the element to inspect, e.g. "#thn-note" or ".thn-widget"

tools.name: thn_internal__list_messages
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Lists all messages currently registered across all THN widget types (note, exit, layer, inliner) on the hotel webpage. Returns each message's ID, name, and the widget it belongs to. Use this as a first step when a THN staff member needs to identify which messages are available before calling thn_internal__get_message_state, thn_internal__show_message, or thn_internal__hide_message. This tool does not filter by visibility or state — it lists all registered messages regardless of whether they are currently shown, hidden, or eligible to display.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_message_state
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns the current runtime state of a specific THN message identified by its ID, including flags such as opened, closed, and the widget type it belongs to. Use this when a THN staff member needs to diagnose why a message is or is not displaying — for example to check whether it has already been opened, closed, or is being suppressed. Use thn_internal__list_messages first to discover available message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to inspect, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__show_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Forces a THN message to display on the hotel webpage, bypassing all normal display guards such as frequency caps, triggers, beacons, and eligibility rules. Returns the message's previous and current state after the forced display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to preview or test a specific message regardless of whether it would normally be shown. This tool mutates widget state and stubs internal widget methods for the duration of the call — it is intended for inspection and testing only, not for production user flows. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs, and thn_internal__hide_message to reverse the effect. Throws an error if the message ID is not found.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to force-display, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__hide_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Hides a currently displayed THN message on the hotel webpage, either by gracefully animating it out of the DOM (if it is actively rendered) or by marking it as closed in state to prevent future display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to dismiss a message during inspection or testing — for example after using thn_internal__show_message to force-display it. This tool mutates widget and message state; it is intended for inspection and testing only. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to hide, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__get_bus_history
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Reads the recent history of events emitted on the THN Web SDK internal event bus, returning each event name and its arguments. Use this when a THN staff member needs to trace SDK activity — for example to verify that a specific event was fired, to understand the sequence of events leading to a behaviour, or to debug event-driven logic. Results can be filtered by a regex pattern on the event name and limited in count (default 50, most recent events returned last). Note that event arguments containing DOM elements or functions are collapsed to compact placeholders to avoid serialization issues.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return: the most recent ones, listed oldest to newest. Defaults to 50.

filter.description: Optional regex pattern to filter events by name, e.g. "message" or "^booking"

tools.name: thn_site__get_hotel_info
tools.description: Returns basic information about the hotel whose website the guest is currently browsing: its name, website URL, main currency, location, geographic area and type of establishment (for example Hotels, Resorts or Apartments). Use this when the guest asks what this property is, where it is located, or which currency it works in. Any piece of information that is not available is returned as null. Takes no input.

tools.name: thn_site__check_availability
tools.description: Checks whether the hotel has rooms available for the given check-in and check-out dates and room occupancy (adults, children and children ages per room). Use this when the guest asks if there is availability on specific dates. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to check, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__compare_rates
tools.description: Compares the hotel's direct rate with other booking channels for the given dates and rooms. Use this when the guest asks about price comparisons or other booking channels. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to compare rates for, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__get_direct_booking_benefits
tools.description: Describes the benefits of booking directly on the hotel website. Use this when the guest asks about why book direct. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__get_rates
tools.description: Returns the hotel's rates for the given dates and occupancy. Use this when the guest asks about prices. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to get rates for, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__list_amenities
tools.description: Lists the hotel amenities and services. Use this when the guest asks about pool, parking, extras, etc. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__list_rooms
tools.description: Lists the room types the hotel offers. Use this when the guest asks what rooms exist. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__start_booking
tools.description: Starts a booking for the given dates and rooms, optionally with a currency, a promo code and a language. Use this when the guest wants to book. Returns a URL to the booking engine where the guest can complete the booking, so open that URL to continue. When a booking URL cannot be built it returns the hotel website URL instead, or null if that is not available either.

rooms.description: The rooms to book, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

currencyCode.description: Currency the guest wants to see prices in, as an ISO 4217 code such as USD. When omitted, USD is used

languageCode.description: Language the guest wants the booking engine in, such as en or zh_TW

promoCode.description: Promo code to apply to the booking

promoCodeType.description: Type of the promo code, when known

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: Use this read-only tool at the start of a HANDOFF session to inspect the live case queue, unread flags, severity, status, and refund state. Do not use it to change a case or infer full case details; call get_case for a specific case before acting.

tools.name: get_case
tools.description: Use this read-only tool first for the judge demo case: call get_case with case_id CASE-1042, then draft_customer_reply with tone apologetic, then propose_refund with amount_usd 2388, then issue_refund, then send_customer_reply. Do not use it to modify state; choose an update or proposal tool for changes.

tools.name: update_case_status
tools.description: Use this tool to update a case workflow status after you have enough context and can explain why in a note. Do not use it for money movement, sending customer replies, on-call paging, or resolving a gated case; those have dedicated approval tools.

status.description: New case status.

note.description: Short operational note explaining why the status changed.

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description: Use this tool to add an agent-authored note to the current case timeline for human review. Public-to-customer visibility means the note is customer-visible context only; it never sends a customer message. Do not use this tool to send replies or change money state.

body.description: Comment body to add to the timeline.

visibility.description: Whether this is internal context or a customer-visible note. Neither option sends a reply.

tools.name: draft_customer_reply
tools.description: Use this tool after get_case for CASE-1042 to create or replace a visible customer reply draft. For the judge demo, pass tone apologetic and a goal that apologizes for the duplicate charge and explains the refund path; then call propose_refund with amount_usd 2388. This tool does not send anything.

goal.description: Goal for the reply, such as apologize and explain the refund path.

tools.name: send_customer_reply
tools.description: Use this destructive tool at the end of the judge sequence after get_case, draft_customer_reply, propose_refund, and issue_refund have completed. Do not call it before a draft exists or before refund approval is complete. It opens a visible human approval gate and waits for Jordan; no customer reply is sent unless Jordan approves.

tools.name: propose_refund
tools.description: Use this tool after drafting the CASE-1042 customer reply to propose amount_usd 2388 for the duplicate Pro Annual charge. It creates a visible pending approval and does not move money by itself; then call issue_refund to open the human approval gate.

amount_usd.description: Refund amount in USD. For CASE-1042 use 2388.

reason.description: Operational reason for the proposed refund.

tools.name: issue_refund
tools.description: Use this destructive tool after propose_refund in the judge sequence for CASE-1042. Do not call it before a refund has been proposed. It opens a visible 'Refund $2,388 to Maya Chen?' approval gate and waits for Jordan; the refund state does not change to issued unless Jordan approves. After approval, call send_customer_reply.

tools.name: page_oncall
tools.description: Use this destructive tool only when billing-primary or incident response needs to be interrupted for the case. It requests human approval and does not page until approved. Do not use it for routine notes, status changes, or customer replies.

message.description: Concise page message for billing-primary.

tools.name: list_pending_approvals
tools.description: Use this read-only tool to inspect all pending human approval gates across HANDOFF. Do not use it to approve, reject, or apply side effects; the human must approve in the UI.

tools.name: resolve_case
tools.description: Use this destructive tool only when the case is truly ready to close and you can provide a concise resolution summary. It requires human approval and refuses to resolve a P1 with an unissued requested refund pending. Do not use it while customer, refund, or on-call work remains unresolved.

resolution_summary.description: Short summary of the final resolution.

tools.name: get_session
tools.description: Use this read-only tool to inspect the live agent session for CASE-1042: session id, owner, watchers, status, elapsed time, agent state, and current plan step. Use it before redirect_agent or handoff_session so you know who is steering.

tools.name: list_watchers
tools.description: Use this read-only tool to list teammates watching SES-1042 without changing ownership. If Sam is absent, the human can click Join as Sam or the session can later be handed off to Sam.

tools.name: redirect_agent

instruction.description: Short steering instruction for the live agent session.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_state_info
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns a runtime snapshot of the THN Web SDK global state on the current hotel webpage, including property and hotel identifiers, booking system, page name, language, device, SDK version, environment, and hostname. Use this when a THN staff member needs to understand the current SDK context — for example to confirm which property is loaded, which environment is active, or which SDK version is running. Do not use this tool for hotel-guest-facing tasks; it exposes internal SDK identifiers that are not meaningful to end users.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_dom_element
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Finds a DOM element on the current hotel webpage using a CSS selector and returns its innerHTML. Use this when a THN staff member needs to inspect the rendered HTML of a specific element — for example to verify that a THN widget or message is present in the DOM and correctly rendered. Returns found: true with the markup in html when the element exists, or found: false when no matching element exists. This tool does not modify the DOM; use thn_internal__show_message or thn_internal__hide_message to control message visibility.

selector.description: A valid CSS selector identifying the element to inspect, e.g. "#thn-note" or ".thn-widget"

tools.name: thn_internal__list_messages
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Lists all messages currently registered across all THN widget types (note, exit, layer, inliner) on the hotel webpage. Returns each message's ID, name, and the widget it belongs to. Use this as a first step when a THN staff member needs to identify which messages are available before calling thn_internal__get_message_state, thn_internal__show_message, or thn_internal__hide_message. This tool does not filter by visibility or state — it lists all registered messages regardless of whether they are currently shown, hidden, or eligible to display.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_message_state
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns the current runtime state of a specific THN message identified by its ID, including flags such as opened, closed, and the widget type it belongs to. Use this when a THN staff member needs to diagnose why a message is or is not displaying — for example to check whether it has already been opened, closed, or is being suppressed. Use thn_internal__list_messages first to discover available message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to inspect, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__show_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Forces a THN message to display on the hotel webpage, bypassing all normal display guards such as frequency caps, triggers, beacons, and eligibility rules. Returns the message's previous and current state after the forced display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to preview or test a specific message regardless of whether it would normally be shown. This tool mutates widget state and stubs internal widget methods for the duration of the call — it is intended for inspection and testing only, not for production user flows. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs, and thn_internal__hide_message to reverse the effect. Throws an error if the message ID is not found.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to force-display, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__hide_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Hides a currently displayed THN message on the hotel webpage, either by gracefully animating it out of the DOM (if it is actively rendered) or by marking it as closed in state to prevent future display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to dismiss a message during inspection or testing — for example after using thn_internal__show_message to force-display it. This tool mutates widget and message state; it is intended for inspection and testing only. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to hide, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__get_bus_history
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Reads the recent history of events emitted on the THN Web SDK internal event bus, returning each event name and its arguments. Use this when a THN staff member needs to trace SDK activity — for example to verify that a specific event was fired, to understand the sequence of events leading to a behaviour, or to debug event-driven logic. Results can be filtered by a regex pattern on the event name and limited in count (default 50, most recent events returned last). Note that event arguments containing DOM elements or functions are collapsed to compact placeholders to avoid serialization issues.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return: the most recent ones, listed oldest to newest. Defaults to 50.

filter.description: Optional regex pattern to filter events by name, e.g. "message" or "^booking"

tools.name: thn_site__get_hotel_info
tools.description: Returns basic information about the hotel whose website the guest is currently browsing: its name, website URL, main currency, location, geographic area and type of establishment (for example Hotels, Resorts or Apartments). Use this when the guest asks what this property is, where it is located, or which currency it works in. Any piece of information that is not available is returned as null. Takes no input.

tools.name: thn_site__check_availability
tools.description: Checks whether the hotel has rooms available for the given check-in and check-out dates and room occupancy (adults, children and children ages per room). Use this when the guest asks if there is availability on specific dates. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to check, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__compare_rates
tools.description: Compares the hotel's direct rate with other booking channels for the given dates and rooms. Use this when the guest asks about price comparisons or other booking channels. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to compare rates for, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__get_direct_booking_benefits
tools.description: Describes the benefits of booking directly on the hotel website. Use this when the guest asks about why book direct. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__get_rates
tools.description: Returns the hotel's rates for the given dates and occupancy. Use this when the guest asks about prices. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to get rates for, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__list_amenities
tools.description: Lists the hotel amenities and services. Use this when the guest asks about pool, parking, extras, etc. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__list_rooms
tools.description: Lists the room types the hotel offers. Use this when the guest asks what rooms exist. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__start_booking
tools.description: Starts a booking for the given dates and rooms, optionally with a currency, a promo code and a language. Use this when the guest wants to book. Returns a URL to the booking engine where the guest can complete the booking, so open that URL to continue. When a booking URL cannot be built it returns the hotel website URL instead, or null if that is not available either.

rooms.description: The rooms to book, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

languageCode.description: Language the guest wants the booking engine in, such as en or zh_TW

promoCode.description: Promo code to apply to the booking

promoCodeType.description: Type of the promo code, when known

tools.name: list_tools
tools.description: List every audio tool on this site with what it does and the agent action it exposes. Call this first to choose the right page for a request, then open_tool to go there. Read-only.

tools.name: open_tool
tools.description: Open one of this site's tools by slug, e.g. "silence-remover". The page navigates after replying; that page then registers its own tools, so call inspect_audio there. Audio already loaded on the current page is not carried over: use send_to_tool for that.

tools.name: inspect_audio
tools.description: Call this first. Read derived facts about the audio loaded on this page: whether a file is loaded, its duration, channels and sample rate, the current selection, every visible setting and the export format. Never returns audio samples or file contents.

tools.name: set_output_format
tools.description: Choose the download format shown in the export bar, and optionally the bitrate for lossy formats. Changes a visible control only; nothing is rendered or saved.

format.description: Output format id.

bitrateKbps.description: Bitrate for lossy formats, in kbps.

tools.name: render_preview
tools.description: Render the result of the current settings locally and show it as a listenable player below the controls. Does not download, upload or replace the original.

tools.name: export_download
tools.description: Finish the job: render the result with the current settings and start a browser download of the edited audio. This saves a file on the device, so call it only after the person has asked for the export or the trimmed file.

format.description: Download format. Default: the format shown in the export bar.

tools.name: send_to_tool
tools.description: Hand the audio on this page to another tool on this site and open it there, with no re-upload. Sends the result of the current settings, rendered losslessly; take "original" sends the file as it was loaded. Slugs come from list_tools. The page navigates after replying; call inspect_audio on the new page.

slug.description: The tool to open next, e.g. "silence-remover".

take.description: What to send. Default: result.

tools.name: load_audio_from_url
tools.description: Open an audio file by URL on this page, as if the person had chosen it: a public https:// URL, a data: URL, or an http://localhost URL served on this machine (an agent with a shell can serve a file the person attached and load it here). The browser fetches it and it stays in the tab. The server must allow cross-origin reads. Otherwise ask the person to choose the file.

url.description: https:// or data: URL of an audio file.

tools.name: set_selection
tools.description: Move the selection handles on the waveform, in seconds from the start of the file. The page clamps the values to the file.

tools.name: set_trim
tools.description: Trim, cut or clip the loaded audio: set the start and end of the selection in seconds, whether to keep that selection or cut it out and join the rest, and whether to fade the new edges. Example: the first 30 seconds is startSec 0, endSec 30, mode keep. Moves the visible controls only; nothing is saved until export_download is called.

startSec.description: Selection start, in seconds from the start of the file.

endSec.description: Selection end, in seconds from the start of the file.

mode.description: "keep" exports only the selection; "cut" removes it and joins the rest.

fade.description: Fade the new edges for 20 ms so a cut never clicks.

tools.name: set_join_gap
tools.description: Set the silent gap in seconds inserted between each pair of files, 0 to 5. Zero joins them with no space at all. The run bar and the total length update at once; nothing is saved until export_download is called.

gapSec.description: Digital silence between tracks, in seconds, 0 to 5. About 2 reads as an album gap; 0 suits segments of one continuous recording.

tools.name: set_split
tools.description: Choose where the cuts go: a fixed number of equal parts, a fixed length for every part, or one cut in the middle of each silent gap. Each method reads only its own knobs. The cut markers on the waveform and the plan text update at once; nothing is saved until export_download is called, which downloads one file per part.

method.description: "equal" splits into a fixed number of parts; "length" makes every part a fixed length with a shorter remainder at the end; "silence" cuts at every gap quieter than the threshold.

parts.description: Number of equal parts for the equal method, 2 to 40.

partLengthSec.description: Length of each part in seconds for the length method, 5 to 900 in steps of 5.

silenceThresholdDbfs.description: Audio below this level in dBFS counts as silence for the silence method, -70 to -20. Room tone sits near -50, so -45 catches it.

minimumGapSec.description: A gap must last at least this many seconds to earn a cut, 0.3 to 5.

tools.name: set_silence_removal
tools.description: Set how quiet gaps are detected and removed: the silence threshold in dBFS, the shortest gap that counts, and the padding kept on each side of a cut. The report under the sliders and the highlights on the waveform update at once; nothing is saved.

threshold.description: Audio below this level, in dBFS, counts as silence. -70 to -20.

minimumGapSec.description: Ignore gaps shorter than this many seconds. 0.1 to 3.

paddingSec.description: Seconds of quiet kept on each side of a cut. 0 to 0.5.
