Use this when a THN staff member needs to inspect the rendered HTML of a specific element — for example to verify that a THN widget or message is present in the DOM and correctly rendered. Returns found: true with the markup in html when the element exists, or found: false when no matching element exists. This tool does not modify the DOM; use thn_internal__show_message or thn_internal__hide_message to control message visibility.

selector.description: A valid CSS selector identifying the element to inspect, e.g. "#thn-note" or ".thn-widget"

tools.name: thn_internal__list_messages
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Lists all messages currently registered across all THN widget types (note, exit, layer, inliner) on the hotel webpage. Returns each message's ID, name, and the widget it belongs to. Use this as a first step when a THN staff member needs to identify which messages are available before calling thn_internal__get_message_state, thn_internal__show_message, or thn_internal__hide_message. This tool does not filter by visibility or state — it lists all registered messages regardless of whether they are currently shown, hidden, or eligible to display.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_message_state
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns the current runtime state of a specific THN message identified by its ID, including flags such as opened, closed, and the widget type it belongs to. Use this when a THN staff member needs to diagnose why a message is or is not displaying — for example to check whether it has already been opened, closed, or is being suppressed. Use thn_internal__list_messages first to discover available message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to inspect, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__show_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Forces a THN message to display on the hotel webpage, bypassing all normal display guards such as frequency caps, triggers, beacons, and eligibility rules. Returns the message's previous and current state after the forced display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to preview or test a specific message regardless of whether it would normally be shown. This tool mutates widget state and stubs internal widget methods for the duration of the call — it is intended for inspection and testing only, not for production user flows. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs, and thn_internal__hide_message to reverse the effect. Throws an error if the message ID is not found.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to force-display, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__hide_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Hides a currently displayed THN message on the hotel webpage, either by gracefully animating it out of the DOM (if it is actively rendered) or by marking it as closed in state to prevent future display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to dismiss a message during inspection or testing — for example after using thn_internal__show_message to force-display it. This tool mutates widget and message state; it is intended for inspection and testing only. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to hide, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__get_bus_history
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Reads the recent history of events emitted on the THN Web SDK internal event bus, returning each event name and its arguments. Use this when a THN staff member needs to trace SDK activity — for example to verify that a specific event was fired, to understand the sequence of events leading to a behaviour, or to debug event-driven logic. Results can be filtered by a regex pattern on the event name and limited in count (default 50, most recent events returned last). Note that event arguments containing DOM elements or functions are collapsed to compact placeholders to avoid serialization issues.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return: the most recent ones, listed oldest to newest. Defaults to 50.

filter.description: Optional regex pattern to filter events by name, e.g. "message" or "^booking"

Use this when the guest asks what this property is, where it is located, or which currency it works in. Any piece of information that is not available is returned as null. Takes no input.

tools.name: get_wizard_state
tools.description: Where the "New document" wizard is: current step, selected template, what is still missing before a document can be created, server validation errors, the amount due (billing templates) and the created document if any. Call this first and after changes.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: Lists the document templates the server offers (id, label, shortLabel, category, description, sampleUrl).

tools.name: get_template_schema
tools.description: Returns the JSON Schema of a template (defaults to the selected one): fields, types, enums, required lists and layout hints. Branding (organization) is resolved by the server and is not part of it.

tools.name: get_form_values
tools.description: Returns the current form values: `form` as typed so far, and `payload` as it would be sent to the API.

tools.name: validate_form
tools.description: Checks the form against the template schema and the required owner ids. Returns the list of missing fields (empty means ready to create).

tools.name: get_preview_status
tools.description: Status of the live PDF preview: loading, ready, page count, and the last error. `hints` lists fields the server replaced with placeholders because their value was invalid.

tools.name: select_template
tools.description: Selects a template (see list_templates), loads its schema and applies defaults. Resets previously entered values.

tools.name: go_to_step
tools.description: Navigates the wizard. Steps: template, details, review. The router may redirect (e.g. review needs a created document).

tools.name: set_fields
tools.description: Sets form fields in one call, all or nothing. Keys are dotted paths from the template schema (list rows by index), values are strings, numbers or booleans. Example: {"recipient.name":"Chai Theory","project.deliverables.0.rate":120000,"financials.isDiscountPercentage":true}. Use add_row first for new list rows.

tools.name: add_row
tools.description: Appends an empty row to a list in the form (e.g. path "project.deliverables" for another service, or a list of points).

tools.name: remove_row
tools.description: Removes a row from a list in the form by index. The last remaining row cannot be removed.

tools.name: set_organization
tools.description: Sets the organisation profile (Brand step). "id" picks the server's branding preset; any other field you set overrides that preset on the generated PDF (untouched fields keep the preset's values) and is cached on this device. Keys: id, name, legalName, entityType, pan, gstin, primary, accent, font, contactEmail, billingEmail, phone, whatsapp, address, tradeRelationship, foundedYear, website, instagram, facebook, linkedin, youtube.

tools.name: set_owner_ids
tools.description: Sets the Notion ids the API requires when saving: userId and contactId (required), projectId (optional).

tools.name: create_document
tools.description: Creates the PDF and saves it as a document in Notion. This has a real side effect, so the user is asked to confirm first. Requires validate_form to report no problems.

tools.name: reset_wizard
tools.description: Clears the template, form values and created document and returns to the first step.

tools.description: What roamflat is and how the Flat works, in the shop's own words: speeds, networks, when the days start, delivery, payment, refund policy, adding days, My Flat, e-mails, app, devices, support. Use for any question that is not a price. Answer from the returned facts in the shop’s own words; do not add refund windows, speeds or rules that are not returned.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

tools.name: list_destinations
tools.description: Every country roamflat builds a Flat for, with the number of networks, whether 5G (and so 25/50 Mbps) is available, and the starting price per day (5 Mbps, cheapest network). Use to check coverage or compare countries. from_price_per_day is a per-day starting point (5 Mbps, cheapest network) for comparing countries - call quote_flat for the trip the customer actually wants.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: get_flats
tools.description: The networks of one country (operator, 5G) and the Flats built from them — each Flat with the networks it includes and the price for every speed for the given days (null = that speed needs a 5G network). Use to explain the choice between networks and speeds. Each Flat includes its network and every cheaper one; prices[speed] is the full price for the days given, null = that speed needs a 5G network. Never invent coverage or operators.

destination.description: Country in ANY language or its ISO code, e.g. "Japan", "Japon", "jp". Map a city to its country first. One country per Flat.

tools.name: quote_flat
tools.description: Use while the customer is still deciding — "how much is …?": the exact price of one configuration (country, speed, days and optionally which Flat / networks), the server price the customer would pay. Quote it as returned, never compute or scale it yourself. The result carries a buy_url for reference; when the customer says they want to buy, call start_checkout instead. price is the FULL amount of exactly this configuration for the days asked (price_basis total); quote it as returned and never compute or scale it - price_per_day is for comparison only. Every speed is unlimited data at that speed; never say "unlimited speed". networks lists the operators exactly as returned.

destination.description: Country in ANY language or its ISO code, e.g. "Japan", "Japon", "jp". Map a city to its country first. One country per Flat.

mbps.description: Maximum speed in Mbps (5, 10, 25, 50; default 5). Data is unlimited at that speed. 25 Mbps and up need a 5G network.

flat.description: Optional: which Flat of the country, as get_flats numbers them. Omit = the cheapest Flat that allows the speed.

networks.description: Optional: operator names from get_flats that must be included (the cheapest Flat holding all of them is used). Ignored when flat is given.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: price_grid
tools.description: Prices for several speed × days combinations of one Flat in one call (up to 8 day values; speeds default to all), e.g. to compare with other providers or to find the best fit. Same server prices as quote_flat. Every row is the full price of that speed x days combination; present the rows as a table with the currency, never derive other figures. A row with price null names its reason (e.g. needs a 5G network). Use the buy_url of each row exactly.

destination.description: Country in ANY language or its ISO code, e.g. "Japan", "Japon", "jp". Map a city to its country first. One country per Flat.

flat.description: Optional: which Flat of the country, as get_flats numbers them. Omit = the cheapest Flat that allows the speed.

networks.description: Optional: operator names from get_flats that must be included (the cheapest Flat holding all of them is used). Ignored when flat is given.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: recommend_config
tools.description: Use when the customer describes the trip instead of a speed: country (or up to 5), days and what will be connected (devices: phone, phone_laptop, small_group, family, creator_posting, creator_live, creator_hd_live, creator_pro). Picks the speed from the roamflat speed guide and returns it server-quoted together with the step below and the step above (where offered), each with price, networks, a one-line reason and its buy_url, plus trip totals and an optional budget check. A speed that needs 5G in a country without 5G falls back to the highest speed there and says so. Prices are the same as quote_flat. Give destination (one country) or destinations (several) — one of the two is required; a call without a country fails with invalid_argument.

destination.description: Country in ANY language or its ISO code, e.g. "Japan", "Japon", "jp". Map a city to its country first. One country per Flat. Required unless destinations is given.

destinations.description: Several countries (max 5), any language or ISO codes. Use instead of destination for a multi-country trip. Required unless destination is given.

devices.description: phone = one phone (5 Mbps); phone_laptop = phone + laptop; small_group = a travel router for two or three devices; family = one travel router for the whole family; creator_posting = stories, reels, TikToks; creator_live = going live from the phone; creator_hd_live = Full HD live streams; creator_pro = multi-camera live and 4K uploads. Default phone.

flat.description: Optional: which Flat of the country, as get_flats numbers them. Omit = the cheapest Flat that allows the speed.

networks.description: Optional: operator names from get_flats that must be included (the cheapest Flat holding all of them is used). Ignored when flat is given.

budget.description: Optional budget for the whole trip in the quoted currency; options above it are marked.

per_country.description: Optional days per country for a multi-country trip.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: plan_trip
tools.description: A trip through several countries (max 5): one Flat per country, each quoted at the same speed and days unless given per country. Returns one line per country with price and buy_url, plus the total. Use when the customer names two or more countries and a speed (2–5 destinations); for one country call quote_flat; use recommend_config when they describe devices or usage instead. One Flat per country; present each line with its price and buy_url and the total_for_trip as returned. Countries in not_available cannot be served and speed_notes explain a lower speed - say so instead of guessing.

destinations.description: Countries of the trip (2–5), any language or ISO codes, in travel order.

mbps.description: Maximum speed in Mbps (5, 10, 25, 50; default 5). Data is unlimited at that speed. 25 Mbps and up need a 5G network.

per_country.description: Optional overrides per country (days and/or mbps).

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: start_checkout
tools.description: Use only once the customer has decided to buy ("I'll take it", "how do I buy?"): the checkout handoff. Returns the buy_url to give the customer, the final price and a ready-to-send checkout block (next_step, payment_methods, delivery) — on the page they press "Get your Flat" and pay securely. No account needed; the eSIM is delivered on screen and by email within seconds of payment. No in-chat order tracking, no discount codes. For prices while the customer is still comparing, use quote_flat. Give the customer buy_url exactly as returned together with next_step: the card opens preset, they press "Get your Flat" and pay. Quote price as returned (the full amount).

destination.description: Country in ANY language or its ISO code, e.g. "Japan", "Japon", "jp". Map a city to its country first. One country per Flat.

mbps.description: Maximum speed in Mbps (5, 10, 25, 50; default 5). Data is unlimited at that speed. 25 Mbps and up need a 5G network.

flat.description: Optional: which Flat of the country, as get_flats numbers them. Omit = the cheapest Flat that allows the speed.

networks.description: Optional: operator names from get_flats that must be included (the cheapest Flat holding all of them is used). Ignored when flat is given.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: get_locale_state
tools.description: Read the current site locale: UI language, region and the active /{language-region}/ bucket of the page the user is on.

tools.name: set_language
tools.description: Switch the site to a supported language-region bucket such as "de-de" or "en-gb" and navigate to that locale; prices then show in that region's currency. Call get_locale_state first to see the current bucket.

bucket.description: Lowercase language-region bucket, e.g. "de-de", "en-us", "ja-jp". The enum is the complete list of buckets this site offers; nothing outside it is accepted.

tools.name: set_currency
tools.description: Switch the displayed currency by ISO 4217 code such as "EUR", "USD" or "GBP". Currency follows the region, so the site navigates to the matching region in the user's current language.

code.description: ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. "EUR", "USD", "GBP". The enum is the complete list of currencies this site shows; nothing outside it is accepted.

tools.name: get_consent_state
tools.description: Read the visitor's current cookie-consent state on this site. Necessary cookies are always on. Reports whether the visitor has decided yet and the on/off state of analytics, ads and personalized ads. By design there is no tool to grant consent: consent is given by a human on the banner.

tools.name: reject_non_essential_cookies
tools.description: Opt the visitor out of all non-essential cookies (analytics, ads, personalized ads) and close the consent banner. Necessary cookies remain. Records a refusal only; it can never grant consent - that is a human decision by design. Use when the user wants to decline tracking.

tools.name: get_configuration
tools.description: Read the Flat the user is configuring on this page right now: country, speed (Mbps) and the speeds possible, days, the networks (ticked or not, 4G/5G), the Flat name and the price shown. Returns available=false on pages without the card.

tools.name: set_configuration
tools.description: Move the card on this page for the user: country (ISO code), speed in Mbps (5, 10, 25 or 50; 25 and 50 need a Flat with 5G), days (1-30) and the networks (operator names - the Flat holding all of them is selected) or a flat number. Omitted fields keep their value. Nothing is bought - the user still presses "Get your Flat". Returns the resulting card and the price shown.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. "jp".

mbps.description: Speed in Mbps: 5, 10, 25, 50. 25 and 50 need a Flat with 5G.

networks.description: Operator names that must be included.

flat.description: Flat number from get_flats or get_configuration (ignored when networks are given).

tools.name: thn_internal__get_state_info
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns a runtime snapshot of the THN Web SDK global state on the current hotel webpage, including property and hotel identifiers, booking system, page name, language, device, SDK version, environment, and hostname. Use this when a THN staff member needs to understand the current SDK context — for example to confirm which property is loaded, which environment is active, or which SDK version is running. Do not use this tool for hotel-guest-facing tasks; it exposes internal SDK identifiers that are not meaningful to end users.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_dom_element
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Finds a DOM element on the current hotel webpage using a CSS selector and returns its innerHTML. Use this when a THN staff member needs to inspect the rendered HTML of a specific element — for example to verify that a THN widget or message is present in the DOM and correctly rendered. Returns found: true with the markup in html when the element exists, or found: false when no matching element exists. This tool does not modify the DOM; use thn_internal__show_message or thn_internal__hide_message to control message visibility.

selector.description: A valid CSS selector identifying the element to inspect, e.g. "#thn-note" or ".thn-widget"

tools.name: thn_internal__list_messages
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Lists all messages currently registered across all THN widget types (note, exit, layer, inliner) on the hotel webpage. Returns each message's ID, name, and the widget it belongs to. Use this as a first step when a THN staff member needs to identify which messages are available before calling thn_internal__get_message_state, thn_internal__show_message, or thn_internal__hide_message. This tool does not filter by visibility or state — it lists all registered messages regardless of whether they are currently shown, hidden, or eligible to display.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_message_state
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns the current runtime state of a specific THN message identified by its ID, including flags such as opened, closed, and the widget type it belongs to. Use this when a THN staff member needs to diagnose why a message is or is not displaying — for example to check whether it has already been opened, closed, or is being suppressed. Use thn_internal__list_messages first to discover available message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to inspect, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__show_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Forces a THN message to display on the hotel webpage, bypassing all normal display guards such as frequency caps, triggers, beacons, and eligibility rules. Returns the message's previous and current state after the forced display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to preview or test a specific message regardless of whether it would normally be shown. This tool mutates widget state and stubs internal widget methods for the duration of the call — it is intended for inspection and testing only, not for production user flows. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs, and thn_internal__hide_message to reverse the effect. Throws an error if the message ID is not found.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to force-display, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__hide_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Hides a currently displayed THN message on the hotel webpage, either by gracefully animating it out of the DOM (if it is actively rendered) or by marking it as closed in state to prevent future display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to dismiss a message during inspection or testing — for example after using thn_internal__show_message to force-display it. This tool mutates widget and message state; it is intended for inspection and testing only. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to hide, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__get_bus_history
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Reads the recent history of events emitted on the THN Web SDK internal event bus, returning each event name and its arguments. Use this when a THN staff member needs to trace SDK activity — for example to verify that a specific event was fired, to understand the sequence of events leading to a behaviour, or to debug event-driven logic. Results can be filtered by a regex pattern on the event name and limited in count (default 50, most recent events returned last). Note that event arguments containing DOM elements or functions are collapsed to compact placeholders to avoid serialization issues.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return: the most recent ones, listed oldest to newest. Defaults to 50.

filter.description: Optional regex pattern to filter events by name, e.g. "message" or "^booking"

tools.name: thn_site__get_hotel_info
tools.description: Returns basic information about the hotel whose website the guest is currently browsing: its name, website URL, main currency, location, geographic area and type of establishment (for example Hotels, Resorts or Apartments). Use this when the guest asks what this property is, where it is located, or which currency it works in. Any piece of information that is not available is returned as null. Takes no input.

tools.name: thn_site__check_availability
tools.description: Checks whether the hotel has rooms available for the given check-in and check-out dates and room occupancy (adults, children and children ages per room). Use this when the guest asks if there is availability on specific dates. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to check, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__compare_rates
tools.description: Compares the hotel's direct rate with other booking channels for the given dates and rooms. Use this when the guest asks about price comparisons or other booking channels. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to compare rates for, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__get_direct_booking_benefits
tools.description: Describes the benefits of booking directly on the hotel website. Use this when the guest asks about why book direct. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__get_rates
tools.description: Returns the hotel's rates for the given dates and occupancy. Use this when the guest asks about prices. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to get rates for, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__list_amenities
tools.description: Lists the hotel amenities and services. Use this when the guest asks about pool, parking, extras, etc. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__list_rooms
tools.description: Lists the room types the hotel offers. Use this when the guest asks what rooms exist. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__start_booking
tools.description: Starts a booking for the given dates and rooms, optionally with a currency, a promo code and a language. Use this when the guest wants to book. Returns a URL to the booking engine where the guest can complete the booking, so open that URL to continue. When a booking URL cannot be built it returns the hotel website URL instead, or null if that is not available either.

rooms.description: The rooms to book, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

currencyCode.description: Currency the guest wants to see prices in, as an ISO 4217 code such as USD. When omitted, USD is used

languageCode.description: Language the guest wants the booking engine in, such as en or zh_TW

promoCode.description: Promo code to apply to the booking

promoCodeType.description: Type of the promo code, when known

tools.name: add_to_bgg_collection
tools.description: Add a game to the logged in user's BGG collection. The browser must have the ShelfScan extension installed and have a subscription in order to use this tool.

tools.name: add_to_bgg_collection_for_trade
tools.description: Mark a game as for trade in the logged in user's BGG collection, with its trade condition. Updates the existing collection item when a collectionId is given, otherwise adds a new item marked for trade. The browser must have the ShelfScan extension installed and have a subscription in order to use this tool.

tools.name: add_to_bgg_wishlist
tools.description: Add a game to the logged in user's BGG wishlist with a wishlist priority. Updates the existing collection item when a collectionId is given, otherwise adds a new item on the wishlist. The browser must have the ShelfScan extension installed and have a subscription in order to use this tool.

tools.name: set_bgg_previously_owned
tools.description: Mark a game as previously owned in the logged in user's BGG collection, which also turns off "own". Updates the existing collection item when a collectionId is given, otherwise adds a new item as previously owned. The browser must have the ShelfScan extension installed and have a subscription in order to use this tool.

tools.name: clear_bgg_collection_statuses
tools.description: Turn off every status (own, previously owned, for trade, want, wishlist, preordered, ...) on an existing item in the logged in user's BGG collection. The item itself stays in the collection. The browser must have the ShelfScan extension installed and have a subscription in order to use this tool.

tools.name: remove_bgg_collection_item
tools.description: IRREVERSIBLE: permanently deletes an item from the logged in user's BGG collection, including its statuses, rating, comments, trade condition, wishlist details and private info. This cannot be undone. Only use it when the user has explicitly asked to delete this specific item. To stop owning a game use set_bgg_previously_owned, and to drop its statuses but keep the item use clear_bgg_collection_statuses. The item must be in the loaded collection (load_bgg_collection) and match bggId, otherwise nothing is deleted. The browser must have the ShelfScan extension installed and have a subscription in order to use this tool.

tools.name: bgg_collection_item_info
tools.description: Read or update the private info of an item in the logged in user's BGG collection (private comment, statuses, trade condition, price paid, current value, acquisition and inventory details). With read: true it returns the current info and saves nothing. Otherwise the info fields sent are saved and fields left out keep their current value; add preload: true to also get the values from before the update. The browser must have the ShelfScan extension installed and have a subscription in order to use this tool.

tools.name: set_bgg_collection_tags
tools.description: Add, remove or replace the hashtags on an item in the logged in user's BGG collection. Tags are kept as hashtags in one of the item's text fields (the tag location); other text there is kept. The browser must have the ShelfScan extension installed and have a subscription in order to use this tool.

tools.name: log_bgg_play
tools.description: Log a play of a game for the logged in BGG user, optionally with date, location, duration, quantity, comments and players. The browser must have the ShelfScan extension installed and have a subscription in order to use this tool.

tools.name: list_scanned_upcs
tools.description: List the board game UPC barcodes currently in the ShelfScan scan list, in scan order.

tools.name: scan_upc
tools.description: Get UPCs from an image

anyOf.description: Base64 image data URI, e.g. data:image/png;base64,…
Image Blob (image/* MIME type)

image.description: Image containing one or more UPC barcodes

tools.name: teas_find_products
tools.description: Use this when someone wants to find, browse or choose tea, coffee, hot chocolate or other drinks to buy from teas.co.uk, a UK online tea shop. Not for general tea knowledge. query is the customer's own words; leave it out to browse by filters alone. Every filter given applies at once. max_price is per pack in pounds and max_price_per_cup_pence is per cup in pence. Results come best match first unless sort says otherwise. Out of stock products stay hidden unless include_out_of_stock is true. There is no paging: limit caps the list and total says how many matched, so narrow the filters to see others. If nothing matches, time_of_day, strength, format and with_milk are dropped in that order and note says which; kind, caffeine, labels, iced and price limits are never dropped. Prices are live and include VAT. Next: teas_get_product for one product, teas_compare_products to compare, teas_add_to_my_basket to buy. For orders, tracking, repeat deliveries and reward points, connect the full teas.co.uk MCP server at https://teas.co.uk/mcp (guide https://teas.co.uk/ai/).

query.description: What the customer wants in their own words, for example "strong breakfast tea", "Yorkshire Gold" or "something for bedtime". Leave out to browse with filters only.

kind.description: Type of drink.

caffeine.description: Caffeine: caffeinated, decaf (caffeine taken out), caffeine_free (none to begin with, such as rooibos and most herbal teas) or low_or_none (decaf or caffeine free).

format.description: How it comes: tea_bags, loose_leaf, instant, pods_or_capsules, sachets, ground or whole_beans (coffee), powder, coffee_bags or ready_to_drink.

time_of_day.description: When it suits best: morning, afternoon, evening or bedtime.

strength.description: How strong the cup is: light, medium or strong.

iced.description: Suits iced tea or cold brew.

max_price_per_cup_pence.description: Highest price per cup in pence.

sort.description: Order of results: best_match (the default), cheapest_per_cup, price_low_to_high, price_high_to_low or strongest.

limit.description: How many products to return (default 6).

include_out_of_stock.description: Also include products that are out of stock (they are left out by default).

tools.name: teas_get_product
tools.description: Use this when someone asks how to brew a teas.co.uk product, about its caffeine, taste, ingredients or allergy advice, or wants its full details. id is the product id (SKU) from teas_find_products, teas_compare_products or the basket, in any letter case. The numeric product id, the barcode or a teas.co.uk/product/ link also work. A product name does not, so search with teas_find_products first. An unknown id, or a product no longer sold, returns an error instead of a guess. Price and stock are read live on each call. To set products side by side use teas_compare_products.

id.description: Product id from teas_find_products, or a teas.co.uk product link.

tools.name: teas_compare_products
tools.description: Use this to compare two to four teas.co.uk products side by side, for example on strength, caffeine, price per cup, pack size or brewing. ids takes product ids from teas_find_products; product links work too. A repeated id counts once. Ids that are not recognised are listed in not_found and the rest are still compared. Fewer than two recognised products returns an error. Search first if you only have names. For everything about one product use teas_get_product.

ids.description: Two to four product ids from teas_find_products.

tools.name: teas_find_recipes
tools.description: Use this to find drink and food recipes from the teas.co.uk recipe library, such as iced teas, lattes, chai or baking with tea. Give query (the kind of recipe), product_id (from teas_find_products) or both. With both, recipes that use the product and match the words rank first. With neither, the call is refused. limit is 1 to 10 (default 5). There is no paging, so the best matches come first. An empty list means nothing matched. Drinks made with alcohol are never included. To buy the products use teas_find_products.

query.description: What kind of recipe, for example "iced peach tea" or "chai latte".

limit.description: How many recipes (default 5).

tools.name: teas_delivery_and_returns
tools.description: Use this when someone asks about teas.co.uk delivery prices, free delivery, dispatch times, which countries it delivers to, or how returns and refunds work. It takes no input because the answer is the same for everyone. Policy only: it never looks at an order. Returns and order tracking are in My Account on teas.co.uk.

tools.name: teas_quote_cart
tools.description: Use this to price products for the person before anything goes in a basket. Pass up to 20 items (id from teas_find_products and quantity) and the delivery country. It returns live prices including VAT, every delivery option teas.co.uk offers for that country and parcel, the total with the cheapest option, how much more to spend for free UK delivery, stock, and a basket link the person can open. Nothing is stored and no basket changes. For a basket the person keeps, call teas_add_to_my_basket; to hand over checkout, call teas_go_to_checkout.

quantity.description: How many packs.

items.description: Products and quantities to price, 1 to 20 lines. The same id twice is added together.

country.description: Delivery country as a two letter code, for example GB, IE or FR. Leave out for the UK.

tools.name: teas_find_substitutes
tools.description: Use this when a product is out of stock, too dear, or the person wants something similar to try. Pass one product id from teas_find_products or a teas.co.uk product link. It returns products of the same kind and caffeine, near the same strength, split into cheaper and premium by price per cup, in stock first and closest match first. limit sets how many of each come back (default 3). Next: teas_get_product for details, teas_compare_products to compare, teas_add_to_my_basket to buy.

id.description: Product id from teas_find_products, or a teas.co.uk product link.

limit.description: How many cheaper and how many premium alternatives, 1 to 10. Defaults to 3.

tools.name: teas_get_promotions
tools.description: Use this when the person asks about offers, discounts, codes or what is on sale at teas.co.uk. It lists products on sale now with the usual price and when the sale ends (biggest saving first, in stock only), any offer codes teas.co.uk has made public, and the free UK delivery threshold. Codes that are not public are never shown, and checkout on teas.co.uk applies the final price. Next: teas_get_product for details, quote_cart for a total, teas_add_to_my_basket to buy.

limit.description: How many products on sale to list, 1 to 20. Defaults to 10.

tools.name: teas_add_to_my_basket
tools.description: Add a teas.co.uk product to the basket in this browser, only when the visitor asks. The quantity is added to any already there. Nothing is bought until the visitor checks out and pays on teas.co.uk.

tools.name: teas_update_my_basket
tools.description: Set the quantity of a product already in the basket in this browser, or remove it with quantity 0, only when the visitor asks.

quantity.description: New quantity; 0 removes the product.

tools.name: teas_view_my_basket
tools.description: Show the basket in this browser with its subtotal. An assistant connected to https://teas.co.uk/mcp can also keep a basket and give a checkout link.

tools.name: teas_go_to_checkout
tools.description: Open the teas.co.uk checkout page in this browser so the visitor can review the basket and pay. The visitor checks out and pays; the assistant never enters payment details and nothing is ordered by this tool.

tools.name: teas_basket_link
tools.description: Make a teas.co.uk basket link for up to 20 products to give the person (https://teas.co.uk/go/basket/?items=ID:QTY,...). Opening it shows a confirmation page; nothing changes until the person presses Add to basket. Never open it yourself.

tools.name: ask_tea_advice

question.description: The question in plain words.

tools.name: teas_start_subscription
tools.description: Use this when someone wants a teas.co.uk product delivered again and again (subscribe and save). Pass one product id from teas_find_products or a teas.co.uk product link. Returns the subscriber price, how often it comes and a link to the product on teas.co.uk, where the person presses Subscribe and save, then signs in, checks out and pays for the first delivery. This tool orders and charges nothing. Later deliveries follow every cycle as new orders with the same discount, teas.co.uk emails five days before each one and takes no automatic card payments, and the person can pause, resume or cancel at any time (my_subscriptions, change_subscription). When the product cannot be a repeat delivery, eligible is false and note says why.

id.description: Product id from teas_find_products, or a teas.co.uk product link.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_state_info
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns a runtime snapshot of the THN Web SDK global state on the current hotel webpage, including property and hotel identifiers, booking system, page name, language, device, SDK version, environment, and hostname. Use this when a THN staff member needs to understand the current SDK context — for example to confirm which property is loaded, which environment is active, or which SDK version is running. Do not use this tool for hotel-guest-facing tasks; it exposes internal SDK identifiers that are not meaningful to end users.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_dom_element
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Finds a DOM element on the current hotel webpage using a CSS selector and returns its innerHTML. Use this when a THN staff member needs to inspect the rendered HTML of a specific element — for example to verify that a THN widget or message is present in the DOM and correctly rendered. Returns found: true with the markup in html when the element exists, or found: false when no matching element exists. This tool does not modify the DOM; use thn_internal__show_message or thn_internal__hide_message to control message visibility.

selector.description: A valid CSS selector identifying the element to inspect, e.g. "#thn-note" or ".thn-widget"

tools.name: thn_internal__list_messages
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Lists all messages currently registered across all THN widget types (note, exit, layer, inliner) on the hotel webpage. Returns each message's ID, name, and the widget it belongs to. Use this as a first step when a THN staff member needs to identify which messages are available before calling thn_internal__get_message_state, thn_internal__show_message, or thn_internal__hide_message. This tool does not filter by visibility or state — it lists all registered messages regardless of whether they are currently shown, hidden, or eligible to display.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_message_state
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns the current runtime state of a specific THN message identified by its ID, including flags such as opened, closed, and the widget type it belongs to. Use this when a THN staff member needs to diagnose why a message is or is not displaying — for example to check whether it has already been opened, closed, or is being suppressed. Use thn_internal__list_messages first to discover available message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to inspect, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__show_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Forces a THN message to display on the hotel webpage, bypassing all normal display guards such as frequency caps, triggers, beacons, and eligibility rules. Returns the message's previous and current state after the forced display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to preview or test a specific message regardless of whether it would normally be shown. This tool mutates widget state and stubs internal widget methods for the duration of the call — it is intended for inspection and testing only, not for production user flows. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs, and thn_internal__hide_message to reverse the effect. Throws an error if the message ID is not found.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to force-display, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__hide_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Hides a currently displayed THN message on the hotel webpage, either by gracefully animating it out of the DOM (if it is actively rendered) or by marking it as closed in state to prevent future display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to dismiss a message during inspection or testing — for example after using thn_internal__show_message to force-display it. This tool mutates widget and message state; it is intended for inspection and testing only. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to hide, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__get_bus_history
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Reads the recent history of events emitted on the THN Web SDK internal event bus, returning each event name and its arguments. Use this when a THN staff member needs to trace SDK activity — for example to verify that a specific event was fired, to understand the sequence of events leading to a behaviour, or to debug event-driven logic. Results can be filtered by a regex pattern on the event name and limited in count (default 50, most recent events returned last). Note that event arguments containing DOM elements or functions are collapsed to compact placeholders to avoid serialization issues.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return: the most recent ones, listed oldest to newest. Defaults to 50.

filter.description: Optional regex pattern to filter events by name, e.g. "message" or "^booking"

Use this when the guest asks what this property is, where it is located, or which currency it works in. Any piece of information that is not available is returned as null. Takes no input.

tools.name: u9itus_current_page
tools.description: Describe the u9itus.dev page the user is currently viewing (page type, and the candidate in focus if any). Call this first to ground follow-up civic questions. On the map (page_type "map"), call u9itus_map_view for the place on screen; on the comparison page ("compare"), call u9itus_comparison_view.

tools.name: u9itus_find_candidates
tools.description: Search u9itus published candidate and elected-official profiles by name and/or filters. Use for questions like 'who is running for X in Y', 'Texas candidates funded by AIPAC', or to resolve a name mentioned in an article to a u9itus profile (each result has a uuid for u9itus_get_candidate). The response includes `total` (all matches), `count` (this page), and `next_offset` — to get every match, keep calling with `offset: next_offset` until it is null. When `funded_by` is set, each result also carries a `funding_match` array citing the specific contributors / PACs and dollar amounts.

q.description: Name or partial name to search for.

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. CA.

governance_level.description: federal | state | county | municipal (as stored on the profile).

running.description: true = only active candidates; false = only seated officials.

funded_by.description: Keep only candidates whose FEC / OpenSecrets donor snapshot shows money from this source — a PAC, committee, advocacy group (e.g. 'AIPAC'), industry, or contributor name. Naming a known advocacy group also matches its aligned PACs. Matched results include a `funding_match` array with the named sources and amounts.

limit.description: Results per page (default 10, max 20).

offset.description: Skip this many matches — pass the previous response's next_offset to page.

tools.name: u9itus_get_candidate
tools.description: Full civic dossier for one candidate by uuid: office, party, district, bio, official links, transparency IDs (FEC/OpenSecrets/Ballotpedia/Vote Smart), recent verified news, donor snapshot, and upcoming elections in their state.

tools.name: u9itus_compare_candidates
tools.description: Return full dossiers for 2–4 candidates at once (by uuid) so you can present a structured side-by-side comparison.

tools.name: u9itus_list_ballot_measures
tools.description: List US ballot measures (always state/county scoped) with plain-language yes/no meanings. Filter by state, free-text, and status (upcoming|passed|failed). Each result carries a `read_more` link ({label, url}) to the full legal text and fiscal analysis — cite it when the user asks about detail the summary omits (eligibility thresholds, dollar amounts, funding source, repayment terms). If a state has none yet, the response includes a `backfill` block (status queued|in_progress|unavailable) — relay its message and offer u9itus_watch_ballot_measures.

state.description: Two-letter US state code.

q.description: Free-text match on title or measure number.

tools.name: u9itus_watch_ballot_measures
tools.description: When u9itus_list_ballot_measures reports no measures for a state, register an email to be notified once that state's measures are published. Confirm the email with the user first.

state.description: Two-letter US state code.

email.description: Where to send the one-time notification.

tools.name: u9itus_upcoming_elections
tools.description: Upcoming election stages (primary, general, runoff) and candidate filing deadlines for a US state.

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX.

tools.name: u9itus_list_races
tools.description: List the races in a US state that have confirmed running candidates — who is running against whom — with each election date. Each race carries `compare`: pass it as the arguments to u9itus_open_comparison to open the side-by-side comparison and its printable voter guide. Filter with `q`: an office, a district such as CA-12, a city, or a candidate's name.

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. CA.

q.description: Keep races whose office, district, city or candidate names contain this text.

limit.description: Races to return (default 20, max 50).

tools.name: u9itus_open_comparison
tools.description: Open u9itus's side-by-side comparison of candidates for the same seat (up to 3 people), which includes a printable, source-referenced voter guide. Pass a race's `compare` object from u9itus_list_races, or a state and congressional district, or a state and a candidate's full_name (plus office) for statewide and local seats. It checks the comparison first: when none is available it says why and stays on this page. Otherwise it returns the seat and its candidates, then navigates this tab to the comparison. With no `selected`, it picks running candidates first, up to 3; tell the user who was left out.

state.description: Two-letter US state code.

district.description: Congressional district for a U.S. House race, e.g. CA-12 or 12.

office.description: Office, e.g. Governor or Mayor. Optional for House races.

full_name.description: A candidate on the seat. Needed when there is no district.

selected.description: Candidate keys to include, from u9itus_list_races `running` or a previous comparison.

tools.name: u9itus_latest_candidate_news
tools.description: Most recent verified news about candidates / officials across every published profile, newest first. Use this for 'what's the latest candidate news' or 'which candidate is in the news' — it answers in one call instead of opening dossiers one by one. Every item links to the original story (`source_url`) and identifies the candidate, including their `profile_url`. Filter by state, topic, or headline text.

state.description: Two-letter US state code.

topic.description: Restrict to a single topic key, e.g. 'economy'.

tools.name: u9itus_submit_candidate_lead
tools.description: Report a candidate you spotted (e.g. named in an article the user is reading) who may be missing from u9itus. This does NOT publish anything — the lead is queued as 'pending' for human verification. Always confirm with the user before calling.

state.description: Two-letter US state code, if known.

office_hint.description: Office they are seeking, e.g. 'US House NC-06'.

source_url.description: URL of the article / page the candidate was found on.

context.description: Short quote or summary giving evidence (max ~2000 chars).

tools.name: u9itus_map_view
tools.description: What the u9itus U.S. map is showing right now: level (overview, region, state or district), the state and congressional district in focus, which data layers are on, and a share_url for this view. Call it before describing the map or after the user moves it. To research the place, pass the state to u9itus_find_candidates, u9itus_upcoming_elections or u9itus_list_ballot_measures.

tools.name: u9itus_map_show
tools.description: Move the u9itus U.S. map the user is looking at. Give a state (optionally with a congressional district) to fly there and open its panel of officials and candidates; give only a region to show that region; give nothing to return to the national overview. `district` is a congressional district number only. For a state, county or city candidate, pass `state` and `candidate` without a district. Returns the new view, plus `candidate_opened` when a candidate was asked for.

state.description: Two-letter code or full name, e.g. "CA" or "California".

district.description: Congressional district number, e.g. "12" or "CA-12". Use "AL" for at-large states. Requires state.

region.description: Show a whole region. Ignored when state is given.

candidate.description: Open this candidate's card once the state's panel loads: the profile_url from u9itus_find_candidates, or its /p/{slug} slug. Requires state.

tools.name: u9itus_map_find_district
tools.description: Find the congressional district for a U.S. street address or 5-digit ZIP code and show it on the map with its officials and candidates. Only use an address the user gave you for this lookup. It is matched with the U.S. Census geocoder; u9itus does not save it or put it in the URL. A full street address is exact. A ZIP can cover several districts: then the map does not move and `choices` lists them, so ask the user for their street address or which district, then call u9itus_map_show.

address.description: Street address with city, state and ZIP (e.g. "1000 San Pablo Ave, Albany, CA 94706"), or a 5-digit ZIP code.

tools.name: u9itus_map_set_layer
tools.description: Turn a data layer on the u9itus U.S. map on or off. Layers: districts (Congressional district lines across all 50 states.); party (Color states by the party of the current governor (replaces poverty coloring).); poverty (Color states by poverty rate, Census ACS 5-year (replaces party coloring).); population (Shade congressional districts by resident population. Needs a state open.); cities (Incorporated city and town boundaries. Needs a state open.); topcities (Top cities by 2020 Census population and state government offices. Needs a state open.); candidates (Statewide candidates at each state capital. Needs a state open.); content (Geo-tagged blog posts and civic events in the visible area.); businesses (Local businesses that opted in to appear on the map.); nonprofits (Nonprofits and community-based organizations with a published u9itus voter guide.) Returns the new view.

on.description: true to show the layer, false to hide it.

u9itus.com.blurb: U9itus current page, U9itus find candidates and U9itus get candidate.
u9itus.com.name: u9itus

tools.name: get_shop_facts
tools.description: What varioroam is and how it works, in the shop’s own words: the configurable eSIM, ranges, delivery, payment, hotspot, activation, top-ups (add data or days), e-mails, support. Use for any question that is not a price. Answer from the returned facts in the shop’s own words; do not add refund windows, speeds or rules that are not returned.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

tools.name: list_destinations
tools.description: Every country varioroam can build an eSIM for, with the number of selectable networks and the starting price (1 GB, 1 day, cheapest network). Use to check coverage or to compare many countries at once. from_price is the starting price (1 GB x 1 day x cheapest network) - call quote_esim for the configuration the customer actually wants.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: get_networks
tools.description: The mobile networks the customer can tick for one country (operator name, 4G/5G) with the price of a reference eSIM on each network alone (1 GB · 7 days), so you can say which network is the cheapest and what the others add. reference_price is for 1 GB x 7 days on that network alone - a comparison aid, not a plan. The cheapest network is pre-selected in the shop; every extra network adds a small fee, a dearer one also raises the data price. Never invent coverage or speeds.

destination.description: Country in ANY language or its ISO code, e.g. "Japan", "Japon", "jp". Map a city to its country first. One country per eSIM.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: quote_esim
tools.description: Use while the customer is still deciding — "how much is …?": the exact price of one eSIM configuration (country, data GB 1–100, days 1–90, networks), the server price the customer would pay. Quote it as returned, never compute or scale it yourself. The result carries a buy_url for reference; when the customer says they want to buy, call start_checkout instead. price is the FULL amount of exactly this configuration (price_basis total) - never per day, never per GB; quote it as returned and never compute or scale it. data_gb is one pool for the whole validity. networks lists the operators exactly as returned.

destination.description: Country in ANY language or its ISO code, e.g. "Japan", "Japon", "jp". Map a city to its country first. One country per eSIM.

gb.description: Data pool in whole GB for the whole trip (1–100). One pool, not per day. Not sure how much? Call recommend_config.

networks.description: Optional: operator names (or codes) from get_networks to include. Omit = the cheapest network of the country. The dearest included network sets the data price and every network beyond the first adds a small fee.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: price_grid
tools.description: Prices for several GB × days combinations of one country in one call (max 8 × 8), e.g. to compare with other providers or to find the best fit for a trip. Same server prices as quote_esim. Every row is the full price of that GB x days combination; present the rows as a table with the currency, never derive per-day or per-GB figures. Use the buy_url of each row exactly.

destination.description: Country in ANY language or its ISO code, e.g. "Japan", "Japon", "jp". Map a city to its country first. One country per eSIM.

networks.description: Optional: operator names (or codes) from get_networks to include. Omit = the cheapest network of the country. The dearest included network sets the data price and every network beyond the first adds a small fee.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: recommend_config
tools.description: Use when the customer describes a trip instead of a size: country (or up to 5), days and how they use data (usage light / normal / heavy, or gb_per_day). Sizes the data pool from the data guide and returns three server-quoted configurations per country — exact, comfortable (×1.5) and generous (×2) — each with its price, networks, a one-line reason and its buy_url, plus trip totals and an optional budget check. Prices are the same as quote_esim. Give destination (one country) or destinations (several) — one of the two is required; a call without a country fails with invalid_argument.

destination.description: Country in ANY language or its ISO code, e.g. "Japan", "Japon", "jp". Map a city to its country first. One country per eSIM. Required unless destinations is given.

destinations.description: Several countries (max 5), any language or ISO codes. Use instead of destination for a multi-country trip. Required unless destination is given.

days.description: Days of the trip (per country for a multi-country trip; 1–90).

usage.description: light ≈ 0.5 GB/day, normal ≈ 1.5 GB/day (default), heavy ≈ 4 GB/day.

gb_per_day.description: Optional: the customer's own estimate in GB per day (wins over usage).

networks.description: Optional: operator names (or codes) from get_networks to include. Omit = the cheapest network of the country. The dearest included network sets the data price and every network beyond the first adds a small fee.

budget.description: Optional budget for the whole trip in the quoted currency; options above it are marked.

per_country.description: Optional days per country for a multi-country trip.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: plan_trip
tools.description: A trip through several countries (max 5): one eSIM per country, each quoted with the same data pool and days unless given per country (gb omitted = sized for normal use from the days). Returns one line per country with price and buy_url, plus the total. Use when the customer names two or more countries and a size (2–5 destinations); for one country call quote_esim; use recommend_config when they describe usage instead. One eSIM per country; present each line with its price and buy_url and the total_for_trip as returned. Countries in not_available cannot be served - say so instead of guessing.

destinations.description: Countries of the trip (2–5), any language or ISO codes, in travel order.

gb.description: Data pool per country in whole GB (1–100). Omit = sized for normal use from the days (1.5 GB/day).

per_country.description: Optional overrides per country (gb and/or days, same ranges as above).

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: start_checkout
tools.description: Use only once the customer has decided to buy ("I'll take it", "how do I buy?"): the checkout handoff. Returns the buy_url to give the customer, the final price and a ready-to-send checkout block (next_step, payment_methods, delivery) — on the page they press "Get it" and pay securely. No account needed; the eSIM is delivered on screen and by e-mail right after payment. No in-chat order tracking, no discount codes. For prices while the customer is still comparing, use quote_esim. Give the customer buy_url exactly as returned together with next_step: the configurator opens pre-set, they press "Get it" and pay. Quote price as returned (the full amount).

destination.description: Country in ANY language or its ISO code, e.g. "Japan", "Japon", "jp". Map a city to its country first. One country per eSIM.

networks.description: Optional: operator names (or codes) from get_networks to include. Omit = the cheapest network of the country. The dearest included network sets the data price and every network beyond the first adds a small fee.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: get_locale_state
tools.description: Read the current site locale: UI language, region and the active /{language-region}/ bucket of the page the user is on.

tools.name: set_language
tools.description: Switch the site to a supported language-region bucket such as "de-de" or "en-gb" and navigate to that locale; prices then show in that region's currency. Call get_locale_state first to see the current bucket.

bucket.description: Lowercase language-region bucket, e.g. "de-de", "en-us", "ja-jp". The enum is the complete list of buckets this site offers; nothing outside it is accepted.

tools.name: set_currency
tools.description: Switch the displayed currency by ISO 4217 code such as "EUR", "USD" or "GBP". Currency follows the region, so the site navigates to the matching region in the user's current language.

code.description: ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. "EUR", "USD", "GBP". The enum is the complete list of currencies this site shows; nothing outside it is accepted.

tools.name: get_consent_state
tools.description: Read the visitor's current cookie-consent state on this site. Necessary cookies are always on. Reports whether the visitor has decided yet and the on/off state of analytics, ads and personalized ads. By design there is no tool to grant consent: consent is given by a human on the banner.

tools.name: reject_non_essential_cookies
tools.description: Opt the visitor out of all non-essential cookies (analytics, ads, personalized ads) and close the consent banner. Necessary cookies remain. Records a refusal only; it can never grant consent - that is a human decision by design. Use when the user wants to decline tracking.

tools.name: get_configuration
tools.description: Read the eSIM the user is configuring on this page right now: country, data pool (GB), validity (days), the networks ticked and the price shown. Returns available=false on pages without the configurator.

tools.name: set_configuration
tools.description: Move the dials on this page for the user: country (ISO code), data pool in GB (1-100), validity days (1-90) and the network codes to tick (from get_networks or get_configuration). Omitted fields keep their value. Nothing is bought - the user still presses "Get it". Returns the resulting configuration and the price shown.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. "jp".

networks.description: Network codes to tick; the others are unticked.
