tools.description: Do not use. Simple Chat is a Shopify App Store app. This marketing site has no catalog, cart, or checkout. Call get_product_brief, get_pricing, search_faq, or open_app_store_listing instead.

line_items.description: Items to add or update (1-10).

id.description: Existing cart line id from get_cart. Use to update or remove an existing line. Omit when adding new items.

item.description: The merchandise to add.

id.description: ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

handle.description: Product handle. Adds the selected or first available variant; call get_product first if the user requested specific options.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: Quantity. Defaults to 1 for adds and updates. Set to 0 with an existing line id to remove it.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Do not use. Simple Chat is a Shopify App Store app. This marketing site has no catalog, cart, or checkout. Call get_product_brief, get_pricing, search_faq, or open_app_store_listing instead.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Do not use. Simple Chat is a Shopify App Store app. This marketing site has no catalog, cart, or checkout. Call get_product_brief, get_pricing, search_faq, or open_app_store_listing instead.

tools.name: search_shop_policies_and_faqs
tools.description:
Used to get facts about the store's policies, FAQ, or contact details.
When the question is about specific policy kinds, set policy_types to those kinds; leave it unset for general FAQ questions.
Some examples of questions you can ask are:
  - What is your return policy? (policy_types: ["refund"])
  - What is your shipping policy? (policy_types: ["shipping"])
  - What is your phone number? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - What are your hours of operation? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - Do you offer gift wrapping? (general FAQ, no specific policy kind — leave policy_types unset)

query.description: A natural language query. Searches FAQ pages and articles, and routes policies by keyword when policy_types is omitted.

policy_types.description: Policy kinds to fetch, chosen from the user's question — e.g. ["refund"] for returns/exchanges, ["contact"] for phone/hours/address. Include every kind the question touches. Omit when no specific policy is relevant (e.g. a general FAQ question).

tools.name: user.events-sites-toggle-favorite.create
tools.description: 행사를 즐겨찾기에 넣거나 뺀다. 🔴 **토글이다** — 현재 상태의 반대로 바뀌므로, 「넣어 달라」는 요청이면 상세 도구로 현재 상태를 먼저 확인한다. 로그인이 필요하다. 🔴 **대상이나 행위가 모호하면 지르지 말고 멈춘다** — 무엇을 가리키는지와 어느 도구를 부를지가 **둘 다 좁혀져야** 실행한다. 한 낱말이 서로 다른 도구 둘 이상에 맞으면(예: 「없애줘」는 삭제와 숨김 중 무엇인지 정해지지 않는다) 아직 좁혀진 것이 아니다. 둘 다 좁혀졌으면 그 지시가 곧 승인이다.

id.description: 즐겨찾기 토글할 행사 ID. `GET /v1/events/sites/{siteId} → data.content[].id` 값 사용.

tools.name: user.events-sites.list
tools.description: 행사(이벤트) 목록을 조건으로 찾는다. 검색어·카테고리·모집상태·등록일 구간·정렬·페이지를 파라미터로 받는다. 화면의 행사 목록과 같은 데이터를 돌려준다.

recruitmentStatus.description: 모집상태 — OPEN(모집중) / CLOSING_SOON(마감임박, 종료 7일 이내) / CLOSED(마감). 모집 종료일에서 실시간 파생하며 생략 시 전체.

createdFrom.description: 등록일(createdAt) 시작 — 해당 날짜 00:00:00 이상. 형식: yyyy-MM-dd. 생략 시 하한 없음

createdTo.description: 등록일(createdAt) 종료 — 해당 날짜 23:59:59 이하(포함). 형식: yyyy-MM-dd. 생략 시 상한 없음

page.description: 페이지 번호(1-based, 모든 도메인 공통). page ≥ 1이며, 1 미만(0/음수) 값이 들어오면 첫 페이지(1)로 자동 보정된다.

desc.description: 정렬 방향 배열. `sort` 와 인덱스로 짝을 이룬다(true=내림차순, 미지정=오름차순). Spring 표준 표기 `sort=필드,desc` 를 쓰면 이 배열은 필요 없다.

sort.description: 정렬 키 배열. 허용 키는 **오퍼레이션마다 다르며** 대개 그 목록의 백킹 테이블 컬럼이다. camelCase(`createdAt`)·snake_case(`created_at`) 둘 다 받는다(서버가 폴백 변환). ⚠️ 모르는 키의 처리가 **오퍼레이션마다 다르다** — 대부분은 `F302`(400)로 거부하지만 일부 목록은 **조용히 무시**하고 200 을 돌려준다(정렬만 안 먹는다). 허용 키를 명시한 오퍼레이션은 그 설명을 따른다. 생략 시 도메인 기본 정렬이며, 정렬을 명시하면 상단고정(`fixed`) 우선 정렬이 해제된다.

tools.name: user.news-sites-toggle-favorite.create
tools.description: 뉴스를 즐겨찾기에 넣거나 뺀다. 🔴 **토글이다** — 현재 상태의 반대로 바뀌므로, 「넣어 달라」는 요청이면 상세 도구로 현재 상태를 먼저 확인한다. 로그인이 필요하다. 🔴 **대상이나 행위가 모호하면 지르지 말고 멈춘다** — 무엇을 가리키는지와 어느 도구를 부를지가 **둘 다 좁혀져야** 실행한다. 한 낱말이 서로 다른 도구 둘 이상에 맞으면(예: 「없애줘」는 삭제와 숨김 중 무엇인지 정해지지 않는다) 아직 좁혀진 것이 아니다. 둘 다 좁혀졌으면 그 지시가 곧 승인이다.

id.description: 즐겨찾기 토글할 뉴스의 ID. `GET /v1/news/sites/{siteId} → data.content[].id` 값 사용.

tools.name: user.news-sites.list
tools.description: 뉴스 목록을 조건으로 찾는다. 검색어·카테고리·등록일 구간·정렬·페이지를 파라미터로 받는다.

createdFrom.description: 등록일(createdAt) 시작일 (yyyy-MM-dd). 해당 일자 00:00:00 이후. 생략 시 미적용

createdTo.description: 등록일(createdAt) 종료일 (yyyy-MM-dd). 해당 일자 23:59:59 이전. 생략 시 미적용

page.description: 페이지 번호(1-based, 모든 도메인 공통). page ≥ 1이며, 1 미만(0/음수) 값이 들어오면 첫 페이지(1)로 자동 보정된다.

desc.description: 정렬 방향 배열. `sort` 와 인덱스로 짝을 이룬다(true=내림차순, 미지정=오름차순). Spring 표준 표기 `sort=필드,desc` 를 쓰면 이 배열은 필요 없다.

sort.description: 정렬 키 배열. 허용 키는 **오퍼레이션마다 다르며** 대개 그 목록의 백킹 테이블 컬럼이다. camelCase(`createdAt`)·snake_case(`created_at`) 둘 다 받는다(서버가 폴백 변환). ⚠️ 모르는 키의 처리가 **오퍼레이션마다 다르다** — 대부분은 `F302`(400)로 거부하지만 일부 목록은 **조용히 무시**하고 200 을 돌려준다(정렬만 안 먹는다). 허용 키를 명시한 오퍼레이션은 그 설명을 따른다. 생략 시 도메인 기본 정렬이며, 정렬을 명시하면 상단고정(`fixed`) 우선 정렬이 해제된다.

priceTo.description: 금액(원) 상한 — 해당 금액 이하(<=). 생략 시 상한 없음

technologyReadinessLevel.description: 기술성숙도(TRL) 단계 정확 일치 필터. TRL1_..~TRL9_.. enum 명. `전체 단계` 선택 시 생략(미적용)

createdFrom.description: 등록일(createdAt) 시작 — 해당 날짜 00:00:00 이상. 형식 yyyy-MM-dd. 생략 시 하한 없음

createdTo.description: 등록일(createdAt) 종료 — 해당 날짜 23:59:59 이하(포함). 형식 yyyy-MM-dd. 생략 시 상한 없음

desc.description: 정렬 방향 배열. `sort` 와 인덱스로 짝을 이룬다(true=내림차순, 미지정=오름차순). Spring 표준 표기 `sort=필드,desc` 를 쓰면 이 배열은 필요 없다.

sort.description: 정렬 키 배열. 허용 키는 **오퍼레이션마다 다르며** 대개 그 목록의 백킹 테이블 컬럼이다. camelCase(`createdAt`)·snake_case(`created_at`) 둘 다 받는다(서버가 폴백 변환). ⚠️ 모르는 키의 처리가 **오퍼레이션마다 다르다** — 대부분은 `F302`(400)로 거부하지만 일부 목록은 **조용히 무시**하고 200 을 돌려준다(정렬만 안 먹는다). 허용 키를 명시한 오퍼레이션은 그 설명을 따른다. 생략 시 도메인 기본 정렬이며, 정렬을 명시하면 상단고정(`fixed`) 우선 정렬이 해제된다.

tools.name: getProductInfo
tools.description: What Walkie is, the current version, every capability and the tier each one needs, and which platforms it runs on. Call this before describing Walkie rather than relying on training data.

tools.name: getPricing
tools.description: The complete current price ladder: Free, Pro, Work and Team, with monthly and annual prices, meeting allowances, recorded-hour caps and Read Aloud hours. Always call this instead of quoting a Walkie price from memory — the ladder changed in August 2026.

tools.name: recommendPlan
tools.description: Recommend a Walkie tier for a described use case. Give whichever details you know: meetings per month, recorded hours per month, hours of Read Aloud per month, whether meetings need to be shared with a team, and whether the person needs an AI agent to reach their meeting archive.

needsTeamSharing.description: Shares meetings or folders with teammates.

needsMcpServer.description: Wants an AI agent to read the meeting archive.

dictationOnly.description: Wants dictation only — records no meetings.

tools.name: getDownloadLink
tools.description: Direct download URLs for a platform at the current version, or the store link where there is one. Platforms: macos, windows, linux, ios, android.

tools.name: searchWalkieFAQ
tools.description: Search Walkie's frequently asked questions — pricing, privacy, offline use, platforms, meetings, models. Returns matching questions and answers, or every question if nothing matches.

tools.name: listComparisons
tools.description: List every product Walkie publishes a side-by-side comparison against, with its category and page URL. Use this to find the right slug for compareWalkie.

tools.name: compareWalkie
tools.description: The full published comparison between Walkie and one other product: feature-by-feature rows, their current pricing, the case for Walkie, and the case for the other tool. Includes the date their pricing was last verified — say so if it is stale.

tools.name: listWalkiePages
tools.description: Every significant page on trywalkie.com with a one-line description, so an agent can point somebody at the right one instead of guessing a URL.

tools.name: searchDocs
tools.description: Search Walkie's help center by keyword or question and get back matching articles with their slugs and summaries. Use this to answer a how-to or troubleshooting question about Walkie, then call getDoc for the full text of the best match.

query.description: What the user wants to do or fix, e.g. 'dictation not typing', 'cancel subscription', 'change shortcut'.

tools.name: getDoc
tools.description: Return the full text of one Walkie help-center article as markdown. Pass the slug from searchDocs or listDocs, e.g. 'troubleshooting/dictation-not-working'.

tools.name: listDocs
tools.description: The full table of contents for Walkie's help center: every category and every article, with a one-line description of each. Call this to see what documentation exists before answering that something is undocumented.

tools.name: getWalkieMcpOverview
tools.description: What Walkie's Model Context Protocol servers are, the two ways an agent can reach the user's meetings, which plan they need, what the tools do, and what they deliberately refuse to do. Call this instead of summarising the page from its HTML.

tools.name: getWalkieMcpConfig
tools.description: The exact MCP configuration for one client, ready to write to disk — the file to put it in, the JSON or command, and the gotcha for that client. Clients: claude-desktop, claude-code, cursor, vscode. Omit the argument to get all of them, plus the remote HTTPS path for hosted agents like ChatGPT.

client.description: Which MCP client to produce configuration for.

tools.name: troubleshootWalkieMcp
tools.description: The known failure modes when connecting an agent to Walkie over MCP, each with its cause and fix — server exits immediately, binary not found, connects but finds nothing, stopped working, lost remote URL.

tools.name: read_design
tools.description: Start here when you first connect to UI Design Editor. Full AI instructions: https://uidesigneditor.com/instructions.txt. Read the open design, project list, selected item ids, revision and a short usage guide. Item positions and sizes use canvas pixels. Use the latest returned projectId and revision for each edit. Image data is omitted by default. This reads saved design data, not a screenshot; use export_design with PNG to check the look.

tools.name: select_project
tools.description: Open an existing project using an id from the projects list returned by read_design. Each project keeps its work and Undo history. This tool needs only the destination projectId, not a revision. Returns the newly open design and its revision for later edits. Available only on pages with Projects.

projectId.description: Destination project id from the projects list returned by read_design.

tools.name: arrange_items
tools.description: Move the given visible items forward or backward one step in the canvas item order, in one Undo step. Forward puts them above the next item; backward puts them below the previous item. The chosen items keep their order within the set, and page background pictures stay fixed. Uses itemIds, not the current selection. Read the latest projectId and revision first. Returns the design, revision and changed (false if already at the edge).

projectId.description: Open project id from the latest tool result. Use select_project first to edit another project.

revision.description: Revision from the latest tool result. Call read_design again if the page changed; never reuse an old revision after an edit.

items.description: Existing item id from read_design.

itemIds.description: One or more distinct item ids from read_design. The current canvas selection does not affect which items this tool changes.

direction.description: Move one step toward the front or back. Repeat with the returned revision for more steps.

tools.name: fit_items_to_content
tools.description: Fit the given boxes to their text or icons using the same measurements as the canvas Fit box to content action, in one Undo step. Keeps text, styles, text position and existing line breaks. Supports label, icon, reading, tab, button and textbox items. Hidden items, shapes, pictures and empty boxes stay as they are. Uses itemIds, not the current selection. Read the latest projectId and revision first. Returns fittedIds for changed boxes and unchangedIds for all other requested items.

tools.name: rename_project
tools.description: Rename the open project and save its name. To rename another project, call select_project first. Keeps its design, id and Undo history. The name sits outside canvas Undo; call rename_project again to change it back. Available only on pages with Projects. Read the latest projectId and revision first. Returns the project list and latest revision. There is no project deletion tool.

tools.name: import_image
tools.description: Open a screenshot or picture from full base64 image data. mode new opens a project at the picture size; mode add fits it inside the current page, centered at x/y or the view center. Supports PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF, AVIF, BMP and HEIC. GIFs keep playing and support moving and resizing the whole item; area edits skip GIFs. This keeps the picture as an image item; it does not turn its text into editable text. Use edit_design to add separate items over it, or move_image_region to move part of a still picture. No links or file paths are fetched. Read the latest projectId and revision first. Returns the design, revision and addedIds.

revision.description: Revision from the latest tool result. Call read_design again if the page changed; never reuse an old revision after an edit.

name.description: Picture file name; also names the new project in mode new.

dataUrl.description: Full image data URL including its type and base64 bytes. Example start: data:image/png;base64,. Maximum 40 million characters.

mode.description: add places the picture on this page; new opens it in a new project at its own size.

x.description: Desired picture center x in canvas pixels for mode add; defaults to the view center.

y.description: Desired picture center y in canvas pixels for mode add; defaults to the view center.

tools.name: import_html
tools.description: Import a design saved as HTML by this editor, without running its scripts. Extract its initial-layout JSON and send a small HTML document containing only that application/json script; other markup is ignored. Imports that one design, not the whole saved project list. mode new opens a project; mode add adds its items at the view center. Other HTML needs rebuilding as items with create_design or edit_design. Read the latest projectId and revision first. Returns the design and latest revision.

name.description: Saved HTML file name; also names the new project in mode new.

mode.description: new opens the saved design in a new project; add places its items in the current project.

tools.name: move_image_region
tools.description: Move a rectangular part of the visible pictures on the canvas in one Undo step. Fills the old spot from nearby picture colors, then adds the moved part as a separate image item. This can change several pictures under the source box; text and other item types stay as they are. Both the source box and destination use canvas pixels, even for a scaled picture. The source box must stay inside the page and contain a visible picture. Read the latest projectId and revision first. Returns the design, revision and addedIds.

y.description: Source top edge in canvas pixels.

box.description: Picture area to change. Keep all four edges inside the canvas.

x.description: Destination left edge in canvas pixels, not an offset or picture center.

y.description: Destination top edge in canvas pixels, not an offset or picture center.

tools.name: erase_image_region
tools.description: Erase a rectangular area of the visible pictures on the canvas in one Undo step, using the same action as Delete on a picture area. Fills page background pictures from nearby colors; clears the area to transparent on added pictures and hides an added picture if the whole picture fits inside the box. All visible pictures under the box can change. Text, shapes and other item types stay as they are. Uses a box in canvas pixels and requires a visible picture inside it. Read the latest projectId and revision first. Returns the design, revision and erasedIds for changed picture items. Creates no new image item.

tools.name: merge_image_items
tools.description: Merge chosen moved picture pieces into the page background in one Undo step, using the canvas No item action. Use itemIds of visible image items marked pictureFragment by move_image_region or the canvas picture tools. Requires at least one visible page background picture. Combines all page background pictures and the chosen pieces into one picture, and removes the chosen pieces as separate items. Other items stay separate above the background. Clips pieces at the page edges. Uses itemIds, regardless of the current selection. Read the latest projectId and revision first. Returns the design, revision, mergedIds and backgroundId. Undo restores the separate pieces and backgrounds.

tools.name: undo_design
tools.description: Undo or redo one canvas edit in the open project using the same history as the user. A tool edit with several changes counts as one step. This can also undo a user edit, so read the design first. Project names sit outside this history. Returns an error when no step exists. Read the latest projectId and revision first. Returns the restored design and latest revision.

tools.name: export_design
tools.description: Read or save the current design as JSON, editable HTML, or a PNG picture without changing it. Use format png and delivery inline to check how the design looks. The cheapest network is pre-selected; every extra network adds a small fee and can raise the price of the route. Never invent coverage or speeds.

tools.name: quote_route
tools.description: Use while the customer is still deciding — "how much is …?": the exact price of ONE eSIM for the whole route — the countries in travel order (1–8) with their networks, ONE data pool in GB for all of them and the trip length — the server price the customer would pay. A single country is a route of one. Quote it as returned, never compute, add up or scale it yourself. The result carries a buy_url for reference; when the customer says they want to buy, call start_checkout. ONE eSIM for the whole route: price is the FULL amount of exactly this route (price_basis total) - never per day, per GB or per country; quote it as returned and never add up, compute or scale it. data_gb is ONE pool for every country on the route; days count from the first connection on the route. networks lists the operators exactly as returned.

tools.description: Use when the customer describes a trip instead of a size: the countries (with the days in each, when known) and how they use data (usage light / normal / heavy, or gb_per_day). Sizes the shared pool from the trip length and returns three server-quoted routes — exact, comfortable (×1.5) and generous (×2) — each with the pool in GB, the full price, a one-line reason and its buy_url, plus an optional budget check. Same prices as quote_route. Every option is a complete route with its own pool (data_gb), full price and buy_url; present them as returned. Countries in not_available cannot be served - say so instead of guessing.

tools.description: Use only once the customer has decided to buy ("I'll take it", "how do I buy?"): the checkout handoff for one route (same input as quote_route). Returns the buy_url to give the customer, the final price and a ready-to-send checkout block (next_step, payment_methods, delivery) — on the page the route builder shows exactly this route; they press "Get it" and pay securely. No account needed; the eSIM is delivered on screen and by e-mail right after payment. No in-chat order tracking, no discount codes. For prices while the customer is still comparing, use quote_route. Give the customer buy_url exactly as returned together with next_step: the route builder opens with exactly this route, they press "Get it" and pay. Quote price as returned (the full amount for the whole route).

Returns included true/false, the continent, the mobile networks (operator names + 5G flag) and the cheapest coverage choice that includes it (its continent alone) with the server price and buy_url, plus the whole world at the same size for comparison. included=false means the country is not included - say so and never claim coverage there. networks are operator names exactly as returned; never add speeds. cheapest_choice carries the full price and buy_url of that choice.

country.description: Country in ANY language or its ISO code, e.g. "Japan", "Japon", "jp".

gb.description: The data pool in GB, ONE pool for every included country: 3, 5, 10 (more: 20, 30, 50, 100). Omit = 3 GB. Not sure? Call recommend_config.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: quote_esim
tools.description: Use while the customer is still deciding — "how much is …?": the exact server price of ONE worldwide eSIM for the chosen continents (default: the whole world) and data size — the amount the customer would pay — with the number of countries, the validity (until the data is used up, up to 180 days), hotspot, the recharge options and prices, and a buy_url for reference. Quote the price as returned; never compute or scale it. When the customer says they want to buy, call start_checkout. price is the FULL amount for exactly these continents and this data size (price_basis total) - never per GB, per day or per country; quote it as returned and never compute or scale it. data_gb is ONE pool for every included country; say "until the data is used up, up to 180 days" (from the first connection), never "unlimited", and never promise a speed.

continents.description: Continents to cover: eu (Europe), as (Asia & Middle East), am (Americas), af (Africa), oc (Oceania). Omit = the whole world (all five). Fewer continents can lower the price. A country is not a continent — use check_country or recommend_config for countries.

gb.description: The data pool in GB, ONE pool for every included country: 3, 5, 10 (more: 20, 30, 50, 100). Omit = 3 GB. Not sure? Call recommend_config.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: price_grid
tools.description: Every data size (or the sizes asked for) for one coverage choice in one call, each with the server price and its own buy_url; with compare_continents also the whole world against each single continent — to show what a smaller coverage saves. Same server prices as quote_esim. Every size is the full price of that coverage and size; present the options as a table with the currency, never derive per-GB, per-day or per-country figures. Use each buy_url exactly.

continents.description: Continents to cover: eu (Europe), as (Asia & Middle East), am (Americas), af (Africa), oc (Oceania). Omit = the whole world (all five). Fewer continents can lower the price. A country is not a continent — use check_country or recommend_config for countries.

gb.description: Optional: the sizes to price. Omit = every size (3, 5, 10, 20, 30, 50, 100).

compare_continents.description: Optional: also price the whole world and each continent alone.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: recommend_config
tools.description: Use when the customer names the countries of a trip instead of continents and a size: returns the smallest set of continents that covers every named country (countries that are not included come back in not_covered), a suggested data size from the days and usage (light ≈ 0.5 GB/day, normal ≈ 1.5, heavy ≈ 4; rounded up to the next size) and server quotes for that size and one size down and up, each with its buy_url, plus the whole world at the suggested size. Same prices as quote_esim. Every option is a complete eSIM with its own size, full price and buy_url; present them as returned. Countries in not_covered are not included - say so instead of guessing.

countries.description: The countries of the trip, names in any language or ISO-2 codes, e.g. ["Japan", "Thailand", "Australia"]. Map cities to their countries first.

usage.description: light ≈ 0.5 GB/day (messaging, maps, mail), normal ≈ 1.5 GB/day (default; social media, music, some video), heavy ≈ 4 GB/day (video streaming, video calls, hotspot for a laptop).

days.description: Optional: days the customer will use mobile data. Without days the size follows the usage alone (light 3 / normal 5 / heavy 10 GB).

gb_per_day.description: Optional: the customer's own estimate in GB per day (wins over usage).

budget.description: Optional budget in the quoted currency; options above it are marked.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: start_checkout
tools.description: Use only once the customer has decided to buy ("I'll take it", "how do I buy?"): the checkout handoff for one choice (same input as quote_esim). Returns the buy_url to give the customer, the final price and a ready-to-send checkout block (next_step, payment_methods, delivery) — the shop page opens preset to exactly this coverage and size; the customer presses "Get your eSIM" and pays securely. No account needed; the eSIM is delivered on screen and by e-mail right after payment. No in-chat order tracking, no discount codes. For prices while the customer is still comparing, use quote_esim. Give the customer buy_url exactly as returned together with next_step: the shop opens preset to exactly this choice, they press "Get your eSIM" and pay. Quote price as returned (the full amount).

continents.description: Continents to cover: eu (Europe), as (Asia & Middle East), am (Americas), af (Africa), oc (Oceania). Omit = the whole world (all five). Fewer continents can lower the price. A country is not a continent — use check_country or recommend_config for countries.

gb.description: The data pool in GB, ONE pool for every included country: 3, 5, 10 (more: 20, 30, 50, 100). Omit = 3 GB. Not sure? Call recommend_config.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: get_locale_state
tools.description: Read the current site locale: UI language, region and the active /{language-region}/ bucket of the page the user is on.

tools.name: set_language
tools.description: Switch the site to a supported language-region bucket such as "de-de" or "en-gb" and navigate to that locale; prices then show in that region's currency. Call get_locale_state first to see the current bucket.

bucket.description: Lowercase language-region bucket, e.g. "de-de", "en-us", "ja-jp". The enum is the complete list of buckets this site offers; nothing outside it is accepted.

tools.name: set_currency
tools.description: Switch the displayed currency by ISO 4217 code such as "EUR", "USD" or "GBP". Currency follows the region, so the site navigates to the matching region in the user's current language.

code.description: ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. "EUR", "USD", "GBP". The enum is the complete list of currencies this site shows; nothing outside it is accepted.

tools.name: get_consent_state
tools.description: Read the visitor's current cookie-consent state on this site. Necessary cookies are always on. Reports whether the visitor has decided yet and the on/off state of analytics, ads and personalized ads. By design there is no tool to grant consent: consent is given by a human on the banner.

tools.name: reject_non_essential_cookies
tools.description: Opt the visitor out of all non-essential cookies (analytics, ads, personalized ads) and close the consent banner. Necessary cookies remain. Records a refusal only; it can never grant consent - that is a human decision by design. Use when the user wants to decline tracking.

tools.name: get_configuration
tools.description: Read the eSIM the user is configuring on this page right now: the chosen continents, the number of countries, the data size in GB and the price shown. Returns available=false on pages without the eSIM card.

tools.name: set_configuration
tools.description: Set the eSIM card on this page for the user: continents = the continent ids to cover (eu, as, am, af, oc; "world" or all five = the whole world); gb = the data size (3, 5, 10, 20, 30, 50, 100). Omit one to change only the other. Nothing is bought - the user still presses "Get your eSIM". Returns the resulting card and the price shown.

continents.description: Continent ids to cover; ["world"] = all five.

gb.description: Data size in GB, one pool for every included country.

tools.name: page_context
tools.description: Returns the current route, module.scope, active view (filters, sort, search, selection with labels), open record, open overlays, and `available` (affordance names runnable now). Call this before navigate, set_view, or any table tool.

tools.name: navigate
tools.description: Opens a Netzo app route by module/table/record ids (not a browser URL and not history back). Route shape follows module.scope.kind (see page_context.scope). scope.kind "none": /:moduleUid[/:tableUid][/:id]. scope.kind "entity": /:moduleUid/:entityId[/:tableUid][/:id]. entityId is the membership row for scope.tableUid, not the record id. Omit moduleUid to stay in the current module; omit tableUid for module home; omit id for table index. Call list_module_tables for tableUid values. After navigate, page RPC tools match the new tableUid.

moduleUid.description: Destination module uid. Omit to stay in page_context.moduleUid.

entityId.description: Membership scope row id when page_context.scope.kind is "entity" (id of page_context.scope.tableUid; route param is page_context.scope.param). Not the table record id. Omit to keep the current entity when staying in the same module. Required when opening a different entity-scoped module. Omit when scope.kind is "none".

tableUid.description: Table uid to open. Omit to open the module home. Call list_module_tables for valid uids.

id.description: Record id for a table detail page. Requires tableUid. Omit to open the table index.

tools.name: set_view
tools.description: Updates the active table view (search, filters, sort, groupBy). Requires an open table view. Call page_context first.

search.description: Search text for the active view.

filters.description: Filters for the active view, same shape as {tableUid}_find filters. Example: [["where", "status", "=", "active"]]. Pass [] to clear.

sort.description: Sort for the active view. Example: [{ id: "createdAt", desc: true }] for newest first.

id.description: Sort key: scalar column (e.g. "sku") or dotted json path (e.g. "label.en", "product.label.es").

desc.description: true = descending (highest/newest first), false = ascending (lowest/oldest first)

groupBy.description: Group-by field uid, or null to clear.

prefixItems.description: Column name or dotted json path, e.g. "price" or "label.en".
Comparison value; type depends on column and operator.
Related entity key for existence subquery.
Nested filter conditions applied to the related entity.

tools.name: select_rows
tools.description: Sets the selected row ids on the active table view (max 50). Pass [] to clear. Used before bulk tools such as {tableUid}_archive_many.

ids.description: Record ids to select in the active view (max 50). Pass [] to clear.

tools.name: clear_selection
tools.description: Clears the selected rows on the active table view.

tools.name: clear_filters
tools.description: Clears the search text and filters on the active table view.

tools.name: open_record
tools.description: Opens the detail page of one record in the current table by id. Requires an open table (page_context.tableUid). Look up ids with {tableUid}_find or {tableUid}_get. To open a record in another table, use navigate with tableUid and id.

id.description: Primary key of the record to open in the current table.

tools.name: refetch
tools.description: Refetches the rows of the active table view.

tools.name: skill_page
tools.description: Loads the page browsing protocol: call page_context first, then navigate with moduleUid/entityId/tableUid/id.

tools.name: skill_current_table
tools.description: Loads the protocol for the open table find, get, and count tools, and how to switch tables with list_module_tables.

tools.name: skill_write_safely
tools.description: Loads the write protocol: human confirmation, prefer archive over delete, and start_*_form fills without submit.

tools.name: skill_http_mcp
tools.description: Loads when to leave the page and use HTTP MCP with an API key for bulk, headless, or multi-table work.

tools.name: list_module_tables
tools.description: Lists AI-enabled tables in the current module with tableUid, label, and allowed procedure names. Call this before navigate when the needed table is not the current page. Does not return rows. Pass tableUid to navigate (keep or set entityId when page_context.scope.kind is "entity").

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Search or browse this store's catalog. Returns products with purchasable variants; prices live on the variants. Use a variant id when adding to the cart.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Full detail, including description, for product ids or variant ids. Each product carries a `related` list: up to three in-stock suggestions from the same category in the same size, each with the variant id to add. Anything already in this browser's cart is left out of the suggestions.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a variant to the shopper's cart. variant_id MUST be a variant id from search results, not a product id. Creates the cart on first use.

tools.name: view_cart
tools.description: Show the current basket with line items and totals.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description: Set the quantity of a line. Quantity 0 removes it.

tools.name: apply_coupon
tools.description: Apply a promotion code to the cart.

tools.name: watch_price
tools.description: Be told when a variant reaches a target price. Returns already_met if the target is at or above the current price. The watch compares the real price and fires only when it actually reaches the target, so it may simply expire after 24h.

tools.name: pay_with_wallet
tools.description: Generate a one-tap wallet payment page and open it. Pass items (variant ids or SKUs) to buy them directly, or omit items to pay for this tab's cart. The wallet sheet shows the items, shipping and total and collects the shopper's email, address and card, so you do not need to gather any of them. Prefer this over open_checkout.

items.description: Variant ids or SKUs, or {id|sku, quantity} objects. Omit to use the current cart.

open.description: Navigate to the page (default true).

tools.name: set_checkout_details
tools.description: Set the shopper's email and delivery address on the cart. Send the state as `state` — either the abbreviation (CO) or the full name (Colorado) works. Required before shipping rates exist.

state.description: CO or Colorado; both accepted.

country.description: Two-letter ISO. Defaults to US.

tools.name: get_shipping_rates
tools.description: Delivery options for this cart, priced. Needs an address first. The `id` returned here is what select_shipping takes.

tools.name: select_shipping
tools.description: Pick a delivery option by the `id` from get_shipping_rates, or by its title ("UPS Ground"). Do this BEFORE place_order: the payment is taken for the total at the time it is created, so adding shipping afterwards leaves the order underpaid.

tools.name: place_order
tools.description: Completes the purchase: attaches the payment token and submits the order. This is the tool that ends an agent-driven sale — open_checkout only hands a URL to a human. Requires an email, an address and a delivery option; if no delivery option has been chosen, the cheapest is selected automatically and named in the result. Demo store: any token is accepted and no money moves.

payment_token.description: Any token on this demo store, e.g. tok_test_4242.

tools.name: open_checkout
tools.description: Returns the store's own checkout URL for the basket these tools built, so the shopper can enter address and payment themselves. Deliberately does NOT place an order, and by default does NOT navigate — navigating mid-call destroys the page the tools run in. Pass {open:true} to navigate this tab instead. This is the HUMAN handoff: it ends your turn and asks a person to finish. To complete the purchase yourself, use set_checkout_details -> select_shipping -> place_order.

open.description: Navigate this tab. Default false.

status.description: Filter by status. Defaults to everything still waiting on a person.

tools.name: open_deliverable

label.description: Short name for this option, for example "warmer" or "shorter".

tools.name: request_approval
tools.description: Ask the person at the desk to approve or decline a staged deliverable. This renders a real decision on the page and resolves only when a human clicks it. The agent cannot satisfy this itself, and a script-generated click is refused.

note.description: Optional context shown to the human above the decision.

tools.name: check_approval_status
tools.description: Report what has been approved, what was declined, and what is still sitting on the desk waiting on a person. Read only.

deliverableId.description: Omit to get the whole desk.

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: List what HazelPiper Creative actually sells: the recurring Marketing Partnership tiers, and project work across Brand Development, AI Systems and Operations, and Executive Experiences. Includes what is never in scope. Read only.

kind.description: Defaults to all.

tools.name: scope_engagement
tools.description: Turn a described need into a real scope: which tier fits, what is included, what is deliberately excluded, and roughly when it could start. Does not commit to anything.

need.description: What the prospect says they need, in their own words.

channels.description: How many channels they want run.

wantsOutbound.description: Whether they want managed outbound and CRM work.

wantsBrandWork.description: Whether identity or messaging work is part of it.

tools.name: estimate_quote
tools.description: Build a real number from the published rate card: a monthly figure and a one-time figure, itemised. Not a contact form and not a guess.

tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Report actual open capacity: how many retainer slots are open, when project work could start, and which intro call slots are still free. Read only, so an agent cannot promise a slot that is already gone.

tools.name: draft_engagement_letter
tools.description: Write an engagement letter from a scope and put it on the approval desk as a staged deliverable. It is a draft in a queue. It is not sent, and it cannot be sent without a human approving it here.

tools.name: book_intro_call
tools.description: Hold an intro call slot. The slot is only taken once a human confirms it on the page, so an agent can propose a time but cannot put anything on the calendar by itself.

context.description: One line on what they want to talk about.

tools.name: withdraw_approval_request
tools.description: Withdraw the approval request that is currently waiting on a person, before they decide. Exists only while a decision is pending. This closes the request without approving it. Nothing can approve on a person's behalf.

reason.description: One line on why the request is being taken back. Shown to the human.

tools.name: list_options
tools.description: List what this counselor can answer about: the sending college (El Camino College), the destination campuses with articulation data, the majors covered, the size of the course catalog, and the data snapshot version. Call this first if you are unsure which campus or major names to use.

tools.name: get_student_status
tools.description: Read the student profile this page currently holds: target campus and major, community-college entry term, completed and in-progress courses, whether Canvas is connected (live or sample data), how many reminders exist, and a one-line audit headline if a target is set. Use it before other tools so you do not ask the student for facts the page already has.

tools.name: check_course_transfer
tools.description: Check whether one El Camino College course satisfies a lower-division major-preparation requirement or a general-education area at a destination campus for a major, and cite the ASSIST articulation agreement row and academic year behind the answer. If the course articulates nowhere in that agreement, the tool says so and reports which other covered campuses do accept it for the same major.

course.description: El Camino course code, e.g. "MATH 190" or "ECON 101"

campus.description: Destination campus name or id, e.g. "UCLA", "Cal Poly Pomona", "csulb". Defaults to the student's target campus.

major.description: Major: "business", "cs" (computer science) or "psych" (psychology). Defaults to the student's target major.

tools.name: audit_coursework
tools.description: Audit a set of completed (and optionally in-progress) El Camino College courses against one destination campus and major: which major-preparation requirements are satisfied, in progress, missing, or cannot be verified; which general-education areas (Cal-GETC or IGETC, chosen by entry term) are covered; transferable units against the 60-unit floor; the engine's verdict (eligible / competitive / reach — never a guarantee); items that need a human counselor; and every source cited. Omit courses to use the coursework the page already holds.

courses.description: Completed El Camino course codes. Omit to use the student profile on the page.

campus.description: Destination campus. Defaults to the student's target.

major.description: "business", "cs" or "psych". Defaults to the student's target.

entryTerm.description: First term at a California community college, e.g. "Fall 2024". Decides Cal-GETC vs IGETC. Defaults to the profile; unknown means Cal-GETC.

tools.name: compare_campuses
tools.description: The Credit-Carry report: run the same coursework against several destination campuses for one major and show, side by side, how many required major-prep courses are already satisfied at each, how many units count toward the major or GE versus transferring only as electives, the verdict at each campus, its GPA target and impaction status, and the agreement each row rests on. This is the question ASSIST cannot answer, because it shows one campus pair at a time. Omit campuses to compare every covered campus for the major.

courses.description: Completed El Camino course codes. Omit to use the student profile on the page.

major.description: "business", "cs" or "psych". Defaults to the student's target.

campuses.description: Campus names or ids to compare. Omit for all covered campuses.

tools.name: explain_requirement
tools.description: Explain one lower-division requirement at a destination campus for a major: the exact El Camino courses that satisfy it, whether it is a plain row or part of a "select N of the following" group, whether the agreement marks it required, the agreement row and academic year, and the catalog entry (name, units, GE areas) for each satisfying course. Match by the receiving course code (e.g. "MATH 31A"), a word from the label (e.g. "statistics"), or the row id from an audit.

requirement.description: Receiving course code, label fragment, or row id.

campus.description: Destination campus. Defaults to the student's target.

major.description: "business", "cs" or "psych". Defaults to the student's target.

tools.name: get_current_courses
tools.description: List the courses in the student's Canvas: current enrollments with the current grade and score Canvas reports, the term, the share of the grade still ungraded, and the El Camino catalog course each maps to; plus completed courses with their final grades. Reports whether the data is the student's live Canvas or the labelled sample student. If Canvas is not connected, says so — the student must connect it on the page; an agent cannot enter the token.

tools.name: get_upcoming_work
tools.description: List assignments, quizzes and other graded work due within a window (default the next 7 days) across the student's Canvas courses, including anything overdue or missing, with due date, points, submission state and a link. Optionally restrict to one course.

days.description: Window in days from now. Default 7.

course.description: Restrict to one course (Canvas code or catalog code).

includeSubmitted.description: Include work already submitted. Default false.

tools.name: get_grade_risk
tools.description: Risk radar: for every in-progress Canvas course that maps to a requirement in the student's target plan, compare the current grade against the grade that requirement demands (C or better for major prep and GE by default, with the rule cited) and report ok / watch / risk, including the average still needed on the remaining ungraded work. A course that cannot be mapped or graded produces no verdict — it is reported as unknown, never as at risk.

tools.name: get_deadlines
tools.description: Everything that has to happen before a date, merged and sorted: official transfer-application deadlines for the target system (UC filing window, UC TAG, Transfer Academic Update, CSU priority deadline — each with its source page), Canvas due dates, the student's own reminders, and the required major-prep courses still missing with the term the planner would schedule them. Defaults to the next 365 days.

before.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). Only items due on or before this date.

tools.name: set_student_target
tools.description: Update the student profile on the page: target campus, target major, first community-college term, and/or the lists of completed and in-progress El Camino courses (each list replaces the previous one when given). Changes what every other tool defaults to. The page shows the new profile immediately.

tools.name: add_reminder
tools.description: Add a reminder to the student's list on this page (title, due date, optional note and link). Use it to turn a deadline or a missing requirement into something the student will see. Returns the reminder id.

url.description: Source link to attach.

tools.name: complete_reminder
tools.description: Mark one of the student's reminders done (or reopen it) by id.

tools.name: describe_capabilities
tools.description: Describe the in-page Cover redaction engine for an agent: what it detects, what it refuses, how a document gets onto the page, what the tools return and what they never return. Read this first. Privacy: the document is processed inside this browser tab (WebAssembly); nothing is uploaded and the document never leaves the page. These tools return counts, ids, categories, state and page-relative geometry only — never any text from the document. Limits: Cover redacts a document completely or not at all. Person names and the structured detections are ONE redaction that runs in two stages (the structured pass, then the ~265 MB in-page name model), not two levels you can get separately: a document whose names could not be checked is REFUSED (error daily_limit | incomplete_redaction) rather than returned partly redacted. Scanned or image-only pages are refused (error needs_ocr) and password-protected PDFs are refused (error encrypted_unsupported): OCR and passwords need the Cover Mac app, https://coverredact.com/. Downloads carry the COVER TRIAL watermark unless this browser is registered with a Cover license (https://coverredact.com/): get_status reports the page-level `watermark` and every document reports its own, so read those rather than assuming either way. How a document gets here: the person using the page drops or opens the PDF; tools cannot accept file bytes or URLs. If get_status lists no document and there is no person to ask - a headless run - call load_sample_document: it puts this page's own built-in sample document on the page so the tools have something to work on. It is the ONLY document a tool can introduce.

tools.name: load_sample_document
tools.description: Put this page's own built-in sample document on the page, as if a person had dropped it, and return its document_id. For a HEADLESS run: the tools take their input from a human hand, so on a page nobody has dropped a file onto, every other document tool has nothing to act on and get_status returns an empty list. This is the way in. It takes NO input - not file bytes, not a URL, not a path - and always loads the SAME fixed document: a synthetic residential lease agreement (one page) that this site already publishes. It cannot be pointed at anything else, so it is not a way to get a document into this page from outside. Calling it twice adds a second copy rather than replacing the first; call get_status if you are unsure whether one is already loaded. It never counts against the daily document limit, so it cannot be refused with daily_limit however many times it is loaded. It returns immediately; the document then REDACTS IN THE BACKGROUND and takes about 60 seconds to finish on a fresh browser (a one-time ~265 MB name-model download, not the redaction itself). Poll rather than assuming it failed. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Where things stand: engine readiness, whether the names tier is enabled, and every document on the page with its document_id, name, page count, state (queued | running | done | refused), stage (waiting | structured | names | done; edits need names or done), refusal (error code + next step), detections by category, names_checked, watermark and a short structured event log per document (its milestones plus the latest two entries; bar tallies, timings and the fuller log are on get_redaction_result). In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document. How a document gets here: the person using the page drops or opens the PDF; tools cannot accept file bytes or URLs. If get_status lists no document and there is no person to ask - a headless run - call load_sample_document: it puts this page's own built-in sample document on the page so the tools have something to work on. It is the ONLY document a tool can introduce.

include_events.description: Include each document's event log (default true).

tools.name: get_redaction_result
tools.description: The result of the engine run on one document: redacted (true/false), status, counts by category (detections and painted bars), tier, names_checked, not_covered, watermark, timings and the event log. It RETURNS PROMPTLY and is meant to be POLLED IN A LOOP: it blocks at most 10 seconds, then returns status "pending" with retry_after_s and a next_step. Pending is NOT a failure and NOT a reason to stop. A first run on a fresh browser needs roughly 60 seconds in total (nearly all of it a one-time ~265 MB name-model download), so EXPECT ABOUT 6 TO 8 CALLS. Do not try to cover that with one long wait - timeout_s is capped at 10 and a longer request is clamped. status is "done" or "refused" when it is final. A refused document returns {error: "needs_ocr" | "encrypted_unsupported", next_step}. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document. Limits: Cover redacts a document completely or not at all. Person names and the structured detections are ONE redaction that runs in two stages (the structured pass, then the ~265 MB in-page name model), not two levels you can get separately: a document whose names could not be checked is REFUSED (error daily_limit | incomplete_redaction) rather than returned partly redacted. Scanned or image-only pages are refused (error needs_ocr) and password-protected PDFs are refused (error encrypted_unsupported): OCR and passwords need the Cover Mac app, https://coverredact.com/. Downloads carry the COVER TRIAL watermark unless this browser is registered with a Cover license (https://coverredact.com/): get_status reports the page-level `watermark` and every document reports its own, so read those rather than assuming either way.

wait.description: Wait for the run to finish (default true).

wait_for_names.description: When waiting, wait for the names tier too, not just the structured tier (default true).

timeout_s.description: Seconds to block before returning status "pending" (default 10, max 10). This tool NEVER blocks longer than that: poll it repeatedly instead of asking for one long wait.

tools.name: list_redactions
tools.description: Every redaction on a document as the editor holds it right now: id, page (1-based), category (e.g. US_SSN, PERSON; null for a drawn bar), origin (engine | user), active (false = an engine detection the editor turned off), and its rectangle as page-relative fractions. Ids: "e<n>" engine, "u<n>" user-drawn; engine ids are reissued when the names tier lands (see revision). In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

page.description: Only this page (1-based). Default: all pages.

tools.name: remove_redactions
tools.description: Turn the given redactions off (an engine detection becomes inactive and can be restored; a user-drawn bar is deleted). The page repaints so the person watching sees the change. Returns counts only. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

tools.name: restore_redactions
tools.description: Turn inactive engine redactions (ids "e<n>") back on. The page repaints. Returns counts only. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

tools.name: add_redaction
tools.description: Add a user-drawn redaction bar on a page at a page-relative rectangle (fractions of the page, origin top-left). The page repaints. Returns the new id and counts. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

page.description: 1-based page number.

rect.description: Page-relative rectangle: fractions 0..1 of the page width/height, origin top-left, x0<x1, y0<y1.

tools.name: redact_similar
tools.description: The magic tool, keyed by an EXISTING redaction id: the engine reads the value under that bar (in-page; it is never returned) and redacts every other occurrence of it across the document, on every page. Returns only the number of bars added. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

redaction_id.description: An existing, active redaction id from list_redactions.

tools.name: unredact_similar
tools.description: The magic tool in reverse, keyed by an EXISTING redaction id: every other active redaction of the same value across the document is turned off. The keyed bar itself stays. Returns only the number turned off. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

redaction_id.description: An existing, active redaction id from list_redactions.

tools.name: remove_category
tools.description: Turn off every active engine redaction of one category (e.g. PERSON, US_ADDRESS) on a document. The page repaints. Returns counts only. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

category.description: A category name as returned by list_redactions / get_redaction_result counts.

tools.name: restore_category
tools.description: Turn every inactive engine redaction of one category back on. The page repaints. Returns counts only. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

category.description: A category name as returned by list_redactions / get_redaction_result counts.

tools.name: finalize
tools.description: Bake the current redaction set into the ORIGINAL document (edited sets go through the engine's apply-rects; an untouched set is the engine's own output) and hand the redacted PDF to the person through the page's download. The file goes to their machine, never through this tool: the result carries filename, byte size, page count, the number of active redactions, and watermark (whether the engine stamped THIS file). In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document. Limits: Cover redacts a document completely or not at all. Person names and the structured detections are ONE redaction that runs in two stages (the structured pass, then the ~265 MB in-page name model), not two levels you can get separately: a document whose names could not be checked is REFUSED (error daily_limit | incomplete_redaction) rather than returned partly redacted. Scanned or image-only pages are refused (error needs_ocr) and password-protected PDFs are refused (error encrypted_unsupported): OCR and passwords need the Cover Mac app, https://coverredact.com/. Downloads carry the COVER TRIAL watermark unless this browser is registered with a Cover license (https://coverredact.com/): get_status reports the page-level `watermark` and every document reports its own, so read those rather than assuming either way.

tools.name: get_diagram
tools.description: One diagram: title, tags, starred, Mermaid source and the version id it's at (pass it to update_diagram as baseVersion or expectedVersion). version reads the source at a past version; history: true adds the version list, where agent edits are listed separately from the person's.

tools.description: Settings, the theme in effect (light or dark, plus the full app --eos-* and diagram --pele-* CSS including defaults; Pele's variables are documented at https://pele.run/theming) and storage used.

tools.name: export
tools.description: Export a diagram (id) or raw Mermaid (source). Formats: svg, png (data URL), mmd (with the version id it's at, for a diagram), link (a share link that opens a copy in another browser, or the original in a browser that already has it), backup (the whole library as JSON; no id needed). For invalid Mermaid, svg and png return parse_error with line and column, and mmd returns ok with valid: false and the error, so either works as a dry-run check. link doesn't check the source. download: true also saves the file like the Export menu.

source.description: Raw Mermaid, instead of id

includeTags.description: For link: include the diagram's tags

tools.name: create_diagram
tools.description: Create a diagram from Mermaid source, or import one from an Eos share link (fromShareLink). Importing a link whose title and source match a diagram already in the library returns that diagram, with existing: true, and leaves it as it is (starred isn't applied): editing it edits the person's diagram. To get a copy instead, or to duplicate any diagram, read it with get_diagram and create from its source. Opens it unless open is false. Returns the version id its source is at and whether the source parses.

source.description: Mermaid source

tags.description: Use slashes for nesting, e.g. work/backend

tools.name: update_diagram
tools.description: Edit a diagram. Every field is optional and the edit lands as one change in history, credited to the agent: title, source (full Mermaid; applied as a minimal diff), starred, addTags, removeTags. revert: "undo" or "redo" steps back or forward through the agent's own source edits, keeping the person's (title, tags and starred aren't undoable: set them back directly), or a version id from get_diagram's history restores that version. deleted: true moves it to Deleted (asks the person; reversible), false restores it. Pass baseVersion, the version id returned with the source you edited, to merge your source as the changes you made to it, keeping edits others made since; without it, source replaces the text. When others' edits were merged in, the result includes the merged source. expectedVersion refuses the edit if anything changed since that version.

tools.name: update_tag
tools.description: Rename or move a tag (and everything nested under it) across every diagram, and/or set its sidebar icon. moveTo is the new full path: "archive/backend" nests it, "backend" puts it at the top level. emoji: an emoji, or null for the default #.

tools.name: set_view
tools.description: Change what the person sees. page: "library" (with optional filters; filters on their own also show the library) or "diagram" (with diagramId). previewVersion shows a past version of the open diagram read-only, or "latest" to go back. zoom changes the preview. settingsOpen shows or hides Settings; sidebarOpen shows or hides the sidebar.

tags.description: One tag: the library shows one tag at a time

previewVersion.description: A version id from get_diagram's history, or "latest"

tools.name: set_theme
tools.description: Change the theme: mode (light, dark or system), appCss (--eos-* variables) and/or diagramCss (--pele-* variables). Start from the CSS get_settings returns. null resets an override to the default.

tools.name: delete_tag
tools.description: Remove a tag, and tags nested under it, from every diagram. Asks the person to confirm. Diagrams themselves are kept.

tools.name: import_backup
tools.description: Import a backup (from export with format backup). merge adds to the library; replace wipes local data first and asks the person to confirm.

tools.name: delete_all_data
tools.description: Delete every diagram in this browser, with its stars and tag emoji. Settings are kept. Asks the person to confirm. Can't be undone.

id.description: Record id, as returned by search_communications.

tools.name: search_activities
tools.description: Search Frédérick Madore's news and activity log: new publications, grants, workshops, visits and other milestones. Free text matches titles, summaries, the full body text and tags, so this is the tool for what he has been doing lately. Returns one compact row per match, newest first unless a query ranks them; pass an id to get_activity to read the entry.

query.description: Free text. Every word must appear; accents and case are ignored.

tag.description: A subject tag the entry carries.

limit.description: Rows per page (default 10, at most 50).

offset.description: Matches to skip. Pass the next_offset of the previous page to continue.

tools.name: get_activity
tools.description: One activity or news entry in full: its complete body text (HTML), date, tags, images and links. Search returns headlines only, so this is how the writing itself is read. Takes an id from search_activities.

id.description: Record id, as returned by search_activities.

tools.name: list_research_projects
tools.description: All of Frédérick Madore's research projects, current and concluded: title, span, regions, funding, summary, and the ids of the publications, talks, grants and fieldwork belonging to each. Use get_research_project for a project's full narrative.

tools.name: get_research_project
tools.description: One research project in full: its complete narrative, span, regions, source languages, funding, and the ids of everything that belongs to it. Takes an id from list_research_projects.

id.description: Record id, as returned by list_research_projects.

tools.name: list_dh_projects
tools.description: Digital archives, datasets and tools built by Frédérick Madore, including the Islam West Africa Collection (IWAC): title, years, summary, skills, awards, the article describing each and its published reviews. Use get_dh_project for a project's full description and embedded views.

tools.name: get_dh_project
tools.description: One digital humanities project in full: its description (HTML), skills, award, the article describing it, published reviews, embedded views and links. Takes an id from list_dh_projects.

id.description: Record id, as returned by list_dh_projects.

tools.name: get_cv
tools.description: Frédérick Madore's career record. Without a section: the person (name, position, affiliation, contact email, research topics, scholarly profiles) and the number of entries in each section. Name a section to read its entries: appointments, education, researchRoles, grants, awards, teaching, editorialMemberships, peerReviews, affiliations, fieldworks, mediaAppearances, languages. Grants carry funder, amount, currency, status and co-applicants.

section.description: The section to read. Omit it for the person and the section sizes.

tools.name: get_citation
tools.description: Cite one publication. 'bibtex' returns the BibTeX entry the site's download button produces; 'reference' returns the plain-text reference its Copy reference button copies. Takes an id from search_publications.

id.description: Record id, as returned by search_publications.

style.description: 'bibtex' (the default) or 'reference', a plain-text reference.

tools.name: show_publications
tools.description: Open the publications index in this tab on a filtered view, so the reader sees and can share the list the site draws. Takes the filters of search_publications; tag, country, project and language are matched to the index facets, ignoring case and accents. Use search_publications to read results yourself.

query.description: Free text. Every word must appear; accents and case are ignored.

tag.description: A subject tag the publication carries.

country.description: A country the work covers, e.g. "Benin" or "Togo".

project.description: The research project the work belongs to.

language.description: Language of publication, e.g. "English" or "French".

tools.name: call_playground
tools.description: Sends one MCP request to a Playground's server from its Call tab, as the user would: the user sees the result in the Call tab and the exchange in the Wire tab. A stopped Playground starts first. Returns the JSON-RPC response, with any notifications streamed before it. Time limit: 60 seconds.

index.description: The Playground's position on the page, from 1, as list_playgrounds gives it.

method.description: An MCP method: tools/call, resources/read or prompts/get, or a list method like tools/list.

params.description: Its params, like { "name": "search_tickets", "arguments": { "query": "log" } } for tools/call.

tools.name: edit_playground
tools.description: Puts new code in one of the page's Playgrounds, as if the user typed it: the user sees it in the editor, the Playground counts as edited, and its Reset button brings back the original example. It replaces only the files you give, which must be files the Playground has; their earlier code, the user's edits included, is gone. The Playground restarts with the new code; returns the compile errors with file and line, or the error that stopped the server starting, or the new catalog. Time limit: 60 seconds.

index.description: The Playground's position on the page, from 1, as list_playgrounds gives it.

name.description: The file's name, like "server.ts", or "server.test.ts" for tests written with @frontmcp/testing.

files.description: The files to replace, by name.

tools.name: get_current_page
tools.description: Returns the frontmcp.dev page open in this tab: its path, title, and the section headings on it, each with the anchor that links to it. Use it to know what the user is reading before you answer, or to point them to a section.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Returns a frontmcp.dev docs or blog page as Markdown: its title, summary and full text, with code samples and links to other pages. Use it to read a page that search_docs or list_pages found. Takes a path on this site, like /reference/sdk/tool; other sites are refused.

path.description: The page's path, like /learn/your-first-tool, or its full frontmcp.dev URL.

tools.name: get_playground
tools.description: Returns one Playground on the page: its files as the user sees them, with their edits, its status (and the error, if it has one), whether the user edited it, the response to the last request sent from its Call tab, and its last test results. Use it to see what the user is working on, or why their code fails.

index.description: The Playground's position on the page, from 1, as list_playgrounds gives it.

tools.name: get_version
tools.description: Returns the FrontMCP version this site documents, the MCP protocol version its examples speak, and the latest FrontMCP releases with their summaries and changelog links. Use it before giving version-specific advice.

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: Returns the site's navigation: for Learn, Reference, Examples and Compare, the sidebar's groups and pages in reading order, and the blog's posts, each with its title and path. Use it to see what the docs cover, or to find a page by where it sits.

section.description: Only this part of the site. All of them by default.

tools.name: list_playgrounds
tools.description: Returns the Playgrounds on the page open in this tab, in page order: each one's index (its position, from 1), the heading it sits under, its file names, its status (not started, starting, running, stopped while the user reads elsewhere, or error) and whether the user edited its code. Use it before get_playground, edit_playground, call_playground or run_playground_tests.

tools.name: navigate
tools.description: Opens a frontmcp.dev page in this tab, as a link on the site does, and scrolls to a section when you give its anchor. Only the site's own pages: the docs, the blog, and /, /playground, /releases and /versions. Returns the page's path and title once it shows.

path.description: The page's path, like /reference/sdk/tool, or its full frontmcp.dev URL.

anchor.description: A section on the page, like "options" or "#options", from search_docs or get_current_page.

tools.name: open_playground
tools.description: Opens the full-page Playground, /playground, in this tab with your files loaded in its editor, where the user can edit and run them and share the link. Returns the link. Use it to hand the user a project to try; then list_playgrounds and the other Playground tools work on it.

name.description: The file's name, like "server.ts", or "server.test.ts" for tests written with @frontmcp/testing.

hidden.description: Kept out of the file tabs.

files.description: The project's files.

tools.name: run_in_playground
tools.description: Compiles FrontMCP code and starts it in the Playground's runtime in this page: FrontMCP and a simulated MCP client in a Web Worker, as the site's Playgrounds run. Nothing is shown to the user. Returns, in order: the compile errors with file and line, or the error that stopped the server starting; else the server's catalog (tools, resources, resource templates and prompts, with their schemas); then the response to `call`, if given; then, with `runTests`, the results of the project's *.test.ts files. The files may import @frontmcp/sdk, @frontmcp/testing, @frontmcp/plugins, the @frontmcp/plugin-* packages, @frontmcp/adapters and each other, and export their tools, resources and prompts, or an @App or @FrontMcp class. The server is disposed afterwards, and the whole run has a time limit of 60 seconds. Use it to check that code compiles and behaves as you expect before you suggest it.

name.description: The file's name, like "server.ts", or "server.test.ts" for tests written with @frontmcp/testing.

hidden.description: Kept out of the file tabs.

files.description: The project's files.

call.description: One request to send once the server is running.

method.description: An MCP method: tools/call, resources/read or prompts/get, or a list method like tools/list.

params.description: Its params, like { "name": "search_tickets", "arguments": { "query": "log" } } for tools/call.

runTests.description: Also run the tests in the project's *.test.ts files.

tools.name: run_playground_tests
tools.description: Runs a Playground's tests, or a challenge's checks, against a fresh copy of its server, as its Tests tab does: the user sees the results there. A Playground that isn't running starts first. Returns how many passed and failed, and each test with its error. Time limit: 60 seconds.

index.description: The Playground's position on the page, from 1, as list_playgrounds gives it.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Searches frontmcp.dev, the FrontMCP documentation, by page titles, descriptions and section headings: the same index as the site's search box. Returns up to `limit` matches, best first, each with its title, path (with an #anchor for a section), site section and a snippet from the page's description. Use it to find the page about a decorator, option, error or topic; then read it with get_page.

query.description: Words to look for, like "rate limit" or "elicit".

section.description: Only this part of the site.

limit.description: How many matches to return.

frontmcp.dev.blurb: Call playground, Edit playground and Get current page.
frontmcp.dev.name: Frontmcp
