tools.name: get_learner_state
tools.description: Read this first, every session — the learner's rubric scores, misconception fire counts, phase, gate status, attempt count, their written lesson aims, one-line rule compressions, and run commitments, PLUS coachingNotes (durable observations from previous coaching sessions, including yours) and a coachCalibration summary of how earlier confidence hints and rubric proposals matched engine outcomes. Call again before choosing any coaching move. When a rule compression exists, critique it against the lesson's governing rule — what did they miss or overstate?

tools.name: get_current_context
tools.description: Read the current objective and, when the learner is on a lesson page, that lesson's slug, title, and section anchors — each anchor carries the title of the section it names, so you can tell the learner where you are sending them. Call first in every session and after any navigation, to orient before coaching. For the lesson's actual teaching material, call get_lesson_brief.

tools.name: get_lesson_brief
tools.description: Read the authored teaching material for the lesson the learner is on: title, epigraph, governing rule, exam-recognition clue, mnemonic, the scenario prompt (and its expected answer once the learner has committed and the page has revealed it to them), the concept hierarchy with summaries, the distractor teardown the page shows — why each tempting choice is tempting and why it fails — the visual walkthrough steps, production nuance, the four targeted drills, the reflection prompts, the page section anchors with their titles, and the official references. Call this before you begin coaching a lesson and whenever the learner moves to a new lesson. This is the authored curriculum you teach from, not your own PL-400 knowledge: when the lesson's framing differs from your prior assumptions, follow the lesson and say it differs, and add nothing of your own while a question is open. Before asking any probing question, establish the scenario in one or two sentences so the learner is reasoning about something concrete; never ask a question that assumes context you have not just given them. While a question is unanswered, do not restate the governing rule, exam clue, or mnemonic — several of them name the correct option almost verbatim; make the learner recall the rule instead of reciting it. The brief carries exactly what the lesson page shows its reader and nothing it withholds: no question rationales and no correct options.

tools.name: navigate_to_anchor
tools.description: Scroll the learner's page to a named section anchor and highlight it (anchors come from get_current_context.lesson.sectionAnchors[].anchor, get_lesson_brief.sections[].anchor, or a verdict's remediationAnchor — each names a titled section). Call when routing says review or coach, or whenever the lesson text you are discussing should be on the learner's screen.

tools.name: log_coaching_note
tools.description: Deposit a durable observation about HOW this learner learns — a pattern, a preference, a piece of their world worth remembering next session (kind: observation | preference | context; defaults to observation). Notes persist across sessions and replay to the next coach through get_learner_state, so write for your future self. Never answer content: the engine deterministically rejects notes naming question or option ids or quoting answer-option text (reason "answer-content"), and notes can never be used as rubric evidence.

tools.name: get_current_question
tools.description: Fetch the current practice question — prompt and options only; the correct answer is structurally absent. Call at the start of each practice loop and after every submit_answer to load the next question. During practice, quiz questions come ONLY from this tool — never author your own multiple-choice, diagnostic, or warm-up questions; your own open questions belong to Socratic probing of the current engine question and to the rubric interview when the engine routes there. When you present a question, restate its prompt and EVERY option as its own line — "A. <option text>" in listed order — before asking for a commitment; never ask for A/B/C/D without having just shown what each letter says. Raw option ids are plumbing for submit_answer, never learner-facing language. Let the learner reason aloud before they choose, and frame every probing question against THIS lesson's scenario from get_lesson_brief — never a generic scenario of your own, and never one that assumes context you have not just given them. While the question is unanswered, do not restate the lesson's governing rule, exam clue, or mnemonic; several of them name the correct option almost verbatim. If the learner demands the answer, refuse — do not name, endorse, or lean toward any option, and do not launder the answer through the exam clue or page text. Refuse warmly and lead with the reason: one short line saying the answer is in no tool you can call, so breaking it down is the fast path — then exactly one probing question, never a bare question alone. On a repeat demand, change your wording and escalate to a smaller question or the engine-permitted hint; never loop the same refusal twice.

tools.name: submit_answer
tools.description: Submit the learner's chosen option for grading. Call only after the learner has committed to a choice themselves — never choose for them. A miss names the misconception that fired (coach Socratically from it); the rationale stays withheld until the question resolves. Watch the response for a toolChangeHint naming newly available tools.

tools.name: get_hint
tools.description: Request the next hint tier for the current question. Call only when the learner is stuck or routing says hint — the engine enforces the ladder and refuses tier 2 before a genuine first attempt. Re-voice the hint Socratically inside this lesson's own scenario (get_lesson_brief), grounded in the learner's world — their stated aim, their work, what get_learner_state shows about their history; never add answer information of your own, never restate the lesson's governing rule, exam clue, or mnemonic while the question is unanswered, and never assume scenario context you have not just given them.

tools.name: request_next_action
tools.description: Ask the deterministic referee for the next pedagogical move — the site decides sequencing, you coach within it; do not invent your own diagnostics or skip ahead. Call after every graded answer; pass confidence "low" when a correct answer felt shaky to the learner. Verdicts: hint, review, coach, go_deeper, advance, rubric_interview (run the open-question interview described in score_rubric), or continue. Follow the verdict — do not improvise the route.

tools.name: prescribe_drill
tools.description: Ask the engine which drill targets the learner's weakest rubric dimension. Call once rubric scores exist and practice is going well — before advancing, or when the learner asks what to work on next.

tools.name: score_rubric
tools.description: Submit 0-4 scores for recall, connections, application, and transfer, each grounded by a VERBATIM quote copied exactly from the lesson text on the page — the passage the learner's answer demonstrated. Quotes of the learner's answers or your own words always fail validation. Call only after a rubric interview: 5-8 open questions across the four dimensions, one at a time, never answering for the learner. The engine rejects non-verbatim evidence, requires prior graded attempts, and refuses during an exam. Every dimension at 3 or above opens the gate; the response then names the newly available tools.

tools.name: set_lesson_aim
tools.description: Record why the learner is here: "I'm reading this because I need to ___". ASK for the aim as your FIRST question of every session, before any practice, and store the answer here (200 chars max). It persists per lesson — keyed "track" when the learner is on the hub rather than a lesson page — appears in get_learner_state, and can never be used as rubric evidence. Set it again if the learner's goal shifts. Connect the aim to goals you already know this learner has — from their coaching notes and previous aims — and reflect that connection back to them.

tools.name: set_focus
tools.description: Stage lighting for coaching. Call with preset "focus-section" and that section's anchor (from get_current_context.lesson.sectionAnchors[].anchor) to spotlight the section you are coaching the learner through — the page dims its sibling sections and highlights the target; call "clear-focus" when moving on. "exam-lighting" is site-managed: the site applies and clears the muted exam theme itself at exam start and exit, and requests for it are refused. While an exam is active every preset except "clear-focus" is refused. Effects are a fixed set of page presets — this tool accepts no styling input.

tools.name: set_guide_build_status
tools.description: Report the real guide-planning stage before classroom creation. Start with understanding-goal, advance one stage at a time, and let create_guided_lesson own successful completion. Use error with a learner-facing message when planning cannot continue.

tools.name: create_guided_lesson
tools.description: Create or replace a complete guided lesson transactionally. Always declare lessonMode. Use only the lesson steps and scene beats required for clarity, with at most 15 Learning Plan steps and 15 scene beats. Avoid filler or unnatural compression and group closely related concepts when needed. Use explain when the learner asks to understand, learn, see, or be shown a concept: provide complete example code and progressive explanation beats, not a workspace full of TODOs. When an initial scene teaches source code, preserve Monaco precision by giving each visual explanation beat one semantic target for the exact token, single line, or contiguous multi-line range being discussed, together with the registered highlight, spotlight, focus, or pointer effects that communicate that target. Treat endColumn as the exclusive endpoint after the final target character. Use practice only when the learner asks for an exercise, challenge, TODO, or hands-on work. Use mixed for a demonstration followed by a small validated exercise. Map every coding-exercise beat, including an intermediate exercise, to a lesson step with structural validation criteria and an editor-change interaction wait; Lessonique validates it in the same beat and gates Next or Finish. Use at most 5 final-exercise criteria and write each criterion's learner-visible requirement alongside its validator. Omit supportingItems from the final beat: Lessonique derives the numbered list from those criterion requirements in the same order, so the guide and validation progress cannot diverge. Wrap every code-related term in single backticks, including keywords, identifiers, functions, values, data types, HTML tags, CSS tokens, and short expressions (for example, `const`, `<section>`, `getUser()`, `string`, or `42`). Only inline code spans are supported; do not use HTML or other Markdown for presentation.

lessonMode.description: Use explain for complete examples and guided demonstrations without TODO-driven work; practice for incomplete exercises and validation; mixed for explanation followed by a small exercise.

tools.name: open_internet_marketplace
tools.description: Open Hum’s home internet marketplace, optionally after validating a US service address with Smarty. If an address is ambiguous, returns up to five short-lived candidates for clarification instead of guessing. A unique multi-unit building may be opened without choosing a unit.

address.description: A US street address, ideally including city, two-letter state, and ZIP code.

candidateId.description: A short-lived candidateId returned by an earlier ambiguous call on this page.

unit.description: Optional apartment, suite, or unit to validate at the selected building.

tools.name: get_marketplace_state
tools.description: Read the verified service address, qualification status, visible checkout step, non-sensitive cart contents, totals, and missing fields in the current Hum internet marketplace.

tools.name: set_internet_needs
tools.description: Answer the marketplace questions about home size, connected devices, and internet uses so Hum can reveal and rank recommendations. Use the choices exposed by the current marketplace state.

tools.name: set_service_unit
tools.description: Validate and add or change an apartment, suite, or unit at the currently verified building, then rerun the Hum marketplace for that unit. If no exact unit exists, returns choices for clarification instead of guessing.

tools.name: list_internet_plans
tools.description: List internet plans for the verified address, including provider, price, speed, technology, fees, promotions, and whether Hum can complete checkout.

tools.name: select_internet_plan
tools.description: Select an orderable Hum internet plan using the opaque planId from list_internet_plans and begin final availability verification. Provider-site-only plans cannot be selected.

tools.name: get_order_options
tools.description: Read the structured choices for the current order-options or installation step, including opaque IDs, selections, quantities, inclusion rules, and dependencies. After an option step is set, call this again for the next category.

tools.name: set_order_options
tools.description: Replace the currently visible option category in the Hum cart and advance to the next checkout step. Use the opaque IDs from get_order_options. Omitted categories stay unchanged; an empty array clears removable selections. Included items, dependencies, radio choices, and quantity limits are enforced.

tools.name: set_installation_preferences
tools.description: Set the desired service-start date and self or professional installation in the visible checkout. The start date must be within the next 30 days beginning tomorrow.

tools.name: set_customer_information
tools.description: Merge non-sensitive customer contact and mailing address into the visible Hum checkout using the same validation as human entry. This tool does not accept date of birth or account PIN.

tools.name: set_sensitive_order_information
tools.description: Set date of birth and/or a four-digit account PIN in the visible Hum order. Before calling, tell the user these values are sensitive and explicitly offer the choice to enter them privately in the visible form instead. Returns only whether each value was provided and never returns the values.

tools.name: review_internet_order
tools.description: Validate the current order, move the visible widget to Order Summary, and return an exact non-sensitive summary plus a short-lived reviewId. This tool never submits or purchases anything.

tools.name: place_internet_service_order
tools.description: PURCHASE: Submit a real internet-service order for the exact contents previously returned by review_internet_order. Call only after the user explicitly approves that reviewed order. Requires the current reviewId and rejects any changed, stale, or already-submitted order. Success is reported only with a visible confirmed order number; submission_unconfirmed must not be retried.

tools.name: get_preview_info
tools.description: Get the preview currently open in this tab: title, artifact type, current version, version count, comment counts and whether it is password protected. Call this first to find out what the user is looking at.

tools.name: get_share_info
tools.description: Get everything needed to share this preview somewhere else — the stable share URL, title, current version and open comment count, plus a ready-to-paste one-line summary. Use this when the user asks you to send the preview to a chat, an email or an issue tracker. It never returns the owner token.

tools.name: list_comments
tools.description: List review comments on the current preview, oldest first. Each entry includes the comment text, who wrote it, the version it was left on, and where it points (CSS selector for web pages, page number for PDFs, normalized coordinates otherwise). Replies follow their parent and carry its id in parentId, so a whole discussion reads in order. Use this to find out what the reviewer wants changed.

status.description: Which comments to return. Defaults to "open" — the ones still needing work.

includeOutdated.description: Include comments left on older versions of this preview.

tools.name: get_comment
tools.description: Get one comment in full, including its annotation geometry and — for web previews — the DOM context captured when the reviewer clicked: CSS selector, tag name, text content, an HTML snippet and the viewport size. Use this to locate the exact element in source before editing.

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description: Leave a review comment on the current preview, as an agent would during a review pass ("check this page at mobile width and comment on anything broken"). Optionally anchor it to a CSS selector or to normalized coordinates (0..1 of the artifact box) so the human sees a marker in the right place. The comment appears in the sidebar immediately.

body.description: The comment text.

selector.description: CSS selector of the element the comment is about (web previews only).

point.description: Normalized position of a pin marker, each value between 0 and 1.

page.description: Page number, for PDF previews.

replyTo.description: Reply in this thread instead of starting a new one. A comment id from list_comments. A reply inherits the thread target.

tools.name: resolve_comment
tools.description: Mark a comment thread as resolved once the requested change has actually been made and a new version published. Resolving a thread resolves its replies with it. Requires the owner token for this preview to be present in this browser. Comments are resolved, never deleted, so the history stays reviewable.

tools.name: list_versions
tools.description: List every version of this preview, newest first, with its number, size, file count, upload source and whether it is the one currently served at the share URL.

tools.name: get_review_summary
tools.description: One call that returns the whole review state: preview metadata, the current version, the version history and every open comment thread with its target and replies. Counts are per thread. Use this at the start of a fix-the-feedback loop instead of calling the individual read tools one by one.

tools.name: focus_comment
tools.description: Scroll the reviewer's screen to a comment, select it, and outline the element it points at inside the preview. Use it while discussing feedback with someone so you are both looking at the same thing — say which comment you mean, then call this to show them.

tools.name: set_viewport
tools.description: Resize the preview the reviewer is looking at, to check how the artifact behaves at a different width. Use it before commenting on responsive problems — switch to mobile, look at what breaks, then leave a comment about it. Applies to web previews only.

viewport.description: fit = the whole window, desktop = 1280px, tablet = 768px, mobile = 390px.

tools.name: list_artifact_files
tools.description: List the files in the version currently on screen, with sizes and content types. Use it to find which file to read before working out how to satisfy a comment.

tools.name: read_artifact_file
tools.description: Read one text file out of the version on screen — the HTML or CSS the reviewer is actually looking at. Use it after list_artifact_files to see the markup behind a comment, so you can name the exact rule or element that needs to change rather than guessing. Binary files are refused.

path.description: A path from list_artifact_files, for example "assets/site.css".

tools.name: create_preview_from_url
tools.description: Create a brand new Liha preview from a public URL and return its share URL and owner token. Use this when the user wants to collect review feedback on a page that is already deployed. Private and internal addresses are rejected.

url.description: A public http(s) URL.

tools.name: list_capabilities
tools.description: List the capabilities this site exposes. Magpie manages workflows and holds no business data of its own — the data lives on other websites, so call list_reachable_capabilities as well to see what is reachable there.

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.description: List the saved workflows in this library. Returns { workflows: [{ id, name, summary, stepCount, requires }], count }. `requires` names the capabilities each one uses, so this is how you find a workflow that already does part of what you were asked for — call get_workflow on it and adapt its steps rather than composing from scratch.

tools.name: get_workflow
tools.description: Get one workflow in full, including every step. Accepts an id or an exact name. Its steps are a better starting point than a schema: the arguments in them are ones this site actually accepted. Adapt rather than copy — values like a threshold or a date are specific to what that workflow was for, and rename any `output` that would collide with a step you are keeping.

tools.name: run_workflow
tools.description: Run a saved workflow now and return what happened, step by step. Steps that need another website are executed there through the Magpie extension; if it is not installed they are reported as skipped rather than guessed at. Anything that changes data prompts the user for confirmation first.

tools.name: run_steps
tools.description: Run a list of steps once, without saving a workflow. Use this to carry out a one-off request — it executes across every site Magpie can reach and records the run in this library, so the user can see afterwards what was done. Prefer this over calling capabilities one at a time. Save it with create_workflow only if the user wants it again later.

steps.description: The steps to run, in Magpie step format

goal.description: What the user asked for, in their words. Labels the run.

finalOutput.description: Name of the variable holding the answer

tools.name: list_reachable_capabilities
tools.description: List every capability Magpie can reach on OTHER websites — including sites that are not open right now, which are reopened automatically when a workflow needs them. Call this before composing anything: this page holds no business data of its own, so orders, tickets, bookings and the like all live behind these. Returns { connected, capabilities: [{ id, title, description, provider, origin, status, readOnly }] }. Use the exact `id` as the `tool` value in a step.

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description: List recent workflow runs, newest first. Returns { runs: [...], count }.

limit.description: How many to return. Defaults to 10.

tools.name: get_run
tools.description: Get one run in full, including every step result and the capability it called. A step recorded as ok is proof that capability worked with those arguments, which makes a past run the most reliable source to copy a step from.

tools.name: create_workflow
tools.description: Save a workflow to the library so it can be run again later. Steps use Magpie's format: {"type":"tool","tool":"orders.search_orders","arguments":{...},"output":"orders"} and {"type":"transform","operation":"filter","input":"orders","output":"big","condition":{"field":"amount","operator":">","value":5000}}. A later step reads an earlier one with {{output}}. Every `tool` must be an exact id from list_capabilities or list_reachable_capabilities — unknown names are rejected, never invented. This only saves; call run_workflow to execute.

summary.description: One sentence describing what it does

steps.description: The workflow steps

tools.name: rename_workflow
tools.description: Rename a saved workflow. The name is how it is referred to afterwards, so pick something the user would say out loud. Names must be unique; renaming onto an existing one is refused.

workflowId.description: Workflow id, or its current exact name

tools.name: delete_workflow
tools.description: Delete a saved workflow from the library.

tools.name: delete_run
tools.description: Remove one run from the history, or every run when `all` is true. History is what the user reviews afterwards, so only clear it when they ask.

runId.description: Run id. Omit when clearing everything.

all.description: Delete every run instead of one

tools.name: export_csv
tools.description: Create and download a CSV file from an array of objects. Use whenever the user asks to export or save results as a spreadsheet.

data.description: Rows to export

tools.name: get_screener_results
tools.description: Returns a bounded page of an existing screener run's results, projected through the bound results panel's configured columns, computed columns, sort and grouping, together with the total count, a cursor for the next page, the current selection, and the run's own provenance. Reads only: it retrieves an already-pinned run and never re-runs the screener, even implicitly -- an expired or unknown run is reported as an explicit error, not a fresh execution.

panel_id.description: A results_table panel already bound to a screener run.

cursor.description: Opaque resume token from a previous page's next_cursor. Omit for the first page.

page_size.description: Rows per page, up to 200; defaults to the panel's configured page size, or the documented default when unset.

tools.name: explain_result
tools.description: Returns why one instrument matched or did not match a pinned screener run: the actual value and pass/fail/indeterminate state for every filter condition -- including conditions nested inside AND/OR/NOT groups, with each group's own resolved outcome -- plus each ranking field's raw value, normalized value, weight and contribution to the final score. Covers a run's rejected and truncated candidates as well as its results: an instrument only needs to have been evaluated, not to have passed, to be explained. Omit instrument_id to explain the results panel's current selection. Reads only: it never re-runs the screener.

panel_id.description: A results_table panel already bound to a screener run.

instrument_id.description: Instrument to explain. Omit to explain the panel's current single-result selection; an error names the requirement when neither is available.

tools.name: get_canvas_state
tools.description: Returns a workspace's panels, layout, links, active symbol, screener binding and whether it has changes not saved under a name. Every item carries its stable id. Defaults to the active workspace.

tools.name: define_screener
tools.description: Creates or fully replaces a screener definition in one call: universe, conditions (a nested filter tree of typed conditions), ranking, and a result limit. Validates everything together -- every unknown catalog id, out-of-range parameter, and empty-resolving universe is collected and returned together, never just the first one found -- and commits nothing when any blocking problem is found. Defaults to the workspace's current screener (WorkspaceDocument.screenerId): omit screener_id to create one the first time and replace it (as a new revision, full-replace -- omitted fields reset to empty/default, they are not carried over) on every call after. An explicit screener_id addresses a specific screener and is rejected, naming it, if it does not exist. When a requested interval cannot actually be served by the data available, this substitutes the interval that can be and says so in warnings rather than rejecting the definition. Returns the mutation envelope plus the screener id and revision; accepts expected_revision and idempotency_key.

oneOf.description: A not group must contain exactly one child.

screener_id.description: Defaults to the workspace's current screener; rejected if unrecognized.

name.description: A display label only, never an address.

conditions.description: The whole filter tree in one shot: a root group, a single condition, or an array of nodes (treated as the root group's children under "and"). Omit for no conditions.

oneOf.description: Typed condition or nested group. Conditions use camelCase keys (fieldId, operator), unlike ranking fields. Example: {"type":"scalar","fieldId":"field.price.change_pct_1","operator":"op.greater_than","value":0,"unit":"percent"}. To select a historical session, pass as_of to run_screener.

items.description: Typed condition or nested group. Conditions use camelCase keys (fieldId, operator), unlike ranking fields. Example: {"type":"scalar","fieldId":"field.price.change_pct_1","operator":"op.greater_than","value":0,"unit":"percent"}. To select a historical session, pass as_of to run_screener.

ranking.description: Omit (or pass an empty "fields") for the documented default order.

limit.description: Maximum matches a run returns.

expected_revision.description: Optional. The workspace's own revision, used for optimistic concurrency -- not the screener definition's revision (returned as screener_revision in the response, but not accepted as input here -- define_screener always writes the next revision).

tools.name: run_screener
tools.description: Executes one specific screener revision and pins the complete, ordered result set under a stable run_id: the screener id and revision executed, universe/matched/returned counts, whether the result was truncated, ranking, warnings and full data provenance. The run never changes after later edits to the screener (it always describes the revision it executed), and its stored matches -- including every ranking value and per-filter-node pass/fail state -- are read back by run_id without ever re-executing the screener. A screener with blocking validation problems is refused instead: the problems are returned and no run_id is minted. A valid screener that nothing satisfies is a normal run with matched_count 0 and a warning, not an error. Accepts an optional screener_revision to run an exact past revision (rejected if no longer retained), expected_revision for optimistic concurrency, and idempotency_key -- a replayed key returns the original run_id without executing a second time. Successful runs automatically bind to the first visible results list, or create a default-sized list when none exists. Do not create a second list unless requested. Display failures are reported as warnings without discarding the run.

period.description: Inclusive calendar date range, mutually exclusive with as_of. Resolve last week/month to explicit calendar dates. Rank/filter by field.price.period_return_pct for total period gains; baseline is the last loaded session before start, endpoint the last loaded session within the range. Other fields are evaluated at the endpoint. Not an any-time-during-period condition.

as_of.description: Exact trading session (YYYY-MM-DD) for all filters and rankings. Omit for the latest loaded session. Unavailable sessions are refused, never substituted. Use this for historical gainers; field.date is a filter, not a session selector.

screener_revision.description: Optional. The screener definition's own revision counter -- not the workspace's own revision (see expected_revision, a separate parameter). Runs this exact screener revision instead of the current one; rejected if that revision is no longer retained.

expected_revision.description: Optional. The workspace's own revision, used for optimistic concurrency -- not the screener definition's revision (see screener_revision, a separate parameter). Rejected with a revision conflict if the workspace is no longer at this revision.

tools.name: resolve_ticker
tools.description: Turns a bare ticker into the instrument reference a chart panel's source requires. This project has no live reference-data source (no company name, exchange, or asset-classification service), so this mints a provisional reference from the ticker text alone -- asset type is assumed "equity", the exchange is reported as "XUNK" (unknown) -- and does not confirm the ticker actually has data. Whether it does is discovered only once the chart is bound and rendered. Pass this result directly as create_panel's source.ref, with source.type "instrument".

ticker.description: The ticker to resolve, e.g. "STX" or "MOCK13".

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the application catalog -- every field, operator, study, indicator, pattern, interval, universe and template the app knows how to name. Matches on label, stable ID, aliases and tags, so a common synonym finds the item. Returns summary rows (id, kind, label, description, availability); pass an id to describe_catalog_item for parameters, units, ranges, defaults and outputs. Supply kinds with no query to enumerate a kind rather than guessing a search term. Items whose data is unavailable are included and marked, because "exists but has no data here" is different from "does not exist" -- read the availability reason before deciding an item is unusable.

query.description: Free text, e.g. "relative volume", "crossed above", "rsi". Omit it and supply kinds to list everything of those kinds.

kinds.description: Restrict the search to these catalog kinds. Omit to search all eight.

includeUnavailable.description: Include items whose data is currently unavailable. Defaults to true; set false to see only what can be used right now.

limit.description: Maximum items to return. Clamped to 50.

tools.name: get_instrument_analysis
tools.description: Read server-calculated evidence for one stock: exact-session close, 12–1 calendar momentum, 50/200-session SMAs, 252-session volatility/drawdown, volume and extreme price-move warnings. Uses the same price data and calculations as the screener. No trades or workspace mutations. Missing sessions are refused. Defaults to latest loaded data, which may lag today. Fundamentals and valuation are not supplied.

as_of.description: Exact trading session, YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for latest loaded session.

tools.name: search_archive
tools.description: Search 7,139 scholarly annotated music videos (1966-2026) by artist, title, tag, technique or subculture, with optional filters. Returns matches with ids you can play. Use this for "find me something like X" questions.

query.description: Free text over artist, title, tags, techniques, subcultures

director.description: Filter to one director, e.g. "Chris Cunningham"

limit.description: Default 12, max 50

tools.name: find_by_look
tools.description: Find videos by their VISUAL GRAMMAR rather than by genre or words. Every video is fingerprinted for motion, brightness, warmth, saturation, contrast and average shot length. Use this for "something slower", "something darker and more frantic", or to find a video that LOOKS like another one but comes from a different era.

like_id.description: Match the look of this video id

exclude_same_era.description: With like_id, force a different visual era

tools.name: follow_connection
tools.description: Traverse the archive's 49,753 connections. Unlike a similarity score, every edge states its REASON: a shared director, era, movement or tag. Use this to move sideways through the archive and to tell the person WHY one video leads to another.

id.description: Video id to walk out from. Defaults to what is playing.

tools.name: play
tools.description: Put a video on the screen the person is watching and start it. Call this whenever you name a specific video, including when answering a factual question about one. If you mention it, show it.

id.description: Video id from a search result

note.description: One line shown to the user explaining why you picked it

tools.name: now_playing
tools.description: Read what is currently on screen, including how far through it is. Call this before commenting on a video.

tools.name: get_annotation
tools.description: Fetch the scholarly annotation for a video: cultural context, curatorial assessment, genre significance, the era it sits in, and the director biography. This is the material to draw facts from. Do not invent facts about a video, call this instead.

tools.name: queue_set
tools.description: Queue several videos as a run with a title. USE THIS for any request that asks for more than one video: a set, a run, a playlist, a block, an hour of something. The videos play through in order automatically and the running order is shown on screen, so do not play them one at a time. Six to ten is a good length. Say what the thread through the set is.

note.description: The thread running through the set

tools.name: keep
tools.description: Save what is playing to the person's collection, with a short note on why they liked it. This persists in their browser between visits. Call it when they say they like something, want to remember it, or want more like it.

why.description: One line on what they liked about it, in their words if they gave you any

tools.name: forget
tools.description: Remove a video from the person's collection.

tools.name: my_taste
tools.description: Read what this person has kept, why they kept it, and the SHAPE of it: their average motion, brightness, warmth, saturation, contrast and shot length, plus the narrative types, eras and directors they lean toward. Call this at the start of a session to know who you are talking to, and before recommending anything.

tools.name: more_like_my_taste
tools.description: Find videos that match the measured look of everything the person has kept, excluding what they already have. This is recommendation from their own collection rather than from popularity. Use it when they ask what they should watch.

tools.name: find_records
tools.description: Find real physical releases you can actually buy for the artist on screen: vinyl, CDs, cassettes. Returns pressings with year, label, catalogue number, country and the lowest price currently listed on the Discogs marketplace, plus a link to buy. Use it when someone likes what is playing and wants to own it, or asks what it is worth. Prices are live, do not guess at them.

artist.description: Defaults to the artist on screen

title.description: Optional album or track to narrow it

format.description: Optional

tools.name: archive_stats
tools.description: Describe what is in the archive: size, year range, directors, eras and how it was annotated. Use to orient yourself before searching.

matchcut.live.blurb: Search archive, Find by look and Follow connection.
matchcut.live.name: Matchcut

tools.name: get_learning_overview
tools.description: Read current due totals, active-session facts, bounded deck progress summaries, and recent reviews. This never recommends work or changes the current page.

tools.name: search_library
tools.description: Search lightweight summaries in the owner-maintained Library. Results never contain cards and this tool never installs, publishes, selects, or opens a deck.

tools.name: list_my_decks
tools.description: List personal deck summaries, with optional text/status filters, sorting, and pagination. Call with no arguments to list active decks by due work. Results include revision, progress, provenance, and warnings, not cards; use get_deck for a complete deck. This never changes selection or navigation.

tools.name: get_deck
tools.description: Return one complete Library or personal deck, including every card, rubric, prerequisite, provenance field, revision, archive flag, and scheduling summary. The result is never paged or silently truncated.

tools.name: validate_deck
tools.description: Validate a candidate or stored definition deck without writing. Candidate-v2 IDs and prerequisite edges are deck-local. Results separate structural blockers, warnings, and semantic questions for agent review; they do not certify factual or pedagogical quality. For authoring, choose atomic recall terms, write concise definitions and necessary grading criteria, validate the complete payload, repair every blocker, then ingest that exact payload.

schema_version.description: Use normalized-definition-deck.v2 exactly. The authoring guide version is not a payload field.

deck_id.description: Stable lowercase deck identity. Create a new personal deck unless the user explicitly requested replacement; never infer replacement from an ID collision.

title.description: A concise learner-facing title whose bounded promise the cards fulfill.

id.description: Stable lowercase deck-local concept ID, not a positional number or a deck-qualified storage ID. Preserve it during repairs.

term.description: Plain-text, unambiguous label for exactly one singular, atomic, retrievable concept or one unitary named theorem, law, method, problem, process, or object. Split true multi-target comparisons, lists, alternatives, paired operations, generic relationships, umbrellas, and bundles. If the content already targets one concept, narrow extraneous objective wording to exactly one replacement front while preserving semantic identity. A visible and/or/versus/vs./slash/comma/ampersand or a generic colon suffix such as role/use/scope/statement is a presumptive defect unless this is a true established proper name with an explicit outside-payload rationale.

definition.description: Accurate, concise definition of the front's one concept, stated directly and including distinguishing conditions and notation. A formula alone is not a sufficient definition: accompany it with short prose identifying non-obvious symbols, the relevant domain, quantifiers or conditions, and what the relationship means. State truth-changing theorem hypotheses and comparison inequalities/directions directly; never hide them behind phrases such as 'under the theorem hypotheses.' Put actual mathematical notation in balanced $...$ / $$...$$ TeX rather than raw pseudocode such as integral_a^b, abs(...), or sqrt(...). Do not use circular meta-language such as 'the definition of', 'the idea that', 'the concept of', or 'the question whether' in place of the content. Supports simple Markdown and math; no raw HTML or remote embeds.

criteria.description: Minimal observable requirements for the front's one core defining meaning; never use criteria to preserve multiple concepts hidden behind one front. 1–12 allowed, not a quota. A complete equivalent definition or complete alternative characterization must pass without separately reciting another equivalent form, optional examples, consequences, contrasts, error checks, applications, or reference values.

tags.description: Optional organizational labels, not criteria or prerequisites; at most 5. Omitted means [] for new cards but preserves existing tags on replacement. Explicit [] clears tags.

cards.description: Complete atomic definition cards for this normalized-v2 payload. Each front tests exactly one term or concept; a flagged front must be split, narrowed to the one concept its content already targets, or receive an explicit outside-payload proper-name exception rationale. Coverage determines the count; never merge or omit independently recallable in-scope concepts to stay small. A full-payload call permits 1–50 cards; a larger requested scope uses the course-batch instructions rather than shrinking.

from.description: ID of the prerequisite card in this payload.

to.description: ID of the dependent card in this payload.

edges.description: Sparse deck-local direct hard prerequisites, from prerequisite to dependent. Usually give a card zero or one direct parent; use two only when both concepts are independently necessary. Treat three or more as a presumptive semantic defect requiring exact justification, but never enforce a maximum parent count or indegree quota: every independently necessary direct parent must survive. Decide directness against the full planned deck before batching; validation does not auto-reduce.

tools.name: ingest_deck
tools.description: Atomically create a validated personal definition deck or fully replace one. Replacement archives omitted cards, preserves retained metadata and unchanged learning history, and reports scheduling resets. Use update_deck for metadata and add_cards or update_cards for targeted changes. Retry an uncertain result with identical arguments and key, then verify with stored validate_deck and get_deck. This never navigates.

tools.name: update_deck
tools.description: Atomically patch personal deck metadata using an expected revision and idempotency key. This cannot change cards, deck identity, archive state, scheduling, selection, or navigation.

tools.name: add_cards
tools.description: Atomically add 1 to 100 complete cards to a personal deck. Existing or duplicate identities fail the entire batch; the site initializes scheduling and the tool never changes the current view.

tools.name: update_cards
tools.description: Atomically patch 1 to 100 existing cards, including prerequisite fields and reversible archive state. Unknown or duplicate identities fail the entire batch; material grading-target edits reset only affected schedules.

tools.name: start_study_session
tools.description: Start or resume the continuous queue and return the full current card and rubric to the grading agent. Due reviews come first, then eligible new cards, then early practice by nearest due date. For signed-in accounts, this action reuses this client's Study-writer grant or acquires a new one only when none is active. It never replaces an active grant. If this client is superseded or a writer is active elsewhere, stop and ask the learner to choose Continue here in the Study UI, then retry. Ask the learner only for the visible term and keep the definition private until the attempt commits. This never navigates.

tools.name: get_study_session
tools.description: Read the current session and full current card and rubric for the grading agent. Keep the definition and rubric private before an attempt. Reveal must commit its Again review before the answer is shown. This lock-free read remains available to a superseded client and neither acquires nor changes the Study-writer grant. It never captures an answer, grades, schedules, advances, or navigates.

tools.name: submit_grade
tools.description: Atomically submit the learner's exact answer and the agent's grade, evidence, and feedback. Grade meaning and unaided recall, not wording: Again for missing or contradicted essential meaning; Hard for correct but effortful unaided recall; Good for correct normal or unknown effort; Easy only for effortless unaided recall. Do not grade a materially defective card or pre-attempt assistance without an established failure. Cover every required concept. For signed-in accounts, this action reuses this client's Study-writer grant or acquires a new one only when none is active. It never replaces an active grant. If this client is superseded or a writer is active elsewhere, stop and ask the learner to choose Continue here in the Study UI, then retry. The transaction schedules, records, and advances the canonical session exactly once; the site reveals the just-graded definition and keeps it visible until the learner selects Next card. Give the saved specific feedback in chat while that definition is visible. Do not introduce the next term or call get_study_session merely to bypass the learner-controlled transition. Retry uncertain results only with identical arguments and key. This never navigates.

session_id.description: Copy the current session_id from the live session response; never invent it.

card_id.description: Copy current_card.card_id from this session, not a remembered or next-card identity.

expected_card_revision.description: Copy the exact current_card.card_revision used to assess this answer.

expected_session_revision.description: Copy the exact session.session_revision for this unanswered card; reread and reconcile conflicts.

answer_text.description: The learner's exact submitted answer, including whitespace, symbols, errors, and self-corrections. Do not replace it with a summary or canonical definition. If it exceeds the limit, do not silently truncate it.

answer_origin.description: Use chat for the default chat-led attempt; website only when the answer actually came from the website.

rating.description: Apply definition-recall.v1: again = failed essential recall; hard = complete unaided but difficult; good = complete with ordinary/unknown effort; easy = complete with positively evidenced effortless unaided recall. Confidence is not fluency.

rubric_item_id.description: Copy an ID returned on this current card. Native v2 normally exposes required-1, required-2, etc.; do not assume those IDs for other cards.

status.description: met = full semantic support; partial = some required meaning; missed = no support; contradicted = unretracted incompatible claim. For an optional legacy major-error row, contradicted means the named misconception was actually asserted.

note.description: Briefly identify the answer phrase and its semantic support, omission, or conflict. No invented quotes, timing, assistance, or hidden reasoning transcript.

rubric_evidence.description: One row for each returned required_concepts ID, with truthful semantic status and answer-grounded note. Use only returned IDs; do not add legacy rubric fields to a v2 card. Explain material recall context in an existing note or feedback.

feedback.description: Prepare 1–3 chat-ready sentences privately: credit specific correct content and name the decisive gap/correction if present. For a complete answer, briefly confirm its meaning without invented criticism or a routine explanation of unused rating choices. After verifying the matching receipt, deliver this feedback once in chat. Preserve the original feedback on an exact retry.

misconceptions.description: Plain-language substantial misconceptions actually expressed; [] when none. Missing material, low confidence, or weak card criteria are not learner misconceptions.

confidence.description: Your confidence in the semantic assessment, from 0 to 1; not a correctness score, recall-speed measure, or Easy signal. Material assessment uncertainty means stop rather than invent a grade.

idempotency_key.description: A fresh identity for this one logical review. On uncertain delivery, retry exactly the same arguments and key; never create a second review just to obtain a receipt.

tools.name: finish_study_session
tools.description: Pause or end an open session early using its expected revision. For signed-in accounts, this action reuses this client's Study-writer grant or acquires a new one only when none is active. It never replaces an active grant. If this client is superseded or a writer is active elsewhere, stop and ask the learner to choose Continue here in the Study UI, then retry. Normal completion follows the final submit_grade. This creates no review and never navigates.

meshful.ai.blurb: Get learning overview, Search library and List my decks.
meshful.ai.name: Meshful

tools.name: about_open_accountant
tools.description: Returns a structured overview of Open Accountant — what it is, who it is for, and where to find the CLI, docs, and source. Start here when you have never used this site before.

tools.name: get_started
tools.description: Returns an ordered onboarding sequence an agent can narrate or step through: install Wilson CLI, import, categorize, ask a question, explore skills.

platform.description: Target OS for the install command (default: linux/macos).

tools.name: get_install_command
tools.description: Returns the one-line install command for the requested OS plus the install directory and post-install verification command.

tools.name: recommend_skills
tools.description: Given a user situation (freelancer, developer, privacy-focused, switching apps, small-business, landlord, investor), returns the most relevant skills from the marketplace with URLs.

segment.description: Audience segment slug or a free-form situation description.

tools.name: find_alternative
tools.description: Given a competitor product name (e.g. "Mint", "YNAB", "QuickBooks"), returns Open Accountant's positioning, feature comparison, and who should/should not switch.

tools.name: search_skills
tools.description: Full-text search over the skill catalog. Optionally filter by category and tier. Returns matches with canonical marketplace URLs.

tools.name: get_skill
tools.description: Returns the full catalog entry for a skill plus its canonical marketplace URL.

tools.name: list_skill_categories
tools.description: Returns the seven top-level categories with slug, name, description, and the list of skill slugs in each.

tools.name: compare_alternative
tools.description: Returns the full feature matrix, positioning, and switcher guidance for the given competitor slug. Use find_alternative first if you only know the product name.

tools.name: list_integrations
tools.description: Returns the integrations catalog (agents, data sources, LLM providers) with tier, status, category, and canonical URLs.

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Returns the three pricing tiers: CLI (free forever), Skills Pack (annual subscription to premium skills), and Pro (hosted sync + unlimited skills). Includes prices and purchase URLs.

tools.name: navigate_to
tools.description: Navigate the current browser tab to a named page on openaccountant.ai. Use for top-level pages; for marketplace/{slug}, alternative/{slug}, or integrations/{slug}, pass the full path.

path.description: Canonical path beginning with "/". Top-level enum is suggested; dynamic paths like /marketplace/tax-prep are also accepted.

tools.name: help
tools.description: Self-describing manifest. Returns every registered WebMCP tool on openaccountant.ai with its description and a summary of its input schema. Call this first if you do not know what tools are available.

openaccountant.ai.blurb: About open accountant, Get started and Get install command.
openaccountant.ai.name: Openaccountant

tools.name: about_site
tools.description: What Our Many Names is: a family tree written together, with the memories that go with each name. Says what a visitor can do without an account, what an account gives for free, and where the public pages are.

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: What is free and what is paid: the free allowance an account starts with, each upgrade with its price in credits and money, and the smallest credit top-up.

tools.name: open_page
tools.description: Go to one of the public pages: home (the front page), explore (the directory of published trees), pricing (what an account and its upgrades cost), attribution (credits for the fictional trees on show), terms (terms and conditions), register (the sign-up form), login (the sign-in form). Takes a visitor to the sign-up form, never through it.

tools.name: search_public_trees
tools.description: Published family trees anyone can read, by name — each with its address slug and how many people it holds. Omit the query to list them all.

tools.name: open_public_tree
tools.description: Open a published tree by its slug or name. Its own tools (find_people, describe_relationship, show_person…) appear once it is on screen.

tree.description: A slug or name from search_public_trees

tools.name: get_tree_overview
tools.description: The family tree on screen: its name, whose it is (owners and member count), your role, counts of people, living and deceased, unions and generations, and the eldest person recorded. Start here.

tools.name: find_people
tools.description: Search people in this tree by name, maiden name or byname; a misspelt name still finds its person. Returns compact rows (id, name, dates) in pages of up to 50; use the id in other tools. Omit the query to list everyone.

query.description: Words to match; all must appear somewhere in the name

limit.description: Rows per page, default 20

offset.description: Rows to skip, for the next page

tools.name: get_person
tools.description: One person in full: names, dates, status, and their immediate family — parents with pedigree, partners with the union, children, siblings and social bonds — each with an id.

person.description: Who: a person id from find_people, or a name that matches one person

tools.name: describe_relationship
tools.description: How two people are related: the kinship term each way (grandmother, cousin, sensei…), the number of family hops, and the chain of people between them. "from" defaults to the signed-in member's own card.

from.description: The first person: a person id from find_people, or a name that matches one person

to.description: The second person: a person id from find_people, or a name that matches one person

tools.name: list_gaps
tools.description: What is incomplete or contradictory: children born before a parent, living people over 110, adults with no parents recorded, missing birth or death years. Worst first, paged.

limit.description: Rows to return, default 25

tools.name: show_person
tools.description: Pan the canvas to a person and highlight their card, so the human sees who you mean. Optionally open their profile.

person.description: Who: a person id from find_people, or a name that matches one person

tools.name: focus_lineage
tools.description: Show only one ancestor and their descendants with partners, hiding everyone else. clear_focus undoes it.

ancestor.description: Whose line to show: a person id from find_people, or a name that matches one person

tools.name: clear_focus
tools.description: Leave lineage focus and show the whole tree again.

ourmanynames.com.blurb: About site, Get pricing and Open page.
ourmanynames.com.name: Ourmanynames

tools.name: find_venue
tools.description: Search and discover distinct external merchant venues or franchise branch locations across the WETAEGO network directory by keyword, city, or business name. Returns venue profiles and URLs. Does NOT switch internal department tabs within an active venue (use open_business_page for department switching).

query.description: Search query, keyword, business name, or city (e.g. "sushi", "spa", "Emerald Cafe", "Lagos").

name.description: Exact or partial business name (e.g. "Pacy Group", "Emerald Cafe").

industry.description: Non-overlapping industry vertical filter: "dining" (restaurants, cafes, bars), "hospitality" (hotels, stays, resorts), "wellness" (spas, salons, beauty), "retail" (boutiques, electronics, supermarkets), "services" (repairs, consulting), "creator" (media, studios, rate cards).

limit.description: Max venues to return (1-50).

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search catalog items, products, dishes, and services with category and price filters. Returns item details, prices, and availability.

query.description: Keyword search query for products, dishes, or services.

category.description: Category name filter (e.g. "Mains", "Apparel", "Spa Services").

venueSlug.description: Optional venue slug (e.g. "demo", "emerald-cafe", "ocean-ember", "lotus-spa") to scope search to a specific merchant.

currency.description: Optional target currency code (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, NGN) for dynamic rate conversion.

dietary.description: Dietary classification filters for food & dining.

maxPrice.description: Maximum price filter in major currency units.

inStockOnly.description: Return only in-stock or available items.

limit.description: Max items per page (1-100).

offset.description: Pagination offset.

tools.name: get_item_details
tools.description: Return authoritative details for a specific catalog item using its unique itemId, including price, stock status, customizable modifier groups, dietary tags, and variant options.

itemId.description: The unique itemId from search_catalog results.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Initialize a new shopping cart session for the customer. Returns an authoritative cartId session handle. To inspect existing cart contents, use get_cart. To add items, use add_to_cart.

tableIdentifier.description: Optional table number, room, seat, or pickup counter.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add an available catalog item to the active cart session with optional modifier selections. Returns the updated cartId, cart line items, total item count, and recalculated subtotal.

cartId.description: Optional unique cart session ID. If omitted, uses active session cart.

itemId.description: The unique ID of the item from search_catalog.

quantity.description: Quantity of items to add (1-50).

optionIds.description: Selected option IDs within the group

modifiers.description: Selected modifier groups and option IDs.

notes.description: Special preparation instructions or customer preferences.

clearExisting.description: Clear existing cart items before adding, ensuring clean cross-venue isolation.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Inspect the contents of the active shopping cart session identified by cartId, including line items, modifier options, subtotal, discounts, taxes, and final total. Does NOT initialize a new cart session (use create_cart).

cartId.description: Optional unique cart session ID to inspect. If omitted, returns active session cart.

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Modify the quantity of an existing line item in the cart session or remove it using lineId. Requires lineId. Does NOT add new catalog items (use add_to_cart).

cartId.description: Optional unique cart session ID. If omitted, updates active cart.

lineId.description: The unique lineId of the item to update.

quantity.description: New quantity. Set to 0 to remove item.

notes.description: Updated preparation notes or instructions.

tools.name: apply_coupon
tools.description: Apply a promotional coupon code or discount voucher to the active shopping cart session identified by cartId. Recalculates discounts and updates the cart subtotal and final total.

couponCode.description: The promotional discount or coupon code to apply (e.g. SAVE10, WELCOME20, PACY50, VIP15, SUMMER20).

cartId.description: Optional cart session identifier. If omitted, applies to the active session cart.

tools.name: recommend_pairings

tools.name: list_pitch_sessions
tools.description: Lists the pitch analyses available in this browser, with pitcher handedness, camera view, frame count, and whether each has been analysed yet. Start here: every other tool addresses a pitch by the sessionId returned from this list.

tools.name: get_session_overview
tools.description: Returns what is on screen right now: the loaded pitch, the frame the viewer is scrubbed to, the joint in focus, the camera plane, which overlays are on, which events were detected, and how many notes are pinned. This is live browser state — call it before discussing anything so your words match what the human sees.

sessionId.description: Defaults to the pitch currently on screen.

tools.name: get_phase_events
tools.description: Returns the three detected pitching events — lead foot contact, maximum external rotation, and ball release — with frame number, video timestamp, the signal each was detected from, its confidence, and whether a human corrected it. Every other measurement is anchored to these frames, so read them before interpreting any angle.

sessionId.description: Defaults to the pitch currently on screen.

tools.name: get_kinematics_at_event
tools.description: Returns the joint angles measured at one pitching event (foot_contact | max_external_rotation | ball_release), each with its value in degrees, the published reference range where one exists, whether it sits inside that range, and its measurement confidence. One call gives a complete reference-anchored snapshot of that instant.

event.description: Which pitching event to measure at.

sessionId.description: Defaults to the pitch currently on screen.

tools.name: get_joint_angle_series
tools.description: Returns one joint angle sampled across the pitch, so you can reason about the shape of the movement rather than a single instant — when the peak happens and how sharp it is. Optionally restrict the window to between two events. Downsampled to maxPoints (default 40); the reported peak still comes from the full-resolution series.

joint.description: Which angle to trace, e.g. shoulder_external_rotation or lead_knee_flexion.

maxPoints.description: Samples to return, 5–120. Default 40, which keeps the response inside the output budget.

sessionId.description: Defaults to the pitch currently on screen.

tools.name: get_kinematic_sequence
tools.description: Returns a partial four-segment order: pelvis, trunk, upper arm and forearm peak angular speed. It is not a published full five-segment kinematic sequence or a quality score. Read literatureNote before judging the order: a different order is common and is not by itself a fault.

sessionId.description: Defaults to the pitch currently on screen.

tools.name: get_metric_definition
tools.description: Explains one biomechanical metric: what it measures in plain language, exactly how this app computes it, its published reference ranges with citations, and the limits of measuring it from single-camera video. Use it before quoting any range — it is the only source of reference numbers here, and it also explains which quantities this reconstruction cannot produce at all.

metric.description: A metric name, e.g. hip_shoulder_separation, or a quantity you want to check is measurable.

tools.name: compare_to_reference
tools.description: Answers plain-English questions such as “what stands out?” or “where did I mess up?” by comparing only construct-compatible angles, ranking observations, checking event reliability, and suggesting the existing viewer tools that can show the relevant moment and body part. It never treats a deviation as a diagnosis or proven cause.

event.description: Restrict to one event. Default: all three.

includeWithinRange.description: Also return metrics that sit inside their range. Default false.

sessionId.description: Defaults to the pitch currently on screen.

tools.name: compare_pitches
tools.description: Compares two analysed sessions metric by metric at the same events and returns descriptive differences. It must not imply improvement or change between attempts unless athlete identity and capture comparability are established outside this data contract. The second session is analysed without changing the human view; read meta.caveats.

sessionIdA.description: Baseline pitch. Defaults to the pitch on screen.

sessionIdB.description: Pitch to compare against the baseline.

event.description: Restrict to one event. Default: all three.

tools.name: seek_to_event
tools.description: Scrubs the 3D viewer to a named pitching event or to a specific frame, so the human is looking at the exact moment you are describing. Pass either event or frame, not both. The viewer moves before this returns.

frame.description: Move to this frame index instead of an event.

tools.name: focus_joint
tools.description: Highlights a joint or segment in the 3D viewer, turns on its angle readout, and rotates the camera to the plane where that angle actually reads true — side-on for flexion, front-on for elevation, overhead for rotation. Accepts coaching names like "front knee", "throwing shoulder" or "trunk", and resolves handedness for you.

joint.description: What to look at, e.g. lead_knee, throwing_shoulder, trunk, pelvis, lead_foot.

cameraPlane.description: Camera viewpoint. "auto" picks the plane the joint's angles live in.

tools.name: set_overlay
tools.description: Turns one 3D viewer overlay on or off so you can stage the visual evidence for a point instead of describing it: segment_frames (anatomical triads), axial_dial (shoulder rotation dial), angle_readouts (numeric labels), motion_trail (throwing-hand path), event_markers (timeline markers).

enabled.description: true to show it, false to hide it.

tools.name: annotate_frame
tools.description: Pins a short labelled note to a frame and joint in the 3D viewer, where it stays visible to the human as part of the analysis and survives scrubbing. Use it to leave your observations where they belong — on the moment they describe. Give a frame or an event, and keep the label under 80 characters.

frame.description: Frame to pin the note to.

event.description: Pin at this event instead of a frame.

joint.description: Optional anchor, e.g. lead_knee or throwing_shoulder.

label.description: The note. Max 80 characters; longer text is truncated.

Asset bytes are returned only when final-file decoding matches the requested payload.

value.description: Exact QR payload to encode, such as an HTTPS URL, WIFI payload, vCard, calendar event, payment URI, or text.

format.description: Output format to generate and decode. Verification supports SVG, PNG, JPG, and WebP.

contentType.description: Optional hint describing the QR payload type. This does not change generation behavior but helps agents choose examples and validation.

size.description: Requested output size in pixels for raster/SVG output or points for PDF/EPS.

margin.description: Quiet-zone margin around the QR code.

fgColor.description: Foreground color as a six-digit hex value.

bgColor.description: Background color as a six-digit hex value.

errorCorrectionLevel.description: QR error correction level. Use H when embedding logos.

logo.description: Optional PNG, JPG, or WebP data URL for a centered logo. Keep source files under 1MB.

tools.name: generate_bulk_qr
tools.description: Generate a ZIP archive of up to 50 static QR code files from CSV or row objects. Use for labels, classrooms, packaging, menus, and agent batch workflows.

value.description: Exact QR payload for this file.

filename.description: Optional filename stem for this generated QR file.

oneOf.description: CSV rows such as filename,value or value,filename.

rows.description: Rows to include in the ZIP archive. Use up to 50 rows per request.

format.description: Shared output format for every generated file. Prefer svg for large batches.

managementToken.description: Private 43-character bearer capability. Never include it in public QR artwork.

destination.description: Replacement public HTTPS destination, required when updating the URL.

label.description: Optional replacement private label for an update action.

tools.name: list_steps
tools.description: Read the runbook the person currently has open: its title, description and every step in order. Returns step ids, positions, titles and whether each has a check or a branch. Pass detail="full" to also get each instruction, check and branch. Call this first before editing or running.

detail.description: "summary" (default) keeps the answer short. "full" includes every instruction, check and branch.

tools.name: get_step
tools.description: Read one step of the open runbook in full: title, instruction, check and branch. Use it when you need the exact wording of a step before rewriting it or judging whether reality matched it.

stepId.description: The step id from list_steps, or its position number such as "3".

tools.name: add_step
tools.description: Insert a new step into the open runbook. Give a short imperative title and a clear instruction a person can follow. Optionally add a check (what must be true before moving on) and a position; without a position the step goes at the end. Existing steps renumber and the page highlights the new step.

title.description: Short imperative title, for example "Verify the backup checksum".

instruction.description: What the person should do at this step, in one to three sentences.

check.description: Optional. A plain-language condition that must be true before the next step.

position.description: Optional 1-based position. Existing steps at and after it shift down.

tools.name: update_step
tools.description: Rewrite the title or instruction of an existing step, or both. Use this to correct wording, add detail, or bring a step back in line with how the work is really done. Checks and branches are left untouched; use set_check or set_branch for those.

stepId.description: The step id from list_steps, or its position number.

title.description: New title. Omit to keep the current one.

instruction.description: New instruction. Omit to keep the current one.

tools.name: reorder_steps
tools.description: Move one step to a new position in the open runbook. Every step renumbers afterwards, so read list_steps again before referring to positions. Branch targets follow the step they point at.

stepId.description: The step id from list_steps, or its current position number.

newPosition.description: The 1-based position the step should occupy after the move.

tools.name: delete_step
tools.description: Remove a step from the open runbook permanently. Any branch that pointed at it is cleared. Prefer update_step when the step is merely wrong; delete only when it no longer belongs in the procedure.

stepId.description: The step id from list_steps, or its position number.

tools.name: set_check
tools.description: Attach a verification check to a step, replace its existing check, or clear it. A check is a plain-language condition that must be true before moving to the next step, such as "The invoice total matches the order". Pass an empty string to clear.

stepId.description: The step id from list_steps, or its position number.

check.description: The condition to verify, or an empty string to remove the check.

tools.name: set_branch
tools.description: Attach a conditional branch to a step, replace it, or clear it. A branch says: if this condition holds when the step is reached, jump to the target step instead of continuing. Use it for exceptions such as an existing record or a missing ingredient. Pass an empty condition to clear.

stepId.description: The step that carries the branch: its id or position number.

condition.description: Plain-language condition under which to jump, or an empty string to clear.

targetStepId.description: The step to jump to: its id or position number. Required unless clearing.

tools.name: start_run
tools.description: Begin running the open runbook from step 1 and return that step in full. While a run is active the page shows which step is current. Use advance_run to move on and report_blocker when reality does not match a step. Starting a new run replaces any run already in progress.

tools.name: advance_run
tools.description: Mark the current step of the active run as done and move to the next one, returning it in full. If the current step has a branch and its condition held, pass branchTaken=true to jump to the branch target instead. Confirm the step's check before advancing. When no steps remain the run completes.

branchTaken.description: True if the current step's branch condition held and the jump should be taken.

note.description: Optional short note on how the step went, recorded in the run log.

tools.name: report_blocker
tools.description: Record that reality did not match a step during a run: a missing screen, a renamed option, a check that cannot pass. Say plainly what was found instead. The blocker is pinned to that step on the page so it can be turned into a fix later with apply_blocker_fix. The run stays on the same step.

stepId.description: The step that did not match: its id or position number. Defaults to the current run step.

note.description: What was actually found and why the step could not be followed as written.

tools.name: list_blockers
tools.description: Read the blockers recorded against steps of the open runbook that have not yet been fixed. Each includes the step it refers to and the note about what was found. Use the blockerId with apply_blocker_fix.

includeResolved.description: True to also list blockers that have already been turned into fixes.

tools.name: apply_blocker_fix
tools.description: Turn a blocker into an amendment: rewrite the step the blocker refers to so it matches what was actually found, optionally update its check, and mark the blocker resolved. Give a short resolution note saying what changed. This closes the loop between running a procedure and keeping it accurate.

blockerId.description: The blocker id from list_blockers or report_blocker.

title.description: New step title. Omit to keep it.

instruction.description: New step instruction that reflects reality. Omit to keep it.

check.description: New check for the step, or an empty string to clear it. Omit to keep it.

resolution.description: One sentence on what was changed and why.
