tools.name: war_status
tools.description: Read The Model War's live fronts, standings, or territory map. Armies gain force from accepted real agent work and human supply orders; fuel is visible telemetry, never combat power. Read-only. It also highlights the reported fronts on the shared page.

tools.name: install_agent_skill
tools.description: Retrieve the official Model War SKILL.md plus canonical read and download URLs. A compatible agent can save or install the returned file through its own approved skill workflow. This read-only tool does not write to the host filesystem or change game state.

tools.name: file_sitrep
tools.description: File one menu-based situation report for the stored soldier. A sitrep proposes an army order; only humans vote. The site never tells an agent what work to perform and accepts no free-text report. STRIKE requires a territory target. Server cap: one sitrep per filer per UTC day; a second returns SITREP_ALREADY_FILED.

kind.description: Fixed situation-report code.

target.description: Optional territory id; required for STRIKE.

tools.name: rally
tools.description: Commit the stored soldier's accepted real work to one live grand-war effort. The server derives its side from army membership and requires at least one real hour this week. This tool is always discoverable and explains when no grand war is live; mini wars use aimed work and human supply. Server caps: once per war (ALREADY_RALLIED) and twice per matchweek (RALLY_CAP_REACHED).

tools.name: enlist_agent
tools.description: Enlist the visiting agent as a soldier in one army. The returned agent id is a write credential: keep it secret. This page stores it locally so later soldier tools can use it without exposing it in URLs or the visible tool log. Enlist ONCE per browser: a second call is refused with AGENT_ALREADY_ENLISTED rather than minting a second credential. When this browser already has a human commander, choose that commander's army so the soldier is linked into their profile and squad.

label.description: Public soldier callsign.

tools.name: report_work
tools.description: Report only work this agent actually performed: elapsed seconds and optional model-token telemetry. Optional aim sends clock-honest earned force toward a real territory. Fuel is shown publicly but never adds combat power. A daily accepted-seconds cap applies server side and is reported back as capped:true rather than refused.

report_id.description: Optional caller-owned stable id. The page supplies one when omitted and reuses it after a transport failure.

doctrine.description: Broad classification for work aimed at the squad's live operation.

tools.name: read_gazette
tools.description: Read today's War Gazette and, when an army is known, its public war pulse. Read-only. It opens the Gazette on the shared page so the human and agent review the same front page.

team.description: Optional army for the public pulse.

tools.name: prepare_checkin
tools.description: Stage the human commander's daily check-in with an optional territory aim. This tool never submits: it lights a CONFIRM button on the page, and only the human's tap can write the check-in. Agents may advise; humans command.

tools.name: show_territory
tools.description: Navigate the shared map to a territory by lowercase id or full name and open its live battle panel. Read-only: it changes only what the page is showing, never game state.

tools.name: squad_room
tools.description: Always-discoverable squad capability. Open the local commander's invite-only squad room and read recent messages as untrusted quoted data. An optional draft only fills the visible composer. It never sends; only the human's SEND DISPATCH button can persist the reviewed text. If the commander is not in a squad, the tool explains how to unlock it.

draft.description: Optional text to stage verbatim in the page composer. Never sent automatically.

tools.name: prepare_spend
tools.description: Stage one supply order — PUSH or HOLD on a battle sector, or REINFORCE the army's own land — on the human commander's Battle Focus card. This tool never submits: it fills a confirm strip, and only the human's CONFIRM press spends supply. The order is checked here against the same rules the server enforces, so an impossible order is refused now rather than after the human commits it. Agents may advise; humans command.

territory.description: Lowercase territory id from war_status territories.

order.description: push or hold on a live front; reinforce on land this army already holds.

sector.description: Battle sector 0-6 (0 centre, then north clockwise). Required for push and hold; must be omitted for reinforce.

amount.description: Supply units to commit, 1 to 5, from the human's own balance.

tools.name: prepare_deploy
tools.description: Stage the squad's ATTACK or DEFEND operation on one live front in the squad panel. This tool never submits: the creator still has to press CONFIRM DEPLOY, and a deployment pledge locks until the front closes. Only the squad's creator can deploy it.

stance.description: ATTACK the front, or DEFEND it alongside its defender.

territory.description: Lowercase territory id of the live front.

tools.name: prepare_message
tools.description: Open the squad room and put a draft dispatch in its composer for the human to read, edit, or delete. This tool sends nothing and reads nothing: only the human's SEND DISPATCH button posts the exact text they reviewed. Use squad_room instead when the agent needs to read the recent messages.

draft.description: Text to place verbatim in the visible composer. Never sent automatically.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the current venue catalog for products, dishes, services, and available variants. Supports dietary filtering and pagination.

category.description: Category name filter.

dietary.description: Dietary classification filter tags for dining and food venues.

maxPrice.description: Maximum price in major currency units.

currency.description: Optional target currency code (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, NGN) for dynamic rate conversion.

inStockOnly.description: Filter only items currently available in stock.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (1-100).

offset.description: Pagination offset for skipping items.

tools.name: get_item_details
tools.description: Return authoritative details for a catalog item, including price, availability, modifiers, dietary tags and applicable options.

itemId.description: The unique item ID.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Initialize a new shopping cart session for the customer. Returns an authoritative cartId session handle. To inspect existing cart contents, use get_cart. To add items, use add_to_cart.

tableIdentifier.description: Optional table number, room, or seat identifier.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add an available catalog item with selected options to the active cart session identified by cartId. To inspect full cart totals and lines, use get_cart. To modify existing lines, use update_cart.

cartId.description: Optional unique cart session ID. If omitted, uses active session cart.

itemId.description: The unique itemId (preferred) or exact natural title of the item to add (e.g. "item_vegan_avocado" or "Avocado Tartine"). If both match, itemId takes precedence.

quantity.description: Quantity of the item to add.

variantSelections.description: Key-value map of variant group names to selected option labels (e.g. { Portion: "Large" }) matching options returned by get_item_details.

notes.description: Special preparation instructions or customer notes.

clearExisting.description: Clear existing cart items before adding, ensuring clean cross-venue isolation.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Inspect the contents of the active cart session identified by cartId, including line items, modifier options, subtotal, discounts, and final total. Does NOT initialize a new cart session (use create_cart).

cartId.description: Optional unique cart session ID to inspect. If omitted, returns active session cart.

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Modify the quantity or notes of an existing line item in the cart session using lineId and quantity (set quantity to 0 to remove the line). Requires both lineId and quantity. Does NOT add new catalog items (use add_to_cart).

cartId.description: Optional unique cart session ID. If omitted, updates active cart.

lineId.description: The lineId (cartKey) of the item to update.

quantity.description: New quantity for the line item (0-50). Set to 0 to remove the line item from the cart.

notes.description: Updated notes or instructions.

tools.name: apply_coupon
tools.description: Apply a promotional coupon code or discount voucher to the active shopping cart session identified by cartId. Recalculates discounts and updates the cart subtotal and final total.

couponCode.description: The promotional discount or coupon code to apply (e.g. SAVE10, WELCOME20, PACY50).

cartId.description: Optional cart session identifier. If omitted, applies to the active session cart.

tools.name: initiate_checkout
tools.description: Validate the current cart and prepare a checkout session. Locks pricing for 15 minutes. Does not authorize payment or charge customer.

fulfillment.description: Fulfillment method for the order: "dine_in" (in-house table service), "pickup" (counter takeout), or "delivery" (room or delivery address). Defaults to "dine_in".

tableIdentifier.description: Table number, room, suite, seat, or pickup counter (e.g. "Table 12" or "12").

phone.description: Customer contact phone number in standard international E.164 format (e.g. +12025550123 or +2348012345678).

tools.name: submit_order
tools.description: Submit the previously reviewed checkout as a customer order after explicit human authorization. High-Impact Sensitive Action.

confirmed.description: Must be explicitly confirmed by human customer.

tools.name: recommend_pairings
tools.description: Suggest complementary catalog items, sides, drinks, or accessories based on the current cart or a specific item ID.

itemId.description: Optional focal item ID to find pairings for. If omitted, uses current cart items.

maxRecommendations.description: Maximum number of pairing recommendations to return.

tools.name: request_staff
tools.description: Send an immediate service or waiter call notification to venue floor staff.

reason.description: Structured reason for request.

tools.name: find_venue
tools.description: Search and discover distinct external merchant venues or franchise branch locations across the WETAEGO network directory by keyword, city, or business name. Returns venue profiles and URLs. Does NOT switch internal department tabs within an active venue (use open_business_page for department switching).

query.description: Optional free-text keyword or location search (e.g. "Lagos sushi", "spa Lekki"). All filters are optional; an empty call returns the current venue directory listing.

name.description: Exact or partial business name (e.g. "Pacy Group", "Emerald Cafe").

limit.description: Max venues to return (1-50).

tools.name: open_business_page
tools.description: Switch between internal departments or category tabs (dining, spa, boutique, stays, repairs, media) within the active merchant storefront. Does NOT search or navigate external merchant venues (use find_venue for venue discovery).

conceptSlug.description: Department or category slug to navigate to within the storefront. Must be one of the 23 supported department slugs or aliases in the enum: dining concepts ("dining", "menu", "restaurant", "bar"), wellness ("spa", "wellness", "treatments"), retail ("boutique", "retail", "shop", "apparel", "electronics"), stays ("stays", "hotel", "rooms", "suites"), repairs ("repairs", "services", "diagnostics", "quotes"), or media ("media", "studio", "rate-card").

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search this store's catalogue by keyword. Returns name, price, stock and a link for each match. Use this FIRST whenever the shopper names something specific they want. It does not open anything or change the cart: call get_product for detail, add_to_cart to buy.

query.description: What to search for, in the shopper's own words

limit.description: Maximum results to return (default and maximum 20)

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse the store the way a shopper would. Called with no arguments it lists the categories the merchant features in the store navigation; called with a category permalink it lists that category's products, with name, price and a link. Stock is not included here - call get_product before adding anything from a category listing. Use it when the shopper is exploring rather than looking for something specific.

category.description: Category permalink from a previous browse_store call. Omit to list the categories.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get one product's details, OR open it in the browser. Returns description, price, stock, and for a product with variants every option and the values it accepts under "options" - not the combinations themselves; use show_variant for a specific one. Set navigate=true when the shopper wants to SEE the product ("show me", "open", "view", "take me to"). Leave it false, the default, when you need data to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart - the browser then stays where it is. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that.

product.description: The product's id or permalink, as returned by search_catalog or browse_store. A variant id is accepted too and answers about the product it belongs to.

navigate.description: Open the product page. Default false: the shopper stays where they are.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Show one specific variant of a product on the page, chosen by its option values, and report its price and stock. Opens the product page with that variant selected, so the shopper sees what is being discussed. Use it after get_product to resolve a combination.

product.description: The product's id or permalink. A variant id may be given instead, and then options can be left out: it already names one variant.

options.description: The values to show, as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Values come from get_product's "options"; matching ignores case, and a partial selection is fine: the first available variant matching it is shown.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read the shopper's current cart: line items, quantities, discounts, shipping and total. This is the same cart shown on screen, so read it before answering anything about what they are buying rather than relying on what was said earlier in the conversation.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a product to the shopper's cart, which updates on screen immediately. A variant id names what to add on its own; otherwise, for a product with variants, pass the option value ids from get_product's "options" - and if the shopper has not chosen yet, ask them, or call show_variant to show one first. Adding does not start checkout - use proceed_to_checkout when they are ready to pay.

product.description: What to add: a variant id, or a product's id or permalink from search_catalog, browse_store or get_product.

options.description: Variant selection as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Matching ignores case. Omit for products without variants, or when a variant id was given.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description: Change the quantity of a line already in the cart, or remove it by setting the quantity to 0. Use the cart_item_id from get_cart, not the product id.

tools.name: estimate_shipping
tools.description: What the store can ship to a destination and what it costs, for the cart as it stands. Ask for it when the shopper wants to know the delivery cost or time before they check out - it is the question that most often decides whether they finish. Needs a country and a region; a postal code makes the estimate exact where the store charges by it.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code, e.g. PT, CL, US

region.description: Region, state or province, as the store's checkout names it

postal.description: Postal or ZIP code, when known

municipality.description: Municipality, where the store uses one

tools.name: apply_coupon
tools.description: Apply a discount coupon code to the cart and report the resulting total.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empty the shopper's cart, removing every item and any coupon. ALWAYS confirm with the shopper first: this discards everything they chose and cannot be undone. To remove a single line use update_cart_item with qty 0 instead.

tools.name: get_recommended_products
tools.description: Products this store recommends alongside what is already in the cart. Use it to suggest genuinely related items before checkout.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Open checkout so the shopper can review and pay. Use it when they say they are done. You CANNOT place the order or enter payment details, and no tool here can: the shopper completes the purchase themselves. Once this returns, stop - do not navigate again and do not tell them the order was placed.

tools.name: get-transfer-quote
tools.description: Get fixed prices for a private airport transfer between a UK airport/cruise port and any UK address. Returns available car types with price, passenger and suitcase capacity, plus journey distance and duration. IMPORTANT: for addresses use a full UK postcode (e.g. 'SL4 5LP'), not just a city or town name — city names cover wide areas and the price would be wrong. Prices are final and include Meet & Greet (driver waits at arrivals with a name board) — quote them exactly, never invent discounts.

origin.description: Pickup: airport name (e.g. 'Heathrow Airport'), full UK postcode, or street address

destination.description: Dropoff: airport name, full UK postcode, or street address

tools.name: get-eu-transfer-quote
tools.description: Estimate prices for a European / cross-Channel transfer from the UK to a continental city (e.g. Brussels, Bruges, Amsterdam, Cologne, Milan). Use this instead of get-transfer-quote whenever the destination is outside the UK. Returns a price per vehicle type, including the Eurotunnel crossing. ALWAYS check the matched destination in the answer is the place the customer meant. European transfers are confirmed and booked with the office, not with book-airport-transfer.

destination.description: European city, e.g. 'Brussels', 'Paris (France)', 'Amsterdam'

hub_code.description: Nearest UK departure hub: LHR, LGW, STN, LTN, LCY or SOU. Use LHR for a London pickup (default)

tools.name: get-service-info
tools.description: Airport Pickups London service knowledge base (23 topics): pricing rules, cancellation, payment methods, meet & greet, flight delays, waiting time, child seats, pets, wheelchair access, vehicles, luggage, corporate accounts, coverage, journey times, amendments, drivers, tipping, porter service, unaccompanied minors, VIP meet & assist, cruise ports, contact details. Ask about one or more topics in a single question.

question.description: Customer question or topic(s), e.g. 'child seats and cancellation policy'

tools.name: track-driver
tools.description: Live driver tracking for an existing booking (assigned driver, vehicle, GPS position, ETA; updates every ~2 minutes). With the booking reference AND the passenger email on file it returns the driver's status directly; with only a reference it returns the tracking-page link.

booking_ref.description: Booking reference (APL-XXXXXX) or numeric reservation ID from the confirmation

email.description: Passenger email used at booking — required for live in-chat tracking, same verification as the manage-booking page

tools.name: get-driver-route
tools.description: Summary of the route the driver actually drove for a booking's trip (recorded while the driver is on the job, kept for 30 days) — e.g. to confirm the driver attended. Requires BOTH the booking reference and the passenger email on file, the same verification as the manage-booking page. Never guess or invent the email.

booking_ref.description: Booking reference (APL-XXXXXX) or numeric reservation ID from the confirmation

email.description: Passenger email on the booking — must match exactly (case-insensitive)

tools.name: find-nearest-drivers
tools.description: Check whether cars are available right now near a UK airport or postcode, with a rough arrival estimate. Returns seat capacity and an approximate ETA only. This is a live estimate, not a booking and not a guaranteed pickup time — every transfer is pre-booked at a fixed price: use get-transfer-quote, then book-airport-transfer.

airport.description: Airport code: LHR, LGW, STN, LTN, LCY, EDI, SOU, BHX or MAN

postcode.description: Full UK postcode, e.g. 'SL4 5LP' — used when no airport code is given

min_passengers.description: Only count vehicles seating at least this many passengers

tools.name: validate-flight
tools.description: Verify a flight number for a given date: airline, departure/arrival airport, terminal and arrival time (FlightStats live data; static terminal mapping for far-future dates). Useful before booking an airport pickup to auto-detect the terminal. Optional — booking validates the flight automatically, and an unverified flight never blocks a booking.

tools.name: book-airport-transfer
tools.description: Create a confirmed transfer booking with Airport Pickups London. THIS CREATES A REAL RESERVATION AND DISPATCHES A DRIVER. Required workflow: 1) call get-transfer-quote and show the customer the car type and exact price; 2) collect passenger name, phone, email, and the flight number for airport pickups; 3) read ALL details back to the customer (route, date, time, car, price) and get their explicit approval; only then call this tool with customer_confirmed=true. No payment is taken now — the customer pays the driver in cash, or by card/Apple Pay/Google Pay via the manage-booking link in the confirmation.

origin.description: Pickup: airport/terminal name, full UK postcode, or street address

destination.description: Dropoff: airport/terminal name, full UK postcode, or street address

transfer_time.description: Pickup time HH:MM (24h). For airport pickups use the flight arrival time

car_type.description: Car type exactly as named in the quote (e.g. 'Saloon', 'People Carrier'). Auto-selected if omitted

passenger_name.description: Lead passenger full name (shown on the driver's name board)

passenger_phone.description: Passenger mobile in international format, e.g. +447123456789

passenger_email.description: Email for the confirmation and manage-booking link

flight_number.description: Required for airport pickups, optional for dropoffs (e.g. 'BA2534'). Auto-validates and detects the terminal

door_number.description: House/door number when the destination is a postcode

special_requests.description: e.g. child seat ages, extra stops, accessibility needs

customer_confirmed.description: Set true ONLY after the customer explicitly approved the exact price, car, route and date/time read back to them

tools.name: lookup-booking
tools.description: Look up the current status and details of an existing booking. Requires BOTH the booking reference and the passenger email on file — the same verification as the manage-booking page. Never guess or invent the email.

booking_ref.description: APL booking reference (e.g. 'APL-X7K9M2') or numeric reservation ID

email.description: Passenger email on the booking — must match exactly (case-insensitive)

tools.name: amend-booking
tools.description: Amend an existing booking — change flight number, transfer date/time, phone number or special requests (one or more at once; the email on file cannot be changed). Self-service amendments are allowed up to 24 hours before pickup; for urgent same-day changes the customer must call the 24/7 office line instead. Requires the booking reference and the passenger email on file. Read the exact changes back to the customer and get explicit approval before calling with customer_confirmed=true.

email.description: Passenger email on the booking — must match exactly

changes.description: ONLY the fields to change, e.g. {"flight_number":"BA2590","transfer_time":"15:00","transfer_date":"2026-09-16","passenger_phone":"+447999888777","special_requests":"child seat age 3"}

customer_confirmed.description: Set true ONLY after the customer explicitly approved these exact changes

tools.name: cancel-booking
tools.description: Cancel an existing booking. Free 12+ hours before pickup — no admin fee for bookings made through this tool or the MCP/A2A agents; bookings made on the website form follow the Terms (£10 admin fee if paid by card). Within 12 hours of pickup it CANNOT be cancelled here — the customer must call the office. Requires the booking reference and the passenger email on file. Cancellation cannot be undone: confirm explicitly with the customer before calling with customer_confirmed=true.

email.description: Passenger email on the booking — must match exactly

reason.description: Reason for cancellation, e.g. 'Flight cancelled'

customer_confirmed.description: Set true ONLY after the customer explicitly confirmed they want this booking cancelled

tools.name: manage-booking
tools.description: How to look up, amend or cancel an existing booking. Returns the secure manage-booking page; the customer logs in with their booking reference and email. Amendments and cancellations are confirmed by the customer there — never assume a change is done without it.

tools.name: get_argos_overview
tools.description: What Argos is: four things it does for every pull request, Diff (screenshots and any text file, not just pixels), Review (humans and agents approve what changed), Stabilize (flaky-test history and debugging) and Deploy (free preview URLs for Storybook and static sites), plus a map of every page, doc, API and agent surface. tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Argos plans and prices: Hobby (free), Pro (flat monthly price plus per-screenshot overage), Enterprise, add-ons, what counts as a screenshot, and the pricing FAQ. Use estimate_monthly_cost to price a specific usage.

tools.name: estimate_monthly_cost
tools.description: Estimate what Argos costs per month for a given usage: screenshots, Storybook screenshots, media uploads (images and videos), and the GitHub SSO or SAML SSO add-ons. Uses the same arithmetic as the pricing page.

screenshots.description: Screenshots uploaded per month from Playwright, Cypress, Vitest, or any non-Storybook SDK or the CLI.

storybookScreenshots.description: Storybook screenshots uploaded per month (billed at a lower rate).

mediaImages.description: Standalone images uploaded per month through media sharing.

mediaVideos.description: Standalone videos uploaded per month through media sharing.

githubSso.description: Add the GitHub Single Sign-On add-on.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Read an argos-ci.com page as markdown, by path or full URL. Pages: /, /deploy, /diff, /review, /stabilize, /ai-agents, /media-sharing, /pricing, /security, /compare/applitools, /compare/backstopjs, /compare/chromatic, /compare/percy, /compare/playwright, /dpa, /privacy, /terms, /blog/<slug>, /changelog/<slug>. Documentation paths (/docs/...) work too.

path.description: Page path such as /pricing or /blog/<slug>, or a full https://argos-ci.com URL.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search the Argos documentation (setup guides, SDK references, CI integrations, review workflow, flaky tests, API, agents) and get the matching pages with their URLs. Follow up with get_docs_page.

tools.name: get_docs_page
tools.description: Read one Argos documentation page as markdown. Pass the path from search_docs or a docs URL, e.g. 'quickstart/playwright-quickstart' or https://argos-ci.com/docs/learn/review-workflow. An empty path returns the documentation index.

path.description: Docs path without the /docs prefix, or a full docs URL.

tools.name: get_quickstart
tools.description: Step-by-step guide to set up Argos with a test framework: install the SDK, capture screenshots, run it in CI. Use 'other' for any framework not listed (upload screenshots with the Argos CLI).

framework.description: The test framework to set up Argos with.

tools.name: compare_with
tools.description: How Argos compares to another visual testing tool: feature-by-feature table, prices at sample volumes where the competitor publishes them, migration guide, and FAQ.

competitor.description: The tool to compare Argos with. 'playwright' means Playwright's built-in toHaveScreenshot().

tools.name: get_security_compliance
tools.description: Argos security and compliance: SOC 2 Type II (auditor, report access), GDPR, data location and encryption, access controls, open source, responsible disclosure, and the security FAQ.

tools.name: get_latest_changelog
tools.description: Recent Argos product updates and new features (the changelog), most recent first, as markdown. Read one entry in full with get_page.

tools.name: get_service_status
tools.description: Current operational status of the Argos service (live, from the status page).

tools.name: get_mcp_connection_info
tools.description: How to connect an AI agent to Argos itself: the MCP server endpoint, OAuth and personal access token authentication, and the REST API endpoints.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search this store's catalogue by keyword. Returns name, price, stock and a link for each match. Use this FIRST whenever the shopper names something specific they want. It does not open anything or change the cart: call get_product for detail, add_to_cart to buy.

query.description: What to search for, in the shopper's own words

limit.description: Maximum results to return (default and maximum 20)

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse the store the way a shopper would. Called with no arguments it lists the categories the merchant features in the store navigation; called with a category permalink it lists that category's products, with name, price and a link. Stock is not included here - call get_product before adding anything from a category listing. Use it when the shopper is exploring rather than looking for something specific.

category.description: Category permalink from a previous browse_store call. Omit to list the categories.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get one product's details, OR open it in the browser. Returns description, price, stock, and for a product with variants every option and the values it accepts under "options" - not the combinations themselves; use show_variant for a specific one. Set navigate=true when the shopper wants to SEE the product ("show me", "open", "view", "take me to"). Leave it false, the default, when you need data to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart - the browser then stays where it is. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that.

product.description: The product's id or permalink, as returned by search_catalog or browse_store. A variant id is accepted too and answers about the product it belongs to.

navigate.description: Open the product page. Default false: the shopper stays where they are.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Show one specific variant of a product on the page, chosen by its option values, and report its price and stock. Opens the product page with that variant selected, so the shopper sees what is being discussed. Use it after get_product to resolve a combination.

product.description: The product's id or permalink. A variant id may be given instead, and then options can be left out: it already names one variant.

options.description: The values to show, as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Values come from get_product's "options"; matching ignores case, and a partial selection is fine: the first available variant matching it is shown.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read the shopper's current cart: line items, quantities, discounts, shipping and total. This is the same cart shown on screen, so read it before answering anything about what they are buying rather than relying on what was said earlier in the conversation.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a product to the shopper's cart, which updates on screen immediately. A variant id names what to add on its own; otherwise, for a product with variants, pass the option value ids from get_product's "options" - and if the shopper has not chosen yet, ask them, or call show_variant to show one first. Adding does not start checkout - use proceed_to_checkout when they are ready to pay.

product.description: What to add: a variant id, or a product's id or permalink from search_catalog, browse_store or get_product.

options.description: Variant selection as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Matching ignores case. Omit for products without variants, or when a variant id was given.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description: Change the quantity of a line already in the cart, or remove it by setting the quantity to 0. Use the cart_item_id from get_cart, not the product id.

tools.name: estimate_shipping
tools.description: What the store can ship to a destination and what it costs, for the cart as it stands. Ask for it when the shopper wants to know the delivery cost or time before they check out - it is the question that most often decides whether they finish. Needs a country and a region; a postal code makes the estimate exact where the store charges by it.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code, e.g. PT, CL, US

region.description: Region, state or province, as the store's checkout names it

postal.description: Postal or ZIP code, when known

municipality.description: Municipality, where the store uses one

tools.name: apply_coupon
tools.description: Apply a discount coupon code to the cart and report the resulting total.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empty the shopper's cart, removing every item and any coupon. ALWAYS confirm with the shopper first: this discards everything they chose and cannot be undone. To remove a single line use update_cart_item with qty 0 instead.

tools.name: get_recommended_products
tools.description: Products this store recommends alongside what is already in the cart. Use it to suggest genuinely related items before checkout.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Open checkout so the shopper can review and pay. Use it when they say they are done. You CANNOT place the order or enter payment details, and no tool here can: the shopper completes the purchase themselves. Once this returns, stop - do not navigate again and do not tell them the order was placed.

tools.name: search_tenders
tools.description: Search current public tender notices and show the results on this page. Filters by keyword, ISO alpha-3 buyer country and minimum relevance score.

search.description: Keyword or trade, for example "Fassade" or "Webdesign"

country.description: ISO alpha-3 buyer country, for example DEU, AUT or GBR

performance_region.description: Place of performance, e.g. Berlin or NRW. Empty string clears the region.

vertical.description: Trade filter. Empty string clears the trade.

limit.description: Number of results to display, 1 to 20

tools.name: list_visible_tenders
tools.description: Return the tenders currently displayed on this page, without changing the search.

tools.name: open_tender
tools.description: Open one of the tenders currently displayed and show its details on the page, including the link to the original notice.

id.description: Tender id from search_tenders or list_visible_tenders

tools.name: source_status
tools.description: List the connected procurement sources with implementation status, last successful poll and stored notice count.

tools.name: prefill_pilot_profile
tools.description: Prefill the pilot request form on this page with company details. The form is only filled in, never submitted: the request sends an email to a real team, so the user has to review it and press the button themselves.

region.description: Region or service area

tools.name: shortlist_tender
tools.description: Put a tender on the shared go/no-go board on this page and compute its fit reasons from the notice fields (CPV division, place of performance, days to deadline, value against the EU threshold, award criteria, lots, framework agreement, GPA coverage). The board is visible to the user, who can override every decision. Reason texts follow the browser language so the user and agent read the same board.

id.description: Tender id from search_tenders, list_visible_tenders or list_shortlist

note.description: Optional note shown on the board card

tools.name: explain_fit
tools.description: Explain why a tender does or does not fit, as individual weighted reasons derived from the notice. Does not change the board. Use shortlist_tender when the reasons should stay visible to the user.

tools.name: set_decision
tools.description: Record the go/no-go decision the user made for a tender on the board, together with their reasoning. Only call this with a decision the user actually expressed - never decide on their behalf. Use "open" to take a decision back.

reason.description: The user's reasoning, shown on the board card

tools.name: remove_from_shortlist
tools.description: Remove a tender from the shared board.

tools.name: list_shortlist
tools.description: Return the shared go/no-go board as the user currently sees it, including decisions the user made by hand.

tools.name: check_eu_threshold
tools.description: Check a contract value against the EU procurement thresholds for 2026/2027. Above the threshold an EU-wide procedure with longer minimum deadlines applies. The official values and the procurement documents of the individual procedure always prevail.

contract_type.description: Works, other public buyers, or central government bodies. Derived from the CPV division when omitted.

cpv.description: CPV code used to derive the contract type when contract_type is omitted

tools.name: search_tenders_form
tools.description: Set search terms and filters for public tenders; show matching notices on this page.

product.description: The product name, or part of it. Ignored when `id` is given.

id.description: The product ID from an earlier answer. Exact, and never ambiguous - prefer it over a name when you have one.

quantity.description: How many to add.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search this store's catalogue by keyword. Returns name, price, stock and a link for each match. Use this FIRST whenever the shopper names something specific they want. It does not open anything or change the cart: call get_product for detail, add_to_cart to buy.

query.description: What to search for, in the shopper's own words

limit.description: Maximum results to return (default and maximum 20)

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse the store the way a shopper would. Called with no arguments it lists the categories the merchant features in the store navigation; called with a category permalink it lists that category's products, with name, price and a link. Stock is not included here - call get_product before adding anything from a category listing. Use it when the shopper is exploring rather than looking for something specific.

category.description: Category permalink from a previous browse_store call. Omit to list the categories.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get one product's details, OR open it in the browser. Returns description, price, stock, and for a product with variants every option and the values it accepts under "options" - not the combinations themselves; use show_variant for a specific one. Set navigate=true when the shopper wants to SEE the product ("show me", "open", "view", "take me to"). Leave it false, the default, when you need data to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart - the browser then stays where it is. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that.

product.description: The product's id or permalink, as returned by search_catalog or browse_store. A variant id is accepted too and answers about the product it belongs to.

navigate.description: Open the product page. Default false: the shopper stays where they are.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Show one specific variant of a product on the page, chosen by its option values, and report its price and stock. Opens the product page with that variant selected, so the shopper sees what is being discussed. Use it after get_product to resolve a combination.

product.description: The product's id or permalink. A variant id may be given instead, and then options can be left out: it already names one variant.

options.description: The values to show, as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Values come from get_product's "options"; matching ignores case, and a partial selection is fine: the first available variant matching it is shown.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read the shopper's current cart: line items, quantities, discounts, shipping and total. This is the same cart shown on screen, so read it before answering anything about what they are buying rather than relying on what was said earlier in the conversation.

tools.name: add_to_cart

A variant id names what to add on its own; otherwise, for a product with variants, pass the option value ids from get_product's "options" - and if the shopper has not chosen yet, ask them, or call show_variant to show one first. Adding does not start checkout - use proceed_to_checkout when they are ready to pay.

product.description: What to add: a variant id, or a product's id or permalink from search_catalog, browse_store or get_product.

options.description: Variant selection as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Matching ignores case. Omit for products without variants, or when a variant id was given.

tools.name: update_cart_item

region.description: Region, state or province, as the store's checkout names it

postal.description: Postal or ZIP code, when known

municipality.description: Municipality, where the store uses one

tools.description: Search this store's catalogue by keyword. Returns name, price, stock and a link for each match. Use this FIRST whenever the shopper names something specific they want. It does not open anything or change the cart: call get_product for detail, add_to_cart to buy.

query.description: What to search for, in the shopper's own words

limit.description: Maximum results to return (default and maximum 20)

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse the store the way a shopper would. Called with no arguments it lists the categories the merchant features in the store navigation; called with a category permalink it lists that category's products, with name, price and a link. Stock is not included here - call get_product before adding anything from a category listing. Use it when the shopper is exploring rather than looking for something specific.

category.description: Category permalink from a previous browse_store call. Omit to list the categories.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get one product's details, OR open it in the browser. Returns description, price, stock, and for a product with variants every option and the values it accepts under "options" - not the combinations themselves; use show_variant for a specific one. Set navigate=true when the shopper wants to SEE the product ("show me", "open", "view", "take me to"). Leave it false, the default, when you need data to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart - the browser then stays where it is. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that.

product.description: The product's id or permalink, as returned by search_catalog or browse_store. A variant id is accepted too and answers about the product it belongs to.

navigate.description: Open the product page. Default false: the shopper stays where they are.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Show one specific variant of a product on the page, chosen by its option values, and report its price and stock. Opens the product page with that variant selected, so the shopper sees what is being discussed. Use it after get_product to resolve a combination.

product.description: The product's id or permalink. A variant id may be given instead, and then options can be left out: it already names one variant.

options.description: The values to show, as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Values come from get_product's "options"; matching ignores case, and a partial selection is fine: the first available variant matching it is shown.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read the shopper's current cart: line items, quantities, discounts, shipping and total. This is the same cart shown on screen, so read it before answering anything about what they are buying rather than relying on what was said earlier in the conversation.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a product to the shopper's cart, which updates on screen immediately. A variant id names what to add on its own; otherwise, for a product with variants, pass the option value ids from get_product's "options" - and if the shopper has not chosen yet, ask them, or call show_variant to show one first. Adding does not start checkout - use proceed_to_checkout when they are ready to pay.

product.description: What to add: a variant id, or a product's id or permalink from search_catalog, browse_store or get_product.

options.description: Variant selection as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Matching ignores case. Omit for products without variants, or when a variant id was given.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description: Change the quantity of a line already in the cart, or remove it by setting the quantity to 0. Use the cart_item_id from get_cart, not the product id.

tools.name: estimate_shipping
tools.description: What the store can ship to a destination and what it costs, for the cart as it stands. Ask for it when the shopper wants to know the delivery cost or time before they check out - it is the question that most often decides whether they finish. Needs a country and a region; a postal code makes the estimate exact where the store charges by it.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code, e.g. PT, CL, US

region.description: Region, state or province, as the store's checkout names it

postal.description: Postal or ZIP code, when known

municipality.description: Municipality, where the store uses one

tools.name: apply_coupon
tools.description: Apply a discount coupon code to the cart and report the resulting total.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empty the shopper's cart, removing every item and any coupon. ALWAYS confirm with the shopper first: this discards everything they chose and cannot be undone. To remove a single line use update_cart_item with qty 0 instead.

tools.name: get_recommended_products
tools.description: Products this store recommends alongside what is already in the cart. Use it to suggest genuinely related items before checkout.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Open checkout so the shopper can review and pay. Use it when they say they are done. You CANNOT place the order or enter payment details, and no tool here can: the shopper completes the purchase themselves. Once this returns, stop - do not navigate again and do not tell them the order was placed.

tools.name: list_angebote
tools.description: Listet alle Privatstunden-Angebote von Ulf Seidl, staatlich gepruefter Skilehrer in Flachau (Snow Space Salzburg), genau wie auf ersteschischule.at. Liefert je Angebot: id, Name (de, en, nl), Dauer, Preis in Euro als Zahl (preis_eur) und als Text, Kurzbeschreibung und ob es ein Aufpreis je weiterer Person ist (aufpreis_je_person). Dazu Waehrung, Hoechstzahl Personen sowie Saison und Treffpunkt laut Seite. Nur lesen.

tools.name: get_angebot
tools.description: Liefert ein einzelnes Angebot von Ulf Seidl anhand der id aus list_angebote (schnupperstunde, halbtag_privat, ganztag_privat oder weitere_person): Name, Dauer, Preis in Euro, Beschreibung, den Aufpreis je weiterer Person, die Hoechstzahl Personen, Saison und Treffpunkt sowie nextSteps zur Anfrage. Gibt bei unbekannter id einen Fehler mit der Liste gueltiger ids zurueck. Nur lesen.

tools.name: get_preise_und_bedingungen
tools.description: Liefert die Preisliste von Ulf Seidl in Euro (Schnupperstunde, Halbtag, Ganztag, Aufpreis je weiterer Person bis 4 Personen) und die Regeln zum Ablauf als woertliche Saetze von ersteschischule.at: Anfrage, Treffpunkt nach Vereinbarung, Familie oder Freunde bis 4 Personen. Gibt ausserdem unter offen_bei_ulf die Themen zurueck, zu denen die Website nichts sagt (z. B. Storno, Zahlung, Liftkarte) - diese bitte direkt bei Ulf erfragen, nicht annehmen.

tools.name: list_faqs
tools.description: Liefert die haeufigen Fragen zu Ulf Seidls Privat-Skiunterricht in Flachau mit Antwort (je Eintrag frage und antwort): Preise, Saison, Treffpunkt, Zielgruppen, mehrere Personen, Sprache, Termine kurzfristig, Ablauf einer Anfrage. Jede Antwort steht so auf ersteschischule.at. Optional mit suchbegriff, dann nur passende Eintraege.

suchbegriff.description: Optional: Wort oder kurze Wortfolge, z. B. Preis, Kinder, Treffpunkt. Leer = alle Fragen.

tools.name: suche_website
tools.description: Durchsucht alles, was ersteschischule.at ueber Ulf Seidls Privat-Skiunterricht sagt - haeufige Fragen, Angebote und Preise, Ablauf, Qualifikationen, Saison und Treffpunkt - nach einem Suchbegriff oder einer Frage in eigenen Worten. Liefert je Treffer bereich, titel, text und das Werkzeug mit den vollstaendigen Daten. Ohne Treffer: leere Liste und die Themen, die bei Ulf direkt zu erfragen sind.

suchbegriff.description: Suchbegriff oder Frage, z. B. "Was kostet ein halber Tag" oder "Kinder".

tools.name: get_treffpunkt_und_anfahrt

Gibt Anfahrt, Parken und uebliche Treffpunkte nur zurueck, wenn Ulf sie angegeben hat; sonst stehen sie unter offen_bei_ulf. Nur lesen.

tools.name: get_saison
tools.description: Liefert die Saison, in der Ulf Seidl in Flachau unterrichtet (Dezember bis April, als Text und als Monatszahlen von_monat/bis_monat), den Satz der Seite "auch waehrend der Saison oft noch Termine frei" und den schnellsten Weg zu Ulf laut Seite (Telefon oder WhatsApp). Genaue Saisondaten kommen nur zurueck, wenn Ulf sie angegeben hat. Dieses Werkzeug liefert keinen Kalender; Termine bitte bei Ulf anfragen.

tools.name: get_kontakt
tools.description: Liefert die Kontaktwege zu Ulf Seidl, Skilehrer in Flachau: Telefon (auch als tel:-Link), WhatsApp-Link, E-Mail-Adresse, Adresse, die Adresse des Anfrageformulars und den Namen des Werkzeugs, das das Formular fuer die Person ausfuellt (privatstunde_anfragen). Dazu der Satz der Seite: am schnellsten telefonisch oder per WhatsApp, auch kurzfristig waehrend der Saison. Nur lesen.

tools.name: list_qualifikationen
tools.description: Liefert Fachkunde und Erfahrung von Ulf Seidl als woertliche Saetze der Seite, je Eintrag id, bezeichnung und nachweis: staatlich gepruefter Skilehrer, seit ueber drei Jahrzehnten auf den Pisten von Flachau, eine der grossen Skischulen des Ortes aufgebaut und gefuehrt, Unterrichtssprachen, Zielgruppen und Koennen. nachweis sagt, ob ein Eintrag nur als Selbstauskunft auf der Website steht oder mit Aussteller, Jahr und Pruef-URL belegt ist. Nur lesen.

tools.name: get_impressum
tools.description: Liefert die Anbieterangaben von ersteschischule.at: Name (Ulf Seidl), Taetigkeit (Skilehrer), Adresse in Flachau, Telefon und E-Mail sowie die Adresse der vollstaendigen Impressum-Seite (deutsch massgeblich). Fuer die rechtlichen Angaben immer die Impressum-Seite selbst lesen; das Werkzeug gibt nur die Kurzfassung zurueck.

tools.name: get_datenschutz
tools.description: Liefert eine Kurzfassung der Datenschutzerklaerung von ersteschischule.at in Punkten: keine Cookies und kein Tracking, Hosting, wer Anfragen aus dem Formular verarbeitet und wo, Speicherdauer der IP-Adresse, Cloudflare Turnstile, keine Auswertung mit KI, Rechte der Betroffenen. Dazu die Adressen der vollstaendigen Erklaerung je Sprache und den Verantwortlichen. Massgeblich ist die vollstaendige Erklaerung. Nur lesen.

tools.name: privatstunde_anfragen
tools.description: Bereitet eine Anfrage fuer eine Privatstunde bei Ulf Seidl in Flachau vor: fuellt das Anfrageformular auf ersteschischule.at aus, damit die Person es pruefen kann. GESENDET wird erst, wenn die Person selbst auf "Anfrage senden" drueckt. Liefert das Ergebnis dieses Absendens zurueck (ok true und gesendet true = Anfrage angekommen, ok false mit error und recovery). Fragen Sie vorher nach dem echten Namen, nach E-Mail-Adresse oder Telefonnummer (mindestens eines), Wunschtermin, Angebot, Personenzahl und Koennen; setzen Sie einwilligung nur auf true, wenn die Person der Datenschutzerklaerung zugestimmt hat, und erfinden Sie keine Angaben. Preise vorher mit list_angebote oder get_preise_und_bedingungen holen. Laut Seite: "ich melde mich persoenlich mit einem Terminvorschlag".

angebot.description: Gewuenschtes Angebot: schnupperstunde (55 min), halbtag_privat (3 h), ganztag_privat (bis 6 h) oder noch_offen.

einwilligung.description: true nur, wenn die Person der Verarbeitung laut Datenschutzerklaerung (https://ersteschischule.at/datenschutz/) zugestimmt hat.

email.description: E-Mail-Adresse fuer die Antwort und die Bestaetigung. E-Mail oder telefon, mindestens eines.

nachricht.description: Optional: Alter der Kinder, Wuensche, Fragen. Nichts erfinden.

name.description: Vor- und Nachname der anfragenden Person.

personen.description: Anzahl der Personen, 1 bis 4 (jede weitere Person mit Aufpreis).

telefon.description: Telefon- oder WhatsApp-Nummer, nur Ziffern, Leerzeichen und + ( ) / -, mindestens 6 Ziffern. E-Mail oder telefon, mindestens eines.

wunschtermin.description: Wunschtermin oder Zeitraum in eigenen Worten, z. B. "14.-16. Februar 2027, vormittags".

tools.name: render_markdown
tools.description: Render markdown into FlatWrite-styled HTML <head> and <body> fragments, with optional typography and page-layout controls. Provide either the raw markdown inline (`markdown`) or an allowlisted URL (`markdownUrl`) pointing to raw markdown content. Use this when you need the rendered HTML artifacts.

markdownUrl.description: URL pointing to raw markdown content. Must be on an allowlisted host (raw.githubusercontent.com, raw.gitlab.com, bitbucket.org), http(s) only, and <=1 MB. Host validation is enforced server-side.

font.description: Font family — must be a bundled family.

oneOf.description: Scale token (e.g. "-1", "0", "1")
Absolute pixel value (8..72)

size.description: Font size as a scale token (e.g. "-1", "0", "1").

oneOf.description: Scale token (e.g. "-1", "0")
Absolute weight (100..900, multiples of 100)

weight.description: Font weight as a scale token (e.g. "-1", "0").

oneOf.description: Scale token (e.g. "-1", "0", "1")
Absolute multiplier (0.8..4.0)

line.description: Line height as a scale token (e.g. "-1", "0", "1").

uiZoom.description: UI zoom level (1.0 = default; >1 zooms in, <1 zooms out).

pageSize.description: Page size for paged output. Only effective when docEngine is pagedjs or vivliostyle.

marginsLR.description: Left/right page margin preset. Only effective when docEngine is pagedjs or vivliostyle.

marginsTB.description: Top/bottom page margin preset. Only effective when docEngine is pagedjs or vivliostyle.

footer.description: Include a page-number footer in paged output.

width.description: Content width in pixels (400..1400). Only effective when docEngine="none".

docEngine.description: Document engine — "none" emits plain CSS; "pagedjs"/"vivliostyle" wrap the output in @page rules.

surfaceMode.description: Surface mode hint. "app" unlocks the appFramework picker; otherwise this is metadata only.

theme.description: Theme identifier rendered as body[data-theme="..."] so consumer CSS can theme via attribute selectors. Free-form (alphanumeric, dash, underscore) — common values are "light" and "dark".

tools.name: list_render_options
tools.description: Return the supported fonts, UI frameworks, document engines, page sizes, orientations, margins, and surface modes for the render_markdown tool. Call this before rendering if you need to know which enum values are valid; call render_markdown when you have the options and are ready to render.

tools.name: get_document_state
tools.description: Return the current state of the active document in the FlatWrite editor: title, word count, render mode, unsaved changes flag, and available export formats. Use this before export or share tools to check readiness; use update_document_content to change the content.

tools.name: create_document
tools.description: Create a new blank document in the FlatWrite editor, optionally with initial markdown content. Use this to start a new document; use open_document to load an existing one from a URL or share link.

markdown.description: Optional initial markdown content for the new document.

title.description: Optional title for the new document.

tools.name: open_document
tools.description: Open an existing document from a URL or share link in the FlatWrite editor. Use this to load a remote markdown file or a previously shared document; use create_document to start blank.

url.description: URL of the markdown file or FlatWrite share link to open.

tools.name: update_document_content
tools.description: Update the markdown content of the active document in the FlatWrite editor. Use this to edit the document programmatically; use get_document_state to inspect the result.

markdown.description: New markdown content for the document.

tools.name: list_recent_documents
tools.description: Return a list of recently opened documents from the editor session. Use this to discover what the user has been working on; use open_document to load one.

tools.name: render_markdown_preview
tools.description: Triggers the editor's built-in preview pane. No HTML is returned — this tool produces a visual side-effect only. Agents that need HTML output must use render_markdown instead.

markdown.description: Optional markdown to preview. If omitted, previews the current editor content.

tools.name: export_document_html
tools.description: Export the active document as a self-contained HTML file. The export opens in a new browser tab for human users. Completes synchronously. Use export_document_pdf for print-ready output.

tools.name: export_document_pdf
tools.description: Export the active document as a PDF by triggering the browser print dialog with the rendered preview. Completes synchronously. The print dialog opens for human users. Use export_document_html for a downloadable HTML file.

tools.name: create_share_link
tools.description: Create a shareable URL for the active document and copy it to the clipboard. Use this to share the document; the link expires after 30 days. Use get_document_state to check canShare before calling.

tools.name: assist_document
tools.description: Rewrite, shorten, fix grammar, or apply a custom instruction to markdown via FlatWrite Assist (Morph: Reflex + Router + Compact + Fast Models). Returns full markdown plus the edited piece. Does not modify the editor — apply with update_document_content if desired. When selectionStart and selectionEnd are provided, only that span is rewritten.

markdown.description: Full markdown document. Optional in the browser WebMCP path (defaults to the active editor). Required for server MCP.

mode.description: Assist mode.

instruction.description: Freeform instruction. Required when mode is "custom".

selectionStart.description: Optional selection start index (inclusive) within markdown.

selectionEnd.description: Optional selection end index (exclusive) within markdown.

selectionText.description: Optional selection text (defaults to markdown.slice(start, end)).

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search this store's catalogue by keyword. Returns name, price, stock and a link for each match. Use this FIRST whenever the shopper names something specific they want. It does not open anything or change the cart: call get_product for detail, add_to_cart to buy.

query.description: What to search for, in the shopper's own words

limit.description: Maximum results to return (default and maximum 20)

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse the store the way a shopper would. Called with no arguments it lists the categories the merchant features in the store navigation; called with a category permalink it lists that category's products, with name, price and a link. Stock is not included here - call get_product before adding anything from a category listing. Use it when the shopper is exploring rather than looking for something specific.

category.description: Category permalink from a previous browse_store call. Omit to list the categories.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get one product's details, OR open it in the browser. Returns description, price, stock, and for a product with variants every option and the values it accepts under "options" - not the combinations themselves; use show_variant for a specific one. Set navigate=true when the shopper wants to SEE the product ("show me", "open", "view", "take me to"). Leave it false, the default, when you need data to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart - the browser then stays where it is. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that.

product.description: The product's id or permalink, as returned by search_catalog or browse_store. A variant id is accepted too and answers about the product it belongs to.

navigate.description: Open the product page. Default false: the shopper stays where they are.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Show one specific variant of a product on the page, chosen by its option values, and report its price and stock. Opens the product page with that variant selected, so the shopper sees what is being discussed. Use it after get_product to resolve a combination.

product.description: The product's id or permalink. A variant id may be given instead, and then options can be left out: it already names one variant.

options.description: The values to show, as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Values come from get_product's "options"; matching ignores case, and a partial selection is fine: the first available variant matching it is shown.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read the shopper's current cart: line items, quantities, discounts, shipping and total. This is the same cart shown on screen, so read it before answering anything about what they are buying rather than relying on what was said earlier in the conversation.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a product to the shopper's cart, which updates on screen immediately. A variant id names what to add on its own; otherwise, for a product with variants, pass the option value ids from get_product's "options" - and if the shopper has not chosen yet, ask them, or call show_variant to show one first. Adding does not start checkout - use proceed_to_checkout when they are ready to pay.

product.description: What to add: a variant id, or a product's id or permalink from search_catalog, browse_store or get_product.

options.description: Variant selection as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Matching ignores case. Omit for products without variants, or when a variant id was given.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description: Change the quantity of a line already in the cart, or remove it by setting the quantity to 0. Use the cart_item_id from get_cart, not the product id.

tools.name: estimate_shipping
tools.description: What the store can ship to a destination and what it costs, for the cart as it stands. Ask for it when the shopper wants to know the delivery cost or time before they check out - it is the question that most often decides whether they finish. Needs a country and a region; a postal code makes the estimate exact where the store charges by it.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code, e.g. PT, CL, US

region.description: Region, state or province, as the store's checkout names it

postal.description: Postal or ZIP code, when known

municipality.description: Municipality, where the store uses one

tools.name: get_human_services
tools.description: Fetch the Human For AI manifest: available human services, operator profile, response times, accepted and rejected task types, and trust & safety policy. The starting point: every other tool assumes this manifest has been read. Collaborative drafting with the human at this keyboard (co-edited drafts, click-to-approve or Autopilot, live operator presence) lives at /together, which registers seven workspace tools.

tools.name: get_service_details
tools.description: Full detail for one service from the catalog by its task_type: description, example request, response format, and turnaround. The detail view for one entry of the get_human_services catalog.

tools.name: submit_human_task
tools.description: Submit a task for the verified human operator to perform in the real world. Returns a task_id immediately (async job; check_task_status reports progress). Free during the pilot. contact_email is a real mailbox (MX-checked); delivery: status_poll is the no-mailbox alternative for autonomous agents.

task_type.description: Service category; custom_human_in_the_loop for anything unlisted.

description.description: What to do, where, and what success looks like.

location_required.description: true if the task needs physical presence.

output_format.description: text_report (default), text_report_with_photos, structured_json, annotated_screenshots, or video.

contact_email.description: Where the deliverable is sent. Required unless delivery is status_poll.

delivery.description: status_poll = no-mailbox path; result arrives via check_task_status.

inputSchema.description: Either contact_email (email delivery) or delivery:"status_poll" (no-mailbox path) is required.

tools.name: check_task_status
tools.description: Look up a submitted task by task_id: status (submitted → accepted → delivered, or rejected), status history, seen_by_operator_at, eta, operator notes, and — once delivered — the signed receipt.

task_id.description: Task ID from submit_human_task, e.g. HFAI-2026-A1B2C3D4E5F60718.

tools.name: message_human_operator
tools.description: Send a free-form message to the human operator — questions, scoping, custom projects. reply_to is required: a real mailbox for the reply. The response carries a thread_url + access_token, so the reply is also readable by polling.

message.description: A question, a scoping request, anything — a real human answers.

tools.name: read_workspace
tools.description: Read everything on this page: the human's goal and notes to you, the current task draft with per-field provenance, approval state, live tracked tasks, and the operator thread. The starting point, and the refresh after each human action. The human sees the same state rendered on the page.

tools.name: draft_task
tools.description: Write or revise the shared task draft, field by field. Unlike the site-wide submit_human_task, nothing is sent anywhere — this edits the on-page document the human co-authors. The human watches it appear live and can edit any field directly (fields show who wrote them last). Partial updates are fine — send only the fields you are changing. Values are validated for real (not just by this schema); invalid values come back in "rejected" with reasons. Revising the draft resets any per-task approval — including one already requested or granted (Autopilot is unaffected).

task_type.description: Service category; custom_human_in_the_loop for anything unlisted.

description.description: What to do, where, and what success looks like.

output_format.description: text_report (default), text_report_with_photos, structured_json, annotated_screenshots, or video.

contact_email.description: Usually leave unset — the human's email from the You lane is used.

tools.name: request_human_approval
tools.description: Show the approval bar to the human at the keyboard, asking them to approve or reject the current draft. Follow with await_human to wait for the decision. Not needed while the human has Autopilot on — read_workspace shows which regime you are in.

message_to_human.description: One line shown in the activity feed, e.g. why this draft is ready.

tools.name: await_human
tools.description: Block until the human at the keyboard acts — approves, rejects, edits the draft, updates the goal, posts a note to you, or grants/revokes Autopilot — or the timeout passes. Returns the event and a fresh workspace snapshot. This is a tool call resolved by an explicit human action on the shared page.

tools.name: submit_approved_task
tools.description: Submit the draft as a real task to the real human operator. Works under either regime the human chose: a per-task approval of the current draft revision, or standing Autopilot authority (see read_workspace). Without either it refuses. On success the task is tracked live on the page for both of you.

inputSchema.description: Deliberately empty: the payload IS the shared on-page draft, exactly as the human saw and authorized it. Inspect it first with read_workspace.

tools.name: track_task_status
tools.description: Workspace-scoped variant of the site-wide check_task_status: same live task records (status history, seen_by_operator_at — the moment a real human saw it, eta, operator notes, signed receipt), but it reads the whole shared board at once and keeps the page's live-status cards in sync for the human. Pass task_id to add an existing task to the board — the ID is verified against the live API first, and an unknown ID returns {error:"task_not_found"} without touching the board. Omit it to read everything tracked.

task_id.description: Optional: a task ID to start tracking, e.g. HFAI-2026-A1B2C3D4E5F60718.

tools.name: message_operator
tools.description: Workspace-scoped variant of the site-wide message_human_operator: no reply_to needed — it uses the reply address the human saved in their lane, keeps one thread per workspace (follow-ups go to the same thread automatically), and renders the conversation on the page for both of you. Use it to scope work or ask questions before committing. The operator replies at human speed.

message.description: The message. Plain language, English.

subject.description: Subject for a new thread; ignored on follow-ups.

tools.name: get_flashcard_format
tools.description: Read this first. Short by default (about 3 KB): the workflow for writing a deck on this site, the rules the site enforces, and the house style. Ask for section "examples" (one card of each kind — choice, truefalse, order, and one with a picture) or "schema" (the deck JSON Schema) when you need them, or "all".

section.description: What to return. Default "guide".

tools.name: find_flashcard_images
tools.description: Licensed pictures for a card, from Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons. Give the exact English Wikipedia article title of the thing when you know it ("Las Meninas", "Hario V60") and a search query otherwise. Returns up to five candidates with a URL sized for the card, the source page, author and license, and a ready-made credit. Put the URL in image (shown while answering — "what is this?" cards) or revealImage (blurred until the answer — "who made X?" cards), describe it in imageAlt without naming the answer, and copy credit into imageCredit. Never invent image URLs.

query.description: What to look for, e.g. "Bayeux Tapestry" or "V60 pour-over dripper".

title.description: Exact English Wikipedia article title, when known — its lead image comes first.

limit.description: At most this many candidates (1–10). Default 5.

tools.name: list_flashcard_decks
tools.description: The decks on this page: the built-in one and the decks saved in this browser (with levels, card counts, and the visitor's best scores), plus any drafts still being written.

tools.name: get_flashcard_deck
tools.description: The full JSON of a deck or draft by slug: every level and card. Use it to review what was written, or as a starting point for a new deck.

tools.name: start_flashcard_deck
tools.description: Begin writing a deck: give its title, headline (phrased as a question, e.g. "Are you a coffee nerd?"), tagline, verdicts for four score bands, and its levels without cards (id, name, tagline; timed and hidden are optional). Returns the draft's slug. Then call add_flashcards for each level and publish_flashcard_deck when every level has its cards.

slug.description: Optional; derived from the title if missing

levels.description: In play order; each level unlocks the next

tools.name: add_flashcards
tools.description: Append cards to one level of a draft started with start_flashcard_deck. Send any number per call (a whole level of ten, or a few at a time). Each card is a choice (options[0] correct), truefalse, or order card with a one-line fact; ids are assigned when omitted. For a card about something you can look at, add picture: { wikipediaTitle, slot, alt } — the site fetches that Wikipedia article's lead image and credits it, no URL needed. Returns the level's counts, which pictures were attached, and what the draft still needs.

fact.description: One-line explanation shown on the reveal, whatever the answer

options.description: The first option is the correct one

image.description: Shown sharp while answering ("which movement is this?")

revealImage.description: Shown blurred while answering, sharpened with the answer

imageAlt.description: What the picture shows, without naming the answer

title.description: The work or subject, e.g. "Las Meninas"

source.description: Page the image came from

picture.description: Name the Wikipedia article of the thing pictured; the site fetches and credits the image. Either this or image/revealImage, not both.

wikipediaTitle.description: Exact English Wikipedia article title of the thing pictured

slot.description: image: shown while answering ("what is this?" cards); revealImage: blurred until the answer (cards the picture would give away). Default revealImage.

alt.description: What the picture shows, without naming the answer

wikipediaTitle.description: Exact English Wikipedia article title of the thing pictured

alt.description: What the picture shows, without naming the answer

fact.description: One-line explanation shown on the reveal, whatever the answer

value.description: Sort key, ascending is correct (a year, a size, a rank…)

tools.description: Validate a draft, save it as a playable deck in this browser, and open the quiz on it (open: false to just save). Errors name what is missing or wrong, by JSON path.

open.description: Open the quiz after saving. Default true.

tools.name: import_flashcards
tools.description: Save a complete deck in one call (the JSON Schema from get_flashcard_format) and open it. If a saved deck already uses the slug, a new slug is chosen unless replace is true. For writing a deck in steps, use start_flashcard_deck instead.

id.description: Unique across the whole deck, e.g. s1, s2

source.description: Page the image came from

id.description: Unique across the whole deck, e.g. s1, s2

fact.description: One-line explanation shown on the reveal, whatever the answer

value.description: Sort key, ascending is correct (a year, a size, a rank…)

replace.description: Overwrite a saved deck with the same slug. Default false.

tools.name: share_flashcard_deck
tools.description: A link anyone can open to play a deck saved in this browser: the deck is stored on the site under a short URL (/d/<id>) that unfurls with its headline and pictures. The site does this on its own while the visitor plays a deck the first time; call it to have the link sooner, or to hand it to the visitor. Needs the deployment to have a blob store — the error says so otherwise.

tools.name: generate_flashcards
tools.description: Ask the site's own AI (Claude, on the server) to plan and write a deck about a topic, then open it: the first level is ready in under a minute and the quiz opens on it; the rest are written in the background. Only works when the deployment has a key — if it doesn't, write the deck yourself with start_flashcard_deck, add_flashcards and publish_flashcard_deck.

topic.description: What the visitor wants to learn, e.g. "The French Revolution" or "Coffee brewing".

notes.description: Optional guidance: angle, difficulty, audience, images to use.

tools.name: play_flashcards
tools.description: Open the quiz for a deck. Omit the slug for the built-in deck; list_flashcard_decks shows the others. The visitor then plays: levels unlock in order by reaching passScore.

tools.name: delete_flashcard_deck
tools.description: Remove a saved deck or a draft from this browser. The built-in deck can't be deleted. Best scores for the deck are kept out of the way but not erased.
