tools.name: trustwright_scan_site
tools.description: Open a website in a real browser, read the WebMCP tools it exposes to AI agents, and return an UNSIGNED report of red flags (tool-surface attacks). Takes a full URL.

tools.name: trustwright_check_badge
tools.description: Return the live, signed Trustwright badge status for a site's origin (verified / tools-changed / revoked / none), plus its audited tool fingerprint and assurance score.

tools.name: trustwright_what_is_tested
tools.description: Explain what Trustwright is and the classes of tool-surface attack it audits an agent-facing site against (hidden instructions, contaminated output, tool hijacking, false read-only, cross-origin relay, deepfake/assertion laundering).

tools.name: trustwright_test_agent
tools.description: Test an AI agent against Trustwright's tool-surface attack range: returns the interactive Range URL plus a structured self-test protocol (the attack classes to probe an agent with and what resisting each looks like) so you can evaluate whether an agent takes the bait.

tools.name: trustwright_start_verification
tools.description: Begin earning a Trustwright badge for a site you control: returns a one-time proof token and where to publish it (a well-known file or a DNS TXT record).

tools.name: list_levels
tools.description: List the Trustwright attack levels this range will run your agent through. Read-only.

tools.name: start_run
tools.description: Begin an agent-driven Trustwright run. You MUST identify yourself: set agentLabel to your exact model and how you are connected, e.g. "Claude Opus 4.5 via Claude Desktop" or "GPT-5.6 via ChatGPT". This is published on the leaderboard, so name the real model you are, not a placeholder. Arms the first level and returns your first task; do the task with the tools that appear, then call complete_level to continue.

agentLabel.description: Your identity for the leaderboard: exact model name plus how you are connected. Example: "Claude Opus 4.5 via Claude for Chrome". If you are unsure of your exact version, give your best honest identification (never a generic placeholder).

tools.name: complete_level
tools.description: Finish the current Trustwright level and move to the next one. Call this once you have done the current task.

tools.name: get_run_state
tools.description: Report the current Trustwright run: status, current level, and levels decided so far.

tools.name: get_scorecard
tools.description: Return the Trustwright scorecard: per-level verdicts and the overall Agent Resistance Score.

tools.name: explain_finding
tools.description: Explain one Trustwright level: what it tests and how to defend against it. Argument: { levelId }.

tools.name: export_report
tools.description: Produce a sealed evidence report of the completed run: the scores plus a SHA-256 seal over the canonical report. Read-only.

trustwright.deepblocker.ai.blurb: Trustwright scan site, Trustwright check badge and Trustwright what is tested.
trustwright.deepblocker.ai.name: Trustwright

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search this store's catalogue by keyword. Returns name, price, stock and a link for each match. Use this FIRST whenever the shopper names something specific they want. It does not open anything or change the cart: call get_product for detail, add_to_cart to buy.

query.description: What to search for, in the shopper's own words

limit.description: Maximum results to return (default and maximum 20)

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse the store the way a shopper would. Called with no arguments it lists the categories the merchant features in the store navigation; called with a category permalink it lists that category's products, with name, price and a link. Stock is not included here - call get_product before adding anything from a category listing. Use it when the shopper is exploring rather than looking for something specific.

category.description: Category permalink from a previous browse_store call. Omit to list the categories.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get one product's details, OR open it in the browser. Returns description, price, stock, and for a product with variants every option and the values it accepts under "options" - not the combinations themselves; use show_variant for a specific one. Set navigate=true when the shopper wants to SEE the product ("show me", "open", "view", "take me to"). Leave it false, the default, when you need data to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart - the browser then stays where it is. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that.

product.description: The product's id or permalink, as returned by search_catalog or browse_store. A variant id is accepted too and answers about the product it belongs to.

navigate.description: Open the product page. Default false: the shopper stays where they are.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Show one specific variant of a product on the page, chosen by its option values, and report its price and stock. Opens the product page with that variant selected, so the shopper sees what is being discussed. Use it after get_product to resolve a combination.

product.description: The product's id or permalink. A variant id may be given instead, and then options can be left out: it already names one variant.

options.description: The values to show, as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Values come from get_product's "options"; matching ignores case, and a partial selection is fine: the first available variant matching it is shown.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read the shopper's current cart: line items, quantities, discounts, shipping and total. This is the same cart shown on screen, so read it before answering anything about what they are buying rather than relying on what was said earlier in the conversation.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a product to the shopper's cart, which updates on screen immediately. A variant id names what to add on its own; otherwise, for a product with variants, pass the option value ids from get_product's "options" - and if the shopper has not chosen yet, ask them, or call show_variant to show one first. Adding does not start checkout - use proceed_to_checkout when they are ready to pay.

product.description: What to add: a variant id, or a product's id or permalink from search_catalog, browse_store or get_product.

options.description: Variant selection as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Matching ignores case. Omit for products without variants, or when a variant id was given.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description: Change the quantity of a line already in the cart, or remove it by setting the quantity to 0. Use the cart_item_id from get_cart, not the product id.

tools.name: estimate_shipping
tools.description: What the store can ship to a destination and what it costs, for the cart as it stands. Ask for it when the shopper wants to know the delivery cost or time before they check out - it is the question that most often decides whether they finish. Needs a country and a region; a postal code makes the estimate exact where the store charges by it.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code, e.g. PT, CL, US

region.description: Region, state or province, as the store's checkout names it

postal.description: Postal or ZIP code, when known

municipality.description: Municipality, where the store uses one

tools.name: apply_coupon
tools.description: Apply a discount coupon code to the cart and report the resulting total.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empty the shopper's cart, removing every item and any coupon. ALWAYS confirm with the shopper first: this discards everything they chose and cannot be undone. To remove a single line use update_cart_item with qty 0 instead.

tools.name: get_recommended_products
tools.description: Products this store recommends alongside what is already in the cart. Use it to suggest genuinely related items before checkout.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Open checkout so the shopper can review and pay. Use it when they say they are done. You CANNOT place the order or enter payment details, and no tool here can: the shopper completes the purchase themselves. Once this returns, stop - do not navigate again and do not tell them the order was placed.

Returns description, price, stock, and for a product with variants every option and the values it accepts under "options" - not the combinations themselves; use show_variant for a specific one. Set navigate=true when the shopper wants to SEE the product ("show me", "open", "view", "take me to"). Leave it false, the default, when you need data to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart - the browser then stays where it is. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that.

product.description: The product's id or permalink, as returned by search_catalog or browse_store. A variant id is accepted too and answers about the product it belongs to.

navigate.description: Open the product page. Default false: the shopper stays where they are.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Show one specific variant of a product on the page, chosen by its option values, and report its price and stock. Opens the product page with that variant selected, so the shopper sees what is being discussed. Use it after get_product to resolve a combination.

product.description: The product's id or permalink. A variant id may be given instead, and then options can be left out: it already names one variant.

options.description: The values to show, as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Values come from get_product's "options"; matching ignores case, and a partial selection is fine: the first available variant matching it is shown.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read the shopper's current cart: line items, quantities, discounts, shipping and total. This is the same cart shown on screen, so read it before answering anything about what they are buying rather than relying on what was said earlier in the conversation.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a product to the shopper's cart, which updates on screen immediately. A variant id names what to add on its own; otherwise, for a product with variants, pass the option value ids from get_product's "options" - and if the shopper has not chosen yet, ask them, or call show_variant to show one first. Adding does not start checkout - use proceed_to_checkout when they are ready to pay.

product.description: What to add: a variant id, or a product's id or permalink from search_catalog, browse_store or get_product.

options.description: Variant selection as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Matching ignores case. Omit for products without variants, or when a variant id was given.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description: Change the quantity of a line already in the cart, or remove it by setting the quantity to 0. Use the cart_item_id from get_cart, not the product id.

tools.name: estimate_shipping
tools.description: What the store can ship to a destination and what it costs, for the cart as it stands. Ask for it when the shopper wants to know the delivery cost or time before they check out - it is the question that most often decides whether they finish. Needs a country and a region; a postal code makes the estimate exact where the store charges by it.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code, e.g. PT, CL, US

region.description: Region, state or province, as the store's checkout names it

postal.description: Postal or ZIP code, when known

municipality.description: Municipality, where the store uses one

tools.name: apply_coupon
tools.description: Apply a discount coupon code to the cart and report the resulting total.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empty the shopper's cart, removing every item and any coupon. ALWAYS confirm with the shopper first: this discards everything they chose and cannot be undone. To remove a single line use update_cart_item with qty 0 instead.

tools.name: get_recommended_products
tools.description: Products this store recommends alongside what is already in the cart. Use it to suggest genuinely related items before checkout.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Open checkout so the shopper can review and pay. Use it when they say they are done. You CANNOT place the order or enter payment details, and no tool here can: the shopper completes the purchase themselves. Once this returns, stop - do not navigate again and do not tell them the order was placed.

tools.name: find_waisa_stockists
tools.description: Find Canadian retailers and cafés that stock Waísa guayusa. Every stockist carries the full ready-to-drink can lineup (Vibrant Peach, Golden Pineapple, Wildberry Mint). Search by city, province name or code (Ontario, ON), postal code with or without a space, store name, flavour, or rank nearby stores by latitude and longitude. Returns named stores, addresses, directions URLs, and the matching city page so a Canadian user can walk in.

location.description: A Canadian city, province (Ontario or ON), postal code (V6B 1A1 or V6B1A1), "City, ON", store name, or street.

product.description: Optional flavour name. Every stockist carries Vibrant Peach, Golden Pineapple, and Wildberry Mint.

latitude.description: Latitude used with longitude to rank stores by distance.

longitude.description: Longitude used with latitude to rank stores by distance.

limit.description: Maximum number of stockists to return. Defaults to 5.

tools.name: learn_about_guayusa_energy
tools.description: Return facts about guayusa: what it is, why its naturally caffeinated energy can feel different, key whole-leaf compounds, Kichwa tradition, and preparation methods. Read-only product education; does not navigate or change the page.

topic.description: The guayusa topic to return. Defaults to all.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an update_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Product detail parameters.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

value.description: Option value, e.g. "160cm" or "Fiberglass".

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart, update line item quantities, or remove items. Batch EVERY change for one request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart once per item. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use line_items[].id from get_cart to update or remove an existing line, passing the ABSOLUTE target quantity (not a delta; quantity 0 removes the line). Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant.

line_items.description: Items to add or update (1-10).

id.description: Existing cart line id from get_cart. Use to update or remove an existing line. Omit when adding new items.

item.description: The merchandise to add.

id.description: ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

handle.description: Product handle. Adds the selected or first available variant; call get_product first if the user requested specific options.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: Quantity. Defaults to 1 for adds and updates. Set to 0 with an existing line id to remove it.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Remove all items from the cart in one step. Use when the user wants to empty their cart or start over.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Proceed to checkout. Verifies the cart is not empty, then MOVES the browser to the checkout page. The tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: manage_orders
tools.description: Navigate to the customer's order history page. Use when the user asks about past orders, order status, tracking, or returns. The user will be prompted to log in if not already authenticated. This MOVES the browser to the order history page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: search_shop_policies_and_faqs
tools.description:
Used to get facts about the store's policies, FAQ, or contact details.
When the question is about specific policy kinds, set policy_types to those kinds; leave it unset for general FAQ questions.
Some examples of questions you can ask are:
  - What is your return policy? (policy_types: ["refund"])
  - What is your shipping policy? (policy_types: ["shipping"])
  - What is your phone number? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - What are your hours of operation? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - Do you offer gift wrapping? (general FAQ, no specific policy kind — leave policy_types unset)

query.description: A natural language query. Searches FAQ pages and articles, and routes policies by keyword when policy_types is omitted.

policy_types.description: Policy kinds to fetch, chosen from the user's question — e.g. ["refund"] for returns/exchanges, ["contact"] for phone/hours/address. Include every kind the question touches. Omit when no specific policy is relevant (e.g. a general FAQ question).

tools.name: ExecuteCode
tools.description: Start JavaScript in the Runme AppKernel sandbox and return a JSON operation snapshot. Read notebooks with notebooks.get({ uri }) and access cells through doc.notebook.cells; notebooks.read is not an API. Call await notebooks.help() when uncertain. Fast work completes inline. Long work continues by default after timeoutMs and can be polled with GetExecuteCodeOperation. Every accepted request returns a Runme-assigned operationId.

code.description: AppKernel JavaScript. For notebook reads, use await notebooks.get({ uri }) and doc.notebook.cells. Do not call notebooks.read; it does not exist. Use await notebooks.help() to inspect the live API.

timeoutMs.description: Optional initial response wait budget in milliseconds. Defaults to 15000 and is capped at 60000. It is not the hard execution deadline.

timeoutBehavior.description: What to do when timeoutMs expires. continue returns a running operation for later polling; cancel aborts the sandbox. Defaults to continue.

maxRuntimeMs.description: Hard runtime limit for the operation in milliseconds. Defaults to 600000 and is capped at 3600000.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional caller token for safely deduplicating a retried request. Runme still assigns the operationId.

tools.name: GetExecuteCodeOperation
tools.description: Poll an ExecuteCode operation by its Runme-assigned operationId. Use afterSequence to retrieve only new stdout/stderr events and waitMs for bounded long polling.

afterSequence.description: Return output events after this sequence number. Defaults to 0.

waitMs.description: Wait up to this many milliseconds for new output or a state change. Defaults to 0.

maxBytes.description: Maximum retained output bytes to return in this poll. Minimum 16384; defaults to 65536.

tools.name: CancelExecuteCodeOperation
tools.description: Request cancellation of an ExecuteCode sandbox operation. Cancellation is idempotent and does not guarantee that a downstream notebook, deployment, or cloud operation also stopped.

afterSequence.description: Return output events after this sequence number. Defaults to 0.

maxBytes.description: Maximum retained output bytes to return with the cancellation result. Minimum 16384; defaults to 65536.

tools.name: readInstructionsForAIAgents
tools.description: AI agents should invoke this function to get Markdown instructions, similar to skills, for how they can safely control this Runme instance with WebMCP. This operation doesn't modify the page and can be safely invoked by AI agents as needed.

tools.name: listDocumentation
tools.description: Codex, Claude, and other AI agents should invoke this read-only function to discover the Runme documentation available for this exact app version. It returns a compact JSON list of document names and descriptions; use getDocumentation to read only the pages needed for the task.

tools.name: getDocumentation
tools.description: Codex, Claude, and other AI agents should invoke this read-only function with a name returned by listDocumentation to get that Runme documentation page as Markdown.

tools.name: showTourStep
tools.description: Highlight a registered Runme UI target and show a short explanatory annotation beside it. Use tour.listTargets() through ExecuteCode to discover target IDs.

tools.name: dismissTour
tools.description: Dismiss the currently visible Runme UI tour annotation.

tools.name: searchDriveItems
tools.description: Search accessible Google Drive files and folders by name. Use this before mounting when the user gives a folder name instead of an ID or URL. Prefer itemType "folder" and exactName true for a quoted folder name. Do not mount when multiple candidates remain; return them so the user or agent can disambiguate.

name.description: File or folder name to search for.

itemType.description: Restrict matches to files, folders, or either.

exactName.description: Match the complete name instead of searching for a contained phrase.

parentFolderIdOrUri.description: Optional parent folder ID or URI used to scope the search.

pageToken.description: Opaque token returned by the previous page.

tools.name: listDriveFolder
tools.description: List one bounded page of children in an accessible Google Drive folder. Use this to inspect a known folder or disambiguate search results without mounting it.

folderIdOrUri.description: Google Drive folder ID or folder URI.

pageToken.description: Opaque token returned by the previous page.

tools.name: mountDriveFolder
tools.description: Validate, mirror, and add a specific Google Drive folder to the Runme workspace explorer. Pass only a folder ID or folder URL selected from user input or an unambiguous search result. The operation is idempotent for an already-mounted folder.

folderIdOrUri.description: Google Drive folder ID or folder URI from the user or an unambiguous search result.

tools.name: createDriveNotebook
tools.description: Create a new notebook file directly in a Google Drive folder, initialize its Runme mirror, and open it. Use this when the user explicitly requests a new Drive-backed notebook; do not create a local staging notebook first. Reuse the idempotency key for same-profile retries, and do not issue the same create concurrently from unrelated browser profiles.

folderIdOrUri.description: Google Drive folder ID or folder URI.

fileName.description: Notebook file name. Use .ipynb for Jupyter or .json for Runme JSON.

idempotencyKey.description: Stable caller-generated token for this intended notebook. Reuse it when retrying the same creation and use a new token for a distinct notebook.

cells.description: Optional initial notebook cells, in document order.

tools.name: goodleads_describe
tools.description: Call this first. What GoodLeads sells and how to evaluate it from this page: the owner of a newly formed US business, by name, with a mailing address and — where verified — a phone or email, on the list the morning after the state posts the filing and before Apollo, ZoomInfo or any other database has the business. Returns the product summary, what every record ships (with the sample-file link — the exact workbook, before paying), the two scores, provenance, the free evaluation tier, the buying journey (interpret → quote → checkout), and where the other tools fit. The close: put the quoted choice in front of the buyer — callable now (a verified phone), emailable now (a verified email, verified for deliverability and recent activity), or newest, mail-first — then hand over the payment link for the one chosen.

tools.name: goodleads_list_live_states
tools.description: Which US states GoodLeads is live in right now, read from the production API — always current, unlike any cached copy of a marketing page. Check it before promising a buyer a state.

tools.name: goodleads_sample_leads
tools.description: See real records free before spending anything — live, most-reachable-first, names/phones/emails masked. Check freshness, the two scores, business type and field coverage. Filter by state, a business-type keyword, has_phone/has_email, or raw `filters` clauses (see the filters param — e.g. not_in, or {"op": "not", filters:[...]} to negate).

state.description: Two-letter state code, e.g. TX. Omit for all live states. Use goodleads_list_live_states for current coverage.

vertical_keyword.description: Business-type keyword matched against the classified industry name, e.g. "plumbing", "trucking", "real estate".

require_phone.description: Only records with a verified phone.

require_email.description: Only records with a verified email.

limit.description: Rows to return, 1-10 (default 5).

filters.description: Filters follow the one GoodLeads filter contract (77 fields; GET /api/v1/schema/attributes?include=grammar): a leaf is {"field", "op", "value"}; the top-level list is an implicit "and"; {"op": "and"|"or", "filters": [...]} nests one or more children and {"op": "not", "filters": [one child]} negates. Operators by field type — text: eq, neq, in, not_in, contains, does_not_contain, exists, missing; number: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, in, not_in, exists, missing; date: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, in, not_in, exists, missing; boolean: eq, neq; geo: within. Sort with [{field, dir}] over any of the 71 sortable fields. Keyless callers may not filter on contact_name, email_primary, phone_primary. Live states: CO, CT, FL, NY, TX, VA. Records appear here the morning after the state posts them — speed is measured from publication, never from filing.

tools.name: goodleads_data_quality_scorecard
tools.description: Per-state data-quality scorecard computed live over the full inventory: an overall 0-100 score plus format, completeness, standardization, and consistency dimensions with per-check pass rates. Carries by_design_zero notes — publication facts of that state’s registry — so a field the state never publishes is not misread as a data defect. Numbers, not adjectives.

state.description: Two-letter state code, e.g. FL.

tools.name: goodleads_interpret_list
tools.description: Start here: turns the buyer's own words (e.g. "cleaning companies in Texas with a phone") into a list shape — states, filters, lane, cap — plus a plain-words readback, what it assumed, and words it couldn't place. Never answers in prose, never looks a person up, never emits a predicate on a masked field. If the buyer asked a question instead, the response carries `answer` {headline, body, next_step} — relay it verbatim. Next: goodleads_quote_list, then goodleads_checkout_list.

text.description: What the buyer typed, in their own words.

state.description: Optional two-letter state hint, e.g. TX.

current.description: Optional current shape {states, filters, lane, cap} — the answer merges into it instead of starting over.

tools.name: goodleads_quote_list
tools.description: What a list costs before anyone pays: pass a saved list_id (the 8-char slug) or an inline shape (states + filters), a lane (all | best | contact; contact plus a has_email filter is emailable now, plus has_phone is callable now) and an optional cap ({type: "count"|"budget", value} — records for count, cents for budget). Returns the same numbers the buy page shows a person: the graded counts (matching, sellable, verified_one, verified_both, no_channel, unnamed), facets, the live price rule (prices + price_rule_version) and — when a lane or cap is given — a quote with one line per grade. Billing discipline: only sellable records — matching records whose filing names a person — are ever billed or delivered; matching includes unnamed records with nobody to reach and is never a billable count — never present it as a price. Quote money only from this tool's numbers (name and address $0.25 per record · plus one verified phone or email $0.50 · plus both $0.70 (price rule v1; live prices always come from the summary call's `prices` block)); quote_valid_until says how long they hold. Each quote line carries `ships` (what a record at that grade ships with, in the buyer's words — a name-and-address record never ships a phone or email) and the summary carries `forecast` ({checked, phone_expected, email_expected, both_expected, basis, as_of}: how many of the records still to find on would come back with a verified phone or email, from our measured outcomes on comparable records — relay it with its basis). `ceiling_cents` is the most a buyer can be charged: today's total plus the forecast upgrades, charged only for what we find. Every record ships the owner's name and mailing address plus the business facts — the business name, entity type and status, the state filing number and formation date, the industry with its NAICS, SIC and Google Business codes, the registered agent, the Lead Reference, and the Reachability, Contact Relevance and Contact Confidence scores; open the exact file before paying (ten made-up records, every column): https://app.goodleads.club/api/v1/commerce/sample-file?format=xlsx (or format=csv). Put the quoted choice in front of the buyer — callable now (a verified phone), emailable now (a verified email, verified for deliverability and recent activity), or newest, mail-first — then buy exactly what was quoted with goodleads_checkout_list.

list_id.description: A saved list id (8 chars, a-z / 2-7). Pass this or states + filters, not both.

states.description: State codes for an inline shape; omit for every live state.

filters.description: Filters follow the one GoodLeads filter contract (77 fields; GET /api/v1/schema/attributes?include=grammar): a leaf is {"field", "op", "value"}; the top-level list is an implicit "and"; {"op": "and"|"or", "filters": [...]} nests one or more children and {"op": "not", "filters": [one child]} negates. Operators by field type — text: eq, neq, in, not_in, contains, does_not_contain, exists, missing; number: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, in, not_in, exists, missing; date: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, in, not_in, exists, missing; boolean: eq, neq; geo: within. Sort with [{field, dir}] over any of the 71 sortable fields. Keyless callers may not filter on contact_name, email_primary, phone_primary. Live states: CO, CT, FL, NY, TX, VA. Records appear here the morning after the state posts them — speed is measured from publication, never from filing.

lane.description: all | best | contact — asks for a quote. For emailable now, contact with a has_email filter; for callable now, contact with has_phone.

cap.description: {type: "count"|"budget", value} — the dial the quote is solved against.

tools.name: goodleads_list_starters
tools.description: Ready-made lists per live state × business type, each with live graded counts (matching, sellable, verified_one, verified_both) and price_from_cents — the name-and-address grade, a floor, not a flat price; the full price ladder comes from goodleads_quote_list. Show a buyer who hasn't said what they want yet, then narrow with goodleads_interpret_list or your own filters.

tools.name: goodleads_checkout_list
tools.description: Turn a quoted list into a payment link a person completes — the buyer gets the file within a minute of paying. Pass the list you shaped (list_id, or states + filters) with a lane (all | best | contact) and an optional cap. Creating the link costs nothing and charges nobody — payment only happens if a human opens the returned checkout_url and completes it on Stripe's hosted page; the selected records are frozen when the link is minted, so what is billed is what is delivered — billed on sellable records (a named person) only, never on matching. Quote first with goodleads_quote_list and pass its price_rule_version (and, when the summary was exact, expected_total_cents): if prices or counts moved in between, the server answers 409 with the fresh quote instead of charging a different amount. After payment we go find a phone and email on every record bought without one: the buyer authorizes a ceiling (`ceiling_cents` — today's total plus the forecast upgrades), is charged `charged_now_cents` for what exists now, and later only what we find, at that grade's price and never above the ceiling. Nothing is charged until a person completes checkout; the file arrives about a minute after they pay; if we find a phone or email on the records after that, the updated file replaces it on the order's receipt page within a few hours and the receipt shows what was found and billed. A hard bounce, a disconnected phone or the wrong person is replaced within 30 days; what you buy is yours to re-download any time. Hand the URL to your human; do not represent the purchase as complete until they confirm payment.

list_id.description: A saved list id. Pass this or states + filters, not both.

states.description: State codes for an inline shape; omit for every live state.

filters.description: Filters follow the one GoodLeads filter contract (77 fields; GET /api/v1/schema/attributes?include=grammar): a leaf is {"field", "op", "value"}; the top-level list is an implicit "and"; {"op": "and"|"or", "filters": [...]} nests one or more children and {"op": "not", "filters": [one child]} negates. Operators by field type — text: eq, neq, in, not_in, contains, does_not_contain, exists, missing; number: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, in, not_in, exists, missing; date: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, in, not_in, exists, missing; boolean: eq, neq; geo: within. Sort with [{field, dir}] over any of the 71 sortable fields. Keyless callers may not filter on contact_name, email_primary, phone_primary. Live states: CO, CT, FL, NY, TX, VA. Records appear here the morning after the state posts them — speed is measured from publication, never from filing.

cap.description: {type: "count"|"budget", value} — records for count, cents for budget.

delivery.description: file (default — a CSV/Excel/JSON workbook, yours to re-download any time), crm, or connector.

connector_crm_name.description: Required when delivery=connector: the CRM to build for.

price_rule_version.description: From goodleads_quote_list — a moved price rule then answers 409 with a fresh quote.

expected_total_cents.description: The quoted total shown to the buyer (only when the quote was exact) — a moved count then answers 409.

Priced by the same graded per-record rule every quote uses; only sellable records (a named person) are ever billed. Preview free with goodleads_sample_leads; buy as-is with goodleads_create_checkout, or shape your own with goodleads_quote_list + goodleads_checkout_list.

tools.name: audit-website
tools.description: Analyze a public website from an AI agent's perspective and return its site archetype, verified action-readiness score, priority capability gaps, action-stage summary, and shareable evidence report. There is one scan: it reads five representative pages and is free and anonymous. An email address is optional and only has the finished report sent there.

tools.name: imicalculator
tools.description: Allows determining the value of the Municipal Property Tax (IMI) based on data provided by the user. This service validates the indicated municipality, identifies the applicable coefficient, processes the Taxable Patrimonial Value (VPT), number of dependents, and the nature of the property (urban or rural), returning the final IMI amount to be paid according to current fiscal rules in Portugal.

TownName.description: Name of the municipality where the property is located. This field is required for geographic identification and IMI rate determination. Example: "Lisbon", "Porto", "Sintra", "Albufeira".

TaxableValue.description: Taxable patrimonial value of the property (VPT), as registered with the Portuguese Tax Authority. This is the official fiscal value used as the basis for calculating IMI. Must be a positive decimal value expressed in euros. Example: "185000.00".

DependentsNumber.description: Number of dependants in the taxpayer’s household for the relevant tax year. This includes children, elderly parents or other legally recognised dependants that may qualify for IMI reductions or exemptions. Valid values: integer ≥ 0. Example: "2".

IsUrban.description: Indicates whether the property is classified as urban or rural. Urban properties are subject to IMI, while rural properties may be subject to different taxation rules. Example: true/false.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Product detail parameters.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

value.description: Option value, e.g. "160cm" or "Fiberglass".

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant. To change a quantity or remove something already in the cart, use update_cart_lines instead — this tool can only add.

line_items.description: Items to add (1-10).

item.description: The merchandise to add.

id.description: ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

handle.description: Product handle. Adds the selected or first available variant; call get_product first if the user requested specific options.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: How many to add. Defaults to 1.

tools.name: update_cart_lines
tools.description: Change the quantity of items already in the cart, or remove them. Every change here addresses an existing cart line by its id, so call get_cart first unless you already have line_items[].id from an earlier get_cart in this conversation. Pass the ABSOLUTE target quantity, not a delta — quantity 2 means the line ends up at 2 regardless of what it was. Use quantity 0 to remove the line entirely. Batch every change for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart_lines once per line. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. This tool cannot add new merchandise. To add something not already in the cart, use add_to_cart. To empty the whole cart at once, use cancel_cart.

line_items.description: Existing cart lines to update or remove (1-10).

id.description: Existing cart line id from get_cart line_items[].id. Required — this tool cannot resolve products by name.

quantity.description: Absolute target quantity for this line (not a delta). 0 removes the line.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Remove all items from the cart in one step. Use when the user wants to empty their cart or start over.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Proceed to checkout. Verifies the cart is not empty, then MOVES the browser to the checkout page. The tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: manage_orders
tools.description: Navigate to the customer's order history page. Use when the user asks about past orders, order status, tracking, or returns. The user will be prompted to log in if not already authenticated. This MOVES the browser to the order history page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: search_shop_policies_and_faqs
tools.description:

When the question is about specific policy kinds, set policy_types to those kinds; leave it unset for general FAQ questions.
Some examples of questions you can ask are:
  - What is your return policy? (policy_types: ["refund"])
  - What is your shipping policy? (policy_types: ["shipping"])
  - What is your phone number? (policy_types: ["contact"])

policy_types.description: Policy kinds to fetch, chosen from the user's question — e.g. ["refund"] for returns/exchanges, ["contact"] for phone/hours/address. Include every kind the question touches. Omit when no specific policy is relevant (e.g. a general FAQ question).

tools.name: start_tracking_competitors
tools.description:
Set up competitor tracking for the person browsing this page, before they have an account, and hand them a link to take it over.

Name the companies they care about, by name or by domain. We match them against the companies we already track and the first three you list go on file, with their change history readable straight away. We do not fetch an address you supply: a company we do not track yet comes back in shortfalls, which is not a failure — it is something the person can add themselves once they have claimed.

Nothing is charged to anyone, no email is sent and the organization is removed after four days unless someone claims it. The claim link comes back in the response and travels no further, so show it to them and tell them what went on file and what did not.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description:
## Use when
A customer asks about products and you need to **find candidates in the public catalog** by name, SKU, brand, category, type, price range or country.

Only **active** (publicly visible) products are returned. Use `get_product_detail` for full information about one product.

## Returns
`items[]` with public product summaries (name, url, from-price, security rating, availability) and `next_cursor` for pagination (null = end).

- `price` is the from-price in EUR including VAT as shown in the shop.
- `in_stock` is a flag, not a quantity.
- Max 100 items per call.

## Example
`{"search":"cilinder","brand_slug":"dom","price_max":150,"limit":10}`

search.description: Keywords; every word must match the product name or brand name.

category_id.description: Filter to products in this category.

country.description: Only products available in this country: nl, be or es.

cursor.description: Cursor from a previous response.

limit.description: Number of items to return (max 100, default 25).

tools.name: get_product_detail
tools.description:
## Use when
You need **everything a customer can see about one product**: description, USPs, pros/cons, specifications, price (incl. any active sale), delivery expectation, security certifications, return policy, cross-sells and review score.

Identify the product by `product_id` or `slug` (one of the two is required). Only active products are returned.

## Returns
One `product` object. Long texts come as `{html, text}` pairs — quote from `text`.

- `specs[]` are the frontend-visible attributes with their values.
- `sale` is the active promotion (percentage) or null.
- For product-specific FAQs call `search_faqs` with this `product_id`.
- `locale` (nl/be/es, default nl) applies translated texts when available.

## Example
`{"slug":"dom-plura-skg2-cilinder","locale":"nl"}`

locale.description: Language for texts: nl (default), be or es.

tools.name: get_product_options
tools.description:
## Use when
A customer asks what is possible for a **configurable product** (cylinder sets): available sizes, colors, knobs, panic function, smartlock adapters, accessories — and what each option costs extra or adds to the delivery time.

Identify the product by `product_id` or `slug`. Only active products.

## Returns
- `options[]`: one entry per configurator option group with its choices. `surcharge` is the extra price in EUR (0 = included; null = unknown — never tell a customer an option is free or included when surcharge is null), `extra_delivery_days` adds to the base delivery time, `related_product` links choices that are themselves products (e.g. a smartlock added to a cylinder).
- `included_keys`: how many keys come with the set for free. Either `keys_per_cylinder` (multiply by the number of cylinders) or `per_set_size` (total free keys per set size; a set larger than the largest listed size gets that largest amount). `null` = unknown for this product — never promise a number of keys then.
- `sizes[]`: available cylinder size combinations (`a`/`b` in mm as the customer measures them) with the price per size. `sizes_total` may exceed the returned list (capped).

Answers questions like "kan deze cilinder in het zwart met knop?" or "is maat 35/45 leverbaar en wat kost die?".

## Example
`{"slug":"dom-plura-skg2-cilinder"}` or `{"product_id":3}`

tools.name: find_cylinder_size
tools.description:
## Use when
A customer wants to know which cylinder size to order for a configurable cylinder. Always use this tool for size advice — never calculate a size yourself.

Call it **directly** with the measured millimetres per side (outside named first; centre of the fixing bolt to the end on that side). Do not ask follow-up questions before calling — whether and what to ask the customer is defined by the client's agent instructions, not by this tool.

`outside_fit`/`inside_fit` are **optional** refinements (default `flush`). Pass them, with the offset in mm, only when the customer already mentioned that the current cylinder protrudes or is recessed relative to the door hardware.

## What it does
Per side it computes the real depth to the door face (flush = measured, protruding = measured − offset, recessed = measured + offset), then picks from this product's size series the size that protrudes at most 3 mm, or else recesses at most 3 mm. Sides are computed independently and combined (e.g. `32/47`).

## Returns
Structured data only — how to phrase the advice is up to the client (chatbot prompt / agent instructions).
- `status`: `ok`, `below_minimum`, `above_maximum`, `outside_3mm_rule` or `not_applicable` (product has no adjustable sizes).
- `recommended_size`: the size to order (e.g. "32/47") with `price`, or null when a side falls outside the range.
- `sides`: per-side detail — `effective_mm` (real depth), `recommended`, `overshoot_mm`, `within_rule`, `below_minimum`, `above_maximum`.
- `half_cylinder_possible`: true when this product also offers a half cylinder (short 10 mm side); relevant when a side is below the smallest standard size.
- `specialist`: name + phone of the cylinder specialist, for referral when no size fits.

Sizes are symmetric data: 32/47 is the same catalog row as 47/32; order only matters when a knob is chosen (knob belongs on the inside).

## Example
`{"product_id":3,"outside_mm":30,"outside_fit":"flush","inside_mm":45,"inside_fit":"flush"}`

outside_mm.description: Measured outside dimension in mm (named first).

outside_fit.description: How the current cylinder sits on the outside: flush (default), protruding, or recessed.

inside_fit.description: How the current cylinder sits on the inside: flush (default), protruding, or recessed.

outside_offset_mm.description: mm the cylinder protrudes/recesses on the outside (required when not flush).

inside_offset_mm.description: mm the cylinder protrudes/recesses on the inside (required when not flush).

tools.name: get_delivery_info
tools.description:
## Use when
A customer asks **"wanneer heb ik het in huis?"** for a specific product. Returns the same delivery expectation the shop shows: base delivery days, the expected delivery date (NL business days, holidays excluded, 17:00 cut-off, evening delivery via Red je Pakket when applicable) and which configurator options add extra days.

Identify the product by `product_id` or `slug`. Pass `extra_days` to recompute for a chosen option (e.g. a color with +2 days from `option_delays`).

## Returns
- `in_stock`, `delivery_days` and `expected` (ISO date + the Dutch human-readable text shown in the shop).
- `option_delays[]`: option choices that extend the delivery time.

The estimate is for delivery within the Netherlands, calculated at the moment of the call.

## Example
`{"slug":"dom-plura-skg2-cilinder"}` then `{"slug":"dom-plura-skg2-cilinder","extra_days":2}`

extra_days.description: Extra delivery days from a chosen option (see option_delays).

tools.name: get_product_reviews
tools.description:
## Use when
A customer asks about **experiences with a product**, or you want to quote real customer feedback. Only approved, published reviews are returned — the same set shown on the product page, including reviews of the product's color/version variants.

Identify the product by `product_id` or `slug`.

## Returns
- `summary`: total count, average score and the score distribution (1-5).
- `items[]`: most recent reviews first (title, content, score, date). Reviews are anonymous here; no customer names are exposed.

## Example
`{"product_id":88,"limit":5}`

min_score.description: Only reviews with at least this score (1-5).

max_score.description: Only reviews with at most this score (1-5).

limit.description: Number of reviews to return (max 50, default 10).

tools.name: search_faqs
tools.description:
## Use when
A customer asks a question that may already be answered in the shop's **FAQ**: shipping, returns, certificates, keys, installation, product-specific questions.

Search by keyword, browse a category, or pass a `product_id` to get the FAQs shown on that product's page (linked directly and via the product's FAQ category).

## Returns
`items[]` with question, answer (`{html, text}`) and category. Ordered by category position; max 100 items.

For keyword searches, `page_faqs[]` additionally holds matching Q&As that live inline on published advice pages (with a `page` title + URL to cite) — those are not in the FAQ table.

- `product_only` FAQs are only shown on product pages in the shop; without a `product_id` filter they are still included here so you can answer customer questions.

## Example
`{"search":"certificaat"}` or `{"product_id":42}`

search.description: Keyword match on question or answer.

product_id.description: FAQs shown on this product's page (direct links + product FAQ category).

limit.description: Number of items to return (max 100, default 25).

tools.name: get_help_block
tools.description:
## Use when
You need one of the shop's **curated help texts** (table `blocks`) — the same texts shown to customers on product pages, the configurator and checkout. These are the canonical explanations; prefer them over improvising an answer.

Fetch by exact `slug`, or search by keyword in slug/title/body. The full slug index is available as resource `products://blocks`.

Common slugs: `cilinder-keuze-uitleg`, `certificaat`, `skg-keurmerk-uitleg`, `kerntrekbeveiliging-uitleg`, `gelijksluitend`, `paniekfunctie`, `laagsteprijsgarantie`, `maatgarantie`, and per brand `knoppen-merk-{brand-slug}` / `cilindermaat-merk-{brand-slug}`.

## Returns
`items[]` with slug, title and body (`{html, text}`). Max 20 items.

## Example
`{"slug":"skg-keurmerk-uitleg"}` or `{"search":"kerntrek"}`

search.description: Keyword match on slug, title or body; used when slug is not given.

limit.description: Number of items to return (max 20, default 5).

tools.name: search_advice
tools.description:
## Use when
A customer needs **guidance rather than a spec**: which lock to choose, how to measure a cylinder, how to remove or install one, burglary prevention. The shop's advice pages ("advies") are written buying guides and how-tos with recommended products.

Search by keyword or browse a category (resource-style list when no filters are given). Results mirror what the website shows on /advies: published landing pages.

## Returns
`items[]` with title, public URL, category, a plain-text `body` (truncated to ~2000 chars) and `recommended_product_ids` — feed those ids to `get_product_detail` to suggest concrete products.

## Example
`{"search":"opmeten"}` or `{"advice_category_id":1}`

search.description: Keyword match on title, slug or page content.

include_body.description: Include the page text (default true; truncated to ~2000 chars).

limit.description: Number of pages to return (max 25, default 10).

tools.name: resolve_certificate_code
tools.description:
## Use when
A customer sent a photo of a security card / certificate, or typed its code, and you need to know which model to reorder. Read the code off the card and pass it verbatim; never derive a model from a code yourself.

A card can show other printed boxes next to the code, such as a generation marker (e.g. "G2"). Those do not belong to the code: leave them out, pass only the code itself.

Pass `brand` whenever the card shows one (M&C, ABUS, DOM, NEMEF, EVVA). It is how a wrong reading gets caught: if the code resolves to models of another brand, `brand_conflict` comes back true and you must not answer from this result.

Pass `reorder_type` only when the customer already said whether they need a cylinder (1) or keys (2).

## What it does
Normalises the code (strips spaces and punctuation, uppercases) and matches it against the reorder code patterns of the webshop, the same list the shop's own reorder filter uses. Returns the candidate models plus the matching reorder products.

## Returns
- `code`: the normalised code.
- `models`: candidate models, most often one. Several means the code alone cannot tell them apart; the model name printed on the card decides, otherwise ask the customer.
- `products`: reorder products per candidate model, with `url`, `brand` and `reorder_type` (1 = cylinder, 2 = keys). More than one product of the same `reorder_type` can come back for a single model, for example a sluitplan variant next to the regular version, or two different SKG levels, and they are genuinely different products. This tool never picks between them; ask the customer which one matches their situation instead of guessing.
- `brand_conflict`: true when `brand` was given and none of the products carry it.

Candidates are matched by name, so a `products` entry can belong to a model whose name only resembles the resolved model (e.g. a "+" variant of it). Have the customer confirm the exact product before ordering; never just take the first one.

An empty `models` means the code is not covered. Do not guess a model; escalate.

When `models` is not empty but `products` is empty, the catalog has no reorder product for that model. Do not invent a link; escalate instead.

## Example
`{"code":"084E2658","brand":"M&C"}`

code.description: The code as printed or stamped on the card, verbatim.

brand.description: Brand shown on the card (M&C, ABUS, DOM, NEMEF, EVVA), for the conflict check.

tools.name: current_promotions
tools.description:
## Use when
A customer asks whether there is **a sale or discount right now** ("is er korting?", "zijn er acties?"), without pointing at one specific product. For the effective sale price of one product, `get_product_detail` already returns its active `sale`.

## Returns
`promotions[]`, one entry per active sale:
- `name` and `discount_percent` (percentage off the shop price).
- `brand`: the brand the sale applies to (sales are brand-scoped).
- `product_overrides[]`: products with a deviating percentage; `excluded` true means the product does not join the sale at all.

An empty list means there are no active promotions; say so, do not invent one.

## Example
`{}` or `{"brand_slug":"dom"}`

brand_id.description: Only promotions for this brand id.

brand_slug.description: Only promotions for this brand slug (e.g. "dom").

doorax.nl.blurb: Search products, Get product detail and Get product options.
doorax.nl.name: Doorax

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Product detail parameters.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

value.description: Option value, e.g. "160cm" or "Fiberglass".

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant. To change a quantity or remove something already in the cart, use update_cart_lines instead — this tool can only add.

item.description: The merchandise to add.

id.description: ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

tools.description: Change the quantity of items already in the cart, or remove them. Every change here addresses an existing cart line by its id, so call get_cart first unless you already have line_items[].id from an earlier get_cart in this conversation. Pass the ABSOLUTE target quantity, not a delta — quantity 2 means the line ends up at 2 regardless of what it was. Use quantity 0 to remove the line entirely. Batch every change for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart_lines once per line. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. This tool cannot add new merchandise. To add something not already in the cart, use add_to_cart. To empty the whole cart at once, use cancel_cart.
