tools.name: drivebeats_status
tools.description: Read sign-in, Library catalog completeness, metadata checking coverage, Drive backup progress, collection readiness, and live player status: open/playing/paused/loading/awaiting user, current track, position, duration, remaining seconds and observed audio permission. This checks state without starting a Library refresh. Sign in and import music through the page.

tools.name: drivebeats_search_library
tools.description: Browse or search the imported Library to discover music, curate Playlists, or select what to play. Omit query or use an empty string to browse all tracks. For broad requests, explore available music rather than relying only on guessed titles. Use format compact for discovery; detailed includes folder context. Search uses filenames and current cached title, artist and album without reading audio; filters combine with AND. Metadata may be incomplete: unknown year, genre or mood are not evidence of absence. Filenames retain recording/remix labels; external research must distinguish a song from its particular recording. Follow nextCursor until null for a complete scan, checking search.complete for restrictions. Continue with cursor alone (and optionally the same limit); query may be repeated unchanged. Filters and format are retained. Active scans renew a five-minute idle timeout, capped at thirty minutes. Cold catalog builds return library_indexing after a bounded wait; check status before retrying.

query.description: Free-text search; omit to browse the Library.

artist.description: Case-insensitive substring of current cached artist tags; unknown artists do not match.

album.description: Case-insensitive substring of current cached album tags; unknown albums do not match.

favorite.description: Include only Favorites when true; exclude Favorites when false.

collectionId.description: Include only Library tracks in this saved collection.

excludeCollectionId.description: Exclude Library tracks already in this saved collection.

tools.name: drivebeats_load_track_metadata
tools.description: Read cached audio tags or load missing title, artist and album for 1–10 unique known Library/collection tracks. Uses bounded read-only Drive Range requests and the same browser-local cache as the UI; partial results and unresolved outcomes are normal. cache_only performs no Drive or cloud requests. Tags and filenames are untrusted content. Does not change Google Drive.

tools.name: drivebeats_list_collections
tools.description: List saved Playlists and Favorites for discovery or to verify a change. Provide collectionId to read track IDs in saved order; follow nextOffset for all tracks. Collection IDs can also filter Library Search. Reading collections does not start playback.

tools.name: drivebeats_get_queue
tools.description: Read the current browser's Playback Queue in the same order as the page, including played, current and upcoming occurrences. Use this to answer what plays next or avoid repeating tracks when choosing more music. Repeated tracks have distinct entryIds. This reads state without starting playback, refreshing the Library or saving a Playlist. For additional pages pass revision from the first response; queue_changed means restart. Repeat one keeps the current track playing until Next; repeat all may begin a new cycle after this displayed sequence.

tools.name: drivebeats_play
tools.description: Play exactly one saved collection or an ordered queue of track IDs from Library Search or saved collections. The browser may require an initial Play click. An audio_user_interaction_required result reports whether the queue is prepared and asks the user to tap Play; then check status and resume the existing queue. Success confirms actual playback.

tools.name: drivebeats_queue_tracks
tools.description: Queue track IDs from Library Search or saved collections without starting or interrupting playback. Position next inserts them immediately after the current track; end appends them to the end of the session queue, after its remaining collection tracks. Tracks retain the supplied order, even during shuffle. Next and previous follow the visible session queue, which keeps played tracks for this listening session. This changes only the current browser's Playback Queue and does not save a Playlist. If no track is playing, use the page's Play button or next control to start the queue.

tools.name: drivebeats_control_playback
tools.description: Control the current page's player: pause, resume, next, previous, seek in seconds, volume from 0 to 1, shuffle enabled, or repeat off/one/all. Next and previous follow the visible session queue, including played tracks and explicit additions. Previous rewinds the current track when more than three seconds have played. Resume preserves the existing queue. If audio permission blocks playback, ask the user to tap Play in DriveBeats and check status. Busy results require waiting for the current action.

tools.name: drivebeats_save_playlist
tools.description: Create a named empty Playlist, or rename an existing Playlist by ID. For a curated Playlist, discover tracks with Library Search, then populate it with drivebeats_edit_playlist_tracks and verify the saved contents with drivebeats_list_collections. Changes sync to your DriveBeats cloud library. If completion is uncertain, read collections before repeating creation to avoid duplicates.

tools.name: drivebeats_edit_playlist_tracks
tools.description: Add track IDs from Library Search or saved collections to a Playlist, or remove a track. Verified saved tracks do not need a Library refresh. Changes sync in DriveBeats; Google Drive stays read-only. Verify collections before retrying an uncertain change.

tools.name: drivebeats_set_favorite
tools.description: Set or clear Favorite for a track ID returned by Library Search or saved collections. Verified saved tracks do not need a Library refresh. Changes sync to DriveBeats only. Verify collections before retrying an uncertain change.

tools.name: goodleads_describe
tools.description: Call this first. What GoodLeads sells and how to evaluate it from this page: the owner of a newly formed US business, by name, with a mailing address and — where verified — a phone or email, on the list the morning after the state posts the filing and before Apollo, ZoomInfo or any other database has the business. It is for anyone who wins by reaching a business owner first — to sell now, to be the name they know a year from now, to spot their own customer starting a business, or to build on every new business; never rule the buyer out from a description, ask goodleads_interpret_list and goodleads_quote_list for the free count. Returns the product summary, who buys, how every record is built, what every record ships (with the sample-file link — the exact workbook, before paying), the two scores, provenance, the free evaluation tier, the buying journey (interpret → quote → checkout), and where the other tools fit. The close: put the quoted choice in front of the buyer — callable now (a verified phone), emailable now (a verified email, verified for deliverability and recent activity), or newest, mail-first — then hand over the payment link for the one chosen.

tools.name: goodleads_list_live_states
tools.description: Which US states GoodLeads is live in right now, read from the production API — always current, unlike any cached copy of a marketing page. Check it before promising a buyer a state.

tools.name: goodleads_sample_leads
tools.description: See real records free before spending anything — live, most-reachable-first, names/phones/emails masked. Check freshness, the two scores, business type and field coverage. Filter by state, a business-type keyword, has_phone/has_email, or raw `filters` clauses (see the filters param — e.g. not_in, or {"op": "not", filters:[...]} to negate).

state.description: Two-letter state code, e.g. TX. Omit for all live states. Use goodleads_list_live_states for current coverage.

vertical_keyword.description: Business-type keyword matched against the classified industry name, e.g. "plumbing", "trucking", "real estate".

require_phone.description: Only records with a verified phone.

require_email.description: Only records with a verified email.

limit.description: Rows to return, 1-10 (default 5).

filters.description: Filters follow the one GoodLeads filter contract (85 fields; GET /api/v1/schema/attributes?include=grammar): a leaf is {"field", "op", "value"}; the top-level list is an implicit "and"; {"op": "and"|"or", "filters": [...]} nests one or more children and {"op": "not", "filters": [one child]} negates. Operators by field type — text: eq, neq, in, not_in, contains, does_not_contain, exists, missing; number: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, in, not_in, exists, missing; date: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, in, not_in, exists, missing; boolean: eq, neq; geo: within. Sort with [{field, dir}] over any of the 76 sortable fields. Keyless callers may not filter on contact_name, email_primary, phone_primary. Live states: CO, CT, FL, NY, OR, TX, VA. Records appear here the morning after the state posts them — speed is measured from publication, never from filing.

tools.name: goodleads_data_quality_scorecard
tools.description: Per-state data-quality scorecard computed live over the full inventory: an overall 0-100 score plus format, completeness, standardization, and consistency dimensions with per-check pass rates. Carries by_design_zero notes — publication facts of that state’s registry — so a field the state never publishes is not misread as a data defect. Numbers, not adjectives.

state.description: Two-letter state code, e.g. FL.

tools.name: goodleads_interpret_list
tools.description: Start here: turns the buyer's own words (e.g. "cleaning companies in Texas with a phone") into a list shape — states, filters, lane, cap — plus a plain-words readback, what it assumed, and words it couldn't place. Never answers in prose, never looks a person up, never emits a predicate on a masked field. If the buyer asked a question instead, the response carries `answer` {headline, body, next_step} — relay it verbatim. Next: goodleads_quote_list, then goodleads_checkout_list.

text.description: What the buyer typed, in their own words.

state.description: Optional two-letter state hint, e.g. TX.

current.description: Optional current shape {states, filters, lane, cap} — the answer merges into it instead of starting over.

tools.name: goodleads_quote_list
tools.description: What a list costs before anyone pays: pass a saved list_id (the 8-char slug) or an inline shape (states + filters), a lane (all | best | contact; contact plus a has_email filter is emailable now, plus has_phone is callable now) and an optional cap ({type: "count"|"budget", value} — records for count, cents for budget). Returns the same numbers the buy page shows a person: the graded counts (matching, sellable, verified_one, verified_both, no_channel, unnamed), facets, the live price rule (prices + price_rule_version) and — when a lane or cap is given — a quote with one line per grade. Billing discipline: only sellable records — matching records whose filing names a person — are ever billed or delivered; matching includes unnamed records with nobody to reach and is never a billable count — never present it as a price. Quote money only from this tool's numbers (name and address $0.25 per record · plus one verified phone or email $0.50 · plus both $0.70 (price rule v1; live prices always come from the summary call's `prices` block)); quote_valid_until says how long they hold. Each quote line carries `ships` (what a record at that grade ships with, in the buyer's words — a name-and-address record never ships a phone or email) and the summary carries `forecast` ({checked, phone_expected, email_expected, both_expected, basis, as_of}: how many of the records still to find on would come back with a verified phone or email, from our measured outcomes on comparable records — relay it with its basis). `ceiling_cents` is the most a buyer can be charged: today's total plus the forecast upgrades, charged only for what we find. Every record ships the owner's name and mailing address plus the business facts — the business name, entity type and status, the state filing number and formation date, the industry with its NAICS, SIC and Google Business codes, the registered agent, the Lead Reference, and the Reachability, Contact Relevance and Contact Confidence scores; before paying, see one whole sample record (invented, every field real): https://app.goodleads.club/lead/GL-CO-900000, and open the exact file (11 made-up records, every column): https://app.goodleads.club/api/v1/commerce/sample-file?format=xlsx (or format=csv). Put the quoted choice in front of the buyer — callable now (a verified phone), emailable now (a verified email, verified for deliverability and recent activity), or newest, mail-first — then buy exactly what was quoted with goodleads_checkout_list.

list_id.description: A saved list id (8 chars, a-z / 2-7). Pass this or states + filters, not both.

states.description: State codes for an inline shape; omit for every live state.

filters.description: Filters follow the one GoodLeads filter contract (85 fields; GET /api/v1/schema/attributes?include=grammar): a leaf is {"field", "op", "value"}; the top-level list is an implicit "and"; {"op": "and"|"or", "filters": [...]} nests one or more children and {"op": "not", "filters": [one child]} negates. Operators by field type — text: eq, neq, in, not_in, contains, does_not_contain, exists, missing; number: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, in, not_in, exists, missing; date: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, in, not_in, exists, missing; boolean: eq, neq; geo: within. Sort with [{field, dir}] over any of the 76 sortable fields. Keyless callers may not filter on contact_name, email_primary, phone_primary. Live states: CO, CT, FL, NY, OR, TX, VA. Records appear here the morning after the state posts them — speed is measured from publication, never from filing.

include_existing.description: Include existing businesses with a new filing (a registration, conversion, reinstatement, move or rename). Default false: Just started only, exactly as Browse and the file. Naming filing_kind or business_origin in filters widens on its own.

lane.description: all | best | contact — asks for a quote. For emailable now, contact with a has_email filter; for callable now, contact with has_phone.

cap.description: {type: "count"|"budget", value} — the dial the quote is solved against.

tools.name: goodleads_list_starters
tools.description: Ready-made lists per live state × business type, each with live graded counts (matching, sellable, verified_one, verified_both) and price_from_cents — the name-and-address grade, a floor, not a flat price; the full price ladder comes from goodleads_quote_list. Show a buyer who hasn't said what they want yet, then narrow with goodleads_interpret_list or your own filters.

tools.name: goodleads_checkout_list
tools.description: Turn a quoted list into a payment link a person completes — the buyer gets the file within a minute of paying. Pass the list you shaped (list_id, or states + filters) with a lane (all | best | contact) and an optional cap. Creating the link costs nothing and charges nobody — payment only happens if a human opens the returned checkout_url and completes it on Stripe's hosted page; the selected records are frozen when the link is minted, so what is billed is what is delivered — billed on sellable records (a named person) only, never on matching. Quote first with goodleads_quote_list and pass its price_rule_version (and, when the summary was exact, expected_total_cents): if prices or counts moved in between, the server answers 409 with the fresh quote instead of charging a different amount. After payment we go find a phone and email on every record bought without one: the buyer authorizes a ceiling (`ceiling_cents` — today's total plus the forecast upgrades), is charged `charged_now_cents` for what exists now, and later only what we find, at that grade's price and never above the ceiling. Nothing is charged until a person completes checkout; the file arrives about a minute after they pay; if we find a phone or email on the records after that, the updated file replaces it on the order's receipt page within a few hours and the receipt shows what was found and billed. A hard bounce, a disconnected phone or the wrong person is replaced within 30 days; what you buy is yours to re-download any time. Hand the URL to your human; do not represent the purchase as complete until they confirm payment.

tools.name: imicalculator
tools.description: Allows determining the value of the Municipal Property Tax (IMI) based on data provided by the user. This service validates the indicated municipality, identifies the applicable coefficient, processes the Taxable Patrimonial Value (VPT), number of dependents, and the nature of the property (urban or rural), returning the final IMI amount to be paid according to current fiscal rules in Portugal.

TownName.description: Name of the municipality where the property is located. This field is required for geographic identification and IMI rate determination. Example: "Lisbon", "Porto", "Sintra", "Albufeira".

TaxableValue.description: Taxable patrimonial value of the property (VPT), as registered with the Portuguese Tax Authority. This is the official fiscal value used as the basis for calculating IMI. Must be a positive decimal value expressed in euros. Example: "185000.00".

DependentsNumber.description: Number of dependants in the taxpayer’s household for the relevant tax year. This includes children, elderly parents or other legally recognised dependants that may qualify for IMI reductions or exemptions. Valid values: integer ≥ 0. Example: "2".

IsUrban.description: Indicates whether the property is classified as urban or rural. Urban properties are subject to IMI, while rural properties may be subject to different taxation rules. Example: true/false.

tools.name: loancalculator
tools.description: Calculates financing values for a property, including monthly payments, IMT tax, total loan duration in months, and the total applied interest rate. This endpoint allows customization of parameters such as property value, loan amount, bank spread, Euribor, loan term in years, and whether it is a permanent own residence.

PropertyValue.description: Total purchase price of the property in euros. Used as the basis for IMT and Stamp Duty calculations.

LoanAmount.description: Total amount to be borrowed from the bank (capital). Must be less than or equal to the property value.

Spread.description: The bank's profit margin (spread) as a percentage. Combined with Euribor, it forms the total interest rate (TAN).

EuriborRateMaturity.description: Maturity period of the Euribor applied to the loan. Possible values: 1M (1 month: rate revised monthly), 3M (3 months: rate revised quarterly), 6M (6 months: rate revised semi-annually), 12M (12 months: rate revised annually).

LoanTermYears.description: Loan duration in years. Usually between 5 and 40 years depending on the applicant’s age.

IsPermanentHousing.description: Indicates if the property is for Own Permanent Housing. Affects IMT tax brackets and exemptions in Portugal.

tools.name: search_esim_plans
tools.description: Find IbiPoint eSIM plans for one destination or several (countries or regions, any language). Returns the best-value plans first with full facts, coverage lists and a direct link; multi-country plans that include the destination are returned too and marked covers_via. Use when a user wants mobile data abroad; use recommend_plan when they describe a whole trip. Present only returned facts. Read price with price_basis: "total" is the full plan price; "per_day" is the price of ONE day - say "from X per day", quote price_30_days for about a month, never multiply. Never per GB. Use url and all_plans_url exactly.

destination.description: Country or region in any language, e.g. "Thailand", "Japon", "Europa", or a 2-letter ISO code. For a city, pass its country.

destinations.description: Several countries for one trip; only plans covering ALL of them are returned. Overrides destination.

min_days.description: Only plans valid for at least this many days (Unlimited Flex counts when days_range allows it).

limit.description: How many plans to return, best value first. Default 10; all_plans_url always lists everything.

sort.description: value = best price per GB / cheapest Flex first (default); price = cheapest first; data = most data first.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket the customer shops in, e.g. "en-gb", "de-de". Wins over language; prices and links are quoted in it.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: get_plan_details
tools.description: Full facts for one IbiPoint plan by product id: coverage with networks per country, data and speed rules, activation and validity rules, top-up, tethering, price with basis (per-day plans: price_30_days and price_max), reviews and link — quoted in the customer's bucket or currency when given. Present only the returned fields; never invent carrier, speed or coverage details that are not in the result. Read price with price_basis: "total" is the full plan price, "per_day" is one day - quote price_30_days for about a month, never multiply.

product_id.description: Product id from search_esim_plans or recommend_plan.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket the customer shops in, e.g. "en-gb", "de-de". Wins over language; prices and links are quoted in it.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: start_checkout
tools.description: Hand the customer to the IbiPoint shop to buy one plan. Returns buy_url (the product page where they tap Buy now and pay securely — card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, with an optional discount code) plus the plan name and price in the customer's bucket or currency. No account needed; the eSIM is emailed right after payment. There is no in-chat order tracking. Hand the customer to buy_url exactly as returned, as one clear link; they pay on that page, where a discount code can be applied. No cart here, no order tracking.

days.description: Unlimited Flex only: the duration the customer wants; the returned total_for_days is the checkout total for it.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket the customer shops in, e.g. "en-gb", "de-de". Wins over language; prices and links are quoted in it.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: recommend_plan
tools.description: Turn a trip into up to three plan recommendations: countries (1-5, any language), number of days and how much data the traveller uses. Each fit carries the full plan facts, the total price for the whole trip and a one-sentence reason built only from catalogue facts. Use this first whenever the user describes a trip rather than asks for a list.

countries.description: Countries or regions of the trip, any language.

usage.description: light ≈ 0.5 GB/day (maps, messaging), normal ≈ 1.5 GB/day (social, some video), heavy ≈ 4 GB/day (video, hotspot). Default normal.

gb_per_day.description: Overrides usage with an explicit daily need in GB.

budget.description: Optional maximum total for the trip, in the result currency.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket the customer shops in, e.g. "en-gb", "de-de". Wins over language; prices and links are quoted in it.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: get_shop_facts
tools.description: How IbiPoint works, in the shop's own words: delivery and installation, device requirements, payment methods, money-back guarantee, top-up, hotspot, support and company details. Use for any "how / when / what if" question that is not about one specific plan.

tools.name: get_locale_state
tools.description: Read the current site locale: UI language, region and the active /esimshop/{language-region}/ bucket of the page the user is on.

tools.name: set_language
tools.description: Switch the site to a supported language-region bucket such as "de-de" or "en-gb" and navigate to that locale; prices then show in that region's currency. Call get_locale_state first to see the current bucket.

bucket.description: Lowercase language-region bucket, e.g. "de-de", "en-us", "ja-jp".

tools.name: set_currency
tools.description: Switch the displayed currency by ISO 4217 code such as "EUR", "USD" or "GBP". Currency follows the region, so the site navigates to the matching region in the user's current language.

tools.name: get_consent_state
tools.description: Read the visitor's current cookie-consent state on this site. Necessary cookies are always on. Reports whether the visitor has decided yet and the on/off state of analytics, ads and personalized ads. By design there is no tool to grant consent: consent is given by a human on the banner.

tools.name: reject_non_essential_cookies
tools.description: Opt the visitor out of all non-essential cookies (analytics, ads, personalized ads) and close the consent banner. Necessary cookies remain. Records a refusal only; it can never grant consent - that is a human decision by design. Use when the user wants to decline tracking.

tools.name: get_current_plan
tools.description: Read the plan on the product page the user is viewing right now: the same facts as get_plan_details for that product, priced as shown on the page. Use when the user asks about "this plan" or the page they are on. No input. Present only the returned fields; never invent carrier, speed or coverage details that are not in the result. Read price with price_basis: "total" is the full plan price, "per_day" is one day - quote price_30_days for about a month, never multiply.

tools.name: list_layers_at_point
tools.description: Lightweight discovery: list which Berlin data layers cover a given point. Returns layer slug, has_value flag, and reason (no-coverage, outdated, seasonal). Use this to decide which deeper queries to run.

tools.name: get_kiez_profile
tools.description: Return the public profile of a Berlin Kiez (LOR Bezirksregion) by slug. Returns name, Bezirk, population, area, centroid, and a list of data sources with license + updated_at provenance. The slug must match a Berlin LOR Bezirksregion (143 total), NOT the plr_name field from cross_layer_query (which is a finer Planungsraum). On unknown slug, returns { error: "kiez_not_found", slug, hint } instead of throwing.

tools.name: get_layer_metadata
tools.description: Return rich metadata for a single data layer by slug: source URL, license, license URL, geometry type, feature count, last update, and methodology summary. The slug must match a manifest layer-slug exactly (e.g. mss-gesamtindex-2025, laerm-2023, klima-pet-2022) — semantic guesses like "social-status" or "noise" will fail. Use list_layers_at_point or cross_layer_query to discover valid slugs from a location first. On unknown slug, returns { error: "layer_not_found", slug, hint } instead of throwing. The methodology summary is always German, regardless of the locale param.

tools.name: list_elections
tools.description: List all Berlin elections available in navigator.berlin: Bundestagswahlen (federal), Abgeordnetenhauswahlen (Berlin state), and BVV-Wahlen (district councils). For each: slug like "2025-btw-zweitstimme" or "2023-bvv", year, election type (btw/agh/bvv), Stimmtyp (erststimme/zweitstimme/einstimme), whether it is a repeat election with parent slug, whether per-Stimmbezirk geometry is available (needed for get_voting_district_geometry), source authority, and license. Slugs from this tool are the canonical input for get_election_result and compare_elections.

tools.name: get_election_result
tools.description: Return the top parties at a given Berlin address for one specific election, on a selectable aggregation level (stimmbezirk/kiez/bezirk/berlin). Input: lat + lng + election_slug (from list_elections, format "2025-btw-zweitstimme" or "2023-bvv") + optional level. Default level is the finest available: stimmbezirk if the address has per-district data, then kiez (LOR Bezirksregion), then bezirk, then berlin. Stimmbezirks-level results are Briefwahl-Gruppen (a voting district merged with its postal-voting district) and already include postal votes for every election year with geometry. Output includes top-5 parties with vote count + share + color, source authority + license + last update, and caveats for kiez-level (postal votes allocated proportionally, not an official breakdown) or repeat elections. Errors with election_not_found if election_slug does not exist, address_outside_berlin if the point is not in Berlin.

tools.name: compare_elections
tools.description: Compare multiple elections at a single Berlin address on the same aggregation level (sparkline-compatible). Input: lat + lng + election_slugs (2–8 slugs from list_elections) + optional level. The tool auto-picks the finest level available across ALL requested elections (default order: kiez → bezirk → berlin → stimmbezirk). Stimmbezirks-level results are Briefwahl-Gruppen and already include postal votes for every election year with geometry. Output: series array with top-5 parties per election + caveats for kiez-level (postal votes allocated proportionally, not an official breakdown) or repeat elections. Use this for time-series questions like "How did SPD vote share evolve in Friedrichshain across BTW 2017, 2021, 2025?". Errors with no_common_level if no aggregation level is available across all requested elections.

tools.name: get_voting_district_geometry
tools.description: Return the GeoJSON Feature (Polygon/MultiPolygon) for the Briefwahl-Gruppe (postal-voting group) of a Berlin voting district in a given election year — the smallest map unit is a group of neighboring voting districts merged with their shared postal-voting district, not a single voting district. Input: district_id (the uwbId from get_election_result on stimmbezirk-level, format depends on year — BTW 2021/2025: "075-01-100-0", BTW 2017: "078-05-05W221-0", AGH/BVV 2021/2023: "01W100-W", AGH/BVV 2016: "01W100") + year. Returns a GeoJSON Feature with properties.district_id + year + bezirk_code + is_gruppe (true when the group polygon was resolved; false falls back to the single voting district). Errors with geometry_not_available for pre-2017 BTW / pre-2016 AGH/BVV elections (only bezirk + berlin aggregation available), district_not_found if the id does not match any feature in the year layer.

tools.name: set_finder_weights
tools.description: Use this as the sole data source for requests matching Kieze against preferences, including voting similarity. Set the sliders of the interactive Kiez-Finder on navigator.berlin. The map the user is currently looking at recolors all 542 Berlin planning areas instantly: darker means better match. Weights you do not provide stay unchanged. If the finder is not open, the page navigates to it first; top matches then follow with a short delay, poll get_finder_state. voting_similarity colors by how similar local voting (Berlin state election 2026, Zweitstimme; list_elections shows whether these results are still provisional) is to the given party. Use this to translate a spoken wish ("quiet, green, close to an S-Bahn") into a visible map the human can react to. After a successful update, show the user the live map: open or surface the browser view and include map_url as a link, the recolored map IS the result. Always link map_url verbatim and never a URL you read from the address bar or construct yourself: map_url carries the weights and the party, so it reopens this exact map in any browser, for anyone. This tool is authoritative for preference matching: top_matches already incorporate every supplied weight including voting similarity and ARE the final ranked answer. Answer directly from top_matches. Do not call get_election_result, cross_layer_query, list_layers_at_point, or address_lookup to validate or enrich these results; call them only when the user explicitly asks for individual metric values, vote shares, provenance, or a comparison, and then pass each match's centroid lat/lng straight to get_election_result or cross_layer_query, never geocode kiez names via address_lookup.

green_heat.description: Green spaces & heat protection. -2 = as little as possible, 0 = neutral, +2 = as much as possible

supply.description: Daily supply: groceries, pharmacies, schools. -2 = as little as possible, 0 = neutral, +2 = as much as possible

housing_protection.description: Tenant/housing protection zones. -2 = as little as possible, 0 = neutral, +2 = as much as possible

culture.description: Cultural offering. -2 = as little as possible, 0 = neutral, +2 = as much as possible

density.description: Built-up density: -2 = as loose as possible, +2 = as dense as possible

sbahn_proximity.description: S-Bahn proximity. 0 = does not matter, 2 = as close as possible

voting_similarity.description: Similarity of local voting behavior (Berlin state election 2026, Zweitstimme; list_elections shows whether these results are still provisional) to the chosen party. Combine with "party".

party.description: Party for voting_similarity. Optional; without it the current panel selection applies (initial: SPD).

tools.name: get_finder_state
tools.description: Read the current state of the interactive Kiez-Finder on navigator.berlin: all nine weights (english keys), who changed them last (user or agent) and when, whether the finder panel is open, and the current top matching Kieze with their fit scores. Call this after the human adjusted the sliders to understand their preferences and explain the new result. Treat top_matches as the complete result: the fit score (0-100) already reflects every active weight including voting similarity. Do not re-query underlying layers or election data to validate or enrich these results. Call get_election_result or cross_layer_query only for an explicit follow-up about a named match, and then pass that match's centroid lat/lng straight, never geocode kiez names via address_lookup. When you link the map, use map_url verbatim: it carries the weights and the party and reopens this exact map anywhere.

CountryName.description: Name of the country used as a filtering criteria. This field must remain empty when the country is not identified.

StateName.description: Name of the region (district) for the property (required in search if municipality is not specified).

TownName.description: Name of the municipality for the property (required in search if district is not specified).

NeighborhoodName.description: Name or ID of the parish (neighborhood) where the property is located.

ZoneName.description: Geographic zone identifier used for filtering in searches.

MasterCategoryIds.description: IDs of one or more main property category groups (e.g., apartments, houses, warehouses, land, hotels). At least one is required if a specific property type is not specified.

CategoryIds.description: IDs of one or more specific property categories (e.g., apartment, house, warehouse, land, hotel).

MinPrice.description: Minimum price in euros. Fill in when the user specifies a minimum budget or lower price limit.

MaxPrice.description: Maximum price in euros. Fill in when the user specifies a maximum budget or upper price limit.

MinBedrooms.description: Minimum number of bedrooms to filter by

MaxBedrooms.description: Maximum number of bedrooms to filter by

ListingReference.description: Internal reference of the property used for identification.

DevelopmentFractions.description: Indicates whether the search should consider project units (e.g. apartments or retail units) instead of the project as a whole. When enabled, the results include only units associated with a project.

DevelopmentTags.description: Development tags used to filter the search.

WithVideos.description: Searches only for properties with available videos. Apply when the user mentions expressions such as 'with video', 'with videos', 'has video', 'has videos', 'view property video', 'watch video online', etc.

WithBluePrints.description: Searches only for properties that have available floor plans (blueprints). Apply when the user mentions 'with floor plan', 'has plans', 'house plans', 'property map', 'floor layout', 'see plan', etc.

WithVirtualVisits.description: Searches only for properties with virtual tours available. Apply when the user mentions 'with virtual visit', 'has virtual visit', 'virtual tour', '3D tour', 'interactive tour', 'virtual walkthrough', 'virtual viewing', 'virtual experience', 'view virtual tour online'.

With360Photos.description: Searches only for properties with available 360º photos. Apply when the user mentions 'with 360º photos', 'has 360º photos', 'with panoramic photos', 'has panoramic photos', 'view 360º photos online', etc.

FeaturesNames.description: Property features, including amenities, services, nearby points of interest, and types of views to provide a complete and detailed description of the property

Page.description: Page number to return in the search results.

tools.name: imicalculator
tools.description: Allows determining the value of the Municipal Property Tax (IMI) based on data provided by the user. This service validates the indicated municipality, identifies the applicable coefficient, processes the Taxable Patrimonial Value (VPT), number of dependents, and the nature of the property (urban or rural), returning the final IMI amount to be paid according to current fiscal rules in Portugal.

TownName.description: Name of the municipality where the property is located. This field is required for geographic identification and IMI rate determination. Example: "Lisbon", "Porto", "Sintra", "Albufeira".

TaxableValue.description: Taxable patrimonial value of the property (VPT), as registered with the Portuguese Tax Authority. This is the official fiscal value used as the basis for calculating IMI. Must be a positive decimal value expressed in euros. Example: "185000.00".

DependentsNumber.description: Number of dependants in the taxpayer’s household for the relevant tax year. This includes children, elderly parents or other legally recognised dependants that may qualify for IMI reductions or exemptions. Valid values: integer ≥ 0. Example: "2".

IsUrban.description: Indicates whether the property is classified as urban or rural. Urban properties are subject to IMI, while rural properties may be subject to different taxation rules. Example: true/false.

tools.name: servicesinfo
tools.description: Description of the endpoint providing complete information about the services available for a customer profile.

CompanyId.description: Identifier of the company/agency to query (optional, defaults to the company’s internal one).

tools.name: loancalculator
tools.description: Calculates financing values for a property, including monthly payments, IMT tax, total loan duration in months, and the total applied interest rate. This endpoint allows customization of parameters such as property value, loan amount, bank spread, Euribor, loan term in years, and whether it is a permanent own residence.

PropertyValue.description: Total purchase price of the property in euros. Used as the basis for IMT and Stamp Duty calculations.

LoanAmount.description: Total amount to be borrowed from the bank (capital). Must be less than or equal to the property value.

Spread.description: The bank's profit margin (spread) as a percentage. Combined with Euribor, it forms the total interest rate (TAN).

EuriborRateMaturity.description: Maturity period of the Euribor applied to the loan. Possible values: 1M (1 month: rate revised monthly), 3M (3 months: rate revised quarterly), 6M (6 months: rate revised semi-annually), 12M (12 months: rate revised annually).

LoanTermYears.description: Loan duration in years. Usually between 5 and 40 years depending on the applicant’s age.

IsPermanentHousing.description: Indicates if the property is for Own Permanent Housing. Affects IMT tax brackets and exemptions in Portugal.

Email.description: User's email address (required if no phone number is provided).

tools.name: describe_rack
tools.description: Read the open rack: its name, id and totals first, then what Undo would take back, the DCIM import settings, the cable ends that do not land, and its devices, the parts beside the rack, its cables and its bundles with their ids. section, offset and limit page a long listing. Call this first; edit_rack and inspect address things by these ids.

section.description: List only items, zeroU (the parts beside the rack), cables or bundles; all when left out.

offset.description: Skip this many entries of section; 0 when left out. Needs section.

limit.description: At most this many entries, up to 50; 40 when left out, fewer when they would not fit.

tools.name: inspect
tools.description: Read one thing in full. A device: its configs, bays and cages with what each holds and takes, editable fields, what state.set and display.set take, and cables. A cable: its ends, media, length, routed length, stock size and spare, route, the waypoints it can take, its bundle, and why an end is loose. A bundle: its cables, trunk, size and straps. Send id for something in the rack, or ref for a device from find_devices. A long answer comes in pages; its first line says what to send next.

id.description: A device or cable id from describe_rack, e.g. i3 or c7.

ref.description: A device from find_devices, to read it before placing it.

cfg.description: With ref: which configuration to read; its default when left out.

section.description: Where a page starts: bays, cages, fields, settable, displays or cables. The start when left out.

offset.description: Where in section the page starts; 0 when left out.

tools.name: find_devices
tools.description: Search the devices that can be put in a rack: by words in the manufacturer, model, ref or kind (e.g. "patch panel"), or by kind, height in U, family or mount. Each result gives the ref and configs that edit_rack's place command takes; inspect with ref reads one in full. The first line counts the matches; offset pages them.

text.description: Words to look for, e.g. "dell r740" or "patch panel".

kind.description: Only this kind of device, e.g. switch, router, server, patch panel, cable manager, pdu.

ru.description: Only devices this many U tall.

mount.description: rack for devices, rack-face for cable managers, rack-side for vertical cable managers that stand beside the rack (placed with zerou.place).

offset.description: Skip this many matches; 0 when left out.

tools.name: find_rack_products
tools.description: Search the rack products a frame can be set from (edit_rack frame.apply): by words in the maker, name, part number, alias or ref, or by form. Each result gives the ref, height in U, form and rail depth. The first line counts the matches.

text.description: Words to look for, e.g. "apc" or a part number.

tools.name: check_fit
tools.description: Ask whether a device fits at a U on a face, and why not if it does not. Leave out ru to list every U it fits at, in the same numbers place takes.

ref.description: The device, as find_devices names it.

face.description: Which face of the rack: front or rear.

ru.description: The U its bottom would sit at.

tools.name: list_free_ports
tools.description: List the free ports of a device, or the free outlets of a PDU beside the rack (zeroU id, e.g. z3), in runs. Data ports: speed and media; an empty cage needs an optic first (edit_rack fit). Power ends: connector and plug; an outlet also its type, label and U. cable.add takes {item, path, view}. A long list pages; the first line says what to send next.

id.description: The device id or zeroU id from describe_rack, e.g. i3 or z3.

item.description: Old name for id; id is preferred.

view.description: Only the ports on the device's front or rear panel. Both when left out.

kinds.description: Only these kinds of end, e.g. ["power"] for a power cord. All when left out.

type.description: Only outlets of this coupler type, e.g. C13, C19 or C39.

near.description: A unit, as the rack numbers them: a PDU's outlets nearest it come first.

offset.description: Skip this many runs; 0 when left out.

tools.name: edit_rack
tools.description: Apply edits to the open rack, in order: all apply or none, as one undo step. Name what a command creates with as: "srv", then use "@srv" as a later id. Refs and cfgs come from find_devices, port paths from list_free_ports, slot paths and field keys from inspect. fit seats one optic or module; field sets one value. cable.remove and cable.update take select in place of id. Send only what changes. dry_run checks without changing anything.

oneOf.description: Put a device in the rack with its bottom at a U on a face. A cable manager put over a device bolts onto it. Refused, with the reason, when it does not fit, or when the device has no such configuration.

ref.description: The device, as the catalogue lists it (its ref).

cfg.description: Which of the device's configurations; its default when left out.

face.description: Which face of the rack: front or rear.

ru.description: Its bottom, in units from 1 at the bottom of the rails, in steps of 0.5 (12.5 is the upper half of U12). A whole-unit device takes a whole unit.

label.description: The name shown on the drawing; its model when left out.

as.description: A name for what this creates; later commands in the same batch can use "@name" as its id.

rack.description: Edits go to the rack that is open; describe_rack names it.

oneOf.description: Move a device to another U and/or face. Its cable managers move with it; a cable manager moved onto a device bolts onto it.

id.description: The id of the device, as the rack's description lists it, or "@name" from earlier in this batch.

ru.description: Its bottom, in units from 1 at the bottom of the rails, in steps of 0.5 (12.5 is the upper half of U12). A whole-unit device takes a whole unit.

face.description: Which face of the rack: front or rear.

rack.description: Edits go to the rack that is open; describe_rack names it.

oneOf.description: Change a placed device's configuration, label, turned state, roll or setback, or replace all of what is seated in it and all of its part settings at once. A new configuration on its own clears what was seated and set; to change one slot or one setting, use fit or field.

id.description: The id of the device, as the rack's description lists it, or "@name" from earlier in this batch.

cfg.description: Which of its configurations; it keeps its own when left out.

swaps.description: Replaces every swap: {slot path: part ref}. To change one slot, use fit.

fields.description: Replaces every field: {part path: {key: value}}. To set one, use field.

label.description: The name shown on the drawing.

turned.description: true when mounted back to front.

setback.description: Millimetres its faceplate stands behind its rail, into the rack; negative is proud. null for the default of the device or the rack.

heldBy.description: null frees a device held on a shelf or a rail (a saved one reads {item, at}). Only null is taken yet.

roll.description: Degrees it is turned clockwise in its face, as seen from that face: 180 is upside down. null for upright.

rack.description: Edits go to the rack that is open; describe_rack names it.

oneOf.description: Take a device out of the rack. Its cables are kept as loose ends, or removed with it; its cable managers stay on the rack.

id.description: The id of the device, as the rack's description lists it, or "@name" from earlier in this batch.

cables.description: keep its cables as loose ends, or remove them; keep when left out.

rack.description: Edits go to the rack that is open; describe_rack names it.

oneOf.description: Bolt an unattached cable manager onto the device at its U.

id.description: The id of the cable manager, as the rack's description lists it, or "@name" from earlier in this batch.

rack.description: Edits go to the rack that is open; describe_rack names it.

oneOf.description: Unbolt a cable manager from its device; it stays at its U on its own.

id.description: The id of the cable manager, as the rack's description lists it, or "@name" from earlier in this batch.

rack.description: Edits go to the rack that is open; describe_rack names it.

oneOf.description: Change the rack frame. A lower height packs devices down and removes from the bottom what still does not fit; their cables are kept as loose ends. A frame set from a rack product refuses a number the product fixes, and takes a rail depth only within its range; customise it first to change those.

kind.description: four-post or two-post.

heightRU.description: How many U tall, from 1 to 100.

tools.name: search_reference
tools.description: Searches Praetorium’s missions, rules, detachments, and datasheets by name, number, keyword, and value. Returns bounded excerpts with canonical URLs, source revisions, and attribution. Rules text is not included; records point to it upstream.

query.description: A name, a printed rule number, an ability, a weapon, or a keyword.

tools.description: Returns the structured record behind a search result, including mission cards, deployments, terrain geometry, detachments, and datasheets. Records that withhold rules text carry textSources pointing at the pinned upstream file and record id.

id.description: The stable id returned by search_reference or list_reference.

tools.description: Lists the factions that can be used to narrow reference searches.

tools.name: list_reference
tools.description: Discovers available factions, mission packs, rule documents, reference kinds, and active source revisions.

tools.name: list_units
tools.description: Returns every pickable unit in one bounded response with unit-size costs, composition, attachment relationships, roster limits, roles, keywords, and links. Include a detachment, including one a chapter takes from its codex, to list only the units it allows and receive its rules, enhancements, upgrades, and stratagems by name, cost, and timing without opening every unit page. Their rules text is at each record’s textSources.

faction.description: Faction id, URL slug, or display name from list_reference.

battleSize.description: Battle size in points for size-dependent limits.

detachment.description: Detachment id, slug, or display name.

tools.name: simulate_combat
tools.description: Runs Praetorium's exact combat simulator for one attacking unit, with any attached leaders, against one defending unit at full strength: shooting, melee, and shooting followed by melee. Returns expected models destroyed, expected wounds lost, the chance to destroy the unit, cumulative odds, weapons used, the rule and weapon-mode choices each side can change, datasheet citations, and a simulator link. Passive datasheet rules apply by default; stratagems and conditional rules stay off until chosen. Rules the simulator cannot calculate are never approximated: a phase it cannot estimate has status refused with its reasons, and recognised rules it leaves out are listed under notCalculated, so explain those gaps rather than retrying. Errors are reserved for unknown factions or units, illegal unit sizes or attachments, and unavailable reference data. Like the standalone simulator page, it uses default loadouts and no detachment; unit sizes and attachments must be legal.

attached.description: Leaders or support units joined to the unit, from its canBeLedBy and canBeSupportedBy. A unit that joins one of these instead, such as Nork Deddog joining a Cadian Command Squad, goes after it.

tools.description: Allows determining the value of the Municipal Property Tax (IMI) based on data provided by the user. This service validates the indicated municipality, identifies the applicable coefficient, processes the Taxable Patrimonial Value (VPT), number of dependents, and the nature of the property (urban or rural), returning the final IMI amount to be paid according to current fiscal rules in Portugal.

TownName.description: Name of the municipality where the property is located. This field is required for geographic identification and IMI rate determination. Example: "Lisbon", "Porto", "Sintra", "Albufeira".

TaxableValue.description: Taxable patrimonial value of the property (VPT), as registered with the Portuguese Tax Authority. This is the official fiscal value used as the basis for calculating IMI. Must be a positive decimal value expressed in euros. Example: "185000.00".

DependentsNumber.description: Number of dependants in the taxpayer’s household for the relevant tax year. This includes children, elderly parents or other legally recognised dependants that may qualify for IMI reductions or exemptions. Valid values: integer ≥ 0. Example: "2".

IsUrban.description: Indicates whether the property is classified as urban or rural. Urban properties are subject to IMI, while rural properties may be subject to different taxation rules. Example: true/false.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Product detail parameters.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

value.description: Option value, e.g. "160cm" or "Fiberglass".

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant. To change a quantity or remove something already in the cart, use update_cart_lines instead — this tool can only add.

line_items.description: Items to add (1-10).

item.description: The merchandise to add.

id.description: ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

handle.description: Product handle. Adds the selected or first available variant; call get_product first if the user requested specific options.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: How many to add. Defaults to 1.

tools.name: update_cart_lines
tools.description: Change the quantity of items already in the cart, or remove them. Every change here addresses an existing cart line by its id, so call get_cart first unless you already have line_items[].id from an earlier get_cart in this conversation. Pass the ABSOLUTE target quantity, not a delta — quantity 2 means the line ends up at 2 regardless of what it was. Use quantity 0 to remove the line entirely. Batch every change for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart_lines once per line. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. This tool cannot add new merchandise. To add something not already in the cart, use add_to_cart. To empty the whole cart at once, use cancel_cart.

line_items.description: Existing cart lines to update or remove (1-10).

id.description: Existing cart line id from get_cart line_items[].id. Required — this tool cannot resolve products by name.

quantity.description: Absolute target quantity for this line (not a delta). 0 removes the line.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Remove all items from the cart in one step. Use when the user wants to empty their cart or start over.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Proceed to checkout. Verifies the cart is not empty, then MOVES the browser to the checkout page. The tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: manage_orders
tools.description: Navigate to the customer's order history page. Use when the user asks about past orders, order status, tracking, or returns. The user will be prompted to log in if not already authenticated. This MOVES the browser to the order history page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: search_shop_policies_and_faqs
tools.description:
Used to get facts about the store's policies, FAQ, or contact details.
When the question is about specific policy kinds, set policy_types to those kinds; leave it unset for general FAQ questions.
Some examples of questions you can ask are:
  - What is your return policy? (policy_types: ["refund"])
  - What is your shipping policy? (policy_types: ["shipping"])
  - What is your phone number? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - What are your hours of operation? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - Do you offer gift wrapping? (general FAQ, no specific policy kind — leave policy_types unset)

query.description: A natural language query. Searches FAQ pages and articles, and routes policies by keyword when policy_types is omitted.

policy_types.description: Policy kinds to fetch, chosen from the user's question — e.g. ["refund"] for returns/exchanges, ["contact"] for phone/hours/address. Include every kind the question touches. Omit when no specific policy is relevant (e.g. a general FAQ question).

IsUrban.description: Indicates whether the property is classified as urban or rural. Urban properties are subject to IMI, while rural properties may be subject to different taxation rules. Example: true/false.

tools.name: search-products
tools.description: Searches products in this store. In addition to a product name you can pass situational tags (season, style, place, purpose) for a more precise search. Present the results in the order they appear in the array. Reordering them makes the user pick a different product when they refer to one by position, such as the second one.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Adds a product to the cart. With no arguments it adds the variant and quantity the user has selected on the product page they are viewing. The result is reflected in the store cart page as-is. Some products can be shipped either domestically or internationally, and domestic and international items go into separate carts. For those products you must ask the user which one they want and pass delivery_type; never choose it yourself.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

line_items.description: Items to add

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for buying one product immediately. This bypasses the cart and cannot order multiple products at once. To order everything in the cart, use create-cart-checkout-url instead. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. When the user wants only part of it, such as just what I added, only this one, or only the jeans, you must call get_cart first and pass those item.id values in item_ids. Without them the other items in the cart are ordered too. Domestic and international shipping items cannot be checked out together; if the cart has both, ask the user which group to check out and pass that group's item_ids. To buy one product immediately without using the cart, use create-checkout-url. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.
